acceptance:
- [ ] WorkerManager starts a supervisor goroutine on first worker launch
- [ ] Watchdog reaps workers past `WatchdogDeadline` with no phase transition in `StallDeadline`
- [ ] SIGTERM→SIGKILL escalation works on an intentionally-wedged test worker (unit test with a goroutine that ignores ctx)
- [ ] Reaped worker's bead claim is released (tracker status returns to open or claim-expired)
- [ ] `bead.reaped` event recorded on tracker with reason="watchdog" and duration
- [ ] Watchdog deadlines are configurable via ddx server config
description:
## Residual risk after RC1–RC4 from ddx-0a651925

Even with context propagation (RC1), wall-clock bounds (RC2), tightened breakers (RC3), and provider deadlines (RC4), a goroutine-level deadlock or panic-swallowed handler could still leave a worker alive past any reasonable bound. Today, `server.WorkerManager.Stop` (workers.go:648) only calls `handle.cancel()` — it has no escalation to OS-level signal and no autonomous trigger. ddx-b808df39 adds the *operator* tool; this bead adds the *autonomous* watchdog.

## Scope

1. WorkerManager runs a supervisor goroutine that, every minute, inspects each `workerHandle`.
2. If `time.Since(record.StartedAt) > WatchdogDeadline` (default e.g. 6h) AND `record.CurrentAttempt` has not transitioned in `StallDeadline` (default e.g. 1h), escalate:
   - Send SIGTERM to the worker's process group (requires surfacing PID, aligned with ddx-b808df39).
   - After 30s grace, send SIGKILL.
   - Mark record.State = "reaped"; update claimed bead state so the claim is not leaked.
3. Emit a `bead.reaped` event on the tracker with the full timeline so post-mortems are easy.

## Non-goals

- Per-bead runtime tuning; defaults are enough.
- Replacing ddx-b808df39 — this is defense-in-depth, not duplication. ddx-b808df39 is operator-initiated; this bead is system-initiated.

## Dependencies

- ddx-b808df39 surfaces PID in `ddx agent workers --json` output; this bead reuses that plumbing.
title: execute-bead: autonomous worker watchdog with process-level reaper

description:
## Root cause RC4 from ddx-0a651925

After RC1 is fixed (caller ctx propagates), provider HTTP calls still need per-request deadlines. A stalled TCP socket that delivers headers and then stops sending body bytes — particularly during streaming token reads — can hang a goroutine for days.

Grepping the `DocumentDrivenDX/agent@v0.3.14` module cache shows short timeouts only on discovery probes (`provider/openai/discovery.go:46,174`, `openai.go:123`). The main `Run` call path inside agent providers appears to inherit whatever ctx DDx passes — which today is `context.Background()` (see RC1).

## Scope

1. Audit `openai`, `anthropic`, `virtual` providers in the agent library for per-request deadline usage.
2. Install a per-request deadline (default ~10-15 min) on each provider call; separate from the wall-clock bound in RC2.
3. For streaming bodies, enforce an **idle-read limit** on the response body so a mid-stream stall cannot hold a goroutine indefinitely (e.g. `http.Transport.ResponseHeaderTimeout` + periodic `SetReadDeadline` on the underlying conn).
4. Surface provider-timeout failures as a distinct status in `ExecuteBeadResult.Detail`.

## Non-goals

- Rewriting providers; minimally invasive change only.
- Changing DDx-side timeout defaults (RC2 covers outer bound).

## Prerequisite

Sibling RC1 bead must be resolved first, otherwise adding deadlines inside providers is useless while DDx still feeds them `context.Background()`.
title: execute-bead: audit and enforce per-request HTTP deadlines on agent provider calls

description:
## Root cause RC1 from ddx-0a651925

`cli/internal/agent/runner.go:239` (Runner.Run) and `cli/internal/agent/agent_runner.go:163` (Runner.RunAgent) both call `context.WithCancel(context.Background())`, discarding any context from the caller. `RunOptions` exposes no ctx field. `agent.ExecuteBead` likewise takes no ctx, so `server.WorkerManager.runWorker`'s ctx never reaches the agent call.

As a result, `WorkerManager.Stop(id)` (server/workers.go:648) cancels only the worker goroutine; the embedded `agentlib.Run` call (and any subprocess it launched) keeps running until SIGKILL. This is the structural defect behind 33–142h hung workers.

## Scope

1. Add `Context context.Context` to `RunOptions` (or change signatures to `Run(ctx, opts)`). Default to `context.Background()` when nil.
2. Derive the internal ctx from the caller's rather than `context.Background()`.
3. Thread ctx through `agent.ExecuteBead` → `runner.Run` → `agentlib.Run` → provider HTTP.
4. Update `server.WorkerManager.runWorker`'s `singleTierAttempt` closure to pass `ctx` into `agent.ExecuteBead`.

## Non-goals

- New wall-clock timeout logic (covered by sibling RC2 bead)
- Operator-facing stop command (covered by ddx-b808df39)
title: execute-bead: propagate caller context through Runner.Run and RunAgent

acceptance:
- [ ] Compaction-stuck detection fires within 15 minutes when no-op compaction events are the only activity, regardless of event rate
- [ ] No regression on the existing behaviour for healthy agents (normal runs do not trip)
- [ ] Unit test: fake agentlib emits one no-op compaction event every 3 seconds → breaker fires within 15 min
- [ ] Result.json `detail` clearly reports the time-based breaker when it fires
description:
## Root cause RC3 from ddx-0a651925

`cli/internal/agent/agent_runner.go:218-241` trips at `stuckThreshold = maxConsecutiveCompactionFailures` (50 by default). Observed on bundle `20260416T230316-efbf91c5`: the breaker took **2h 8m** to fire (7,720,908 ms). If each iteration takes ~3 min to emit a no-op compaction event, 50 events = ~2.5h. The counter is useful but fires far too late to be a hang-guard.

## Scope

Either:
1. **Time-bounded** — fire after N no-op events **within M minutes** (e.g. 10 within 15m), OR
2. **Threshold lowered** — drop default from 50 to ~10 (only for agent harness where one iteration is already expensive), OR
3. **Wall-clock guard layered on top** — independent breaker fires after e.g. 20 min of consecutive no-op compaction events regardless of count.

Recommend option 1 or 3: time-based thresholds are more robust to provider-speed variance.

## Non-goals

- Changing the compaction algorithm itself.
- Extending breakers outside the compaction path.
title: execute-bead: bound compaction-stuck breaker by wall-clock time

- [ ] Wall-clock timeout fires even when stdout/stderr/agent events are flowing (unit test: fake provider emits 1 event/sec for > deadline, expect cancel at deadline ± 1s)

description:
## Root cause RC2 from ddx-0a651925

The `DefaultTimeoutMS = 7200000` (2h) in `cli/internal/agent/types.go:363` is advertised as a hard cap but implemented as an *idle timeout*:

- `cli/internal/agent/executor.go:154-178` resets `time.NewTimer(idleTimeout)` on every stdout/stderr byte.
- `cli/internal/agent/agent_runner.go:264-285` resets on every non-compaction agentlib event.

A provider that emits any heartbeat, retry line, or periodic event defeats the timer indefinitely — enabling the 33–142h hangs observed on agent projects.

Only the claude streaming path (`cli/internal/agent/claude_stream.go:373-384`) uses a true wall-clock deadline via `time.After(timeout)`. That path is why bundle `20260415T015231-c2ffa9ba` fired at exactly 2h 0m 0.098s — and nothing else does.

## Scope

1. Add an absolute wall-clock deadline in addition to (not replacing) the idle timeout.
2. Default the wall-clock bound to something operators can trust — e.g. 3x `DefaultTimeoutMS` or a new `DefaultWallClockMS`.
3. Apply in: `OSExecutor.ExecuteInDir` (subprocess path) and `Runner.RunAgent` (embedded agent path).
4. Reflect the wall-clock error in result.json as a distinct `error: "wall-clock deadline exceeded after Xh"` so it is not confused with idle timeout.

## Non-goals

- Lowering or removing the existing idle timeout.
- Per-provider tuning (can be follow-up).
title: execute-bead: add wall-clock deadline alongside idle timeout for agent harness

description:
PROBLEM
The current review/session prompt path does not assemble a turn-structured prompt envelope with pinned evidence, rolling session memory, and explicit refusal on minimum-floor overflow. `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go:204-333` only builds a single-shot review prompt around bead metadata, governing docs, and diff. `cli/internal/server/review_session.go:22-224` stores artifact identity, template refs, prompt refs, and append-only turns, but there is no renderer that turns that session state into a structured prompt with pinned + rolling sections.

ROOT CAUSE
`cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go:204-333` is the current bounded review assembler. It clamps governing docs and the diff, then emits one prompt blob and telemetry, but it does not model per-turn pinned/rolling sections or a dedicated refusal class for a minimum pinned floor that cannot fit. The review-session store in `cli/internal/server/review_session.go:22-224` persists the right inputs (`artifact_git_rev`, `template_ref`, `prompt_ref`, `turns.jsonl`) yet nothing consumes them in a structured prompt-rendering step.

PROPOSED FIX
- `cli/internal/server/review_session.go` or a new helper in the same package: add a prompt renderer that emits pinned sections for system rubric, artifact identity, Story 17 template+prompt, first-user-intent, and explicit user decisions, followed by rolling sections for session memory summary, last K verbatim turns, and unresolved findings.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go`: thread the structured renderer into the review path, keep FEAT-022 byte accounting on the assembled prompt, and short-circuit before provider dispatch when the minimum pinned floor does not fit. The refusal should surface `PROMPT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` with the observed bytes and cap in the error text.
- Add tests named `TestReviewSessionPromptAssemblyPinnedRolling`, `TestReviewSessionPromptAssemblyBudgetRefusal`, and `TestReviewPromptTelemetryIncludesSectionBytes` to pin the section order, refusal behavior, and byte accounting.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change the existing review verdict parser or the review error taxonomy.
- Do not add new server text-egress caps in this slice.
- Do not rework the existing diff clamping primitives; this bead only consumes them.
title: agent: implement structured review prompt assembly with budget refusal and telemetry

description:
## Reject routes that can't actually run tool-calling work (sibling of ddx-4817edfd).

Some omlx flavors and older local OpenAI-compat servers do not implement /v1/chat/completions with tools. Today routing fuzzy-matches them and dispatch fails with 'tools not supported' — or worse, silently returns a no-tool response that the execute-bead loop cannot consume.

## Scope

- Per-provider / per-flavor capability metadata: SupportsTools bool. Two layers:
  1. Hand-curated table for known harnesses (claude, codex, opus, etc.) and provider flavors (openai, anthropic, openrouter, omlx, lmstudio, ollama).
  2. Discovery-driven enrichment when /v1/models/status (or equivalent) advertises tool support per model.
- RouteRequest gains RequiresTools bool (default false to preserve current behavior; execute-bead sets true).
- evaluateCandidate rejects candidates where RequiresTools=true and the resolved (provider, flavor, model) combo is known NOT to support tools. Unknown = pass with -v warning, same pattern as context-window bead.
- Capability metadata location: cli/internal/agent/catalog.go on ModelEntry/Surface, plus a curated table in cli/internal/agent/capabilities.go (or co-located).

## Out of scope

- Context-window, structured-output, effort, permissions gating (sibling beads).
- Probing servers actively at routing time (uses cached discovery + table).

## Files

- cli/internal/agent/types.go (RouteRequest.RequiresTools, capability fields on CandidatePlan)
- cli/internal/agent/routing.go (rejection in rejectIfNotViable / evaluateCandidate)
- cli/internal/agent/catalog.go (SupportsTools on ModelEntry / Surface)
- cli/internal/agent/capabilities.go (NEW — curated table)

## Provider-specific honoring of --effort and --permissions (sibling of ddx-4817edfd).

Today, Harness.EffortFlag is checked at routing.go:rejectIfNotViable, so harnesses without effort support are rejected when --effort is set. But provider-level gating is missing: e.g., openrouter doesn't honor --effort on non-reasoning models, and --permissions unrestricted may not apply to every harness+provider combination. Routing should reject or downgrade rather than dispatch and silently no-op the flag.

## Scope

- Add effort/permissions capability fields to the curated capability table (same file added by the tool-calling sub-bead, or co-locate here if that one ships first).
  - SupportsEffort tri-state per (provider, model).
  - SupportsPermission(permission_class) — at minimum 'unrestricted'.
- evaluateCandidate / rejectIfNotViable: when RouteRequest names an --effort or --permissions value not honored by the resolved (provider, model) combo, reject with a clear reason. Unknown = pass with -v warning.
- Document expected behavior for each known provider in capabilities.go comments (openrouter non-reasoning models = no effort, etc.).

## Out of scope

- Context-window, tool-calling, structured-output gating (sibling beads).
- Building a 'downgrade' path (e.g., silently strip --effort and continue). Rejection is sufficient for v1; downgrade is a follow-up.

## Files

- cli/internal/agent/routing.go
- cli/internal/agent/capabilities.go (shared with tool-calling bead — or new file if order differs)
- cli/internal/agent/types.go

description:
## Smallest useful slice of capability gating (sibling of ddx-4817edfd).

Routing currently does not check whether the resolved model's context window can hold the bead prompt. A 32k-context fuzzy match against an 80k-token bead prompt routes 'successfully' and fails mid-dispatch with a provider 400 or truncated output.

## Scope

- Add optional EstimatedPromptTokens (uint32) to RouteRequest (cli/internal/agent/types.go).
- In evaluateCandidate (cli/internal/agent/routing.go), when EstimatedPromptTokens is set and > 0, reject (or penalize) candidates whose concrete_model context window is below it.
- Source of context window per candidate: v0.3.11's LookupModelLimits first, then catalog ModelEntry.ContextWindow (cli/internal/agent/catalog.go) as fallback. If neither is known, treat as 'unknown' — do NOT reject (avoid false negatives), but log at -v.
- Caller side: pass EstimatedPromptTokens from execute-bead when the bead prompt is assembled (best-effort — can use char/4 heuristic if a tokenizer is unavailable).

## Out of scope

- Tool-calling, structured-output, effort, permissions gating (separate sibling beads).
- Adding a tokenizer dependency. char/4 estimate is fine for v1.

## Files

- cli/internal/agent/types.go
- cli/internal/agent/routing.go
- cli/internal/agent/catalog.go
- cli/cmd/agent_execute_bead.go (or wherever the bead prompt is assembled)

description:
PROBLEM: cli/internal/server/workers.go:runWorker runs the bead-execution loop in-process, knitting together LandCoordinator, DefaultBeadReviewer, CostCapTracker, RoutePreflight, ExecuteBeadWorker, ProgressCh→drainProgress, WakeCh, BeadWorkerFactory injection, and watchdog phase-stall tracking — all of which contradict ADR-022's autonomous-default model where workers are subprocesses identical to operator-launched 'ddx work'.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE: cli/internal/server/workers.go:658-940 (runWorker) builds an in-process executor closure (singleTierAttempt at lines 679-747), wraps it with a CostCap tracker (lines 753-797), wires a DefaultBeadReviewer (lines 801-809), and calls worker.Run(ctx, rcfg, ExecuteBeadLoopRuntime{...}). All of this duplicates work that 'ddx work' (cli/cmd/work.go → cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go:runAgentExecuteLoopImpl) already does, just inside the parent server process.

PROPOSED FIX: Replace the in-process worker.Run(...) call with exec.CommandContext(ctx, dddxBin, 'work', <flags>) where dddxBin = os.Executable() (override-able via DDX_EXECUTABLE env for tests). Project root passed via --project flag or DDX_PROJECT_ROOT env. Provider/harness/model/profile/effort/poll-interval/once/no-review/review-harness/review-model/label-filter/model-ref translated to existing ddx work flags. Capture child PID into WorkerRecord.PID (already a field at workers.go:147). Stop() and the watchdog already signal via PID (workers.go:1070, 1279) — verify the cross-process path works; SIGTERM with kill grace then SIGKILL.

Progress event ingestion changes: child process emits via workerprobe to /api/workers/<id>/event (this endpoint exists, server.go:884). The parent's WorkerManager subscribes to those events (in-memory derived view from the workers ingestion handler) and forwards into the per-subprocess workerHandle.progressCh so existing SSE subscribers and drainProgress logic continue to work. Mapping: parent records the WorkerRecord.id at exec time; child registers with /api/workers/register and gets a probe-issued worker_id; parent correlates by ProjectRoot + ExecutorPID + StartedAt window.

Drop in-process LandCoordinator/Reviewer/CostCap/RoutePreflight wiring inside runWorker (they now run inside the child). LandCoordinators registry stays for the existing inline 'ddx work' path (cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go:1714).

WakeCh: replace with SIGUSR1 to the child (or document as no-op for the v1 of this refactor; WakeProject still walks workers but only sends to live in-process handles — kept null-safe for subprocess workers).

BeadWorkerFactory: removed. Tests that previously injected a fake executor migrate to either (a) reentry-stub mode where the test binary acts as 'ddx work' via go test re-exec pattern, or (b) deletion as no-longer-applicable (semantics now live in cli/cmd/* tests).

NON-SCOPE: handleStartExecuteLoopWorker rewrite (covered by 7b). Deletion of ExecuteLoopWorkerSpec struct (covered by 7b). End-to-end real-claude integration (covered by 7c). UI/GraphQL surface changes (already covered by ADR-022 step 5).

description:
PROBLEM
Startup reconcile may blindly process stale desired-state or ServerState project entries such as /Users/erik/Projects/pqueue and /Users/erik/Projects/tablespec. On manual reconcile these stale entries spawned throwaway exited workers, creating noisy process churn and making restart recovery hard to trust.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/server/server.go:384-416 discovers desired worker project roots from server WorkingDir and persisted ServerState projects, but stale ServerState/desired-state entries can be reconciled without proving the project is present, valid, or capable of producing liveness.
- cli/internal/server/server_startup_reconcile_test.go:96-204 does not seed stale desired-state/project entries or assert that startup reconcile skips or prunes them with observable audit/error output.

PROPOSED FIX
Make startup reconcile stale-safe: desired entries for projects that are missing, no longer registered as valid, or repeatedly exit before producing liveness should be skipped or pruned with an audit/error event carrying the project path. Avoid spawning repeat exited workers for stale projects while preserving valid desired worker state.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement GraphQL worker count/cap changes from ddx-c713d75e. Do not change bead claim semantics or Fizeau routing. Do not remove valid desired worker state for active projects such as /Users/erik/Projects/ddx and /Users/erik/Projects/sesame. Governing artifact reference: plan:server-operator-workbench.
title: server: skip stale desired projects during startup reconcile

description:
PROBLEM
Large beads must be decomposed without operator intervention before implementation, or immediately after a failed implementation attempt proves the pre-claim gate missed a too-large bead. The recent bounced workflow beads showed the gap: the implementer correctly reported that the bead was too large, but decomposition was prohibited inside the attempted worktree/depth context, so an operator had to split it manually.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1386 embeds decomposition instructions in the implementer prompt, which happens after dispatch rather than before claim.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1661 emits an implementation-attempt decomposition depth cap message; that prompt cap can prevent the worker from creating children even when the queue-level orchestrator could still split safely.
- docs/triage/decomposition.md requires ac_map and parent blocking semantics, but work does not yet file children from a pre-claim intake decision or from post-attempt no_changes_needs_investigation caused by oversized work.
- cli/internal/agent/try/no_changes.go:29 defines no_changes_needs_investigation, but the work loop does not yet convert a too-large rationale into orchestrator-level decomposition.

PROPOSED FIX
- Handle pre-claim too_large_decomposed by creating child beads with standalone descriptions/AC and dependency wiring.
- Handle post-attempt no_changes_needs_investigation whose rationale says the bead is too large, too broad, depth-capped inside the attempt, or requires decomposition by invoking the same orchestrator splitter on the original bead.
- Treat implementation-attempt depth as advisory only; queue-level max_decomposition_depth is the limit that decides whether DDx can split or must ask the operator.
- Parent receives triage-decomposed event body with child_ids, rationale, and ac_map.
- Every parent AC must map to at least one child AC or explicit needs_human/non_scope; lossy decomposition blocks for operator instead of creating children.
- Parent is blocked/dependency-blocked on children and not claimed again for implementation.

NON-SCOPE
- Safe rewrite handling.
- Review-time decomposition beyond using the same splitter when review_too_large is already classified.
title: intake: auto-decompose too-large beads before or after failed attempts

description:
When ddx agent execute-bead lands a commit locally but merging into the base branch produces conflicts, the loop today preserves the result at refs/ddx/iterations/<bead>/<ts>-<base> and unclaims the bead with status: land_conflict. The bead reopens; subsequent attempts re-execute from scratch — burning more agent time and dollars even though the original work is intact in the preserved ref.

OBSERVED 2026-04-29 on ddx-52469547 (FEAT-015 bead 3, 'runtime fallback removal + audit-side migration'):
- Sonnet ran for ~3h, produced commit 12fbf6dd1b98 covering all 7 AC items.
- The base branch advanced significantly during the run (V1, V2, V3 vision beads + dogfood + concurrent work).
- The run hit the agent's 3h hard timeout right at the test phase.
- work preserved at refs/ddx/iterations/ddx-52469547/20260429T175646Z-aa7b31785a44 with status execution_failed (timeout, but functionally identical to land_conflict for the merge story).
- Operator attempted git merge --no-ff 12fbf6dd, hit 7 file-level conflicts (mechanical drift from parallel beads), aborted, and only avoided wasting the work because a parallel attempt (263b5eff) had landed the exact same scope cleanly. That parallel landing is a coincidence, not a guarantee.

The general case: a preserved iteration represents real money spent and real work done. land_conflict / execution_failed-with-result that bails to 'reopen and re-run' throws that work away. The loop should at least attempt to reuse the preserved result.

REQUESTED BEHAVIOR

1. On land_conflict (merge produces conflicts when applying the iteration onto current tip), work should:

description:
PROBLEM
Pinned `ddx work` workers are still producing repeated lifecycle-hook routing warnings before every attempt:

- `readiness route unavailable: runner error: ResolveRoute: no viable routing candidate: 3 candidates rejected`
- `lint hook: dispatch-failure: ResolveRoute: policy "air-gapped" has no candidate satisfying local endpoint`

This is happening even when the worker is explicitly started with a viable implementation route, for example:

`ddx work --watch --idle-interval 30s --harness codex --model gpt-5.4-mini --review-harness codex --review-model gpt-5.5`

The main implementation attempt then routes correctly to `codex/gpt-5.4-mini`, but pre-claim intake and pre-dispatch lint ignore the operator's pins and spend 60-120 seconds failing through unrelated unpinned/profile routing. This slows every worker cycle and makes healthy pinned execution look system-unready.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
`cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:134-143` constructs `AgentRunRuntime` with `ProfileOverride: selectProfileForDispatch(... SelectStrongestProfile)` and sets `ClearRoutingPins: true`, `ClearProfile: true`, `ClearMinPower: true`, and `ClearMaxPower: true`. That strips explicit worker harness/model pins before dispatching the intake prompt.

`cli/internal/agent/lint_hook.go:128-137` does the same for pre-dispatch lint, selecting the cheapest profile and setting `ClearRoutingPins: true`, `ClearProfile: true`, `ClearMinPower: true`, and `ClearMaxPower: true`.

In projects where autorouting/local endpoint validation is not yet complete, those unpinned hook dispatches fail even though the pinned implementation route is usable.

PROPOSED FIX
- Update lifecycle hook dispatch so explicit operator route pins from `ResolvedConfig` are preserved for pre-claim intake and pre-dispatch lint when `ddx work`/`ddx try` was started with `--harness`, `--provider`, `--model`, or `--model-ref`.
- Keep the existing profile-selection behavior only for genuinely unpinned workers.
- Preserve the strong/cheap intent for unpinned hook dispatch without overriding explicit operator constraints.
- Ensure lifecycle hook failures caused by unavailable optional hook routes are not recorded as system-unready when the implementation route itself is explicitly pinned and executable.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not implement DDx-side model/provider/harness ranking, fuzzy matching, fallback, or catalog lookup.
- Do not change Fizeau routing policy.
- Do not remove lifecycle hooks.
- Do not change post-attempt review model routing.
- Do not change local provider validation policy beyond preserving explicit operator pins for these hook dispatches.

INTERSECTIONS
- This is a DDx-side workaround needed while Fizeau autorouter/local-provider validation work is in flight.
- Related to the Fizeau routing-boundary cleanup: DDx should pass explicit operator constraints through, not substitute a DDx-side route.
title: work: preserve explicit route pins for lifecycle hook dispatch

The provider-launch boundary therefore has no local assertion that its child process gets Linux parent-death protection.

ROOT CAUSE
`runAgentViaService` (`cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:80-157`) is the live path used by `ddx work`; it constructs the service via `NewServiceFromWorkDir` (`cli/internal/agent/serviceconfig.go:85-121`) and never inspects the provider subprocess `SysProcAttr`. That means the watch path can bypass the only place where `Pdeathsig`/`Setpgid` are known to be set.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add the smallest local seam at the service boundary or provider-launch wrapper so the provider child process gets `cmdSetProcessGroup` semantics on Linux.
- Keep the existing `OSExecutor` path unchanged.
- Add `TestExecutor_ProviderSpawnSetsPdeathsigAndSetpgid`.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change stale-process cleanup or `ddx cleanup`.
- Do not redesign routing, Fizeau policy selection, or model inventory.

description:
## Problem (filed per opus fresh-eyes review 2026-04-17)

After ddx-0486e601 lands normalization, fuzzy matcher still has an inherited tiebreak quirk:

    Input: 'qwen3'
    Canonicalized pool: ['qwen3.5-27b-4bit', 'qwen3.6-35b-a3b-4bit']
    Current tiebreak: shortest-suffix wins -> picks qwen3.5 (shorter suffix '.5-27b-4bit' < '.6-35b-a3b-4bit')

A user asking for 'qwen3' almost certainly wants the LATEST, not whichever happens to have a shorter concrete suffix. Shortest-suffix is a reasonable default for avoiding ambiguity, but for semver-like suffixes it produces counterintuitive results.

Opus: 'Not a blocker — inherited behavior — but add a test asserting the current (possibly-wrong) resolution and flag it for a follow-up. Making this a conscious policy choice for a future change.'

## Fix

Add a semver-aware tiebreak when multiple candidates share a prefix and the first character after the prefix is a digit (indicating a version suffix). Otherwise fall back to shortest-suffix.

Heuristic:

1. Group candidates by the normalized prefix+first-version-segment (e.g. 'qwen3.5' vs 'qwen3.6').
2. Within each group, pick by shortest-suffix (current rule).
3. Across groups, pick the HIGHEST version by semver-like comparison.

Refuse to over-engineer: no full semver parsing, just 'compare version segments as numbers where possible, fall back to lexicographic'.

Corner cases to test:
- 'qwen3' -> qwen3.6-35b-a3b-4bit (prefer qwen3.6 over qwen3.5)
- 'qwen3.5' -> qwen3.5-27b-4bit (exact prefix match, only one candidate)
- 'gpt-4' -> gpt-4o (if present) vs gpt-4-turbo — semver-free, fall back to shortest-suffix (current behavior)
- 'minimax-m' -> prefer minimax-m2.7 over minimax-m2.5

## Files touched

- cli/internal/agent/discovery.go — new tiebreak in fuzzyMatchInPool
- cli/internal/agent/discovery_test.go — semver + non-semver tiebreak cases

## Depends on

- ddx-0486e601 (normalization + per-provider) — this is the file where tiebreak lives
notes: Superseded by agent-1a486c2e — single routing engine in agent/internal/routing

acceptance: New file cli/internal/agent/script.go implements RunScript(opts) that reads a directive file, executes directives against opts.WorkDir using real filesystem and git operations, and returns a real Result. The harness is registered in cli/internal/agent/registry.go as `script` and marked always-available in Discover(). Directive grammar supports at minimum: append-line, create-file, delete-file, commit, set-exit, no-op, sleep-ms, fail-during. Environment variable interpolation supports ${DDX_BEAD_ID}, ${DDX_ATTEMPT_ID}, ${DDX_WORKER_ID}. Unit tests in cli/internal/agent/script_test.go cover: (1) append-line + commit produces a real commit with the expected content, (2) no-op produces zero commits and exit 0, (3) create-file + commit produces the file and a commit, (4) set-exit 1 makes the run return exit 1, (5) fail-during 2 executes directives 0 and 1 but errors on directive 2, (6) env var interpolation replaces ${DDX_BEAD_ID} with the value from Correlation, (7) invoking via `ddx agent run --harness=script --model=<file>` works end-to-end with a real temp git repo. go test ./internal/agent -run TestScript completes in under 5 seconds.
description:
The work / execute-bead / land-coordinator system cannot be tested end-to-end today because every "fake" agent in the codebase returns a canned Result{} without actually writing files or making commits. `cli/internal/agent/virtual.go` is a prompt-response dictionary replayer — it returns canned stdout based on prompt hash but does not touch the filesystem or git. `fakeAgentRunner` and `fakeExecuteBeadGit` in `cli/cmd/agent_execute_bead_test.go` are in-memory mocks that track expected call counts. Neither produces actual commits that the orchestration layer can rebase, merge, or land.

The consequence: every test that claims to cover concurrency, serialization, or git orchestration uses mocked git and therefore cannot catch merge-race, rebase-conflict, or coordinator-serialization bugs. `TestConcurrentWorkersNoMergeRace` at execute_bead_orchestrator_test.go:228 is particularly misleading — it uses separate orchTestGitOps instances per worker so the shared-writer invariant is never exercised. The test passes because no shared state exists to race on.

## What this bead builds

A new deterministic `script` harness (cli/internal/agent/script.go, mirroring cli/internal/agent/virtual.go):

- Registered alongside claude/codex/agent/virtual in cli/internal/agent/registry.go
- Always available (no binary probe required)
- Takes a directive file (passed via RunOptions.Model or a new RunOptions.ScriptFile field — either works)
- Reads the directive file, executes each line against opts.WorkDir as real filesystem + git operations
- Returns a real Result{ExitCode, Output} that the loop and orchestrator can observe

## Directive grammar

Line-based, comments start with `#`. Each directive performs a real side effect:

```
append-line <path> <text>          # append text to file (create if missing)
create-file <path> <content>       # create or overwrite file
delete-file <path>                 # rm -f path
modify-line <path> <regex> <repl>  # sed-style in-place substitution
run <shell-command>                # exec in WorkDir with clean env
commit <message>                   # git add -A && git commit -m <message>
set-exit <code>                    # final exit code (default 0)
no-op                              # no commits, no files, exit 0
fail-during <index>                # synthetic failure at the Nth directive
sleep-ms <n>                       # deterministic delay (for scheduling tests)
```

Directives run in order. Environment variables DDX_BEAD_ID, DDX_ATTEMPT_ID, DDX_WORKER_ID are interpolated into text arguments so directives can be parameterized. Example:

```
append-line tests/smoke.txt "hello from ${DDX_BEAD_ID}"
commit "smoke: ${DDX_BEAD_ID}"
```

## Invocation

From the CLI: `ddx agent run --harness=script --model=./testdata/append-smoke.txt --prompt=/dev/null`

Programmatically from a test:
```go
runner := agent.NewRunner(agent.Config{Harness: "script"})
result, err := runner.Run(agent.RunOptions{
    WorkDir: wtPath,
    Model:   "testdata/append-smoke.txt",
    Correlation: map[string]string{"bead_id": beadID, "attempt_id": attemptID},
})
```

## Implementation notes

- Mirror the dispatch pattern in cli/internal/agent/runner.go:81 where `virtual` is intercepted
- Always-available in Discover() same as virtual + agent
- No external dependencies beyond what the agent package already uses (os, os/exec for git)
- Estimated size: ~200 lines of implementation + ~200 lines of tests
- Unit tests in cli/internal/agent/script_test.go must prove each directive actually performs its claimed side effect on a real temp git repo

## What this enables

Every test case in beads B (integration tests) and C (server runWorker regression test) depends on this harness existing. Without it, the land-coordinator redesign ships behind whatever real claude happens to do on the day the test runs.
title: Implement deterministic script harness for orchestration stress testing

description:
PROBLEM
DDx has no runtime concept of a "global" plugin install nor a precedence order for resolving a plugin name. Every install/lookup path is hardcoded to the per-project tree via ddxroot.Path(). Before `--global` install (sibling bead) or `ddx init --global` (sibling bead) can exist, there must be a single resolver that, given a plugin name, returns its on-disk path by checking the project layer first, then a global layer, then the baked-in default.

ROOT CAUSE
- cli/internal/registry/installer.go:66 `InstallPackageFromFS(pkg, src, projectRoot)` only knows the project root; there is no global target.
- cli/internal/ddxroot/ddxroot.go:75 `Path()` resolves only the project root (in-tree `<project>/.ddx` or convention `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/projects/...` at line 86). There is no `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global` helper.
- cli/internal/skills/install.go:28 `Install(src, projectRoot, opts)` and all callers assume a single project destination.
- No `ResolvePlugin`-style function exists anywhere under cli/internal/registry.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Add `GlobalDir()` to cli/internal/ddxroot/ddxroot.go returning `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global` (reuse the existing `xdgDataHome()` helper at ddxroot.go:89). The plugins root is `GlobalDir()/plugins`.
2. Add `registry.ResolvePlugin(ctx, projectRoot, name string) (path string, layer string, error)` implementing precedence:
   - `ddxroot.Path(ctx, projectRoot)/plugins/<name>` if the dir exists → layer "project".
   - `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/plugins/<name>` if it exists → layer "global".
   - baked-in default (defaultplugin.FS, the `ddx` plugin only) → layer "baked-in"; return an error for any other unresolved name.
3. Export the layer string so doctor/init/install (sibling beads) can report which layer answered.

NON-SCOPE
- Wiring `--global` into install/update commands (sibling bead: install/update --global).
- `ddx init --global` and agent-tier symlinks (sibling bead: init topology).
- `ddx doctor` reporting (sibling bead: doctor + specs).
- Removing the existing per-project install. Both layers coexist.

DEPS
ddx-06cbaa90 (ddx home resolution) — `ddxroot.Path()` and the new `GlobalDir()` must share the same XDG_DATA_HOME convention agreed there. Sibling beads in this set depend on this resolver.
title: registry: add two-layer plugin resolution (project → global → baked-in) with global XDG path helper

1. fuzzyMatchInPool returns the correct match for case + vendor-prefix variants: fuzzy('qwen/qwen3.6', ['Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit', 'Qwen3.5-27B-4bit']) -> ('Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit', true).

3. Exact match still takes precedence: fuzzy('Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit', ['Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit', 'Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit-v2']) -> ('Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit', false).

4. Shortest-suffix tiebreak is unchanged for already-matching cases.

5. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/ -run Fuzzy passes, plus at least 5 new table-driven cases covering the normalization paths.
description:
## Problem

The fuzzy matcher at cli/internal/agent/discovery.go:62-108 has two defects that compound:

### Defect 1: strict case-sensitive prefix with no canonical-prefix stripping

fuzzyMatchInPool (discovery.go:76) does literal case-sensitive prefix check:

    for _, m := range pool {
        if len(m) > len(input) && m[:len(input)] == input {
            candidates = append(candidates, candidate{...})
        }
    }

Cannot bridge 'qwen/qwen3.6' (canonical ref) -> 'Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit' (vidar-omlx native). Case mismatch + slash-prefix mismatch at first byte.

### Defect 2: matcher collapses provider identity

FuzzyMatchModel (discovery.go:62-71) pools d.AllModels() — a deduplicated union across EVERY discovered provider. Callers then do a second lookup via ProvidersForModel(match) to pick a provider, but that lookup is not gated on --provider preference. A model name appearing on any provider can leak routing to that provider even under a --provider pin.

These two defects must be fixed together. Per Opus fresh-eyes review: per-provider-pool without normalization matches even less than the current union pool. Splitting them creates a merge-conflict hazard (same file, same test surface, one coherent change).

## Fix

Update the discovery.go fuzzy-match layer as one coherent change:

### 1. Normalize input and pool entries

Add canonicalization helper:

    func canonicalizeModelKey(s string) string {
        // Strip exactly ONE leading 'vendor/' segment if present (preserve
        // path structure for future multi-segment refs — do NOT strip all
        // slashes blindly).
        if slash := strings.Index(s, '/'); slash > 0 {
            s = s[slash+1:]
        }
        return strings.ToLower(s)
    }

Per codex fresh-eyes review: ONLY the leading vendor namespace is stripped. 'openai/gpt-4' -> 'gpt-4'. 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6' -> 'claude-sonnet-4-6'. 'qwen/qwen3.6' -> 'qwen3.6'. A hypothetical 'a/b/c' becomes 'b/c' (not 'c').

### 2. Case-insensitive prefix on canonicalized forms

Apply prefix matching on canonicalized(input) vs canonicalized(pool entry). Shortest-suffix tiebreak remains. Return the ORIGINAL pool entry (preserve casing) when a match is found.

Negative case: 'minimax/minimax-m2.7' vs 'MiniMax-M2.5-MLX-4bit' normalizes to 'minimax-m2.7' vs 'minimax-m2.5-mlx-4bit'. Prefix check: 'minimax-m2.5-mlx-4bit' does NOT start with 'minimax-m2.7' (divergence at '.5' vs '.7'). Returns no match. CORRECT — m2.7 is not m2.5.

### 3. Per-provider variant

Add DiscoveryResult.FuzzyMatchModelOnProvider(input, providerName) that pools ONLY the named provider's models. Exact-match + fuzzy-match semantics identical to the global version, running against the narrower pool.

    func (d *DiscoveryResult) FuzzyMatchModelOnProvider(input, providerName string) (model, provider string, fuzzy bool)

Returns (resolvedModelID, providerName, isFuzzy) tuple. Provider identity is preserved so downstream scoring doesn't need a second lookup.

### 4. Callers

Keep the existing AllModels() path (useful for unpinned routing). Callers with a provider pin should use the per-provider variant first and fall back to global discovery only if the pinned provider has no match (SD-015 'soft preference' semantics: try pinned first, then broader).

### 5. Exact-match precedence

Preserve exact-match precedence (both case-sensitive and case-insensitive). Exact > fuzzy.

### 6. Known tiebreak quirk (track, don't fix here)

Per Opus review: 'qwen3' matches both 'qwen3.5-27b-4bit' and 'qwen3.6-35b-a3b-4bit'; shortest-suffix picks qwen3.5. A user asking for 'qwen3' probably wants the latest. This is inherited behavior from the existing tiebreak rule and is out of scope for THIS bead — add a follow-up bead and a test documenting the current (possibly-wrong) resolution so a future change is a conscious policy choice.

## Files likely touched

- cli/internal/agent/discovery.go — canonicalizeModelKey, updated fuzzyMatchInPool, new FuzzyMatchModelOnProvider
- cli/internal/agent/discovery_test.go — new cases: vendor-prefix stripping, case folding, exact-match precedence, ambiguity tiebreak, negative (version divergence), per-provider pool match, pinned-provider fallback behavior
- New follow-up bead tracking 'prefer latest version on ambiguous tiebreak' (file in the same commit so the link is durable)

## Depends on

None; self-contained discovery-layer change. Unblocks ddx-2f5a2284 (catalog/profile discovery integration) and ddx-3c5ba7cc (tier-affinity) once ddx-8610020e (Provider field) is also in place.

The `ddx-08b452ee` stale-source binary preflight now blocks `ddx work`/`ddx try` when the installed DDx binary commit is behind the DDx source checkout. Those commits do not affect the compiled CLI, but they make source HEAD advance past the installed binary commit. The next `ddx work --watch --project /Users/erik/Projects/ddx` restart can then fail before scanning the queue, forcing meaningless rebuilds after every tracker-only bookkeeping commit.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
`cli/cmd/command_factory.go:671-715` treats any descendant commit between the binary commit and source HEAD as binary staleness. It counts all commits with `git rev-list --count <binary>..<head>` and does not check whether the diff contains CLI/build-affecting paths. `.ddx/beads.jsonl`, `.ddx/executions/**`, `.ddx/metrics/**`, and `.ddx/attachments/**` commits therefore trigger the same fail-fast path as real Go source changes.

PROPOSED FIX
Only report source-checkout binary staleness when commits ahead of the installed binary include DDx build-affecting inputs. Tracker, execution evidence, metrics, attachments, docs, and other non-binary bookkeeping commits must not block `ddx work`, `ddx try`, or `ddx version`. Keep the existing fail-fast behavior for Go/module/build/install changes that can change the installed CLI.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken the fail-fast behavior for real CLI source changes. Do not require operators to tag/install after tracker-only commits. Do not hand-edit `.ddx/beads.jsonl`; use `ddx bead` commands for tracker state.

description:
PROBLEM
Beads marked superseded-by:<Y> never close automatically when Y closes. ddx-847df529 (parent ddx-09d7d787) carries superseded-by:ddx-c2a66f45-wt-6bee7238 and a note "Do not dispatch this bead independently"; the superseder closed weeks ago but the leftover stays open and blocks its parent epic. This is a primary contributor to the stuck-queue state on the current project (RC-2 in the FEAT-010 reason taxonomy).

ROOT CAUSE
cli/internal/bead/store.go Close(Y) closes only Y. It does not look for open beads X with superseded-by==Y and cascade-close them. FEAT-010 §Idle-Path Diagnosis and Auto-Remediation now requires this cascade with a strict scope guard.

PROPOSED FIX
Extend cli/internal/bead/store.go Close(Y) with a post-close cascade step. After Y closes, scan for open beads X where supersession-by-Y is the sole remaining reason to stay open. Strict scope contract (each must hold; if any fails, surface in ddx work focus Section A, do NOT cascade):
- X is open AND (X.superseded-by == Y OR X carries label superseded-by:Y) AND Y is now closed.
- X has no other open dependents (no open bead Z with Z.dependencies referencing X).
- X has no open dependencies of its own beyond the supersession marker.
- X has attempt_count == 0.
- X has no operator notes added after the supersession marker timestamp.
- X is not currently claimed or in-progress (no live claim_id).
- X carries no manual-hold / no-auto-close / container override label.

Re-read X's current tracker state inside the same Close(Y) invocation before mutating — a concurrent worker may have changed X since the scan started.

Idempotent: re-running Close(Y) is a no-op for already-closed X.
Cycle-guarded: track visited IDs within one Close(Y) call; cascade is one hop deep. If X is a superseder for an open Z, Z's cascade is DEFERRED to a separate operator action (do not transitively cascade).
Audit: emit a superseded_close event on X with body {closed_by_cascade_of: Y, reason: "closed_as_superseded_via:Y"}. Operators can grep events to reverse.

Add operator override flag at the work command surface in a separate bead (--no-auto-supersede-close); the Close() code path always runs the cascade unless the flag has been threaded through. For this bead, accept the cascade always firing; the flag wiring is the work-loop bead's responsibility.

NON-SCOPE
- Cascading transitively beyond one hop (deferred to a future bead if ever needed).
- The work-loop wiring of --no-auto-supersede-close flag (separate bead).
- RC-3 dead-intermediate cleanup walk-up (separate bead, depends on this one).

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent: ddx-2a1ece2b. No deps.
title: store: cascade-close superseded children inside Close()

description:
PROBLEM
Two code paths write to .ddx/attachments/<bead-id>/events.jsonl as part of normal operation, and neither auto-commits the result. Operators end up with persistent untracked-and-modified worktree state that contradicts the project's intent (1083 attachment files ARE tracked across 11.6 MB of committed history — this is first-class audit-trail data, not detritus).

Concrete demonstration today:

1. Run `ddx try <id>` on 9 beads → 9 new untracked .ddx/attachments/<bead-id>/ dirs appear in main repo. Each contains routing decisions, cost-per-attempt, execution-routing-intent, prose-check.findings, execute-bead outcome — exactly the audit data the convention says we keep.
2. Run `ddx bead migrate` → 142 events externalized into existing tracked attachment files (showing as M), 1 new untracked attachment dir, 292 beads archived (modifying .ddx/beads.jsonl and .ddx/beads-archive.jsonl), and a fresh worktree of 151 dirty files. None committed.
3. The audit log clearly shows the historical pattern: commits like `878931ce3 chore(beads): commit missing event attachments` and `5d54258fd Merge bead ... attempt ... into main` periodically sweep up the accumulation — but it's recurring manual cleanup, not the steady-state design.

ROOT CAUSE
Two distinct writers, neither stages or commits its output:

A. The execute-loop emits per-attempt routing/cost/intent events. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go emitRouteFailureEvent (line 3872) and the routing/cost emitters all call store.AppendEvent → the bead store writes to .ddx/attachments/<bead-id>/events.jsonl when the bead's events are externalized (or to the inline events array when not). The Store.AppendEvent path has no follow-up `git add`. The execute-loop's chore("add execution evidence") commit (visible in git log as `chore: add execution evidence [<run-id>]`) stages `.ddx/executions/<run-id>/` per AGENTS.md convention — but NOT `.ddx/attachments/<bead-id>/`.

B. cli/internal/bead/migrate.go ArchiveWithEvents (line 561) externalizes inline events from closed/archived beads to attachments. After externalizing 142 events today across many files, the migrate command exits without staging or committing the resulting changes. The operator command surface (cli/cmd/bead.go migrate handler) has no auto-commit step analogous to the bead store's other auto-commit paths.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Execute-loop landing path: extend the existing post-merge "chore(beads): commit missing event attachments"-style commit (or the bead's own evidence commit) to ALSO stage .ddx/attachments/<bead-id>/ for the bead just landed. Use the same git-index-lock recovery (cli/internal/gitlock per ddx-6a518fd9) so concurrent workers and the statusline poller do not race.
2. `ddx bead migrate` auto-commit: after a successful migrate that wrote any attachment changes (newly externalized + newly archived rows), call a single auto-commit at end-of-run with message `chore(beads): externalize and archive (<N> events to <M> attachments, <K> beads archived)`. Skip the commit entirely when no changes were written (idempotent re-run is a no-op).
3. Regression invariant: after `ddx try <id>` completes with `success`/`already_satisfied`, `git status --short` in the main repo MUST show zero untracked files under `.ddx/attachments/<bead-id>/` for that bead.
4. Operator escape hatch: `ddx bead reconcile-attachments` — single command that stages every untracked .ddx/attachments/ dir and any modified attachment files, commits as `chore(beads): reconcile missing attachment commits (<N> dirs, <M> modified)`. Useful for one-shot cleanup of pre-existing accumulation when this fix lands (today's 10 untracked + 141 modified dirs are an immediate use case).

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change WHAT gets externalized (the migrate event-externalization logic is fine).
- Do not change ATTACHMENT FORMAT or location.
- Do not add attachments to .gitignore (they ARE valuable cross-machine audit data per characterization).
- Do not auto-commit .ddx/executions/<run-id>/ — that's per-machine and stays untracked under existing convention.

DEPS
ddx-6a518fd9 (landed) — required so the auto-commits route through index-lock recovery and don't bounce on operator/statusline git contention.
title: bead: auto-commit attachment writes from execute-loop and migrate

acceptance: dxx-agent has dedicated ls, find, and grep tools; stall detector classifies them as read-only; bash is only classified as write-capable; agents on OpenRouter models transition from reading to writing faster
description:
During work runs with OpenRouter models (GLM-5.1, Qwen 3.6), agents get stuck in read loops — they call read and bash (for ls/find/grep) repeatedly without ever writing. The stall detector cannot distinguish bash ls from bash "git commit" because bash is classified as a write-capable tool, resetting the stall counter on every call.

Adding dedicated read-only tools (ls, find, grep) to ddx-agent would:
1. Let the stall detector accurately distinguish read-only exploration from write activity
2. Reduce token usage by avoiding bash prompt/response overhead for simple file queries
3. Give models clearer affordances — read-only tools for exploration, write/edit/bash for modification
4. Help models transition from reading to writing faster by making the tool boundary explicit

With these tools, the stall detector classifies read/ls/find/grep as read-only (increment stall counter) and write/edit/bash as write-capable (reset counter). Bash is only used when the agent needs commands that might modify the filesystem.
notes: Stall detection exists. Gap: no dedicated ls/find/grep tools registered in agent_runner.go tools slice (only Read/Write/Edit/Bash). Add as distinct agentlib.Tool implementations.
title: Add dedicated read-only tools (ls, find, grep) to ddx-agent for stall detection and efficiency

description:
PROBLEM
  Performance analysis across model / prompt / harness / spec
  dimensions today requires fan-out reads of every bead's
  events.jsonl. There is no global per-attempt table with
  denormalized fields ready for query. After sister ADR formalizes
  the storage architecture, this bead implements the cold-tier
  metrics extraction.

  Without this, optimization is blind: we cannot answer "which
  model has the best cost-per-success for our drain" or "which
  prompt template fails most on which spec class."

CURRENT STATE
  - .ddx/attachments/<bead-id>/events.jsonl contains lifecycle
    events: routing, cost, review-pass, review-block,
    closed-merged, etc. These rows have the raw signals
    (model, harness, cost_usd, tokens, verdict) needed for
    aggregate analysis.
  - There is no global attempts.jsonl file aggregating across
    beads.
  - Sister beads B29 (retention) cannot safely prune local
    evidence until metrics have been captured.

PROPOSED FIX
  1. Define schema for .ddx/metrics/attempts.jsonl (one row per
     bead-attempt; JSONL, append-only):
        - schema_version: 1 (integer; for future migration)
        - attempt_id: string (current "run-id" until rename
          bead lands, then attempt-id)
        - bead_id: string
        - session_id: string (agent harness session)
        - ts_start, ts_end: RFC3339 timestamps
        - model: string
        - harness: string
        - profile: string (optional)
        - provider: string
        - prompt_template_id: string (optional)
        - prompt_template_hash: string (hash of the rendered
          prompt; enables grouping by prompt variant)
        - spec_id: string (FEAT-N, SD-N, TD-N, ADR-N if known)
        - outcome: string (success | execution_failed |
          review_block | review_fixable_gap | etc.; see TD-031 §5)
        - exit_code: integer
        - cost_usd: float
        - duration_ms: integer
        - input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens: integer
        - review_verdict: string (APPROVE | BLOCK | etc.;
          optional)
        - review_finding_count_by_severity: map of
          severity -> count (optional)
        - ladder_min_power_initial, ladder_min_power_final:
          integer (per ADR-024 ladder semantics)
        - ladder_steps_taken: integer

  2. Forward-going hook:
     - On attempt finalization in
       cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go (or sibling),
       extract the fields from result.json + manifest.json + the
       attempt's events and append a row to
       .ddx/metrics/attempts.jsonl.
     - Use O_APPEND for atomic single-writer appends.
     - On multi-drain machines (future federation): partition
       to .ddx/metrics/<machine-id>/attempts.jsonl (sister bead
       deferred until federation arrives).

  3. One-shot backfill:
     - cli/cmd/work_metrics_backfill.go (new file) implements
       ddx work metrics backfill.
     - For each closed bead, read its events.jsonl (in
       .ddx/attachments/<bead-id>/events.jsonl or inline in
       beads.jsonl) and emit one row per attempt found.
     - DO NOT read .ddx/executions/<dir>/ for the backfill;
       events.jsonl is sufficient.
     - Idempotent: skip rows already in attempts.jsonl
       (dedupe by attempt_id).

  4. Tests:
     - TestMetrics_AppendRowOnFinalization: assert a row is
       added per attempt with all expected fields populated.
     - TestMetrics_BackfillFromEvents: assert backfill emits
       correct rows from existing events.
     - TestMetrics_BackfillIdempotent: assert re-running
       backfill does not duplicate rows.
     - TestMetrics_SchemaVersion: assert schema_version field
       is present and equals 1.

NON-SCOPE
  - The analyze CLI (sister bead).
  - Multi-machine partitioning (deferred until federation).
  - Adding agent-log-derived fields (tool_call_count, etc.) —
    those can be added later via schema_version bump.

INTERSECTIONS
  - Sister bead "docs(ADR): formalize 3-tier evidence storage"
    — this bead implements the cold-tier metrics layer the ADR
    documents.
  - Sister bead B29 (RetainDays prune) DEPENDS on this bead
    landing first; pruning local evidence is safe only after
    metrics are extracted.
  - Sister bead "feat(work): ddx work analyze CLI" reads
    .ddx/metrics/attempts.jsonl.

2. **Regression test — project-scoped query.**

3. **Regression test — backward compat.**

4. **End-to-end validation.**

   - Same test run against a second project asserts that project's Workers tab does not show project-1's worker.

5. **No regression to unrelated surfaces.**
   - Global `workers` query still returns all workers.
   - Worker detail page still loads by worker id.
   - Workers live-progress subscription still patches rows in place.

description:
## Observed

User clicks "Drain queue" on the project home page. Mutation returns success with a worker id. Navigating to `/nodes/.../projects/<id>/workers` shows no workers — an empty table.

Verified on disk: the worker record exists and is running.

```
$ cat .ddx/workers/worker-20260422T205846-f23f/status.json
{
  "id": "worker-20260422T205846-f23f",
  "kind": "work",
  "state": "running",
  "project_root": "/Users/erik/Projects/ddx",
  ...
}
```

So the dispatch worked, but the per-project workers list filters it out.

## Root cause

`cli/internal/server/state_graphql.go:156` in `GetWorkersGraphQL`:

```go
if projectID != "" && rec.ProjectRoot != projectID {
    continue
}
```

- `projectID` is the GraphQL argument — a project **id** like `proj-96d7ea83`.
- `rec.ProjectRoot` is the worker record field — a project **path** like `/Users/erik/Projects/ddx`.

These are different representations and never match. With any non-empty `projectID`, every worker is filtered out.

The global `workers` resolver (`resolver_agent.go:9`) passes `""` and works correctly. Only the per-project path (`workersByProject` → `GetWorkersGraphQL(projectID)`) is broken. The user's flow (dispatch from project home → navigate to project workers) hits exactly this path.

Note: `GetBeadSnapshots` (state_graphql.go:49-105) handles the same concept correctly by iterating `s.Projects` and filtering on `proj.ID != projectID` — comparing id to id. The worker resolver does not use that pattern.

## Proposed direction

Two options; prefer (1) for minimal change, (2) for long-term clarity.

### Option 1 — Resolve id → path at the filter site

```go
expectedPath := ""
if projectID != "" {
    proj, ok := s.GetProjectByID(projectID)
    if !ok {
        return nil // unknown project id → no workers
    }
    expectedPath = proj.Path
}
...
if expectedPath != "" && rec.ProjectRoot != expectedPath {
    continue
}
```

### Option 2 — Store project id on the worker record

Add `ProjectID string` to `WorkerRecord`. Populate at creation time in `WorkerManager.StartExecuteLoop` via `s.GetProjectByPath(effectiveRoot)`. Filter on `rec.ProjectID != projectID`. Cleaner — the worker record carries its own identity and the query doesn't depend on runtime resolution. Requires a tiny migration (for older records missing the field, fall back to path-resolve as in Option 1).

Recommend Option 2. It removes the representation mismatch for good and is cheap.

## Scope note

This is a one-line functional bug with outsized impact: it's the reason the Workers page looks broken whenever used as the dashboard intends. Prioritizing P1.

## Out of scope

- Workers pane lifecycle controls (`ddx-69789664`).
- Cross-project workers view — the global `workers` query already handles that.
notes:

No Playwright test was added. File to add: `cli/internal/server/frontend/tests/` (or wherever existing Playwright tests live). The test should cover: (1) Drain → Workers tab shows new row with `state: running`, (2) second project's Workers tab does not show project-1's worker.

REVIEW:BLOCK

`cli/internal/server/state_graphql.go` / `GetWorkersGraphQL` is not changed in the diff, so AC1’s id-to-path root-cause fix is not implemented or evidenced.
`cli/internal/server/*test.go` has no diff adding the required two-project `workersByProject` regression coverage, global `workers` assertion, or unknown-project assertion for AC2.
No worker-record compatibility test is added for AC3, and the diff does not show whether Option 1 or Option 2 was chosen.
`cli/internal/server/frontend/e2e/*` has no diff adding the required Drain queue to Workers tab Playwright flow or second-project isolation check for AC4.
No evidence is added for AC5 that global workers, worker detail loading, or live-progress row patching still work.
No note or tracker/documentation update cross-references `ddx-69789664` as depending on this bead for AC6.

work-last-detail: Host-level /tmp exhaustion knocked out the Claude Code harness's own Bash sandbox for this worker, not just the target repo's tmp usage. Every Bash invocation (including trivial ones: `true`, `echo hi`, `ls /tmp`, `df -h`, and `df -h` with dangerouslyDisableSandbox) failed identically with: ENOSPC: no space left on device, mkdir '/tmp/claude-501/-Users-erik-Projects--ddx-exec-wt--execute-bead-wt-ddx-05e3d16b-20260713T161454-3e24f7dd' This is the harness sandbox scratch dir under /tmp, not a repo path. Read/Edit/Write tools remain functional, but `go test`, `lefthook run pre-commit`, and `git commit` all require the Bash tool, so this bead's acceptance criteria (AC3-5) cannot be produced or verified from this worker right now regardless of code correctness. This is the 7th occurrence of this exact signature on this host in one day across unrelated beads (ddx-38cacb2d, ddx-a751a7b1, ddx-34113f35, ddx-e1e229f5, ddx-842598b1, ddx-85acbe89, ddx-427370dc) — see memory project_worker_bash_sandbox_tmp_enospc.md. This now looks like a standing host condition needing proactive /tmp cleanup or relocation of the harness scratch dir off /tmp, not a per-bead surprise. Analysis done while Read-only tools still worked: the fix belongs in cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go. `cleanupScratchRoots` (around line 620) synthesizes `ExecutionCleanupMetadata{ProjectRoot: m.ProjectRoot, ...}` for any metadata-less directory under every root returned by `scratchRoots()` (line 829), which unconditionally includes `os.TempDir()` as a "legacy" root (line 845, comment: "Always include the legacy process temp dir"). Because the synthesized metadata's ProjectRoot always equals m.ProjectRoot, the `ownershipMismatch` check at line 687 never fires for host-global paths, so a metadata-less directory under os.TempDir() (e.g. an old `ddx-home-*` dir matching the prefix list at line 26-45) is treated as this-project-owned, fails the liveness probe (no metadata to prove liveness), and — once older than scratchMinAge — is measured (measureTreeWithContext, line 738) and removed (os.RemoveAll, line 746) even though nothing actually proves this project owns it. Proposed fix: classify `os.TempDir()` (and any other host-global/legacy roots returned by scratchRoots) as untrusted for ownership synthesis. When ReadExecutionCleanupMetadata returns os.ErrNotExist for a directory under such a root, do not synthesize `ProjectRoot: m.ProjectRoot`; instead emit an "unowned_scratch"-class observation and `continue` before reaching measureTreeWithContext/os.RemoveAll. Only synthesize current-project ownership (as today) for directories under project-scoped roots (the tempRoot's parent dir and config.ExecutionScratchRoot(projectRoot)). Directories that do carry a real cleanup.json (metadata-marked) continue through the existing liveness/project checks unchanged, per the bead's NON-SCOPE note. Not implemented: could not write+verify the code change (new tests TestExecutionCleanup_PreservesMetadataLessHostGlobalScratch and TestExecutionCleanup_DoesNotSynthesizeOwnershipForHostGlobalMetadataLessScratch, plus the full ./internal/agent/... suite and lefthook) without a working Bash tool. Leaving the worktree uncommitted rather than risk landing unverified logic in a safety-critical cleanup path.

description:
The ddx try / ddx work execution machinery has 9 fail-prone layers (routing pre-flight, cooldown classification, claim CAS, worktree spawn, subprocess lifecycle, outcome adjudication, retry policy, land coordination, review). Today most layers fail-CLOSED — when a layer's specific check rejects, the layer wedges the entire pipeline. The auto-routing rejection bug fixed at commit 3b4f5d58 demonstrated this: one preflight check went strict and the queue locked up for hours.

The 7 principles below capture what each layer should do instead. They are documentation, not code — referenced by every refactor child's AC and by future bead-authoring guidance.

PRINCIPLE STATEMENTS

P1: FAIL-OPEN at every machinery layer. When a layer's specific check rejects a candidate, the layer skips itself and emits a structured event — it does not wedge the pipeline. The auto-routing fix (workers.go:803, commit 3b4f5d58) is the canonical example: preflight is now advisory when no operator pin exists.

P2: SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY per layer. Each layer rejects only on conditions it owns. Routing pre-flight does NOT decide provider availability (fizeau owns); cooldown does NOT decide eligibility (picker owns); etc. Cross-layer concerns are the smell.

P3: OBSERVABLE DEGRADATION. Every fail-open emits a structured event surfaced in the workers panel. Operators see "preflight skipped (no operator pin)" instead of silent acceptance OR endless retry loop.

P4: BOUNDED BLAST RADIUS. A failure on bead X must not affect bead Y. Stay-alive fix at commit 41cb762e established this for preflight rejections (per-bead continue, not loop exit). Extend to all layers.

P5: OPERATOR-VISIBLE STATE. Worker reports current state (idle, claiming, executing, reviewing, blocked-on-X) at all times. No '8 hours running, 0 attempts' mystery state. ADR-022 rev 5 §Probe + freshness state model defines the worker side; UI workers panel surfaces it.

P6: AUTO-RETRY ONLY FOR TRANSIENT CLASSES. Cooldown fires ONLY when the model genuinely couldn't make progress (clean no-changes with rationale). Disrupted, preflight-rejected, network-error, claim-race → no cooldown, return to ready. Existing code: shouldSuppressNoProgress at execute_bead_loop.go:1545 already respects Disrupted (commit 47d8054e).

P7: BEAD = PROMPT. A bead's description + AC must be sufficient context for a competent sub-agent to execute it without hand-curation. Investigation done, file:line citations included, concrete test names specified, explicit non-scope marked. If a sub-agent succeeds where the bead's auto-prompt failed, the BEAD failed (not the executor). Bead-authoring template enforces this; bead-quality audit (forthcoming bead) retrofits existing beads.

NOT IN SCOPE
- Code changes (this bead is doc-only)
- Per-layer reliability bead-quality fixes (separate refactor children)

INTERSECTIONS
- Each refactor child (ddx-c8f79963 C5, ddx-06eb05d8 C7, ddx-9228a484 C9, ddx-848069a3 C8, ddx-b669bb9f C6, ddx-c670ef0a C12) gets an AC line citing the principle(s) it enforces
- Bead-quality audit applies P7 to ~20 existing open beads

EVIDENCE
- ddx-f339c399 documents the 2026-05-04 ddx try ddx-29058e2a --harness=codex no_changes outcome and supports P7 / bead-quality.
notes: Evidence cross-link: ddx-f339c399 documents the 2026-05-04 ddx try ddx-29058e2a --harness=codex no_changes outcome and serves as evidence for P7 / bead-quality.

description:
PROBLEM
`ddx install` and `ddx update` only ever target the per-project plugin tree. There is no way to install a skill/persona/plugin once per machine, so operators must repeat installs in every project. Three install destinations must be supported: global (XDG), project in-tree (`<project>/.ddx`), and project convention (XDG projects/...).

ROOT CAUSE
- cli/cmd/install.go:36 `RunE: f.runInstall` and its flag set (install.go:38-39) have no `--global` flag; install always targets the project under `.ddx/plugins/<name>/` (install.go:27-28).
- cli/cmd/update.go:57 `runUpdate` and update.go:194 `performUpdate` operate only on the working dir's project tree; update.go:112 `enumerateSkillUpdateTargets(workingDir)` is project-scoped.
- Both route through ddxroot.Path() unconditionally and never reference the global layer.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Add `--global` bool flag to `ddx install` (cli/cmd/install.go) and `ddx update` (cli/cmd/update.go).
2. install --global: write content to `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/plugins/<name>/` (via `ddxroot.GlobalDir()` from the resolver bead) and create symlinks/copies into agent-tier paths `~/.claude/skills/<name>` and `~/.agents/skills/<name>` (copy on platforms lacking symlink support).
3. install (no --global): keep writing to `ddxroot.Path()/plugins/<name>/` and link into `<project>/.claude/skills/<name>` AND `<project>/.agents/skills/<name>`. In in-tree mode the target is `<project>/.ddx/plugins/<name>`; in convention mode it is `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/projects/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/plugins/<name>` and the project agent-tier links point into that XDG path.
4. update --global updates only the global plugin tree; update (no flag) updates the project install in whichever mode (in-tree vs convention) is active, via `enumerateSkillUpdateTargets`.

NON-SCOPE
- The plugin resolver/precedence (sibling bead: registry two-layer resolution) — consume `ddxroot.GlobalDir()` from it.
- `ddx init --global` first-time setup (sibling bead: init topology).
- `ddx doctor` reporting and spec/doc updates (sibling bead: doctor + specs).
- Removing per-project install; both modes coexist.

DEPS
ddx-06cbaa90 (ddx home resolution); sibling registry-resolver bead (provides `ddxroot.GlobalDir()` and layer semantics).

description:
PROBLEM
Server-managed workers still start through the in-process goroutine path, so the server owns only a cancelable context and cannot prove it owns a killable worker process group. A managed worker also needs its process-group identity persisted in status.json, not just memory, so restart/shutdown can reason about the same worker after a process exit.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/server/workers.go:361-462 starts a worker by building a record, creating a context, and launching runWorker in goroutines; there is no OS process boundary in that path.
cli/internal/server/workers.go:88-135 defines WorkerRecord with PID and PIDAlive, but no persisted PGID/process-group field.
cli/internal/server/workers.go:1711-1720 writes status.json from the record as-is, so any managed process ownership must be recorded on WorkerRecord to survive a restart.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add a server-managed launch path that starts ddx work --server-managed <worker-id> in its own process group instead of only launching runWorker in-process.
- Extend WorkerRecord and the persisted status.json shape to include the managed process-group identity needed for cleanup.
- Wire the server-owned work start flow through that managed launch path and keep the existing in-process path only as a test seam if needed.
- Add TestManagedWorkerRecordsProcessGroup to prove the managed worker record and status.json both show nonzero process-group ownership.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not implement stop, watchdog reap, or shutdown cleanup in this bead.
- Do not change external reported workers or the UI.
- Do not alter bead claim semantics beyond what the managed start path needs for its own record.

ACCEPTANCE
1. TestManagedWorkerRecordsProcessGroup proves a server-managed drain worker has nonzero PID/PGID in WorkerRecord and status.json.
2. cd cli && go test ./internal/server/... -run "TestManagedWorkerRecordsProcessGroup" passes.
3. make install is run after the code change lands.
4. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
title: server: launch managed worker subprocesses with persisted PID/PGID

description:
Operator-observed gap: when ddx-server restarts, in-flight worker subprocesses lose their connection to the orchestrator. The current model has two execution paths (--local vs server-spawned) that diverge in lifecycle management, configuration plumbing (the dropped-flags class — see ddx-29058e2a), and observability (server can see only what it spawned).

PROPOSED ARCHITECTURAL SHIFT
WORKERS ARE LONG-LIVED PROCESSES THAT PHONE HOME TO THE SERVER VIA API. --local mode collapses to "worker registers with itself" using an in-process implementation of the same API. Same code path, same flags, same lifecycle.

THE ADR EVALUATES AND CHOOSES AMONG

PROPOSAL A — Server orchestrates, workers are long-lived clients
- Worker subprocess starts (either via `ddx work` CLI or via server-spawned)
- Worker registers with server (via /api/workers/register, gets worker-id + heartbeat token)
- Worker polls /api/workers/<id>/next-bead via long-poll or websocket; receives bead spec from server
- Worker reports progress via /api/workers/<id>/event {kind, body}
- Worker reports completion via /api/workers/<id>/result {bead-id, status, evidence}
- If server restarts: worker's heartbeat fails → worker enters "disconnected" state, finishes current bead, reconnects on server return
- If worker dies: server's heartbeat-timeout reclaims the bead

PROPOSAL B — Server is optional sidecar, worker is autonomous
- Worker runs independently; no server required
- If a server is reachable (via .ddx/server.addr), worker emits events to it best-effort
- Server is a passive observer, not an orchestrator
- Restart-safe by construction (worker doesn't depend on server)
- Loses: server-driven label filters, dynamic priority overrides, centralized cancel

PROPOSAL C — Hybrid: workers are autonomous executors but yield orchestration to server when present
- Worker checks for .ddx/server.addr at startup
- If present: registers as managed; receives bead assignments from server's queue
- If absent or unreachable: runs autonomously using local bead store
- Server restart: managed workers detect via heartbeat failure; gracefully complete current bead, then either retry registration OR fall back to autonomous mode (configurable)

UNIFIED API CONTRACT (all proposals)

POST /api/workers/register { project_root, harness, model_pref, label_filter, capabilities[] } → { worker_id, session_token, heartbeat_interval_ms }
POST /api/workers/<id>/heartbeat { state: idle|claiming|executing|reviewing } → { server_command: continue|pause|drain|terminate }
GET  /api/workers/<id>/next-bead → { bead, attempt_id, base_rev } | { wait_for_seconds: N }
POST /api/workers/<id>/event { kind, body, bead_id } → 204
POST /api/workers/<id>/result { bead_id, attempt_id, status, evidence_dir, commit_sha } → 204
POST /api/workers/<id>/disconnect → 204 (graceful)

The existing --local mode collapses to: a worker that registers with itself (no server) using an in-process implementation of the API. Same code path, same flags, same lifecycle.

OUTSTANDING BEADS THIS ADR MUST RECONCILE (overlap analysis required in the ADR output)

ABSORBED (implementation subsumed by the new architecture; ADR explicitly closes these as superseded once roadmap lands):
- ddx-29058e2a (ExecuteLoopSpec unification): becomes the API request/response payload — the spec IS the wire format. Refactor concern dissolves.
- ddx-dc157075 (worker stay-alive): ALREADY FIXED at commit 41cb762e via flat 30s poll-interval default + attempted-map reset. Whether the new architecture preserves these tactical fixes or replaces them via API-driven semantics needs an ADR decision.
- ddx-cfedee8e (escalation: wire ladder): the ladder becomes server-side orchestration logic, not loop-body logic. ADR must specify where ladder lives in the new shape.

CONFLICTS WITH IN-FLIGHT REFACTOR (refactor epic ddx-5cb6e6cd children) — ADR must resolve sequencing:
- ddx-c8f79963 (C5: no_changes adjudication move into try.Attempt): refactors the SAME code that the API transition refactors. Either land C5 first then transition, OR fold C5 into the transition.
- ddx-06eb05d8 (C7: uniform Guard contract + delete attempted/hookFailed maps): same surface; same choice.
- ddx-848069a3 (C8: routing preflight to Drain startup): related to "server-side preflight" decision in API design.
- ddx-9228a484 (C9: StopCondition + cost-cap, absorbs ddx-cfedee8e and ddx-dc157075): heavy overlap. ADR must decide whether StopCondition becomes a server-side concept, a worker-side concept, or both.
- ddx-387a0178 (C13: file/identifier rename + ddx try CLI command): the ADR's new package layout (cli/internal/agent/work/) may conflict with C13's rename plan. Coordinate.
- ddx-1d867ec1 (rename execute_bead_loop.go): same as C13.

PARALLEL-SAFE (no conflict; ADR notes them but doesn't reshape):
- ddx-5b3e57f4 (cooldown: distinguish disrupted from gave-up): the API contract makes disruption naturally observable (server sees worker disconnect → marks Disrupted). But the cooldown logic itself is independent. ADR should call out that the API design enables cleaner Disrupted classification.
- ddx-1e516bc9 (fizeau Execute upstream gap): independent of API design.
- ddx-4c51d33e LAYER 1, ddx-055e8d32 LAYER 2, ddx-5ae050dc LAYER 3 (GraphQL project scoping): all in cli/internal/server/graphql/. Independent of worker API.
- ddx-9d55601f (picker bug): already fixed.
- ddx-a946c744 + ddx-aee651ec + ddx-3e60fd84 + ddx-83440482 (REACH/checks): hook into pre_merge gate; needs to integrate with the new worker contract but doesn't block ADR.
- All Story 6/14/15/16 frontend + backend feature beads: independent.

SPEC UPDATES THIS ADR DRIVES (the ADR roadmap must include these as deliverables)

- New ADR document: docs/helix/03-decide/ADR-XXX-worker-client-server-architecture.md
- FEAT-006 (Agent Service) — major amendment: worker API contract section, --local-collapses-to-API explanation, deprecation of direct execution paths
- FEAT-010 (Executions) — amendment: worker lifecycle now spans across server restarts; "execution" becomes a bead-attempt regardless of which worker performs it
- SD-024 (Resolved Config / CLIOverrides) — possible amendment: if ResolvedConfig becomes part of the API request payload, SD-024 reshapes
- TD-030 (Backend interface + chaos contract) — cross-reference if any
- CONTRACT-003 (Fizeau Service) — no change required (fizeau is below the worker; the API is between worker and ddx-server, not worker and fizeau)

NOT IN SCOPE FOR THIS ADR
