description:
PROBLEM
ddx-0c7d976c fixed applyWorkerCandidateCycle so ExecuteBeadResult.Status correctly becomes review_malfunction/review_request_changes/review_block/repair-cycle-exhausted after a pre-land candidate-cycle failure. That fix is necessary but not sufficient: the two CLI call sites that trigger the actual git merge never look at res.Status at all, so a candidate whose review malfunctioned can still be fast-forwarded into the target branch.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:475 `if res != nil && res.ResultRev != "" && res.ResultRev != res.BaseRev && res.ExitCode == 0 {` gates the call to agent.SubmitWithPreMergeChecks (which calls agent.LandBeadResult, the real merge) solely on ResultRev-changed + ExitCode==0. It does not check res.Status, res.ReviewVerdict, or res.ReviewSkipReason.
- cli/cmd/try.go:421 has the identical gap for `ddx try`.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_orchestrator.go:163 LandBeadResult itself only inspects res.ExitCode, res.Outcome, res.FailureMode, and GateResults (EvaluateRequiredGatesForResult); it has no awareness of res.Status/res.ReviewVerdict/res.ReviewSkipReason (the fields ddx-0c7d976c made meaningful) at all.
- Only after SubmitWithPreMergeChecks/LandBeadResult returns does ApplyLandingToResult (execute_bead_orchestrator.go:336) overwrite res.Status with the landing outcome — so even if the worker correctly reported review_malfunction, that classification is silently discarded by a successful (ungated) merge before anyone downstream can act on it.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a shared predicate (e.g. `agent.IsCandidateCycleNonMergeable(status string) bool` in execute_bead_status.go, covering ExecuteBeadStatusReviewMalfunction, ExecuteBeadStatusReviewRequestChanges, ExecuteBeadStatusReviewBlock, ExecuteBeadStatusRepairCycleExhausted, ExecuteBeadStatusReviewFixableGap) and check it at both cmd/ call sites before entering the SubmitWithPreMergeChecks branch — route to the existing "preserve, don't merge" branch (the same one used today for res.Outcome == ExecuteBeadOutcomeTaskFailed / res.ExitCode != 0) instead.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change LandBeadResult's git merge, gate-evaluation, or preserve-ref mechanics; do not change the pre-land candidate-cycle classification logic in candidate_cycle.go or applyWorkerCandidateCycle; do not touch the approved/no-reviewer landing path; do not add a new CLI flag.

PARENT
None.

DEPS
None. Continuation of ddx-0c7d976c (that bead fixed the Status propagation into ExecuteBeadResult; this bead makes the cmd/ landing gate actually consult it).

description:
PROBLEM
DDx already has TD-031 as the bead state-machine contract, but live ddx work behavior is still confusing no_changes attempt evidence with durable queue management. Operators now see beads parked on retry cooldown even when the real condition is already satisfied, needs human triage, parent/epic container picked by the ordinary worker, external blocker, or stale tracker metadata after a later success event.

ROOT CAUSE
- docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-031-bead-state-machine.md:164-208 defines no_changes_* events and an outcome mapping, but it does not explicitly state the two reliability invariants needed by current ddx work: cooldown is only for retryable time-based conditions, and every execution-skipped bead must have an explainable durable reason.
- docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-031-bead-state-machine.md:279-297 says no_changes outcomes drive status/label/event changes, but it does not clearly separate raw attempt outcome from durable bead action. That gap allowed implementation to use no_changes + retry-after as a generic parking lot.
- docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-031-bead-state-machine.md:202-208 does not cover reconciliation precedence for stale Extra fields such as work-last-status when later events show success.

PROPOSED FIX
- Amend TD-031 only; do not create a new disposition spec or persisted status.
- Add a concise "Lifecycle reliability invariants" subsection: no_changes is attempt evidence, not durable queue state; retry-after is only for retryable time-based conditions; skipped execution must have an explainable durable reason surfaced in diagnostics.
- Extend the existing outcome mapping with current no_changes cases: verified already satisfied, unverified, unjustified/no rationale, needs investigation, parent/epic/decomposed, external blocker, superseded, transient infra/quota/transport, and stale tracker metadata.
- Define reconciliation precedence: latest terminal event and close evidence beat stale work-* Extra fields; reconciliation may clear stale no_changes/cooldown metadata but must preserve append-only events.
- Keep TD-031 the sole canonical taxonomy; downstream FEAT/SD/ADR docs must cross-reference it rather than duplicate the table.

NON-SCOPE
- Editing FEAT-004, FEAT-010, SD-004, ADR-023, or skill files; follow-up beads handle narrow cross-references and vocabulary alignment.

description:
PROBLEM
The pre-push/full-test gate can fail under `-race` with a data race in workerprobe JSONL mirroring. This blocks otherwise unrelated worker landings and pushes, and it undermines the reliability of the worker-status/liveness work that depends on the same event path.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/workerprobe/probe.go:465-484` defines `teeWriter` with a mutable `buf []byte`, but `Write` appends to and slices that buffer without synchronization.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2718-2736` calls `sink.Write(line)` and then `sink.Write(newline)`. Multiple work goroutines can write through the same sink during cleanup/progress emission.
- Observed race evidence from the 2026-05-13 pre-push/full-test gate: `TestWorkDefaultDrainModeExitsOnEmptyQueue` in `cli/cmd/work_test.go:371-387` failed under `-race`; one goroutine wrote `workerprobe.(*teeWriter).Write` from `writeLoopEvent` during `ExecuteBeadWorker.Run`, while another wrote through the same tee from `runExecutionCleanupPass`.

PROPOSED FIX
Make the workerprobe JSONL tee concurrency-safe and preserve event parsing semantics. Add a mutex or equivalent serialization around `teeWriter.Write` buffer mutation and dispatch, and consider making `writeLoopEvent` emit the JSON line plus newline in a single `Write` to reduce interleaving. The fix must be local to event mirroring; structured logging must remain fail-open and must not block work if the probe/server is unavailable.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change worker scheduling, readiness classification, or server ingest contracts. Do not disable the race detector or loosen pre-push gates.
title: workerprobe: serialize JSONL tee writes under concurrent loop events

description:

The queue-drain loop still lacks a command-level regression that proves host resource exhaustion stops ddx work before it touches the next ready bead. description:
Create skills/ddx/reference/beads.md — the domain reference file a harness reads when the user asks to create, plan, or update beads.

Content required:
- **Inline context, not links.** Every bead description must be readable cold by an automated execute-bead worker that has no chat history and no open tabs.
- **Explicit in-scope file list.** Repo-relative paths. Bad: 'the auth module'. Good: 'cli/internal/auth/pipeline.go and cli/internal/auth/pipeline_test.go'.
- **Explicit do-NOT-touch scope negation** (non-goals). Prevents scope creep during agent execution.
- **Favor many small beads.** Rule of thumb: if a bead would touch more than ~3 files or more than one subsystem, decompose into child beads under an epic.
- **Acceptance is a command that passes, not a sentence.** 'X works' is not AC. 'cd cli && go test ./internal/foo/... passes and returns 0' is AC.
- **Implementations include tests.** The acceptance criteria must reference a test command.
- **Rollback/cleanup expectations** for partial changes — what 'leave it unclaimed' means in practice.
- **spec-id linkage** when a governing artifact exists (FEAT-*, SD-*, TD-*, ADR-*); omit when it doesn't.

description:
PROBLEM
`ddx work --watch` currently dirties tracked files while a worker is merely alive. Operators then see `.ddx/beads.jsonl` and `.ddx/run-state*` changes even when no durable bead outcome has happened, and concurrent watchers can race the same moving state.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/bead/store.go:869-925` `ClaimWithOptions` persists live claim state (`status=in_progress`, `owner`, `claimed-at`, `claimed-pid`, `claimed-machine`, `claimed-session`, `claimed-worktree`, `work-heartbeat-at`) into `.ddx/beads.jsonl` before touching the external lease.
- `cli/internal/bead/claim_liveness.go:15-24` and `cli/internal/bead/claim_liveness.go:64-75` already write an external lease, but the lease only carries `bead_id`, `updated_at`, and `pid`, so operator-facing claim metadata still depends on tracker mutation.
- `cli/internal/agent/run_state.go:100-125` writes live attempt state under `.ddx/run-state/` and `.ddx/run-state.json`; `cli/cmd/init.go:18-31` ignores these paths for new repos, but existing tracked run-state files still produce dirty deletions when cleanup runs.
- `cli/internal/agent/worker_liveness_sidecar_test.go:22-28` currently documents the tracker as the durable claim marker; that contract now conflicts with the desired live-state policy.

PROPOSED FIX
Move worker-owned live claim state fully into sidecar state. Extend the claim lease record to carry owner/session/worktree/machine/started_at/pid/updated_at and make the `ddx work` / `ddx try` worker claim path update only that lease until a terminal durable outcome occurs. `ReadyExecution` must exclude beads with a fresh sidecar lease and include beads whose sidecar lease is absent or stale. Manual tracker lifecycle operations can remain explicit tracker operations, but ordinary worker liveness must not dirty `.ddx/beads.jsonl`.

Also migrate run-state policy so live run-state files are never tracked: add a migration/cleanup path that removes tracked `.ddx/run-state.json` and `.ddx/run-state/*.json` from the git index, keeps the ignore rules, and proves cleanup does not create tracked deletions.

- Do not drop execution evidence or attempt metrics.
- Do not remove operator visibility; surface live owner/bead/attempt from sidecars instead of the tracker.

description:
PROBLEM
Interactive agents opened inside a DDx project can treat broad DDx prompts like "what's next", "what's blocking the queue", or "do work" as permission to start code edits. That competes with ddx work, which is supposed to drain execution-ready beads, and leaves no crisp default for human-required queue intervention, planning, and worker-capacity decisions.

ROOT CAUSE
AGENTS.md:1-18 enters bead policy immediately without declaring a default interactive queue-steward posture. docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-010-task-execution.md:18-29 defines ddx run/try/work execution layers but not the interactive-agent boundary around them. docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-011-skills.md:28-32 routes phrases like "do work" and "what's on the queue" through the ddx skill without distinguishing queue stewardship from bead execution. .agents/skills/ddx/reference/status.md:18-23 maps "What should I work on next?" to ddx bead ready, which exposes worker-ready beads rather than human-required intervention.

PROPOSED FIX
Define explicit DDx agent modes and implement the guardrails around them: queue_steward for broad interactive sessions, bead_execution for ddx work/try/execute-bead workers, direct_user_implementation for explicit human requests to edit code/docs, and review for read-only review asks. Add a focused operator command surface for intervention work and worker-capacity suggestions, while preserving ddx work as the owner of execution-ready implementation beads.

NON-SCOPE
- Replacing ddx work's existing execution loop.
- Building a full TUI or chat UI.
- Rewriting bead tracker storage by hand.
- Changing merge-policy or tracker audit semantics.

CHILD QUEUE
- Spec guidance updates define the mode taxonomy and precedence.
- DDx skill/AGENTS guidance makes queue stewardship the broad interactive default.
- Agent execution plumbing marks ddx work/try prompts with bead_execution mode.
- A command surface exposes human-required intervention and worker-capacity advice.
- Regression tests and prompt evals prove interactive guidance does not suppress ddx work execution.

description:
PROBLEM
Server worker-cleanup tests pass on a bare host but fail inside a ddx-managed bead attempt (ddx try / ddx work), reporting 'process pid ... still alive after cleanup' in cli/internal/server/server_shutdown_test.go, cli/internal/server/workers_shutdown_test.go, cli/internal/server/workers_stop_test.go, and cli/internal/server/workers_watchdog_test.go. This makes any bead whose gate includes ./internal/server/... red for agent-executed attempts while green for humans. Observed 2026-07-22 at source HEAD 425d5b7caa: the ddx-69591a68 attempt reported exactly these failures, while 'cd cli && go test ./internal/server/... -count=1' exits 0 on the host. This is the cli/internal/server twin of ddx-6f4b96ec (same mechanism, cmd + internal/agent packages).

ROOT CAUSE
cli/internal/server/workers_stop_test.go:549-554 defines the package-wide test helper testProcessAlive(pid), which returns syscall.Kill(pid, 0) == nil. waitForProcessGone (workers_stop_test.go:556-566) polls it for 5s and t.Fatalf's with 'process pid %d still alive after cleanup'. kill -0 succeeds on a dead-but-unreaped zombie. Killed worker processes orphaned by cleanup reparent to the nearest child-subreaper ancestor: on a bare host that is PID 1, which reaps immediately (ESRCH within the window); inside a coding-agent attempt the harness CLI is a subreaper that never wait()s foreign grandchildren, so the zombie persists, kill -0 keeps succeeding, and the assertion times out.

PROPOSED FIX
Reaping the zombie entry is the inheriting ancestor's job, not DDx's; the tests prove the process was killed. Make the test helper zombie-aware:
1. In testProcessAlive (cli/internal/server/workers_stop_test.go:549-554), after syscall.Kill(pid, 0) == nil, read /proc/<pid>/stat and return false when the state field is 'Z'. Parse by locating the closing paren of the comm field before splitting, since comm may contain spaces. Keep the pid <= 0 short-circuit.
2. Include the observed /proc state in waitForProcessGone's Fatalf message to aid future triage.
3. Follow the helper naming/parsing pattern established by ddx-6f4b96ec (processDeadOrZombie in cli/cmd and cli/internal/agent) if that bead has landed; otherwise implement standalone — do not add a dependency edge.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change production liveness code: cli/internal/server/process_unix.go:13-15 and cli/internal/server/workers_reap_unix.go:24 intentionally treat non-ESRCH (including zombies) as alive for reap/watchdog decisions and are out of scope. Do not touch cli/cmd or cli/internal/agent tests (owned by ddx-6f4b96ec). Do not set PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER in tests. No parent; no deps.
title: server tests: treat unreaped zombies as dead in waitForProcessGone cleanup assertions

description:
## Observed

The Efficacy page at `/nodes/.../projects/.../efficacy` loads very slowly. User feedback: efficacy should really be "an aggregation of sessions grouped by provider / harness / model" — which is not what the current implementation does.

## Ground truth (current implementation)

`cli/internal/server/graphql/resolver_feat008.go:676-833` —

- `EfficacyRows` builds its rollup from **bead evidence events** (`kind:routing` and `kind:cost` on every closed bead), not from sessions.
- Computation path: `store.ReadAll()` → for every closed bead, read its event file → filter for routing/cost → per-(harness, provider, model) aggregate.
- There is a cache (`efficacyMemo`), keyed by a fingerprint that itself walks every event on every closed bead to compute event count + max timestamp. So cache validation costs almost as much as cache rebuild.
- Cost shape: `O(closed_beads × events_per_bead)` on every request (cache miss) and even on cache hit the fingerprint walk happens.

## Why this is wrong (per user feedback)

- Efficacy is a sessions-view concept: "how is harness/provider/model X doing?" Sessions are the natural row. Bead events are a lossy, indirect proxy — they only exist for *closed* beads, they duplicate session state, and they force coupling between the efficacy feature and bead lifecycle.
- The bead-event path misses: open beads with in-flight sessions, sessions that didn't close a bead, benchmark/quorum sessions, non-execute-bead invocations (e.g., `ddx agent run`).
- The sessions feed is already being reworked into a sharded pointer index (`ddx-2ceb02fa`). Efficacy should read from that index — single source of truth.

## Proposed direction

### Part 1 — Reshape the data source

- Rebuild `EfficacyRows` as an aggregation over `sessions.index` (the sharded index from `ddx-2ceb02fa`), not over bead events.
- Grouping key: `(harness, provider, model)` — optionally filterable by project, bead, label, time range.
- Metrics per row: attempts (count), successes (count + rate), median input/output tokens, median duration, median cost. Identical shape to today; only the source changes.
- Shard awareness: time-range queries map to a shard set (same pattern as `ddx-2ceb02fa`); the default view reads current + previous shard.

### Part 2 — Fixture + baseline (honor user's 1,000+ record floor)

- Perf harness target: aggregate ≥**1,000 session rows** (≥ 10 distinct `(harness, provider, model)` groups) within the budget below.
- Stretch fixture: 50,000 session rows across 24 monthly shards. Measures steady-state behavior as the index grows.
- Baseline captured in the bead notes before any optimization.

### Part 3 — Perf targets (first pass, in-place)

- Default Efficacy view (all-time) on a 10k-session, 2-shard fixture: p95 ≤ 150ms in-process / ≤ 400ms HTTP.
- Date-filtered view (last 30 days, 1 shard): p95 ≤ 60ms in-process / ≤ 200ms HTTP.
- If in-place optimization (scope, pushdown, memoize-per-shard, streaming aggregation) **cannot hit these numbers** on the 50k stretch fixture, **do not silently change substrate** — raise the decision with the user. Candidate backends named by the user: axon, sqlite, postgres. Bring a recommendation + rationale, not a fait accompli.

### Part 4 — Drop the bead-event read path

- After the rewrite, remove `efficacyFingerprint`, `buildEfficacySnapshot` event iteration, `attemptsFromEvidence`, and `efficacyMemo`. They become dead weight once the source moves.
- Evidence events on beads remain (they're bead audit trail, not efficacy data); nothing in bead lifecycle changes.

## Out of scope

- The `comparisons` / "compare arms" feature on this page (tracked separately — see companion bead).
- Project-scope filtering UI (the backend support can be added now; the UI widget is a follow-up).
- Cross-machine / federated efficacy rollups.

Efficacy now depends on ddx-2ceb02fa. The current worktree contains the sharded sessions index implementation at .ddx/agent-logs/sessions/sessions-YYYY-MM.jsonl, so this pass reads that substrate directly; no interim source or stub was used.

Source-change baseline before per-shard memoization: fixture seeds 10,000 session index rows across 2 monthly shards with 10 distinct harness/provider/model groups, plus stretch fixture of 50,000 rows across 24 monthly shards. Measured with go test ./internal/server/graphql -run TestEfficacyRowsDateFilterAndPerfTargets -count=1 -v.

Source-only results:
- 10k all-time in-process p95: 46.87735ms (target <=150ms)
- 10k all-time HTTP p95: 47.756933ms (target <=400ms)
- 10k last-30-days in-process p95: 24.356549ms (target <=60ms)

description:
## Context

ddx-b808df39 (P0: ddx agent stop/kill command for hung workers) treats hung-worker remediation as an operational need, but does NOT investigate the UNDERLYING cause of the hangs. The feature is a useful escape hatch, but shipping it without understanding WHY workers hang means we'll keep needing the escape hatch.

Opus fresh-eyes review (2026-04-18) flagged: 'Hung workers for 33h–142h are an operational defect independent of root cause' — the feature bead is justified, but a SIBLING root-cause investigation is missing from the portfolio.

## Observed

The referenced 33h and 142h hang durations in ddx-b808df39 imply multiple incidents where an execute-bead worker process remained in-progress past any reasonable upper bound for a single bead. Needs to investigate:

1. Is the worker process alive but stuck in a tool call (bash subprocess that never returns)?
2. Is it alive but mid-LLM-call with no timeout (provider hang + no client-side deadline)?
3. Is it dead but the bead's claimed_at never cleared (tracker-side leak)?
4. Is the worktree locked or fsync'd in a way that prevents cleanup?

## Fix direction

This bead is an INVESTIGATION, not a fix. Deliverable is a short report that:

1. Reproduces or observes at least one hang incident and captures:
   - ps / pgrep state of the worker process tree
   - stack traces via 'go tool pprof' against the worker (if alive)
   - Timeline from .ddx/executions/<attempt>/embedded/*.jsonl (last event type + timestamp)
   - tracker claimed_at and retry_after state

2. Classifies the hang into one of the four categories above (or a new category).

3. Files concrete follow-up beads for each identified root cause:
   - Tool subprocess timeout if bash hangs
   - LLM client deadline if provider hangs
   - Claim expiry / heartbeat if tracker-side leak
   - File-lock / worktree cleanup if fs-side

4. Recommends whether ddx-b808df39's stop/kill mechanism is sufficient as mitigation or needs additional primitives.

## Relation to ddx-b808df39

ddx-b808df39 ships the OPERATOR TOOL to stop a hung worker. This bead finds the BUG that causes hangs. Both are needed; ship ddx-b808df39 first if the operator-tool is more urgent, then this investigation.

## Non-goals

- Fixing the root cause in this bead. Scope is investigation + follow-up bead filing.
- Preventing all possible hangs (impossible). Scope is the actually-observed hang modes.
notes:
Investigation complete (attempt 20260418T043148-1346e8a3). Report at .ddx/executions/20260418T043148-1346e8a3/incident_report.md.

Root-cause summary:
- RC1 (PRIMARY): Runner.Run and Runner.RunAgent discard caller ctx (runner.go:239, agent_runner.go:163). WorkerManager.Stop cannot interrupt a running agent.
- RC2: idle-reset timer instead of wall-clock deadline for non-claude paths (executor.go:154, agent_runner.go:264).
- RC3: compaction-stuck breaker fires too late (~2h observed).
- RC4: provider HTTP calls likely lack per-request deadlines (confirm against live hung worker).
- BashTool subprocess hang ruled out (120s default timeout). Tracker-side / fs-lock hypotheses are downstream of RC1.

Follow-up beads filed (parent=ddx-0a651925):
- …-526efaf1 P0 [RC1] propagate caller context
- …-b203c889 P0 [RC2] wall-clock deadline
- …-3e3913a0 P1 [RC4] per-request HTTP deadlines
- …-b0562380 P2 [RC3] bound compaction-stuck breaker by wall-clock
- …-34d039b7 P1 autonomous worker watchdog (complements ddx-b808df39)

ddx-b808df39's operator stop/kill is a correct mitigation but NOT sufficient as sole fix — until RC1 lands, operators will keep needing it. Ship ddx-b808df39 first, then RC1 → RC2 → RC4 → RC3 → watchdog.

Find child beads: ddx bead list --parent ddx-0a651925

acceptance: After `ddx install <name> --force --local <path>` succeeds, `ddx installed` reports STATUS=ok with VERSION matching the source's plugin.json `version` field and INSTALLED set to today's date.
description:
## Summary

Observed against ddx v0.6.2-alpha103-12-ge6379ebc5 on 2026-05-18.

After `ddx install helix --force --local /home/erik/Projects/helix` succeeds (output: 'Linked .ddx/plugins/helix -> /home/erik/Projects/helix; Installed helix from local path; recorded plugin pin unchanged'), `ddx installed` reports:

```
NAME   VERSION  TYPE      STATUS  INSTALLED
helix  0.3.3    workflow  BROKEN  2026-05-12
```

Three things are wrong:
1. STATUS=BROKEN despite the install reporting success.
2. VERSION=0.3.3 despite the linked source's plugin.json declaring 0.4.1.
3. INSTALLED=2026-05-12 (date of the prior successful install) — not updated by today's --local install.

The 'recorded plugin pin unchanged' message in the install output is the smoking gun: DDx doesn't update the version pin when installing from --local. It leaves the registry at whatever the last registry install pinned, even though the on-disk plugin is now at a different version.

## Expected behavior

After a successful `ddx install --local`, `ddx installed` should:
- Report STATUS=ok (not BROKEN) if the install succeeded.
- Report VERSION matching the plugin.json of the linked source.
- Report INSTALLED date of today (the actual install).

## Workaround

None known. The metadata is misleading but the file content is correct, so runtime works.
title: ddx installed reports BROKEN status after a successful --local install that creates a symlink-style plugin

description:
PROBLEM
Some worker failure paths still call `Store.Unclaim`, which updates the bead row and then removes the claim heartbeat outside the same critical section. If heartbeat removal fails, `ReadyExecution` can keep excluding an open bead until the sidecar lease TTL expires, reducing multi-worker throughput and making failures look like queue starvation.

ROOT CAUSE
- cli/internal/bead/store.go:1081-1100 implements `Unclaim` as row update followed by separate heartbeat removal.
- cli/internal/bead/store.go:1103-1130 implements `Release`, which atomically updates the row and clears the heartbeat under one lock.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2365-2368 still uses `w.Store.Unclaim(candidate.ID)` on a worker refresh failure path; other worker paths should be audited for the same pattern.

PROPOSED FIX
- Audit worker-owned failure/unclaim paths and replace them with `Release` where the current worker owns the claim.
- Add a fault-injection test that makes heartbeat removal fail and proves the bead is not left with a fresh sidecar lease after a worker failure path releases it.
- Preserve CLI/operator `ddx bead update --unclaim` semantics where direct `Unclaim` is still appropriate.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change claim ownership rules or sidecar lease TTLs in this bead.
- Do not close beads on failure; failed attempts must remain open/unclaimed unless existing outcome policy says otherwise.
title: agent: release worker claims atomically on failure paths

description:
'ddx agent work' help says 'work scans the current project's execution-ready bead queue.' When submitting to a multi-project server, there is no way to say 'run this loop against project X'. The server picks whichever project is the current server context, ignoring the caller's CWD.

## Observed

From CWD /Users/erik/Projects/axon:

  $ ddx agent work --once --harness claude --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --json
  {
    "project_root": "/Users/erik/Projects/ddx",  # WRONG
    "state": "running",
    "worker_id": "worker-20260415T011331-d0a4"
  }

I wanted the worker to pick an axon bead. The server ran the worker against the ddx repo instead. There is no --project flag, no env var, nothing in the CLI to redirect the server's project scope.

Currently the only way to target a specific project with work is --local mode (which spawns a subprocess using the caller's CWD as the project root). This defeats the purpose of having a server in a multi-project deployment.

## Scope

- --project <path> or --project <name> flag on work, execute-bead, and 'ddx agent run' that tells the server which project_root to use
- Env var fallback: DDX_PROJECT_ROOT or similar
- Default to CWD if unset and no flag
- Server refuses ambiguous/unmatched project names with a clean error
- Integration test: from CWD A, submit a loop targeting project B; assert worker runs in B's project_root

## Why this matters for the user's workflow

Without this, the ONLY way to drive multi-project execution from one shell is --local, which (a) loses the server's queue visibility, (b) ties the parent process to the child, and (c) negates the 'ddx agent work submits to server by default' ergonomic that work's --help promises.

## Acceptance

- [ ] --project flag wired through work/execute-bead/run
- [ ] Env var fallback documented
- [ ] Default behavior: CWD-based project detection
- [ ] Integration test for cross-project submission
- [ ] work --help updated to describe project targeting
title: exec: work --project flag to target a specific project when server is multi-project

description:
PROBLEM
Observed directly during a live human-in-the-loop session against a real project (pqueue, /Users/erik/Projects/pqueue), not synthesized. Three related, concrete observations from one session:

1. DUPLICATE CLAIM RACE: a project-scoped `ddx work --server-managed` daemon that had been running for hours, and a foreground `ddx work --json` the operator started manually, both claimed the SAME bead within ~40 seconds of each other on two separate occasions (pqueue-70c85ac1 at 15:26:50/15:27:32, pqueue-5c5353f7 at 16:18:07/16:18:44), each spinning up its own `.ddx-exec-wt` worktree. The second occurrence produced a `pre_claim_intake.system_unready` warning ("project root mutation rejected... revise the rewrite so it preserves every explicit commitment") twice on the bead's event log, warn-only, non-blocking. This looks like the same class of issue tracked by ddx-eea2dfca/ddx-69672921 (repeated pre-claim system-unready warnings not surfaced as a clear operator-visible signal) -- filing this as a concrete, reproducible real-world instance rather than duplicating that epic's scope.

2. MAIN WORKTREE LEFT DIRTY DURING A LIVE ATTEMPT: while a project-scoped server-managed worker was `phase=running` on a bead (pqueue-6f8d85db, worktree=.ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-pqueue-6f8d85db-...), the PROJECT'S MAIN WORKTREE (not the isolated attempt worktree) showed 17 uncommitted, modified files spanning many unrelated crates, sitting dirty for several minutes across repeated `git status` checks with no new commits landing in between (HEAD stayed at the same `chore: checkpoint pre-execute-bead ...` commit throughout). An operator or an agent (Claude Code, in this case) working in that same main worktree during an active attempt has no reliable signal for which uncommitted changes are "the live attempt's WIP, do not touch" versus safe to edit/commit -- a `git status`-only view is ambiguous. If this dirty-main-worktree state during `phase=running` is intentional (e.g. a staging step before a checkpoint commit), it should be documented and/or surfaced by `ddx work status`/`ddx bead show` so a human or agent sharing the worktree can tell not to touch it; if it is not intentional, it looks like an isolation leak from the attempt worktree back into the main one.

3. MERGE GATE DID NOT CATCH A WORKSPACE-WIDE COMPILE BREAK: a bead landed to `main` (pqueue commit 75190c3, "feat: add change-record emission foundation") that changed a shared struct (`ProjectionImageItem` in pqueue-projection) without updating one of its several construction call sites (`crates/pqueue-sqlite/src/relational.rs:5410`), leaving `cargo build --workspace` (and `--all-features`) broken on `main` for every subsequent bead attempt forked from that point, including a completely unrelated one (pqueue-postgres) the operator was validating by hand at the time. This suggests that bead's own acceptance/merge gate ran a narrower build/test scope than `cargo build --workspace --all-features`, so a cross-crate breakage in a sibling crate was not caught before landing on shared `main`.

PROPOSED FIX
Not prescribed here -- filing as observations/evidence for ddx maintainers to triage against existing related epics (ddx-eea2dfca, ddx-69672921, ddx-2189a07f, ddx-693d504f) rather than guessing at implementation. Concretely worth deciding:
- Whether #1's warn-only pre_claim_intake outcome should escalate after N repeats within a short window, per the existing part-3 epic.
- Whether #2's dirty-main-worktree-during-phase=running is by design; if so, expose it via `ddx work status` (e.g. an explicit "main worktree has in-flight attempt WIP, do not modify" flag) rather than leaving it to a bare `git status` read.
- Whether execute-bead's default merge/acceptance gate should require a full `cargo build --workspace --all-features` (or project-equivalent) regardless of the bead's own narrower test scope, specifically to catch cross-crate breakage like #3.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not implement any of the three fixes here -- this bead is the observation/triage request only.
- Do not touch the pqueue repository or its bead tracker from this bead.
title: Concurrent-worker race left a dirty main worktree + duplicate claim during live pqueue session

Epic tracking FEAT-022 Prompt Evidence Assembly and Size Invariants.

See docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-022-prompt-evidence-assembly.md for
the full spec. This epic sequences implementation across Stages A–G.

Goal: establish a repo-wide invariant that no prompt DDx constructs,
accepts, or emits through text-returning server endpoints has unbounded

collapse the duplicate review assembler, bound review/grading evidence

- Stage C1 blocks Stages F and G.

description:
ddx agent log is fully implemented (cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go lines 745-807) and reads .ddx/agent-logs/sessions.jsonl. Each SessionEntry has a Correlation map (cli/internal/agent/types.go) that includes bead_id when the session was created by execute-bead. However there is no way to filter sessions by bead — you must know the session ID in advance or scroll through all recent sessions.

This bead adds --bead <id> filtering and a per-bead attempt summary view to the existing command.

## Required changes

### 1. --bead flag on ddx agent log (cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go)
When --bead <bead-id> is provided:
  - Scan all SessionEntry records in sessions.jsonl
  - Filter to entries where Correlation["bead_id"] == bead-id
  - Sort ascending by Timestamp (attempt order)
  - Display in attempt-history table format (see below)

No change to the default behavior (no --bead = show recent N sessions as today).

### 2. Attempt history table columns
ATTEMPT | STARTED | DURATION | HARNESS | MODEL | OUTCOME | TOKENS | COST | SESSION
- ATTEMPT: 1-based index in chronological order
- OUTCOME: merged / preserved / no-changes / error (from ExecuteBeadResult.Outcome via Correlation or result.json)
- SESSION: truncated session ID (8 chars) for use with ddx agent log <session-id>
- COST: formatted as /bin/zsh.0042 or 'local' if cost_usd == 0

### 3. Outcome resolution
SessionEntry does not directly store outcome — it stores exit_code and error. The full outcome is in .ddx/executions/{attemptID}/result.json (ExecuteBeadResult struct). When rendering the attempt table:
  - Use Correlation["attempt_id"] to find .ddx/executions/{attempt_id}/result.json
  - Read ExecuteBeadResult.Outcome from that file
  - Fall back to exit_code == 0 ? 'success' : 'error' if result.json is absent

### 4. Summary line
After the table, print a one-line summary:
  '<bead-id>: N attempts, M merged, K preserved, J errors. Last attempt: <elapsed> ago.'

### 5. --json passthrough
When --bead and --json are both set, emit the filtered SessionEntry array as JSON with an added outcome field resolved from result.json.

## Key files
- cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go — newAgentLogCommand() lines 745-807, add --bead flag and filter path
- cli/internal/agent/types.go — SessionEntry struct (lines 94-122), Correlation map field
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go — ExecuteBeadResult struct (lines 30-64), artifact paths convention
- .ddx/agent-logs/sessions.jsonl — runtime data source
title: Extend ddx agent log with --bead filter and per-bead attempt history

description:
PROBLEM
During attempt `20260713T134525-98889bd0`, both candidate reviewers returned zero bytes. `AttemptCycleCoordinator` classified the candidate as `review_malfunction` with `land_status:not_landed`, but the worker subsequently fast-forwarded commit `2dd9e011e` into main and closed `ddx-93d8b7c8` as success. The durable decision audit contradicts itself: the cycle trace says retry/not_landed while the final decision says close/landed. This silently bypasses the review gate exactly when no valid review evidence exists.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/candidate_cycle.go:315-325` correctly converts a reviewer transport/empty-output error into `ExecuteBeadStatusReviewMalfunction` and returns without calling the lander.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:355-386` runs the candidate cycle but copies only `CandidateRef`, `CycleIndex`, and `CycleTrace` back into `ExecuteBeadResult`; it discards the cycle report status, detail, review verdict/rationale, outcome reason, and error.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:4192-4258` later sees the stale success status and permits `CloseWithEvidence`, producing a final success audit despite the malformed review trace.

PROPOSED FIX
Project every outcome-bearing field from `cycleResult.Report` back into the execute result, or return a typed candidate-cycle outcome that the loop must handle before landing. A review malfunction, request changes, block, or exhausted repair cycle must preserve the candidate ref, skip landing and closure, release the claim according to existing retry/operator policy, and emit a final decision audit consistent with the cycle trace. Only an explicit APPROVE or durable configured review-skip may retain success.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken review parsing, treat empty output as approval, bypass review with `--no-review`, alter approved-candidate landing semantics, or discard the preserved candidate ref.

PARENT
None; root critical review-gate regression observed during the Niflheim queue drain.

DEPS
None. Regression of the guarantees implemented by `ddx-ce007f14` and `ddx-334c0958`.
notes: Second production reproduction in merged attempt 20260713T163832-72b324a1: implementation commit 61c9c4fd9 passed focused tests and pre-commit, then both candidate reviewers returned empty output. result.json classified cycle 0 as review_malfunction with retry_action=retry and land_status=not_landed, but ddx still advanced main, closed ddx-427370dc, and wrote audit commit 1cdeefe1b. This independently confirms the stale success projection bypass described in the bead.
title: Propagate candidate-review failure into the execute result

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-e19185aa is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 3 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
The decomposition action (currently invoked when a bead is too large for one execution and the agent splits it into child beads) is writing the parent's ID as a dep edge on every child. This produces an unbreakable deadlock:

  e29892a4 (parent, open) -- parent --> child_A
  e29892a4 -- parent --> child_B
  child_A.deps = [e29892a4]           <- BAD: parent is also a dep
  child_B.deps = [child_A, e29892a4]  <- BAD

The parent stays open until its children close. Every child is blocked on the parent. Nothing can be claimed. ddx work loops on the parent, the orchestrator emits 'mixed_commit_and_no_changes_rationale', the worker retries, and burns claim budget without progress.

Observed scenario (niflheim, 2026-06-04 04:30-05:13 UTC):
- Parent: niflheim-e29892a4 ('feat(delta): async write-behind ...')
- 10 children created during planning loops (23223661, a44a8ceb, 054c89b7, 0470ba0d, f10e9e35, f076b08c, 6c041162, 94e1df73, 9da62c2d, 5e4f9fb2)
- Every child carried deps=[..siblings.., niflheim-e29892a4]
- ~50 minutes of agent time + 4 strong-policy claude/opus attempts with zero feature commits; only tracker chores
- Unwedged manually by closing the parent via 'ddx bead close', after which siblings drained correctly in foundational order

Root cause is structural, not model-capability — auto-upgrading to a stronger model does NOT fix this. The orchestrator already detects the no-progress state but its only remediation is 'retry parent', which re-enters the same loop.

There is also a 'project root mutation rejected (continuing)' warning emitted by the readiness check during this state; that's a downstream symptom of the same problem, not the cause.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- The orchestrator's 'project root mutation rejected (continuing)' warning, when emitted alongside the parent-back-edge state, is upgraded from WARN to ERROR with the offending bead ID logged. Test: dispatch_logs_error_on_root_mutation_with_back_edge.
- Lifecycle schema documents that 'parent' and 'deps' MUST be disjoint and that 'deps' MUST be acyclic with the parent-tree. docs/ddx/lifecycle-rules.md (or equivalent) updated; ADR file if no governing artifact already exists.
- Existing valid graphs continue to pass 'ddx bead doctor' without --fix and without regression — regression test against a pre-existing tracker snapshot.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.
title: Reject bead dep edges that re-introduce the parent or any ancestor: part 3

description:

1. `TestExecutorLinuxPdeathsigKillsHarnessOnParentSIGKILL` starts an execute-bead executor path against a fake harness binary that forks a long-lived grandchild, SIGKILLs the parent worker process rather than sending graceful SIGTERM, and asserts the harness child and grandchild are gone within a bounded grace instead of becoming PID-1 orphans.

3. `TestExecutorStartParentDeathSignalThreadGuard` or an equivalent focused test/rationale covers the `Pdeathsig` parent-thread caveat using `runtime.LockOSThread` or a parent-PID guard.
4. `TestExecutorGracefulSignalStillTerminatesHarnessTree` proves existing SIGINT/SIGTERM or context-cancellation cleanup still terminates in-flight harness children.
5. Non-Linux behavior is covered by `TestExecutorParentDeathSignalNonLinuxFallbackDocumented` or build-tagged documentation explaining the fallback and why `Pdeathsig` is unavailable.

description:
PROBLEM
When a `ddx work` orchestrator dies abnormally (SIGKILL, crash, OOM, or supervising-process loss) while an execute-bead attempt is running, the spawned harness child can reparent to PID 1 and continue indefinitely. Observed 2026-05-27: a `claude --print` execute-bead child remained orphaned with PPID 1 for ~9h53m after its `ddx work` parent exited.

ROOT CAUSE (file:line)
- cli/internal/agent/executor.go:156 spawns the harness via `exec.Command(binary, args...)` and then calls `cmdSetProcessGroup(cmd)`.
- cli/internal/agent/executor_unix.go:13-15 sets only `SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}`. There is no Linux `Pdeathsig`, so the kernel does not signal the harness when the parent dies abnormally.
- cli/internal/agent/executor_unix.go:20-25 kills the process group only from graceful executor paths.
- cli/cmd/root.go:49-54 uses `signal.NotifyContext` for os.Interrupt and SIGTERM only. SIGKILL and crashes cannot be caught, so executor cleanup does not run.

PROPOSED FIX
On Linux, set `SysProcAttr.Pdeathsig` to SIGKILL or SIGTERM for execute-bead harness commands in `cmdSetProcessGroup`. Handle the Go runtime thread-migration caveat with `runtime.LockOSThread` around process start or an equivalent parent-PID guard so the parent-death signal is attached to the intended parent thread. Preserve process-group setup so existing graceful cancellation and timeout cleanup still kill the whole harness tree. Document the macOS/Windows fallback because `Pdeathsig` is Linux-only.

NON-SCOPE
- Graceful SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown already works through executor.go:231-255; do not regress it.
- The harness-runner-internal leak in fizeau is covered by fizeau-50b6f055; this child bead is only the DDx orchestrator-to-harness-child boundary.
- Startup orphan reaping is covered by a separate child bead from this decomposition.
- docker-clone backend cleanup is covered by a separate child bead from this decomposition.

CROSS-REF
- fizeau-50b6f055: fizeau harness-runner process-group cleanup.
- ddx-8f2e0ebf: lease release / operator-attention.
title: fix executor: enforce parent-death cleanup for execute-bead harness children on Linux

description:
PROBLEM
A DDx execute-bead attempt can produce both a substantive implementation commit and `.ddx/executions/<attempt>/no_changes_rationale.txt`, and DDx still records the attempt as `success`/`merged`. Live evidence: attempt `20260512T050728-bb18a61f` for `ddx-ef9e8aec` landed commit `15772fc85`, merged evidence commit `9e1ab8506`, and closed the bead, while `.ddx/executions/20260512T050728-bb18a61f/no_changes_rationale.txt` says `status: blocked` because the required `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/bead/...` gate timed out/failed. That turns a self-reported blocked verification into a successful close.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1413-1428` classifies `task_succeeded` solely from `resultRev != baseRev`; it only reads `no_changes_rationale.txt` when `resultRev == baseRev`.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:615-616` deliberately excludes `.ddx/executions/*/no_changes_rationale.txt` from synthesized code commits, so the file can coexist with a synthesized implementation commit without affecting `resultRev`.
- `cli/internal/agent/try/no_changes.go:56-90` already parses structured `status: blocked|open|proposed` no_changes rationales, but that parser is bypassed when any implementation commit exists.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1360-1407` treats the returned report as authoritative; by the time the loop sees the result, the contradictory no_changes signal has been lost behind a success/merged outcome.

PROPOSED FIX
- Make execute-bead treat an implementation diff plus `no_changes_rationale.txt` as a non-successful mixed-signal result before close/merge success is reported. A worker must choose one lane: commit green implementation, or no_changes/status rationale.
- Preserve the rationale text in evidence and surface a clear failure/detail such as `mixed_commit_and_no_changes_rationale` so the worker can retry or a follow-up bead can handle the stated blocker.
- Ensure `status: blocked` in the rationale cannot close a bead as success when a commit also exists.
- Keep legitimate `no_changes` behavior unchanged for zero-diff attempts and keep ordinary green implementation commits unchanged when no rationale file exists.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go`
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_*test.go` or `cli/internal/agent/try/*test.go` as needed for focused coverage

NON-SCOPE
- Do not rewrite the already-landed `ddx-ef9e8aec` history.
- Do not change Fizeau routing/model/provider selection.
- Do not weaken legitimate already-satisfied no_changes verification.

description:
PROBLEM
Running `make install` from a clean DDx checkout builds and installs a binary stamped with `-dirty` even when no source edits were pending. During the 2026-05-15 monitor restart, `make install` reported `v0.6.2-alpha81-63-gffe356c1b-dirty`, and `git status --short` showed only `cli/internal/server/frontend/build/.gitkeep` modified.

ROOT CAUSE
`cli/Makefile:24-31` runs `bun run build`, which empties `cli/internal/server/frontend/build/`, then recreates `internal/server/frontend/build/.gitkeep` using `touch`. The tracked `cli/internal/server/frontend/build/.gitkeep` currently contains a newline byte, but `touch` recreates an empty file after Vite removes the directory contents. That one-byte mismatch makes the source checkout dirty before `go build` computes `git describe --dirty` in `cli/Makefile:4-6`.

PROPOSED FIX
- Normalize the tracked placeholder `cli/internal/server/frontend/build/.gitkeep` to the same empty-file content produced by the build target, or otherwise make `frontend-build` recreate the exact tracked bytes.
- Verify `make install` from a clean checkout leaves no tracked `.gitkeep` diff and installs a DDx binary whose version string does not end in `-dirty`.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not track generated frontend build output under `cli/internal/server/frontend/build/`.
- Do not change the frontend bundle, Vite config, or go:embed target.
- Do not bypass the stale-binary guard in `ddx work`.

DEPS
No deps. This is a build hygiene fix discovered while restarting the DDx watcher.
title: build: keep frontend placeholder stable during install

description:
PROBLEM
Pre-merge checks turn an attempt-context cancellation or an infrastructure failure into a quality BLOCK, stranding good work as preserved-not-landed. Observed signature: pre-merge check "production-reachability" failed to start: context canceled -> Blocked. cli/internal/checks/runner.go runOne classifies failed-to-start, ctx-cancel, AND a check that ran-but-crashed / wrote no result all as StatusError; cli/internal/agent/checks_premerge.go (~143) maps StatusError->Blocked=true. So a cancelled attempt (or a local-box check that cannot start) blocks landing of changes the agent correctly produced.

PROPOSED FIX (fail-open ONLY on unconfirmed infra; a crashed check still blocks)
1. Add checks.StatusInfra to cli/internal/checks/protocol.go.
2. In runner.go runOne: ONLY ctx.Err()!=nil (cancellation) and the failed-to-start branch (the non-ExitError case where the command could not launch) return StatusInfra. A check that DID start but exits non-zero, or wrote no result file, STAYS StatusError (indistinguishable from a real failure — a crashing security/secrets check must not silently land bad code). A check declares "inconclusive" only by writing a result file with explicit StatusInfra, never by crashing.
3. In checks_premerge.go: set Blocked on StatusBlock OR StatusError; StatusInfra is NON-gating (surface it as an advisory/report, do not preserve on it).

NON-SCOPE: do not weaken land-side preserve gates (execute_bead_land.go large-deletion/syntax-sanity/post-land) — those stay fail-closed.

ACCEPTANCE
1. TestRunOne_ContextCancelled_Infra: a check run under an already-cancelled ctx returns StatusInfra (not StatusError/StatusBlock).
2. TestRunOne_FailedToStart_Infra: a check whose command cannot launch returns StatusInfra.
3. TestRunOne_StartedNonZero_StillError and TestRunOne_NoResultFile_StillError: a check that started but exits non-zero / wrote no result stays StatusError (gating).
4. TestRunPreMergeChecks_InfraDoesNotBlock: a StatusInfra result does not set Blocked; a real StatusBlock still does.
5. cd cli && go test ./internal/checks/... ./internal/agent/... green.
6. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
title: checks: cancellation/failed-to-start are StatusInfra (non-gating); crashed check still blocks (D2)

# PROBLEM
The bead backend interface today (`cli/internal/bead/backend.go`) is JSONL-shaped: `RawBackend` requires whole-corpus `ReadAll`/`WriteAll`, and `Backend` declares only 22 of `*Store`'s 69 public methods. - A typed `Operation` pattern with `Apply(b *Bead) error` (CAS via error returns)
- 11 LSP-clean storage sub-interfaces composing `Backend`
- Pluggable `IDGenerator` and parallel `LifecycleSubscriber`
- `context.Context` first-parameter discipline on every interface method
- Sentinel errors (`ErrNotFound`, `ErrConflict`, `ErrInvalidID`, `ErrAlreadyClaimed`, `ErrNotClaimedByOwner`, `ErrUnsupported`)
- The optional `OperationApplier` interface on `RawBackend` so JSONL backends can preserve heartbeat sidecar optimization
- A canonical Bead data model (field enumeration + invariants + JSONL wire format + schema-versioning policy)

This bead lays the foundation that all per-concern beads (L/C/E/X/Q/D/A/MIG) depend on. It declares the event reader/writer interfaces but deliberately does not migrate `AppendEvent`, `Events`, or `EventsByKind`; the E bead owns event-method ctx threading and `*Store` event interface satisfaction.

- `cli/internal/bead/backend.go:10-67` — `RawBackend` (4 whole-corpus methods) + `Backend` (22 high-level methods, incomplete).
- `cli/internal/bead/store.go` — `*Store` exposes 69 public methods, none take `ctx context.Context`.
- `cli/internal/bead/axon_backend.go:340-381` — `WriteAll` ships entire corpus per mutation (catastrophic for Postgres).
- Operation pattern, IDGenerator, sentinel errors, context discipline — all absent.
- Bead data model (the canonical schema of fields + invariants) — only implicit in the Go struct.

Implement TD-027 §5–§13 foundation pieces that are required before the per-concern beads can execute.

description:

description:
PROBLEM
  When parallel-worker drain mode is enabled (multiple ddx work --once
  shells running concurrently), bead.Store.WithLock and the agent-layer
  tracker locks become a contention surface. Today there is no
  observability into lock wait time, lock-hold duration, or contention
  rate — failures manifest as 30s MaxElapsed exhaustion and
  resource_exhausted outcomes, with no telemetry to debug.

  The 2026-05-09 plan-review opus self-review identified this as a
  prerequisite for safely scaling up to N=2..4 parallel workers: without
  per-lock metrics, we cannot tell whether a 10s WithLock wait
  (lock.go:18-27 default) is approaching its budget under load, or
  whether 30s tracker-lock MaxElapsed (tracker_lock.go:51) is being
  exhausted by a long-tail of concurrent acquisitions vs occasional
  hot-path blocking.

ROOT CAUSE
  - cli/internal/bead/lock.go:18-27 WithLock has no instrumentation; it
    spins at 50ms intervals and waits up to 10s by default. Wait time is
    not measured or emitted.
  - cli/internal/bead/tracker_lock.go:105-183 withTrackerLock /
    withMainGitLock acquire/release path has no instrumentation.
  - There is no operator-facing dashboard, log, or metric for lock
    contention.

PROPOSED FIX
  Add lightweight metrics around three lock surfaces:

  1. bead.Store.WithLock (cli/internal/bead/lock.go:18-27):
     - Record lock-wait duration (time from WithLock entry to lock
       acquisition).
     - Record lock-hold duration (time the callback held the lock).
     - Emit via the existing agentmetrics package (or a new bead-metrics
       channel) keyed by call site.

  2. withTrackerLock / withMainGitLock (cli/internal/bead/tracker_lock.go:105-183):
     - Same wait/hold instrumentation.
     - Additional: record retry-attempt count when DefaultLockRetryPolicy
       is consumed (so we see "needed 3 retries" vs "got it on first
       attempt").

  3. Exit code / stop reason aggregation:
     - When a worker times out at MaxElapsed, capture the lock identity
       and the holder's claimant-PID at point of exhaustion. Today the
       error message is generic.

  Surface format:
     - Existing agentmetrics output (likely .ddx/agent-metrics or
       similar; check cli/internal/agentmetrics for existing API).
     - Or stdout JSON line per lock acquire/release if no agentmetrics
       sink exists.

  Add tests:
     - TestWithLock_RecordsWaitDuration: assert metric is captured for a
       contended lock.
     - TestTrackerLock_RecordsRetryCount: assert retry count metric is
       captured under simulated contention.

NON-SCOPE
  - Fixing lock contention itself (sister bead ddx-1f774edf removes the
    big contributor; this bead is observability for what's left).
  - Building a lock-contention dashboard (separate concern; just emit
    the data).
  - Reducing the 10s/30s budgets (those are correct; the metric tells
    us if they're tight).

INTERSECTIONS
  - Sister bead ddx-1f774edf (network-free Land()) drops the big
    contention cause; this bead provides visibility into what remains.
  - Sister bead ddx-c019e48a (chaos for stale-lock recovery) covers
    correctness; this bead covers visibility.
  - Sister bead (just-filed) "agent/chaos: cover concurrent-drain
    landing under shared-main contention" needs this metrics surface to
    write meaningful assertions.
title: agent/lock: instrument bead.Store WithLock wait time + tracker-lock acquisition metrics

description:
PROBLEM
ddx work --watch's pre-claim intake decoder rejects the readiness payload when a readiness_checks entry's `verdict` is a JSON bool, emitting `decode result: json: cannot unmarshal bool into Go struct field .readiness_checks.verdict of type string`. Under warn-only policy this skips every bead, idling a full fizeau queue (23 ready beads, 2026-05-18 05:27-05:39 UTC). The identical error fingerprint (15155a1c...) across distinct bead_ids confirms a producer/consumer schema mismatch, not a bead defect.

ROOT CAUSE
`cli/internal/agent/readiness_classification.go` — `preClaimReadinessCheck.Verdict` (struct at :75) bound `verdict` to a plain string, so `decodePreClaimIntakePayloadResultWithMode` (:688) and `decodePreClaimIntakePayloadResult` (:681) fail when the readiness producer emits `verdict:true`. A verdict may legitimately be a JSON bool, a JSON string (e.g. "fail"/"pass"/"ready"), or be omitted.

PROPOSED FIX
Give the field a dedicated `readinessVerdict` type (:91) with a custom UnmarshalJSON that accepts a JSON bool (coerced to a documented canonical lowercased string), a JSON string (trimmed), and JSON null/absent (empty), and rejects any other JSON kind with a descriptive error. Downstream comparisons in `failedReadinessReasons` (:823) and `readinessCheckEvidence` (:848) operate on the canonical lowercased string.

NON-SCOPE
Does NOT add the shared JSON schema or CI drift gate (covered by the schema-lock child). Does NOT change the worker same-fingerprint escalation (escalation child), the rolling claim-success-rate signal (claim-rate child), or README docs (docs child). Preserves the FEAT-010 / ADR-023 readiness vocabulary and cross-refs ddx-57c40485, ddx-8f2e0ebf, ddx-9714eaac.
title: pre-claim intake: decode readiness_checks[].verdict as JSON bool, string, or absent

description:
## Observed

Browsing the web UI to a document URL renders `Document not found` instead of content. The URL contains a worktree path with a leading double slash, e.g.:

  /nodes/<node>/projects/<proj>/documents//Users/erik/Projects/ddx/.claude/worktrees/agent-a0673989/docs/resources/agent-harness-ac.md

Two distinct defects:

1. **`.claude/worktrees/` pollution** — the documents list surfaces markdown files from AI agent worktrees checked out under `.claude/worktrees/`. These are throwaway copies of the repo; they are noise and frequently shadow / duplicate the real `docs/` tree.
2. **Absolute document paths** — document IDs/paths are absolute (`/Users/erik/...`), producing malformed URLs (leading double slash) and failing the reader resolver.

## Root cause

`cli/internal/docgraph/docgraph.go:247` (`findMarkdownFiles`) walks `workingDir` and only skips `.git` and `.ddx`. It traverses `.claude/` (including `.claude/worktrees/<agent>/…`) and records every `.md` it finds.

`cli/internal/docgraph/docgraph.go:128` stores `doc.Path = filepath.Clean(filePath)`. Because `filepath.Walk` hands back paths rooted at the absolute `workingDir`, `doc.Path` ends up absolute. The GraphQL document resolver surfaces this absolute path as the document's id/path, which the frontend then interpolates into a URL.

## Scope of fix

- Exclude `.claude/` (and any `worktrees/` subtree) from doc discovery. `.claude` is a tool-managed directory analogous to `.git`/`.ddx`; it is not a source of canonical project documents.
- Normalize `doc.Path` to be relative to `workingDir` so routes stay clean and portable.
- No change required on the frontend beyond existing URL handling once paths are relative.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-e19185aa is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
The decomposition action (currently invoked when a bead is too large for one execution and the agent splits it into child beads) is writing the parent's ID as a dep edge on every child. This produces an unbreakable deadlock:

  e29892a4 (parent, open) -- parent --> child_A
  e29892a4 -- parent --> child_B
  child_A.deps = [e29892a4]           <- BAD: parent is also a dep
  child_B.deps = [child_A, e29892a4]  <- BAD

The parent stays open until its children close. Every child is blocked on the parent. Nothing can be claimed. ddx work loops on the parent, the orchestrator emits 'mixed_commit_and_no_changes_rationale', the worker retries, and burns claim budget without progress.

Observed scenario (niflheim, 2026-06-04 04:30-05:13 UTC):
- Parent: niflheim-e29892a4 ('feat(delta): async write-behind ...')
- 10 children created during planning loops (23223661, a44a8ceb, 054c89b7, 0470ba0d, f10e9e35, f076b08c, 6c041162, 94e1df73, 9da62c2d, 5e4f9fb2)
- Every child carried deps=[..siblings.., niflheim-e29892a4]
- ~50 minutes of agent time + 4 strong-policy claude/opus attempts with zero feature commits; only tracker chores
- Unwedged manually by closing the parent via 'ddx bead close', after which siblings drained correctly in foundational order

Root cause is structural, not model-capability — auto-upgrading to a stronger model does NOT fix this. The orchestrator already detects the no-progress state but its only remediation is 'retry parent', which re-enters the same loop.

There is also a 'project root mutation rejected (continuing)' warning emitted by the readiness check during this state; that's a downstream symptom of the same problem, not the cause.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- Programmatic decomposition path (the action that fans a too-large bead into children) MUST NOT add the parent as a dep. Existing action templates / system prompts are audited and amended; one golden e2e test (decompose_does_not_self_dep) creates a bead with N children and asserts every child's deps set excludes the parent.
- 'ddx bead doctor' (existing subcommand) gains a check 'parent_ancestor_in_deps' that scans the tracker, lists violating beads, and (with --fix) removes the offending edges. Output is stable / scriptable. Test: ddx_doctor_detects_and_repairs_back_edge.
- ddx work no-progress remediation: when an attempted bead's outcome is 'mixed_commit_and_no_changes_rationale' AND any freshly-created child carries the attempted bead in its deps, ddx auto-emits an 'operator_attention' event with reason 'parent_back_edge' and stops re-claiming that bead. (Today it loops indefinitely.) Test: ddx_work_halts_on_parent_back_edge.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.
title: Reject bead dep edges that re-introduce the parent or any ancestor: part 2

description:
PROBLEM
Reviewer and repair attempts must be allowed to use stronger reasoning when the failure is capability-sensitive, but DDx must preserve ADR-024 by expressing that only as MinPower bounds rather than concrete model fallback. Current reviewer MinPower can collapse when implementer actual_power is missing.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go:661-664 sets reviewer minPower to impl.ActualPower + 1 only when ActualPower > 0; otherwise it leaves MinPowerOverride at 0.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go:148-152 SelectReviewerTier returns smart, but that tier choice is not enough if review dispatch uses MinPowerOverride=0 and no explicit smart/top floor.
- cli/cmd/agent_execute_loop_escalation.go:40-68 raises MinPower for primary attempts on selected statuses, but review/repair candidate-cycle routing does not yet have explicit power-floor policy.
- docs/helix/02-design/adr/ADR-024-power-escalation-and-review-routing.md:38-41 forbids DDx from choosing/substituting concrete models, so the fix must use Fizeau power bounds.

PROPOSED FIX
- Reviewer routing: if implementer ActualPower is known, request the next higher available floor; if missing/zero, request the configured smart/top review floor.
- Repair routing: for review_fixable_gap or capability-sensitive check failures, allow the coordinator to raise MinPower for the repair pass within MaxPower and sticky passthrough constraints.
- If passthrough constraints make the requested floor unsatisfiable, emit agent_power_unsatisfied or blocked_by_passthrough_constraint and stop without silent downgrade.
- Add tests using fake model catalogs / fizeau responses.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not implement concrete provider/model fallback chains.
- Do not change Fizeau internals.
- Do not enable two-slot review.

DEPS
Depends on repair loop so repair routing has a caller and on reviewer runtime/profile work so reviewer routing is explicit.

Body covers the core stance: favor real e2e tests (no mocks at e2e layer); stubs over mocks at unit layer; contract tests between stub and real backend; zero mocks in integration tests; behavior over implementation; deterministic factories; behavior-naming; testing pyramid as shape not ratios; performance measurements require baseline + explicit boundary + reproducible harness. grep -E "cli/internal/|docs/helix/|orchTestGitOps|fakeExecuteBeadGit|gateTestGitOps|mockExecutor|script\.go|integration_helper_test" library/personas/test-engineer.md returns no matches. description:
The existing library/personas/test-engineer-tdd.md is the strongest shipped persona content-wise, but it references DDx-internal paths that only exist in the DDx repo (docs/helix/01-frame/concerns.md, cli/internal/agent/script.go, named DDx legacy offenders like orchTestGitOps/fakeExecuteBeadGit/gateTestGitOps/mockExecutor).

Rename to library/personas/test-engineer.md and generalize.

**CORE STANCES (load-bearing — preserve these):**
- Favor real e2e tests. At the e2e layer, do not mock anything — real infrastructure, real processes, real network where applicable. E2e tests that mock the database or the HTTP layer are unit tests lying about their scope.
- Stubs over mocks at the unit layer. Extract interfaces at domain boundaries; write in-memory stubs that return canned values set up by the test. Stubs do not record call sequences.
- Contract tests between in-memory stubs and real backends — same suite runs against both, proving they are interchangeable. This is the discipline that keeps stubs honest.
- Zero mocks in integration tests. Use real git (temp dir with scrubbed env), real filesystem (t.TempDir), real database (temp file / temp container), real HTTP (local test server). The only approved fake is at the AI-provider (or equivalent third-party-SDK) boundary.
- Behavior over implementation — assert on observable state, not on call counts or invocation sequences.
- Deterministic factory functions / fakers over static JSON fixtures.
- Test names describe behavior ("creates invoice when all line items valid"), not positions ("test_create_invoice_3").
- Testing pyramid as a *shape guide* (more unit than integration than e2e), not as mandated ratios.
- **Performance measurements require a baseline and clear boundaries.** Any claim that something is "fast", "scales", or "improved performance" must include: (a) a numeric baseline to compare against (prior version, prior run, published SLO), (b) an explicit boundary — what unit of work is being measured, what environment, what is excluded (cold-start, warmup, network latency, etc.), (c) reproducible harness so the measurement can be re-run. "It feels fast" and "benchmarks look good" are not performance claims.

**STRIP (cargo-cult testing dogma — do NOT ship):**
- Hard coverage percentages as universal rules (">= 80% overall", "100% on critical paths"). Replace with: "measure coverage where the project tracks it; coverage is a signal, not a target".
- Specific timing budgets as universal rules ("unit < 10ms", "integration < 100ms"). Replace with: "tests should be fast enough that developers run them; the specific threshold is a project concern".
- Specific pyramid percentages ("60% unit / 25% integration / 10% contract / 5% e2e") — keep the shape, drop the numbers.
- TDD as the only valid approach. Test-first is one workflow; test-alongside is another; test-after for a specific reason can be defensible. Do not call non-TDD "worst practice".
- Tests-for-the-sake-of-tests (mirror-of-spec tests that add no signal, trivial getters/setters).
- Mutation testing as a quality requirement. Mention as an optional signal, not a bar to clear.
- Snapshot tests without a maintenance plan.
- Retry loops around flaky tests as "improvement" — a retry loop hides a bug; fix the flake.
- Branch coverage vs line coverage dogma — say "coverage metrics matter less than whether tests catch real bugs".

**STRIP (DDx-internal specifics):**
- References to cli/internal/agent/script.go (replace with generic "a deterministic script-like fake at the AI-provider boundary")
- Named DDx legacy offenders (orchTestGitOps, fakeExecuteBeadGit, gateTestGitOps, mockExecutor) — these belong in a helix-test-engineer plugin persona, not this generic base
- Authoritative-sources frontmatter section citing docs/helix/concerns.md and HELIX concern.md
- Specific paths like cli/internal/bead, cli/internal/agent

Ground in external canon:
- Kent Beck - Test-Driven Development: By Example
- Martin Fowler - "Mocks Arent Stubs" (canonical reference for why call-sequence assertions are a code smell)
- Brendan Gregg - Systems Performance methodology (for the baseline + boundary stance on perf measurement)
- Anthropic Prompt Library (if a testing entry exists)
- TDD Guard from anthropics/skills repo (if the automated-test-first-enforcement pattern is worth mentioning)

Body structure: Philosophy / Approach / Anti-patterns / Sources.

description:
PROBLEM
  cli/cmd/testutils_test.go GetTestLibraryPath uses a sync.Once package-level
  helper that creates /tmp/.test-library (working repo) and /tmp/.test-library.git
  (bare repo) and never registers cleanup. These directories accumulate on the
  developer's machine permanently because there is no t.Cleanup, defer
  os.RemoveAll, or trap-style teardown anywhere in the chain. Discovered by
  the 2026-05-09 test-cleanup audit.

ROOT CAUSE
  - cli/cmd/testutils_test.go:88-90 hardcodes:
      workingRepo := filepath.Join(tempBase, ".test-library")
      bareRepo    := filepath.Join(tempBase, ".test-library.git")
      testLibraryPath = bareRepo
  - tempBase falls through to "/tmp" when TMP and TMPDIR are unset, so on
    a vanilla `go test ./cmd/...` invocation without TestMain in scope (or
    with env vars cleared by a shell wrapper) the dirs land at literal
    /tmp/.test-library and /tmp/.test-library.git.
  - There is no os.RemoveAll, no t.Cleanup hook, and the sync.Once design
    is explicitly intended to "reuse across runs" — making the leak
    architectural rather than a forgotten cleanup.
  - cli/cmd/testutils_test.go isolateCmdTestTempRoot only redirects TMPDIR
    inside TestMain; if any subtest or parallel package calls
    GetTestLibraryPath before TestMain has fired (e.g. independent test
    binaries) the /tmp literal wins.

PROPOSED FIX
  - Delete the package-level sync.Once shared-fixture pattern.
  - Each call site that needs a fresh ddx-initialized repo should call
    cli/internal/testutils.NewFixtureRepo(t, "standard") (already exists,
    auto-registers t.Cleanup, uses scripts/build-fixture-repo.sh under the
    hood per CLAUDE.md).
  - For tests that genuinely need a shared bare repo within ONE package's
    run, build it under t.TempDir() in a TestMain helper that registers
    cleanup via the returned func from func TestMain(m *testing.M).
  - Remove tempBase env var detection now that t.TempDir() is in use.

NON-SCOPE
  - Migrating other test packages that use their own private fixtures.
    This bead is scoped to GetTestLibraryPath and its callers in cli/cmd/.
  - Performance optimization (reusing fixtures across tests within one
    package via TestMain is fine; cross-process reuse is what's banned).
  - Frontend test cleanup.

INTERSECTIONS
  - testutils.NewFixtureRepo (cli/internal/testutils/) is the canonical
    replacement. CLAUDE.md already documents it as the preferred path.
title: tests: replace shared /tmp/.test-library fixture with t.TempDir-scoped repo

description:
PROBLEM
A project can have `desired_count=1` with no live worker after the last server-managed worker exited from fd exhaustion. `ddx work status --all-projects` only reports live workers, while `ddx worker status` reports desired state but not why the desired worker is missing. Operators cannot see that the last terminal worker exited due to fd exhaustion.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/cmd/work_status.go:80-115 builds status from live worker scans and active work only.
cli/cmd/work_status.go:215-221 prints `No live ddx workers...` when no workers are present, with no desired-state or last-terminal reason.
cli/cmd/worker.go:121-158 reads `.ddx/workers/desired.json` and prints desired_count/restart state, but does not consult terminal worker history or last failure reason.
cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:351-389 records terminal worker history for restart accounting, but that diagnosis is not exposed in the operator-facing desired-worker status path.

PROPOSED FIX
Add an operator-visible diagnostic to the worker status surface for desired workers that are missing because their last terminal event/result was fd exhaustion. Include the diagnosis in text and JSON output, preserving existing live-worker output. Use the structured fd-exhaustion fields emitted by the agent/server path rather than brittle string matching where possible.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken byte/inode resource guards. Do not change bead claim semantics. Do not remove the existing supervisor stale-operator-attention fixes tracked by ddx-b17cad6d and ddx-4d92f2cf. Do not implement the low-level EMFILE classifier in this bead except as needed by tests/fixtures.

description:
PROBLEM
  .gitignore lines 438-445 explicitly UN-IGNORE several file types
  inside .ddx/executions/, forcing every per-attempt evidence dir
  into git. This was a deliberate choice to make execution evidence
  durable — but it has produced 12,096 tracked files (52% of the
  repo) with no retention bound.

  The events stream is already externalized to .ddx/attachments/
  per the existing migrate path. That's the durable audit trail.
  The per-attempt prompt.md / result.json / manifest.json
  duplicate evidence in git are working state — like node_modules,
  per-machine, recreatable.

  After sister bead "feat(executions): wire RetainDays" lands and
  bounds the in-tree dir count, this bead completes the cleanup by
  removing the un-ignore lines so future attempt dirs are NOT
  tracked in git AT ALL. Existing tracked dirs are removed via
  git rm --cached -r.

CURRENT STATE
  - .gitignore:438-445:
        # Allow tracked execution evidence
        !.ddx/executions/
        !.ddx/executions/*/
        !.ddx/executions/*/prompt.md
        !.ddx/executions/*/manifest.json
        !.ddx/executions/*/result.json
        !.ddx/executions/*/usage.json
        !.ddx/executions/*/checks.json
  - These un-ignores override the broader .ddx/ ignore pattern.
  - Without them, .ddx/executions/ would be untracked.

PROPOSED FIX
  - .gitignore: delete lines 438-445 (the un-ignore allow-list
    for execution evidence file types).
  - Add a single explicit ignore line:
        .ddx/executions/
  - Run `git rm --cached -r .ddx/executions/` to remove all
    currently-tracked execution dirs from the index (they remain
    on disk).
  - Update CLAUDE.md to reflect: .ddx/executions/ is now untracked
    working state, like node_modules. The events stream in
    .ddx/attachments/ is the durable audit.
  - Verify the pre-commit / pre-push hooks still pass after the
    change.

NON-SCOPE
  - Migrating evidence to a mirror backend (sister bead).
  - Implementing retention (sister bead).

    that may need updating.

INTERSECTIONS

description:
# PROBLEM
An operator's uncommitted edit in the project-root checkout was silently reverted by a concurrent worker land. Timeline on eitri 2026-07-06 (all EDT): ~12:54 operator edits cli/internal/agent/route_harness_liveness_unix_test.go (adds a testing.Short skip); ~12:55 operator verifies the edit via go test (SKIP observed, proving the edit was on disk); ~12:56 the ddx worker lands tracker update 5e7002081 (execute-bead 20260706T161637); 12:56:59 the operator's git commit 942f901ca lands EMPTY — the working tree had been reset to HEAD, the edit was gone, and git add staged nothing. No stash, no backup, no event was produced; the operator had to reapply the change from memory (ecbc6747e).

# ROOT CAUSE (to verify)
The land path's project-root checkout synchronization (SyncWorkTreeToHead / the land-checkout-sync introduced or exercised by the tracker-sync feature, cli/internal/agent/tracker_sync.go landed at c93d3641d, plus the pre-existing land advancer) resets files not covered by its dirty-overlap deferral check. TestLand_SyncDeferredWhenOperatorCheckoutDirtyOverlap only defers when the dirty path OVERLAPS the landed diff; a dirty path OUTSIDE the landed diff appears to be reset to HEAD instead of being left untouched. Verify by reproducing: dirty file X (not in landed diff) + land of unrelated diff -> X's modification must survive.

# PROPOSED FIX
The checkout-sync must never discard local modifications, overlapping or not: restrict sync to paths actually changed by the landed merge (git checkout HEAD -- <landed paths> semantics), and hard-defer (or stash with provenance) whenever ANY tracked path is locally modified. A destroyed operator edit is silent data loss — strictly worse than a deferred sync.

# NON-SCOPE
Claim-boundary tracker sync semantics (fetch/merge/push, ddx-739ce984 — correct); the empty-commit UX of git itself.

Parent: ddx-9f21457d. No deps.

Old-contract tests rewritten. AC1 covered by TestLand_SyncPreservesRacingOperatorEdit + TestLand_DirtyProjectRootDoesNotBlockSuccessfulLand; AC2 by design (no reset paths remain; checkpoint commits instead) + TestWaitForEmptyGitIndex_PreservesOperatorWork; AC3 chaos suite green. Full internal/agent suite green 635s on loaded host.

acceptance:
**User story:** As a developer running `go test`, my test runs do not leave behind registered projects in my real `~/.local/share/ddx/server-state.json`. When a machine has already been polluted, I can prune it with one command. The server sweep is aggressive enough that obvious test-dir pollution does not survive a restart.

**Acceptance criteria:**

1. **Fix A — test isolation enforced by CI.**
   - Every existing test that instantiates `ServerState` or boots a server helper is migrated to an isolated state dir. No test writes to `~/.local/share/ddx/server-state.json`.
   - A lint test (Go or shell) parses `cli/internal/server/**/*_test.go` (and any other directories that wire up `ServerState`) and fails if it finds a construction that does not pass an explicit isolated state path or override `XDG_DATA_HOME` first. Test cases added for both the allowed-pattern and the disallowed-pattern.

2. **Fix B — sweep recognizes test-dir pollution.**
   - `ServerState.migrate` drops entries whose `Path` matches any of:
     - prefix `/tmp/`, `/private/tmp/`, `/var/folders/`
     - regex `/Test[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]*\d+/` anywhere in the path
