acceptance:
1. A transient .git/index.lock contention failure during the durable-audit/tracker commit does NOT exit the worker: it is classified transient, the bead is released, and the drain loop continues. Verified by a new test (e.g. TestWork_IndexLockContentionDuringAuditCommitIsTransientNotFatal in cli/internal/agent) that injects an index.lock failure on the tracker/audit commit and asserts the worker continues rather than returning the operator-attention exit.
2. A genuine, non-lock git failure during the audit commit still surfaces as operator attention (regression).
3. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... green.
4. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
Under multi-worker operation, a ddx work worker EXITS with "operator attention required: DDx could not commit durable audit outputs; resolve the git failure before continuing autonomous work" when the durable-audit/tracker commit hits transient .git/index.lock contention. Observed 2026-05-27: with 2 ddx workers + a fizeau worker + the server sharing one project .git, a worker died on `git add` tracker -> ".git/index.lock: File exists ... no owner found but lock is fresh (age 19s < 30s)". A transient lock conflict stops the whole worker; the more workers, the more often this fires, directly defeating unattended steady-state drain.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- git .git/index.lock carries no pid, so gitlock.IndexLockOwner finds no owner. RecoverGitIndexLock (cli/internal/gitlock/gitlock.go:144-158) only reaps an ownerless lock once age >= StaleAge (30s, gitlock.go:26); below that it returns Removed=false ("no owner found but lock is fresh").
- RunGitWithIndexLockRecovery retries only RecoveryAttempts=3 (gitlock.go:30) with LiveOwnerWait=500ms (gitlock.go:34) ~= 1.5s total, far short of the 30s reap floor, then returns the index.lock error.
- commitTrackerLocked (cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2153) calls runGitWithIndexLockRecovery for `git add`; its error becomes "staging tracker: ...". That propagates to the durable-audit-commit exit at cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1175, which stops the worker (operator attention) instead of treating transient lock contention as retryable.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Do NOT exit the drain on transient .git/index.lock contention during the durable-audit/tracker commit. Classify index.lock contention as transient (mirroring the pre-claim tracker-contention class from ddx-df77e668), release the bead, and continue the loop so the next iteration retries. A transient lock must never stop a worker.
2. AND/OR raise the recovery patience for tracker/audit commits to a bounded backoff that can outlast typical contention (up to ~the StaleAge window) before failing.
3. Optional: reap a provably-orphaned lock sooner (e.g. confirm no live git holds the repo via lsof) while keeping the 30s floor when liveness is unknown.
Recommend (1) as the primary fix: transient lock contention is retryable, not operator-attention-worthy.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not weaken safety against removing a live git process index.lock.
- Do not change the landing-path read-tree retry (already has backoff, ddx-7e659c95).

CROSS-REF: same multi-worker-resilience theme as ddx-57c40485 (lock scoping) and ddx-df77e668 (pre-claim tracker-contention). This is the post-fix gap on the COMMIT side.
notes: Already fixed by operator direct-fix (bootstrap-hostile to dogfood): transient index.lock during durable-audit commit now classified retryable via gitlock.IsIndexLockError, worker continues instead of exiting. Landed 48631b2ed; TestWork_IndexLockContentionDuringAuditCommitIsTransientNotFatal + regression pass; full internal/agent gate green; reinstalled.
title: execute-bead: worker exits on transient index.lock contention during durable-audit commit instead of retrying — kills unattended multi-worker drain

description:
PROBLEM: Restarting the DDx user service during active supervised work can hang until systemd times out, leaving systemd to SIGKILL server child processes. Live evidence from 2026-07-07 03:05:19 EDT: `ddx server stop` did not return until systemd marked `ddx-server.service` failed with `Result: timeout` and killed leftover git subprocesses, interrupting the Axon worker attempt that was in post-execution handling.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE: `cli/internal/server/server.go:379-385` cancels the supervisor and then waits on `supervisorDone` with no timeout. Worker cleanup is only reached afterward at `cli/internal/server/server.go:388-395`. The worker shutdown path itself has a bounded wait (`cli/internal/server/workers.go:1696-1703`), but it is unreachable while the supervisor goroutine is stuck in a reconcile/git operation. The installed systemd unit generated from `cli/cmd/server_service.go:26-42` has no explicit stop timeout or ExecStop mitigation, so the default systemd timeout eventually kills the whole cgroup.

PROPOSED FIX: Make server shutdown bounded and ordered so worker cleanup always runs promptly even when supervisor reconciliation is slow or stuck. A good implementation is to cancel the supervisor, wait only a short bounded grace for `supervisorDone`, continue to `supervisorRegistry.Shutdown()` / `workers.Shutdown()` on timeout, and surface/log the supervisor timeout without preventing worker cleanup.

NON-SCOPE: Do not rewrite worker execution semantics, change bead claim/lease policy, or alter unrelated service install behavior.

Parent: none. Dependencies: none.

description:
PROBLEM
A server-managed worker must be fully cleanable. Stop, watchdog reap, restart, and server shutdown must not leave ddx work, claude, codex, shell, or sleep descendants behind.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/server/workers.go:192 says WorkerManager manages in-process work workers as goroutines. cli/internal/server/workers.go:438 creates a cancelable context, but no OS process boundary. cli/internal/server/workers.go:1234 reads WorkerRecord.PID and :1282-1286 terminates a process group only when pid > 0. cli/internal/server/workers.go:1453-1457 has the same limitation in watchdog reap. Because server-owned workers are often goroutines with PID zero, the server cannot guarantee child harness cleanup.

PROPOSED FIX
Introduce a server-managed process boundary. Preferred implementation: spawn a child ddx work --server-managed <worker-id> in its own process group and record PID/PGID in WorkerRecord. If a transitional in-process path remains for tests, every harness child process group must be registered on the worker handle and killed through the same cleanup helper. Stop/reap/shutdown should send SIGTERM, wait WatchdogKillGrace, SIGKILL remaining descendants, release bead claims, persist terminal status, and be idempotent.

NON-SCOPE
Do not kill external reported workers or interactive Claude/Codex sessions. Do not change bead claim semantics except releasing claims for the stopped/reaped managed worker. Do not implement UI controls.

description:
PROBLEM
BLOCKING for any non-localhost write enablement. In the coordinator topology (Story 14), the originating peer identity attestation is not forwarded from coordinator to client — any non-localhost write goes through the hub without carrying who initiated it. The spoke cannot authorize on both origin and coordinator identity because neither is transmitted.

ROOT CAUSE
- cli/internal/federation/fanout.go: current federation supports query fan-out only. No RouteMutationToProjectOwner, no ForwardMutation, no identity header propagation.
- Risk ('Multi-node authorization gap'): A compromised or misconfigured hub can forward mutations on behalf of any origin, with the spoke unable to distinguish legitimate coordinator-forwarded requests from hub-originated attacks. Without dual authorization, spoke trusts the hub implicitly.
- The /tmp/story-15-final.md plan file cited in the original bead is ephemeral and not available to sub-agents on other machines; relevant content is inlined below.

PLAN-LOCKED DECISIONS (from story-15 planning):
- Multi-node routing (point 6): hub picks single owning spoke by project ID from FederationRegistry; no broadcast of mutations.
- Identity forwarding: X-DDx-Origin-Identity = verified WhoIs peer at coordinator edge (NOT coordinator self); X-DDx-Coordinator-Identity = hub's own attested identity. Both mandatory on forwarded mutations.
- Dual authorization on spoke: requireTrusted augmented to check BOTH origin (WhoIs / loopback policy) AND coordinator (registered federation hub); 403 if either fails.

description:
PROBLEM
`ExecuteBeadResult.ResultRev` is overloaded. Depending on where the caller observes it, the field can mean the worker implementation commit, a merge commit, or the trailing evidence commit. That makes candidate review, landing, replay, server state, and UI drill-down ambiguous.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE

description:
The embedded 'agent' harness can complete a task successfully (commit produced, tests pass) but then fail to terminate, getting stuck in a compaction retry loop with compaction always failing. The parent work never observes task_succeeded and hangs forever.

## Observed

Running 'ddx agent work --once --local --harness agent --model qwen/qwen3-coder-next' against axon-43ed769b (axon auth-core-types bead):

1. qwen3-coder-next ran the task correctly, producing commit 91d4bdb with 636 LOC of types + 109 green tests + clippy clean. The commit was present in the worktree at /tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-axon-43ed769b-20260415T005652-ebe7a16a.

2. Instead of terminating, the agent kept generating events. After ~20 minutes the session log was 33 MB (8461+ events, 249 messages) and stuck in:

    {"type":"compaction.start",...}
    {"type":"compaction.end",...,"data":{"messages_after":249,"messages_before":249,"no_compaction":true,"success":false}}
    {"type":"compaction.start",...}
    {"type":"compaction.end",...,"data":{"messages_after":249,"messages_before":249,"no_compaction":true,"success":false}}
    ...

3. Parent ddx process in __futex_wait. Had to SIGTERM the parent (PID 4141811) and manually fast-forward-merge the worktree commit to land the work.

4. A1 (previous bead) ran the same harness/model and terminated correctly in ~14 min with identical-looking commit shape. The difference was bead size: A2's output was a single 633-line Rust file, vs A1's 350-line SQL + 290-line test file. A2 didn't exceed what A1 did — so the context-limit explanation doesn't fully account for it.

## Expected

- After the agent commits and has nothing more to do, it should emit task_succeeded and terminate
- Compaction should either succeed (messages_after < messages_before) or bail out cleanly, not retry indefinitely
- If the context genuinely cannot be compacted, the agent should report a structured failure and preserve the commits, not spin

## Scope

- Detect mid-turn compaction returning success=false repeatedly and bail with a structured 'compaction_stuck' status
- Bound the total number of compaction attempts in a single turn
- Ensure task termination happens immediately after a successful commit + no pending tool calls
- Add a watchdog at the work level: kill the child if no commit+progress event is observed within a budget

## Evidence

- Session log: /Users/erik/Projects/axon/.ddx/executions/20260415T005652-ebe7a16a/embedded/agent-1776214612561376672.jsonl (33 MB)
- Rescued commit: 91d4bdb on axon master
- Parent process: PID 4141811 (killed)

## Acceptance

- [ ] Compaction retry loop is bounded and fails structurally
- [ ] Post-commit termination path is deterministic
- [ ] Watchdog detects and terminates stuck sessions with a preserved-commit outcome
- [ ] Regression test reproduces the stuck state (seeded session with large no-op tool calls)
title: bug: embedded agent stalls in post-commit compaction loop

description:
PROBLEM: Running 2 concurrent ddx workers on the same project, tracker/audit commits repeatedly fail with 'fatal: unable to write new index file: exit status 128' and 'Unable to create .git/index.lock: File exists'. This fails attempts and eventually trips the resource_exhausted breaker (worker exits), throttling the multi-worker drain. Observed continuously this session in the ddx worker logs.
ROOT CAUSE: tracker commits and durable-audit-output commits run git add/commit against the MAIN working tree's shared .git/index. Workers serialize via .ddx/.git-tracker.lock, but the underlying git index.lock still collides — the tracker lock does not cover the full git index mutation window, OR the durable-audit-commit path runs outside the tracker lock. Prior lock-scoping beads (ddx-329a08b8, ddx-90d41915, ddx-23ac2796, ddx-0b743e7e, ddx-57c40485) are CLOSED but the collision persists.
PROPOSED FIX: close the remaining gap so concurrent main-repo index mutations never collide — e.g. hold a single per-project index mutex across the entire add+commit window for tracker + durable-audit + land, OR commit tracker/audit via a dedicated index (GIT_INDEX_FILE) so they never touch the shared working-tree index.

description:
Discovered 2026-04-15 while attempting to route tier:local tagged beads to vidar-coder. ddx-agent providers listed vidar as "connected (8 models)" based on GET /v1/models responding successfully, but the actual chat/completions call returned:

400 Bad Request {
  "message": "No models loaded. Please load a model in the developer page or use the 'lms load' command.",
  "type": "invalid_request_error",
  "param": "model",
  "code": null
}

Root cause: LM Studio /v1/models returns models available to load, not models currently in memory. An inference call to an unloaded model fails. The providers status "connected (N models)" is therefore a weak liveness signal — it proves the HTTP server is up but not that inference is ready.

Impact on cost-tiered routing (bead ddx-dc231144 tier-based auto-escalation): the policy will mis-route work to providers that SEEM available but immediately fail on chat/completions. Every failed attempt burns time + forces escalation, defeating the cost optimization.

Fix: probing should attempt a tiny inference call (e.g. "Reply with OK") against the configured model with a short timeout. Providers that fail this probe are marked unavailable even if /v1/models responds.

Alternative: parse LM Studio specific responses or add a /v1/status-like endpoint probe when the provider type is lmstudio.

Scope:
- Update routing/health probe in cmd/ddx-agent/routing.go (or equivalent) to perform tiny inference probe instead of (or in addition to) models list
- Bound probe to short timeout (e.g. 3s) and ~20 tokens max
- Cache probe results per provider for a short TTL to avoid probing on every route decision
- Surface the distinction in ddx agent providers output: "connected" vs "inference-ready"

description:
PROBLEM: When a `ddx try`/`ddx work` attempt fails with any non-success
outcome (`provider_connectivity`, `no_evidence_produced`, `execution_failed`,
`structural_validation_failed`, `land_conflict`, `post_run_check_failed`),
its execute-bead worktree under `~/.cache/ddx/exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-<bead>-<attemptID>/`
is not removed. Cleanup happens only when a *subsequent attempt of the same bead*
is launched and `RecoverOrphans` runs as pre-spawn sweep.

OBSERVED 2026-05-28 in niflheim drain: a 6.6 GB worktree
`.execute-bead-wt-niflheim-07f6f8ff-20260528T164209-f179349f` remained 9+
hours after its attempt failed with `provider_connectivity` (bragi 502).
The bead's retry resolved as `already_satisfied` without spawning a new
execute-bead worktree (the AC was already met by partially-landed commits
from the failed attempt), so `RecoverOrphans` was never called for that
bead — the leak is permanent until another attempt at the same bead runs.

The user reports seeing this pattern consistently across drains, not just
on the one observed bead.

ROOT CAUSE: `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_orchestrator.go:393-411`
defines `RecoverOrphans` with the docstring "the parent's responsibility —
call it before spawning new workers so stale worktrees from crashed previous
attempts do not accumulate." The function matches strictly by
`basenamePrefix := ExecuteBeadWtPrefix + beadID + "-"` and is only invoked
on a new-attempt pre-spawn path. Two leak conditions follow:

  (a) Bead's retry succeeds via `already_satisfied` (no new worktree
      spawned because the AC check resolves before agent invocation).
      The orphan from the prior failed attempt is never matched.
  (b) Bead is closed for any reason after a failed attempt and is never
      re-attempted (most common in real flows — failures often resolve
      via decomposition into different child beads, never returning to
      the original).

The post-attempt outcome classifier at
`cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1966` (Classify worker outcome:
task_succeeded / task_failed / task_no_changes / ...) is the natural place
to call `WorktreeRemove` for non-success classes, but does not.
The existing landing path at
`cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:1088,1329,1679` calls
`gitOps.RemoveWorktree` correctly for landing-time temp worktrees, but
those are different (per-landing) worktrees, not the per-attempt execute-bead
worktree under `~/.cache/ddx/exec-wt/`.

PROPOSED FIX: Add an attempt-finalize cleanup hook that runs after outcome
classification (around `execute_bead.go:1966-2017`) and removes the
per-attempt execute-bead worktree when the outcome is anything other than
`task_succeeded`. Preserve only when:
  1. The operator explicitly opted in via `ddx try --no-merge` (preserve
     for inspection regardless of outcome).
  2. An `executions_mirror.go` write or evidence-capture step requires the
     worktree to persist past classification (verify by reading the call
     chain at `execute_bead.go:2069-2114`).

Implementation steps the executing agent should follow:
  1. Read `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1423-2017` to confirm the
     outcome-classification flow and identify the right post-classify hook
     point.
  2. Add a helper `cleanupAttemptWorktree(gitOps, workDir, wtPath, outcome,
     preserveFlag)` that calls `gitOps.WorktreeRemove(workDir, wtPath)` for
     non-success outcomes unless `preserveFlag` is set.
  3. Wire it into the outcome-classification path.
  4. Add a unit test asserting the cleanup branch for each non-success
     outcome class, and a negative test confirming success-path keeps the
     worktree (landing path owns that cleanup).
  5. Update `RecoverOrphans` docstring to reflect that it's now a
     belt-and-suspenders sweep, not the primary cleanup path.

NON-SCOPE:
- Changing `RecoverOrphans` behavior or call sites (keep it; it covers
  hard-crash cases the new hook can't reach).
- Adding a periodic background sweeper or `ddx doctor` flag for stale
  worktrees (potential follow-up).
- Changing the worktree path under `~/.cache/ddx/exec-wt/`.
- Changing outcome-classification logic or outcome taxonomy.
- Adding telemetry/metrics for leak rates.

IN-SCOPE FILES:
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go (add the cleanup hook + helper)
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_test.go or sibling _test file (add
  cleanup tests for each non-success outcome)
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_orchestrator.go (docstring update on
  RecoverOrphans only; behavior unchanged)

OUT-OF-SCOPE FILES:
- execute_bead_land.go — landing-time temp-worktree cleanup is correct
  and untouched.
- Any code under cli/cmd/ — no CLI surface change required.
- docs/ — documentation update is downstream of the spec-evolution bead
  ddx-828a1b8f (worktree resource isolation) and not required here.

description:
Fourth child of ddx-b7ee0d6f. .ddx/beads.jsonl is a git-tracked mutable ledger. Multiple writers on different machines or in parallel worker processes produce divergent files that require manual textual merge. git merge can sometimes append-merge JSONL cleanly if each side touches disjoint lines, but when both sides touch the same bead (claim / close / add-event), the merge is semantically broken even when git reports it as resolved.

## Evidence

On axon, eitri and sindri both wrote to beads.jsonl independently for 14 days. Local has 134 commits touching the tracker; origin has 336. When I tried to rebase my planning commit onto origin, git reported conflicts in .ddx/beads.jsonl — and these conflicts would have been 'resolved' by git's textual merge logic even when the semantic outcome is wrong (e.g. two machines claiming the same bead with different claimed-machine values).

The existing work help text says:

    By default work submits to the running ddx server as a background
    worker and returns immediately. Use --local to run inline in the current
    process.

So a ddx server EXISTS and is supposed to coordinate. But .ddx/beads.jsonl is still the ledger, which means the server is not the source of truth — it's just a submission surface. The git-tracked file is authoritative, and that's what's racing.

## Options (pick one during implementation)

**A. Server-authoritative tracker.** When the ddx server is running, it owns beads.jsonl. All reads and writes go through the server's API. The git-tracked file becomes a periodic snapshot for backup/offline use, not the source of truth. Workers on multiple machines talk to a shared server.

**B. CRDT append-only log.** Replace the current representation with an append-only log keyed by (machine_id, bead_id, sequence, timestamp). Each writer appends to its own partition; readers compute the effective state by merging partitions with a conflict-resolution rule (last-writer-wins per (bead_id, field), or better). git textual merge of the partitioned log is always safe because writers never share lines.

**C. Per-bead lock files with atomic rename.** Each bead mutation acquires a lock file (beads/<id>.lock), writes beads/<id>.json atomically via rename, releases the lock. The JSONL aggregate is regenerated from per-bead files. Git tracks per-bead files, not the aggregate. Safe across local parallelism but not across machines without network coordination.

**Recommendation**: A is the cleanest if the ddx server is already deployed as authoritative infrastructure. B is the best fit for the current decentralized model. C is a stopgap that solves intra-machine parallelism but not multi-machine drift.

## Scope note

Do NOT conflate this bead with the fetch/push/rebase triad (ddx-bd42f640, ddx-83ec1430, ddx-6aa50e57). Those three fix the git-level divergence; this bead fixes the tracker-level divergence. Both are needed — the triad without tracker safety would still produce semantically-conflicting beads.jsonl merges even when the underlying git history is linear.

## Test cases

- Two workers on the same machine claim different beads concurrently: both claims persist correctly
- Two workers on different machines claim different beads concurrently: both claims persist correctly (requires network coordination)
- Two workers attempt to claim the same bead: one wins, the other sees 'already claimed' and picks a different one
- Recovery from crash between claim and CloseWithEvidence: the bead returns to unclaimed after a heartbeat timeout
- Tracker state is deterministic from any valid ordering of concurrent writes (CRDT option)
title: work: .ddx/beads.jsonl concurrent-write safety

description:
# PROBLEM
Every bead close in production records `review_status: skipped, review_skip_reason: review_not_configured` — the strong-model / cross-provider review ladder never fires. Live evidence from eitri 2026-07-06: ddx-a6e99ad3 (implemented by claude/sonnet, .ddx/executions/20260706T010735-b8f37b75/result.json) and ddx-c8506158 (implemented by codex/gpt-5.4-mini via server-managed worker, .ddx/executions/20260706T014520-dd22d724/result.json) both show cycle_trace[0].review_status=skipped despite review being 'on by default' per ddx try --help. No review/review-error/review-pairing-degraded events exist in either bead's attachments events.jsonl.

# ROOT CAUSE
Two disconnected wirings, both dead:
1. The production close path is owned by the candidate-cycle reviewer, but the AttemptCycleCoordinator constructed at cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:362 omits the Reviewer field — and cli/internal/agent/candidate_cycle.go:208 documents `Reviewer CandidateReviewer // nil → skip candidate review (future)`. The 'future' was never wired.
2. The legacy post-merge reviewer (RunPostMergeReview, cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_post_review.go:86) is gated behind `runtime.PostMergeReview` (cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:151, checked at :3903) — a repo-wide grep shows NO caller ever sets it. The DefaultBeadReviewer that cmd/try.go:262 and cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:267 construct is therefore never consulted.

The reviewer machinery itself is complete and correct for the cost-tier goal: reviewerDispatchProfile (execute_bead_review.go:868) floors reviewer MinPower at implementer ActualPower+1, escalates one ladder step per prior review error, selects the strongest satisfiable profile, and emits review-pairing-degraded when the reviewer resolves to the implementer's provider (cross-provider pairing intent, execute_bead_review.go:800-803). It is simply unreachable.

# PROPOSED FIX
Wire a CandidateReviewer adapter over DefaultBeadReviewer into the AttemptCycleCoordinator at execute_bead.go:362 (plumb runtime.Reviewer / spec.ReviewHarness / spec.ReviewModel through executeCandidateCycle), honoring NoReview and review:skip labels. Alternatively (implementer's choice) set runtime.PostMergeReview=true when a Reviewer is configured — but prefer the candidate-cycle wiring since the close path comment (execute_bead_loop.go:3901-3903) declares candidate-cycle review the owner. Remove or deprecate whichever path is not chosen so the audit cannot silently report review_not_configured while a reviewer is configured.

# NON-SCOPE
- Changing reviewer power-ladder policy or provider-pairing policy (already correct in execute_bead_review.go).
- ddx bead review CLI (manual review path works).

Related: ddx-57faa17c, ddx-a6e99ad3 (their closes are the live evidence). No deps.

description:
PROBLEM
ExecuteLoopSpec fields are declared in parallel structs across three independent code sites. When a flag or worker mode is added to cobra, the developer must also update the REST handler request struct in server.go and the GraphQL adapter request struct in graphql_adapters.go; missing one silently drops the field at runtime. The new work-loop contract requires one vocabulary across CLI parsing, worker persistence, REST, and GraphQL: mode plus idle_interval, with no public compatibility alias for the removed polling flag.

ROOT CAUSE
Each work field traverses six independent declaration points with no compile-time linkage:

1. cobra flag extraction plus local vars: cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go:1582-1605 extracts fromRev, harness, model, profile, provider, modelRef, effort, once/watch mode, idleInterval, noReview, reviewHarness, reviewModel, maxCostUSD, requestTimeout, minPower, and maxPower as naked locals.

2. positional-param pass-down: cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go:1744-1773 closes over these locals and assembles config.CLIOverrides by hand; no single struct groups them.

3. ExecuteLoopWorkerSpec definition: cli/internal/server/workers.go:25-49 is hand-maintained in parallel with cobra and has historically missed fields.

4. handleStartExecuteLoopWorker request struct: cli/internal/server/server.go:2395-2409 is a separate anonymous struct, so newly added fields can be silently lost for server-spawned workers.

5. StartExecuteLoop literal: cli/internal/server/server.go:2441-2455 plus cli/internal/server/workers.go:345-361 hand-assembles the worker spec; any field absent in step 4 cannot appear here.

6. GraphQL adapter request struct plus StartExecuteLoop literal: cli/internal/server/graphql_adapters.go:63-76 plus 127-141 is a third parallel declaration; fixes to REST can leave GraphQL broken.

The consumer (cli/internal/server/workers.go:658-926 runWorker) reads MaxCostUSD from escalation.DefaultMaxCostUSD hardcoded (line ~753) instead of spec.MaxCostUSD because the field was never plumbed through. OpaquePassthrough has two validation skip gates that must both fire (workers.go:357-361 and the ValidateForExecuteLoopViaService branch in runWorker).

PROPOSED FIX
- cli/internal/agent/spec.go or cli/internal/agent/executeloop/spec.go: define ExecuteLoopSpec with all fields currently spread across the six layers. Fields: ProjectRoot, Harness, Model, Profile, Provider, ModelRef, Effort, LabelFilter, Mode, IdleInterval, NoReview, ReviewHarness, ReviewModel, OpaquePassthrough, MaxCostUSD, RequestTimeout, MinPower, MaxPower, FromRev, SpecVersion int. JSON tags drive both REST wire format and disk persistence.
- Mode is the canonical once/drain/watch selector. CLI --once maps to Mode=once. CLI --watch maps to Mode=watch. Default is Mode=drain.
- IdleInterval is meaningful only for Mode=watch. --idle-interval without --watch is a usage error in the cobra layer and must not be represented as a separate polling mode in the persisted spec.
- Do not add, accept, document, or emit a public compatibility alias for the removed polling flag. Historical worker records may be read best-effort as unknown/legacy input, but new CLI/server/API inputs use Mode plus IdleInterval.
- Add Spec.Validate() and Spec.ApplyDefaults(). Add parseExecuteLoopSpec(cmd *cobra.Command) (ExecuteLoopSpec, DispatchOptions, error) as the single cobra-to-spec conversion.
- cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go:1582-1605: replace naked-local extraction with parseExecuteLoopSpec. Remove positional-param closure pattern; pass spec by value.
- cli/internal/server/workers.go:25-49: replace ExecuteLoopWorkerSpec with (or alias to) ExecuteLoopSpec from the new package. Delete the parallel struct.
- cli/internal/server/server.go:2395-2409: delete the anonymous request struct in handleStartExecuteLoopWorker; decode directly into ExecuteLoopSpec. Call ApplyDefaults() then Validate() before StartExecuteLoop.
- cli/internal/server/graphql_adapters.go:63-76 plus 127-141: delete the parallel anonymous struct and parallel StartExecuteLoop literal; route through the same server-side ApplyDefaults + Validate + StartExecuteLoop as REST.
- cli/internal/server/workers.go:~753: replace hardcoded escalation.DefaultMaxCostUSD with spec.MaxCostUSD, with DefaultMaxCostUSD as fallback when zero.
- cli/internal/agent/spec_test.go or cli/internal/agent/executeloop/spec_test.go: TestExecuteLoopSpec_RoundTripsAllFields_Reflection uses reflect over exported fields; sets non-zero value per field; marshals; unmarshals; asserts round-trip. New field = automatic coverage.

NON-SCOPE
- ddx-eccc6efb (ADR-022 step 7) owns replacing runWorker with exec ddx work; this bead does not change the subprocess vs in-process dispatch decision.
- Other commands (ddx agent run, ddx try, MCP agent dispatch) may have the same smell; covered by sister bead ddx-fb290074.
- Reshaping LabelFilter from string to []string is owned by ddx-9d55601f; keep LabelFilter as string.

SEQUENCING
ddx-29058e2a (this bead) vs ddx-eccc6efb (ADR-022 step 7 - server-spawn migration to exec ddx work): lands independently and before ddx-eccc6efb. ADR-022 says ddx-29058e2a remains valuable as worker-side struct unification (cobra to in-process flow) and should land independently. When ddx-eccc6efb lands later, it will delete ExecuteLoopWorkerSpec from workers.go as part of the exec migration; the unified ExecuteLoopSpec should already live in the durable agent package. If ddx-eccc6efb lands first, the scope of this bead narrows to the cobra and worker-facing layers that still exist.
notes: Fresh-eyes cleanup: removed the public compatibility-alias requirement from the unified spec bead. The canonical worker input is now Mode plus IdleInterval; historical disk tolerance is explicitly read-only and must not become a supported CLI/API alias.

description:
PROBLEM
Observed on 2026-06-29 in this repo while draining the queue. Worker pid 4014720 hit 4 consecutive 'transport: exit status 1' outcomes within ~2h on different beads (ddx-9aa2151d, ddx-95d80f7e, ddx-1c865bdb, ddx-aef568e7) without any successful merge. Load average was 38-52 throughout (8-core host). After each transport failure the worker advances to the next ready bead and the cycle repeats; closed counter unchanged across the period.

Specific log signature:
  do response complete in <N>m
  tracker_lock section=durable_audit wait=1ms hold=<seconds>
  ✗ ddx-<id> → transport: exit status 1

Some attempts had very short responses (1m37s) suggesting codex died early; others completed long (32m+) then died at durable_audit. Common factor: the provider subprocess exits status 1, which DDx classifies as 'transport' (not tests_red, not no_changes, not timeout).

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- The outcome classifier maps any non-zero provider exit (codex/claude/etc.) to 'transport: exit status 1' regardless of cause (OOM, kill, network error mid-stream). Inspect cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go around the outcome-mapping path for the codex/provider exit code (search 'transport: exit status'). The classifier does not distinguish 'load-killed' from 'genuine bug' from 'provider API error'.
- Under high system load (load avg > ~3-5x CPU count), the provider subprocess gets starved during the durable_audit / land phase (which is git+disk heavy), bumps into kernel OOM-killer or hits its own internal heartbeat/timeout, and exits non-zero. DDx then walks the queue trying the next bead which also dies, burning context+tokens with zero forward progress.
- There is no backoff/cooldown when transport failures cluster (e.g., 3+ in N minutes).

PROPOSED FIX
1. Add load-pressure detection: before each claim, sample /proc/loadavg and compare to runtime.NumCPU(); if 5-min loadavg > k * cores (k=2-3 reasonable), emit a structured backoff observation and sleep proportional to overload before claiming.
2. Add transport-failure cooldown: when N (≥3) 'transport: exit status 1' outcomes occur within the last M minutes, the worker should pause for a longer interval (e.g., 5-15 min) before next claim instead of immediately consuming another bead.
3. Capture and surface the provider subprocess's exit reason where possible: check WaitStatus for signal-killed (SIGKILL → OOM-likely, SIGTERM → graceful), and distinguish in the outcome string (e.g., 'transport: provider killed by SIGKILL (likely OOM)').

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go (outcome classifier + claim-loop pacing)
- cli/cmd/work.go (worker pacing/backoff)
- cli/internal/workerstatus/ (if load sampling needs a place)

OUT-OF-SCOPE
- Do not change the queue ordering.
- Do not change the durable_audit commit flow itself.
- Do not implement a general-purpose host load manager.

AC
1. New helper LoadPressureSnapshot() in cli/internal/workerstatus or cli/internal/agent returning normalized loadavg/cores; unit test covers >threshold and <threshold paths.
2. Worker pre-claim path checks the snapshot; when pressure exceeds k (default 2.5), logs a structured 'load_pressure_backoff' observation and sleeps before claim. Unit test asserts the path is invoked with k configurable.
3. Worker tracks last N (≥3) 'transport: exit status 1' outcomes by wall-clock timestamp; when 3 occur within 10m, the next claim is delayed by an extended cooldown (>=5m). Unit test simulates 3 failures within window and asserts the delay.
4. Outcome classifier distinguishes signal-killed (SIGKILL/SIGTERM) provider exits in the outcome string. Unit test asserts the distinct outcomes.
5. cd cli && go test ./cmd/... ./internal/agent/... ./internal/workerstatus/... -count=1 green.
6. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
notes: Reopened after cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... completed green in the active worker. The high-load/provider-test CPU regression observed during that run is separately tracked by ddx-aa6cc320.
title: execute-bead: cluster of 'transport: exit status 1' under high system load wastes attempts without progress

description:
PROBLEM (captured live, 2nd 2-worker collision): With two `ddx work --watch` workers on /Users/erik/Projects/ddx, the DURABLE-AUDIT commit path correctly retried index contention (ddx-82c89a10: "transient git index/ref contention committing durable audit outputs ... will retry next iteration" -> merged), BUT a SEPARATE commit path — the tracker commit at cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2286 (`return fmt.Errorf("committing tracker: %s: %w", ...)`) — does NOT route through the transient-retry, so the SAME "fatal: unable to write new index file: exit status 128" contention FAILED 3 beads outright: ddx-3fd19af1, ddx-122e0ec5, ddx-e6f047cd ("committing tracker: fatal: unable to write new index file: exit status 128"). So the resilience added for the durable-audit commit (ddx-23ac2796, and pending ddx-83361480/ddx-e8bf0695) does NOT protect the tracker-commit call-site.

ROOT CAUSE: the tracker commit at execute_bead.go:2286 (and its caller) returns the git error directly as a hard failure; it does not classify "unable to write new index file" / index.lock / "signal: killed" as transient nor retry, unlike the durable-audit path's finalizeDurableAuditOrStop + isTransientGitContention (execute_bead_loop.go:1026,1288). Two workers committing tracker state to the same shared .git/index contend, and the loser fails its bead instead of retrying.

PROPOSED FIX: Route the tracker commit through the SAME transient-contention handling as the durable-audit commit — classify index-write/index.lock/ref-lock/SIGKILL/deadline contention (via the shared isTransientGitContention, extended by ddx-83361480) as transient and retry on a later iteration (the tracker commit should be idempotent — re-deriving and re-committing the same staged state), rather than failing the bead. Prefer a single shared resilient-commit helper used by BOTH the durable-audit path and the execute_bead.go:2286 tracker path so the two cannot diverge again.

NON-SCOPE: the durable-audit classifier/deadline (ddx-83361480, ddx-e8bf0695 — this bead reuses that classifier); worktree/file leaks (ddx-b320e794, ddx-274943fc).
title: execute-bead: 'committing tracker' commit path lacks transient-retry on index contention — fails beads under 2-worker load

description:
PROBLEM
The test TestPreDispatchDirtyPreserveRequiresStableImplementationDirt at cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_stay_alive_test.go:836 fails on a normally-loaded developer machine because it uses a fixed 150ms context.WithTimeout for an in-process worker.Run() call that has to claim + execute + land + close one bead and continue polling. The 150ms budget is too tight; observed outcome on base revision edbcd9aa5: err is nil (work completes before deadline OR worker exits cleanly via another path), so require.ErrorIs(t, err, context.DeadlineExceeded) at line 882 fails.

This is a release-blocker: lefthook run pre-commit fails, blocking every subsequent bead from landing. Diagnosed in ddx-47d9100a's no_changes_rationale (the implementer correctly identified it as out-of-scope pre-existing breakage from commit 4555a083f, introduced by ddx-df319cf9).

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_stay_alive_test.go:871 — context.WithTimeout 150*time.Millisecond
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_stay_alive_test.go:882 — require.ErrorIs(t, err, context.DeadlineExceeded)
- Adjacent test ~line 726 (TestPreDispatchDirtyPreservePersistsStableImplementationDirt) uses the correct pattern: 30s outer timeout, worker.Run in a goroutine, require.Eventually polling for bead closure, then cancel(). See the comment at lines 772-774 explaining why 750ms was too tight.

PROPOSED FIX
Rewrite TestPreDispatchDirtyPreserveRequiresStableImplementationDirt to match the surrounding require.Eventually pattern:
1. Outer ctx timeout: 30*time.Second.
2. Run worker.Run in a goroutine, push result+err to a runCh.
3. require.Eventually (25s budget, 50ms tick) polls store.Get("ddx-int-0001") until Status == StatusClosed.
4. cancel() the outer ctx; <-runCh to collect outcome.
5. Assertions become: outcome.err is one of context.Canceled or context.DeadlineExceeded (use require.True with errors.Is check), Attempts=1, Successes=1, Failures=0, OperatorAttention nil, no "loop.pre_dispatch_dirty_preserved" event, no refs/ddx/pre-dispatch references.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_stay_alive_test.go (only the failing test)

OUT-OF-SCOPE
- Do not modify production code.
- Do not touch the passing adjacent test.
- Do not modify other 150ms or sub-second timeouts in this file; this bead targets only the named test.

AC
1. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_stay_alive_test.go:TestPreDispatchDirtyPreserveRequiresStableImplementationDirt rewritten to use require.Eventually + goroutine pattern with 30s outer timeout, mirroring TestPreDispatchDirtyPreservePersistsStableImplementationDirt at ~line 726.
2. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run 'TestPreDispatchDirtyPreserve' -count=5 green (5x to confirm non-flaky).
3. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -count=1 green.
4. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
5. The test still verifies the same invariants: a single bead claim+close happens, OperatorAttention is nil, no pre-dispatch refs are written.
title: test: fix flaky 150ms timeout in TestPreDispatchDirtyPreserveRequiresStableImplementationDirt

description:
PROBLEM
The bead-lifecycle readiness/lint skill documents advisory fields such as `suggested_fixes`, but it does not fully document the JSON contracts that DDx lifecycle hooks enforce. Agents following only the skill can emit unsupported classifications, array-shaped fields where strings are required, or omit the machine-consumable rewrite evidence. The result is repeated lifecycle hook decode warnings, lost safe refinements, and workers continuing only because DDx fail-opens unavailable hooks.

LIVE EVIDENCE
- `ddx-cf8fb41c` worker log: `readiness check unavailable: decode result: json: cannot unmarshal array into Go struct field preClaimIntakePromptRewrite.rewrite.acceptance of type string`.
- `ddx-ef9e8aec` worker log: `readiness check unavailable: unknown classification "safely_refinable"`.
- `ddx-ef9e8aec` worker log: `lint hook: bad-json: json: cannot unmarshal array into Go struct field LintResult.rationale of type string`.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `.agents/skills/ddx/bead-lifecycle/SKILL.md:73-118` defines the READINESS MODE JSON shape with `suggested_fixes`, `suggested_child_beads`, and `waivers_applied`, but no `rewrite` object or `rewrite.changed_fields` guidance.
- `.claude/skills/ddx/bead-lifecycle/SKILL.md:73-118` has the same missing readiness rewrite schema text.
- `.agents/skills/ddx/bead-lifecycle/SKILL.md:156-188` and `.claude/skills/ddx/bead-lifecycle/SKILL.md:156-188` document lint output but do not stress that `rationale` is an array of objects only in lint mode, while readiness `rationale` is a string and hook parser fields must match mode-specific schema exactly.
- `cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake.go:72-76` defines `PreClaimIntakeRewrite` with string `description`, string `acceptance`, and `changed_fields`.
- `cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:399-424` accepts only known readiness classifications and promotes `classification=needs_refine` to `actionable_but_rewritten` only when a valid rewrite is present.

PROPOSED FIX
- Update both shipped bead-lifecycle skill copies to document the exact mode-specific JSON contracts for readiness and lint.
- State that readiness classification values are exactly `ready`, `needs_refine`, `needs_split`, `operator_required`, or `system_unready`; do not emit synonyms such as `safely_refinable`.
- State that readiness `rewrite.changed_fields` is required when proposing `needs_refine` as an intent-preserving replacement rewrite, and that `rewrite.description` and `rewrite.acceptance` are strings, not arrays.
- Clarify the distinction: `suggested_fixes` is advisory diagnostic output; `rewrite` is the machine-consumable replacement contract DDx may apply before claim.
- Clarify mode-specific `rationale` shape so lint output and readiness output do not cross-contaminate each other.
- Add or update tests that verify the skill prompt/schema text contains these contracts and that parsers accept the documented shape and reject the observed malformed shapes.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change bead lifecycle state transitions.
- Do not weaken operator-required handling for rejected or lossy rewrites.
- Do not change DDx-side routing or Fizeau integration.

DEPS
No deps.
title: skills: document lifecycle hook JSON contracts

description:
PROBLEM
ddx work currently emits "No execution-eligible beads in the queue" and exits when the only ready beads are epics with open children, mislabeled closure candidates, superseded leftovers, dead intermediates, or epic-of-epic chains. Operators have to manually triage every blocker class. This violates the factory rule that ddx work must self-unstick (reliability principle P10, just added).

ROOT CAUSE
docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-004-beads.md:122-167 (post-edit) and docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-010-task-execution.md "Idle-Path Diagnosis and Auto-Remediation" subsection (just added) now mandate diagnose+auto-remediate semantics. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1263-1315 today only reads ReadyExecutionBreakdown into result.NoReadyWorkDetail, then sleeps/exits — no diagnoser, no remediation dispatch. cli/internal/bead/lifecycle.go:218 isOrdinaryEpicContainer conflates openChildCount with totalChildCount, mislabeling 6 of 10 ready epics in the current project as containers when they are actually closure candidates.

PROPOSED FIX
Build the diagnose+auto-remediate idle path per FEAT-010 §Idle-Path Diagnosis and Auto-Remediation: per-bead Diagnose function with the closed reason taxonomy; remediator handlers for RC-1 (lifecycle classifier fix), RC-2 (supersession cascade in Close), RC-3 (dead-intermediate cleanup), RC-6 (auto-epic-decompose wrapping runPreClaimDecomposer); idle-path wiring in execute_bead_loop.go that runs diagnoser, fires matching remediators, re-scans without sleeping on success; operator surface (ddx work focus) two-section output that NEVER silently hides auto-remediable beads; ddx work plan --explain/--json flags for inspection. All safety guards (attempt cap, cost budget, cooldown, cycle guard, operator overrides, audit events) per the spec.

NON-SCOPE
- Building the FEAT-004 epic-scoped worker mode (dedicated branch/worktree, sequential child execution). Explicitly deferred in the FEAT-004 update.
- Replacing the operator-invoked bead-breakdown skill. It stays the right tool for top-down planning from a fresh spec/plan.
- Two-worker concurrency redesign — current tracker serialization is reused.

- RC-1: classifier split openChildCount/totalChildCount (cli/internal/bead/lifecycle.go)
- RC-2: supersession cascade in Close() (cli/internal/bead/store.go)

description:
PROBLEM
Since ddx-79148c01 landed (f53bc86fa3, public Store.WriteAll now enters Store.WithLock), four cmd acceptance tests deadlock deterministically at the 10s collection-lock timeout: TestArtifactRegenerateRecordsProducedArtifact, TestExecCommandsValidateRunHistoryAndResult, TestExecAgentDelegation, TestMetricCommandsValidateRunHistoryAndCompare ('bead: lock timeout (owner pid: <dead>)'). Reproduced locally with and without -race. Release runs v0.6.2-alpha127 (rerun) and v0.6.2-alpha128 failed on exactly these. The regression shipped because the landing gate covered ./internal/agent and ./internal/bead but not ./cmd.

ROOT CAUSE
cli/internal/exec/bead_runtime.go:400 and :479 call Collection.WriteAll(beads) INSIDE Collection.WithLock(...) read-modify-write blocks (saveDefinition, saveRunRecord). WriteAll now re-enters the same non-reentrant dir lock (cli/internal/bead/store.go:452-456) and spins until the 10s timeout at cli/internal/bead/lock.go:148. store.go:447-451 documents that in-lock callers must use writeAllLocked, but writeAllLocked is unexported so cli/internal/exec cannot comply.

PROPOSED FIX
Export the locked write path as Store.WriteAllLocked (documented: caller must hold Store.WithLock) delegating to the existing writeAllLocked, and switch bead_runtime.go:400 and :479 to it. Keep the surrounding WithLock blocks (the run-record path also renames attachment dirs under the lock).

NON-SCOPE
Lock re-entrancy support; lock timeout tuning; the ddx-79148c01 serialization itself (correct and stays).
title: exec: fix re-entrant collection-lock deadlock introduced by serialized WriteAll

description:
PROBLEM
An interrupted/killed execute-bead attempt can leave DDx-managed execution evidence (.ddx/executions/<run-id>/manifest.json, prompt.md, result.json — tracked via the project .gitignore ! negations) STAGED but uncommitted in the landing worktree. The next pre-claim landing-index guard then refuses to claim: 'pre-claim hook: landing worktree has staged changes after waiting 2s: A .ddx/executions/.../result.json (systemic; leaving beads untouched)'. The queue stalls until the durable-audit flow happens to commit that orphaned evidence on a later iteration. Observed live on niflheim (attempt 20260706T171624 left staged evidence that jammed worker-20260706T175949 until a restart).

ROOT CAUSE
The index-clean wait in cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:550-574 only recovers when the drifted index matches a recent ancestor tree (readTreeHead). Newly-staged .ddx/executions evidence matches no committed tree, so recovery does not apply and it fails with 'landing worktree has staged changes'. isStagedTrackerContentionError (cli/internal/agent/work/guard.go:227) does not treat .ddx/executions paths as managed (trackerpaths.IsManagedTrackerPath excludes them), so the staged set classifies as systemic rather than recoverable. Neither path unstages the orphaned evidence; it only clears when eventually committed — which is exactly the execution-log committing under review.

PROPOSED FIX
In the index-clean guard (execute_bead_land.go), before failing with 'staged changes', add a recovery branch: if EVERY staged path is under .ddx/executions/ (DDx-managed per-machine evidence, not real work), UNSTAGE it (git reset -q HEAD -- .ddx/executions) and re-check 'git diff --cached --quiet'; return nil when clean. A mixed or code-bearing staged set is still refused (unchanged). Unstaging (not committing) the orphaned evidence unblocks the queue and aligns with the convention that .ddx/executions is per-machine untracked working state (the durable audit trail is .ddx/attachments). Do NOT auto-unstage non-evidence .ddx paths (e.g. beads.jsonl).

NON-SCOPE
- The broader decision to stop committing execution evidence to git entirely (separate; this fix is compatible with it).

AC
1. A landing worktree whose ONLY staged paths are under .ddx/executions/ is recovered by unstaging them; the guard returns nil (clean) instead of erroring. TestLandingIndex_UnstagesOrphanedExecutionEvidence in cli/internal/agent.
2. A landing worktree with a code file (or a mixed .ddx/executions + code set) staged still errors 'landing worktree has staged changes' (unchanged). TestLandingIndex_RefusesStagedCode.
3. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run 'LandingIndex_' green.
4. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
title: pre-claim: orphaned staged .ddx/executions evidence jams the landing-worktree guard

description:
PROBLEM (Principle 2 of epic ddx-602ae31a)

Skills/personas/plugins can live in two install layers (project-scoped under ddxroot.Path() and machine-wide under ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/). Runtime callers need a single authoritative resolver that picks the right on-disk plugin directory with a defined precedence, otherwise the dual-location install surface has no consumer and project installs cannot shadow global ones.

ROOT CAUSE
- cli/internal/registry/resolve.go:22 ResolvePlugin must implement precedence project → global → baked-in. The project path is filepath.Join(ddxroot.Path(ctx, projectRoot), "plugins", name) (resolve.go:23); the global path is filepath.Join(ddxroot.GlobalDir(), "plugins", name) (resolve.go:28); baked-in (defaultplugin.FS()) is valid only for name == "ddx" (resolve.go:33). ddxroot.GlobalDir() is defined at cli/internal/ddxroot/ddxroot.go:90.
- Before this layer existed, install/update targeted ddxroot.Path() unconditionally and there was no precedence rule, so an operator with both a project and a global copy had undefined resolution.

PROPOSED FIX
1. ResolvePlugin(ctx, projectRoot, name) returns (path, layer, err): when both project and global copies exist, return the project path with layer "project"; when only the global copy exists, return its path with layer "global"; when neither exists and name == "ddx", return ("", "baked-in", nil) so callers fall back to defaultplugin.FS(); otherwise return a non-nil error naming all three layers.
2. The project path resolves through ddxroot.Path() so it is correct in BOTH in-tree mode (<project>/.ddx/plugins/<name>) and convention mode (${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/projects/<identity>/plugins/<name>).
3. SPEC IMPACT: file/update the skill-install-topology ADR (docs/helix/02-design/adr/ADR-025-or-equivalent) documenting the three-layer precedence, and update the CLAUDE.md "Persona System" section to state the project-over-global-over-baked-in lookup precedence.

NON-SCOPE
- Does NOT remove the per-project install path (both layers coexist).
- Does NOT migrate any legacy ~/.config/ddx paths.
- Does NOT add agent-harness path discovery beyond Claude Code and Codex.
- Writing the plugin content / creating agent-tier links is handled by the install and init child beads, not here.

DEPS
ddx-06cbaa90 (ddx home resolution) — project path routes through ddxroot.Path() and the global path through ddxroot.GlobalDir(); both must be agreed-on. Governing epic: ddx-602ae31a (Principle 2: skills/personas install-to-agent vs install-in-project).

Core stances:
- Simplicity beats sophistication — the right architecture is the simplest one that works for the real load, not the one that scales to 10x imagined load
- Prefer monolith first — microservices have operational cost that only pays back at real scale
- Event-driven only when async decoupling earns it — not by default
- Data model beats clever caching — design the schema right, the cache falls out naturally

- Abstracting over unclear requirements (YAGNI at the architecture layer)

acceptance:
AC1. ProviderTimeout is configurable per-project via .ddx/config.yaml under agent.routing or agent.endpoints — e.g. agent.endpoints[provider].request_timeout_seconds — and the current 15-minute hardcoded constant becomes a default that can be overridden upward (or removed entirely) per provider.

AC2. ProviderTimeout is configurable per-tier via the model-overrides path: cheap tier on a known thinking model (qwen3.6, deepseek-r1, etc.) defaults to a longer cap (e.g. 60 min or unlimited). Cloud chat models keep the 15-min default.

AC3. The idle-read timeout (DefaultProviderIdleReadTimeout = 5 min) is the primary stalled-TCP-socket defense; documentation in cli/internal/agent/serviceconfig.go and the user-facing config docs explain the relationship between idle-read and wall-clock-request timeouts and when each fires.

AC4. When ProviderTimeout fires, the error message names the exact timeout setting and the path to override it (e.g. 'request_timeout=15m exceeded; configure agent.endpoints.<name>.request_timeout_seconds in .ddx/config.yaml').

AC5. work / execute-bead --request-timeout DURATION CLI flag exists for one-off overrides during debugging.

AC6. Default for known-thinking-model surfaces (provider.type=lmstudio AND model name matches qwen3.6/qwen-r1/deepseek-r1 etc., or some other declared 'thinking' attribute) is bumped to a sensible value (e.g. 60 min) without requiring per-project config.
description:
Source: cli/internal/agent/serviceconfig.go:30
  const DefaultProviderRequestTimeout = 15 * time.Minute

This is hardcoded, not surfaced through .ddx/config.yaml or any flag, and is applied uniformly to every provider regardless of model class. It is set on every service path:
  - cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:116  ProviderTimeout: DefaultProviderRequestTimeout
  - cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:153           ProviderTimeout: DefaultProviderRequestTimeout

The comment justifies it as 'Defeats RC4 of ddx-0a651925: a stalled TCP socket that has delivered headers but stopped emitting body bytes would otherwise pin a goroutine until the outer wall-clock (3h) frees it.'

But that scenario is already handled by a separate idle-read timeout immediately below, on line 34:
  const DefaultProviderIdleReadTimeout = 5 * time.Minute

The 5-minute idle-read timeout is exactly the right tool for the stalled-TCP-socket case (no body bytes for 5 min → fail). The 15-minute wall-clock cap on a single request is the WRONG tool — it kills any legitimately long single Chat call regardless of streaming health.

Concrete impact observed today (2026-04-29 axon repo):

1. axon-db7a6d0a worker (qwen3.6-35b-a3b on bragi via lmstudio)
   - status: no_changes
   - duration_ms: 1,762,081 (29 min total — one timeout + retry)
   - log: 'WARN provider error, retrying attempt=1 err="provider request timeout: wall-clock 15m0s" delay=1s'
   - Retry consumed another full 15 min, also timed out, no commits produced.

2. axon-80979cb8 + axon-db7a6d0a + axon-ab2e52e0 (3-worker cascade re-launch)
   - All 3 hit 'provider request timeout: wall-clock 15m0s' on the first attempt
   - User killed the run before retries could waste another 15 min × 3 each

Why thinking models hit this:
qwen3.6-35b-a3b and similar 'thinking' / chain-of-thought reasoning models can spend 5–10+ minutes generating reasoning tokens before producing the first body delta the harness considers progress. Streaming output IS happening (so the idle-read timeout would NOT fire), but the harness is counting wall-clock against the entire request. A single hard problem can blow the 15-minute cap legitimately.

Why arbitrary timeouts are not helping:

a) Same value for cloud providers (claude, codex) and local providers (lmstudio, omlx). Local thinking models routinely need >15 min on hard prompts; claude rarely does. Same cap is wrong for both classes.

b) No way to opt out of the cap per provider, per model, per request, per project. /home/erik/Projects/axon/.ddx/config.yaml has no knob.

c) Retries inherit the same cap. A timeout-prone session retries with the same fate. Burns cycles and tokens.

d) The cap defeats the cascade: when a cheap-tier qwen times out, escalation to standard claude is intended — but on a thinking model the timeout doesn't mean 'broken provider', it means 'this prompt is hard'. We then escalate after wasting 15 min, and the standard tier solves the problem in 2. Net effect of cheap-tier-first becomes negative.
title: agent: hardcoded 15-minute DefaultProviderRequestTimeout kills thinking-model requests; not configurable

description:
PROBLEM

Dogfood on 2026-06-14 while executing ddx-3141b561 exposed a provider-supervision failure. The worker route was Claude (`claude/sonnet`), but the Claude-run attempt repeatedly spawned Codex and Gemini provider CLIs as direct children of the `ddx work` process: `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/codex --no-alt-screen` on TTYs and `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/gemini` with Node grandchildren. DDx status sometimes surfaced Codex as a provider child, but DDx did not continuously quarantine it and did not surface Gemini in status. The operator manually killed multiple Codex/Gemini process groups during one successful bead. A routed DDx execution must not depend on, leak, or silently fan out to unrelated provider CLIs whose local configuration may be absent or incompatible.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE

- `cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:313-330` only calls `reapSupersededProviderChildren` when a route is resolved. Provider CLIs spawned after route resolution are not continuously checked during the long running phase.
- `cli/internal/agent/provider_children.go:100-123` reports provider children to status, but non-route children remain observational unless another route-resolution or attempt-end cleanup happens.
- `cli/internal/agent/provider_children.go:157-170` can reap superseded providers, but it is only invoked at route-start rather than as a watchdog while the active route is running.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1105-1123` captures a process baseline and performs cleanup only after `attemptBackend.Run` returns. If a provider keeps itself alive by spawning provider CLIs or background monitors, DDx waits for the provider instead of enforcing the route boundary.

PROPOSED FIX

Add a running-phase provider child guard owned by `ddx work`/`ddx try`: after the active route is known, periodically scan descendants of the worker process, terminate provider CLIs whose provider does not match the active route/harness, include grandchildren such as Gemini's Node child process group, and write durable evidence (`provider-children.json` plus an operator-attention event or work status detail). The active route provider must not be killed. The guard must be covered by tests that use fake provider binaries and process groups rather than real Claude/Codex/Gemini installs.

IN-SCOPE FILES

- cli/internal/agent/provider_children.go
- cli/internal/agent/provider_children_test.go
- cli/internal/agent/service_run.go
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go
- cli/cmd/work_status_test.go

NON-SCOPE

Do not change Fizeau route selection or provider catalog behavior. Do not require Claude, Codex, or Gemini to be installed for tests. Do not hand-edit `.ddx/beads.jsonl`. Do not remove the attempt-end cleanup path; this is an additional running-phase guard.

DOGFOOD EVIDENCE

During attempt `20260613T235859-7bf046b7` for ddx-3141b561, DDx status showed the active route as Claude while `ps` showed repeated non-route provider children: Codex PIDs 3629941, 3662216, 3669904, 3731569, 3791392, 3835991 and Gemini process groups 3630001, 3662292, 3669978, 3731696, 3791479, 3836056. The operator manually ran `kill -TERM -<pgid>` for each non-route provider group. The bead still completed, proving the extra providers were not legitimate required route work.
title: agent: quarantine non-route provider descendants during attempts

description:
PROBLEM
  TestOSExecutor_EarlyCancel at cli/internal/agent/agent_test.go:1012
  spawns `sleep 60` with a 10-second context timeout and expects the
  early-cancel path to fire when the context expires. In the most recent
  audit run the test ran for 60.0 seconds, not the expected ~10 seconds.
  Either (a) the context cancel is not propagating to the subprocess kill
  signal, (b) the kill is firing but process-group cleanup waits for the
  full sleep, or (c) the early-cancel branch is wired up correctly but a
  separate wait loop is blocking the test goroutine until natural exit.
  Whichever the root cause, this is a real correctness gap: production
  agent execution relies on context cancellation killing runaway
  subprocesses promptly.

ROOT CAUSE
  - cli/internal/agent/agent_test.go:1012 TestOSExecutor_EarlyCancel
    invokes OSExecutor.ExecuteInDir with a 10s ctx timeout against
    `sleep 60`.
  - cli/internal/agent/agent_test.go:1019-1023 asserts
    result.EarlyCancel == true and result.ExitCode == -1.
  - The test PASSES (assertions are met) but takes ~60s wall-clock,
    suggesting one of:
      a. OSExecutor.ExecuteInDir's kill path is not signalling SIGKILL
         to the subprocess on context cancel.
      b. The kill signal fires but cmd.Wait() blocks until the OS reaps
         the process tree (no setsid, no -PGID kill).
      c. The function returns at 10s but the test goroutine is held by a
         separate mechanism (e.g. captured stdout reader not closing).
  - Read OSExecutor.ExecuteInDir at cli/internal/agent/agent.go (or
    wherever ExecuteInDir is defined) to determine which.

PROPOSED FIX
  - Investigate OSExecutor.ExecuteInDir; identify which of (a), (b), (c)
    explains the 60s wall-clock.
  - For each plausible cause:
      a. Add explicit kill on context cancel: when ctx.Done() fires before
         cmd.Wait() returns, send syscall.Kill(-cmd.Process.Pid, SIGKILL)
         (requires cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}
         on Unix).
      b. Use process-group kill so descendants of the spawned subprocess
         also die.
      c. Close stdout/stderr pipes when ctx fires so any reader goroutines
         unblock.
  - Add explicit assertion that the test completes in under 15s wall
    clock: wrap test body with start := time.Now(); … ; require.Less(
    time.Since(start), 15*time.Second, "TestOSExecutor_EarlyCancel must
    not run longer than 15s").
  - Verify on Linux and macOS (cli is multi-platform per Makefile).

NON-SCOPE
  - General refactor of OSExecutor; only the early-cancel path.
  - Replacing OSExecutor with a different executor implementation.
  - Adding testing.Short() skip — the test SHOULD complete fast; if it
    doesn't, that's a bug. The fix is to make it fast, not to skip it.

INTERSECTIONS
  - No deps.
title: fix(agent): TestOSExecutor_EarlyCancel should cancel in <=10s not 60s

acceptance:
**User story:** As an operator, I expect the Sessions page to reflect reality — if I ran `ddx work` today, today's sessions appear within seconds. And I expect the feed not to silently break again the next time the agent execution path is refactored.

**Acceptance criteria:**

1. **Session-index source of truth.** A single writer (invoked from `service.Execute` or a thin wrapper that every production agent-execution path calls) appends one line per completed agent invocation to `.ddx/agent-logs/sessions.index.jsonl`. Fields are pointer-only: id, projectID, beadID, harness, surface, model, startedAt, endedAt, durationMs, cost, tokens, outcome, exitCode, bundlePath (relative), nativeLogRef (relative). No prompt or response bodies embedded.

2. **Single-call-site guarantee.** Unit test enumerates every production code path that executes an agent (execute-bead, work, `ddx agent run`, quorum, replay if still present) and asserts each appends exactly one index row. If a new path is added later without wiring this up, the test fails.

3. **Visibility restored.** GraphQL `sessions` query reads `sessions.index.jsonl`. Running `ddx work` (or any agent-execution path) against a fixture project causes the new session to appear in a GraphQL query within 2 seconds of completion. E2E test demonstrates this.

4. **Body lazy-load.** A new resolver `session(id: ID!) { prompt response stderr }` loads the heavy fields on demand from the execution bundle (`.ddx/executions/<ts>-<hash>/`) or the agent-log path, without reading every session in the index.

5. **Legacy migration.** A one-shot command (e.g. `ddx agent log reindex`) seeds the index from the existing `.ddx/agent-logs/sessions.jsonl` (397 MB corpus on the current repo), preserving historical sessions. Integration test uses a fixture `sessions.jsonl` and asserts the index has one row per legacy entry with all pointer fields populated.

6. **Deprecated-file behavior.** After migration, the legacy `sessions.jsonl` is not read by the server. `ddx agent usage` and related CLI commands (`cli/cmd/agent_usage.go:197,246,348`, `cli/cmd/status.go:179`) are updated to read from the index too, verified by their existing tests.

7. **Perf sanity.** The GraphQL `sessions` list resolves in ≤100ms p95 on a fixture with 10,000 index entries; current behavior times out or OOMs. Benchmark captured in bead notes as baseline + after-fix.

8. **UI note.** If there is a gap in the index (e.g. the 2026-04-19 → 2026-04-22 gap on the current repo, assuming backfill from executions/agent-logs is not feasible), the Sessions page surfaces a single-line banner "No sessions recorded between X and Y" so the gap is not silently invisible. If backfill is feasible, do it instead and skip the banner.

9. **Playwright e2e.**
   - Seeds a fixture project with `.ddx/executions/` bundles from both before and after a simulated gap.
   - Runs the migration command.
   - Opens `/sessions`, asserts the most recent session timestamp matches the latest bundle, asserts a clicked row lazy-loads prompt/response from the bundle rather than from an embedded payload.
   - Asserts the feed updates live (within 2s) after a new simulated session is written.
description:
## Observed

The Sessions page at `/nodes/.../projects/.../sessions` shows nothing newer than **2026-04-19**, three days ago. ddx is definitely still running — `.ddx/executions/` contains bundles from 2026-04-22 (today), `agent-s-*.jsonl` from 2026-04-21, `agent-loop-*.jsonl` from 2026-04-20. The UI simply cannot see them.

## Root cause

The Sessions GraphQL resolver reads exclusively from `.ddx/agent-logs/sessions.jsonl` (`cli/internal/server/state_graphql.go:504-516`). That file stopped being appended on 2026-04-19 19:46.

The only writer is `Runner.logSession` (`cli/internal/agent/runner.go:847-914`). It is called from four sites today:

- `cli/internal/agent/runner.go:229` (Runner.Run — legacy)
- `cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:216`
- `cli/internal/agent/claude_stream.go:516`
- `cli/internal/agent/virtual.go:206`

Production execute-bead / work no longer goes through any of them. The Runner-to-service refactor series (`5b933103`, `280f58e0`, `74eceda9`, `7cc1eb58`, `e05c785e`, `9f79f037`) routed the common path through `service.Execute` directly and did not carry forward the sessions.jsonl append. The last sessions.jsonl write lines up with the day that refactor set became default.

## Secondary issue (same fix should address)

`sessions.jsonl` is 397 MB for only 895 entries because each entry embeds the full `result.Output` (see `SessionEntry.Response` at `runner.go:879`). Growth is unbounded, there is no rotation, and `GetAgentSessionsGraphQL` (`state_graphql.go:476-490`) reads the whole file, parses every entry, and sorts in memory on every query. Even if we just restore the writer, the feed is fragile and will become a perf problem again quickly — relevant to `ddx-ad0db8fd` (bead detail was also O(N) scan).

## Proposed direction

Do not simply paper over by re-plumbing `logSession` into `service.Execute`. The right fix is:

1. **Decide the source of truth for "a session".** Current candidates on disk:
   - `.ddx/executions/<ts>-<hash>/{manifest.json,prompt.md,result.json}` — already written per execute-bead attempt.
   - `.ddx/agent-logs/agent-*.jsonl` and `agent-s-*.jsonl` — per-run streams from the agent harness.
   - Bead evidence events (kind:cost already written per attempt, see `execute_bead.go:492`).
   A session record should be derivable from a combination of execution bundles + agent-log streams, not from a separately-appended aggregate. The aggregate should be an **index**, not a **copy**.

2. **Introduce a lightweight index.** A thin `.ddx/agent-logs/sessions.index.jsonl` containing `{id, projectID, beadID, harness, model, startedAt, endedAt, durationMs, cost, tokens, outcome, bundlePath}` — pointer fields only, no embedded response bodies. Existing `sessions.jsonl` is deprecated to a read-only legacy file during a grace period.

3. **Write the index from `service.Execute`** (or a wrapper the execute-bead / run / work paths all share). One place to touch. Unit test guards that every production code path that executes an agent appends exactly one index row.

4. **GraphQL reads the index, streams bodies on demand.** `sessions { edges { node { ... } } }` reads the index. A new `session(id: ID!) { prompt, response, stderr }` lazy-loads the heavy fields from the execution bundle or agent-log file when the user expands a row.

5. **Legacy sessions.jsonl compatibility.** The index can be seeded once from the existing 397 MB file so historical data is not lost, then the old file is not read again. One-shot migration command (`ddx agent log reindex` or similar).

## Out of scope

- Replaying or regenerating sessions for the 2026-04-19 → 2026-04-22 gap. If the evidence exists in executions/agent-logs we can backfill the index; if not, accept the gap and cap it with a dated marker in the UI.
- A full telemetry rework. This bead just restores visibility and fixes the shape.
notes:
## 2026-04-22 — User-directed amendment: shard the index

Per user feedback: a single `sessions.index.jsonl` just replays the same problem at smaller scale. The aggregate needs to be split.

### Revised storage shape

- Directory: `.ddx/agent-logs/sessions/` (per-project, under each registered project's `.ddx`).
- Inside: **monthly shards** named `sessions-YYYY-MM.jsonl`.
- Each shard is pointer-only, same fields as the previously-proposed index (id, projectID, beadID, harness, surface, model, startedAt, endedAt, durationMs, cost, tokens, outcome, exitCode, bundlePath, nativeLogRef).
- Writer resolves the target shard from `time.Now().UTC()` at append time and creates the shard file lazily on first write of the month.
- Heavy bodies (prompt, response, stderr) stay where they already live — `.ddx/executions/<ts>-<hash>/` and agent-log streams — and are lazy-loaded by the `session(id:)` resolver.

### Why monthly, not daily / size-based / SQLite

- **Daily** — produces tens of thousands of files over the project lifetime; ReadDir becomes the cost.
- **Size-based** — requires coordinating rotation with the append; race-prone and hard to test.
- **SQLite** — overkill for first pass; revisit if a single monthly shard grows past tens of MB.
- **Monthly** — ≤12 shards/year, human-readable filenames, date-range queries map trivially to shard selection, bounded shard size in practice.

### Reader behavior

- Default Sessions query loads the **current + previous shard** (covers "recent activity" for any current date).
- Date-range queries map the range to a shard set and read only those.
- Pagination beyond the default window triggers older-shard loads on demand.
- No shard-coordination lock needed: each month's file is append-only and only the current-month shard is actively written.

### Legacy migration

- `ddx agent log reindex` reads the existing `.ddx/agent-logs/sessions.jsonl` once and splits by each entry's `timestamp` field into the appropriate monthly shards under `.ddx/agent-logs/sessions/`.
- After migration, the legacy file is renamed `sessions.jsonl.legacy` (not deleted) and never read again by the server. Hand-removal is the user's call.
- Idempotent: re-running the command merges without duplicating (index row dedup by `id`).

### Revised acceptance criteria (supersedes criteria 1, 5, 6, 7 on original description)

1. **Sharded index writer.** Single shared call site (from `service.Execute` or equivalent wrapper) appends one line to `.ddx/agent-logs/sessions/sessions-YYYY-MM.jsonl`, computing the shard from `time.Now().UTC()`. Test: write across a simulated month boundary and assert two shards exist with the correct split.

5. **Legacy migration shards too.** `ddx agent log reindex` splits `sessions.jsonl` into monthly shards by entry timestamp. Integration test uses a fixture with entries across 3 distinct months and asserts 3 shards are produced with correct contents and no duplicates on re-run.

6. **Server reads the shard directory.** `GetAgentSessionsGraphQL` reads `.ddx/agent-logs/sessions/*.jsonl`, respects any date-range arg, and loads only the shards that intersect the range. Unit test seeds 6 monthly shards and asserts a 2-month query reads exactly 2 files.

7. **Perf on sharded index.** Default Sessions view (current + previous shard) resolves in ≤50ms p95 on a fixture with 12 monthly shards × 10k entries each (120k total). Capture baseline (single-file read of same corpus) vs sharded in bead notes.

(Criteria 2, 3, 4, 8, 9 from the original acceptance list remain as written.)

### Scope clarifier

This amendment does not change the single-call-site writer guarantee or the lazy-body resolver — those remain the load-bearing ideas. The amendment is specifically about **how the pointer index is physically stored**.
## 2026-04-23 — Implementation benchmark and evidence

Baseline: `go test ./internal/agent -run '^$' -bench 'Benchmark(ReadSessionIndexDefaultWindow|LegacySessionsJSONLFullScan)$' -benchtime=1x` measured legacy single-file full scan/sort of 120k legacy-shaped rows with 2KB embedded responses at `BenchmarkLegacySessionsJSONLFullScan-12 1 1731705957 ns/op`.

After fix: the same command measured the sharded default-window reader at `BenchmarkReadSessionIndexDefaultWindow-12 1 8103661 ns/op` for 12 monthly shards x 10k rows each (120k total), with the default query reading only the current + previous shard window. Environment footer: linux/arm64, Go go1.26.2.

Acceptance evidence: `TestSessionIndexWritesMonthlyShards`, `TestSessionIndexShardFilesSelectsOnlyIntersectingDateRange`, `TestReindexLegacySessionsSplitsShardsAndDedupes`, `TestRunViaServiceWithAppendsOneSessionIndexRow`, `TestProductionAgentExecutionPathsUseIndexedServiceWriter`, `TestGraphQLAgentSessions`, `TestAgentLogReindexMigratesLegacyFile`, existing agent usage/status/processmetrics tests, and `e2e/sessions.spec.ts` cover writer sharding, bounded reads, migration, lazy body loading, deprecated-file read removal, UI gap banner, and live refresh.

REVIEW:BLOCK

Missing session index writer: no changes to `service.Execute`, shared execution wrappers, or agent execution paths to append `.ddx/agent-logs/sessions.index.jsonl`.
Missing GraphQL changes: no update to `cli/internal/server/state_graphql.go` for index-backed `sessions` or lazy `session(id:)` body loading.
Missing migration command: no `ddx agent log reindex` or equivalent CLI implementation and no fixture-based migration test.
Missing CLI usage/status updates: no changes to `cli/cmd/agent_usage.go` or `cli/cmd/status.go` to stop reading legacy `sessions.jsonl`.
Missing performance validation: no benchmark or fixture proving 10,000 index entries resolve within the required threshold.
Missing UI gap/banner behavior and Playwright coverage for `/sessions`, lazy loading, migration, and live feed updates.

REVIEW:BLOCK

**AC 4**: No `session(id: ID!)` resolver for lazy-loading prompt/response/stderr from execution bundles.
**AC 5**: No `ddx agent log reindex` command or migration logic.
**AC 6**: `cli/cmd/agent_usage.go` and `cli/cmd/status.go` are untouched.
**AC 7**: No benchmark captured.
**AC 8–9**: No frontend changes or Playwright tests.
