description:
PROBLEM
Landing failures that are really ref-lock, already-landed, or staged-evidence coordination issues still look like ordinary implementation failures to the worker. That causes fresh implementation reruns and the wrong retry lane instead of reconciliation or operator attention.

ROOT CAUSE
`cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_orchestrator.go:292-312` wraps every `LandingAdvancer` error as a generic `land advancer` failure, which loses whether the candidate was already landed, whether `refs/heads/main` could not be locked, or whether the landing worktree was dirty. `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_report_test.go:57-62` only proves the current detail string records land failure; it does not distinguish the coordination class from implementation failure.

PROPOSED FIX
- Split land/ref/index/evidence-staging failures into explicit retry actions: reconcile, retry-land, or operator-attention.
- If the candidate commit or merge is already landed or is an ancestor of the target, reconcile and continue without rerunning implementation.
- If the landing worktree has staged generated evidence or DDx metadata, preserve or retry the land/evidence step according to local policy rather than escalating the model.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change review gating, decomposition detection, or power escalation policy in this child.
- Do not reimplement low-level tracker/index contention fixes owned by sibling work.
title: agent: classify land coordination failures as reconciliation

<principles>Spec-first development · Executable specifications · Audit trail required · Work is a DAG · Drift is debt · Inspect and adapt</principles>
<concerns>go-std | security-owasp | testing</concerns>
<practices>Go domain interface with contract tests against real implementations · project-scoped durable files · no call-recording mocks · go test + lefthook</practices>

<governing>FEAT-006 Worker Contract: connected mutations use the server; disconnected manual workers apply the same operations locally and reconcile before new online writes.</governing>

PROBLEM
workerprobe knows Connected versus NotConnected and buffers events, but execution code has no transport-neutral coordination abstraction or durable offline mutation journal. Each CLI invocation therefore constructs its own local land coordinator.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/workerprobe/probe.go:129-224 owns only connection state and an in-memory event buffer. cli/cmd/try.go:256-259 and cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:280-282 construct NewLocalLandCoordinator directly. No durable idempotency-keyed coordination record exists.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add a coordination domain package under cli/internal/agent with typed claim/lease, tracker-transition, and landing requests/outcomes.
- Add a durable project-scoped ordered offline journal with monotonic sequence, idempotency key, payload hash, precondition, outcome, and acknowledged-through compaction.
- Add a real local implementation that holds a cross-process project coordination lock and uses existing bead-store/landing implementations.
- Define one behavioral contract suite that runs against the local implementation and the later HTTP implementation.

NON-SCOPE
Do not add server routes, wire Cobra commands, centralize bead picking, or change process ownership.

PARENT
- ddx-635ae251.

DEPS
- No deps.

description:
# PROBLEM
`*Store` exposes 3 dependency-graph methods (`DepAdd`, `DepRemove`, `DepTree`) and 3 queue-ordering methods (`QueueTop`, `QueueMove`, `QueueClear`). Per TD-027 §6 the dep methods belong on `BeadDependencyReader`/`BeadDependencyWriter` sub-interfaces (signature-only change — ctx added). Queue ordering is operator-driven workflow; per TD-027 §14 it belongs in `ops/queue/` helpers with typed `Operation` values.

# ROOT CAUSE
`cli/internal/bead/store.go` exposes these 6 methods. Foundation declared the `BeadDependencyReader`/`BeadDependencyWriter` interfaces but ctx isn't yet on `*Store`'s dep methods. `BeadQueue` isn't an interface in TD-027 — queue ops are workflow concerns that live as helpers.

# PROPOSED FIX

## Dependencies (signature-only)

1. Update `*Store.DepAdd(ctx, id, depID)`, `DepRemove(ctx, id, depID)`, `DepTree(ctx, rootID)` to take ctx.
2. Compile-time assertions: `var _ BeadDependencyReader = (*Store)(nil)`, `var _ BeadDependencyWriter = (*Store)(nil)`.
3. Thread ctx through callers. Narrow field types opportunistically (e.g., `ddx bead dep tree` CLI handler can narrow to `BeadDependencyReader`).

## Queue (helper-migration; methods removed)

4. Add named `Operation` types to `cli/internal/bead/operation.go`:
   - `QueueSetTop{}` — move bead to top of queue (sparse rank ordering).
   - `QueueSetPosition{Position int}` — operator move-to-position.
   - `QueueClearOp{}` — remove queue rank.
5. Create `cli/internal/bead/ops/queue/queue.go`:
   - `Top(ctx, l, id) error` — wraps `QueueSetTop{}`.
   - `Move(ctx, l, id, position int) error` — wraps `QueueSetPosition`.
   - `Clear(ctx, l, id) error` — wraps `QueueClearOp{}`.
6. Migrate callers (operator queue manipulation in `cli/cmd/bead.go` queue subcommands) from `*Store.QueueTop`/`QueueMove`/`QueueClear` → `ops/queue/` helpers.
7. Remove `*Store.QueueTop`, `QueueMove`, `QueueClear`.

# NON-SCOPE
- Dependency cycle detection — handled at higher layer.
- Queue rank renormalization algorithm — internal to ops/queue; sparse-rank logic remains as-is.
- Other concerns — separate beads.
- Module boundary lockdown — `ddx-74452926`.

# Acceptance criteria

1. `*Store.DepAdd`, `DepRemove`, `DepTree` take ctx. Compile-time assertions for `BeadDependencyReader` and `BeadDependencyWriter` compile.
2. `cli/internal/bead/operation.go` declares `QueueSetTop`, `QueueSetPosition{Position}`, `QueueClearOp` types with `Apply(b *Bead) error` impls. Tests: `TestOperation_QueueSetTop_AssignsTopRank`, `TestOperation_QueueSetPosition_RespectsBucket`, `TestOperation_QueueClearOp_RemovesRank`.
3. `cli/internal/bead/ops/queue/` package exists with helpers + tests: `TestOpsQueue_Top_MovesBeadToFront`, `TestOpsQueue_Move_PreservesPriorityBucket`, `TestOpsQueue_Clear_RemovesOperatorOverride`.
4. `*Store` no longer exposes `QueueTop`, `QueueMove`, `QueueClear`. Verified by grep.
5. Caller files no longer reference these methods on `*Store` outside the bead package.
6. Queue-ordering invariants (SD-004 §"Ready queue" / queue derivation) preserved — operator overrides apply within a priority bucket; explicit rank wins over missing rank within bucket. Test: `TestQueueOrdering_OperatorRankWithinBucket`.
7. `cd cli && go test ./...` is green.
8. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.

description:
PROBLEM
When a bead in one repo is blocked on work in ANOTHER repo (e.g. niflheim beads blocked on heimq), operators hand-carry 'SKIP these heimq-blocked beads' as prose across sessions and compactions. They wanted to mark them blocked but had to fall back to priority-4 + notes.

CURRENT STATE (from adversarial review — gap is NARROWER than first thought)
- An external-blocker primitive ALREADY exists: cli/internal/bead/lifecycle.go has StatusBlocked + a required ExternalBlockerReason, a LifecycleBucketBlockedExternal bucket, an ExternalBlocked() store query (store.go), and a manual recheck workflow (operator reopens when cleared).
- The RESIDUAL gap: the blocker reason is FREE TEXT with MANUAL reopen. There is no STRUCTURED cross-repo reference (<repo>#<bead>) and no AUTOMATED recheck.

WHAT TO PRODUCE (design, not implementation)
- A short design doc specifying: a structured cross-repo blocker reference field (repo + bead id) layered on the existing ExternalBlockerReason, and an automated recheck that flips the bead back to open when the referenced bead closes. Cover: how the recheck observes another repo's tracker (the referenced repo may be local or remote), failure modes, and backward compatibility with free-text reasons.
- Decompose into child build beads with command-based ACs depending on this epic.

NON-SCOPE (for THIS bead)
- No implementation in this bead — design + child beads only.
- Do not replace the existing external-blocker primitive; build ON it.
- No new lifecycle statuses.
title: DESIGN: structured cross-repo blocker ref + auto-recheck

description:
PROBLEM
DDx/FIZ worker failures can still surface as underspecified execution failures when provider availability, model availability, credentials, endpoint reachability, or harness configuration differs across machines. DDx is the abstraction that should let unattended workers continue through provider variance; a generic provider failure that gives no typed cause, no fallback action, and no durable route-health evidence is a product bug.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:287-290 returns pre-dispatch Fizeau Execute errors as a generic `agent: execute: %w`, leaving the execute loop without a typed provider/model/configuration failure contract.
cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:332-376 copies final service error text into Result.Error/ExitCode, but downstream classification still depends on free-text heuristics rather than a required typed route-health outcome for provider unavailable, model unavailable, auth missing, quota/rate limit, endpoint timeout, or harness misconfiguration.
cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:516-544 and :588-612 contain the unpinned route-exclusion/escalation path, but that path only works when the failure is already recognized as provider_connectivity/no_viable_provider; untyped provider/configuration failures can stop or preserve the bead without proving fallback was attempted or intentionally impossible.

PROPOSED FIX
- Define a typed provider failure taxonomy at the DDx/Fizeau boundary: provider_connectivity, provider_auth, provider_rate_limit, provider_quota, provider_model_unavailable, provider_harness_unavailable, provider_config_invalid, no_viable_provider, and unknown_provider_failure.
- Normalize both pre-dispatch Execute errors and final failed events into that taxonomy before ExecuteBeadReport construction.
- For unpinned workers, convert retryable provider/model/harness availability failures into route-health evidence and continue fallback/escalation without parking the bead.
- For explicit operator pins, fail loudly with a typed hard-pin exhausted/operator-action report that names the pin and available remediation, without silently widening pins.
- Persist durable evidence on the bead/run showing requested constraints, resolved route if any, typed failure, retryability, whether fallback was attempted, and why fallback stopped.

NON-SCOPE
Do not move concrete route selection into DDx; Fizeau still owns routing, aliases, model discovery, and provider catalog behavior. Do not remove explicit operator pins. Do not call real providers in tests.
title: agent: type provider failures and enforce fallback semantics

description:
PROBLEM
The no-changes contract and parser still accept a pseudo-status needs_investigation, then park the bead via labels and cooldown metadata. That bypasses the upstream status set and prevents ddx work from rerunning investigation-quality work with a smart agent when autonomous progress is possible.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/try/no_changes.go:16-23 defines NoChangesKindNeedsInvestigation.
- cli/internal/agent/try/no_changes.go:25-35 defines NoChangesLabelNeedsInvestigation and related events/extra keys.
- cli/internal/agent/try/no_changes.go:60-64 parses `status: needs_investigation`.
- cli/internal/agent/try/no_changes.go:136-140 defines NoChangesActionNeedsHumanNoCooldown.
- cli/internal/agent/try/no_changes.go:203-215 maps needs-investigation to a needs-human action and label.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1786-1796 instructs workers to output `status: needs_investigation` for ambiguous no-change cases.

PROPOSED FIX
Replace the no-changes pseudo-status contract with status-owned outcomes. If the bead is already satisfied, close it. If no change happened but autonomous smart-agent work remains possible, leave status=open with explanatory no-changes metadata and route the next retry with smart power. If operator decision is required, transition to status=proposed with explicit reason/suggested action metadata. Reserve status=blocked only for external recheckable blockers. `status: needs_investigation` is not accepted in new live no-changes output; stored historical values are handled by the one-way lifecycle migrator.

NON-SCOPE
Do not rewrite preclaim intake, terminal review, GraphQL, or frontend surfaces in this bead. Those have separate integration beads.

DEPS
Depends on store/query semantics because no-changes outcomes must be visible in the new worker-ready/operator-attention buckets.

description:
## Goal

Delete `agent.routing.profile_ladders`, `agent.routing.model_overrides`, the `--escalate` and `--override-model` flags, all their consumers, and the deprecation warnings. The duplicated routing layer is dead — the corpse should not haunt every config load.

The migration `ddx-87fb72c2` made these opt-in. This bead completes the migration: opt-in becomes opt-out becomes gone.

## Scope (delete with prejudice)

### Config schema
- `cli/internal/config/types.go` — delete `RoutingConfig.ProfileLadders` and `RoutingConfig.ModelOverrides` fields (and `defaultProfileLadders`, `DefaultProfileLadders()`).
- `cli/internal/config/schema/config.schema.json` — delete the `profile_ladders` and `model_overrides` properties.
- `cli/internal/config/config.go` — delete the deprecation warning code paths that detect these fields and print the migration hint. Hard reject any project config that still sets them: clear error pointing at the (then-archived) migration doc, exit non-zero. Same blast radius as `default_harness` already gets.
- `cli/internal/config/routing_migration_test.go` — delete or repurpose to test the new hard-reject behavior.

### CLI flags
- `cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go` — delete `--escalate` and `--override-model` flag definitions and their plumbing into `WorkerSpec` / RouteRequest. The `WorkerSpec.Escalate` field added by `ddx-c7081f89` becomes dead and goes too.
- `cli/cmd/agent_execute_loop_*.go` — same.
- Any flag wiring in the worker submit path (`cli/internal/server/server.go`, `cli/internal/server/workers.go`).

### Helpers and consumers
- `cli/internal/agent/profile_ladder.go` — delete entirely (`ResolveProfileLadder`, `ResolveTierModelRef`, `NormalizeRoutingProfile`'s ladder semantics, the test seam call counters, `DefaultRoutingProfile`).
- `cli/internal/escalation/escalation.go` — delete `AdaptiveMinTier`, `AdaptiveMinTierResult`, `AdaptiveMinTierThreshold`, `AdaptiveMinTierMinSamples`, `TierResolver`, `classifyAttemptTier`, `TierOrder`, `TiersInRange`, `tierIndex`. Keep `EscalationSummary`, `TierAttemptRecord`, `BuildEscalationSummary`, `AppendEscalationSummaryEvent`, `EscalationWinningExhausted`, `EscalatableStatuses`, `ShouldEscalate`, `IsInfrastructureFailure`, `ProviderCooldownDuration`, `FormatTierAttemptBody`, `BeadEventAppender`, `SuccessStatus` — these are still used by other paths (loop status, bead events, cooldown).
- `cli/internal/server/workers.go:658-820` — delete the entire escalation-on branch (the `if !escalationEnabled { ... } else { ...tier loop... }` split). `escalationEnabled` always false; collapse to the single-call path.
- `cli/cmd/agent_route_status.go` — drop the `--adaptive` flag and `reset` subcommand if they target the now-deleted state. Keep the rest of route-status.
- `docs/adaptive-min-tier.md` — delete.

### Documentation
- `docs/migrations/routing-config.md` — delete (or replace with a one-line stub: "agent.routing.profile_ladders and agent.routing.model_overrides were removed in vX.Y.Z; configs that still set them are rejected at load.").
- `cli/internal/server/frontend/README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` — search and remove any user-facing references to `--escalate` or `--override-model`.

### Tests
- Delete tests that exclusively cover the deleted paths: `*_escalation_*_test.go`, `profile_ladder_test.go`, `routing_migration_test.go`, etc. Where a test covers BOTH a deleted path and a kept path, narrow it to the kept path.
- Add one test that asserts `ddx work --once --local` on a project that still has `routing.profile_ladders` in its config exits non-zero with an error message naming the field.

## Affirmative non-goals

- Do **not** preserve any "transition" behavior. There is no warning-then-error grace period; `ddx-87fb72c2` already shipped the warning. This bead is the deletion.
- Do **not** keep dead `Escalate` / `MinTier` / `MaxTier` / `ModelRef` fields on `WorkerSpec` "for future use". If something needs them later, file a fresh bead.
- Do **not** keep the helpers in case some out-of-tree consumer imports them. DDx is a binary, not a library.
- Do **not** touch agent SDK internals — `ProfileEscalationLadder` and `escalateProfileLadder` live agent-side and stay.

## Out of scope

- Default profile change (separate bead if pursued).
- HistoricalSuccess injection into `RouteRequest.Inputs` (separate bead).
- Bead-id resolver bug (`ddx-7eab13a6`) — already filed.
- The 12 malformed-ID beads — `ddx-7eab13a6` covers their repair.

## Acceptance

1. `cd cli && go test ./...` passes (full tree, not just routing packages — the kept escalation helpers may have other callers).
2. `grep -rnE 'profile_ladders|model_overrides|ProfileLadders|ModelOverrides|ResolveProfileLadder|ResolveTierModelRef|AdaptiveMinTier|--escalate|--override-model' cli/ docs/ --include='*.go' --include='*.md' --include='*.yaml' --include='*.json'` returns matches only in:
   - this bead's own description (if grepped from .ddx/beads.jsonl)
   - the deletion test fixture / commit message
   - upstream-vendored code under cli/internal/server/frontend/node_modules/ if any
   No matches in source files.
3. `cd /home/erik/Projects/ddx && /home/erik/.local/bin/ddx work --once --local` against the current project (with `agent.routing` already removed) runs cleanly, no warnings, no flags needed.
4. A test fixture project with `agent.routing.profile_ladders: ...` in its `.ddx/config.yaml` causes any `ddx ...` command that loads config to exit non-zero with a message identifying the field. Same for `agent.routing.model_overrides`.
5. `--escalate` and `--override-model` flags are gone from `--help` output of `ddx work`, `ddx agent run`, `ddx agent execute-bead`, `ddx agent work`. Verifiable: `/home/erik/.local/bin/ddx work --help 2>&1 | grep -E 'escalate|override-model'` returns nothing.
6. `docs/adaptive-min-tier.md` and `docs/migrations/routing-config.md` are either deleted or replaced with single-line stubs noting the removal.

## Rollback

If the deletion proves too aggressive, revert the deletion commits. The migration doc (`docs/migrations/routing-config.md`) at HEAD before deletion has the full feature description; the git history retains the helpers.

This bead handles BLOCK + substantive failures only. Two SEPARATE beads cover related-but-distinct concerns:

- ddx-c6e3db02: per-bead rate-limit retry honoring Retry-After (provider stays in rotation)

Failure modes triaged HERE:
- post-merge review BLOCK → either (a) re-attempt-with-context (BLOCK reasons embedded in next prompt), (b) escalate to next tier in the S10_2 ladder, or (c) file follow-up bead capturing BLOCK reasons + mark original needs_human

acceptance: execute-bead prompt contract explicitly invites no_changes with a rationale. The fake-agent test harness seeds a no_changes rationale file; execute_bead_test.go asserts ExecuteBeadResult.NoChangesRationale is populated; work uses the rationale to classify 'already_satisfied' when it references a prior commit SHA or test name; the rendered log (ddx server workers log) shows the rationale on its own line; 'agent made no commits' no longer appears without context.
description:
Today when execute-bead exits with no_changes, the operator sees 'agent made no commits' and nothing else. That's useless for triage — the operator cannot tell whether:
- the bead is genuinely already satisfied (work present in a prior commit)
- the agent gave up because it couldn't find the relevant files
- the agent classified the task as ambiguous or too risky
- the agent hit a tool limit or context cap
- the prompt contract was unclear

The fix is to make no_changes a structured result that carries a short rationale from the agent itself, written at the point where the agent decided not to commit. Example of what the operator should see:

  status:    no_changes
  rationale: The epic filter requested by this bead was already added in
             commit 1da6495 (cli/internal/bead/store.go readyFiltered). I
             reviewed the current code and tests, confirmed the filter
             excludes 'epic' beads from ReadyExecution, and verified
             TestReadyExecutionExcludesEpics exists and passes. Nothing
             to do. Ref: 1da6495, TestReadyExecutionExcludesEpics.

This is specifically the case that motivated this bead: a continuous-drain worker processed ddx-b44ca394 ('Prevent work from launching open epics by default') after the epic filter had already been implemented on main. The agent instead made a synthesized no-op commit that only retargeted 17 .claude/skills/helix-* symlinks, which the loop classified as 'success' because a commit was produced. Had no_changes carried a rationale pointing at the prior commit, the loop could have closed the bead as 'already_satisfied' and moved on cleanly.

Scope:
1. Execute-bead prompt contract must explicitly instruct the agent: if you determine the bead's work is already present or cannot be done, report that in a structured way — do NOT make a synthesized commit to 'land something'. Today the prompt says 'Making no commits (no_changes) should be rare' which actively pushes agents toward the wrong behavior.
2. The agent's exit mechanism needs a way to carry a rationale string back. Simplest version: the agent writes a file to the worktree like .ddx/executions/<attempt-id>/no_changes_rationale.txt before exiting. ExecuteBead reads it if no commits were produced and attaches the text to the result.NoChangesRationale field.
3. The ExecuteBeadResult struct gains a NoChangesRationale string field, populated only when outcome == no_changes. Status: success and the unused 'reason' field need not change.
4. work close semantics: when no_changes arrives with a non-empty rationale pointing at a prior commit, the loop can optionally close the bead as already_satisfied with the rationale recorded in the close event body (instead of waiting for MaxNoChangesBeforeClose=3 strikes). Gate this behind a 'rationale references existing commit' heuristic to avoid flapping — if the rationale is a vague 'nothing to do', keep current cooldown behavior.
5. ddx server worker log should render the rationale prominently, not bury it in session metadata.
6. The prompt contract note that no_changes should be 'rare' is replaced with: 'If the work is already present, say so and provide a reference (commit SHA, test name, file path). A well-justified no_changes is always preferred to a cosmetic synthesized commit.'
title: no_changes reports must include a rationale the operator can act on

description:

Spec saves from the GraphQL API can still overwrite a document when the caller's optimistic concurrency token is stale, and the current mutation schema exposes only path and content. description:
## Problem

When 'ddx work --provider P' is invoked with a pinned provider and the cheap-tier attempt fails (for any reason: execution_failed, land_conflict, no_changes repeated, etc.), DDx escalates to the standard or smart tier using the project config's tier model overrides WITHOUT checking whether those escalation-target models actually exist on the pinned provider.

Observed on eitri 2026-04-17 (DDx v0.6.0-alpha22):

    .ddx/config.yaml:
      agent:
        routing:
          profile_priority: [cheap]
          model_overrides:
            cheap:  qwen/qwen3.6
            fast:   kimi/k2.5
            smart:  minimax/minimax-m2.7

    $ ddx work --once --local --provider vidar-omlx
    # cheap-tier attempt on vidar-omlx fails (for whatever reason — in this
    # session it was catalog-missing model on vidar-omlx; see ddx-e59e7fe8)
    # smart-tier escalation tries minimax/minimax-m2.7 — also routes to
    # vidar-omlx because of --provider pinning — fails with 404 'Model not
    # found' because vidar-omlx has MiniMax-M2.5-MLX-4bit, not m2.7.
    #
    # Final outcome: 'escalation exhausted: ...404 Not Found...'

Evidence: .ddx/executions/20260418T005017-ac81ac97/.

## What escalation should do instead

When --provider P is pinned, tier escalation options (in preference order):

1. **Restrict escalation to models that resolve on the pinned provider.**
   For each tier in profile_priority after the failing tier, check whether the
   tier's model_override resolves (via catalog) to a concrete ID that the
   pinned provider serves. If yes, use it. If no, skip that tier.

2. **If no higher tier resolves on the pinned provider, cap escalation.**
   Surface a clear diagnostic: 'escalation capped at cheap tier — smart
   (minimax/minimax-m2.7) does not resolve on provider vidar-omlx'. Honor
   --max-tier as a hard cap regardless of provider pinning.

3. **Do NOT silently widen to a different provider unless the user opts in.**
   'ddx work --provider P' is a pinning directive; spontaneously routing to
   openrouter because smart-tier doesn't fit on P violates the user's intent
   and leaks cost/quota to the wrong place.

4. **Separate case: --provider is NOT pinned (no flag).** Current behavior
   of picking a different provider for higher tiers is fine; this bead is
   only about the pinned case.

## Fix sketch

In cli/internal/agent/routing.go (or wherever tier escalation lives):

description:
PROBLEM
Concurrent stale breakers can classify the same canonical main-git lock from independent stale snapshots and both mutate it, because observation and mutation of the canonical lock are not serialized across processes. The crash-safe guard primitive now exists but is not held around the observe+mutate transition, and guard contention does not yet consume the retry budget or surface a bounded timeout.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go:238-278 (withTrackerLockPolicy) classifies the existing lock object and, via breakStaleTrackerLock, removes or renames it with no cross-process transition guard. cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go:309-328 (breakStaleTrackerLock) reads pid/acquired_at and os.RemoveAll(lockDir) without serializing observation and mutation across processes. The LockRetryPolicy budget (MaxRetries/MaxElapsed) at cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go:251-254 governs canonical acquisition but not guard contention.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
Phase 0 WB-5 single-winner cross-process stale-break protocol: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase0-stop-the-self-harm-plan-2026-07-13.md:124-132.

PROPOSED FIX
Acquire the crash-safe guard (from the guard-primitive child) immediately before the classify+break transition and release it immediately after, so only one process at a time observes-and-mutates the canonical lock. The guard MUST NOT be held across the ordinary os.Mkdir happy-path acquisition, pid/acquired_at metadata publication, the fn callback, the retry sleep, git/harness operations, or private tombstone removal — only across the observe+break critical section. Guard contention consumes the same LockRetryPolicy MaxRetries/MaxElapsed budget already threaded through the loop; on deadline, return TrackerLockTimeoutError (via lockTimeoutError) without invoking fn and without mutating the canonical lock. Reuse trackerLockContendedAttemptHook-style determinism for tests where needed.

NON-SCOPE
This child does NOT implement the guard type, its Unix/Windows advisory-lock backends, or the sidecar path helper (owned by the guard-primitive child and consumed here). It does NOT touch synthesizeCommitExcludePathspecs, preDispatchCheckpointIgnoredPath, or checkoutSyncDeferralIgnoredPath (owned by the ignore-wiring child). Do not change tracker record format, trackerLockStaleAge, LockRetryPolicy defaults, lockmetrics caps, harness/Fizeau behavior, bead-store locks, git index locks, or the execution-cleanup lock in cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_loop.go:116-156. Do not extract a shared lock package; Phase 1 WB-8 owns unification. Do not implement token-bearing lease release.

PARENT
ddx-1c8d9319

DEPS
Sibling guard-primitive child (crash-safe main-git transition guard primitive with sidecar path helper) — provides the guard type and path helper consumed here.

description:
PROBLEM
  Today's Land() in cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go performs git
  fetch, push --ff-only, and push-race auto-recovery as part of the core
  drain flow. This causes 30-120s lock holds spanning network I/O, which
  in turn produced ddx-08e90869 (work landed only on a preserved iteration
  ref because tracker lock contention prevented the main merge) and
  ddx-15a51f8c (push-race remediation commit). The user's architectural
  position is: Land() should perform only the worktree-merge into local
  main; origin-sync (fetch) and push are separate concerns, operator-driven
  or background-deferred, never coupled to Land() or the drain.

  The spec corpus partially reflects this position already:
  FEAT-012-git-awareness.md:134 declares "DDx does not invoke `git push` at
  all." But FEAT-010 (the governing feature for task execution) does not
  state the network-free boundary as a requirement, and the multi-machine
  docs (API-001 §"Land And Preserve Semantics", SD-020) describe a
  push/fetch-coupled lifecycle that is correct for distributed mode but
  contradicts the single-node invariant.

  This is a doc-only bead. It lands the requirement in the right anchor
  spec, then reconciles every cross-reference so the spec corpus is
  coherent and complete. Implementation removal of push/fetch from Land()
  is a separate sister bead (ddx-1f774edf, rewritten in parallel).

ROOT CAUSE
  - docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-010-task-execution.md ##Requirements
    section (around line 1057) enumerates functional + non-functional
    requirements but has no "Network isolation" or "Sync decoupling"
    requirement.
  - docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-012-git-awareness.md:134 declares the
    correct invariant ("DDx does not invoke `git push` at all") but has no
    cross-reference to FEAT-010 or to the implementation status.
  - docs/helix/02-design/solution-designs/SD-025-task-execution-lifecycle.md
    Layer 2/3 sections do not mention push/fetch — silent on the boundary,
    so implementers may inadvertently reintroduce network I/O.
  - docs/helix/02-design/contracts/API-001-execute-bead-supervisor-contract.md:221-225
    §"Land And Preserve Semantics" prescribes "fetch origin before rebase"
    and "push --ff-only ... atomic ref-update is the serialization point".
    This was written for the multi-machine coordinator topology and
    contradicts the single-node invariant.
  - docs/helix/02-design/solution-designs/SD-020-multi-machine-coordinator-topology.md
    lines 51, 60, 79, 83, 117, 123, 136, 155 reference git push/fetch as
    part of the lifecycle; these are correctly scoped to multi-machine but
    need an explicit preamble distinguishing single-node from multi-machine.
  - docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-023-sync.md exists but does not
    explicitly position itself as the designated home for origin-sync
    semantics complementing FEAT-010's drain boundary.
  - docs/helix/06-iterate/reliability-principles.md enumerates P1-P8
    execution-loop invariants; the network-free drain is the natural P9.

PROPOSED FIX
  All edits are doc-only:

  1. FEAT-010: under ##Requirements, add a new functional requirement:
     "Network-free drain boundary: Land() performs only the worktree-merge
     into local main, under a brief local lock. Origin-sync (git fetch +
     merging origin/main into local main) and origin-push (git push) are
     separate operations, operator-driven or background-deferred, and are
     never invoked from Land() or from the drain loop."
     Plus a non-functional requirement bullet:
     "Network isolation: single-developer/single-node drain does not block
     on remote I/O; origin sync and push are decoupled and may run in
     parallel or in the background without holding the drain or land lock."

  2. FEAT-012:134 — keep the existing line; add a cross-reference sentence
     pointing to FEAT-010's new requirement and noting the implementation
     gap is being closed by the sister implementation bead.

  3. SD-025 — under Layer 2 (bead attempt) and Layer 3 (queue drain), add a
     one-sentence cross-reference: "Per FEAT-010 network-free drain
     boundary, this layer performs no network I/O; origin-sync and push are
     out-of-band per FEAT-023."

  4. API-001:221-225 §"Land And Preserve Semantics" — add an explicit
     preamble: "These semantics describe the multi-machine coordinator
     topology (SD-020). For single-node mode (FEAT-010 default), Land() is
     local-only; the fetch+push lifecycle described below applies only when
     multi-machine coordination is active."

  5. SD-020 — at the top of the doc, add a one-paragraph preamble making
     the single-node vs multi-machine distinction explicit, with a pointer
     to FEAT-010.

  6. FEAT-023-sync.md — add a sentence positioning it as the designated
     home for origin-sync semantics, complementing FEAT-010's drain
     boundary. Defer the actual `ddx sync` helper to the future
     multi-machine work; this is just a naming/scoping clarification.

  7. reliability-principles.md — add P9 "Network-free drain": short
     principle text, file:line citations to FEAT-010 and Land(),
     justification (single-node drain must not block on network I/O).

NON-SCOPE
  - The implementation removal of push/fetch from Land() and the
    LandingGitOps interface (sister bead ddx-1f774edf, rewritten).
  - Designing or building a `ddx sync` helper (downstream of multi-node
    work; the user explicitly deferred this).
  - Updating prompt templates / eval data / closed beads that reference
    push_failed semantics (downstream impact, separate beads).
  - Changing TD-031 (state machine is unaffected).

description:

  and routing) was moved from github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau to a
  new home at easel/fizeau, with a new published release. DDx today

  across 53 .go files in cli/. The integration is mechanical (import
  path swap + go.mod update + go.sum refresh + verify build/tests).

  Top-priority because: (a) the old import path may be deprecated or
  receive no further releases; (b) we want the latest fizeau release
  features/fixes (likely includes routing or wedge-relevant
  improvements); (c) this is a blocking integration — every other
  agent-side fix depends on stable fizeau access.

  Per user memory feedback_no_local_replace.md: ddx must always import
  a properly tagged release; no go.mod replace directives, even
  temporarily.

  - 53 .go files in cli/ import github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau or
    a sub-package thereof. Verify with:

  - The new module path is at easel/fizeau (likely
    github.com/easel/fizeau — confirm via `go list -m
    github.com/easel/fizeau@latest` or by checking the upstream repo
    directly). The latest published release tag should be discovered

          canonical Go import path.

        - Remove `github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau v0.10.15`.

description:
PROBLEM
Concurrent DDx index-lock recovery can move or delete a fresh native Git index.lock after another breaker has already disposed of the stale file. A unique tombstone name alone does not make the transition single-winner. Recovery also treats every failed or unavailable owner probe as "unowned", can mutate malformed path types, and derives the wrong index.lock path in linked worktrees.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/gitlock/gitlock.go:69-87 derives <worktree>/.git/index.lock by pathname. In a linked worktree, .git is a gitdir indirection file and the real index lock is under the linked-worktree gitdir, so recovery may inspect the wrong path.

cli/internal/gitlock/gitlock.go:96-123 collapses missing lsof, lsof timeout, execution errors, empty output, and malformed output into PID zero. cli/internal/gitlock/gitlock.go:149-195 then classifies and removes the canonical pathname with no cross-process transition guard. Lines 165-168 and 180-184 remove whatever occupies the path at mutation time. No regular-file check or source-identity proof binds that mutation to the file inspected at lines 152-160.

Counterexample: recovery processes A and B both inspect stale file S. A renames and disposes S, making the canonical pathname available; native Git creates fresh lock W. Delayed B then renames the canonical pathname to B's unique tombstone and deletes W. Unique tombstone names protect only the destination, not the observed source.

Git owns index.lock creation, contents, and release. DDx cannot add owner_token metadata or migrate Git to a DDx lease. The source identity must therefore be the actual filesystem object, and unknown ownership must fail closed.

PROPOSED FIX
Resolve index.lock to the actual gitdir for primary and linked worktrees, using Git's --git-path index.lock semantics or an equivalent correctly parsed gitdir indirection. Derive a stable sibling transition-guard path and unique private tombstone paths inside that gitdir so none appear in checkout status or staging.

Add a package-local crash-safe cross-process transition guard. Use a never-deleted advisory-lock sidecar plus a keyed same-process mutex. Unix uses nonblocking flock. Windows uses golang.org/x/sys/windows LockFileEx with LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY|LOCKFILE_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK over byte zero, length one, and maps lock contention without unsafe fallback. Ordinary recovery never unlinks or recreates the sidecar.

Split owner probing into typed outcomes: live owner, proven no owner, and unknown. Missing lsof, timeout, execution failure, malformed output, and platform probe errors are unknown and never authorize mutation. Preserve the current stale policy only with proof: a positively dead identified PID is stale, or a regular lock with a proven-absent owner and age at least StaleAge is stale. Fresh, live, and unknown-owner locks remain untouched.

Inspect and pin the candidate before transition by opening the actual regular file and retaining a platform-appropriate identity handle. Acquire the transition guard nonblockingly, then compare the current canonical object with the pinned candidate using os.SameFile. Only an exact identity match may be renamed to a contender-unique sibling tombstone. Verify the tombstone still has the pinned identity before deleting it. On any identity mismatch, malformed path, guard/open/lock failure, or unknown owner, fail closed and do not delete the canonical path or tombstone.

Release the transition guard before deleting a successfully verified private tombstone. Never hold it across lsof, git subprocesses, retry sleep, or caller work. Guard contention returns Removed=false and a stable diagnostic; RunGitWithIndexLockRecovery retains the existing RecoveryAttempts and LiveOwnerWait bounds.

Keep RecoverGitIndexLock, RunGitWithIndexLockRecovery, and existing caller signatures unchanged. Do not write DDx metadata into index.lock and do not introduce a lease or release API: native Git remains the sole index-lock owner.

Add deterministic subprocess and barrier tests. Stage signals must be emitted from inside candidate identity capture and actual advisory-guard acquisition. Force both contenders to capture stale S before A renames it; keep A inside the guard after rename, create byte-distinct fresh W at the canonical path, then release delayed B with its old candidate. Prove B cannot move, alter, or delete W. Add crash-release, stable-sidecar identity, owner-probe fail-closed, malformed-path, bounded-contention, and linked-worktree path tests.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change StaleAge, LsofTimeout, RecoveryAttempts, LiveOwnerWait, native Git lockfile behavior, lockmetrics caps, tracker locks, collection locks, or main-git lock semantics. Do not write owner_token, pid, or timestamp metadata into Git's index.lock. Do not extract a shared lock package; Phase 1 WB-8 owns consolidation. Orphan private-tombstone reaping after a process crash is separate cleanup work.

## Status update (filed 2026-04-29 12:50 UTC)

The bulk of this unification **already shipped** as `ddx-87fb72c2` (epic `ddx-fdd3ea36`) before this epic was filed:

- `agent.routing.profile_ladders` and `agent.routing.model_overrides` are now opt-in (consulted only with `--escalate` / `--override-model`).
- The default execute path on the CLI (`cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go`) calls `ResolveRoute` once per attempt instead of iterating a tier ladder.
- `agent.routing.default_harness` was removed (hard error if still present).
- `agent.ResolveTierCandidates` (from `ddx-5538aa5b`) replaced the broken literal-tier-name-as-Model pattern; tier resolution now consults the catalog.
- See `docs/migrations/routing-config.md` for the migration the user-facing CLI surface follows.

**Remaining gap (this epic now scopes only this):** the server worker path in `cli/internal/server/workers.go:650` was not updated by `ddx-87fb72c2`. It still derives `escalationEnabled := spec.Harness == "" && spec.Model == ""` instead of mirroring the CLI's `escalate && harness == "" && model == ""`. That mismatch is why `ddx work` (default mode, server-submit) still hits "all tiers exhausted — no viable provider" with `model_overrides` pointing at non-served models, while `ddx work --local --no-adaptive-min-tier` succeeds. Verified live in this session: `worker-20260429T033325-bedf` failed; `--no-adaptive-min-tier` got `ddx-98e6e9ef` to merge at `115b47c0` on local-tier qwen for zero cost.

Sole child: `ddx-c7081f89`. Once that lands, this epic closes.

## Strategic direction (preserved for future reference)

DDx embeds the agent SDK as a Go library to produce traceable execution units: `(bead, input_state) → (output_state, processing_metadata)`. DDx owns the execution unit and its metadata (bead events, cost ledger, escalation summary, evidence directories), and it owns operator policy (`--harness`/`--model`/`--profile`/`--max-cost`/`--no-review`/`--escalate`). It does **not** need to own provider/harness/cost/local-first routing — agent SDK already does that.

| Concern | DDx (now, post-87fb72c2) | Agent SDK |
|---|---|---|
| Profile selection | `RouteRequest.Profile` straight to agent | `default/cheap/standard/smart/local/offline/air-gapped/fast/code-smart/code-high` |
| Per-tier model pinning | opt-in via `--override-model` | `RouteRequest.Model` |
| Escalation on no-provider | opt-in via `--escalate` (CLI path); **not yet on server worker path** | `escalateProfileLadder` walks `ProfileEscalationLadder=[cheap,standard,smart]` on `ErrNoLiveProvider` |
| Cost-aware ranking | n/a (delegated) | `internal/routing/score.go` ranks by `CostClass` (local=0 wins) |
| Adaptive success-rate gating | `escalation.AdaptiveMinTier` (sticky 50-window cheap-tier lockout, only consumed via `--escalate`) | `routing.Inputs.HistoricalSuccess map[harness]float64` |
| Decision trace | bead events `kind:tier-attempt` per RouteCandidate | `RouteDecision.Candidates []RouteCandidate` |

## Optional follow-ups (not in this epic — file separately if/when needed)

These are no longer blockers; track separately if pursued:

- **Default profile = `local`** so the operator-default honors the local-LLM-first goal without an explicit `--profile local`. Currently default is `default` which maps via project config.
- **Inject `routing.Inputs.HistoricalSuccess` per-harness** to replace `escalation.AdaptiveMinTier` with agent-native success-rate routing. Frees DDx from maintaining its own success-window state machine.
- **Delete `cli/internal/agent/profile_ladder.go` helpers** once no caller (CLI or server) consumes them. Currently consumed only via `--escalate`; if `--escalate` is dropped or moved into agent, these can go.
- **Delete `cli/internal/escalation/escalation.go::AdaptiveMinTier`** once the HistoricalSuccess injection above is in place.

## Out of scope for this epic

- Changes to agent SDK source — if a gap is found, file an upstream bead under `~/Projects/agent/.ddx/`.
- UI/e2e work — the parent e2e drift epic `ddx-ccdf9cf9` covers that and is independent.
- Server source changes outside `cli/internal/server/workers.go` — no API endpoint changes, no GraphQL schema changes.

description:
PROBLEM
During the current monitor on 2026-05-15, a worker executing ddx-bdc0065e cancelled several stale beads. Multiple ddx bead update commands ran close together from the execute-bead context. The tracker ended clean, but the auto-commit audit trail was noisy: one commit subject said it updated ddx-387a0178 while it also picked up additional bead-row changes, another update failed with .git/index.lock, and another commit reported nothing to commit. That makes tracker history misleading and is the same class of dirty/index-lock noise the operator wants eliminated.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/cmd/bead.go:134-154 builds bead auto-commit config and calls bead.AutoCommitFilesWithRecovery directly. cli/internal/bead/git_autocommit.go:10-17 wraps git add/commit with gitlock.RunGitWithIndexLockRecovery, but that only recovers from stale/transient .git/index.lock; it does not serialize the whole add/commit pair under the process-shared main git lock. cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go:98-118 documents and implements withMainGitLock/withTrackerLock for primary-checkout git writes, and cli/internal/gitlock/gitlock.go:22-24 says DDx writers serialize through that lock, but the bead CLI auto-commit path is outside it.

PROPOSED FIX
- Route bead CLI auto-commit add/commit operations through the same process-shared main git lock used by landing and pre-dispatch checkpointing.
- Preserve existing stale index.lock recovery inside the lock, so stale locks are still repaired and live owners still fail or wait according to policy.
- Add a concurrent regression where multiple bead update/create auto-commits run against one repo and produce either deterministic serialized commits or one explicitly combined commit; no index.lock failures, no misleading commit subjects that omit paths actually included.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change .ddx/beads.jsonl format.
- Do not remove auto-commit recovery for stale index locks.
- Do not squash, amend, or rewrite existing execute-bead history.
- Do not hand-edit .ddx/beads.jsonl.

description:
PROBLEM: `go test ./internal/server/...` hits the 600s test timeout. The goroutine dump shows hundreds of leaked fizeau aliveness / quota-refresh / refresh-scheduler goroutines waiting in `select { <-ctx.Done() }`, and the test driver goroutine itself is stuck in `svc.RouteStatus(ctx)` → `subprocessHarnessAutoRoutingModels` → `pi --list-models` subprocess wait. Under CI / loaded systems the synchronous subprocess wait inside `RouteStatus` exceeds any reasonable per-test budget, compounding with the goroutine accumulation.

ROOT CAUSE:
1. `cli/internal/agent/serviceconfig.go:88` (`NewServiceFromWorkDir`) and `cli/internal/agent/serviceconfig.go:96` (`NewStatusProbeServiceFromWorkDir`) construct the fizeau service with `agentlib.ServiceOptions{}` — leaving `QuotaRefreshContext` as `context.Background()`. Inside fizeau (`service.go:1079`), this drives `startAlivenessProbeLoop`, `startQuotaRecoveryProbeLoop`, `startPrimaryQuotaRefreshWorker`, and `refreshScheduler.Start(startupCtx)`, all of which spawn goroutines that only terminate on ctx cancel. Every short-lived HTTP / MCP / GraphQL request that constructs a fresh service leaks ~6 goroutines for the lifetime of the test binary.
2. `cli/internal/server/providers.go:108`, `providers.go:113`, `providers.go:130`, `providers.go:142`, `providers.go:391`, `providers.go:411` — `listHarnessInfos` and `liveRouteStatusReport` use the bare-`Background` factory. `svc.RouteStatus(ctx)` internally invokes `pi.DefaultModelSnapshot` at `fizeau@v0.14.33/internal/harnesses/pi/runner.go:352`, which hard-codes `context.Background()` when shelling out to `pi --list-models` — meaning the caller's ctx deadline does not propagate.
3. Same pattern leaks at `cli/internal/server/agent_models.go:38`, `agent_models.go:138`, `cli/internal/server/workers.go:853`, `workers.go:868`, `cli/internal/server/graphql/resolver_providers.go:83`, `resolver_providers.go:99`, `resolver_providers.go:193`, `resolver_providers.go:309`, and `cli/internal/server/graphql/resolver_provider_models.go:176`.

PROPOSED FIX:
- Add `agent.NewServiceFromWorkDirCtx(ctx, workDir)` and `agent.NewStatusProbeServiceFromWorkDirCtx(ctx, workDir)` in `internal/agent/serviceconfig.go` that pipe ctx into `ServiceOptions.QuotaRefreshContext`. Document the goroutine-lifecycle caveat on both the legacy and ctx-aware factories.
- Update all 11 server-package callsites (HTTP handlers, MCP wrappers, GraphQL resolvers, worker manager) to use the ctx-aware factory. HTTP / MCP handlers get a bounded 10s timeout (`providerHandlerTimeout`) so a slow upstream subprocess cannot stall the request indefinitely.
- Wrap `svc.RouteStatus` and `svc.ListHarnesses` calls in `internal/server/providers.go` in detached goroutines bounded by ctx, since the upstream library still ignores ctx in some subprocess paths (pi/runner.go:352).
- Fix the one in-test direct `agent.NewServiceFromWorkDir(dir)` call in `internal/server/providers_test.go` to use the ctx-aware variant with a `t.Cleanup`-bound cancel.

NON-SCOPE:
- Upstream fizeau context-propagation bug (pi/runner.go:352, `DefaultModelSnapshot` ignoring ctx) is not fixed here — it would require a fizeau release. The detached-goroutine wrapper compensates.
- The agent-dispatch flow used by TestMCPAgentDispatchTrustedAllowed has the same upstream blocker for its own reasons; not in this bead.
- Pre-existing perf-budget flake `TestServerStateBeadSnapshotLatencyBudget` (p95 > 50ms under load) is unrelated.
title: fix(server): pipe ctx into fizeau service to cancel probe goroutines and bound RouteStatus subprocess hang

description:
PROBLEM
  After sister bead ddx-1f774edf removes network I/O from Land(), the
  drain becomes safe for external parallelism (multiple ddx work --once
  shells running concurrently). However, parallel workers will land their
  own bead's worktree against the same local main and may produce
  overlapping changes — multi-worker conflict frequency on Land()'s
  git merge step is unmeasured. The 2026-05-09 plan-review opus
  self-review identified this as a key risk: under high parallelism,
  preservation (resource_exhausted to iteration ref) could become the
  common path rather than the exception, defeating the gain.

  This bead adds chaos coverage for the parallel-landing case and a
  sentinel that fails if the preservation rate exceeds an acceptable
  threshold under simulated load.

CURRENT STATE
  - cli/internal/bead/chaos_test.go and chaos2_test.go cover
    bead.Store-layer concurrency only.
  - cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock_test.go covers single-worker
    semantics.
  - Sister bead ddx-c019e48a covers stale-lock recovery for a single
    worker's local-only land. It does not cover N>1 workers landing in
    parallel.
  - No test verifies what happens when worker A lands branch-A into
    main, then worker B (whose worktree was branched from pre-A main)
    tries to land branch-B with overlapping changes.

PROPOSED FIX
  Add three chaos tests in cli/internal/agent/landing_chaos_test.go (new
  file, or extend tracker_lock_test.go):

  1. TestConcurrentLand_NonOverlappingChanges_BothLandClean:
     - Spawn 3 worker goroutines, each with its own bead/worktree
       touching disjoint files.
     - All three call Land() concurrently.
     - Assert: all three land on local main, in some order; no
       preservation; main contains all three commits.

  2. TestConcurrentLand_OverlappingChanges_OneLandsRestPreserve:
     - Spawn 3 worker goroutines, each touching the same file with
       different content.
     - All three call Land() concurrently.
     - Assert: exactly one lands; the other two are preserved to
       iteration refs; the preserved branches are intact and contain
       their bead's full work.

  3. TestConcurrentLand_PreservationRateUnderLoadIsBounded:
     - Spawn N worker goroutines (N=4) over M cycles (M=10), each with
       a randomized mix of overlapping/non-overlapping changes.
     - Assert: preservation rate is < 50% (i.e., at least half of
       attempts land cleanly). This is a smoke check that parallel
       drain is viable, not a hard SLA.

  Use deterministic timing (channels or synctest), not wall-clock.
  Use testutils.NewFixtureRepo or t.TempDir() per test.
  Depends on sister bead ddx-1f774edf so the lock holds are sub-second
  (otherwise the test exercises today's contention bug, not the
  parallel-landing concern).

NON-SCOPE
  - Multi-process chaos (these are goroutine-level concurrent landings
    using fake LandingGitOps that mirror the real merge logic).
  - Coordinating workers via a "land queue" abstraction (separate
    architectural concern; this bead establishes the baseline measurement
    against which any such work would be evaluated).

INTERSECTIONS
  - Sister bead ddx-1f774edf (depends on it landing first).
  - Sister bead (just-filed) "agent/lock: instrument bead.Store
    WithLock wait time" — its metrics are referenced by these tests'
    assertions if available.
  - Sister bead ddx-c019e48a complements this for the single-worker
    stale-lock case.
title: agent/chaos: cover concurrent-drain landing under shared-main contention

acceptance:
1. Add `TestExecuteBeadWorkerCannotMutatePrimaryGitConfig` or equivalent, using a real primary repo plus execute-bead worktree, that contaminates the worker attempt with commands such as `git config --local core.bare true`, `git config --local user.email fixture@ddx.test`, and a nested test subprocess with Git-local env vars set.
2. The test asserts after the attempt that the primary checkout satisfies `git status --short`, has no `core.bare`, has no stray `core.worktree`, and does not contain fixture `user.name`/`user.email`.
3. The fix ensures linked worktree attempts have per-worktree config isolation and/or scrubbed Git env for all agent/test subprocesses that DDx launches.
4. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./cmd/... ./internal/git/... -run "TestExecuteBeadWorkerCannotMutatePrimaryGitConfig|TestGitFixtureHelpersStripHookEnv|TestCheckGitRepoHealthDetectsCoreBare" -count=1` passes.
5. `sh scripts/git-config-health.sh` passes after the new regression runs.
6. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.
description:
PROBLEM
During live `ddx work --watch --harness codex --model gpt-5.4` on bead `ddx-fa6eedcc` at 2026-05-15 05:38 ET, the primary checkout `/Users/erik/Projects/ddx` flipped to `core.bare=true`. `git status --short` in the primary checkout failed with `fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree`; `git config --local --get core.bare` returned `true`. I repaired the local checkout with `git config --unset-all --local core.bare`, but worker attempts must not be able to corrupt the operator's primary repo config.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
`cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:391-396` creates linked worktrees with `git worktree add --detach`; `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1242-1247` launches the worker in that isolated worktree. Doctor knows the corruption class at `cli/cmd/doctor.go:1035-1044` (`extensions.worktreeConfig` disabled can corrupt shared config), but this incident occurred while the main repo had `extensions.worktreeConfig=true`, so the execute-bead isolation contract still lacks an end-to-end guard that worker commands and tests cannot mutate the primary checkout's `.git/config` or `.git/config.worktree`.

PROPOSED FIX
Add an execute-bead regression that snapshots the primary checkout git config before a worker attempt, runs a script/agent attempt that intentionally tries to set `core.bare=true` and fixture identity from inside the attempt worktree and test subprocesses, and proves the primary checkout remains a valid worktree with no `core.bare`, no stray `core.worktree`, and no leaked fixture user config after the attempt. Harden the worker environment or worktree setup as needed.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken git-config-health hooks. Do not hide the failure by suppressing `git status` errors. Do not rewrite execute-bead history or skip worker isolation; the fix must preserve isolated worktree execution while protecting the primary checkout.
title: execute-bead: prevent worker attempts from mutating primary git config

description:
PROBLEM
During ddx-42124c23 verification on 2026-06-13, `lefthook run pre-commit` exited 0 even though its `go-test` step printed FAIL for `github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/ddx/cmd`. That makes the required automated gate a false green and lets broken verification pass.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
lefthook.yml:206-214 builds a package list from staged paths and runs `go test -short -race -timeout 30m "./$pkg"` inside a shell `for pkg in $packages; do ... done` loop. The script does not accumulate failures or `set -e`, so when an early package fails and a later package passes, the shell returns the last command status. In the observed run, `cmd` failed but `internal/activework` and `internal/agent` passed, and Lefthook reported a successful hook.

PROPOSED FIX
Make the staged-package go-test hook fail if any package test fails. Preserve per-package output. Add a deterministic test or script-level check that simulates two packages where the first fails and the second passes and proves the hook exits non-zero.

NON-SCOPE
Do not fix the unrelated existing `cmd` package failures in this bead unless they are needed to prove the hook status propagation. Do not relax the staged package test gate.
title: test: make pre-commit go-test fail when any package fails

acceptance:
- [ ] New command or subcommand: `ddx doctor divergence` or `ddx divergence check` prints the divergence report
- [ ] Thresholds are configurable via .ddx/config.yaml (default: 5 commits each side, 7 days merge-base age)
- [ ] work refuses to start in ERROR state unless --force passed
- [ ] Structured event 'divergence_status' emitted at loop start and on every doctor run
- [ ] Optional webhook integration via config.yaml alert_webhook_url
- [ ] Unit tests: each state (clean, ahead, behind, diverged, network-down, drift)
- [ ] Integration test: run the loop on a diverged repo and observe the refuse-to-start behavior
- [ ] Docs: README section on divergence monitoring, thresholds, and how to recover
description:
Fifth child of ddx-b7ee0d6f. The 14-day silent divergence on axon (eitri local 134 commits ahead of merge-base, sindri/origin 336 commits ahead) was caught only because a human happened to try pushing. A trivial monitor running a few times a day would have flagged the problem at 5 commits, not 470.

## Required behavior

Add a lightweight divergence check that runs either:
- At the top of each work iteration (cheap, ~50ms), OR
- Periodically via a scheduled task (ddx doctor or similar), OR
- Both

The check computes:
- `git fetch origin <branch>` (tolerant of network failure)
- local_ahead = `git rev-list --count origin/<branch>..HEAD`
- origin_ahead = `git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/<branch>`
- merge_base_age = `git log -1 --format=%ar $(git merge-base HEAD origin/<branch>)`

Emit a structured event 'divergence_status' with these fields. If:
- local_ahead > threshold (default 5): warn
- origin_ahead > threshold (default 5): warn
- both > 0: ERROR — diverged, neither side is a strict ancestor
- merge_base_age > threshold (default 7 days): warn (drift)

Integration surface:
- `ddx doctor` prints the divergence report
- `ddx agent work` refuses to start if in the ERROR state (both sides ahead) unless --force is passed
- An optional webhook / notification channel (config: alert_webhook_url) for ops teams

## Why this is P1 not P0

The fetch/push/rebase triad (P0) prevents NEW divergence. This bead catches EXISTING divergence and alerts before it grows. Without the P0 fixes, this alert would fire constantly; with them, it should fire rarely. Still valuable as defense in depth.

## Test cases

- Fresh clone: report is clean (0 ahead / 0 behind)
- Local 3 commits ahead: report shows local_ahead=3, no warning
- Local 6 commits ahead: report shows local_ahead=6, warning emitted
- Both sides ahead: ERROR status, work refuses to start
- Merge base 10 days old with both sides at 0: drift warning, work continues
- Network unreachable: report shows 'unknown', no ERROR, work continues
title: work: divergence monitoring and alerting

acceptance:
1. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go: when implementer returns no_changes (BaseRev == ResultRev and zero commits), reviewer dispatch is skipped.
2. The existing no_changes triage path handles routing; behavior is preserved (labels, cooldowns, status transitions match pre-change baseline).
3. A "reviewer-skipped-empty-diff" event is emitted on each skip so operators can see the optimization.
4. TestNoChanges_SkipsReviewer asserts reviewer is NOT invoked when outcome is no_changes.
5. TestSomeChanges_StillInvokesReviewer asserts reviewer IS invoked when implementer produced any commit.
6. TestNoChangesWithReviewSpecGapClassification_RoutesToProposed asserts spec-gap path still routes to proposed without reviewer gating.
7. TestReviewerSkippedEmptyDiffEvent asserts the structured event is emitted.
8. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./cmd/... green.
9. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
  When an implementer attempt produces no_changes (BaseRev ==
  ResultRev, no commits), the drain still dispatches the reviewer
  agent. The reviewer is paid for an empty-diff review; it
  contributes nothing because there are no changes to evaluate.
  This is pure cost waste — the no_changes triage path (existing,
  cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go around the no_changes
  outcome handling) already routes the bead correctly without
  needing a reviewer signal.

  Per ADR-024 P1 (cheapest first), the reviewer's cost on an
  empty-diff dispatch is unjustified. Cost optimization includes
  "skip the unnecessary".

CURRENT STATE
  - cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go: when implementer
    returns no_changes, the dispatch flow proceeds to reviewer
    invocation regardless.
  - No early-exit / lazy-dispatch logic.
  - Reviewer cost: typically smart-tier, $0.30-1.00 per invocation.
  - Multiplied across N no_changes attempts per bead (N=2-3 in
    smart-retry path), this is real money on no-op operations.

PROPOSED FIX
  - cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go: before invoking the
    reviewer, check the implementer outcome:
      - If outcome is no_changes (BaseRev == ResultRev and zero
        commits produced): skip reviewer entirely.
      - Route directly to the existing no_changes triage path
        (which classifies, applies labels, sets cooldowns or
        re-status as needed).
      - Emit a "reviewer-skipped-empty-diff" event so operators
        can see the optimization fired.
  - Preserve all existing no_changes handling logic — the only
    change is "don't pay the reviewer when there's nothing to
    review."
  - Edge case: review_spec_gap diagnosis happens at the IMPLEMENTER
    level (the implementer says "I can't because the spec is
    gappy"); the reviewer doesn't gate this. Confirm the no_changes
    triage path handles the spec-gap routing without reviewer.

  Tests:
     - TestNoChanges_SkipsReviewer: assert reviewer is NOT invoked
       when implementer outcome is no_changes.
     - TestSomeChanges_StillInvokesReviewer: assert reviewer IS
       invoked when implementer produced any commit.
     - TestNoChangesWithReviewSpecGapClassification_RoutesToProposed:
       assert the spec-gap path still routes to proposed without
       reviewer gating.
     - TestReviewerSkippedEmptyDiffEvent: assert event is emitted.

NON-SCOPE
  - Skipping reviewer for non-no_changes outcomes (out of scope;
    those genuinely need review).
  - Tuning reviewer dispatch for partial-changes cases (out of
    scope).

INTERSECTIONS
  - Sister bead ddx-451cdead (ADR-024 amendment) — P1 cost
    optimization principle.
  - Sister bead ddx-cf79f10c (no_changes stepwise) — same
    no_changes path; this bead skips the reviewer cost; that
    bead handles the implementer escalation. Compose cleanly.
title: feat(review): skip reviewer dispatch when implementer produced no commits

description:
PROBLEM
ddx work --watch's pre-claim intake decoder fails to unmarshal the readiness_checks response when verdict is a JSON bool. Every claim attempt produces the identical warn-only rejection ("decode result: json: cannot unmarshal bool into Go struct field .readiness_checks.verdict of type string"), so the worker logs a warning and skips. With a full ready queue and a single fizeau-scoped daemon, the entire queue goes idle indefinitely. Fizeau observation 2026-05-18 05:27-05:39 UTC: identical fingerprint 15155a1cd44e96daf53eabb14c8eb3ccd8b0e5271d881208cfcbbf2869899f4f recurred across distinct bead_ids, confirming a schema mismatch rather than a bead-specific issue.

ROOT CAUSE
The verdict field in the readiness-check struct is typed as a plain Go string, so encoding/json rejects a bool payload. See cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:77-82 (preClaimReadinessCheck struct) and the decode entry point decodePreClaimIntakePayloadResult / decodePreClaimIntakePayloadResultWithMode at cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:709-725. Producers emit verdict as a JSON bool (true/false) while the consumer parsed string only.

PROPOSED FIX (parent proposed-fix A)
Introduce a custom readinessVerdict type at cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:95-125 with an UnmarshalJSON that accepts JSON bool, JSON string, and null/absent, coercing each to a single documented canonical form (e.g. bool true -> "pass", false -> "fail", string lowercased, null/absent -> empty). Wire the preClaimReadinessCheck.Verdict field to the new type so the array/object payload decoder at cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:386-416 succeeds for every verdict shape.

NON-SCOPE
- CI schema drift gate (sibling child: schema lock).
- Same-fingerprint warn escalation / warn-only 100%-failure guard (sibling child: escalation).
- claim-success-rate operator signal (sibling child: claim-rate window).
- README documentation (sibling child: docs).

CROSS-REF
Governing artifact: AR-2026-05-17 follow-up beads (blocked by this idle). Adjacent silent-failure bugs in this session: ddx-57c40485 (index.lock held minutes), ddx-8f2e0ebf (worker wedges on route resolution). Shared theme: silent failures inside the worker that look healthy from the outside.
title: pre-claim intake decoder: accept readiness_checks[].verdict as JSON bool, string, or absent

description:
PROBLEM
There is no reusable parser for DDx document status stamps, so verification-coverage, duplicate-id, stale-observation, and CLI checks cannot reliably distinguish Complete/Implemented/Proposed/In Progress/Deferred/Aspirational documents from unstamped SD/TD/ADR documents.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The Phase 2 plan defines WB-1 as a new `cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/` lint package and states that status markers are heterogeneous: body `**Status:**` lines, YAML frontmatter `status:`, and 40 of 56 design docs with no marker, including SD-013 and TD-027 (`docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:58`, `docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:60`). The intended local pattern is a sibling lint package with analyzer, tests, and fixtures (`cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer.go:39`, `cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer_test.go:12`), but `cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/` is absent.

PROPOSED FIX
Create `cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/` with `analyzer.go`, `analyzer_test.go`, and focused Markdown test fixtures. Implement a deterministic, read-only parser API that recognizes a body `**Status:**` line and YAML frontmatter `status:` key, normalizes free-text qualifiers to a base status such as `Complete`, `Implemented`, `Proposed`, `In Progress`, `Deferred`, or `Aspirational`, and reports missing status for SD/TD/ADR documents. This child only builds the parser and package foundation; it does not need to wire a command-line docs-directory traversal.

NON-SCOPE
Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Do not implement verification-coverage, waiver, duplicate-id, or stale-observation logic here. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not add pre-commit or CI wiring in this child.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
`docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md` WB-1, especially steps 1-2 and validation expectations at lines 58-72.

description:
PROBLEM
After an unpinned `ddx work` successfully merged ddx-c3219628, later ready beads failed before agent execution because `.ddx/metrics/attempts.jsonl` remained dirty and the pre-execute checkpoint guard treated it as implementation work. The worker failed ddx-6cde5ffd, ddx-9d39d510, and ddx-c019e48a with `checkpoint refused to absorb implementation changes outside DDx bookkeeping: .ddx/metrics/attempts.jsonl`.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:719-733` defines `preDispatchCheckpointAllowedPath` for DDx bookkeeping paths, but it includes beads, executions, runs, and run-state paths only.
- Attempt metrics written to `.ddx/metrics/attempts.jsonl` are durable DDx bookkeeping produced by the worker after an attempt, but they are not included in the checkpoint allowlist.
- The next queue iteration therefore fails before execution even though the dirty path is DDx-owned evidence, not bead implementation work.

PROPOSED FIX
Allow `.ddx/metrics/` paths in the pre-dispatch checkpoint guard so metrics dirt is checkpointed with the same DDx bookkeeping treatment as `.ddx/beads.jsonl`, `.ddx/executions/`, `.ddx/runs/`, and `.ddx/run-state/`. Add regression coverage that writes `.ddx/metrics/attempts.jsonl` and proves `checkpointPreDispatchDirt` commits it instead of rejecting it.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken rejection of non-DDx implementation files. Do not change metrics schema or attempt cost accounting. Do not ignore metrics silently; they should remain durable evidence.
title: execute-bead: checkpoint attempt metrics bookkeeping

description:
Reopening a closed bead after a failing review currently takes 3-4 separate commands: update --status open, update --notes (append), optionally update --description, optionally update --acceptance. This is error-prone and loses the atomicity guarantee that a reopen is a single logical event.

## Scope
- ddx bead reopen <id> [--reason <text>] [--append-notes <text>]
- Atomically: set status=open, append a reopen event to the event log, optionally append notes, clear claim fields
- Emit an event of kind=reopen that shows in ddx bead show
- Works from CLI and from ddx agent work review-rejection path

## Context
Observed during axon ADR-018 loop: first attempt merged, opus review rejected, I had to run three ddx bead update commands plus a description rewrite to get the bead back into a ready-for-second-attempt state. An atomic reopen would have been one command.

description:
PROBLEM
When a worker abandons a bead (route-resolution timeout, watchdog fire, or any failure release), the bead's claim/lease must be cleared atomically and `ddx bead status` must reflect the lease state. Claiming a bead today atomically transitions it to in_progress, but there is no symmetric release path that, in a single locked write, transitions the bead back and clears the lease. The parent bug (ddx-8f2e0ebf) observed "bead has a claim but ddx bead status shows In progress: 0" — claim and lifecycle status not atomically coupled on the release side.

ROOT CAUSE
cli/internal/bead/store.go: Store.Claim (~lines 863-930) is atomic — under WithLock it calls transitionLifecycleInPlace(StatusInProgress) + sets Owner + WriteAll, then writeClaimHeartbeat writes the lease sidecar. There is NO symmetric Store.Release that, under the same WithLock, transitions status back (default open), clears Owner, WriteAll, AND removes the claim-heartbeat lease sidecar in one critical section. Failure-release paths can leave a stale lease sidecar while status reports not-in_progress, producing the phantom-lease inconsistency.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Add Store.Release(id, assignee, targetStatus) mirroring Store.Claim: under WithLock, read beads, transitionLifecycleInPlace to target status (open by default), clear Owner, WriteAll, and remove the claim-heartbeat lease sidecar — all in one locked operation.
2. Route the worker's failure-release paths through Store.Release so claim clearing and status are coupled.
3. Ensure `ddx bead status` counts reflect lease state: a released bead is not counted in_progress and has no owner; a claimed bead is in_progress with an owner.

NON-SCOPE
Route-resolution timeout (sibling child A), heartbeat watchdog (child B), same-bead-twice guard (child D), operator-attention query surface + docs (child E). This bead only establishes atomic claim/release symmetry and status accuracy. This is a decomposition child of ddx-8f2e0ebf.
title: bead: add atomic Store.Release so failure-release clears the claim and status reflects the lease
