description:
<context-digest>
Review area: execute-bead semantics, executable bead contracts, readiness validation, and DDx/HELIX boundary ownership. Evidence covers FEAT-006, FEAT-010, FEAT-013, SD-012, server-driven execution discussions, and cli/cmd/agent_execute_bead.go.
</context-digest>
Define DDx bead execution around the functional model `W' = execute(bead, W)`, where `W` is a clean git-backed workspace input state and `ddx agent execute-bead` materializes that state in an isolated worktree before mutation.

## Required design outcomes
1. Clarify that `ddx agent execute-bead` starts from a resolved base revision, treats the caller's dirty worktree as outside the transform, checkpoints it separately, and executes only against the isolated worktree state.
2. Define the bead as the executable transform contract: the bead must carry the instruction/prompt, acceptance, declared context inputs, execution policy, landing/preservation policy, and post-run validation policy needed for replayable execution.
3. Unwind DDx designs that currently imply DDx derives governing artifacts, prompt construction, or workflow policy from the live document graph at execution time. DDx should provide composable graph/exec tools, not hidden workflow orchestration.
4. Define a generic DDx execution-readiness validation surface for beads, such as `ddx bead validate --execution` or equivalent inspection semantics, that checks structural executability without embedding HELIX-specific policy.
5. Specify the success/failure state machine around execution: structural validation, agent execution, post-run validity checks / required executions, preserve-on-failure evidence semantics, and land-on-success semantics.
6. Make the automation boundary explicit: future humans, HELIX flows, or `ddx server` worker pools must consume the explicit bead contract and validator output rather than relying on hidden prompt assembly or runtime artifact inference.
7. Preserve room for multi-project server execution: the contract must not assume a single served repo or a single server process, and must remain valid when project-scoped worktrees are managed by a multi-project `ddx server`.
8. Make HELIX's responsibility explicit: HELIX should author the executable bead contract and create a new contract document in `docs/helix/02-design/contracts/` that defines the DDx/HELIX boundary for executable bead execution. The contracts directory does not currently exist in this repo, so this work must establish it.

## Spec and design scope
- Reconcile FEAT-006 agent-service workflow with the workspace-transform model
- Reconcile FEAT-010 execution-definition language so execution selection and required checks are explicit input or separately composed query output, not hidden bead-context derivation
- Preserve FEAT-013's substrate-not-orchestration boundary while still supporting async server-managed worker pools
- Align SD-012 git-awareness wording with the actual clean-input/worktree model, checkpoint semantics, and preserve-vs-land outcomes
- Establish how the generic execution-readiness surface is consumed by future automation without embedding HELIX policy in DDx

## Expected artifact work
- New contract under `docs/helix/02-design/contracts/` for the executable bead boundary
- Updates to the affected feature / solution design docs so they all describe the same execution contract
- Follow-on design beads for server-managed supervision and multi-project server topology
- Follow-on implementation beads only after the contract is settled
title: Define execute-bead workspace-transform contract and readiness validation

acceptance:
AC1. ResolveTierModelRef (or its replacement) consults the model catalog as the default source of tier→model mapping when agent.routing.model_overrides is not set, returning the first surface→model pair whose harness is available and whose model resolves to a healthy provider.

AC2. `ddx agent work --once --local --no-adaptive-min-tier` succeeds against a fresh project (no model_overrides in .ddx/config.yaml) when the catalog has at least one tier with a reachable harness/model/provider chain.

AC3. When EVERY catalog surface for the resolved tier is unreachable, the tier-attempt event records the concrete reason for each surface tried (e.g. 'codex: harness not installed', 'claude: provider cooldown', 'embedded-openai: model qwen3.6 has no reachable provider'), not a generic 'no viable harness found' with empty fields.

AC4. `ddx agent doctor` (or `ddx agent catalog show`) emits a warning when a tier's catalog entries reference a model id that has no matching named route AND no provider /v1/models entry across configured providers, so the user discovers the gap before invoking work.

description:
When agent.routing.model_overrides is not set in a project's .ddx/config.yaml, ResolveTierModelRef in cli/internal/agent/profile_ladder.go:44 returns the literal tier name ("cheap", "standard", "smart") as the model identifier. ResolveRoute is then called with model="cheap"/"standard"/"smart" — strings that match no model id and no named route. Every tier resolves to an empty harness/empty model and is recorded as a tier-attempt with body "no viable harness found". The loop exhausts all tiers and reports "work: all tiers exhausted — no viable provider found".

This is happening today on a workstation that has bragi/vidar/hel hosting qwen3.6, plus working claude and codex harnesses. execute-bead succeeds with the same providers when --harness/--model are pinned explicitly, proving the underlying routing is fine. Only the tier→model resolution path is broken.

The model catalog (~/.ddx/model-catalog.yaml or built-in defaults, surfaced via `ddx agent catalog show`) ALREADY contains the tier→surface→model mapping that would make this work. The resolver just doesn't consume it. Surfaces and concrete models are listed per tier (e.g. cheap: embedded-openai→qwen3.5-27b, codex→gpt-5.4-mini, claude→claude-haiku-4-5) — the resolver should walk these surfaces in order, picking the first whose harness is healthy and whose model resolves to a reachable provider via model_routes. Per-project model_overrides should be an OPTIONAL override layered on top of catalog defaults, not the only thing that makes tier resolution work.

Caller-side workaround: every project must add agent.routing.model_overrides to .ddx/config.yaml before work will function. This is silent: there is no diagnostic from `ddx agent doctor`, no warning from `ddx agent catalog show`, and no hint in the "no viable provider" error pointing at the missing config. Users have to read source to understand why a fully-healthy provider/harness fleet produces zero viable tiers.

Repro:
1. Fresh project with .ddx/config.yaml lacking agent.routing.model_overrides
2. Healthy provider config in ~/.config/agent/config.yaml (any qwen/claude/codex)
3. `ddx agent work --once --local --no-adaptive-min-tier`
4. Every tier-attempt event records "no viable harness found"; loop exits with 'all tiers exhausted'

Related symptom — the adaptive min-tier promotion uses cheap-tier success rate to skip cheap, but with the bug above no cheap-tier attempt has ever produced a successful harness invocation, so the trailing window is biased to 0% by design rather than by actual model performance.
title: work: tier resolver should consume catalog instead of requiring per-project model_overrides

description:
# PROBLEM
The current Axon migration path still rewrites the JSONL corpus into `.ddx/axon/` instead of inserting rows into Postgres. `cli/internal/bead/migrate.go:623-680` reads active + archive JSONL and calls `writeAxonSnapshotFiles`, while `cli/internal/bead/migrator.go:54-57` still returns `ErrDeprecated` from `MigrateToAxon`. There is no importer path that exercises `axonStore.Create` / `axonStore.Apply`.

# ROOT CAUSE
`migrateToAxon` is a snapshot copier, not a data importer. It deduplicates in-memory beads and serializes them back to axon JSONL files, which cannot populate Lakebase Postgres or prove row-level write semantics.

# PROPOSED FIX
- Add `cli/internal/bead/internal/storage/import_postgres.go` or equivalent with an importer that reads `.ddx/beads.jsonl` and `.ddx/beads-archive.jsonl`.
- Use `axonStore.Create(ctx, &b)` for bead insertion and `axonStore.Apply(ctx, id, AppendEventOp{...})` for event appends.
- Treat conflict errors as idempotent skips, not failures.
- Preserve event ordering by `created_at` when appending imported events.
- Add tests that prove the write path uses the Postgres-style API and is safe to re-run.

# NON-SCOPE
- Dry-run accounting, verification read-back, and attachment upload behavior.
- CLI flag parsing and command help changes.
- Real-wire Postgres integration; this bead only makes the importer logic executable against the AxonStore abstraction used by tests.

# ACCEPTANCE
1. `cli/internal/bead/internal/storage/import_postgres.go` (or equivalent) exists and the implementation calls `axonStore.Create` plus `axonStore.Apply` for bead + event writes.
2. `TestImporter_Apply_WritesToPostgres` proves the importer writes the expected rows/events through the backend abstraction.
3. `TestImporter_Apply_Idempotent_OnReRun` proves a second apply skips existing rows instead of duplicating them.
4. `TestImporter_PreservesEventOrdering` proves imported events are appended in monotonic `created_at` order.
5. `cd cli && go test ./internal/bead/...` is green.
6. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.

PROBLEM
The spechonesty analyzer has no way to tell whether a Verification mapping row's evidence target names an inspectable runtime artifact, nor to resolve that target to a concrete path it can inspect. Without that resolution step, a Complete/Implemented stamp can rest on an artifact name nobody can check.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and no component classifies or resolves runtime-artifact evidence targets parsed from Verification rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, which requires every Complete/Implemented mapping row to name an exact evidence target, with current-revision executable verification reinforced at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:176.

On top of the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child and the Verification mapping-parser child, add a resolver that (a) classifies a parsed mapping row's evidence target as an inspectable runtime artifact or not, and (b) resolves an inspectable runtime artifact target to a repository path or generated fixture artifact path, reporting resolved/unresolved without network access. The resolver is a pure read-only lookup: it returns resolution results and never emits analyzer diagnostics and never writes files. Diagnostic emission is the sibling child's job.

Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not enforce requirement coverage cardinality or duplicate mapping counts — the coverage-cardinality child owns that. Do not resolve Go Test* symbols or static check names — the evidence-target child owns those checks. Do not enforce command allowlisting — the verification-command allowlist child owns that.

description:
PROBLEM
The mandatory `cd cli && go test -short -race -timeout 30m ./internal/agent` gate recursively launches the package test binary as the hidden DDx provider wrapper. In attempt `20260713T190502-df5adc46`, one `agent.test` spawned five concurrent `agent.test __provider-launch <real-provider>` helpers for more than three minutes, produced a 666 MB testlog, and left a real `codex --no-alt-screen` process reparented to the managed worker for twelve minutes at about 188 MiB RSS. The package gate therefore creates the CPU, memory, and orphan condition it is supposed to prevent.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:102-113` calls `os.Executable()` unconditionally and passes the result to `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH`.
- `cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:152-163` repeats the same unconditional installation.
- `cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go:83-118` writes shims that execute `<ddxBinary> __provider-launch <realBinary>`. Under `go test`, `os.Executable()` is `agent.test`, not the DDx CLI. Re-executing it starts the test suite again because the hidden Cobra command exists only at `cli/cmd/provider_launch.go:25-68`.
- The two call sites and the fail-closed validation must land together: a resolver-only intermediate still lets the full package hook recurse, while a suite-only guard leaves one production call site unsafe.

PROPOSED FIX
Add one provider-shim executable resolver/validator shared by both service call sites. Refuse a Go test executable before creating a shim or mutating PATH, with an actionable diagnostic. Add a suite-wide guard proving package tests never install `agent.test` as the wrapper, while direct provider-wrapper tests continue to supply an explicit real/fake DDx CLI binary. Keep production PATH shims, `Pdeathsig`, dedicated process groups, and the real CLI hidden-command behavior unchanged. Land the resolver, both callers, suite guard, and preservation tests atomically so this child is independently green.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not remove provider parent-death protection in production.
- Do not replace Fizeau routing or provider discovery.
- Do not weaken the full `internal/agent` race gate, merely raise its timeout, or suppress a failed gate.
- Do not kill unrelated provider processes from other repositories.
- Scanner injection remains owned by `ddx-02200b1e`; the predispatch fixture tripwire remains owned by `ddx-26bf19c7`.

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent `ddx-b291b0f6`. No implementation deps. This atomic child replaces invalid deterministic split fragments `ddx-b939e409` and `ddx-d8026131`.

description:
PROBLEM
During the 2026-06-16 DDx repo canary, server-managed worker worker-20260616T203031-1ef9 was cancelled and then exited with `signal: killed` while preparing pre-dispatch commits for bead ddx-d4d764ea. The worker log ended with `tracker_lock section=pre_dispatch_commits wait=0s hold=580ms retries=0`, `Cancel received, shutting down gracefully`, and `tracker_lock section=durable_audit wait=0s hold=3ms retries=0`. The lock metrics then recorded an `index.lock` acquire for `operation=index.commit` by holder_pid=3750227 at 2026-06-16T20:35:38.271560856Z with no release row. After the process was gone, `.git/index.lock` still existed and blocked git status until the operator verified no lsof holder and removed it manually. Desired-count refill correctly spawned worker-20260616T203538-0fad, but the stale lock violated the lock lifetime contract and made the landing worktree unsafe.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/lockmetrics/lockcap.go defines lock cap enforcement, but this canary showed no automatic stale `.git/index.lock` removal or lock-violation artifact when a managed worker died during `index.commit`.
- cli/internal/server/workers.go runExternalWorker finalization records failed/reaped worker exits and refills desired count, but it does not prove or trigger cleanup for git locks owned by the dead worker PID before replacement continues.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go / pre-dispatch commit path emits `pre_dispatch_commits` lock metrics, but the killed worker left an acquire-without-release row and a physical `.git/index.lock` file.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a regression path that simulates or drives a server-managed worker death during an index commit / pre-dispatch commit window, then ensure server/lock-cap cleanup removes stale `.git/index.lock` owned by the dead worker before refill or before the next git operation. Record an operator-visible lock-violation or worker event naming worker id, PID, lock path, operation, and cleanup outcome. Preserve normal lock behavior for live holders; never remove a lock still held by a running process.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change desired-count refill semantics except to make cleanup happen before replacement can proceed. Do not change bead execution routing or startup reconcile stale-project filtering. Do not broaden this bead to all durable-audit SIGKILL classification work tracked by older lock-contention beads; this bead is specifically about stale physical lock cleanup after managed-worker death.

DEPS
No deps.
title: server: release stale index lock after killed managed worker

The work correctly selects and claims beads, but the agent harness never runs the work.
CRITICAL: ddx agent run --harness agent works perfectly on the same machine, pointing to a
model-resolution bug specifically in execute-bead/work.

PROOF: direct agent run works, work fails:
  ddx agent run --text "Hello" --harness agent --timeout 60s → succeeds with qwen3.5-27b on vidar
  ddx agent work --once --json --harness agent → fails with z-ai/glm-5.1 via OpenRouter 404

ROOT CAUSE: Model resolution in execute-bead injects --model z-ai/glm-5.1, overriding the
native ~/.config/agent/config.yaml provider config (default_provider: vidar, model: qwen3.5-27b).
The z-ai/glm-5.1 model is not defined in models.yaml or the native config — it appears to come
from stale execute-bead routing metadata. Even explicit --model flags on work don't
propagate correctly to the spawned execute-bead subprocess.

PROVIDER STATUS on eitri:
- vidar (http://vidar:1234/v1, qwen3.5-27b): WORKS — confirmed with ddx agent run
- bragi (http://bragi:1234/v1, qwen3.5-27b): DOWN — connection refused
- grendel (http://grendel:1234/v1, qwen3.5-27b): DOWN — connection refused
- openrouter (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1): FAILS — 404 guardrail restriction on claude-haiku

MACHINE CONTEXT (eitri, Linux):
- Hostname: eitri, paths use /home/erik/ and linuxbrew
- ~/.config/agent/config.yaml defines providers with default_provider: vidar
- models.yaml defines code-high profile → agent.openai: gpt-5.4 (OpenRouter surface)
- No ~/.ddx.yml config file
- No project-level .agent/config.yaml
- Codex and claude harnesses nearly out of quota — reserved for review, not bulk execution
- work was working previously (existing ddx beads show successful runs)
- z-ai/glm-5.1 string appears nowhere in source — comes from runtime routing metadata

ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES: No AGENT_PROVIDER, AGENT_BASE_URL, AGENT_API_KEY, or AGENT_MODEL set.
All routing comes from native ~/.config/agent/config.yaml.

IMPACT: ddx agent work is the primary execution surface for HELIX beads. If the only
working provider (vidar → qwen3.5-27b) cannot be used from work, entire queues drain
as failures. The loop records each with retry_after (6 hours) and retries indefinitely.

SUGGESTED FIXES:
1. Fix execute-bead model resolution: respect native .agent/config.yaml provider config or
   properly propagate the --model flag from work → execute-bead
2. Add provider health checks: ddx agent doctor should test the actual provider with a
   minimal API call, not just check binary existence
3. Fail open on provider errors: when the default provider fails, fall back to the next
   available provider in config rather than hard-failing
4. Guardrail error clarity: surface OpenRouter 404 as "provider unavailable due to
   account restrictions" rather than generic API error
5. Execute-loop resilience: when all providers fail, mark bead truly blocked instead of
   infinite retry_after cycles

FILES INVOLVED:
- cli/internal/agent/agent_runner.go (resolveNativeAgentProvider, resolveAgentConfig, resolveModel)
- cli/cmd/agent_execute_loop.go (work model flag propagation)
- cli/cmd/agent_execute_bead.go (execute-bead model override logic)
- ~/.config/agent/config.yaml (machine config with vidar provider)

acceptance:
1. ddx work --watch never holds .git/index.lock across an LLM subprocess (claude/codex/gemini/etc.) invocation; lock is released before the subprocess starts and re-acquired only for the actual git mutation. Verified by an integration test that runs an execute-bead and asserts .git/index.lock mtime is older than the subprocess invocation timeline.
2. Same property for .ddx/.git-tracker.lock: scope to the actual tracker file write, not across subprocess wait.
3. Lock lifetime metric is emitted as a structured event (JSON line with lock_name, acquired_at, released_at, duration_ms, holder_pid, operation) for every acquire/release; visible in ddx logs.
4. A configurable hold-time cap (default 10s for index.lock, 30s for tracker lock) is enforced: if a holder exceeds the cap, the worker logs an error, releases, and surfaces the violation in its execution evidence.
5. A multi-worker integration test (5+ concurrent ddx work --watch on independent beads) asserts p99 lock hold time stays under the cap and no operator-issued ddx bead create/update/close in a sibling shell times out.
6. Documentation update in ddx README or AGENTS.md naming the lock-lifetime contract.
description:
PROBLEM
ddx work --watch workers running execute-bead can hold the host repo's .git/index.lock for many minutes during a single bead execution. This serializes every other tracker-affecting operation in that repo (filing beads, dep edits, commits) and produces cascading tracker-lock-timeout failures for operators and other workers.

OBSERVATION (Fizeau, 2026-05-17 21:38–21:44+ EDT)
- .git/index.lock mtime 21:38; still held at 21:44 = 6+ minutes uninterrupted.
- Holder: ddx work --watch (PID 90753) running execute-bead for fizeau-4b76e6b8 in worktree .ddx/executions/20260518T013652-2344d0e4.
- Side-effects observed in the operator session: bead create commands intermittently failed with 'tracker lock timeout (max elapsed, lock: /Users/erik/Projects/fizeau/.ddx/.git-tracker.lock, owner pid: 2615737)' and 'tracker lock timeout (max elapsed, lock: ..., owner pid: 2809592)'. Both the git index.lock and the .ddx/.git-tracker.lock exhibit the same pattern: held far longer than the operation needs.
- Five concurrent ddx work --watch daemons (PIDs 87523, 88624, 89333, 90753, 949868) plus a worker-spawned claude subprocess. The lock is held across the entire claude subprocess lifetime, not just the actual git mutation.

WHY THIS IS A BUG
git's index.lock and any short-lived mutation lock should be held only for the duration of the mutation itself (single-digit seconds at most). Holding it across the full bead-execution lifetime (which includes a multi-minute LLM subprocess) means:
1. Any concurrent ddx bead create/update/close from operators or other workers may time out.
2. Operators cannot do tracker hygiene (annotate findings, file follow-ons) while a long bead runs.
3. The error surface is misleading — 'tracker lock timeout' looks like a tracker bug, but the actual culprit is the index/staging-area lock.
4. Other ddx work --watch daemons sit idle when they could be making progress on independent beads.

PROPOSED FIX
A. Scope every git mutation lock to the minimum operation, never across the LLM subprocess invocation. Specifically: do not hold .git/index.lock or .ddx/.git-tracker.lock while ddx is waiting on a claude/codex/gemini subprocess to return.
B. Instrument lock lifetime — emit a structured metric (lock_name, acquired_at, released_at, duration_ms, holder_pid, operation) for every acquire/release.
C. Fail-fast threshold — abort with a loud error if any worker holds a lock beyond a configured cap (proposed default: 10s for index.lock, 30s for tracker lock). Hung workers should release and let others through, not block the whole tracker.
D. CI / load test — a multi-worker scenario test that proves 5 workers can each acquire and release the lock with p99 hold time under the cap.

CROSS-REF
Filed from Fizeau alignment-review session 2026-05-17 (AR-2026-05-17-repo). Originally surfaced during the no-static-fallback bead chain (parent fizeau-89eca738). No local Fizeau bead — this is a DDx infrastructure bug, filing directly here per AGENTS.md cross-repo triage pattern.
notes: Decomposed into child beads: ddx-0b743e7e (lock scoping), ddx-d8c98e4c (metrics), ddx-9465a062 (multi-worker test), ddx-e46ef410 (documentation)
title: execute-bead workers hold git index.lock for minutes; need lifetime tracking + fail-fast

description:
PROBLEM
Existing beads and lifecycle metadata can carry needs_human, triage:needs-investigation, no_changes_needs_investigation, cooldowns, and lifecycle_reconciled labels. Under the new state machine those labels cannot remain active runtime controls, and DDx startup must refuse to run until old queues are migrated.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/bead/reconcile.go:8-27 defines lifecycle labels and extra keys including LabelNeedsInvestigation and LabelNeedsHuman.
- cli/internal/bead/reconcile.go:156-223 adds or clears needs-investigation labels/cooldown metadata during lifecycle reconciliation.
- cli/internal/bead/reconcile.go:281-284 includes triage labels in currentLifecycleFields.
- cli/internal/bead/types.go:206-216 defines BlockerKindNeedsInvestigation and BlockerKindNeedsHuman as first-class blocker kinds.
- cli/cmd/bead_migrate.go:10-108 and cli/internal/bead/migrate.go:23-40 implement archive/event/backend migration but no one-way lifecycle migration.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a one-way lifecycle migration command/path, for example `ddx bead migrate --lifecycle --dry-run|--apply`, that converts legacy lifecycle labels/metadata into status-owned state. open+needs_human and equivalent human-required outcomes become status=proposed with reason/suggested-action metadata. triage:needs-investigation is removed as an active lane; each row becomes status=proposed when operator input is required, remains status=open when autonomous smart-agent work should proceed, becomes status=blocked only for external recheckable blockers, or terminal status where evidence already proves closed/cancelled. After apply, record a lifecycle schema marker used by the startup gate. This is not backwards compatibility: old labels are migration input only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not preserve needs_human or triage:needs-investigation as worker-exclusion labels. Do not auto-apply migration at startup. Do not hand-edit `.ddx/beads.jsonl` outside the migration command.

DEPS
Depends on store/query wiring and transition write API so migration output validates against the new queues.
title: bead: migrate legacy lifecycle labels to status-owned states

description:
Per principle P7 (RELIABILITY-PRINCIPLES bead): a bead's description + AC must be sufficient context for a competent sub-agent to execute without hand-curation. Today many beads punt the investigation, omit concrete test names, and leave non-scope implicit. Hand-curated sub-agent prompts have been compensating; this bead surfaces the gap and produces a template.

ROOT CAUSE
Beads were authored expecting the executor to investigate first. Sub-agents (and ddx try / ddx work workers) need investigation done UPFRONT to execute reliably. Without it, the executor either:
- Gives up (no_changes after limited investigation), OR
- Produces wrong work (wrong file, wrong scope), OR
- Asks for clarification (not possible in autonomous drain)

ROOT CAUSE 2
No formal authoring template exists. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md describe bead types but not bead structure or quality bar. New beads inherit whatever the operator was thinking at the moment.

SCOPE
1. Audit 20 representative open beads (mix of priorities, areas, types) against a quality rubric.
2. Identify common gaps; quantify (how many beads miss test names, how many lack file:line cites, etc.).
3. Produce bead-authoring-template.md at docs/helix/06-iterate/.
4. Update CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and DDx skill at .agents/skills/ddx/ to reference the template.
5. Identify which 10-15 high-impact open beads warrant retrofit (the next round of execution work depends on them).

QUALITY RUBRIC (the audit measures each bead against)
- (a) Title: one-line scope clarity
- (b) Description: problem + ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE + proposed fix + non-scope
- (c) AC #1-N: numbered, verifiable, includes specific test names
- (d) AC includes 'wired-in' assertion when introducing new code paths
- (e) AC includes go test command + lefthook gate
- (f) Labels: phase + area + kind + cross-refs (adr/spec/prevention)
- (g) Parent + Deps: explicit
- (h) Description reads as sufficient sub-agent prompt (no operator hand-curation needed)

Score per bead: 8/8 = passes; less = needs retrofit.

NOT IN SCOPE
- Retrofitting beads (separate follow-up beads filed from the audit's recommendations)
- Auto-validating bead structure on creation (future tooling bead)
- Reorganizing existing bead labels or hierarchies

INTERSECTIONS
- RELIABILITY-PRINCIPLES bead (this audit operationalizes P7)
- Retrofit recommendations from this audit gate the dispatch of refactor children C4-C13 (bead retrofit MUST land before sub-agent dispatch with verbatim prompts)

description:
# PROBLEM
Observed live on eitri 2026-07-05 20:40-21:00 EDT (ddx v0.6.2-alpha104-4162-g772c3f55a): for every project with ready beads (ddx, snorri, pqueue), the supervisor spawns a fresh `ddx work --server-managed` worker on its 10s tick; the worker claims the top ready bead, prints 'readiness check: starting', then ~5s later receives SIGINT ('Cancel received, shutting down gracefully', exit status 130) and dies. The next tick spawns a replacement, which repeats the cycle. No bead ever executes; each cycle can invoke the codex-backed pre-claim intake hook, burning provider spend every 10 seconds per project. The cayce worker — whose queue was empty and which therefore never claimed — survived the whole window, so the kill correlates with the claim path, not worker age. Worker record example: /Users/erik/Projects/snorri/.ddx/workers/worker-20260706T004055-5645 (state=failed, last_error='exit status 130', log ends 'readiness check: starting' → 'Cancel received').

This is a distinct manifestation from ddx-c8506158 (duplicate long-lived workers on sindri after handle loss): here the workers hold live in-memory handles (spawned by the current server process) and are killed, not duplicated.

# ROOT CAUSE HYPOTHESIS
Something in the per-tick reconcile path revokes the fresh worker's claim or stops it by ID. Grep entry points:
- cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:253-260 ReconcileAt: every tick, staleIDs (running-on-disk, no in-memory handle) go through stopStaleDiskEntry.
- cli/internal/server/workers.go:1406-1459 stopStaleDiskEntry: unclaims the bead recorded on the stale record (`store.Unclaim(beadID)`) — with ~150 historical worker dirs per project, a stale record naming the SAME top-ready bead the live worker just claimed would release the live worker's claim out from under it; the worker's claim-guard then cancels the attempt (matches the observed SIGINT-equivalent graceful cancel). Verify whether stopStaleDiskEntry can fire repeatedly (writeRecord failure leaves state=running) or whether many distinct stale records reference the current top bead.
- cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:286-344 snapshotWorkers: confirm hasWorkerHandle is true for subprocess-launched workers of the CURRENT server generation; if false they land in staleIDs and get stop-stale'd (claim released + record flipped) within one tick of spawning — which matches the observed ≤10s lifetime exactly.

# PROPOSED FIX
Determined by which hypothesis verifies. Candidates: make snapshotWorkers classify current-generation subprocess workers via OS-liveness (kill(pid,0)) instead of in-memory handle only; make stopStaleDiskEntry skip unclaim when the bead's current claim does not belong to the stale record's worker/attempt; one-shot stale sweep at startup instead of per-tick.

# NON-SCOPE
- ddx-c8506158 (adopt-or-terminate handle-less duplicates across restarts) — sibling, same root-cause area but different invariant.
- workerprobe TLS registration failure (ddx-a6e99ad3).
- Operator-attention relaunch suppression not being honored (separate bead).

Related: ddx-c8506158, ddx-a6e99ad3.

No deps.
notes: Fixed in beae546b2 (merged ac7a2c929, manual land of preserved ref after land-coordinator staged-changes jam). stopStaleDiskEntry now checks the claim lease (staleDiskEntryCanReleaseClaim) before releasing a bead claim, so stale-record cleanup no longer steals fresh claims from live workers. AC verified: TestSupervisorReconcile_FreshClaimingWorkerSurvivesTicks and TestStopStaleDiskEntry_DoesNotUnclaimForeignClaim PASS; full internal/server package green; lefthook pre-commit passed in-attempt. Live verify on eitri: after rebuild+restart with desired_count=1 restored for ddx/snorri/pqueue, workers survived >10min past claim and are mid-implementation (old behavior killed them at ~5s). /api/workers shows connected workers (with ddx-a6e99ad3 landed).

description:
Execution bundles under .ddx/executions/<attempt>/ are the primary forensic record of what DDx automation did, but the most valuable part — the per-iteration agent trace at embedded/agent-*.jsonl — cannot reasonably be checked in. Individual traces can exceed 50 MB; a busy automation day produces hundreds of MB. Axon hit this on 2026-04-15 when GitHub warned about a 50.18 MB embedded trace file, and embedded/ is now gitignored per-repo.

We still want that level of detail for *every* run, for post-mortems, routing/model analysis, and training-data curation. We need a configurable out-of-band mirror.

## Proposed shape

1. **Archive target** configured via `.ddx/config.yaml` (and/or env var):
   - `executions.mirror.kind: local | s3 | gcs | http`
   - `executions.mirror.path: s3://bucket/ddx-executions/{project}/{attempt_id}/` (template with `{project}`, `{attempt_id}`, `{date}`, `{bead_id}`)
   - `executions.mirror.include: [manifest, prompt, result, usage, checks, embedded]` (allow excluding embedded for bandwidth-sensitive setups, but default = everything)
   - `executions.mirror.async: true` (upload in background after execute-bead returns so it never blocks the hot path)

2. **When to mirror**: at execute-bead finalization, after result.json is written. On failure, retry async with bounded attempts; log failures to `.ddx/agent-logs/mirror.log` but do not fail the bead.

3. **Index**: each mirrored bundle gets a pointer row appended to a local `.ddx/executions/mirror-index.jsonl` (attempt_id, bead_id, mirror_uri, uploaded_at, byte_size). This gives analysts a quick `jq` lookup without walking the remote store.

4. **Retrieval**: `ddx agent executions fetch <attempt_id>` pulls a bundle back to .ddx/executions/<attempt_id>/ for local inspection.

5. **GC**: optional local retention policy (`executions.retain_days`) that prunes old local bundles while the mirror keeps the full history.

## Non-goals

- Not a full audit trail service — just a mirror of DDx's existing bundles.
- Not a replacement for git-tracked manifest/prompt/result/usage summaries — those stay checked in.
- Not a distributed log aggregator — one-shot copy per bundle, no streaming.

## Why now

Axon's ADR-018 session produced ~85 MB of execution artifacts in a single day; only 1.5 MB of that is useful as checked-in summary. Without a mirror, every project using DDx execute-bead faces the same tension: either gitignore the traces and lose the forensic data, or commit them and bloat the repo forever.
title: execution-bundle archive: configurable mirror for .ddx/executions/ (including embedded traces)

This silently freezes important work whenever a worker is disrupted (killed, server restart, network blip, OS issue) — disruption produces ExecutionFailed + no commit, indistinguishable from "model genuinely tried and produced nothing."

OBSERVED (today, 2026-05-02)
After the picker fix investigation found the four "starved" P0 beads (ddx-dc157075, ddx-aee651ec, ddx-29058e2a, ddx-9d55601f) all had work-retry-after timestamps ~3 hours in the future. Investigation per ddx-9d55601f confirmed these were NOT genuine model failures — they were prior worker disruptions during this development session (worker kills, server restarts) being treated as model-gave-up.

User directive: "Cooldown should be reserved for cases where the model is truly unable to make progress on a task."

CURRENT COOLDOWN POLICY (cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go)
- LandConflictCooldown = 15min — short cooldown after merge/land conflicts (line 64)
- noProgressCooldown = 6h default — when shouldSuppressNoProgress is true (line 367)
- MaxLoopCooldown = 24h — push_failed, push_conflict, decomposition decline (line 57)

shouldSuppressNoProgress (line 1550): returns true if BaseRev != "" AND ResultRev != "" AND BaseRev == ResultRev. This catches:
- Model wrote nothing AND came back cleanly (true no_progress) ✓
- Worker killed mid-execution before commit (FALSE no_progress — disruption)
- Network/provider error before model started (FALSE no_progress — disruption)
- Routing preflight rejection (FALSE no_progress — config issue)

The mis-classification is the bug.

PROPOSED FIX

Add a Disposition::Disrupted variant (or equivalent flag on ExecuteBeadReport) that explicitly marks results that are NOT evidence of model inability:
- ctx.Err() != nil (cancellation, deadline, parent died)
- syscall.SIGTERM / SIGINT received during execution
- Provider-side 5xx, connection refused, timeout (transport disruption)
- Worker process killed (parent never received clean result)
- Server-restart-detected marker
- Routing preflight rejection (operator config issue, not model failure)

For Disrupted: skip cooldown entirely (or use a tiny defer like 30s) and unclaim the bead so the next worker pickup is immediate.
For genuine no-progress (model returned clean with no commit AND rationale present): keep current 6h cooldown.

ALTERNATIVE: exponential backoff per bead. First failure: 5min; second: 30min; third: 2h; cap at 24h. Resets on any successful attempt or operator clear. This is more forgiving than the current flat 6h on the first hiccup.

PROBABLY BOTH: Disrupted skips cooldown entirely; non-Disrupted failures use exponential backoff starting at 5min, not flat 6h.

DETECTION POINTERS

- ctx.Err() check at the call site that produces ExecutionFailed (line 513, 629, 637, 1011)
- Check for `.ddx/executions/<run-id>/no_changes_rationale.txt` presence — if missing, the model never wrote one (likely disruption)
- Check the executor's exit code: SIGKILL/SIGTERM = disruption; clean exit with empty result = no-progress
- Track parent process restart count or boot ID; if changed since the attempt started, mark Disrupted

NOT IN SCOPE
- Changing the cooldown duration constants themselves
- Reworking the per-bead retry policy framework (separate concern)
- Changing land-conflict or push-failed cooldowns (those are correct as-is)
- The exponential-backoff alternative is OPTIONAL; primary fix is Disrupted classification

INTERSECTION WITH OTHER BEADS
- ddx-dc157075 (worker stay-alive): the stay-alive fix prevents some classes of disruption (worker no longer exits on empty poll), but does NOT fix the cooldown-on-disruption mis-classification
- ddx-076147ee (worker client-server architecture TD): if workers become long-lived clients, server-restart disruption goes away by construction. But this fix is needed BEFORE that TD is implemented because the disruption classification is needed regardless.
- ddx-9228a484 C9 (StopCondition enum): may absorb this — the StopCondition enum could include Disrupted as a state. Verify and align.
title: work: distinguish worker-disrupted from model-gave-up; do not cooldown on disruption

description:
## Goal

Today, when work dispatches a coarse bead (an unsplit epic) to an agent, the agent often returns `no_changes` with reasoning like "this is an epic, needs child-bead breakdown, not monolithic execution" — wasting a worker attempt, leaving the bead in a half-owned claimed state, and forcing manual operator intervention.

Concrete recent example: `agent-6c7a4c11` (Harness × Model Matrix Benchmark — initial tranche) on this user's `agent` repo was dispatched as a single bead, the agent declined to execute monolithically, the worker exited without unclaiming. The bead is now stuck claimed by a dead worker with no change applied.

The fix is to run a triage step **before** Claim: evaluate whether the bead is atomic (one PR's worth of work, single AC focus) or decomposable (multiple distinct deliverables, AC items map to separable PRs). If decomposable, run a splitter that produces child beads (parent-linked, AC-distributed), and skip dispatch of the parent. Children themselves re-enter triage — recursive decomposition with a depth cap.

## Concrete change

Insert a `complexityGate` phase in `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go` between bead-pick and Claim:

```
next-candidate → ResolveRoute → preflight gate (ddx-98e6e9ef)
  → complexityGate (NEW)
  → if atomic:        Claim → invoke
  → if decomposable:  splitter → file children with parent link → mark parent blocked-by-children → re-pick
  → if ambiguous:     surface to human triage (event + label), don't claim
```

Two prompts, both shipped with the default DDx plugin under `library/prompts/triage/`:

1. **`complexity-eval.md`** — given bead body + AC + deps + history (prior attempts, reviewer BLOCKs), classify `{atomic, decomposable, ambiguous}` with reasoning + confidence.
2. **`bead-split.md`** — given a decomposable bead, emit N child beads (JSON) with: title, AC, parent link, spec-id inheritance, in-scope files subset, labels. Children must collectively cover the parent's AC.

Both prompts use the embedded `agent` harness with profile=default (cheap tier, local-first) — the gate's cost/latency must be << a wasted dispatch.

## Historical evidence engineering

Both prompts must be engineered against historical evidence, not vibes. Harvest a corpus from `.ddx/beads.jsonl` (this project + the user's `agent` project, which has 5 months of bead history including known epic-rejection cases):

- Beads closed `no_changes` whose status text mentions "epic", "split", "breakdown", "scope", or "monolithic" → positive examples for **decomposable**.
- Beads with `attempt_count >= 3` or repeated `kind:reopen` events from reviewer BLOCKs citing scope → positive examples for **decomposable**.
- Beads that were eventually split manually (parent epic + N child tasks filed in a single tracker batch) → use parent body as splitter input, the actual children as ground-truth output.
- Beads closed cleanly on first attempt with single-file or small-diff commits → positive examples for **atomic**.

Hold out 20% as eval. Report `complexity-eval` accuracy/F1 on classification; report `bead-split` AC-coverage rate (children's AC tokens together cover parent's AC) and child-count distribution vs. ground-truth.

The harvest script (`scripts/triage/harvest-corpus.go` or equivalent) is committed and reproducible.

## Recursion + depth cap

Children re-enter the gate. Default depth cap = 3, configurable via `agent.triage.max_decomposition_depth` in `.ddx/config.yaml`. At cap: surface to human (`kind:triage-overflow` event, `status=blocked`, `label=needs-human-decomposition`). Never silently dispatch a parent that hit cap.

## In-scope files

- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go` — new `complexityGate` phase pre-Claim
- `cli/internal/agent/triage.go` (new) — gate logic, prompt invocation, child filing
- `library/prompts/triage/complexity-eval.md` (new)
- `library/prompts/triage/bead-split.md` (new)
- `cli/internal/agent/triage_test.go` (new) — unit tests against held-out historical corpus
- `library/prompts/triage/eval-corpus.jsonl` (new) — frozen eval slice (training slice can be regenerated)
- `scripts/triage/harvest-corpus.go` (new) — corpus regeneration
- `docs/triage/decomposition.md` (new) — operator docs

## Out of scope (file follow-ups if/when needed)

- Backfill triage on already-claimed in-flight beads (e.g. unsticking agent-6c7a4c11 retroactively) — operational bead, not part of this feature.
- A web UI for visualizing the triage decision per bead — consumer bead.
- Per-team customization of split rules — premature; ship the default and iterate.

## Anti-goals

- Do **not** rewrite an existing bead in place. Splitting always files children; the parent stays as an epic with `status=blocked-by-children`.
- Do **not** make the gate silently optional. If disabled via flag or config, emit a one-time warning per worker boot.
- Do **not** use a model larger than the cheap tier for the gate prompts.
- Do **not** duplicate routing logic in the gate; it should be a thin caller of the agent SDK with the gate's two prompts.

## Why P1

The failure mode it prevents — claimed-but-undeliverable beads — corrupts the queue's claim semantics, wastes operator time, and silently inflates `attempt_count` on epics that will never close. Without this gate, the rest of the routing-cleanup work (`ddx-fdd3ea36` umbrella) ships into a queue with structurally bad inputs.

title: pre-claim triage: complexity evaluator + auto-splitter for recursive epic decomposition before agent dispatch

description:
PROBLEM (regression found live 2026-06-03; D3 ddx-bd47e2c4 shipped this incomplete)
Operator-reopening a consecutive-wedge-parked bead via `ddx bead update <id> --status open` does NOT clear the work-consecutive-wedges marker, so on the next claim the loop's consecutiveWedgeGuardTrips (cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1745) reads the stale count>=threshold and instantly re-parks the bead ("consecutive-wedge guard: <id> wedged 2 consecutive claims; flagged for operator attention"), WITHOUT attempting it. Observed: 7 beads un-parked with --status open all re-wedged at claim until the marker was manually `--unset work-consecutive-wedges`. D3's AC #2 ("a reopened bead is claimable and attempted, not instantly re-parked") is therefore NOT satisfied in production even though the bead closed.

ROOT CAUSE
clearConsecutiveWedge (execute_bead_loop.go ~5844) is only called on a clean guard-free completion (~2604). Nothing clears the marker (or makes consecutiveWedgeGuardTrips return false) when a bead transitions back to an execution-eligible state by OPERATOR action (status proposed/blocked -> open). The reopen and the marker live in different layers (store update vs loop guard state).

PROPOSED FIX
When the loop encounters a ready bead whose status was reopened by an operator after the wedge was recorded (e.g. the wedge marker's timestamp predates the bead's last status->open transition, OR a dedicated reopened-since marker), consecutiveWedgeGuardTrips must return false AND clearConsecutiveWedge must run so the bead gets a fresh attempt. Simplest robust option: clear the work-consecutive-wedges marker at the store layer whenever a bead is transitioned to status=open from proposed/blocked (so any reopen path — CLI or programmatic — drops the stale wedge state). Add the operator-reopen clear so no manual --unset is ever needed.

ACCEPTANCE
1. New test: a bead with work-consecutive-wedges{count>=threshold} transitioned proposed->open (operator reopen) has NO wedge marker afterward (cleared at the store transition), OR consecutiveWedgeGuardTrips returns false for it on the immediately-following claim. Assert the loop ATTEMPTS it (claims + dispatches) rather than re-parking.
2. Regression: simulate the exact observed sequence (record wedge count=2, set status=open, run one drain iteration) and assert the bead is claimed/attempted, not re-flagged operator-attention.
3. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/bead/... green.
4. lefthook run pre-commit passes.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-24949caf is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 3 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM: Restarting the DDx user service during active supervised work can hang until systemd times out, leaving systemd to SIGKILL server child processes. Live evidence from 2026-07-07 03:05:19 EDT: `ddx server stop` did not return until systemd marked `ddx-server.service` failed with `Result: timeout` and killed leftover git subprocesses, interrupting the Axon worker attempt that was in post-execution handling.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE: `cli/internal/server/server.go:379-385` cancels the supervisor and then waits on `supervisorDone` with no timeout. Worker cleanup is only reached afterward at `cli/internal/server/server.go:388-395`. The worker shutdown path itself has a bounded wait (`cli/internal/server/workers.go:1696-1703`), but it is unreachable while the supervisor goroutine is stuck in a reconcile/git operation. The installed systemd unit generated from `cli/cmd/server_service.go:26-42` has no explicit stop timeout or ExecStop mitigation, so the default systemd timeout eventually kills the whole cgroup.

PROPOSED FIX: Make server shutdown bounded and ordered so worker cleanup always runs promptly even when supervisor reconciliation is slow or stuck. description:
PROBLEM
The landed zero-footprint refactor introduced `ddxroot.Path(ctx, projectRoot)` and a pre-commit audit, but the audit only catches `filepath.Join(..., ".ddx", ...)`. Production code still has direct `.ddx` state-root consumers that will keep reading or committing the project worktree instead of the XDG state repository in convention mode.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
`cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1791-1837` stats the tracker via `ddxroot.JoinProject(projectRoot, "beads.jsonl")`, but then checks/stages/commits literal `.ddx/beads.jsonl` in `projectRoot`. In convention mode that never commits the XDG tracker repo.
`cli/internal/attemptmetrics/attemptmetrics.go:19-101` defines `.ddx/metrics/attempts.jsonl` as a relative constant and joins it directly under `projectRoot`, bypassing `ddxroot`.
`cli/cmd/work_plan.go:82-87` and `cli/cmd/work_clear_cooldowns.go:46-47` open `projectRoot + "/.ddx"` directly, so convention-mode projects show empty or wrong queues.
The new audit command in `lefthook.yml` only searches for `filepath.Join(..., ".ddx")`, so these regressions are invisible to pre-commit.

PROPOSED FIX
Route the concrete residual state-root consumers above through `ddxroot.Path` / `ddxroot.JoinProject`. When committing tracker state in convention mode, run git in the actual DDx state root repository and stage `beads.jsonl` relative to that repo; preserve existing in-tree behavior and execute-bead merge-policy commits. Update the audit so it fails on production direct state-root patterns such as `projectRoot + "/.ddx"`, `WorkingDir + "/.ddx"`, and constants joined under projectRoot for DDx-managed state, while still allowing relative artifact path strings used inside worker prompts and git pathspec filters.

NON-SCOPE
Do not migrate this repository out of in-tree mode. Do not rewrite prompt text that intentionally tells agents where evidence appears in an execution worktree. Do not change the bead storage format or attachment externalization policy.
title: ddx home: route residual state-root consumers through ddxroot

Safe rewrite policy is currently ambiguous. The append-only preservation guard prevents deletion of stale or noisy wording, but appending more text can make future bead prompts longer and more confusing. PROPOSED FIX
Update the governing specs to define safe rewrites as validated replacement rewrites: replacement bead text is allowed when a deterministic validator preserves intent, acceptance criteria, non-scope, durable evidence, and unresolved product choices; original text is retained in audit evidence, not duplicated into the prompt body. NON-SCOPE

acceptance: 1. TD authored for the axon-backend integration (data model mapping, claim/lock semantics, archive policy, multi-machine concurrency story). 2. Axon-backend implementation lands behind a feature flag or selectable backend in cli/internal/bead/backend.go. 3. description:
The current .ddx/beads.jsonl backend (atomic JSONL writes wrapped in flock; events accumulating per-bead; archive split per ADR-004) is showing strain:

1. Multi-worker contention via the git tracker-commit step (see ddx-da11a34a — the file lock around git add/commit is a v1 patch, not the real fix)
2. Events array per bead is unbounded and dominates archive size
3. Cross-machine concurrency is not addressed (Story 14 federation will require it)
4. The current model bakes one process-local store + git-as-replication; doesn't compose cleanly with a real database

Two backend paths under consideration:

**Axon (PRIMARY, per user inclination)**: integrate as the first DDx-side consumer of axon. User owns the stack; tight integration possible; proves axon's value as a substrate. Requires authoring an axon backend implementing the bead schema's storage contract (per ADR-004 / SD-004 — collection abstraction, claim semantics, atomic writes, JSONL interchange compatibility for bd/br).

**bd / doltdb (FALLBACK)**: delegate to bd which already speaks doltdb (git-for-data). Trivial integration; downside is tracking an external codebase as a hard dependency.

This epic frames the evaluation, designs the integration, prototypes, and migrates. Children break down the work. The lock-contention patch (ddx-da11a34a) remains relevant as stability scaffolding while this plays out — when axon ships and is adopted, the JSONL+git path may retire entirely (or stay as a portable interchange backend per FEAT-004's bd/br semantics).
notes: decomposed into ddx-6bb51a52 (TD), ddx-bbdd7564 (Backend interface), ddx-95ec5ed5 (axon impl), ddx-cb63cdfc (migration tool), ddx-743bc194 (chaos tests), ddx-8835a765 (bd fallback doc), ddx-6602559c (perf bench). Original epic was too big: 6 ACs spanning unrelated subsystems (design, refactor, new impl, migration, tests, docs, perf). Children form a DAG: TD → interface → {axon impl, bd doc}; axon impl → {migration, chaos, perf}.

So the cap is observed but not enforced — no force-release watchdog.

PROPOSED FIX: Wire withTrackerLockPolicy through lockmetrics.InstrumentCapped with CapConfig{Cap: lockmetrics.CapFor("tracker.lock")} so a hold past the cap fires the watchdog (stack capture, force-release, lock-violation.json evidence). Keep existing Instrument metrics behavior. This is a safety backstop; the land beads (L1/L2) remove the legitimate slow holds so the watchdog should not fire in normal operation.

description:
PROBLEM
ddx work's readiness check emits a misleading parse error during routine bead reads, blaming a specific line number that is NOT actually corrupt. Observed in /Users/erik/Projects/fizeau today at 19:25:58 during pickup of fizeau-8ebac59d:

  19:25:58 readiness check: starting
  bead: read line 18: bead: unmarshal: unexpected end of JSON input
  23:26:03 readiness route claude/opus reason=policy=default; score=99.5

The route still succeeded — the error is non-fatal — but the operator-facing log line tells them line 18 of .ddx/beads.jsonl is corrupt when it is not. python3 json.loads on every line of the 210-line file returns no errors; line 18 specifically is a 10441-byte fully-valid JSON record.

ROOT CAUSE (hypothesis — verify in fix)
The "line 18" in the error message is almost certainly NOT a line in the on-disk JSONL file. Plausible causes:
1. A relative buffer offset inside a streaming json.Decoder that has been mistaken for a file line number when formatting the error.
2. A partial read race: the tracker is being read concurrently with a write (auto-doc-stamp from `ddx bead create`/`ddx bead update`), and the reader hit EOF mid-record. The "line 18" is the line index inside the partial buffer, not the file.
3. A bead's events array contains an embedded string with newlines that the reader's line counter is tokenizing on, throwing off the line index.

The error is non-fatal because the reader presumably skips the bad bead and continues — but it surfaces to the operator as if the file itself is corrupt, prompting them to inspect / fsck / restore a perfectly good tracker file.

REPRO
Observable any time `ddx work` (and likely `ddx bead list`, `ddx work plan`, etc.) reads the tracker while another `ddx bead create`/`update`/`dep add` is mid-write. Most reliably reproducible on a project with active auto-doc-stamp commits flying (i.e., any project running `ddx work` continuously). The 210-line fizeau beads.jsonl reproduces it under contention.

PROPOSED FIX
1. **Fix the error formatting.** The error should report either:
   - The actual on-disk line number where the parse failed (compute via byte offset / newline scan).
   - OR "(partial record at byte offset N)" if a streaming decoder hit EOF mid-record.
   - Never report a number that is not a real file line, especially when telling operators to "reconcile manually."
2. **Distinguish "transient partial read" from "persistent corruption."** A partial read during concurrent write should be retried (with a short backoff or via a read lock around the tracker file). A genuine corruption should fail the read and surface a louder error. Today both look identical to the operator.
3. **Add coverage.** Test that simulates concurrent write+read on a tracker file (write a long record byte-by-byte while the reader does a full scan) and asserts the reader either retries cleanly OR reports an accurate diagnostic. Failure: today's behavior of "line 18: unmarshal: unexpected end of JSON input" against a non-line-18 problem.

NON-SCOPE
- Replacing JSONL with a different tracker format.
- Adding a file lock around all tracker writes (probably needed eventually but out of scope here — this bead is strictly about diagnostics + transient-read handling).
- The actual readiness-check race condition that caused the read in the first place — that's incidental; any concurrent reader would hit it.

PARENT AND DEPS
No parent. No deps.

EVIDENCE FILE
Worker log preserved at /tmp/fizeau-worker-1778973834.log (line containing "bead: read line 18: bead: unmarshal: unexpected end of JSON input"). Companion file: /Users/erik/Projects/fizeau/.ddx/beads.jsonl, 210 lines, all of which parse cleanly via `python3 -c "import json, sys; [json.loads(l) for l in open('.ddx/beads.jsonl')]"`.
title: bead tracker: 'bead: read line N: bead: unmarshal: unexpected end of JSON input' fires when JSONL is well-formed

acceptance: When `gitleaks` is unavailable, the `lefthook` fallback secret scan still catches obvious secret assignments but does not fail on ordinary `.ddx/beads.jsonl` tracker updates; the fallback inspects staged additions rather than whole files or otherwise avoids re-flagging historical tracker content; and a deterministic repro covers a staged tracker diff containing `token-awareness.md` text without any added secrets.
description:
<context-digest>
Tracker-only DDx bead commit from /Users/erik/Projects/ddx after filing work alpha findings. Environment does not have `gitleaks`, so the `lefthook` pre-commit hook used the fallback grep path in `lefthook.yml`.
</context-digest>

The fallback `secrets` hook in `lefthook.yml` produces false positives on staged `.ddx/beads.jsonl` changes because it scans the entire staged file with a broad `token|auth|password|...` regex instead of scanning added lines with tighter assignment-oriented patterns.

## Reproduction
1. Ensure `gitleaks` is not installed.
2. Stage a normal tracker-only change to `.ddx/beads.jsonl`.
3. Run `git commit`.
4. Observe the `secrets` hook fails and prints a line from `.ddx/beads.jsonl` where text like `token-awareness.md` and later quoted JSON content satisfy the fallback regex even though no secret was added.

## Observed gap
The fallback pattern is broad enough to match ordinary prose containing words like `token` or `auth`, and because it scans the whole staged file it re-trips on historical tracker content whenever `.ddx/beads.jsonl` changes.

## Why this matters
In environments without `gitleaks`, normal bead creation becomes effectively uncommittable. That blocks DDx's own tracker workflow and makes it harder to land the very bugs discovered during alpha execution.
title: Fix fallback secret scan false positives on tracker JSONL commits

description:
PROBLEM
ddx work --watch's pre-claim intake decoder fails to unmarshal a readiness_checks response when an entry's verdict is a JSON bool. The worker logs the warn-only rejection 'decode result: json: cannot unmarshal bool into Go struct field .readiness_checks.verdict of type string' and skips the bead. When the faulty payload is produced for every candidate, the whole queue idles (observed Fizeau 2026-05-18, identical fingerprint 15155a1c... across distinct bead_ids).

ROOT CAUSE
cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:75-80 defines preClaimReadinessCheck with 'Verdict string `json:"verdict,omitempty"`' (line 77). preClaimReadinessChecksPayload.UnmarshalJSON (cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:322-352) decodes each entry into preClaimReadinessCheck via json.Unmarshal at lines 331 (array case) and 334 (singleton-object case). When the producer emits verdict as a JSON bool (true/false) instead of a string, json.Unmarshal returns the type error, the decode aborts, and the payload is rejected as system_unready.

PROPOSED FIX
Make the verdict field tolerant: introduce a custom JSON type (e.g. a 'readinessVerdict' string newtype with UnmarshalJSON, or a custom UnmarshalJSON on preClaimReadinessCheck) that accepts a JSON bool, a JSON string, or an absent/null value and coerces to a documented canonical string form:
  - JSON bool true  -> "pass"
  - JSON bool false -> "fail"
  - JSON string     -> trimmed value, passed through unchanged (e.g. "pass", "fail", "ready", "not_ready")
  - absent / null   -> "" (empty, same as today)
The downstream fail-detection failedReadinessReasons (cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:782-794) already lower/trim-compares Verdict to "fail", so false->"fail" keeps fail semantics intact; true->"pass" is a non-fail verdict. Document the bool->string mapping in a doc comment on the verdict type.

NON-SCOPE
Do not add the shared JSON schema / CI drift gate (separate child), the same-fingerprint escalation (separate child), the claim-success-rate signal (separate child), or README docs (separate child). Only the decoder tolerance + its unit test.

Landed at merge 854ef1817 (fix commit 4d3f829c0).

description:
PROBLEM
`ddx server install` installs a singleton per-user service, but until this fix its default `WorkingDirectory` and log path were derived from the DDx project root that happened to run the install. In practice, the host had a single `ddx-server.service` rooted at `/home/erik/Projects/axon`; reinstalling from `/home/erik/Projects/ddx` merely moved the singleton to another project, which is still wrong. A per-user multi-project server must not be bound by default to Axon, DDx, or any other project checkout.

ROOT CAUSE
`cli/cmd/server_service.go:49-68` defaulted service config to `CommandFactory.WorkingDir`, and `cli/internal/service/systemd.go:21-27` wrote that into `WorkingDirectory` plus project-scoped log paths. The multi-project server contract in `docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-002-server.md:21-33` and `docs/helix/02-design/solution-designs/SD-019-multi-project-server-topology.md:349-373` says the long-lived service is per-user and stores registry state under XDG, but the service-manager section still preserved the older project-root default. Separately, `cli/internal/service/systemd.go:92-96` used `systemctl --user enable --now`, which rewrites the unit but does not restart an already-active service, so even a corrected unit can leave the old project-rooted process running.

PROPOSED FIX
- Make default service installs use a neutral user working directory (`$HOME`) and user-scoped logs (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/ddx/logs/ddx-server.log` or `~/.local/share/ddx/logs/ddx-server.log`).

- Update systemd install so active reinstalls restart after `daemon-reload`; inactive installs enable then start.
- Update FEAT-002 and SD-019 so service-manager docs align with the per-user multi-project topology.

NON-SCOPE

- Do not change server API compatibility aliases.
- Do not migrate or mutate unrelated project trackers.

description:
ddx server workers show <id> reports Attempts: 0  Success: 0  Failed: 0 for a worker that has been running for 30+ minutes and has visibly completed multiple beads (per the worker log stream and per landed commits in main). The counters only update at the end of worker.Run(), when the loop exits. While the loop is mid-flight the server WorkerRecord stays at zero, making the show endpoint useless for live progress.

Root cause: in cli/internal/server/workers.go startWorker(), the call site is:

    loopResult, err := worker.Run(ctx, ...)  // BLOCKING — only returns when loop exits
    // THEN updates record.Attempts = loopResult.Attempts

The ExecuteBeadLoopResult is built up in a local variable inside the loop Run() (see cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go line 147 'result := &ExecuteBeadLoopResult{}', incremented at line 255 'result.Attempts++' etc.) but the server holds no reference to it during execution.

Fix options:

A) ExecuteBeadLoopOptions gains a Progress field of type pointer to ExecuteBeadLoopResult. The caller pre-allocates one, passes it in, and the loop writes to it under a sync.Mutex. The server reads from the same pointer (with the mutex) when serving GET /api/agent/workers/{id}.

B) ExecuteBeadLoopOptions gains an OnBeadResult callback that fires after each bead. The server subscribes and updates record.Attempts/Successes/Failures incrementally.

C) The server already passes an EventSink and the loop already emits bead.result events to it. The server can subscribe to its own sink (parse the JSONL events) and update the counters from those events.

Option A is simplest and least invasive. Option C is cleanest because it reuses the existing event stream.
title: Server worker record Attempts/Successes/Failures stuck at 0 until loop exits

description:
PROBLEM
The readiness hook can over-weight stale external-blocker history and under-weight explicit operator notes that say the blocker was cleared. This produces misleading `intake.warn` text and can steer an implementation attempt toward obsolete infrastructure conclusions even when the bead is intentionally unblocked for forward progress.

OBSERVED EVIDENCE
Niflheim bead `niflheim-439a49ae` has notes saying: `Unblocked 2026-05-18: the prior Redpanda/AIO blocker was stale after commit 90cd8348 bounded Redpanda test storage with an owned tmpfs mount... The container became ready and was cleaned up.` During `ddx work --once` on 2026-05-21, readiness still emitted `bead readiness blocked: redpanda environment can support 32-partition stress test... prior_attempts show a hard external blocker: Redpanda fails to start due to AIO slot exhaustion on WSL2`. The attempt continued because readiness was warn-only, but the warning contradicted current bead notes and polluted the agent context.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
`cli/internal/agent/triage_hook.go:60` includes bead notes in the triage/readiness payload model, and `cli/internal/agent/types.go:298` carries notes in the execute-bead payload, but the readiness prompt/contract does not require stale prior blockers to be discounted when a later note explicitly clears them. The current tests in `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_intake_test.go` cover warn-only continuation and intake event recording, but not precedence between later unblocked notes and older `no_changes_blocked`/external-blocker events.

PROPOSED FIX
Update the readiness prompt/contract and pre-claim intake tests so later explicit operator notes or reopen/unblocked notes supersede older external-blocker events unless current evidence revalidates the blocker. Readiness may still mention stale blocker history as historical context, but it must not phrase the bead as currently blocked or require operator action when a newer note says the blocker was cleared and no fresh recheck failed.

NON-SCOPE
- Changing lifecycle status semantics for actual `status=blocked` beads.
- Suppressing all prior-attempt history.
- Removing warn-only readiness behavior.
- Niflheim benchmark implementation.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_intake_test.go`
- `cli/internal/agent/bead_lifecycle_skill_contract_test.go`
- DDx bead-lifecycle skill text under `.agents/skills/ddx/bead-lifecycle/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/ddx/bead-lifecycle/SKILL.md` if the prompt contract lives there.
- Any pre-claim intake prompt assembly code that formats notes/events for readiness.

description:
Two related bugs causing 'ddx server workers list' (and other server-talking CLI commands) to fail with 'connection refused dial tcp 127.0.0.1:<stale-port>' even when a live server is running.

## Diagnosis

**writeAddrFile already exists** at cli/internal/server/server.go:287-312 and is called from line 273 on every startup. So the file IS written. The real bugs are:

**Bug A: No singleton-server guard.** Multiple 'ddx server' instances can start on the same machine concurrently. Each one calls writeAddrFile and overwrites the previous record. When one dies (e.g., a manual launch test), it leaves the address-file pointing to itself even though it's no longer running. systemd unit (Type=simple) prevents systemd-spawned duplicates of the same unit name but does NOT stop a manual 'ddx server' from racing.

Observed today: live systemd server PID 3442304 listening on 7743 (started ~14:27), but address file shows PID 3482077 / port 4174 (started ~15:01, died). Some manual or test launch overwrote the file then died.

**Bug B: CLI doesn't validate pid-alive before trusting the address file.** ReadServerAddr at cli/internal/server/server.go:328+ returns whatever's in the file. CLI commands then dial the recorded URL. If the recorded pid is dead, dial fails. No fallback to the systemd default (127.0.0.1:7743), no warning.

## Fix

Two halves, same surface (server bootstrap + CLI client read path):

**Server-side (singleton guard):**
- On startup, server acquires flock on ~/.local/share/ddx/server.lock
- If lock is held by an alive process: refuse to start with clear error ('ddx server already running, pid=<N>, addr=<URL>; only one ddx server per machine'). Exit non-zero.
- If lock is acquired (or stale — held by dead pid): proceed; release-on-exit handler clears the lock.
- writeAddrFile happens AFTER the lock acquires — so the address file always corresponds to the lock-holder.

**Client-side (defense in depth):**
- ReadServerAddr (or its callers) validates the recorded pid is alive (kill -0 equivalent on Unix, OpenProcess on Windows)
- If pid is dead: emit warning ('server.addr points to a dead pid <N>; falling back to default 127.0.0.1:7743') and use the default
- Optionally clear the stale file (best-effort; don't fail if unwritable)

## Out of scope

- Multi-server-per-machine support (the singleton guard is intentional — one server per machine is the design per FEAT-020)
- Federation: hub/spoke topology (Story 14) is multi-node, NOT multi-server-per-node

description:
PROBLEM
Stale breaking for the process-shared main-git lock has no crash-safe single-winner transition guard. Concurrent stale breakers can classify the same canonical lock path from stale snapshots, and a permanent guard sidecar would become runtime dirt unless all DDx git/checkpoint/checkout-sync surfaces ignore it explicitly.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go:215-278 retries os.Mkdir on the canonical lock and classifies existing directories or malformed regular files before mutating the pathname. cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go:309-328 reads lock metadata and removes or renames the canonical object without serializing observation and mutation across processes. cli/internal/agent/gitops_real.go:165-205 synthesizes git-add pathspec exclusions, cli/internal/agent/predispatch_dirty.go:477-488 checks pre-dispatch dirt, and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:923-931 handles checkout-sync deferral; each must explicitly ignore the stable sidecar independently of project .gitignore state.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
Phase 0 WB-5 requires a single-winner cross-process stale-break protocol at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase0-stop-the-self-harm-plan-2026-07-13.md:124-132.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a package-local crash-safe transition guard for the process-shared main-git lock. Use a never-deleted sibling advisory-lock file with a deterministic name ending in .lock, plus keyed same-process coordination. The OS lock must release automatically on handle close or process death. Non-contention open/lock errors fail safe. Ordinary acquisition/release must never delete or recreate the sidecar inode/path. Guard contention must consume the existing LockRetryPolicy budget and return TrackerLockTimeoutError on deadline. Add one package-local path constant/helper for the sidecar, and use it from synthesize-commit exclusions, pre-dispatch dirt, and checkout-sync deferral so these surfaces cannot drift. Provide Unix and Windows guard implementations; because the current dependency graph does not cross-compile for Windows, include a self-contained GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go test -c file-list command naming the final guard source/test files.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change tracker mutation semantics, tracker record format, trackerLockStaleAge, LockRetryPolicy defaults, lockmetrics caps, harness/Fizeau behavior, bead-store locks, git index locks, or the separate execution-cleanup lock in cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_loop.go:116-156. Do not extract a shared lock package; ddx-dffb7454 and ddx-3f156500 own separate sites and Phase 1 WB-8 owns unification. Do not implement token-bearing lease release or stale directory/file disposal semantics except as needed to exercise guard acquisition/release and ignored-path behavior.

PARENT
ddx-8b22914e

DEPS
None. ddx-dffb7454 is a related collection-lock implementation, not a prerequisite or shared-package dependency.
title: agent: add stable main-git transition guard

description:
PROBLEM
In the recommended "let fizeau route" mode (no --harness/--model/--profile pin), the worker's liveness record keeps harness/model/route EMPTY for the whole attempt: liveness.SetAttempt is called once pre-dispatch with the REQUESTED (empty) pins and never updated with the route fizeau resolves mid-stream. The progress watchdog (cli/internal/agent/work/watchdog.go:50 phaseEmpty) treats harness==""&&model==""&&route=="" as a wedge; at the 30-min Running budget it cancels the HEALTHY attempt, which trips the consecutive-wedge guard (threshold 2) and parks the bead to operator-attention. This is the dominant false-wedge (16 beads carry needs-human-reason=consecutive_wedge). fizeau v0.14.41 already fixed the routing-side codex false-reject; this is the ddx-side half.

ROOT CAUSE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2440 calls liveness.SetAttempt(candidate.ID, provAttemptID, PhaseRunning, profile, harness, model, profile, 0) — the 4th arg (route) is "profile" (with no profile pin it is ""), harness/model are the empty requested pins. fizeau emits the resolved route in-stream as agentlib.ServiceRoutingDecisionData (Harness/Provider/Model), decoded in drainServiceEventsWithRenderer at cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:257 (no-watchdog fast path) AND :388 (drain-watchdog path), but nothing propagates it back to the loop's liveness reporter (set up at execute_bead_loop.go:1116).

PROPOSED FIX (the watchdog is already correct in spirit — it resets when a non-empty route field appears; only the route is never recorded)
1. Add to cli/internal/agent/work/liveness.go: func (r *SidecarLivenessReporter) UpdateRoute(beadID, harness, model, route string), guarded on r.rec.CurrentBead==beadID, overwriting only non-empty fields, same mutex discipline as SetAttempt.
2. Add field to AgentRunRuntime (cli/internal/agent/types.go): OnRouteResolved func(harness, provider, model string).
3. In drainServiceEventsWithRenderer (agent_runner_service.go), add an onRouteResolved callback param, invoke it in BOTH "case decoded.RoutingDecision != nil" branches (:257 and :388) with decoded.RoutingDecision.Harness/Provider/Model. Update both callers: service_run.go:294 passes runtime.OnRouteResolved; agent_runner_service.go:150 (runAgentViaService / ddx run) passes nil.
4. Thread the callback from the loop to where AgentRunRuntime is built (execute_bead.go:1666 runRuntime): pass OnRouteResolved through agenttry.AttemptOpts -> Executor -> execute_bead. In the loop near execute_bead_loop.go:2440 set it to func(h,p,m string){ liveness.UpdateRoute(candidate.ID, h, m, p) }. Also fix the SetAttempt 4th arg so route is not "profile".
5. Do NOT change phaseEmpty or LastActivityAt logic: OnTick advances LastActivityAt unconditionally (wall-clock, liveness.go:87-97); resetting the watchdog on heartbeat-advance would DISABLE it (reintroduces the 80-min wedge). The fix is recording the route, nothing else.

NON-SCOPE: D1b/D1c/D1d/D2/D3 are separate beads. Do not weaken the watchdog or consecutive-wedge guard.

ACCEPTANCE
1. TestSidecarLiveness_UpdateRoute (cli/internal/agent/work/liveness_test.go): after SetAttempt(bead,...,route="",harness="",model=""), UpdateRoute(bead,"fiz","sonnet-4.6","anthropic") makes Snapshot() report non-empty Harness/Model/Route; CurrentBead mismatch is a no-op; empty args do not blank existing values.
2. Test asserts OnRouteResolved fires once with the resolved triple in BOTH drainServiceEventsWithRenderer branches (no-watchdog + drain-watchdog) before Final — stub a ServiceEvent channel emitting RoutingDecision then Final.
3. Watchdog test: an attempt with populated route fields past the 30-min Running budget is NOT flagged wedged (progressWatchdog.observe returns fired=false); the existing all-empty frozen case still fires.
4. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/agent/work/... green.
5. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
