description:
PROBLEM (Principle 2 of epic ddx-602ae31a)

`ddx update` must update the same install layer the operator selected. `ddx update --global` should mutate only the global plugin tree and global installed state, while plain `ddx update` should mutate only the active project install in in-tree or convention mode. This can be implemented independently from install, init, lookup, doctor, and docs.

ROOT CAUSE
- `cli/cmd/update.go:57` owns the `ddx update` command flow and is the point where `--global` must branch away from project update behavior.
- `cli/cmd/update.go:204` updates project state and must continue to respect `ddxroot.Path()` for in-tree versus convention mode.
- `cli/cmd/update.go:296` is the global update path and must operate exclusively under `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/`.
- `cli/cmd/install.go:213` remaps install targets and should be reused or mirrored so update writes plugin content and skill links to the correct layer.

PROPOSED FIX
Add or verify `--global` on `ddx update`. In global mode, load global installed state, reinstall or refresh only `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/plugins/<name>/`, and refresh home-tier skill links under `~/.claude/skills/<name>` and `~/.agents/skills/<name>` without touching project `.ddx/` or project skill links. Without `--global`, update the project install under `ddxroot.Path()/plugins/<name>/`; in in-tree mode that is `<project>/.ddx/plugins/<name>/`, and in convention mode it is `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/projects/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/plugins/<name>/`.

GOVERNING ARTIFACTS
- Principle 2 of epic ddx-602ae31a.
- Depends on ddx-06cbaa90: update paths route through `ddxroot.Path()` and `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/`.
- ADR-027 skill install topology or equivalent must stay consistent with update behavior.

PARENT
- ddx-602ae31a

DEPS
- ddx-06cbaa90

NON-SCOPE
- Removing the existing per-project install entirely; global and per-project modes coexist.
- Migrating `~/.config/ddx/` legacy paths if any exist.
- Agent-harness path discovery beyond Claude Code and Codex-facing `.agents/skills`; add others only when those harnesses define their skill paths.
title: update: honor global and project plugin install layers

description:
Finding from fresh-eyes review of DDx-owned retry semantics.

Problem:
The current DDx plan correctly says DDx owns success classification and retry, but it does not define a hard eligibility matrix for when a failed run may be retried with higher MinPower. The upstream agent contract distinguishes capability/semantic failures from deterministic setup failures and says dirty worktrees, merge conflicts, invalid bead metadata, unresolved dependencies, config parse errors, missing binaries, auth failures, and command-not-found cases are not eligible for power retry.

Why this matters:
Without an explicit matrix, DDx can burn stronger models on failures where model power is irrelevant. That keeps DDx involved in agent execution behavior in an ad hoc way and makes retry outcomes impossible to audit.

Required fix:
Extend FEAT-010 and ddx-9f82f325 with a retry eligibility table. DDx may escalate MinPower only for classified outcomes where more capable reasoning could plausibly change the result, using agent status/output as evidence but not inspecting provider/model routing details. Deterministic environment, tracker, dependency, config, auth, missing-binary, and passthrough-unsatisfied failures must stop as blocked/operator-action-required.

Acceptance:
- Retry policy has named eligible and ineligible status classes.
- Tests cover at least one capability failure that escalates MinPower and several deterministic failures that do not.
- Audit records include the classification reason used for retry/stop.
- The policy never branches on provider/model identity except for passthrough constraint exhaustion reported by the agent as a typed status.
title: review finding: define retry eligibility before escalating agent power

description:
PROBLEM
  Today no test runner emits durable timing data. lefthook pre-push,
  pre-commit, Makefile test target, and the GitHub Actions ci.yml
  full-suite step all run `go test ./...` and emit elapsed-time only to
  stdout. There is no JUnit, no `go test -json`, no aggregated artifact,
  no dashboard. The result: when a test gets slow (e.g.
  TestOSExecutor_EarlyCancel becomes a 60s test instead of a 10s test),
  the regression goes unnoticed until a developer manually inspects
  pre-push output. Splitting into unit / integration / e2e tiers is hard
  without baseline timing data.

CURRENT STATE
  - .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `go test -race -cover ./...` and
    emits stdout only.
  - .github/workflows/ci.yml uploads two artifacts (e2e-test-output,
    prompt-size-report) but neither is structured timing data.
  - No `go test -json` invocation anywhere in the repository.
  - Makefile has no test-with-json target.

PROPOSED FIX
  - Add a CI step (in .github/workflows/ci.yml, in the existing test
    job or a new test-timing job) that runs:
        cd cli && go test -json -race -cover ./... 2>&1 | tee /tmp/test-output.json
    Then upload /tmp/test-output.json as a GitHub Actions artifact named
    `test-timing-<run-id>.json` retained for at least 30 days.
  - Optionally add a small Go program under cli/tools/test-timing/ that
    parses go-test-json events and emits a top-N-slowest-tests Markdown
    summary; write the summary as `test-timing-summary.md` and upload
    alongside.
  - Document in CLAUDE.md: "CI uploads test timing as a JSON artifact;
    use it to investigate slow-test regressions."
  - Do NOT modify the lefthook hooks — local pre-push timing is not
    durable and a JSON dump there would just clutter the developer's
    machine.

NON-SCOPE
  - Building a test-timing dashboard or a regression-detection alarm
    (separate concern; this bead just produces durable data).
  - JUnit format (the audit recommended JSON; JUnit is a separate
    concern if test-result reporters are needed).
  - Any change to `go test` invocation in lefthook.

INTERSECTIONS
  - Independent of all sister beads. Composes with the perf-tag and
    -short-gate beads (this bead measures; those beads optimize).
title: ci: emit go test -json across the test suite and upload as artifact for timing visibility

description:
PROBLEM
A Verification mapping row that cites only a test file path — with no specific mapped test, check, or artifact target — reads as evidence to the cardinality join and silently satisfies a requirement that has no pinned proof. Without this exclusion, FEAT-009/FEAT-002/FEAT-012-style documents can pass the coverage gate by pointing at whole files.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer package does not exist in this checkout — the expected path cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1 is absent (cli/tools/lint/ currently contains only evidencelint, routinglint, runtimelint). The sibling cardinality pass counts any mapping row as coverage, with no granularity predicate distinguishing a bare file path from a row naming a concrete target. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, which requires coverage by a Verification mapping row rather than an unspecific pointer.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a citation-granularity predicate to the coverage-cardinality pass: a mapping row whose evidence field resolves to a test-file path without an exact mapped test, check, or artifact target does not count as requirement coverage. Such rows are excluded before the cardinality join, so an otherwise-Complete requirement covered only by file-only citations is reported as uncovered by the sibling cardinality diagnostics. Rows naming a concrete target are unaffected. Follow the package and test conventions in cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer.go and cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer_test.go, including golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis and analysistest-style fixtures where applicable. The analyzer is read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement the zero-evidence (empty row set) diagnostic — that is the sibling zero-evidence child. Do not implement the uncovered/duplicate cardinality diagnostics themselves — that is the sibling cardinality child; this child only supplies the exclusion predicate feeding it. Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not implement status parsing — that is the scaffold child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not resolve whether named Test* symbols, static checks, or artifacts actually exist on disk — evidence-target resolution is a sibling child; this child only inspects whether the row names a target at all. Do not enforce the executable verification command allowlist — command allowlist enforcement is a sibling child.

DEPS: parent ddx-29449fa5 (and its parent ddx-471d66b6); the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model; the sibling coverage-cardinality child. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.
title: spechonesty lint: treat file-only citations as non-coverage in cardinality join

description:
Context:
When `SubmitWithPreMergeChecks()` (cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:131-178) calls `RunPreMergeChecks()` and the outcome is Blocked, `PreserveAfterPreMergeChecks()` writes the result under `refs/ddx/iterations/<bead-id>/<timestamp>-<basesha>` and skips the merge. The bead's evidence list never receives a `pre_merge_check_failed` event with the check name, output, or rationale.

This made a real incident on 2026-05-08 invisible: bead `fizeau-bd5193ca` (in /Users/erik/Projects/fizeau) was redriven 4 times across ~50 minutes / ~$9 of agent cost. Each attempt's result.json reported `outcome: task_succeeded, status: success` (worker classification, written before the gate) and the orchestrator silently preserved the result. `ddx bead evidence list fizeau-bd5193ca` only showed routing + cost events; `ddx bead show` had no hint that pre-merge checks had blocked anything. Operator had no way to discover the rejection without reading orchestrator source.

Reproduction:
1. Claim any bead via `ddx work` whose worker output trips a pre-merge check.
2. Observe result.json status=success, iteration ref preserved, bead remains open, evidence list devoid of pre-merge-check info.

Proposed fix:
- Emit a structured `pre_merge_check_failed` evidence event from `PreserveAfterPreMergeChecks()` (or its caller) with at least: check_id/name, exit_code, stdout/stderr tail, attempt_id, base_rev, result_rev. Append via the same evidence path used by routing/cost events so it shows up in `ddx bead evidence list` and `ddx bead show`.
- The orchestrator's terminal status (post worker + gate) should also be reflected back into result.json's status field — currently it stays `success` regardless of the gate outcome, which is misleading. Either rewrite result.json with the orchestrator's verdict, or add a separate `orchestrator_status` field.
title: execute-bead loop: surface pre-merge check failures as bead evidence

description:
PROBLEM
  Today, when a bead persistently fails (ladder exhausted on
  multiple drain cycles, repair cycles exhausted, or
  review_spec_gap / review_too_large fires), the only path is
  status=proposed → operator action.

  ADR-024 P5 (no human-in-the-loop, sister bead rank 19) requires
  automatic recovery: before parking to proposed, the system must
  attempt automatic reframe (rewrite description + AC) AND/OR
  decompose (split into child beads). Only if both fail does the
  bead reach proposed.

  Today only intake-time reframe (PreClaimIntakeActionableButRewritten
  in cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake.go) can rewrite the bead.
  Post-failure reframe does not exist. Decomposition only fires
  for review_too_large, not for "implementer keeps failing"
  patterns.

CURRENT STATE
  - cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake.go: intake can apply
    actionable_but_rewritten edits. ONE-shot, before claim.
  - cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go has hooks like
    PostAttemptDecompositionHook for review_too_large but NOT a
    general post-ladder-exhaustion hook.
  - status=proposed is the default escape hatch for spec gaps,
    too-large, ladder-exhausted, repair-cycle-exhausted.
  - No consecutive_ladder_exhaustions counter; the system can't
    distinguish "first ladder exhaustion" from "third".
  - No reframer or decomposer prompt templates exist.

PROPOSED FIX
  Add a new post-failure recovery pipeline. After ladder exhaustion
  triggers consecutive_ladder_exhaustions >= 2 (per TD-031 §6 new
  field, sister bead rank 19):

  1. Determine the failure class:
     - review_spec_gap, review_missing_acceptance → REFRAME path.
     - review_too_large or repeated execution_failed at top tier →
       DECOMPOSE path.
     - Other persistent execution_failed → REFRAME first, then if
       reframe doesn't help on next cycle, DECOMPOSE.

  2. Operator opt-out: if bead has label "recovery:manual",
     skip auto-recovery entirely and park to status=proposed
     (matches ADR-024 Operator escape hatches subsection).

  3. REFRAME path:
     - Add prompt template at library/prompts/agents/reframer.md
       — defines the reframer role's input contract (bead body +
       failure history) and output contract (structured edits to
       description and AC).
     - Dispatch a strong-tier (smart+) agent with role=reframer.
     - Apply the edits via the same actionable_but_rewritten path
       intake uses (preserves history, records reframe-applied
       event per TD-031 §5 row from sister bead rank 19).
     - Set status=open; clear consecutive_ladder_exhaustions;
       bead re-enters queue at next cycle.

  4. DECOMPOSE path:
     - Add prompt template at library/prompts/agents/decomposer.md
       — defines the decomposer role's input contract (bead body
       + failure history) and output contract (2-5 child bead
       specs in JSON).
     - Dispatch a strong-tier (smart+) agent with role=decomposer.
     - File the children via Store.Create (with parent set), wire
       deps, set parent's execution-eligible=false.
     - Existing parent → status=open with execution-eligible=false
       so the children get worked first.
     - Emit decompose-applied event per TD-031 §5 row.

  5. Both paths emit structured events (TD-031 §5 rows) with:
     from-rev, to-rev (if any), reframer-cost, reviewer-confidence-score.

  6. ESCAPE HATCH: only if reframe AND decompose BOTH fail (e.g.,
     reframer agent times out, decomposer returns no children) does
     the bead reach status=proposed with auto-recovery-failed event.

  7. Cost: recovery-hook costs accumulate against the per-bead
     budget (sister bead rank 22). If budget exhausts during
     recovery, fall through to per_bead_budget_exhausted (NOT

description:
PROBLEM
After rebuilding ddx (make install), the installed binary at ~/.local/bin/ddx is correct. But subsequent commits land in the source tree, and the operator forgets to rebuild. New flags / subcommands appear in source but silently disappear from the operator's CLI surface. Today's session bit this twice: 'ddx work plan --limit' worked, then later returned 'unknown flag: --limit' — not because the feature was broken, but because the binary was stale relative to source.

OBSERVED (2026-05-03 session)
- Built + installed at commit c0f95380; 'ddx work plan --limit' worked.
- ~10 commits later: 'ddx work plan --limit' returned 'unknown flag.'
- Source still had the flag definition; binary was stale.
- Operator wasted time investigating a non-existent regression before remembering to rebuild.

This compounds because:
1. Source can drift hours-to-days ahead of the installed binary during active development.
2. Cobra's 'unknown flag' / 'unknown command' errors give NO hint that the binary is stale.
3. ddx work auto-spawns workers — those workers also use the stale binary, propagating the gap.

ROOT CAUSE
cli/cmd/version.go implements 'ddx version' and 'ddx --version'. It prints the build-time-injected version string (e.g., 'v0.6.2-alpha12-12-g86848d21') from ldflags but does NOT compare against the source tree's current HEAD when invoked from inside a ddx project repo. No stale-binary detection exists in cli/cmd/doctor.go either. The build SHA is injected at link time via main.go -ldflags but never compared against runtime git rev-parse HEAD.

PROPOSED FIX
Extend 'ddx --version' (or add 'ddx doctor' check) to:
1. Detect when invoked from inside a git repo whose origin matches the ddx project (DocumentDrivenDX/ddx).
2. Compare the binary's build SHA (from -ldflags / main.go version injection) against the repo's HEAD.
3. If HEAD is ahead of the binary's SHA, print a warning to stderr: 'WARNING: installed ddx is built from <binary-sha>; source tree HEAD is <head-sha> (<N> commits ahead). Run "make install" to refresh.'
4. Exit 0 (informational, not fatal).

Optional: emit same warning on EVERY ddx command invocation when inside the ddx project (cheap: one git rev-parse).

NON-SCOPE
- Auto-rebuilding (operator should explicitly rebuild).
- Comparing against upstream remote (only local source tree).
- Detection from outside the ddx project repo.
title: cli: 'ddx --version' should warn when installed binary is behind source tree

description:
PROBLEM
The work applies bead-scoped cooldowns to infra-class failures, contradicting documented policy and violating the forward-progress invariant. Observed today: 14 beads all routed to a temporarily-unreachable LM Studio host received 15-min cooldowns in sequence, then the worker went idle with the entire queue gated for 15 minutes despite cloud providers being reachable. A separate worker also hit a 2nd-strike preclaim cooldown after .ddx/beads.jsonl was momentarily staged between two parallel workers' tracker commits — recoverable in milliseconds, but the policy parked the bead for minutes anyway. Both cases produced the failure the operator named: "cooling down every bead in the queue when we are failing to find a provider, how is that going to fix anything?"

ROOT CAUSE — code violates existing spec
The forward-progress invariant and the right cooldown policy are already documented; the code does not honor them.

- reliability-principles.md P6 (docs/helix/06-iterate/reliability-principles.md:35): "Cooldown fires ONLY when the model genuinely couldn't make progress (clean no-changes with rationale). Disrupted, preflight-rejected, network-error, claim-race -> no cooldown, return to ready." Today's code violates this for `provider_connectivity` and `no_viable_provider`.
- ADR-024 §Infrastructure And Rate-Limit Fallback (docs/helix/02-design/adr/ADR-024-power-escalation-and-review-routing.md:96): "Infrastructure failures are not capability failures... do not consume escalation budget... apply a retry-after cooldown only when time passing could plausibly fix the same attempt class." Loose "or" wording lets the current implementation skirt the intent.
- TD-031 §3.1 (docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-031-bead-state-machine.md:75): "Continuous forward progress is the default. Before a bead can move to `status=proposed`, the drain loop MUST exhaust every applicable automatic path in priority order." Says MAY set retry-after for `no_viable_provider`; the code unconditionally sets 15 min regardless of whether alternative routes exist.

Implementation sites that violate the spec:
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2283-2284 — provider_connectivity sets bead cooldown unconditionally after applyProviderConnectivityRouteExclusion already recorded the failed route. With ddx-71629938 + fizeau-8134d6db landed, the exclusion is the correct mechanism; the cooldown is now redundant deadweight.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2294-2306 — no_viable_provider sets bead cooldown unconditionally; should transition the WORKER to a paused state (like paused-quota), not penalize the bead.
- cli/internal/agent/work/guard.go:96-107 — preclaim-hook-failed sets bead cooldown on 2nd strike regardless of whether the cause is bead-specific (real divergence) or systemic (transient tracker race / index lock). The existing isSystemicPreClaimError path correctly avoids cooldown for global failures; staged-tracker / index-lock races belong in the same class.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:~968 (NoReadyWork branch) — when every ready bead is in cooldown for the same infra reason, the worker goes idle instead of transitioning to a paused-infra state and resuming when the condition clears. Violates "forward progress in all possible scenarios."

PROPOSED FIX
1. Restore code-to-spec conformance for infra-class outcomes:
   - provider_connectivity: drop SetExecutionCooldown call; the work-failed-routes entry + RouteExclusionWindow TTL is the correct mechanism. Bead is immediately reclaimable; next attempt routes around the failed (provider, model).
   - no_viable_provider: drop SetExecutionCooldown; instead transition the WORKER to paused-infra (new state), poll every 2 min, leave every bead immediately reclaimable.
   - preclaim-hook-failed: classify staged-.ddx/beads.jsonl-only and index-lock-races as systemic-transient (existing isSystemicPreClaimError path); skip cycle without cooldown. Only bead-specific persistent failures (across distinct attempts) trigger cooldown.
2. Add paused-infra worker state to TD-031 §4 with entry/exit conditions mirroring paused-quota. Surface in workers panel (P5 operator-visible state) with resume-at timestamp.
3. Worker idle-check (execute_bead_loop.go:~968): before returning NoReadyWork, scan whether every active cooldown shares an infra-fault status. If yes, transition to paused-infra with the earliest cooldown.until as the resume target. Worker sleeps until then, then re-evaluates the full queue.
4. Tighten loose spec wording:
   - TD-031 §3.1 line 73 — "MAY set retry-after (15 min)" for no_viable_provider becomes "MAY set retry-after only when no alternative routing path exists and the condition is purely time-dependent; when alternate routes exist, leave bead immediately reclaimable."
   - ADR-024:96 — replace ambiguous "or" with a crisp rule: cooldown applies only when no alternate route exists AND the condition is purely time-dependent.
5. Operator escape hatch: `ddx bead clear-cooldown [--all] [--reason <class>]` clears work-retry-after on matching beads. Today this requires per-bead `ddx bead update <id> --unset work-retry-after` (14 invocations today).

NON-SCOPE
- Escalation ladder behavior (ddx-8a7a6843 already in progress).
- Fizeau-side route health (fizeau-8134d6db already shipped in v0.14.0).
- Cooldown for genuinely bead-faulting outcomes (no_progress, no_changes with rationale, repair_cycle_exhausted) stays unchanged — those are documented bead-fault cases where time passing may help.
title: work loop: rework cooldown policy — code violates documented forward-progress invariant

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-e19185aa is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 1 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
The decomposition action (currently invoked when a bead is too large for one execution and the agent splits it into child beads) is writing the parent's ID as a dep edge on every child. This produces an unbreakable deadlock:

  e29892a4 (parent, open) -- parent --> child_A
  e29892a4 -- parent --> child_B
  child_A.deps = [e29892a4]           <- BAD: parent is also a dep
  child_B.deps = [child_A, e29892a4]  <- BAD

The parent stays open until its children close. Every child is blocked on the parent. Nothing can be claimed. ddx work loops on the parent, the orchestrator emits 'mixed_commit_and_no_changes_rationale', the worker retries, and burns claim budget without progress.

Observed scenario (niflheim, 2026-06-04 04:30-05:13 UTC):
- Parent: niflheim-e29892a4 ('feat(delta): async write-behind ...')
- 10 children created during planning loops (23223661, a44a8ceb, 054c89b7, 0470ba0d, f10e9e35, f076b08c, 6c041162, 94e1df73, 9da62c2d, 5e4f9fb2)
- Every child carried deps=[..siblings.., niflheim-e29892a4]
- ~50 minutes of agent time + 4 strong-policy claude/opus attempts with zero feature commits; only tracker chores
- Unwedged manually by closing the parent via 'ddx bead close', after which siblings drained correctly in foundational order

Root cause is structural, not model-capability — auto-upgrading to a stronger model does NOT fix this. The orchestrator already detects the no-progress state but its only remediation is 'retry parent', which re-enters the same loop.

There is also a 'project root mutation rejected (continuing)' warning emitted by the readiness check during this state; that's a downstream symptom of the same problem, not the cause.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- 'ddx bead dep add <bead> <dep>' HARD-REJECTS the edge when <dep> is <bead>'s parent OR any ancestor in the parent chain. Error message names the offending ancestor and prints the relevant parent-chain. Test: ddx_bead_dep_add_rejects_parent_ancestor.
- 'ddx bead create --depends-on X --parent Y' with X == Y (or X an ancestor of Y) HARD-REJECTS at creation time with the same error shape as AC #1. No silent rewrite.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.
title: Reject bead dep edges that re-introduce the parent or any ancestor: part 1

description:
PROBLEM
First-time per-machine setup has no entry point, and `ddx init` eagerly installs the default ddx plugin into every project. The intended model is: `ddx init --global` does one-time machine setup (global default plugin + agent-tier links + global config), while plain `ddx init` only creates `<project>/.ddx/` and lazily resolves plugins from the global layer on first use.

ROOT CAUSE
- cli/cmd/init.go:73 `runInit` always installs the default ddx plugin (init.go:271-284 via `registry.InstallPackageFromFS(pkg, defaultplugin.FS(), workingDir)`), producing `.ddx/plugins/ddx`, `.agents/skills/ddx`, `.claude/skills/ddx` unconditionally.
- There is no `--global` flag and no `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/config.yaml` writer.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Add `--global` bool flag to `ddx init` (cli/cmd/init.go).
2. init --global: install the default `ddx` plugin to `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/plugins/ddx` (via the install-global path from the sibling install bead), create agent-tier links `~/.claude/skills/ddx` and `~/.agents/skills/ddx` pointing into the global plugin dir, and write `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/config.yaml` with convention defaults.
3. init (no flag): create `<project>/.ddx/` and the manifest, but do NOT install any plugin — plugins lazy-resolve via `registry.ResolvePlugin` (sibling resolver bead), preferring project over global, on first use. Remove the eager install at init.go:271-284 from the no-flag path.

NON-SCOPE
- The resolver precedence itself (sibling bead: registry two-layer resolution).
- install/update `--global` wiring (sibling bead).
- `ddx doctor` reporting and spec/doc updates (sibling bead: doctor + specs).
- Migrating any `~/.config/ddx/` legacy paths.

DEPS
ddx-06cbaa90 (ddx home resolution); sibling registry-resolver bead; sibling install/update --global bead (reuse its agent-tier link helper).

acceptance: See bead body — 3 verifiable AC items: unit tests covering the four classification scenarios; lefthook green; manual smoke confirming worker emits 'server unreachable' instead of flagging beads when server is down.
description:
**Problem**

When `ddx work --watch` runs against a `ddx server` that is partially
unavailable (e.g. TLS handshake failure, agent-service connection
refusal, persistent route-resolution failures with no candidates), the
worker treats every individual bead as the failure unit. Each attempt
gets flagged with `operator_attention` via the progress-watchdog or
`execution_failed` via the routing preflight, then the next bead is
tried, then the next.

Result: a single server-side problem (one bad TLS cert, an expired
provider credential, a stale model catalog) silently turns the entire
ready queue into "needs human" beads, even though the *beads* are fine
— the *server* is broken. The worker keeps idling, the operator sees
"0 closures in 24h" with no clear signal that this is environmental.

Observed concretely on niflheim on 2026-05-31:

- `ddx server` was serving a TLS cert from
  `$DDX_PROJECT_ROOT/.ddx/server/tls/cert.pem` (Apr 17 fingerprint)
  while the client `ddx work` pinned the cert in `~/.ddx/server/tls/`
  (May 18 fingerprint). The server logged
  `http: TLS handshake error from 127.0.0.1:XXXXX: remote error: tls:
  bad certificate` every ~5 min for ~36 hours.
- Every `niflheim-71365a9f` attempt during that window failed with
  `ResolveRoute: no viable routing candidate: 16 candidates rejected,
  outcome_reason=no_viable_provider`.
- After 15+ attempts the worker flagged the bead for operator
  attention, then quietly idled with `execution-ready=0 blocked=47
  operator-attention=17 needs-human/investigation=10`. No clear
  signal to the operator that the *server* was the cause.

**Desired behavior**

The worker should detect server-level failures separately from
bead-level failures. Two-tier classification:

1. **Bead-level failure** (current behavior): the bead's tests/lint
   fail, the agent commits something invalid, etc. → mark the bead
   `execution_failed`, retry per policy, eventually
   `operator-attention`.
2. **Server-level failure** (new): TLS handshake error, agent-service
   connection refused, persistent `no_viable_provider` across ≥ K
   distinct beads in the last M minutes (default K=3, M=10) → mark
   the *server* unavailable, NOT the individual beads. Loop into a
   probe-and-resume mode: every 30 s ping
   `https://server/api/health`; the moment the server returns 200
   and a small `ddx run --text` smoke test succeeds, re-enter the
   queue. None of the beads attempted during the server-failure
   window get penalized.

The server-failure backoff prevents the per-bead operator-attention
flagging storm we observed. It also makes the actual root cause
visible — `ddx work` should emit a single distinctive log line
("server unreachable: holding queue until /api/health returns") and
expose that state via `ddx work status` so the operator notices it.

**In-scope files (likely; verify before edit)**

- `cli/internal/agent/service_run.go` — wraps `ResolveRoute` →
  classification site for routing failures.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead*.go` — the place where
  `no_viable_provider` is turned into `outcome_reason` for the bead.
- The watcher loop in `cli/internal/work/` (or wherever `ddx work
  --watch` lives) — needs the new server-unavailable state machine.
- `cli/internal/agent/` — health-probe helper.
- New unit tests covering: (a) K consecutive `no_viable_provider`
  across distinct bead IDs trips server-failure mode; (b)
  server-failure backoff doesn't penalize the beads it was about to
  try; (c) successful health probe transitions back to normal queue
  drain; (d) TLS handshake error from the server is classified as
  server-level regardless of bead.

**Acceptance**

1. `go test ./cli/internal/agent/... ./cli/internal/work/...` passes
   with the new tests above.
2. `lefthook run pre-commit` (or equivalent gates) green.
3. Manual smoke: stop `ddx server`, run `ddx work --watch`; observe
   the worker emits "server unreachable" within 30 s and does NOT
   flag any beads for operator attention while the server is down.
   Restart `ddx server`; observe queue drain resumes.

**Out of scope**

- Auto-repairing server-side issues (TLS cert refresh, credential
  rotation). Operator still has to fix the server. The worker just
  has to detect and not amplify the failure.
- Multi-server failover.
- Changing the existing per-bead `operator-attention` semantics —
  those stay for true bead-level failures.

**Severity**: P1. Prevents quiet queue-stall pattern that wastes
operator hours on triage when the actual cause is environmental.
title: ddx work: detect server-level failures separately from bead-level (don't flag beads when server is unavailable)

acceptance: Either: (a) ddx work --watch survives bead-only commits to .ddx/beads.jsonl without exiting, OR (b) when ddx work decides to restart, it actually re-execs the new binary rather than just exiting. Reproducer: run ddx work --watch in any project, then run ddx bead create from another shell — the worker should not die.
description:
Reproducer captured 2026-05-20 in helix repo:

  ddx work: detected installed ddx binary changed (current commit 8bd0ae88e, installed commit ee65c467f); starting replacement worker and exiting

Symptoms: worker exits cleanly on every ddx repo HEAD advance. In a project where ddx bead create / ddx bead update auto-commits to .ddx/beads.jsonl (which they do — see chore(beads): create ddx-* doc-stamp commits), the ddx repo HEAD advances repeatedly. The worker detects this as "binary changed" and self-terminates. No replacement worker is spawned automatically. The user must restart manually.

Result: worker uptime is capped at ~one-or-two bead writes between externally-induced restarts. In a heavy-write session this means a restart every few minutes.

Two issues:
1. The "binary changed" check compares the installed ddx commit against something — what? If it is the running worker process commit hash, then any ddx repo HEAD advance (including bead commits that do not change Go code) triggers a false positive.
2. Even when the check is correct, "starting replacement worker" never actually starts one. The worker just exits.

Suggested fix: only restart on Go-code-affecting changes (track go.mod/internal/ paths in the diff), OR actually spawn the replacement, OR drop the auto-restart entirely and require operator restart on intentional binary upgrades.
title: work --watch self-terminates after every bead commit in same-repo workflows

description:
PROBLEM
A transient route/provider outage parked 23 open beads behind `triage:needs-investigation`. Their latest actionable event was `execute-bead summary=execution_failed` with detail/body `work: all tiers exhausted — no viable provider found`. Once routing recovered, these beads remained excluded from `ddx work` until an operator manually removed the triage label.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_status.go:103-108 already classifies `no viable harness`, `no harness configured`, `failed to initialize routing service`, and `no viable provider` as FailureModeNoViableProvider.

PROPOSED FIX
Handle FailureModeNoViableProvider as a retryable transport outage, not a needs-investigation condition. A no-viable-provider attempt should unclaim the bead and either set a short retry cooldown or leave it retryable according to the existing retry policy, but it must not add or preserve `triage:needs-investigation` solely because routing was unavailable. `ddx work` diagnostics should distinguish provider outage from human-investigation blockers.

PROBLEM (Principle 2 of epic ddx-602ae31a)

`ddx install` targets the project path unconditionally and has no `--global` surface. Operators who want one Claude Code install per machine must repeat the install per project, and project installs do not correctly distinguish in-tree vs convention mode.

ROOT CAUSE

PROPOSED FIX
1. Add `--global` to `ddx install`, `ddx plugin list`, and `ddx plugin show`. When `--global` is set: resolve target via the GlobalPluginDir resolver from the dependency bead (${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/plugins/<name>/), write the plugin content there, and create symlinks (or copies where the OS requires) into the agent-tier skill paths the user's agents read — ~/.claude/skills/<name> and ~/.agents/skills/<name> (and ~/.codex/skills/<name> where the agent registry defines it). 2. Without `--global`: write to ddxroot.Path()/plugins/<name>/ and create project-tier links under <project>/.claude/skills/<name> AND <project>/.agents/skills/<name>. In in-tree mode the links point into <project>/.ddx/plugins/<name>; in convention mode (no <project>/.ddx/) they point into ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/projects/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/plugins/<name>.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx currently duplicates Fizeau policy intent with numeric power on initial zero-config implementation dispatch. In the current code path, DDx selects the `default` Fizeau policy for ordinary implementation work and then also sets `MinPower` to that policy floor. That makes the request shape `Policy=default, MinPower=7` instead of letting Fizeau fully interpret the selected policy.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
`cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:396-401` selects an implementation profile and raises `initialMinPower` to `selection.MinPower` on the first attempt. `cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:426-442` then passes `requestedMinPower` into `singleTierAttempt`, which writes it into `config.CLIOverrides.MinPower` at `cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:289-294`. `cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:241-258` sends both `Policy` and `MinPower` to Fizeau. The same first-attempt pattern exists for `ddx try` at `cli/cmd/try.go:293-322`. Current command tests assert this duplicated shape in `cli/cmd/work_test.go` and `cli/cmd/try_test.go`, so the tests encode the wrong contract.

DESIRED ROUTING CONTRACT
For initial zero-config implementation work, DDx should select an opaque Fizeau policy by metadata and send only that policy. Example: ordinary work selects `Policy=default`, `MinPower=0`. Fizeau owns the model choice and may choose a lower-power model inside that policy if the policy permits it.

For implementation fallback escalation, DDx should keep policy intent and add a numeric floor only after evidence of failure. Example: DDx selects `Policy=default`; Fizeau chooses a power-5 model; the attempt fails; DDx retries with `Policy=default, MinPower=6`. If repeated failures or ladder exhaustion require moving policy bands, DDx may reselect the appropriate policy by metadata, but numeric floors are evidence-driven retry constraints, not initial policy duplication.

For review routing, DDx may use `MinPower` immediately when the reviewer must be stronger than the implementation route or when review pairing evidence requires it.

PROPOSED FIX
Change zero-config implementation routing so first attempts do not copy the selected policy floor into `MinPower`. Preserve explicit operator `--min-power`, bead numeric tier hints, reviewer escalation, and retry escalation. On retry, derive the next floor from the actual route power when available; otherwise use the selected policy floor/ladder only as an escalation basis, not as an initial dispatch floor.

NON-SCOPE
Do not hard-code Fizeau policy names. Do not add DDx-side provider/model selection. Do not change Fizeau policy definitions. Do not remove MinPower support for explicit user flags, review escalation, or implementation retry escalation.
title: routing: send MinPower only for review and fallback escalation

acceptance: cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go ExecuteBead() contains ONLY: worktree setup (or accept pre-made worktree), prompt construction, agent harness dispatch, progress event emission, and a final completion event. No Merge, no UpdateRef, no preserveRef, no evaluateRequiredGates, no outcome classification beyond {task_succeeded, task_failed, task_no_changes}. All merge/preserve/gate logic moved to a new parent-side orchestrator that can be run interactively. Regression test: two workers on two different beads complete in arbitrary order; parent process merges both sequentially with interactive conflict resolution if needed; no worktree-internal merge code paths are exercised.
description:
The current execute-bead worker does WAY too much: creates a worktree, runs the agent, evaluates required gates, decides merge-by-default vs preserve vs land-conflict, writes preserve refs, synthesizes commits on IsDirty, classifies 7+ outcomes, manages heartbeats, handles claim/unclaim contention, runs recoverOrphans on stale worktrees. This surface is why (a) two concurrent workers race on the main-branch merge and the loser's good work ends up under refs/ddx/iterations/ needing manual rescue, (b) no_changes gets misclassified as synthesized-commit success, (c) the gate-enforcement path and the merge path are entangled, and (d) the worker needs special privileges (update-ref, merge, rebase) that a simple task-runner should never have.

The correct design is the one the operator just described: execute-bead is a thin worker. 'I have been handed a worktree and a task. I will execute that task and make commits in the worktree. I will stream progress events to ddx server. I will notify ddx server when I am done, reporting the worktree branch and the commit(s) I made. Then I exit.' That's it.

Everything else — merge to main, conflict resolution, required-gate evaluation, preserve-under-ref, decide whether to close the bead — moves to the PARENT process (the operator, or a driver tool running interactively in the terminal). Merge conflicts are resolved interactively the same as any other merge. A human (or an outer agent with full git authority) reviews the agent's commits and decides what to do with them.

This simplification deletes most of ExecuteBead() in cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go and moves:
- resolveBase / baseRev tracking → parent
- Merge() call → parent
- preserveRef / UpdateRef / refs/ddx/iterations/ writes → parent
- evaluateRequiredGates → parent (or a separate 'ddx agent check' step)
- outcome classification 'merged/preserved/land-conflict/error' → parent
- recoverOrphans → parent (cleanup runs when parent next launches workers)
- heartbeatIsStale reclaim logic → parent (parent tracks worker health)

What the worker keeps:
- Take a worktree dir + task description (prompt) as input
- Launch the agent harness with the prompt
- Stream progress events to ddx server (session log + structured JSONL)
- On exit, emit a final event: worktree path, branch, commit shas (or empty), exit code, duration
- That's it

Execute-loop likewise shrinks or goes away. In the clean design, a driver loop in the parent process picks ready beads, creates a /tmp worktree per bead, calls 'ddx agent execute-bead' (worker-only mode), waits for the worker's exit event from ddx server, reviews the result, and merges or discards. When two beads are in flight concurrently, the parent serializes the merge step — no race possible.
title: Simplify execute-bead worker: task-only, no merge/preserve/gate logic

description:
PROBLEM (epic ddx-602ae31a, Principle 2)

First-time machine setup needs a single umbrella command (`ddx init --global`) that installs the default ddx plugin globally, creates the agent-tier links, and writes the global config. A plain `ddx init` must create the project workspace WITHOUT installing plugins (they lazy-resolve from the global/baked-in layers on first use). `ddx doctor` must surface both install layers so operators can see whether a project install exists or is lazy-resolving to global.

ROOT CAUSE
- `ddx init --global` dispatches to `initGlobal()` (cli/cmd/init.go:75,318), which: creates ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/plugins/ddx (init.go:319-323), installs the bundled default plugin there (init.go:328), creates agent-tier links so every harness discovers the skill (init.go:314-316), and writes ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/config.yaml with convention defaults via `writeGlobalConfig` (init.go:351-366).
- Plain `ddx init` (no flag) must create `<project>/.ddx/` and must NOT write to plugins/ — plugins lazy-resolve via ResolvePlugin (project→global→baked-in).
- `ddx doctor` topology reporting lives at cli/cmd/doctor.go:415 `reportSkillInstallTopology`, which prints `Global Install (<globalPath>) — ok|missing` (doctor.go:447) and `Project Install (<projectPath>) — ok|missing|lazy-resolves-to-global` (doctor.go:448), using `registry.ResolvePlugin` to detect lazy resolution (doctor.go:431-444).

PROPOSED FIX
1. Verify `ddx init --global` creates ~/.claude/skills/ddx and ~/.agents/skills/ddx pointing into ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/plugins/ddx/ and writes the global config.
2. Verify plain `ddx init` creates the project workspace and writes nothing under plugins/.
3. Verify `ddx doctor` renders both the "Global Install" and "Project Install" lines, including the `lazy-resolves-to-global` project status when no project install exists but the global one does.

NON-SCOPE
- Runtime lookup precedence implementation (sibling child — ResolvePlugin).
- The `--global` install/update surface and project install modes (sibling children).
- Removing the existing per-project install entirely (both modes coexist).
- Migrating any ~/.config/ddx/ legacy paths.
- Agent-harness path discovery beyond Claude Code and Codex.

DEPS
- ddx-06cbaa90 (ddx home resolution) — initGlobal and doctor topology both route through `ddxroot.GlobalDir()`.
title: init/doctor: `ddx init --global` umbrella setup, `ddx init` lazy (no plugin install), doctor reports both layers

acceptance: `ddx install --force --local <path>` against a repo containing broken symlinks ONLY under gitignored paths completes successfully. The validation logic either consults .gitignore or skips well-known scratch/dotfile paths.
description:
## Summary

Observed against ddx v0.6.2-alpha103-12-ge6379ebc5 on 2026-05-18.

`ddx install <plugin> --force --local <repo>` validates ALL symlinks in the source tree, including those under gitignored paths. Result: any scratch/tmp file with a stale symlink (e.g. files written by a previous `ddx doctor` invocation under doctor/home/.codex/tmp/) breaks the install despite being gitignored and never intended to ship.

## Reproduction

1. In a repo with `doctor/home/.codex/tmp/` gitignored (matches `.codex`)
2. Run any operation that creates broken symlinks under that dir (e.g. an old codex CLI install no longer present)
3. Run `ddx install helix --force --local /path/to/helix`
4. Install fails: `validating package structure: ... broken symlink target ...`

Repro on HELIX:
```
ddx install helix --force --local /home/erik/Projects/helix
# Error: validating package structure:
#   doctor/home/.codex/tmp/arg0/codex-arg0zt0PZe/apply_patch: broken symlink target ...
```

Workaround: rm -rf the offending tmp paths and retry.

## Expected behavior

`ddx install --local` should skip files that are gitignored in the source repository (run via `git check-ignore -v <path>` or read `.gitignore` directly). At minimum, it should skip paths the user could not have intended to ship: well-known scratch/tmp directory names, dotfiles outside the plugin manifest's declared paths, etc.

## Related

- Related to (but distinct from) ddx-efadca32 (lifecycle worktree empty) filed 2026-05-16.
- Blocks HELIX's `ddx install helix --force` for any operator with tmp scratch state present.
title: ddx install --local walks gitignored paths and fails validation on broken symlinks in scratch/tmp dirs

description:
PROBLEM
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1263-1315 today reads ReadyExecutionBreakdown into result.NoReadyWorkDetail, emits loop.idle, and either returns (--once / drain) or sleeps (--watch). It never diagnoses or auto-remediates. FEAT-010 §Idle-Path Diagnosis and Auto-Remediation requires the loop to diagnose every non-ready bead, fire matching remediators, and re-scan without sleeping when at least one remediation succeeded.

ROOT CAUSE
No diagnose+dispatch logic exists at the insertion point.

PROPOSED FIX
Inside execute_bead_loop.go, after ReadyExecutionBreakdown populates breakdown (~line 1265) and before applyStop/sleepOrWake (~line 1271), insert the idle-path auto-remediation block.

Pseudo-flow (translate to Go):
1. Build childIndex, openChildIndex, depIndex from the store (these may already be computed inside ReadyExecutionBreakdown; expose them or rebuild as needed).
2. Walk breakdown.Epics ∪ breakdown.DepWaiting ∪ breakdown.OperatorAttention. For each bead, call bead.Diagnose(...) (from cli/internal/bead/diagnose.go).
3. Switch on the BlockReasonCode:
   - superseded_pending_close: queue a no-op (the cascade happens automatically inside any subsequent Close(); to actively trigger it on a known X, call store.Close on the SUPERSEDER Y if it's somehow still open in this branch — typically not; if X is the bead and Y is already closed but the cascade never ran, call a new store.RunSupersededCascade(X, Y) helper that runs the same scope-checked cascade out of band).
   - closure_candidate_misclassified: this should disappear once the RC-1 classifier fix lands; if it still appears, log and surface (defensive).
   - dead_intermediate_all_children_closed: trigger the existing closure-evaluation path against the bead.
   - dead_intermediate_open_children_pending OR epic_of_epic: skip (recursion via children handles it).
   - genuinely_needs_decomposition: queue an AutoDecomposeEpic call. At most ONE auto-decompose dispatch per loop iteration (track a counter). Skip if --no-auto-epic-decompose set.
   - dep_blocked_by, parent_child_state_conflict, claimed_in_progress, provider_route_unavailable, gated_by_budget_or_cooldown, malformed_parent_or_dep_ref, dependency_cycle, closed_or_missing_parent, auto_remediation_exhausted, no_diagnosis: no idle-path action; will surface via ddx work focus.
   - stale_graph_index: trigger an index rebuild and re-diagnose next loop.
4. Execute queued remediations sequentially. Track count of successes.
5. If any remediation succeeded, emit loop.auto_remediated event with {remediation_counts: {...}, total_attempted, total_succeeded}, clearTransientCandidateSkips, and `continue` (re-scan without entering sleepOrWake).
6. If none succeeded, fall through to the existing emit("loop.idle", ...) + sleepOrWake path.

Add operator override flags to cli/cmd/work.go: --no-auto-supersede-close, --no-auto-epic-decompose, --no-auto-closure-reclassify. Plumb them through to the work loop via runtime config (mirror how existing --max-recovery-cost flows in).

Add config key work.autoRemediations: { autoSupersedeClose: bool, autoEpicDecompose: bool, autoClosureReclassify: bool } with defaults of true. Flags override config; per-project config overrides defaults.

Reuse existing cost budget threading: AutoDecomposeEpic counts against --max-recovery-cost just like the existing post-TooLarge decomposer does. Honor SmartRetryCooldown / SetExecutionCooldown precedent for per-bead cooldown after failed auto-decompose (already implemented in the auto_decompose_epic bead).

NON-SCOPE
- Implementing the diagnoser, RC-1 fix, RC-2 cascade, RC-3 walk-up, RC-6 handler — those are separate beads this one depends on.
- Operator surface changes (ddx work focus, ddx work plan) — separate beads.

description:
## Observed

The Sessions page ($ sums `session.cost` into one "Total Cost" card, `cli/internal/server/frontend/src/routes/.../sessions/+page.svelte:21,28,91`). The underlying `cost_usd` field is fed from three very different billing realities and the UI treats them as one:

1. **Cash paid (pay-per-token).** API providers (OpenRouter, direct OpenAI, direct Anthropic API). `cost_usd` = actual billed amount.
2. **Subscription-equivalent.** Claude Code, Codex — flat-rate subscriptions. The CLI/harness emits `total_cost_usd` as the **dollar-equivalent** for tokens consumed under the subscription (what you would have paid pay-per-token). You paid a flat fee up front; this is a value-extracted number, not a cash-out number.
3. **Local compute.** Embedded `agent` harness, ollama/vllm endpoints. Today emits cost 0 because no one is billing; real cost is electricity + hardware amortization, not currently modeled.

A user reading "Total Cost: $X" does not know which of those X is.

## What's needed

Three independent rollups, each explicitly labeled, each computable without ambiguity:

1. **Cash** — sum of `cost_usd` across sessions whose billing mode is `paid`.
2. **Subscription-equivalent** — sum across sessions whose billing mode is `subscription`. Copy: "Dollar-equivalent for tokens consumed via Claude Code / Codex subscription. You did not pay this in cash; it's the pay-per-token rate you would have been charged."
3. **Local** — either a count of sessions (if no rate is configured) or a computed dollar estimate if `local_cost_per_1k_tokens` is set in config. Default: count-only, to avoid inventing numbers.

## Backing data model

Session records (the sharded index from `ddx-2ceb02fa`) need a new field `billingMode: "paid" | "subscription" | "local"`. Derive at write time:

- `paid`: harness is an API-endpoint provider (openrouter, openai-compat with an API key, anthropic API, …). Probably any harness with `Surface == "openai-compat"` or a known public-api provider prefix.
- `subscription`: harness is `claude` (Claude Code) or `codex` or `gemini-cli` when using a Google account. Identify by harness name + surface.
- `local`: harness is `agent` (embedded) OR endpoint is localhost / private IP / configured-as-local in provider config.

Classification lives in one place — a small `billingModeFor(harness, surface, baseURL)` function — so the logic isn't duplicated between writer and reader.

## Scope

### Part 1 — Data model

- Extend `SessionEntry` / the session index row with `billingMode string` (enum validated on write).
- Add `billingModeFor(...)` helper + unit tests for each harness/surface combination.
- Back-fill: `ddx agent log reindex` (from `ddx-2ceb02fa`) computes `billingMode` when re-shard-writing legacy sessions.

### Part 2 — Backend rollup

- Modify the sessions GraphQL query (or add a sibling `sessionsCostSummary(projectId, since?)`) to return `{ cashUsd, subscriptionEquivUsd, localSessionCount, localEstimatedUsd? }`.
- Reuse the perf-safe path from `ddx-0a33bc5f` (sessions-index aggregation, shard-aware date filter).

### Part 3 — UI

- Replace the single "Total Cost" card on the Sessions page with three cards:
  - **Cash paid** ($X.XX) — tooltip "Billed by pay-per-token APIs (OpenRouter, direct API keys)"
  - **Subscription value** ($X.XX) — tooltip "Dollar-equivalent for tokens consumed under Claude Code / Codex subscriptions. Not cash out of pocket."
  - **Local sessions** (N) — tooltip "Sessions served locally. Compute cost not modeled." If `local_cost_per_1k_tokens` is set, show "$X.XX est." instead of a count.
- Per-row: small badge `cash` / `sub` / `local` in the cost column, color-coded (green/blue/gray). Tooltip explains the row's bucket.

### Part 4 — Optional config

- `.ddx/config.yaml` gains `cost.local_per_1k_tokens: <float>`. When set, local-session total gets rendered as dollars. When unset, count-only. No auto-estimation.

## Out of scope

- Subscription flat-rate cost modeling ("I pay $20/month for Claude Code"). A useful adjacent bead: divide flat rate by consumption to show $/1M-tokens realized value. Not here.
- Quota trend / headroom. Covered by `ddx-23978824`.
- Reclassifying historical sessions beyond what reindex can infer from their stored harness/surface fields.

description:
PROBLEM (epic ddx-602ae31a, Principle 2)

Operators who run one Claude Code/Codex install per machine need a `--global` surface so skills/personas install once into the machine-wide DDx tree and are discoverable from every project without per-project setup. Today the global install and update paths must write to ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/plugins/<name>/ and link into the home-tier agent skill dirs, using a separate global state file so they never touch a project's install.

ROOT CAUSE
- `ddx install` carries the `--global` flag at cli/cmd/install.go:49 and routes through `resolveInstallDirs(global)` (install.go:184) and `selectInstallState(global)` (install.go:202). For global=true, resolveInstallDirs returns installRoot=`ddxroot.GlobalDir()`, agentSkillsDir=`~/.agents/skills`, claudeSkillsDir=`~/.claude/skills` (install.go:185-193); selectInstallState returns `registry.LoadGlobalState`/`SaveGlobalState` (install.go:206-208). Targets are remapped by `adjustInstallTargets`/`remapSkillTargets` (install.go:215,235). Global installs skip the project auto-commit (install.go:174).
- `ddx update --global` routes through `performGlobalUpdate` (cli/cmd/update.go:300), which operates exclusively on `registry.LoadGlobalState()`/`ddxroot.GlobalDir()` (update.go:301,337,345) and never touches the project tree; the flag is parsed at update.go:395 and dispatched at update.go:66.
- The `--global` flag must also be present on `ddx plugin list`/`ddx plugin show` so query surfaces can target the global tier.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Verify `ddx install <name> --global --silent` writes the plugin under ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/plugins/<name>/ and creates a symlink-or-copy under ~/.claude/skills/<name> and ~/.agents/skills/<name>, recording the result in the global state file (not the project state).
2. Verify `ddx update --global` updates only the global plugin tree and leaves any project install untouched.
3. Add/confirm `--global` on `ddx plugin list` and `ddx plugin show`.
4. Document the global install location in library/skills/ddx/SKILL.md "How this skill works".
5. The ddx-validate pre-commit hook (ddx-777f4a09) must continue to scope skill validation to staged skill files regardless of install location.

NON-SCOPE
- Runtime lookup precedence (sibling child — ResolvePlugin).
- Project (non-global) install behavior and init/doctor wiring (sibling children).
- Removing the existing per-project install entirely (both modes coexist).
- Migrating any ~/.config/ddx/ legacy paths.
- Agent-harness path discovery beyond Claude Code and Codex.

DEPS
- ddx-06cbaa90 (ddx home resolution) — global install routes through `ddxroot.GlobalDir()`.

description:
PROBLEM
The governing docs still disagree on parts of multi-worker execution. SD-013 describes concurrent claims as serialized with "last writer wins", while TP-021 requires one claim to win and losing concurrent `ddx try` attempts to exit without terminal-looking evidence. API-001 and FEAT-012 still describe rebase+fast-forward landing, while repository merge policy forbids history rewriting on execute-bead branches.

ROOT CAUSE
- docs/helix/02-design/solution-designs/SD-013-multi-agent-coordination.md:49 uses stale claim-race language.
- docs/helix/02-design/contracts/API-001-execute-bead-supervisor-contract.md:223-239 describes rebase+fast-forward and push behavior that conflicts with current no-history-rewrite policy.
- docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-012-git-awareness.md:224-239 and :410-416 need to align with the bounded mutation-window contract introduced by TP-021.

PROPOSED FIX
- Amend SD-013 to say concurrent claim attempts are atomic and at most one runner owns the bead.
- Amend API-001/FEAT-012 landing language to distinguish local merge/preserve semantics from any future multi-machine coordination, and remove stale rebase-as-normal wording where it conflicts with no-history-rewrite policy.
- Update reliability-principle references that still say there are 7 principles when the doc now defines P1-P10.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change code behavior in this docs-only bead.
- Do not redesign multi-machine coordination; file separate beads if SD-020 needs implementation changes.
title: docs: align multi-worker claim and landing contracts

description:
PROBLEM
A Niflheim ddx work attempt for bead niflheim-27416d39 reached execution and then failed after DDx/Fizeau routed the continuation to provider vidar model Qwen3.6-27B-MLX-8bit. The route failed with provider_connectivity: openai POST http://vidar:1235/v1/chat/completions dial tcp 100.108.162.80:1235 i/o timeout.

IMPACT
The project queue remains worker-ready, but attempts can fail after useful work if the default/cheap route selects an unreachable Vidar endpoint. This is infrastructure, not a Niflheim acceptance failure.

EVIDENCE
Niflheim attempt id: 20260518T190003-d738a271. Worker output ended with: provider_connectivity, provider=vidar, model=Qwen3.6-27B-MLX-8bit, endpoint http://vidar:1235/v1/chat/completions, i/o timeout.

PROPOSED FIX
Make provider health or route selection avoid unreachable Vidar endpoints, or mark Vidar unhealthy before dispatch so DDx falls back to a reachable provider. Add regression coverage for provider-connectivity failures so a failed route is recorded and retried/falls back without consuming the useful attempt.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change Niflheim beads. Do not mask genuine task failures as provider failures.
notes: 2026-05-21 repro: Niflheim bead niflheim-439a49ae failed attempt 20260521T080548-f4200852 after auto-routing selected `policy=cheap` / `provider=vidar` / `model=Qwen3.6-27B-MLX-8bit` for a medium validation task. Route failed with `connect: connection refused` to `http://vidar:1235/v1/chat/completions`. Bead event recorded `work-failed-routes` for vidar, but the once-worker exited after one failed route instead of retrying/falling back to a reachable route. This confirms the bug remains live and should block further Niflheim burn-down until route failure exclusion/fallback is fixed or Vidar health is marked unavailable before selection.
title: Avoid unreachable Vidar route after provider_connectivity failure

PROBLEM
During ddx-0be85773 dogfood on 2026-06-13, `go test ./cmd/...` and the pre-commit race package loop spawned real provider CLI children (`codex --no-alt-screen`, `claude`, and `gemini`) from cmd tests. Automated DDx tests must be hermetic; they cannot depend on or leave behind live provider processes.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cmd tests run through real routing/discovery code paths without a fake Fizeau/provider discovery layer. Observed tests included TestZeroConfigWork_NoConfigDoesNotEmitUnderSpecified, TestWorkResourceExhaustionEndToEnd_StopsBeforeNextClaim, and TestWorkDoesNotSpawnProviderAfterUnderSpecifiedRouting. cli/cmd/testutils_test.go and cli/cmd/run_test_helpers_test.go set some hermetic env, but they do not block provider CLI discovery or force fake harness binaries for all cmd tests.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add a cmd-test-wide provider isolation guard that removes real provider CLI directories from PATH or points codex/claude/gemini discovery at harmless fake binaries.
- Force Fizeau discovery/cache paths into each test temp root and disable subscription refreshes/network calls in tests.
- Add a leak assertion around cmd tests that fails if a test leaves a descendant provider process alive.
- Update zero-config and work resource tests to use fake harness/service routes instead of real provider discovery.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken production provider discovery. Do not skip the affected tests. Do not kill unrelated interactive provider sessions as part of test cleanup.

description:
PROBLEM
The docker-clone attempt backend is unusable on a remote, rootless, or de-nested Docker daemon (e.g. OrbStack on this machine, docker info Name=orbstack). Every attempt fast-fails in 17-39ms before any agent work with: docker: Error response from daemon: invalid mount config for type "bind": bind source path does not exist: <host path>. Outcome is classified execution_failed / transport.

ROOT CAUSE
cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:612 dockerRunArgs() constructs the container with five classes of HOST bind-mount (--mount type=bind,src=<hostpath>):
  - :622 src=ws.WorkDir            dst=/work               (cloned repo)
  - :623 src=exe                   dst=/usr/local/bin/ddx  (ddx binary, os.Executable())
  - :636 src=ws.DockerRun          dst=/ddx-runtime        (HOME/cache/tmp + injected creds)
  - :641-642 gocache, work-tmp                              (Go build/test cache)
  - :644-649 dockerToolMounts() -> claude/codex/gemini      (agent CLIs via exec.LookPath)
A de-nested/remote daemon's filesystem namespace does not include this machine's /home/erik/... , so every src path 'does not exist' from the daemon's view. Confirmed: 4 attempts on ddx-b5816493 failed this way; failing paths included /home/erik/.local/bin/ddx and /home/erik/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.145. A short -v probe 'succeeded' only because docker silently auto-created an empty dir (the classic -v footgun), proving the source was not visible.

PROPOSED FIX (decomposed into child tasks)
Adopt the standard create -> cp -> start -> cp-out -> rm pattern used for remote/rootless daemons, plus bake static tooling into the image and use daemon-managed named volumes for caches. Only the daemon's own storage (image layers + named volumes) is reliably reachable; everything dynamic is copied in/out.
  1. Bake agent CLIs into the attempt-runner image; drop their bind-mounts.
  2. Keystone: move workspace + ddx binary in via docker create/cp instead of bind.
  3. Convert Go caches + runtime dir to named volumes.
  4. Inject credentials via env/docker cp instead of the runtime-home bind.

NON-SCOPE
- The worktree and local-clone backends (unaffected; worktree is the working default).
- Routing/provider selection.

NOTE: filed from an operator session after switching the live queue drain to --attempt-backend worktree to work around this. Child tasks carry their own file:line scope and AC.
title: docker-clone attempt backend: eliminate host bind-mounts for remote/de-nested daemon compatibility

acceptance:
**User story:** As an operator looking at the DDx web UI, I want to understand at a glance what Workers are vs Sessions, and I want to stop a misbehaving worker or start a new queue drain without dropping to a terminal, so the UI is a real operator surface instead of a read-only status page.

**Acceptance criteria:**

1. **Copy + IA.** Workers page header includes a one-sentence description distinguishing it from Sessions. Sessions page likewise. Each links to the other. Playwright asserts both descriptions are present and the cross-links navigate.

2. **Worker → Sessions navigation.** On worker detail, a "Sessions" section lists sessions produced by that worker (join on `session.workerId`). Empty state reads "No sessions recorded yet." If session records do not yet carry a worker ID, that gap is filled as part of this bead and backfilled for existing sessions in the current run (no historical backfill required).

3. **Session → Worker backlink.** Expanded session row shows worker ID as a clickable link when present.

4. **Stop worker.** Each row with `state == 'running'` shows a Stop button. Clicking prompts for confirm, then fires a GraphQL mutation that stops the worker. UI updates within 2s via the existing subscription/poll path. Integration test asserts: button visibility is gated on state, confirm dialog is required, and mutation invokes the same code path as `ddx agent workers stop`.

5. **Start worker.** A "Start worker" button in the Workers page header opens a form (harness/profile, effort, optional label filter). Submitting fires a `startWorker` mutation. On success the new worker appears in the list within 2s. Form validation prevents empty submissions. The code path reuses `ddx work` / work internals — not a separate implementation.

6. **Audit trail.** Every lifecycle action (start, stop, cancel) is recorded as a timestamped event visible on the worker detail page, including the actor identifier the server has for the requester.

7. **No regressions.** Existing live log streaming, recent events, and phase overrides continue to work. Playwright smoke of the worker detail page passes.

8. **Playwright e2e.**
   - Navigates to Workers page, asserts header description.
   - Clicks "Start worker", fills form, submits, asserts new row appears.
   - Clicks Stop on that row, confirms, asserts row state transitions to `stopped`.
   - Clicks into the stopped worker, asserts the Sessions section renders (or the empty state).
   - Asserts the "Sessions" link in the worker page header navigates to the Sessions page.

9. **Design review sign-off.** Before implementation begins, a short design note (one page or less) in `docs/helix/02-design/` captures the Workers-vs-Sessions mental model, the chosen controls, and any CLI primitives that need to exist. Implementation PR links to that note.
description:
## Observed

`/nodes/.../projects/.../workers` renders a table of workers but has no buttons, no controls, and no explanation of how it differs from `/sessions`. The layout (`cli/internal/server/frontend/src/routes/nodes/[nodeId]/projects/[projectId]/workers/+layout.svelte`) shows ID / Kind / State / Current Bead / Attempts — read-only. Clicking a row drills into live-streaming logs and recent events, but offers no actions there either.

This raised a fair question: **what is this screen for, and how is it different from Sessions?** The answer isn't in the UI.

## Ground truth (from the CLI)

- **Worker** = a persistent work process draining the bead queue (`ddx work` / `ddx agent work`). Has a lifecycle: running / idle / stopped / error. Has a *current bead* and cumulative attempts/successes/failures. Can be stopped via `ddx agent workers stop`. Long-lived.
- **Session** = a historical record of one agent invocation (harness, model, bead, tokens, cost, outcome, start/end). Immutable after completion. One worker produces many sessions over its lifetime.

So: Workers are *processes you operate*. Sessions are *events you review*. The current UI exposes both as flat tables and lets the reader guess which is which.

## Gaps

1. **No disambiguation.** No page-level copy, no link between the two, no worker→sessions navigation ("show sessions produced by this worker"), no session→worker backlink.
2. **No lifecycle controls on Workers.** The CLI has `ddx agent workers stop` and `ddx work` (start). The UI has neither button. No stop, start, restart, or "cancel current bead" affordance. The State column is a spectator sport.
3. **No worker start UX.** There is no way to start a queue drain from the UI — users must drop to a terminal.
4. **Unclear empty state.** "No workers found." does not say whether that is normal (nothing running) or broken (server can't see workers). No hint about how to start one.
5. **No worker details beyond logs.** Worker detail page shows live phase + log tail + tool calls but not: worker config (project path, profile/harness, started-at, last-heartbeat), resource usage, or the list of sessions this worker has produced.

## Proposed direction

Split into two deliverables — do them together if we're touching this screen anyway, but they are independently landable:

### A. Information architecture (copy + navigation)

- Add a short header description to each page: "Workers drain the bead queue. Sessions are the history of what they ran."
- Mutual links: Workers page links to "Recent sessions →", Sessions page links to "Workers →".
- On worker detail: a "Sessions" tab or section listing sessions where `session.workerId == this.id` (requires session records to carry workerID; check whether they do).
- On session detail (expandable row already exists): if the session has a workerID, surface it as a link back to the worker.

### B. Lifecycle controls

- **Stop** button per running worker row → calls a GraphQL mutation that invokes the equivalent of `ddx agent workers stop <id>`. Confirms before acting.
- **Start worker** button in the page header → opens a small form (project, profile/harness, effort, optional bead filter) and calls a `startWorker` mutation that shells out to `ddx work` in the background. The form should default to sane values and be submittable in one click for the common case.
- **Cancel current bead** action on the worker detail page — signals the worker to abandon the in-flight bead without killing the loop. (Only if CLI primitive exists; otherwise descope and note in the bead.)
- All mutations must be idempotent and log an audit record viewable in the UI (who did it, when). Reuse existing session-event plumbing if possible.

### Out of scope

- Rewriting work semantics.
- Cross-project worker orchestration.
- Auth / permissions model for who can stop workers (assume single-operator for now; file a follow-up if multi-operator becomes real).

description:
PROBLEM: `cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go:151-156` defines
`TrackerLockSample{LockDir, Wait, Hold, Retries}` and a global
`TrackerLockMetricsSink func(TrackerLockSample)` (line 161). The hook fires
on every acquire+release cycle at line 232. **No production code wires the
sink to anything operator-visible** — the sample is computed and dropped on
the floor. Similarly, `lockmetrics.Instrument("tracker.lock",
"tracker.commit", fn)` at line 231 always passes the literal label
"tracker.commit" regardless of which of the five call sites
(`durable_audit.go:50`, `execute_bead.go:694`, `execute_bead.go:1493`,
`execute_bead_land.go:839`, `execute_bead_land.go:857`,
`execute_bead_land.go:1210`) is holding the lock — so the metric cannot
distinguish a slow durable-audit commit from a slow Land or a slow
pre-dispatch worktree creation.

OBSERVED 2026-05-28: a niflheim drain with two concurrent `ddx work`
processes saw worker B (pid 681801) time out on the tracker lock with
`tracker lock timeout (max elapsed, lock: ..., owner pid: 424293)` after
the 30s `MaxElapsed` budget defined in `DefaultLockRetryPolicy`. We have
no log of how long A held the lock or which call site was holding —
diagnosis required reading the source to enumerate the call sites and
infer plausible candidates (pre-dispatch worktree creation, Land merge).
The metric to answer "was that a 31s hold or a 2.9s hold blocked by a
30s queue" is computed but never logged.

ROOT CAUSE: Two coupled gaps —
  1. `withTrackerLock` / `withMainGitLock` (line 145 and 128) take no
     section/caller identifier, so the sink receives only `LockDir`
     plus timings. There is no way to attribute a long hold to a
     specific call site from the metric alone.
  2. No worker startup code installs a `TrackerLockMetricsSink`. The
     hook is a dead extension point in production.

PROPOSED FIX:

A) Plumb a section identifier through the lock API:
   1. Extend `withMainGitLock` and `withTrackerLock` to accept a
      `section string` parameter (e.g. "durable_audit", "pre_dispatch",
      "land", "preserve_dirt", "ancestry_local").
   2. Extend `TrackerLockSample` with `Section string`.
   3. Pass `section` to `lockmetrics.Instrument` (replacing the hardcoded
      "tracker.commit") so cap- and metrics-level views also distinguish
      sites.
   4. Update all six call sites listed above to pass a stable section
      string.

B) Wire the sink to the worker log in `ExecuteBeadLoopRuntime`:
   1. In `execute_bead_loop.go` near where the runtime / log is
      constructed (search for `runtime.Log` usage near `emit(...)`
      callsites), install a sink that, on every release, emits a
      structured line. Use the existing `emit` event stream when
      available (`emit("loop.tracker_lock", map[string]any{...})`) so
      the data shows up in the same channel as `loop.idle`,
      `loop.operator_attention`, etc. Always also write a plain-text
      log line for terminal monitors:
        `tracker_lock section=<x> wait=<dur> hold=<dur> retries=<n>`
   2. Make the install per-worker and idempotent (the sink is a package
      global today; if multiple workers run in the same process the
      sink must serialize or use sync/atomic). For per-process worker
      isolation as it stands, idempotent install at worker start is
      sufficient.

C) Surface lock samples in `ddx work status`:
   - Out of scope for this bead. Track separately if useful — the log
     wiring is the immediate need.

NON-SCOPE:
- Narrowing the lock-held region itself — tracked separately in the
  sibling bead about pre-dispatch and Land lock-surface narrowing.
- Changing the retry policy (30s MaxElapsed, 200 MaxRetries, 1s ceiling).
- Adding a new metric backend or storage; emit through existing
  `loop.*` event stream and `runtime.Log`.
- Adding telemetry to non-execute-bead lock sites (e.g.
  `cmd/bead.go:167`).

IN-SCOPE FILES:
- cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go (add Section field, plumb param)
- cli/internal/agent/durable_audit.go (pass "durable_audit" section)
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go (pass "preserve_dirt" at 694,
  "pre_dispatch" at 1493)
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go (pass "ancestry_fetch" at 839,
  "ancestry_local" at 857, "land" at 1210)
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go (install sink at worker start)
- cli/cmd/bead.go (pass a section identifier at line 167 —
  "cmd_bead_write" or similar)
- cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock_test.go (extend tests for Section
  field and sink behavior)

OUT-OF-SCOPE FILES:
- gitlock package
- cli/internal/lockmetrics — already accepts the label parameter; only
  change is in callers
- ddx work status command (separate bead if surfaced there later)
title: execute-bead: wire TrackerLockMetricsSink to worker log with section identifier (current sink is unread, lock hold/wait times invisible)

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-937de9fc is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 5 of 5 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM (Principle 2 of epic ddx-602ae31a)

Skills, personas, and plugin content need to install in two distinct locations depending on operator intent:
