description:
PROBLEM
ddx bead create and ddx bead update each auto-commit a single tracker change (the bead's JSONL line plus events). When .git/index.lock is held by a transient external git process (notably the Claude Code statusline poller running `git diff --quiet` every second or two), the auto-commit fails with "fatal: Unable to create '.git/index.lock': File exists. Another git process seems to be running in this repository, or the lock file may be stale". Observed multiple times today: filing or updating a bead during routine session activity bounced on the statusline poll's transient lock and required a manual retry. The earlier fix (71699db95 fix(agent): recover stale .git/index.lock by owner liveness + age) added recoverGitIndexLock + runGitWithIndexLockRecovery, but those are only wired into the execute-loop's commitTrackerLocked and readTreeHeadWithRetry — not into the bead-create/update auto-commit path.

ROOT CAUSE
cli/internal/bead/store.go (the auto-commit on bead mutation) invokes git add / git commit via the standard internalgit.Command wrapper without the index-lock recovery. cli/cmd/bead.go's `runBeadCreate`, `runBeadUpdate`, `runBeadClose`, `runBeadDep*` all funnel into the same Store.WithLock + Store auto-commit path. Today the recovery helper is package-private to cli/internal/agent (runGitWithIndexLockRecovery); the bead package cannot use it.

PROPOSED FIX
- Lift runGitWithIndexLockRecovery and recoverGitIndexLock from cli/internal/agent into a small shared package (e.g. cli/internal/gitlock) so both the agent and bead packages can call into it.
- Wire the bead-mutation auto-commit path (Store.AutoCommit or equivalent in cli/internal/bead/store.go) to use the recovery helper for git add / git commit / git update-ref calls.
- No retry budget escalation: the recovery is identical (3 attempts ~1s worst case), bead operations stay fast.
- Migrate cli/internal/agent's call sites to use the shared package so we don't keep two copies.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change bead-create or bead-update semantics. Recovery is transparent.
- Do not change the index.lock recovery heuristic itself; just reuse it.
- Do not change the ddx work execute-loop path (already covered).

DEPS
None.
title: bead: route ddx bead create/update auto-commits through git-index-lock recovery

description:
## Status: classified — ddx-agent bug (not DDx, not omlx server)

Wire-level evidence captured 2026-04-18 with v0.3.12's AGENT_DEBUG_WIRE=1 (upstream bead agent-941e7e42, landed in this session). Evidence: /tmp/vidar-omlx-wire.jsonl (3 events for a single failing attempt).

## Root cause

ddx-agent is sending an Anthropic-specific 'thinking' field in the OpenAI-compatible request body:

    POST http://vidar:1235/v1/chat/completions
    Content-Type: application/json
    body (18989 bytes, includes):
      "stream":true,
      "stream_options":{"include_usage":true},
      "thinking":{"budget_tokens":8192,"type":"enabled"},
      "tools":[... 6 tools ...],
      "model":"Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit"

vidar-omlx opens a valid SSE stream (HTTP 200, Content-Type: text/event-stream), emits the first assistant-role delta frame correctly, then silently terminates the stream after 186 bytes without writing data: [DONE] or an error frame. The OpenAI Go client parses the one valid frame, hits stream termination, and surfaces 'unexpected end of JSON input'.

The 'thinking' field is Anthropic extended-thinking config. It is NOT in the OpenAI chat-completions schema. omlx (OpenAI-compatible) has no handler for it; the server reaches a silent error path in its generation pipeline when it encounters it in the processed request.

## Responsibility

ddx-agent owns per-flavor request serialization. The library must use Provider.DetectedFlavor() (landed in v0.3.12 via agent-92f0f324) to gate which fields are included in the wire body. Non-Anthropic providers must NOT see 'thinking'.

This bead now tracks the DDx-side work to:
1. Confirm the classification and hand off to upstream via a concrete agent-repo bead.
2. Retry vidar-omlx once the upstream fix lands in a v0.3.13 bump.

Upstream bead to file in ~/Projects/agent: 'provider: strip non-portable fields (thinking) from non-Anthropic request bodies using DetectedFlavor() gate'.

## Classification was correct to wait for evidence

Prior to this capture, the bead's framing (upstream fix assumed) could have been over-scoped. The fresh-eyes review (codex + opus, 2026-04-17) flagged that the 'direct curl works' isolation was insufficient — 'unexpected end of JSON input' is equally consistent with (a) DDx sending a malformed request, (b) ddx-agent parser defect, (c) omlx server defect. The wire capture shows:

- (a) partially true: DDx IS passing a preset that triggers the thinking field, but this is a library responsibility to gate by destination flavor.
- (b) false: the parser reads what it gets; it errors because there is literally no more data to parse, not because the data is malformed.
- (c) partially true: omlx silently terminates instead of returning a 400 with 'unknown field: thinking', which is poor error handling — but the root cause is the library sending a field omlx shouldn't receive.

The layer that MUST fix this is ddx-agent: the library builds the request; the library knows the destination flavor (agent-92f0f324 DetectedFlavor); the library must strip fields that would be ignored-or-fatal at the destination.

## Evidence

/tmp/vidar-omlx-wire.jsonl preserved. Three events: request (body captured, Authorization redacted), response headers (HTTP 200, text/event-stream), response body (186 bytes, one valid assistant-role delta frame, then EOF).

Failed bead from retry: agent-b1c2d3e4 (in ~/Projects/agent; not a DDx bead). Same failure shape as the prior two attempts on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit and Qwen3-Coder-Next-MLX-4bit — confirms model-independent + project-independent.

## DDx-side action

1. File the upstream bead in ~/Projects/agent with the wire evidence inlined. See agent-<hash> filed in the same commit as this update.
2. Close THIS bead as 'evidence-gathered, scope-handed-off' per its own AC #3.
3. When upstream ships the fix in a v0.3.13+ bump, file a chore bead for the dep bump and retry vidar-omlx.

description:
Third child of ddx-b7ee0d6f. When two workers run in parallel on the same machine (each in its own execute-bead worktree), and both complete and attempt to land, the orchestrator uses `git merge --no-edit` with the ort strategy to fold one worker's commits into master. This produces a merge commit tree instead of a linear history, and triggers repeated 'chore: checkpoint before merge' commits when the working tree isn't clean.

## Evidence (source)

cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_orchestrator.go:59-69 defines the Merge function:

    // Merge merges rev into dir's working tree via git merge. It commits any...
    func Merge(dir, rev string) error {
        _ = osexec.Command("git", "-C", dir, "commit", "-m", "chore: checkpoint before merge").Run()
        ...
        out, err := osexec.Command("git", "-C", dir, "merge", "--no-edit", rev).CombinedOutput()
        if err != nil {
            _ = osexec.Command("git", "-C", dir, "merge", "--abort").Run()
            return fmt.Errorf("merge: %s: %w", strings.TrimSpace(string(out)), err)
        }
    }

## Evidence (symptom on axon)

git reflog master on axon's eitri machine shows 12+ `Merge made by the 'ort' strategy` entries on 2026-04-13 within a 2-hour window, each one merging a sibling SHA that never appeared on origin:

    master@{8}  merge 5eb67fd0afab40ba4f9b06a8228760d69187af9d
    master@{12} merge 77999324c59bb715ee6ef290255a5b31e17b1930
    master@{13} merge 79772765312e3bc5a0715a6d9a2860016463e594
    master@{17} merge 268f63283af2df6bfde94200b5159222ea4f996d
    ... and nine more

Interleaved with 'chore: checkpoint before merge' commits. This is the signature of two+ parallel workers each producing sibling branches that get merged back into master one at a time, each merge preceded by a defensive checkpoint.

## Required behavior

Replace merge-based landing with rebase-based landing:

1. When a worker completes, its worktree is at commit W (child of base B)
2. Between B and now, master may have advanced to M (due to sibling workers or fetch-from-origin)
3. Instead of `git merge --no-edit W` on master, do:
   a. `git rebase --onto M B W` in the worker's worktree (or equivalent plumbing via `git cherry-pick B..W` onto M)
   b. On conflict: preserve the worker's commits under refs/ddx/iterations/<bead>/<timestamp>/ (existing infrastructure at execute_bead_orchestrator.go:21-26), unclaim the bead, stop the worker loop
   c. On clean rebase: fast-forward master to the rebased tip
4. NO checkpoint commits. If the master worktree is dirty, that's a bug in the preceding workflow (should have been committed by the worker) — fail loudly, don't paper over with a checkpoint

## Why rebase over merge

- Linear history — no fan of merge parents from parallel runs
- Conflicts surface earlier (during rebase, not as a semantically-broken merge)
- Each bead produces exactly one commit on master; a clean log of 'this bead → this commit'
- Push-ff-only from the sibling push bead (ddx-83ec1430) works because history stays linear

## Interaction with fetch bead

With ddx-bd42f640 ensuring HEAD is current with origin before work starts, and this bead ensuring intra-machine landings are linear, a worker's commit sequence is always: fetch → linear base → work → rebase → push. No merges, no sibling fans.

## Remove the checkpoint-before-merge pattern

The 'chore: checkpoint before merge' commits exist because the Merge function tries to handle a dirty worktree by committing it first. In the rebase model, a dirty worktree is illegal — the worker must have committed everything before the landing phase. If the worktree is dirty at landing time, error out immediately with a clear message about the worker not having committed cleanly. Do not silently checkpoint.
title: work: rebase sibling workers instead of git merge --no-edit (ort)

ddx update --force unconditionally overwrites files under library/ with their registry-version counterparts. Today this destroyed in-progress, uncommitted edits to library/skills/ddx/SKILL.md and library/skills/ddx/reference/work.md (a "Starting and monitoring workers in the background" section added earlier in the session that had not yet been committed). - Optionally: when overwriting under --force --discard-local, save the original to .ddx/update-backup/<timestamp>/<path> so the operator can recover.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change update's git-merge behavior for the project's own files (not library/).
- Do not change the registry-fetch mechanism.

None.

description:
PROBLEM: ddx accumulated ~132 phantom dependency edges (dependencies[].depends_on_id pointing to bead IDs absent from beads.jsonl AND beads-archive.jsonl), which permanently blocked ~29 beads from readiness and stalled the live queue (readyFiltered/classifyLifecycleQueue treat a missing-target dep as unsatisfied forever). The REPAIR + one write-path guard already landed (merge to main: ddx bead doctor gained a 'dangling_dep' finding that prunes such edges archive-aware; Store.updateBead now rejects NEWLY-introduced dangling edges). This bead closes the REMAINING source paths so phantoms stop appearing.

ROOT CAUSES still open (from investigation):
1. cli/internal/bead/merge.go MergeTrackerConflictJSONL set-unions the dependencies list via mergeObjectLists(dependencyMergeKey,...) with NO referential-integrity check (merge.go:~162). A parent's dep edges merge in while child records on a dropped branch do not -> dangling. PRIMARY accumulation path for ddx-internal merges (ddx bead import / sync).
2. cli/internal/bead/import.go:~281 detects dangling deps but only WARNS ('dangling dep (skipped)') and appends the bead WITH the dangling dep intact. The '(skipped)' wording is false.
3. cli/internal/bead/store.go detectPrefix (~:3070-3087) returns filepath.Base(workingDir)/filepath.Base(cwd) when 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel' is unavailable; run inside an execute-bead worktree this yields a prefix like '.execute-bead-wt-...', producing malformed child IDs (one such ID is live in the tracker). ValidateID should have rejected a leading '.', so these bypass Create/GenID validation via raw WriteAll/import/merge.

PROPOSED FIX:
- merge.go: after the union, drop any dependency edge whose depends_on_id is not present in the merged bead set UNION the archive sibling (mirror doctor.go loadArchiveBeadIDs). Add a referential-integrity pass in MergeTrackerConflictJSONL (or ValidateTrackerJSONLUnique).
- import.go: actually strip dangling deps (filter them out of the bead's Dependencies) and report count; keep the warning but make it true.
- detectPrefix: reject a derived prefix that fails the ValidateID charset (or contains '.'/'/'); fall back to DefaultPrefix. Optionally validate GenID output against ValidateID before returning.
NON-SCOPE: the doctor 'dangling_dep' finding + updateBead guard are already landed; do not redo them. Do not change readiness semantics here (separate decision).

CONTEXT: the durable cross-machine convergence works today because doctor --fix bumps updated_at and the supervisor union resolver keeps newest-updated_at, so pruned records propagate. This bead is about stopping NEW phantoms at the ddx write/merge/import layer.
title: Close the remaining phantom-dep write paths: merge union, import, and worktree-prefix ID contamination

description:
PROBLEM
`ddx work` startup cleanup can already reap stale worktrees and stale worker-sidecar directories, but it does not terminate or report the underlying DDx-owned process group when a stale sidecar corresponds to an already-orphaned attempt descendant. That leaves the queue controller looking healthy while the host still burns CPU or holds ports.

ROOT CAUSE
`cli/cmd/startup_housekeeping.go:97-126` only reads run-states and then calls `scanWorktrees`, `scanWorkerDirs`, and `scanExecutionDirs`; there is no process-cleanup pass in the pre-claim path.
`cli/cmd/startup_housekeeping.go:218-267` only reaps stale `.ddx/workers/agent-loop-*` directories after liveness checks. It does not consult process-group evidence or emit a structured observation when a stale attempt descendant is reaped or preserved.

PROPOSED FIX
- Wire the same conservative attempt-process pass used by the cleanup manager into startup housekeeping before the next bead claim.
- Emit a structured cleanup observation when startup reaps or preserves a process group so operators can see why the host was or was not cleaned.
- Keep the existing worktree, worker-dir, and execution-dir retention logic intact, including the cleanup lock/jitter behavior already in place for long-lived workers.
- Add command tests that prove startup cleanup runs the process pass before claim and preserves live run-state / worker-sidecar / registered-worktree / other-project processes.

NON-SCOPE
- `ddx cleanup` JSON/text shaping is covered by the sibling cleanup-command bead.
- The process-census/reaper logic itself lives in the sibling agent bead.
- Documentation updates in `docs/` are handled separately.
- No change to worker modes, queue selection, or retention-policy semantics.
title: cmd: run stale attempt-process cleanup during work startup

acceptance:
**User story:** As a developer on the Efficacy page, I understand what Compare is for the moment I see it, and I can either select rows I already care about and compare them, or I can ignore the feature entirely if it's not for me.

**Acceptance criteria (assume outcome (2) — "redesign in place"; rewrite these if (1) or (3) is chosen):**

1. **Decision note.** One-pager in `docs/helix/02-design/` records the chosen outcome (relocate / redesign / remove), the evidence behind it (usage grep, dependency scan), and the scope of remaining work. Implementation PR links to it.

2. **Row-selection entry point.** Efficacy table rows gain a leading checkbox column. Selecting ≥2 rows enables a "Compare selected" button in the page header. With 0 or 1 rows selected the button is disabled (not hidden) with a tooltip explaining why.

3. **Pre-seeded comparison.** Clicking "Compare selected" launches the existing comparison flow with arms pre-populated from the selected rows' `(harness, provider, model)` tuples. The prompt field is still required (comparisons need a prompt) but is the only field the user has to fill in — the arm list is done.

4. **Removed from cold-start.** The standalone "Compare" button on the Efficacy page (the one that creates an empty comparison) is removed. New comparisons originate from a row selection. If users legitimately want a from-scratch comparison, that path lives on a separate `/experiments` page (out of scope for this bead unless the design note calls for it).

5. **Empty-state copy.** When the Efficacy table is empty, the Compare affordance is hidden entirely (no point selecting zero rows).

6. **Playwright e2e.**
   - Seeds the fixture with ≥3 efficacy rows.
   - Asserts the Compare button is disabled with 0/1 selections and enabled with 2+.
   - Selects 2 rows, clicks Compare, asserts the comparison form opens with arms pre-populated from those rows and only the prompt field is empty.

7. **No regression to efficacy perf.** All perf targets from `ddx-0a33bc5f` still hold. Adding a checkbox column does not change the payload the resolver returns.
description:
## Observed

The Efficacy page has a "Compare" button that opens a flow for adding "arms" and writing a prompt. User feedback: they're not sure what to do with it. It does not match their mental model of what efficacy is (a session aggregation grouped by provider / harness / model).

## Ground truth

- The backing feature is `Query.comparisons` and the comparison record set (`cli/internal/server/graphql/resolver_feat008.go:211-226`). It's an A/B-style "run the same prompt across N arms and compare results" tool. That is a real capability — just not what a rollup/efficacy dashboard is for.
- It's colocated with Efficacy today probably because both involve harness/model performance. The colocation is creating confusion: the Efficacy page promises "how are things doing" and the Compare button promises "design an experiment" — different audiences, different tasks.

## Decision required

Before implementation, decide one of three:

1. **Relocate.** Move Compare to its own top-level surface (e.g., `/experiments` or `/compare`) and cleanly separate "how did things go" (efficacy) from "design an A/B" (compare). Efficacy page loses the Compare button entirely.
2. **Redesign in place.** Keep it on the Efficacy page but recast as "Compare these rows" — the user selects 2+ efficacy rows and launches a comparison pre-seeded from them. Removes the cold-start prompt-entry UX; connects directly to the rollup the user is already looking at.
3. **Remove.** If comparisons are not being used by real workflows, drop the feature and the associated UI/resolver. Least code, least surface area.

The user did not mandate a specific choice — they flagged the confusion and the mental model. Option 2 aligns best with their stated mental model (efficacy = session aggregation); option 1 is the cleanest separation of concerns; option 3 is viable only if usage data supports it.

## Proposed direction

Run the design decision as a short spike (≤ half a day):

- Check whether `comparisons` is referenced by anything beyond this UI page: CLI, docs, specs, other server endpoints. Deletion cost is a function of that.
- Usage check: grep agent-logs + bead evidence for any `comparison_id` or `compare` correlation over the last 30 days. Is anyone actually running comparisons?
- Write a one-page decision note in `docs/helix/02-design/` recording the choice, the evidence that supports it, and the scope of the implementation work.

This bead's remaining acceptance criteria are written assuming the outcome is (2) "redesign in place" — the most-likely-to-be-built option. They should be rewritten when the decision is made if the outcome is (1) or (3).

## Out of scope

- Anything the Efficacy perf/source rework (`ddx-0a33bc5f`) covers.
- Multi-run orchestration changes to how comparisons execute.
title: Efficacy 'Compare arms' button is unclear and misplaced: decide whether to relocate, redesign, or remove

description:
PROBLEM
A pinned DDx worker still launched a non-pinned provider child during the 2026-06-13 dogfood run. The worker command was `ddx work --watch --idle-interval 30s --harness codex --model gpt-5.4-mini --review-harness codex --review-model gpt-5.4-mini --request-timeout 20m` for bead ddx-aef128f7. At 2026-06-13T16:10:51Z, worker pid 4105977 still owned `codex exec ... -m gpt-5.4-mini` pid 4116435, but also owned `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/gemini` pid 4130588. That violates the DDx/Fizeau provider-independence contract: explicit passthrough constraints must apply to every DDx-owned lifecycle, review, and execution subprocess, and DDx must not silently widen to a different harness/provider.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/dispatch.go:70-82 and cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:208-224 preserve rcfg harness/provider/model only at the AgentRunRuntime dispatch boundary. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1456-1459 records route evidence after the provider returns, but there is no worker-level invariant or test that all DDx-owned child processes created during a pinned worker run match the requested harness/model or have explicit lifecycle routing evidence. Existing hidden lifecycle callers still use ClearRoutingPins in cli/internal/agent/recovery_reframe.go:89, cli/internal/agent/triage_hook.go:118, cli/internal/agent/lint_hook.go:132, and cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:556; any one of these can create a provider child that escapes the operator pin.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add an execution-level regression that starts a pinned worker/attempt with fake codex and fake gemini/claude executables on PATH and fails if any DDx-owned child process invokes an unrequested provider binary.
- Audit every AgentRunRuntime with ClearRoutingPins=true in lifecycle/review/intake/reframe paths and make each caller either preserve explicit worker passthrough constraints or record an explicit, operator-approved autonomous route decision.
- Add worker process-tree attribution/evidence for provider child commands during lifecycle and execution phases so future failures name pid, phase, requested route, selected route, and command.
- Ensure the fix does not implement a DDx model catalog or provider fallback policy; DDx should pass constraints and enforce invariants, while Fizeau owns concrete route resolution.

NON-SCOPE
Do not remove support for Gemini, Claude, or other harnesses. Do not kill unrelated interactive provider sessions. Do not make DDx choose replacement models. Request-timeout process cleanup is covered by sibling bead ddx-aef128f7; this bead is specifically about preventing non-pinned provider children from launching in the first place.

INTERSECTIONS
- ddx-aef128f7: same dogfood run also proved request-timeout/process-tree cleanup failure; this bead supplies the provider-escape invariant that cleanup alone cannot solve.
- ddx-34d96048 and ddx-3d80038f: prior fixes covered pinned route preflight and decomposition routing, but this dogfood run shows another provider escape remains in execution/lifecycle subprocess ownership.
title: work: prevent pinned workers from launching unrequested provider children

description:
PROBLEM
Long-running DDx entrypoints can start work even when the project-local skill install is broken. In /Users/erik/Projects/fizeau, post-attempt triage logged `triage hook: skill missing: bead-lifecycle (continuing)` only after an execution failed. The operator had to infer that the project still had a pre-migration skill layout and needed `ddx update --force` / `ddx doctor`.

ROOT CAUSE
`cli/cmd/work.go:106` delegates directly to `runAgentExecuteLoopImpl` without a lightweight runtime preflight. `cli/cmd/try.go:102-120` resolves execution flags and proceeds toward store/runtime setup without checking project-local skill prerequisites. `cli/cmd/server.go:98-146` starts the server without surfacing degraded project-local skill layout. `cli/cmd/doctor.go:281-287` already detects legacy skill symlinks and prints `run: ddx update --force`, but that diagnostic is only available when the operator explicitly runs `ddx doctor`.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add a shared lightweight project-runtime preflight helper for long-running entrypoints. It should reuse existing doctor/install helper logic where practical, but must not run the full `ddx doctor` checks.
- Wire the helper into `ddx work`, `ddx try`, compatibility `ddx agent work`, and `ddx server` before execution begins.
- For work/try/work: fail on missing required project/tracker state, warn once per process for optional lifecycle-hook degradation in WARN-ONLY mode, and include remediation.
- For server: fail on required server project state, but log degraded startup diagnostics for missing lifecycle skills or legacy skill symlink layout.
- Checked paths for `bead-lifecycle` must be `.agents/skills/ddx/bead-lifecycle/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/ddx/bead-lifecycle/SKILL.md` under the resolved project root.
- Remediation text must include `ddx update --force` first, then `ddx doctor`.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not add network, package-manager, route/provider, stale-doc, or Fizeau health probes to this preflight.
- Do not change bead-lifecycle hook classification semantics.
- Do not make `ddx server` refuse to start solely because `bead-lifecycle` is missing.
- Do not edit `.ddx/beads.jsonl` manually; tracker mutation is handled by this bead record only.

PARENT + DEPS

description:
PROBLEM
Queue-control startup and pre-claim cleanup can remove stale worker sidecar directories, but it does not run the conservative stale attempt-descendant process pass before claiming more work. A worker can therefore continue draining while orphaned DDx-owned processes from older attempts still burn CPU or hold ports.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/cmd/startup_housekeeping.go:218-267` removes stale `.ddx/workers/agent-loop-*` sidecar dirs, but it does not terminate or report the underlying stale DDx-owned process tree when a stale sidecar corresponds to an orphaned attempt descendant.
- `cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:230-527` owns cleanup of stale DDx execution artifacts, but work startup/pre-claim cleanup does not invoke the same conservative process pass before queue claim.
- `cli/internal/agent/orphan_harness_reaper.go:42-152` handles startup reaping for orphaned top-level harnesses only and does not cover shell, cargo, benchmark, or test-server descendants left under stale execution worktrees.

PROPOSED FIX
Wire the same conservative stale attempt process cleanup pass into work startup/pre-claim cleanup before the next bead is claimed. Preserve existing cleanup lock and jitter behavior so multiple workers do not race to kill the same process group. Emit a structured cleanup observation whenever startup/pre-claim cleanup reaps, preserves, or cannot safely reap a stale process group. The startup path must use the same ownership and liveness rules as `ddx cleanup --apply`: current-project execution root, stale or missing run-state liveness, dead owner PID, no live worker sidecar, and no active registered worktree.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- `cli/cmd/startup_housekeeping.go` and existing work-startup cleanup tests.
- `cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go` only as needed to reuse the process cleanup pass.
- `cli/internal/workerstatus/*` or `cli/internal/agent/orphan_harness_reaper*` only for reused process-scanning helpers, not broad rewrites.
- `docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-010-task-execution.md` and `docs/helix/02-design/solution-designs/SD-025-task-execution-lifecycle.md` only if this child changes the documented cleanup contract.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not edit Niflheim.
- Do not duplicate `ddx-e0de6369`; that bead owns `.ddx/harness-sessions/` scratch ignore/prune behavior.
- Do not duplicate `ddx-bbea954f`; that bead owns dirty timeout worktree edit preservation before cleanup deletion.
- Do not replace the existing parent-death/process-group fixes from `ddx-0d7d5f0e`, `ddx-3113d524`, or `ddx-418c3849`.
- Do not implement a general-purpose port scanner or host process manager. Port conflict recovery here comes only from safely reaping stale DDx-owned attempt process groups.
- Do not kill processes outside the current project's DDx execution root, processes tied to live run-state/worker liveness, active registered worktrees, or non-DDx user workloads.

GOVERNING ARTIFACTS
- `spec:FEAT-010`
- `spec:SD-025`

description:
PROBLEM

Dogfood on 2026-06-14 reproduced a false ddx sync failure immediately after successfully pushing HEAD to origin/main. The worktree was on dogfood/provider-failure-20260613 with HEAD and origin/main both at c0b72bd30028e8daa8f9775adc6d57f540f12ac7, but `ddx sync` fetched, merged origin/main, then failed twice with non-fast-forward. This makes the required sync-after-land step unreliable whenever the operator works from a non-main branch that tracks origin/main.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE

- cli/cmd/sync.go:198-200 documents and executes `git push origin main`. In git, that pushes the local branch named `main`, not the current HEAD. When the current branch is a dogfood/work branch and local `main` is stale, sync pushes stale local main and gets a legitimate remote rejection even though the checked-out branch is already aligned with origin/main.
- cli/cmd/sync.go:201-210 treats any rejected/non-fast-forward output as retryable, then as terminal after the second identical stale-branch push, without comparing current HEAD to origin/main after fetch.
- cli/cmd/sync_test.go:188-221 covers double push failure, but does not cover the non-main-branch success case where current HEAD equals origin/main and local main is stale.

PROPOSED FIX

Change sync push semantics to publish the checked-out commit to origin/main explicitly, e.g. `git push origin HEAD:main`, or otherwise resolve the current HEAD ref and push that SHA/ref to main. Before retrying or aborting on non-fast-forward, fetch and compare `rev-parse HEAD` with `rev-parse origin/main`; if already equal, treat sync as success and clear any failure marker. Add regression coverage using fake git responses for stale local main plus aligned HEAD/origin/main.

NON-SCOPE

Do not introduce force-push, rebase, squash, or no-verify behavior. Do not change execute-bead merge policy. Do not make sync manage arbitrary non-DDx dirty files.
title: sync: push current HEAD to origin/main from non-main branches

description:
PROBLEM
Eight Linux process-reaping tests pass on a bare host but fail when the suite runs inside a ddx-managed bead attempt (ddx try / ddx work), where the executing coding-agent harness is an ancestor process. This makes the mandatory 'cd cli && go test ./...' gate red for any bead executed by the queue worker, while the same suite is green for a human operator. Observed on 2026-07-22 at source HEAD 425d5b7caa: two consecutive attempts (beads ddx-69672921, ddx-3452fd6d) returned no_changes/tests_red with rationale 'the provider process exits as a zombie and remains visible to kill -0 within the 5s assertion window', while the identical command 'go test ./internal/agent/... ./cmd/... -count=1' exited 0 on the host.

ROOT CAUSE
The tests assert 'process is gone' by polling syscall.Kill(pid, 0) until ESRCH, e.g. cli/cmd/work_provider_orphan_linux_test.go:165-173 (TestWork_WatchKillingWorkerReapsProviderChildWithin5s). kill -0 succeeds on a dead-but-unreaped zombie. When the parent of the stub provider is SIGKILLed, the orphan reparents to the nearest ancestor child-subreaper. On a bare host that is PID 1, which reaps immediately, so ESRCH arrives within the window. Inside a coding-agent attempt, the harness CLI (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) sets PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER for its sandbox and never wait()s foreign grandchildren, so the zombie persists, kill -0 keeps succeeding, and the assertion times out. DDx source sets no subreaper itself (verified: no prctl/SUBREAPER references outside tests).

Affected assertions (all use bare kill-0/ESRCH liveness polls):
- cli/cmd/work_provider_orphan_linux_test.go:94 TestWork_WatchKillingWorkerReapsProviderChildWithin5s (poll at :165-173)
- cli/cmd/work_provider_orphan_linux_test.go:275 TestProviderLaunchTimeoutReapsProviderOnly (poll at :265, :335-336)
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_no_changes_verify_test.go:92 TestDefaultVerificationCommandRunnerTimeoutKillsProcessGroup
- cli/internal/agent/executor_linux_test.go:74 TestOSExecutorExecuteInDir_LinuxPdeathsigKillsHarnessOnParentSIGKILL
- cli/internal/agent/executor_linux_test.go:157 TestOSExecutorExecuteInDir_GracefulCancellationStillKillsProcessGroup
- cli/internal/agent/orphan_harness_reaper_realproc_linux_test.go:143 TestWorkStartupReaper_KillsOrphanGrandchildProcessGroup
- cli/internal/agent/provider_children_test.go:345 TestRunningProviderGuardReapsProviderGrandchildrenByProcessGroup
- cli/internal/agent/provider_children_test.go:407 TestWork_NonRouteProviderPidNotProcessGroupLeaderIsReaped

PROPOSED FIX
What these tests actually prove is that the target process was KILLED (pdeathsig fired, process-group kill delivered). Reaping the zombie entry is the job of whatever ancestor inherits it, not DDx. So the liveness predicate should treat a zombie as dead:
1. Add a shared Linux test helper, one per package (cli/cmd and cli/internal/agent), e.g. func processDeadOrZombie(pid int) bool: return true when syscall.Kill(pid, 0) returns ESRCH, OR /proc/<pid>/stat field 3 is 'Z'. Parse /proc/<pid>/stat by locating the closing paren of the comm field before splitting, since comm may contain spaces.
2. Replace the bare kill-0/ESRCH polls in the eight tests above with the helper. Failure messages should include the observed /proc state.
3. Unit-test the helper against a real zombie: fork a short-lived child, do not wait it, confirm kill(pid,0)==nil while helper returns true; then reap and confirm helper still returns true via ESRCH.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change production reaper/executor code (cli/internal/agent executor, provider guard, startup reaper). Do not make the tests set PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER themselves. Do not touch non-Linux test variants. No deps; no parent.
title: tests: treat unreaped zombies as dead in process-reaping liveness assertions

description:
Build the integration test suite for work orchestration using the script harness + real git temp repos. This is the test gap the opus test-plan review identified as the most critical coverage hole: every "concurrency" or "merge race" test today uses in-memory fakes with per-worker orchestrators, so the shared-writer invariant the meta-bead design depends on is never actually exercised.

## Test infrastructure helper

Build a shared helper `newScriptHarnessRepo(t *testing.T) (projectRoot, initialRev string)` in a new file `cli/internal/agent/integration_helper_test.go` that:

1. Creates a temp dir via t.TempDir()
2. Runs `git init` with scrubbed GIT_* env (so the test's own pre-commit hook env doesn't leak)
3. Creates and commits an initial seed commit on `main`
4. Seeds .ddx/beads.jsonl with N ready beads (parameterized by test)
5. Returns projectRoot + the initial SHA

The helper must NOT inherit any GIT_DIR from the parent test environment.

## Test cases

Create cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_integration_test.go with these cases. Each runs against the script harness and real git:

1. **TestIntegration_ScriptHarness_SingleBead_AppendLine_Merged** — one bead, directive appends a line and commits, asserts git log main shows +1 commit, worktree is cleaned up, bead closed with closing_commit_sha.

2. **TestIntegration_ScriptHarness_NoOp_ClassifiedAsNoChanges** — directive no-op, asserts outcome=no-changes, bead stays open (below adjudication threshold), no commit on main.

3. **TestIntegration_ScriptHarness_DirtyWorktreeSynthesized** — directive creates files but omits explicit commit, asserts SynthesizeCommit fires, outcome=merged, single synthetic commit on main with the expected files.

4. **TestIntegration_ScriptHarness_FailedExit_WithCommits_Preserved** — directive commits then set-exit 1, asserts outcome=preserved, refs/ddx/iterations/<bead>/<ts>-<sha> exists, main unchanged.

5. **TestIntegration_ScriptHarness_FiveConcurrentBeads_LinearHistory** — seed 5 distinct beads, spawn 5 workers concurrently (single store, single projectRoot), assert `git log --merges main | wc -l` is 0, `git rev-list main ^initial | wc -l` is 5, every bead closed. **This is the ddx-6aa50e57 acceptance test that cannot be written today.**

6. **TestIntegration_ScriptHarness_TwoWorkersSameBead_ClaimedOnce** — seed 1 bead, spawn 2 workers against the same store, assert exactly one executes and the other reports no_ready_work. **This is the ddx-3315dce2 acceptance test.**

7. **TestIntegration_ScriptHarness_RebaseConflict_Preserved** — two beads both modify the same line in the same file, workers start from the same base, first lands cleanly, second gets rebase conflict and is preserved under refs/ddx/iterations/. Main has exactly +1 commit, ref exists for bead 2. (Only passes once the land coordinator from ddx-8746d8a6 is in place.)

8. **TestIntegration_ScriptHarness_ContextCancelBetweenIterations** — two beads, cancel context after first completes, assert second bead is not claimed. **This is the regression for commit 21d16e6.**

9. **TestIntegration_ScriptHarness_NoChangesRationale_ClosesBeadFast** — directive writes a no_changes_rationale.txt citing a commit SHA, asserts the bead closes as already_satisfied without the 3-strike cooldown wait.

Each test runs in isolation, cleans up its temp dir, and completes in under 10s. The full suite runs in under 60s. Use `-race` to catch any coordinator goroutine races.

## Out of scope

- Server-layer wiring (that's bead C)
- Real-AI acceptance tests (gated tier 4)
- Multi-project isolation (a separate bead, not filed here)
- Cross-machine scenarios (multi-machine topology bead)
title: Integration tests for work orchestration using script harness + real git

description:
PROBLEM
The unattended `ddx work` drain halts with "worker exited: operator attention required" when a tracked skill SYMLINK is materialized into a real directory by an external skill-install/sync, leaving the project worktree dirty with a non-tracker path. Observed 2026-05-27 06:26: a continuous ddx worker closed 3 beads, then on the next pre-claim found `.crush/skills/nano-banana-pro-openrouter` dirty — git tracks it as a symlink (mode 120000) but the working tree had it as a directory (SKILL.md/assets/scripts) — and exited via the uncommitted-implementation-changes guard rather than continue. Operator had to restore the symlink (rm + git checkout) and restart the worker. This breaks the unattended-drain goal: a stray tool-managed skill dir stops the whole queue.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2480 emits "operator attention: project worktree %s has uncommitted implementation changes; released %s" and exits the drain when the landing worktree has any non-allowlisted dirty path (message built at execute_bead_loop.go:955-957).
- cli/internal/agent/work/guard.go:38-48 trackerMetadataPaths only allowlists DDx-managed files (.ddx/beads.jsonl, .ddx/metrics/attempts.jsonl, …) — added by ddx-df77e668. Tool-managed skill symlinks under .crush/skills/ (and likely .claude/skills, .agents/skills) are NOT covered, so their symlink->dir materialization reads as implementation dirt and halts the drain.

PROPOSED FIX (pick one; implementer/operator decides)
A. Pre-claim: treat a tracked symlink that has been materialized into a directory whose content matches the symlink target as benign (optionally auto-restore the symlink) instead of implementation dirt.
B. Pre-claim: allowlist tool-managed skill-dir roots (.crush/skills, .claude/skills, .agents/skills) in the cleanliness check, analogous to trackerMetadataPaths.
C. Repo hygiene: gitignore + untrack these tool-materialized skill paths so they never read as dirty (note: they are currently committed as symlinks, so this is a deliberate structural change).
Recommend A (most precise; only neutralizes the spurious symlink->dir case, preserves the guard for genuine edits).

NON-SCOPE
- Do not weaken the guard for genuine uncommitted source/test/doc edits.
- Do not change what materializes the symlink (external skill tooling) — make ddx resilient to it.

CROSS-REF: extends the tracker-file allowlist from ddx-df77e668; same unattended-drain-resilience theme.

description:
## Observed

The graph view at `/nodes/.../projects/.../graph` renders a long flat list of amber-styled warnings, currently dominated by `duplicate document id "AC-AGENT-001" in "/Users/erik/Projects/ddx/.claude/worktrees/agent-a2818c5c/docs/resources/agent-harness-ac.md"` and similar entries. Two distinct concerns:

1. **Input noise** — most duplicates today come from `.claude/worktrees/<agent>/...` copies of the repo being indexed (tracked in `ddx-12cae4dd`). That fix will eliminate a large class of false positives but will not make the warning surface usable.
2. **Brittle degradation** — when documents have real problems (duplicate IDs in the canonical tree, broken frontmatter, missing `depends_on` targets, `id_to_path` mismatches), the system doesn't just warn — downstream consumers (documents list, staleness, UI routing) misbehave. And there is no workflow for a user to triage, diff, or fix the offending files.

## Current state of warnings

- `cli/internal/server/frontend/src/routes/nodes/[nodeId]/projects/[projectId]/graph/+page.svelte:22-30` dumps `graph.warnings: string[]` into a flat amber block. No grouping, no categorization, no links to the offending file, no way to dismiss or act.
- Warning strings are generated in `cli/internal/docgraph/docgraph.go` (duplicate id, parse failure, required-root-missing, id_to_path mismatch/missing, cascade unknowns) as unstructured `fmt.Sprintf` output.
- No stale-document-pruning: if a `.md` is deleted on disk, any id_to_path entry pointing at it yields a warning instead of being auto-cleaned.

## Scope of this bead (deliberately not overlapping ddx-12cae4dd)

Assume `.claude/worktrees` noise is gone. This bead delivers the **integrity surface** that remains valuable: a way to see, categorize, and act on real document problems.

### Deliverables

1. **Structured warnings** — extend `docgraph.Graph.Warnings` from `[]string` to `[]GraphIssue{kind, path, id, message, relatedPath?}` and plumb through GraphQL. Keep a `messageLines(): []string` shim for any caller still using the old shape during the grace period.
2. **Integrity panel on /graph** — replace the flat amber block with a collapsible panel grouped by issue kind (Duplicate ID, Missing dep target, Broken id_to_path, Parse error, Required root missing). Each group shows count + expandable list; each row shows file path (clickable → document viewer), the offending ID, and a copyable message.
3. **Summary badge** — small badge next to the page title showing total issue count, so a clean graph reads clean.
4. **Audit GraphQL query** — `query { docGraphIssues { kind, path, id, message, relatedPath } }` usable independently of the full graph for future dashboard use. Reuses the same structured slice.
5. **Repair affordances (minimum viable)** — for two common cases:
   - Duplicate ID: show both file paths side-by-side and a "copy suggested unique ID" button (deterministic suggestion, e.g., append a short hash of the path). No auto-write.
   - Missing dep target: show the document declaring the missing dep, and a copy-to-clipboard snippet of the frontmatter line to remove. No auto-write.
   Auto-repair is explicitly out of scope until we trust the detection.
6. **CLI parity** — `ddx doctor` (or `ddx docs audit`) prints the same structured issues in a terminal-friendly form, so headless users and CI can surface problems.

### Out of scope

- Fixing `.claude/worktrees` indexing (owned by `ddx-12cae4dd`).
- Auto-rewrite of source files.
- Cross-project graph integrity (today's graph is per-project).
notes:
**AC 7 — command path**: The command is registered as `ddx doc audit` (`cli/cmd/doc.go:59`), but the acceptance criteria specifies `ddx docs audit` (or `ddx doctor docs`). If `doc` is the existing noun, this is arguably fine, but the AC should be reconciled. The `Aliases: []string{"integrity"}` alias doesn't cover the spec'd names.
**AC 7 — `--json` exit code**: `cli/cmd/doc.go:79-83` — when `--json` is set, the command encodes issues and returns `nil` unconditionally. The AC requires exit 1 when issues are present regardless of output format, so CI pipelines using `ddx doc audit --json` would incorrectly report success on a broken graph. The test `TestDocAuditCommand_JSONOutput` even documents this as intentional ("--json always succeeds (exit 0) so piping into jq works"), which contradicts the AC. Either the AC should be amended or the `--json` path should also return `ExitError` when issues exist (with a `--exit-zero` escape hatch for pipe-friendly use).

`cli/internal/server/frontend/e2e/graph.spec.ts:177` — AC 8 asks for a Playwright e2e on a fixture repo with one seeded duplicate-id pair and one missing-dep target. The test directly injects `duplicate_id` and `missing_dep` objects through a mocked `/graphql` response, so it does not exercise docgraph detection, GraphQL resolver plumbing, or project fixture routing end-to-end.

PROBLEM

description:
PROBLEM
The workerprobe mirrors loop events via `TeeJSONL`, so during a long-running attempt with no intermediate loop event, the server's `last_event_at` stays at claim time. The server cannot distinguish an actively-working worker from a silent/stale one. The new periodic liveness mechanism must also fail open: when no server address is configured or the server refuses connections, work must continue without errors, status churn, new failure states, or cooldowns.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/work/heartbeat.go:13-35` ticks but emits no event to the probe.
- `cli/internal/agent/workerprobe/probe.go:209-228` `RecordEvent` already best-effort posts to `/api/workers/<id>/event` when connected and buffers when not — but nobody calls it for heartbeat-cadence events.
- `cli/internal/server/worker_ingest.go:110-120` updates `last_event_at` only when `/api/workers/<id>/event` receives an event.
- `cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:174-186` connects the probe but only `TeeJSONL`-mirrored loop events flow through it.

PROPOSED FIX
Wire a probe-aware liveness emitter into the `WithHeartbeat` tick: on each tick, when a `*workerprobe.Probe` (or a minimal `RecordEvent`-shaped interface) is available, call `probe.RecordEvent(Event{Kind: "worker.heartbeat", BeadID: ..., AttemptID: ..., Body: <small JSON>})`. The body should be a compact envelope (worker_id, current_bead, attempt_id, phase, ts) — enough to refresh `last_event_at` server-side and provide minimal context. `RecordEvent` is already non-blocking and best-effort. When no addr / connection refused / no probe, the call must be silent (a single debug-level log line is acceptable) and must not propagate errors to the attempt path.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change the probe's connection lifecycle, register/backfill behavior, or backoff/jitter constants.
- Do not add a new server endpoint; reuse the existing `/api/workers/<id>/event` path.
- Do not write the local sidecar (covered by sibling bead ddx-1be8df2b).

Parent: ddx-a3589116. Dependencies: none (independent of ddx-1be8df2b — the two together complete the parent).
title: worker: workerprobe emits periodic worker.heartbeat events with fail-open when no server

description:
PROBLEM (Principle 2 of epic ddx-602ae31a)

`ddx update` targets the project path unconditionally with no `--global` surface, `ddx doctor` does not report the global vs project install layers, and the install-topology decision is undocumented.

ROOT CAUSE

PROPOSED FIX
1. Add `--global` to `ddx update`. When set, update only the global plugin tree under ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/plugins/<name>; do not touch the project tree.

Land the spec/docs updates: file-or-update the skill-install-topology ADR (ADR-025 or the equivalent skill-topology record), document install locations in library/skills/ddx/SKILL.md "How this skill works", document agent-tier paths in library/skills/ddx/reference/agents.md if that file exists, and document the install precedence in the CLAUDE.md "Persona System" section.

8. ddx work --model qwen3.6 --provider vidar prefers vidar if it has a match; ignores vidar and routes to bragi if vidar lacks it.

13. Profile routing (--profile cheap) does NOT auto-select uncataloged discovered models.

T5. Provider affinity is soft: preferred provider ignored when it lacks the model.

T8. Provider alone selects best cataloged model from that provider.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx records work-failed-routes on every provider_connectivity failure but never passes the list to Fizeau on the next attempt. Fizeau therefore re-selects the same (provider, model) and the bead loops on the same dead route until the operator intervenes. ROOT CAUSE
cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go around the RouteRequest construction does not populate any caller-side exclusion field. The bead's work-failed-routes Extra is read only by recentProviderConnectivityMinPower (cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:409) to nudge MinPower, never to express "do not pick this (provider, model)". description:
## Observed On the bead detail panel, a long bead id overflows and visually overlaps the Claim/Unclaim/Edit/Delete/Close buttons on the right. Reporter example: `.execute-bead-wt-ddx-0a651925-20260418T043148-1346e8a3-526efaf1` (~60 chars). ## Root cause `cli/internal/server/frontend/src/lib/components/BeadDetail.svelte:211-221` — ```svelte
{bead.id} ← shrink-0 prevents truncation {bead.status} {#if bead.owner} @ {bead.owner} {/if}
[Claim/Unclaim] [Edit] [Delete] [Close]
``` The bead-id span has `shrink-0`, so it never truncates regardless of length. The outer panel is `max-w-xl` (576px). A 60-char monospace id occupies roughly 400-500px on its own; combined with the status pill, owner chip, and the action-button group (also `shrink-0`), it pushes past the available width. Flex layout collapses by overlapping rather than wrapping, so the id draws on top of the buttons. ## Proposed direction 1. **Replace `shrink-0` on the bead-id span with `truncate min-w-0`.** The parent `
` already establishes a shrinkable container. 2. **Add `title={bead.id}` so hovering shows the full value** (important — truncating monospace ids from the right loses the distinguishing suffix). 3. **Add a copy-to-clipboard icon button** next to the id so operators can grab the full value with one click when the id is truncated. Small icon button, no extra visual weight. 4. **Sanity check:** the reporter's example starts with `.` and has the shape of an execute-bead worktree name. Worth briefly checking whether something is producing such a value as a bead id (worktree name leaking into bead creation?) — but that's a separate investigation. The UI still needs to degrade gracefully regardless. ## Out of scope - Changing bead id generation or enforcing max length on ids. - Redesign of the detail-panel header layout.

description:
## Problem

Projects that include .ddx/executions/ in their .gitignore (including fizeau and any repo using the standard DDx .gitignore template) silently fail to land any bead. The failure is invisible: implementation is correct, tests pass, but agent.Land() preserves instead of landing on every attempt.

## Root Cause

cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:717 — RealLandingGitOps.StageDir:

  args := append([]string{"add", "--", relPath}, EvidenceLandExcludePathspecs()...)
  out, err := internalgit.Command(context.Background(), dir, args...).CombinedOutput()

git add without --force silently skips gitignored paths (exit 0, no output, no error). When .ddx/executions/ is gitignored, StageDir stages nothing. CommitStaged sees an empty index and returns sha="". landEvidence calls evidenceDirHasTrackedFiles which also returns false (gitignored files not tracked), so it returns error "no staged evidence files under .ddx/executions/...". preserveAfterEvidenceFailure fires, rolls back master, and creates a preserve ref.

Compounding issue: ApplyLandResultToExecuteBeadResult maps ALL non-pre-merge-check preserve reasons (including "evidence commit failed") to reasonForStatus="merge conflict", which ClassifyExecuteBeadStatus returns as "land_conflict" (escalatable). This causes runEscalatingSingleTierAttempts to burn the entire model escalation ladder (min_power 5→7→8→9) before exhausting.

Confirmed in fizeau on multiple beads — every attempt preserved by evidence commit failure. Originally filed as easel/fizeau bead fizeau-af9d5f1c; refiled here because the source files live in the DDx CLI repo, not in fizeau.

## Proposed Fix

Part 1 (fix): In cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:717, change `args := append([]string{"add", "--", relPath}, ...)` to `args := append([]string{"add", "--force", "--", relPath}, ...)`. Evidence files are DDx infrastructure, not user source. They must be committed even when the project's .gitignore covers .ddx/executions/.

Part 2 (defensive): In execute_bead_status.go, add "evidence commit failed:" as a non-escalatable prefix in isPreservedNeedsReviewReason so infrastructure failures do not burn the escalation ladder.

## Origin

Refiled from easel/fizeau bead fizeau-af9d5f1c (was filed in the wrong repo — fizeau vendored a copy of DDx CLI source which has since been removed).
title: fix: StageDir must use git add --force so evidence commits succeed in projects that gitignore .ddx/executions/

description:
PROBLEM
During Niflheim ddx work monitoring, attempt 20260518T021035-da282d6e for bead niflheim-bc47ed66 violated the execute-bead contract while still landing as success. The prompt told the implementer to run gates before committing, rerun lefthook after staging when staged files are required, commit exactly once, and stop after the commit.

Observed behavior:
- The agent ran lefthook before staging, so every hook skipped with no matching staged files.
- The agent committed 1551674d, then a later post-commit lefthook/clippy run found compile errors.
- The agent edited after the commit and amended to e7ae0424.
- A later cargo check found more missing shard_id initializers; the agent edited after the second final summary and amended again to 66beb39b.
- After those amendments, lefthook evidence still included a no-staged-files run, not a meaningful staged pre-commit gate.
- DDx accepted the attempt as success and landed it with result.json status=success/outcome=merged.

This makes the execution audit trail less trustworthy: a successful attempt can contain post-commit mutation, multiple amended implementation commits, and gate output that did not actually test the staged commit set.

PROPOSED FIX
- Teach execute-bead result validation to detect when the implementation commit was amended or replaced after the first successful commit event, and either reject the attempt or record a blocking validation error.
- Treat lefthook runs that report no matching staged files/no staged files as non-evidence for pre-commit acceptance when the prompt requires staged-file gates.
- Add a structured post-agent validation step that compares the first implementation commit event, final implementation_rev, dirty state, and evidence commands before marking success.
- Preserve successful retry behavior by allowing the orchestrator to rerun the bead in a fresh attempt instead of letting an in-attempt agent rewrite its own commit history.

EVIDENCE
Niflheim repo attempt: /home/erik/Projects/niflheim/.ddx/executions/20260518T021035-da282d6e
Final DDx result: implementation_rev=66beb39ba598dfe12301dec195f0673e750e1c98, status=success, outcome=merged.
Agent log shows commits 1551674d, e7ae0424, and 66beb39b in the same attempt.
title: execute-bead: reject post-commit mutation and empty gate evidence

description:
## Observed / Motivation `.ddx/executions/-/{manifest.json, prompt.md, result.json}` bundles are already being produced per `ddx agent execute-bead` attempt — 469 of them on the current repo. They contain the canonical record of what an agent was asked to do and what verdict the attempt produced. **Nothing in the web UI surfaces them today.** A user who wants to ask "why did this bead end up in this state?" has to drop to the filesystem. Sessions (`sessions.jsonl` / sharded index per `ddx-2ceb02fa`) carry the harness/cost/token telemetry but not the verdict and not the bead linkage. Agent log streams (`agent-*.jsonl`) carry the tool-call trace but are scattered across hundreds of files. **Executions are the natural join** — they connect a bead, a session, a prompt, a verdict, and a tool-call stream. ## Ground truth Per-execution on disk: ``` .ddx/executions/-/ manifest.json { harness, model, base_rev, result_rev, verdict, bead_id, execution_dir } prompt.md the prompt that was sent result.json { verdict, rationale, ... } ``` Relations: - `manifest.bead_id` → bead - a session id is recorded in bead events (`kind:cost`, `kind:routing`) and in the agent-log stream; both can map back to an execution via correlation metadata - tool calls live in `.ddx/agent-logs/agent-*.jsonl` (and `agent-s-*.jsonl`), keyed by session id ## Scope ### Part 1 — GraphQL surface - `executions(projectId, first, after, beadId?, since?, until?, verdict?, harness?)` — paginated list of execution bundles. - `execution(id)` — one bundle, fully materialized: manifest fields, prompt markdown, result JSON, linked bead (id + title), linked session (id + harness + model + cost + token totals), tool-call stream pointer. - `executionToolCalls(id, first, after)` — paginated tool-call stream for the execution, read lazily from the agent-log file. Matches the event shape used by the workers detail page. Executions source of truth: directory scan of `.ddx/executions/` filtered/paginated at the resolver. Shard discipline: follow the sessions-index monthly shard pattern (`ddx-2ceb02fa`) if listing all executions grows beyond tens of thousands — per standing directive `ddx-9ce6842a`, raise the storage decision with the user before switching substrate. ### Part 2 — Sidebar + routes - Add "Executions" to the project sidebar (`NavShell.svelte`). - Routes: - `/nodes//projects/

/executions` — list view with filters (verdict, harness, bead, date range, free-text over prompt). Table columns: timestamp, bead, harness/model, verdict (pass/block/error), duration, cost. - `/nodes//projects/

/executions/` — detail view with five tabs: **Manifest**, **Prompt** (rendered markdown), **Result** (rationale + raw JSON toggle), **Session** (harness, model, cost, token totals, link to `/sessions/`), **Tool calls** (virtualized lazy-scroll list of tool_use + tool_result pairs with expandable payloads). ### Part 3 — Cross-links (make the graph real) - **Bead detail:** new "Executions" section listing all executions for this bead with verdict + timestamp + link. Already have data: manifest.bead_id. - **Session detail:** new "Execution" link pointing to the execution this session ran for, when the session has a linked execution. - **Commits page:** already shows commits; if a commit was produced by an execution (result_rev == commit sha), surface the execution link. - **Graph/Docs pages:** out of scope for this bead. ### Part 4 — Perf - Fixture: ≥1,000 executions, per standing directive `ddx-9ce6842a`. Tool-call streams seeded for 10% of them. - Targets: list view p95 ≤ 200ms HTTP, detail view without tool calls p95 ≤ 150ms HTTP, tool-call page-1 (first 50) p95 ≤ 300ms HTTP. - If these can't be met with filesystem scan + in-memory filter, raise DB-substrate decision with user per standing directive. ## Out of scope - Writing new execution bundles (that's already happening). - Executions from other projects/nodes (keep per-project for v1). - Tool-call payload redaction / privacy. File a follow-up if relevant. - `.claude/worktrees/` worktree lifecycle tracking — covered by companion bead per user's split request.

description:
PROBLEM
The service-drain watchdog cancels a healthy run when it sees no "meaningful" events for a window, but a long quiet tool call (build, test, or a slow/stalled model turn) emits no events it classifies as meaningful — fabricating a failure on work that is actually progressing. See cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go (the drainWatchdog idle path; re-pin line against HEAD — the meaningful-event classification + idle timer reset).

ROOT CAUSE
The idle timer resets only on events classified as "meaningful" (final, certain progress). Tool-call lifecycle events and token deltas during a long subprocess are not counted, so a genuinely-working attempt trips the idle cancel.

PROPOSED FIX
Count tool-call lifecycle events (tool_call start, tool_result) and token/progress deltas as meaningful activity that resets the idle timer. Bound the cancel only on PROVEN silence — no events of ANY kind for the window — not on "no events we classified as meaningful". Keep ToolCallTimeout as the per-tool hung-subprocess cap (separate concern).

NON-SCOPE: D1 route recording (merged), D1d tool-timeout config seam (separate bead).

ACCEPTANCE
1. New test in agent_runner_service_wedge_test.go: a stream that emits only tool_call/tool_result/progress events (no "final") for longer than the idle window does NOT cancel (idle timer keeps resetting on those events).
2. A stream that emits NOTHING for the window still cancels (true silence).
3. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... green.
4. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
notes: ELEVATED to P0 2026-06-02: D1 (route recording) fixed the false phaseEmpty wedge but exposed this gap — a routed-but-hung attempt (model stalling at 0.0 tok/s, e.g. ddx-06f820f4 hung silent ~1h42m) is caught by NEITHER the phaseEmpty watchdog (route is now non-empty) NOR ToolCallTimeout (not in a tool call). The idle/drain watchdog must catch sustained no-real-progress (repeated 0-token model responses / event silence) and cancel + reroute (ideally failover to a different harness). Critical: a single stuck bead blocked the whole queue for ~2h.
title: agent drain: idle watchdog counts tool-call/token activity as progress (D1b)

description:
PROBLEM
  TD-031 §5 outcome→Extra mapping table is missing rows for
  push_failed and push_conflict. Today's implementation parks
  push_failed at 24h cooldown (cli/internal/agent/try/attempt.go:272-283),
  which violates the §5 invariant: "work-retry-after may be
  set only when retrying the same bead after time passes could
  plausibly succeed without human/spec/dependency changes."

  push_failed is caused by branch protection, auth-token expiry,
  pre-push test failures (which require code fixes), or a data race
  in executor.go (also a code fix). NONE of these are recheckable
  by time elapsed alone. Without the spec row, implementers add
  cooldowns that survive long after their cause is resolved. Today's
  drain idled ~10h because of stale push_failed cooldowns set during
  a data-race incident that was fixed within the hour.

  This is a doc-only bead. It lands the spec row + the invariant
  before the implementation fixes (sister beads handle code).

CURRENT STATE
  - docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-031-bead-state-machine.md
    §5 has rows for review_pass, already_satisfied, review_fixable_gap,
    review_spec_gap, review_too_large, review_error, execution_failed,
    no_changes (multiple variants), parent/epic, external blocker,
    superseded, transient infra/quota/transport, stale no_changes
    metadata.
  - No row for push_failed.
  - No row for push_conflict.
  - The §5 preamble invariant about work-retry-after is
    correctly stated but lacks a concrete enumeration of which
    outcomes may set the field vs which must not.

PROPOSED FIX
  Edit docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-031-bead-state-machine.md
  §5:

  1. Add row for push_failed:
     - Status transition: in_progress → open (claim released).
     - Label changes: optional explanatory label (e.g.,
       blocked-on-branch-protection if applicable).
     - Events: push-failed with stderr detail and base-rev.
     - Extra updates: Extra["last-run"] only; DO NOT set
       work-retry-after. Operator action OR a code fix on
       origin clears the implicit block.

  2. Add row for push_conflict (remote diverged, fast-forward
     rejected by non-FF):
     - Status transition: in_progress → open (claim released).
     - Label changes: (none).
     - Events: push-conflict.
     - Extra updates: may set work-retry-after at 15min
       (recheckable — remote advanced; a brief wait + re-fetch
       resolves naturally).

  3. Strengthen the §5 invariant prose:
     - Add an explicit list of outcomes that MUST NOT set
       work-retry-after: push_failed,
       declined_needs_decomposition, review_spec_gap,
       review_missing_acceptance, review_too_large at depth cap.
     - Note: push_conflict, no_viable_provider, land_conflict,
       transient infra/quota/transport ARE recheckable and may
       use cooldowns.
     - Reinforce: cooldown lifetime should match the recheckable
       window (15min for transient, NOT 24h).

NON-SCOPE
  - Implementation fixes (sister beads).
  - Bulk operator clear command (sister bead).
  - Rev-bound auto-invalidation logic (sister bead).
  - Other sections of TD-031.

INTERSECTIONS

    depends on this row landing first.
  - Sister bead "fix(try): declined_needs_decomposition use

    invariant prose.

description:
Reporter: nexiq+axon 2026-04-18/19/20. Symptom 3 of review-malfunction report. Most damaging of the three report findings because it hides incomplete work.

Observed on axon `axon-c5cc071a` (RBAC field/row/entity spec, ~2000-word AC) 2026-04-19:

```json
{
  "id": "axon-c5cc071a",
  "claimed-at": "2026-04-19T23:20:45Z",
  "claimed-machine": "sindri",
  "claimed-pid": "3479503",
  "work-heartbeat-at": "2026-04-19T23:20:45.364638776Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-04-19T23:25:18.98959532Z",
  "status": "closed",
  "events": []
}
```

4m33s from claim to closed, `events: []`, no execution bundle under `.ddx/executions/` referencing the bead, no git commit referencing the id, no branch, no notes. Reopened 2026-04-20 as `axon-c5cc071a`. Evidence this is worker-side: no other actor claimed the bead, `claimed-pid` matches work PID pattern, `work-heartbeat-at` was set at claim — a manual `ddx bead update` would not leave `events: []` while setting `status: closed`.

Root-cause hypothesis from report: the worker's cleanup path closes the bead on primary-task success even when the reviewer sub-step errors out without returning a parseable verdict (e.g. context-overflow `n_keep: 1,868,459 >= n_ctx: 196,608` seen in reporter's LLM server logs, or any exception in the review state-machine path). A `bead.result` event that never gets emitted still leaves the bead closed if the exit path is not gated on verdict presence.

Closure contract should be: a bead transitions to `status=closed` only when a valid terminal review verdict (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / BLOCK / SKIP) is recorded alongside an execution bundle and at least one bead event. Worker crash, malformed reviewer output, or context-overflow during review must transition the bead back to `in_progress` with a retry marker — never to `closed`.

Prior related bead `ddx-b57be3ab` (closed) addressed BLOCK-with-empty-rationale but treated the rationale-missing case as `review_malfunction` without closing; this report shows a separate path where the closure itself happens despite reviewer failure.
title: exec: bead closes without valid reviewer verdict — silent false-closure hides unfinished work

description:
PROBLEM
  The reviewer is a load-bearing gate: it BLOCKs fake-work and
  APPROVEs real-work. But the reviewer is itself an AI model
  whose performance can drift (prompt regressions, model
  version changes, distribution shifts in bead content).
  Today there is no signal on reviewer accuracy — we cannot
  tell whether the reviewer is BLOCKing real work as
  false-positives or APPROVing fake work as false-negatives.

  Three observed fake-work cases (ddx-1f774edf, ddx-94a368b6,
  ddx-d22293ba/ddx-cccb4763) on 2026-05-10 were reviewer
  false-negatives. We caught them by manual coherency review;
  there's no system signal that would have alerted us.

  Closing this loop requires a feedback signal: when the
  reviewer's verdict diverges from the eventual truth, record
  it.

CURRENT STATE
  - cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go produces verdicts
    APPROVE | BLOCK. No accuracy telemetry.
  - The metrics extraction bead (ddx-054b2449, queued) will
    record review_verdict per attempt, but not whether that
    verdict was correct.
  - No mechanism captures the operator's eventual override
    (e.g., a BLOCKed bead the operator manually closes; an
    APPROVEd bead the operator later reopens for fake-work).

PROPOSED FIX
  Add an "review accuracy event" emitted when the reviewer's
  verdict is contradicted by a later authoritative signal.

  Sources of authoritative signal:

  1. **Operator override**: operator manually transitions a
     reviewer-BLOCKed bead to status=closed (without further
     work). Or operator reopens a reviewer-APPROVEd bead with
     a "fake-work" or "rework" reason.
     - Hook: cli/internal/bead/store.go Close/Reopen paths.
     - Emit: "review-accuracy-override" event on the bead, with
       fields {verdict_was, operator_action, reason}.

  2. **Downstream test/build failure on landed work**: if a
     reviewer-APPROVED bead's land introduces a build break or
     test failure within N days, that's a false-negative.
     - Hook: post-merge CI signal (when available) OR a
       periodic sweep that diffs landed beads against
       eventual main HEAD.
     - Out of scope for v1 — rely on operator-override signal.

  3. **AC-check disagreement**: when ac-check.json says fail
     but the reviewer issued APPROVE, that is a likely
     false-negative. The sister bead ddx-a9ff01a1 (reviewer
     ratifies ac-check) requires the reviewer to OVERRIDE
     ac-check with explicit reason; this bead records those
     overrides for later auditing.
     - Hook: cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go,
       at verdict emission time.
     - Emit: "review-ac-override" event when reviewer's
       per-AC grade contradicts ac-check.json's mechanical
       result.

  Per-attempt fields added to the metrics row (extends
  ddx-054b2449's schema):
    - reviewer_acmismatch_count: int — number of ACs where
      reviewer and ac-check disagree
    - reviewer_override_reasons: list[string] — reasons cited
      in judgment_override
    - reviewer_accuracy_signal: enum {confirmed, override,
      contested, unknown} — set by the operator-override hook
      after the fact

  `ddx work analyze --by reviewer-model` (extends ddx-09ceb430):
  query the metrics file to surface reviewer false-positive /
  false-negative rates by model. Cross-reference signals tell
  us when to iterate on the reviewer prompt or escalate
  reviewer routing.

  Tests:
    - TestReviewAccuracy_OperatorOverride_EmitsEvent
    - TestReviewAccuracy_ACCheckDisagreement_RecordedInMetrics
    - TestAnalyze_ByReviewerModel_SurfacesFPRate

NON-SCOPE
  - Downstream test/build failure as a signal (v1 uses
    operator-override + ac-check disagreement; CI integration
    is a future bead).
  - Auto-tuning reviewer routing based on accuracy (separate
    concern).
  - UI/dashboard for accuracy time series (separate concern).

INTERSECTIONS
  - Depends on ddx-054b2449 (metrics extraction) for the row
    schema.
  - Depends on ddx-09ceb430 (analyze CLI) for the query
    interface.
  - Depends on ddx-a9ff01a1 (reviewer ratifies ac-check) for
    the AC-check disagreement signal.
title: feat(metrics): reviewer accuracy tracking — record false-positive/negative for reviewer-quality drift detection

description:
PROBLEM
HELIX is now available as a marketplace plugin, so the plugin model should feel like an npx dependency: projects record intent, payloads live outside the repo, and local agent surfaces are generated adapter state. Marketplace plugin installs already do this, but the built-in ddx skill remains an exception: ddx init / ddx plugin sync copy the full embedded ddx skill tree into .agents/skills/ddx and .claude/skills/ddx as real files. Those paths are ignored by ddx init today, but the behavior still normalizes generated asset trees in every project instead of a cache-backed adapter surface.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/skills/install.go:20-21 documents skills.Install as copying skills into .agents/skills and .claude/skills as real files and never creating symlinks.
- cli/cmd/builtin_plugin_sync.go:16-26 calls skills.Install over the baked-in default plugin FS, so the built-in ddx adapter is copied from embedded files instead of resolved through the same cache/shim path as registry plugins.
- cli/cmd/plugin_materialization_test.go:71-90 explicitly blesses built-in ddx adapters as real-file directories, not symlinked/cache-backed generated adapters.
- docs/helix/02-design/adr/ADR-027-skill-install-topology.md:27-33 and docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-015-installation-architecture.md:278-285 define the npx-like model and generated shims/links, but they do not spell out whether the built-in ddx adapter should also use an XDG cache materialization layer.

PROPOSED FIX
Materialize the embedded default ddx plugin payload into the XDG plugin cache on demand, then expose .agents/skills/ddx and .claude/skills/ddx as generated adapter shims/links to the cached skills/ddx directory. Keep the baked-in embedded FS as the offline source of truth and fallback when the cache is missing. Preserve the existing guarantee that plain ddx init does not create .ddx/plugins/ddx or require network access.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not make HELIX built into DDx.
- Do not change marketplace plugin install semantics that already write plugins.lock.yaml and XDG cache payloads.
- Do not require project repositories to commit marketplace plugin payload trees or generated skill adapter directories.
- Do not remove local developer overlays; ddx plugin install <name> --local <path> remains a symlink-to-checkout mode.
- Do not reintroduce global/home plugin state.

description:
PROBLEM (epic ddx-602ae31a, Principle 2)

Without `--global`, `ddx install`/`ddx update` must target the active project install location, which differs by mode: in-tree mode (a `<project>/.ddx/` exists) writes under `<project>/.ddx/plugins/<name>/`; convention mode (no `.ddx/`) writes under `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/projects/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/plugins/<name>/`. In both modes the project-scoped agent skill dirs (`<project>/.claude/skills/` and `<project>/.agents/skills/`) must link into whichever plugins/ path the mode resolves to.

ROOT CAUSE
- For global=false, `resolveInstallDirs` (cli/cmd/install.go:184) returns installRoot=`ddxroot.Path(context.Background(), f.WorkingDir)` and skill dirs under `f.WorkingDir/.agents/skills` and `f.WorkingDir/.claude/skills` (install.go:195-197). `ddxroot.Path()` is what selects the in-tree vs convention plugins root, so the install root automatically follows the mode.
- `ddx update` (no flag) must update the project install in whichever mode is active; the non-global path in update.go (dispatched when `opts.Global` is false, update.go:66) operates on the project working dir's resolved root.
- Project installs auto-commit trackable project changes (install.go:174-176) — global installs do not.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Verify `ddx install <name>` (no --global) in in-tree mode installs to `<project>/.ddx/plugins/<name>/` and links under `<project>/.claude/skills/<name>` and `<project>/.agents/skills/<name>`.
2. Verify `ddx install <name>` (no --global) in convention mode installs to `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/projects/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/plugins/<name>/` and the project-tier links point into that XDG plugins/ path.
3. Verify `ddx update` (no flag) updates the project install in whichever mode is active and does not touch the global tree.
4. The ddx-validate pre-commit hook (ddx-777f4a09) must continue to scope skill validation to staged skill files regardless of mode.

NON-SCOPE
- Runtime lookup precedence (sibling child — ResolvePlugin).
- The `--global` install/update surface (sibling child).
- init/doctor wiring (sibling child).
- Removing the existing per-project install entirely (both modes coexist).
- Migrating any ~/.config/ddx/ legacy paths.
- Agent-harness path discovery beyond Claude Code and Codex.

DEPS
- ddx-06cbaa90 (ddx home resolution) — project install root is computed by `ddxroot.Path()`, which encodes the in-tree vs convention decision.
title: install/update: project install honors in-tree vs convention mode + project-tier skill links

description:
PROBLEM
The pre-claim intake contract and its failure-class behavior are undocumented for operators. When a worker silently idles on a full queue (the ddx-f9ddaa68 symptom), an operator has no written guidance on what pre-claim intake is, how warn vs operator-attention vs hard-error outcomes differ, or how to diagnose silent-idle.
