acceptance: A worker claiming a bead updates work-heartbeat-at every HeartbeatInterval while the bead is in_progress. A second worker scanning the queue reclaims a bead whose heartbeat is older than HeartbeatTTL and resets it to open before claiming. A bead with no heartbeat and claimed-at older than ClaimTTL is also reclaimable. Conditional write prevents TOCTOU race between two workers both detecting the same stale bead. A structured log entry is written when a stale bead is reclaimed. Existing in_progress beads written before heartbeat was introduced are reclaimable via the ClaimTTL fallback. Tests: (1) worker goroutine killed mid-execution leaves heartbeat timestamp in the past; second worker reclaims it; (2) two workers simultaneously detect a stale bead; only one successfully reclaims it; (3) active worker heartbeat prevents reclaim by another worker.
description:
When an work worker crashes mid-execution, the bead it was working on is left in status=in_progress indefinitely. The only recovery today is manual: ddx bead unclaim <id>. This blocks the queue from making progress on that bead.

Root cause: cli/internal/bead/store.go Claim() writes claimed-at (RFC3339) and claimed-pid once at claim time and never updates them. There is no heartbeat, no TTL check, and ReadyExecution() in execute_bead_loop.go skips in_progress beads unconditionally.

## Required changes

### 1. Heartbeat writes (cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go)
While a bead is in_progress, the owning worker goroutine must periodically update a heartbeat field in bead.Extra. Recommended field name: work-heartbeat-at (RFC3339). Write interval: every 30s (configurable via HeartbeatInterval on the loop config struct). The heartbeat goroutine runs alongside the agent executor and is cancelled when the bead completes or errors.

### 2. Stale claim detection (cli/internal/bead/store.go or ReadyExecution)
ReadyExecution() currently skips all in_progress beads. Change it to also yield beads where:
  - status == in_progress
  - work-heartbeat-at is set AND is older than HeartbeatTTL (default: 3 * HeartbeatInterval = 90s)
  - OR claimed-at is older than ClaimTTL (default: 10 minutes) AND work-heartbeat-at is absent (supports beads claimed before heartbeat was introduced)

When a stale bead is yielded, the claiming worker should first reset status to open via a conditional write (matching the stale heartbeat timestamp to guard against a TOCTOU race) before claiming it as its own. If the conditional write fails, skip and continue scanning.

### 3. Stale-claim log entry
When a worker reclaims a stale bead, write a structured log entry to the worker log: { event: 'stale-claim-reclaimed', bead_id, previous_claimed_machine, previous_claimed_pid, previous_heartbeat_at, stale_for_seconds }.

### 4. Config surface
Expose HeartbeatInterval and ClaimTTL on the loop config. For --local workers, read from .ddx/work.toml if present. CLI flags: --heartbeat-interval (default 30s) and --claim-ttl (default 10m).

## Key files
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go — main loop, claim call at line 124, add heartbeat goroutine
- cli/internal/bead/store.go — Claim() at line 439, ReadyExecution() stale check
- cli/internal/bead/types.go — StatusInProgress constant, Extra field conventions
title: Worker heartbeat and stalled-bead TTL reclaim for work

description:
PROBLEM: ddx can derive malformed bead ID prefixes from execute-bead worktree directory names when git root discovery fails. That can produce IDs with invalid leading characters such as '.', contaminating the tracker with IDs that normal Create/GenID validation should reject.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE: cli/internal/bead/store.go:3070 falls back in detectPrefix to filepath.Base(workingDir) or filepath.Base(cwd) when git rev-parse --show-toplevel is unavailable. In an execute-bead worktree, that basename can be '.execute-bead-wt-...', and detectPrefix returns it without validating the prefix against the ValidateID character rules. Raw WriteAll/import/merge paths can then persist malformed IDs.

PROPOSED FIX: Harden detectPrefix so any derived prefix that would fail ValidateID when used in a bead ID, or that contains '.' or '/', is rejected and DefaultPrefix is returned instead. Optionally add a final GenID validation guard before returning generated IDs so invalid prefixes cannot escape even if another derivation path is added later.

NON-SCOPE: The doctor dangling_dep finding and Store.updateBead guard are already landed; do not redo them. Do not change readiness semantics here. Do not address merge-time or import-time dangling dependency filtering in this child bead.

CONTEXT: Cross-machine convergence already relies on doctor --fix bumping updated_at and the supervisor union resolver keeping newest-updated_at records, so pruned records propagate. This child is only about stopping new malformed IDs at the prefix-generation layer.
title: Reject invalid worktree-derived bead prefixes

description:
PROBLEM
The ddx-validate pre-commit hook runs ddx doctor on every commit that touches .ddx.yml, templates/, patterns/, or prompts/. It rejects the commit if ddx doctor exits non-zero. Today this blocked a 1121-file rename commit because ddx doctor was flagging unrelated legacy skill symlinks under .agents/skills/helix and .claude/skills/helix — which were not part of the staged change. The operator had to remove the symlinks (or know about the doctor issue) to unblock an entirely unrelated commit. The hook scope is too coarse: it validates GLOBAL repo health, not the staged change.

ROOT CAUSE
lefthook.yml ddx-validate hook (see scripts/) runs `ddx doctor` with no scoping. ddx doctor checks installation health, plugin layout, git config, skill symlinks, sync status, etc. — all repo-global, none of which are mutated by an arbitrary staged change touching .ddx.yml or templates. A skill-symlink issue (or any other doctor finding unrelated to the staged files) thus blocks unrelated commits.

PROPOSED FIX
- Replace the global `ddx doctor` invocation with a scoped validation that only checks the categories of state actually mutated by the staged change:
  - If .ddx.yml staged → run config-only validation (parse + schema).
  - If templates/, patterns/, prompts/ staged → run resource-only validation (the staged file's syntax/schema).
- Add a ddx doctor --scope=staged or ddx doctor --paths <file>... flag that takes a path list and only runs checks whose subject is in that list. Hook passes the staged path list.
- Keep the full doctor available as an operator command; just don't run it on every commit.
- Document the new scoping model in scripts/ or AGENTS.md.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change what ddx doctor checks at the full-run level; only scope it for hook usage.
- Do not change other lefthook hooks.

DEPS
None.
title: lefthook: scope ddx-validate pre-commit hook to changes that need validation

acceptance:
1. Package cli/internal/ddxroot exists with `Path(ctx, projectRoot) string`.
2. TestDDxRoot_InTreeMode asserts Path returns <projectRoot>/.ddx when that dir exists.
description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-06cbaa90 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 1 of 5 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM (Principle 1 of epic ddx-602ae31a)

Eliminate hardcoded .ddx/ paths so that DDx state anchors correctly regardless of whether the project has a .ddx/ folder. Today every code path joins filepath.Join(projectRoot, ".ddx", ...) directly, so introducing an XDG fallback or any other root strategy means a many-callsite rewrite.

DESIGN

ddxroot.Path(ctx, projectRoot) is the single accessor. It returns:
- <projectRoot>/.ddx — when that directory exists (in-tree mode)
- ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/projects/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/ — otherwise (convention mode)

Project identity in convention mode is parsed from `git remote get-url origin`:
- https://github.com/easel/ddx.git → github.com/easel/ddx
- git@github.com:easel/ddx.git → github.com/easel/ddx
- https://gitlab.example.com/team/repo → gitlab.example.com/team/repo
- Local (no remote) → local/<basename>-<short-hash-of-abs-path>

The XDG project directory IS a git repository — `git init`ed on first bootstrap. All DDx state for that project (beads.jsonl, attachments, archive, plugins, etc.) lives there and is versioned. Operators can `git remote add` it to a server to share state with teammates.

WORKTREE REGISTRY (required, not speculative)

Each XDG project root maintains <xdg>/worktrees.json:

  {"paths": [{"path": "/Users/erik/Projects/ddx", "first_seen_at": "...", "last_seen_at": "...", "hostname": "..."}], "master": "/Users/erik/Projects/ddx"}

- The first worktree to bootstrap an XDG project is auto-marked master.
- Subsequent worktrees register as non-master.
- `ddx project worktree list` shows the registry.
- `ddx project worktree master <path>` re-pins.
- Audit log entries (bead events with result_rev/base_rev) include the master path so downstream tools resolve commit SHAs to a known worktree.

DDX_ROOT NEVER PUNNED — bootstrap is atomic, idempotent, and a no-op when the directory already exists. Two concurrent ddx invocations on the same project must not race-create or race-write worktrees.json. Use file-locking (existing gitlock pattern from ddx-6a518fd9) where needed.

AUDIT — every Go file in cli/ that contains the literal ".ddx" as a path segment must route through ddxroot.Path. Touched packages at minimum:
- cli/cmd/ (every command that reads/writes state)
- cli/internal/agent/ (execute_bead*, work/, escalation/)
- cli/internal/bead/ (store, migrate, lifecycle)
- cli/internal/serv
...[truncated]

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- Package cli/internal/ddxroot exists with `Path(ctx, projectRoot) string`.
- TestDDxRoot_InTreeMode asserts Path returns <projectRoot>/.ddx when that dir exists.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.
title: ddx home: presence-based root resolution + per-project worktree registry: part 1

description:
The ddx-bead skill guides bead creation but underspecifies what makes a bead *execution-ready* for automated execute-bead runs. Observed during axon ADR-018 work driving: beads that technically met the current skill's requirements (title, AC, labels, description pointing at spec-id) still produced bad execute-bead outcomes because the description lacked the context the agent needed to ship correct code in one pass.

## Gaps in the current skill

1. **Description quality is underspecified.** The skill gives AC quality rules but the description field just says 'per SD-004 Section 2' is OK. In practice, agents need:
   - Exact file paths to touch (e.g., 'crates/axon-server/src/auth_pipeline.rs')
   - Cross-bead context when dependencies are listed (e.g., 'A1 landed the credential_revocations table in crates/axon-storage/src/auth_schema.rs — query it via SELECT 1')
   - Inline spec excerpts, NOT just doc-id references. If the spec is ADR-018 §4's failure table, paste the table into the description. Don't say 'see ADR-018 §4'.
   - Files NOT to touch (scope negation)

2. **spec-id and the doc graph are unreliable for execution context.** The current skill implies spec-id linkage is sufficient. It is not — spec-id drives docgraph.BuildGraphWithConfig() which only resolves HELIX-shaped doc references. Generic beads on non-HELIX projects have no equivalent. AND even when resolution works, the agent only gets a file path, not the relevant section. The bead description is the only place that carries content the agent can rely on.

3. **No guidance on cross-bead context.** When bead B depends on bead A, B's description should describe what A landed (file paths, type names, key APIs) — not assume the agent will reopen A's history. Automated execute-bead does not have that context; each bead is read cold.

4. **No guidance on verification commands in AC.** AC items like 'unit tests green' are too vague. Should be 'cargo test -p axon-server green' or 'bun test passes in sdk/typescript'. Named commands.

5. **No guidance on bead size.** A bead should be one unit of testable work, sized so a single agent pass can complete it. Too small is overhead; too large defeats review. Heuristic: if the AC lists more than ~12 checkboxes, consider splitting.

6. **No guidance on incorporating review findings on reopen.** When a bead is reopened after a REQUEST_CHANGES review, the author should either (a) fold the review findings into the description for the next attempt to see, or (b) rely on the tool to thread review events into the prompt (a separate ddx bead — see ddx-a317208c). The skill is silent on this.

7. **No template for description.** A recommended description template (Scope / Files to touch / Cross-bead context / Verification / Quality bar) would make good beads cheaper to author.

## Scope

Update skills/ddx-bead/SKILL.md to add:

- A 'What makes a bead execution-ready' section that codifies the points above
- A 'Description template' with recommended sections: Scope, Files to touch, Files NOT to touch, Cross-bead context, Verification commands, Spec excerpts inline
- A 'Bead sizing' section with the ~12-AC heuristic
- A 'Review-driven reopen' section that tells authors to update the description in place when a bead is reopened after a review rejection
- A 'Common anti-patterns' section enumerating the mistakes observed during the axon work:
  - Listing doc IDs without inlining the relevant text
  - Not naming file paths in the description
  - AC items that are not verifiable by a named command
  - Depending on unmerged work without explaining what it landed

Keep the existing required-fields and label-conventions sections — they are correct.

## Context

Observed during axon ADR-018 work:
- Bead A1 was well-sized but initially had scope creep in its description (audit_retention_policies, which belonged to F1). Agent added the scope-creep table faithfully.
- Bead A2's initial description said 'UserIdentity { provider, subject, user_id }' — a typo carried over from an earlier ADR revision. Agent implemented 'subject' faithfully even though ADR-018 §3 said 'external_id'. The description was the contract the agent followed.
- Bead B1 is being re-authored right now with a richer description (inline ADR-018 §4 failure table, exact file paths, cross-bead context about A1 schema and A2 types) — this is the experiment to validate the authoring changes proposed in this bead.

## Acceptance

- [ ] skills/ddx-bead/SKILL.md gains 'What makes a bead execution-ready' section
- [ ] Description template added with the 6 recommended sections
- [ ] Bead sizing heuristic documented
- [ ] Review-driven reopen guidance added
- [ ] Common anti-patterns enumerated
- [ ] Skill still lints against any existing skill-format CI check
title: skill: improve ddx-bead SKILL.md with authoring discipline for execution-ready beads

description:
PROBLEM
DDx/FIZ is supposed to be the execution surface that absorbs provider availability and configuration differences. During dogfood on 2026-06-13/14, Claude `model=fable` was reachable via the local Claude CLI for a trivial prompt, but DDx did not accept or route it; real review prompts then stalled/timed out outside DDx. Separately, provider/config failures still surface to operators as generic worker/process failures or "check harness configuration" guidance instead of typed provider/model/config failures with fallback when the route is not explicitly pinned. That is a product bug: workers must either fail over within policy or emit a typed, actionable provider/config diagnosis, never an underspecified failure.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/cmd/try.go:163-173 performs pre-execution route validation for explicit harness/model/provider flags before the execute loop has a chance to apply typed provider-failure retry/fallback policy. cli/cmd/agent_execute_loop_provider_process_test.go:13-80 covers model-not-found fallback for an unpinned worker, but it does not cover the operator-facing fable-style case where a caller supplies a new dynamically available model alias/name that DDx/FIZ should pass through or resolve without a hardcoded DDx model list. cli/internal/agent/provider_failure_test.go:74 asserts typed provider disruption reporting, but the current dogfood failures still produce underspecified worker/process guidance in status/attention paths.

PROPOSED FIX
Make provider/model availability a typed DDx/FIZ execution concern end-to-end. For unpinned or policy-routable work, model-not-found, harness-unavailable, provider-config, timeout, and transport failures must record typed evidence and retry an alternate route when available. For explicitly pinned routes, do not widen the pin, but preserve the raw harness/provider/model, classify the failure with a stable reason, and surface concrete remediation in `ddx work status`, execution evidence, and operator-attention output. NON-SCOPE
Do not implement provider-specific Claude business logic in the worker loop. Do not silently ignore explicit `--harness`, `--provider`, or `--model` pins. Do not change the public meaning of power bounds; FIZ remains responsible for concrete route selection.

description:
PROBLEM
A bead that exists at claim time can vanish from the tracker mid-attempt when several attempts run concurrently against one project. The claiming worker then aborts:
  picker skip stale candidate ddxfixture-7c72d707 before attempt: bead no longer exists in the tracker
This is data loss, not a scheduling hiccup: a row that was durably written is gone.

Observed 2026-07-21 while load-testing internal/integration concurrent-try tests under -race.

ROOT CAUSE
The bead store persists the collection by rewriting the whole beads.jsonl file (cli/internal/bead/, see Store write path). Two concurrent writers that each read-modify-write the full file will lose whichever update landed first, because the second writer's in-memory snapshot predates it. The collection lock exists (cli/internal/bead/lock.go) but either is not held across the full read-modify-write window for every mutation path, or a land-time sync/checkout reverts beads.jsonl to an older committed revision after a sibling has already appended.

Both candidate mechanisms must be distinguished before fixing:
  (a) lost update between two whole-file rewrites, or
  (b) a land/sync `git checkout`/reset of beads.jsonl clobbering an uncommitted concurrent append.

PROPOSED FIX
- Determine which mechanism applies by instrumenting the store write path and the land sync path, then fix that one.
- If (a): ensure every mutating store operation performs read-modify-write entirely inside withMainGitLock / the collection lock, and re-reads the file after acquiring the lock rather than reusing a pre-lock snapshot.
- If (b): exclude .ddx/beads.jsonl from land-time worktree restoration, or re-apply concurrent appends after sync (compare with cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go syncWorkTreeToHeadExcludingPaths, which already has a skip-path mechanism).

NON-SCOPE
- Do not convert beads.jsonl to a different storage format.
- Do not address the land compare-and-swap retry gap or the pre-dispatch dirty guard (sister beads).
title: bead: prevent lost updates when concurrent attempts rewrite beads.jsonl

description:
PROBLEM

Cancelling a long-running 'ddx work' with Ctrl-C (SIGINT) prints noisy
error spam after the graceful-shutdown lines. Observed output:

    Cancel received, shutting down gracefully
    project: /home/erik/Projects/niflheim
    worker exited: stopped by signal
    attempts: 0  |  closed: 0  |  changed: 0  |  already-satisfied: 0  |  failures: 0
    Error: context canceled
    Usage:
      ddx work [flags]
      ddx work [command]

    Examples:
      # Drain the current execution-ready queue and exit
      ddx work
      ... (full usage/examples dump)

The "Cancel received..." line and the terminal summary are fine. The
"Error: context canceled" line AND the entire "Usage:"/"Examples:" block
are spam. A clean Ctrl-C of a long-running command should exit quietly
(exit code 130), not print a raw error and the help text.

ROOT CAUSE

There are two compounding defects, both on the 'ddx work' RunE -> Cobra path:

1. The execute loop returns the raw context.Canceled error up to RunE.
   cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:662-666: after worker.Run returns with
   err wrapping context.Canceled, line 662-664 writes the terminal
   summary, then line 665-666 does `if err != nil { return err }`,
   returning context.Canceled to runWork.
   - runWork (cli/cmd/work.go:134-157) returns that error unchanged via
     `return f.runAgentExecuteLoopImpl(cmd, true, "")` at work.go:156.

2. The 'work' command does NOT set SilenceUsage/SilenceErrors, and neither
   does the root command, so Cobra's ExecuteContext prints both the raw
   error and the usage block before the error can be mapped to a clean exit.
   - newWorkCommand (cli/cmd/work.go:22-127) builds the cobra.Command at
     work.go:23-73 with NO SilenceUsage/SilenceErrors field (contrast
     cli/cmd/try.go:46 `SilenceUsage: true` and cli/cmd/run.go:26
     `SilenceUsage: true`, which is why ddx try / ddx run do NOT dump usage).
   - The root command, NewRootCommand (cli/cmd/command_factory.go:136-226,
     command spec at 143-168), also sets neither field.
   - Because SilenceErrors is unset, Cobra prints "Error: context canceled".
     Because SilenceUsage is unset and context.Canceled is a runtime
     (non-arg-parse) error, Cobra also dumps the full Usage/Examples block.

3. The clean-exit mapping happens too late to suppress the spam.
   cli/cmd/root.go:52-56: executeRootCommand returns, and Execute maps a
   context.Canceled error to NewExitError(130, "") so cli/main.go:33-38
   prints nothing and exits 130. But this mapping runs AFTER
   rootCmd.ExecuteContext (cli/cmd/root_signal.go:47) has already printed
   the "Error:" line and the Usage block. So exit code 130 is correct, but
   the spam is already on stderr.

WORKING REFERENCE: ddx try (cli/cmd/try.go:46) and ddx run
(cli/cmd/run.go:26) set SilenceUsage:true on their command structs, so a
runtime error never dumps usage for those commands. ddx work just needs
the same treatment plus suppression of the raw context.Canceled error.

PROPOSED FIX

- cli/cmd/work.go:23-73  add `SilenceUsage: true` (and `SilenceErrors: true`)
  to the cobra.Command literal in newWorkCommand, mirroring try.go:46 /
  run.go:26, so a runtime error from runWork never dumps the usage block.
- cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:662-666  when err wraps context.Canceled
  (operator SIGINT), do NOT return the raw error up to RunE after the
  terminal summary has been written; return nil (or a sentinel that
  main.go maps to exit 130) so Cobra prints no "Error: context canceled"
  line. DeadlineExceeded / other errors must still propagate as today.
  Preserve the existing exit-code-130 behavior: if you return nil here,
  ensure SIGINT still yields exit 130 (e.g. keep the root.go:52-56
  context.Canceled -> NewExitError(130,"") mapping reachable, or return an
  ExitError(130,"") sentinel from this layer). Do not regress the exit code.
- Keep the "Cancel received, shutting down gracefully" line and the
  "worker exited: stopped by signal" terminal summary; only the
  "Error: context canceled" line and the Usage/Examples dump are removed.

NON-SCOPE

- ddx try and ddx run already set SilenceUsage (try.go:46, run.go:26); do
  not touch them beyond what is needed to share a helper if you choose to.
- Do not change the graceful-shutdown announcer (cli/cmd/root_signal.go)
  or the "stopped by signal" summary text (cli/cmd/work.go:260-261).
- Do not alter DeadlineExceeded handling or non-signal error propagation.
title: ddx work: exit cleanly on Ctrl-C without printing 'context canceled' + usage dump

description:
PROBLEM
Live `ddx work` attempts are landing substantial implementation changes inside `chore: checkpoint pre-execute-bead ...` commits instead of the required conventional substantive commit tagged with `[ddx-<id>]`. This weakens the execute-bead audit trail: cost, latency, retry, and review tooling can no longer reliably treat the checkpoint as tracker/caller-dirt bookkeeping and the tagged commit as the bead implementation.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:542-599` defines `checkpointPreDispatchDirt`, which stages `git add -A -- .` through a temporary index and creates a `chore: checkpoint pre-execute-bead <attempt>` commit.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1050-1064` runs `commitTrackerLocked` and then `checkpointPreDispatchDirt` before resolving the base revision and creating the isolated execute-bead worktree.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_concurrent_predispatch_test.go:17-29` and `:124-138` assert the lock-scope and HEAD-race behavior, but not the content contract for checkpoint commits.
- Observed evidence: `df5b591ec chore: checkpoint pre-execute-bead 20260513T175830-e116edd8` contains 305 lines of readiness-timeout implementation across seven code/test files, and `c53f2b0fe chore: checkpoint pre-execute-bead 20260513T183205-80b61705` contains 170 lines of `readiness_checks` implementation across three files. The later tagged commit for `ddx-90b84d73` contained only follow-on CLI/docs plumbing, so the main implementation was attributed to the checkpoint.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a checkpoint content guard so pre-dispatch checkpoint commits cannot silently absorb ordinary implementation files. The guard should either: (a) restrict checkpoints to known durable tracker/evidence/caller-dirt paths and reject code/test paths with an actionable execution failure, or (b) require dirty parent checkout implementation files to be committed under the active bead's `[ddx-<id>]` commit before checkpointing. Preserve the existing serialized lock behavior that prevents concurrent HEAD CAS failures.

NON-SCOPE
Do not remove the pre-dispatch checkpoint mechanism entirely. Do not weaken the existing concurrent worker lock tests. Do not rewrite existing history to repair already-landed checkpoint commits.
title: execute-bead: prevent checkpoints from absorbing implementation changes

description:

Evidence covers ddx's partial `agent.agent_runner` mirror in `.ddx/config.yaml`, the native `ddx-agent` config model in `.agent/config.yaml`, and the need to support existing provider/backends such as OpenRouter without duplicating or losing configuration surface.

description:
PROBLEM
ddx work's idle path (cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1263-1315) reads ReadyExecutionBreakdown into result.NoReadyWorkDetail and then sleeps or exits. There is no per-bead diagnosis of WHY each non-ready bead is non-ready, so the loop cannot fire targeted auto-remediations. FEAT-010 §Idle-Path Diagnosis and Auto-Remediation now requires a closed reason taxonomy with one code per non-ready bead.

ROOT CAUSE
No diagnoser exists. ReadyExecutionBreakdown returns bucket lists (Epics, EpicClosureCandidates, DepWaiting, OperatorAttention) but does not annotate each entry with why-it-is-blocked detail at a granularity the work loop can switch on.

PROPOSED FIX
Add cli/internal/bead/diagnose.go with a pure function Diagnose(b Bead, childIndex map[string][]Bead, openChildIndex map[string][]Bead, depIndex map[string][]Dependency) BlockReason. BlockReason is a typed struct: { Code BlockReasonCode; Detail string; CitedIDs []string }. BlockReasonCode is a typed-string enum with exactly the codes listed in FEAT-010 §Idle-Path Diagnosis and Auto-Remediation (superseded_pending_close, closure_candidate_misclassified, dead_intermediate_all_children_closed, dead_intermediate_open_children_pending, epic_of_epic, dep_blocked_by, genuinely_needs_decomposition, parent_child_state_conflict, claimed_in_progress, provider_route_unavailable, gated_by_budget_or_cooldown, malformed_parent_or_dep_ref, dependency_cycle, closed_or_missing_parent, stale_graph_index, auto_remediation_exhausted, no_diagnosis). The function is pure — no I/O — and takes pre-built indexes so it can be called from both the loop and the CLI.

Detection rules per code are specified in the FEAT-010 table. For superseded_pending_close, read the bead's superseded-by field OR a superseded-by:<Y> label, then verify Y is closed in the index. For closure_candidate_misclassified, check IssueType==epic AND len(openChildIndex[b.ID])==0 AND len(childIndex[b.ID])>0. For genuinely_needs_decomposition, check IssueType==epic AND len(childIndex[b.ID])==0 AND no manual-hold/no-auto-decompose/container label. For dep_blocked_by, cite every open dep's ID and status. Match codes in the order they appear in the FEAT-010 table; first match wins.

NON-SCOPE
- Wiring Diagnose into the work loop (separate bead).
- Inventing new reason codes beyond the FEAT-010 taxonomy.
- Mutations of any kind.

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent: ddx-2a1ece2b. No deps.
title: diagnose: per-bead idle-scan reason classifier

2. TestUpdate_RespectsConventionVsInTreeMode (cli/cmd/update_test.go): `ddx update` (no flag) updates the in-tree `<project>/.ddx/plugins/` when an in-tree root exists, and the convention `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/projects/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/plugins/` dir when it does not, without touching the global tree in either case.

description:
PROBLEM (Principle 2 of epic ddx-602ae31a)
`ddx update` must mirror the install topology: `--global` updates only the machine-wide plugin tree under `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/plugins/`, while the no-flag form updates the active project install in whichever mode (in-tree or convention) is currently in effect, leaving the other tier untouched.

ROOT CAUSE
- cli/cmd/update.go:58 `runUpdate` branches on `--global` (comment at update.go:65) to cli/cmd/update.go:300 `performGlobalUpdate`, otherwise to cli/cmd/update.go:204 `performUpdate(workingDir, opts)` which operates on `ddxroot.Path`-resolved targets and `enumerateSkillUpdateTargets` (update.go:122).
- Without locked-in tests, a `--global` update could touch the project tree (or a project update could touch global), violating tier isolation.

PROPOSED FIX
- Ensure `ddx update --global` writes only under `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/plugins/` and never mutates any project plugins/ dir.
- Ensure `ddx update` (no flag) updates the project install resolved by `ddxroot.Path()` — `<project>/.ddx/plugins/` in in-tree mode, the XDG `projects/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/plugins/` dir in convention mode — and does not mutate the global tree.
- Tests sandbox `XDG_DATA_HOME`/`HOME`, seed both tiers, run the command, and assert mtimes/content changed in exactly one tier.

NON-SCOPE
- Install/init surfaces — sibling beads.
- doctor reporting and spec/docs updates — sibling bead.
- Removing the per-project install (both modes coexist).
- Migrating legacy ~/.config/ddx paths.
- Agent-harness path discovery beyond Claude Code and Codex.

DEPS
- ddx-06cbaa90 (ddx home resolution) for `ddxroot.Path()` / `ddxroot.GlobalDir()`.
- Sibling install beads (global + project install must exist to seed update targets).
title: update: `ddx update --global` updates global tree only; `ddx update` is mode-aware

description:
PROBLEM
While validating the landed `ddx-7eb97e4e` side-worktree reporting fix on 2026-05-15, the broad agent package gate failed once in `TestIntegration_ScriptHarness_FiveConcurrentBeads_AllLanded`. The failure closed only 4 of 5 seeded beads and `git show HEAD:bead-0005.txt` failed with `fatal: path 'bead-0005.txt' does not exist in 'HEAD'`. A direct rerun of the same test immediately passed, so this is either a real concurrent worker race or a nondeterministic integration-test assumption. Either way, this test currently cannot serve as a trustworthy gate for concurrent bead landing safety.

Observed failing command:
`cd cli && go test ./cmd/... ./internal/agent/... -count=1`

Observed focused rerun:
`cd cli && go test ./internal/agent -run TestIntegration_ScriptHarness_FiveConcurrentBeads_AllLanded -count=1 -v` passed in 0.483s.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_integration_test.go:408-423` starts 5 workers concurrently with `Once:false` against one store and shared project root.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_integration_test.go:432-451` asserts all 5 beads are closed and all bead files are reachable from HEAD, but the failure showed one bead missing from both the tracker terminal state and landed git state.
- The current test does not dump per-worker `ExecuteBeadLoopResult`, claimed bead IDs, terminal statuses, or preserved refs on failure, which makes it impossible to distinguish an actual claim/land race from a test harness timing assumption using only CI output.

PROPOSED FIX
Reproduce under stress, then either fix the underlying concurrent claim/land behavior or make the test harness deterministic without weakening the invariant. Add failure diagnostics that print each worker result, bead lifecycle summary, and git refs when the invariant fails. The invariant must remain: five concurrent workers over five ready beads eventually close and land all five distinct beads exactly once.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not skip, delete, or loosen the concurrent landing invariant.
- Do not hide the test behind short mode.
- Do not change production queue ordering or retry policy except where a real race is proven and fixed.

DEPS
None.
title: agent: stabilize concurrent script-harness landing test

acceptance:
**User story:** As an operator, I can see every execute-bead worktree on my project, understand which ones are active vs completed vs abandoned, and clean up abandoned ones with confirmation without shelling out to git commands.

**Acceptance criteria:**

1. **Inventory resolver.** `executeBeadWorktrees(projectId)` returns structured entries as described. Unit test covers: (a) active worktree with live worker, (b) completed worktree with matching execution bundle and head==result_rev, (c) abandoned worktree past the threshold, (d) orphan (path without git registration).

2. **State classification.** `state` is computed deterministically from inputs (workers list, execution bundles, git worktree list, filesystem stat, configured threshold). Classifier is a single pure function with table-driven tests covering all four states and at least two edge cases per state.

3. **UI — list view.** `/worktrees` route renders a table with columns path/branch/bead/execution/state/created/last-activity/disk. Sortable by any column. Filters: state, bead. Default sort: newest `last activity` first.

4. **UI — actions.** Per-row: Remove (confirm-gated), Force-remove (for orphans, extra-confirm-gated with typed confirmation of the path). Both actions call through to git + filesystem via a mutation; neither is performed client-side.

5. **CLI — prune.** `ddx server state worktree-prune [--dry-run] [--project <path>]` lists abandoned+orphan worktrees and prompts for removal (unless `--yes`). Dry-run prints the list without touching anything. Integration test runs against a fixture repo with one of each state and asserts only the expected ones are targeted.

6. **Sweep + notice.** Server background sweep runs at a configurable interval (default 15m), logs a summary, and exposes a GraphQL counter (`executeBeadWorktreeCounters { total, active, abandoned, orphan }`) for dashboard rollup. Sweep never deletes unless `worktrees.auto_prune: true` is set in config.

7. **Cross-links.**
   - From a worktree row, click execution → navigates to `/executions/<id>` (depends on `ddx-726bc5f2`).
   - From an execution detail page, a "Worktree" section shows the worktree (if still present) with the same state badge.

8. **Fixture + perf.** Per standing directive in `ddx-9ce6842a`, seed a fixture with ≥100 worktrees (mix of states). List view p95 ≤ 200ms HTTP. This is small-n territory; should be well within filesystem-scan limits, no DB substrate expected.

9. **Playwright e2e.**
   - Seeds fixture with one worktree of each of the four states.
   - Navigates to `/worktrees`, asserts all four rows with correct state badges.
   - Clicks Remove on an abandoned worktree, confirms, asserts the row disappears within 2s and the worktree is gone from `git worktree list`.
   - Attempts Remove on an active worktree, asserts the confirm dialog warns and the action is gated.

10. **Path convention decision note.** Before Part 4 lands, a one-page note in `docs/helix/02-design/` records the canonical location choice and the migration plan. Parts 1-3 may ship without this note; Part 4 requires it.

11. **Cross-references.** Notes link to: `ddx-12cae4dd` (documents noise), `ddx-71fbe968` (long id overlap — same worktree-name leak into UI), `ddx-726bc5f2` (executions UI — worktrees complement it), `ddx-15f7ee0b` (project registry cleanup pattern reused here).
description:
## Observed `git worktree list` on the current ddx repo shows **39 worktrees**: - 1 main worktree (the clone itself). - ~37 under `.claude/worktrees/agent-/` from execute-bead runs. Branch names `worktree-agent-`. - At least 1 under `/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-ddx---` (detached HEAD) — different path convention, different semantics. There is no UI visibility into any of this. A user cannot see which worktrees exist, what bead each one belongs to, whether each is active/abandoned/completed, or clean them up short of `git worktree prune` + `rm -rf`. The `.claude/worktrees/` entries also leak into other surfaces (already tracked): - Documents view noise (`ddx-12cae4dd`). - One was surviving in the project registry cleanup earlier today (`proj-4c1ca90e: agent-a7bf6d44`). ## Why the two path conventions? - `.claude/worktrees/agent-` — created with a branch (`worktree-agent-`), likely by interactive execute-bead runs or an earlier worktree convention. - `/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-ddx---` — detached HEAD, under `/tmp`, convention that ships with current execute-bead (this is what's producing the long "bead id"-shaped names that leaked into UI in `ddx-71fbe968`). Two conventions is itself a smell: inconsistent path discipline makes cleanup harder and makes cross-referencing an execution bundle → worktree unreliable. ## What's needed ### Part 1 — Inventory resolver - GraphQL: `executeBeadWorktrees(projectId)` → list of `{path, branch, beadId?, executionId?, baseRev, headRev, state, createdAt, lastActivityAt}`. - Source: `git worktree list --porcelain` + filesystem stat + manifest lookup for executions whose `execution_dir` matches or whose path correlates. - `state` ∈ `{active, completed, abandoned, orphan}`: - **active** — an execute-bead session is currently running against this worktree (cross-reference workers / sessions). - **completed** — associated execution bundle exists with a verdict; head matches `result_rev`. - **abandoned** — no recent activity (configurable, default 24h), no matching running worker, but worktree still present. - **orphan** — path on disk but `git worktree list` does not know about it (or vice versa). ### Part 2 — Sidebar + route - New "Worktrees" view, or slot this into the Executions detail (`ddx-726bc5f2`) as a sidebar panel since every worktree is for some execution. Design call; recommend a dedicated view so orphans (which have no execution) are still visible. - Route: `/nodes//projects/

/worktrees`. - Columns: path, branch, bead (link), execution (link), state, created, last activity, disk usage. - Row actions: **Open execution**, **Remove worktree** (confirm-gated; calls `git worktree remove` and cleans up `.claude/worktrees/`), **Force remove** (for orphans; `-f`). ### Part 3 — Policy + cleanup - Background sweep (server-side, already has a sweep pattern from project registry): every N minutes, list worktrees, detect abandoned state, emit a notice (but **never auto-delete** — user-confirmed cleanup only by default). - `ddx server state worktree-prune [--dry-run]` CLI command that enumerates and optionally removes abandoned worktrees. Same deletion path as the UI action. - Config: `.ddx/config.yaml: worktrees.abandoned_after: 24h`, `worktrees.auto_prune: false`. Opt-in auto-prune for teams that want it. ### Part 4 — Path convention unification - Decide a single canonical location for execute-bead worktrees. Recommend `.claude/worktrees/--/` or a sibling `.ddx/worktrees/` — **pick one and stick with it**. - Migrate existing paths lazily: on first sweep after upgrade, record the path as-is and leave it; new worktrees use the new convention. Old ones phase out as they complete or get cleaned. - This is a separable sub-effort; acceptable to land Parts 1-3 against the current mixed reality and do Part 4 afterward. ## Out of scope - Changing how execute-bead creates worktrees (beyond the canonical-location choice in Part 4). - Documents-view noise — covered by `ddx-12cae4dd`. - Long-id display overlap — covered by `ddx-71fbe968`.
title: Track execute-bead worktree lifecycle: 39 worktrees on one repo, no UI visibility, no cleanup policy

description:
PROBLEM
Claude readiness runs can return classification "executable" even when the prompt asks for "ready". During the server-managed DDx canary on worker-20260615T172921-149f for ddx-cf0cafef, the worker logged: readiness schema drift: unknown classification "executable": expected one of ready, needs_refine, needs_split, operator_required, system_unready. The worker continued, but this makes Claude readiness less reliable and can prevent ready beads from claiming cleanly.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/readiness_classification.go:179 normalizeReadinessClassification maps several ready synonyms (ready/actionable_atomic/atomic/ok/actionable/pass) but omits the common Claude wording "executable" / "executable_as_written". cli/internal/agent/readiness_classification_test.go lacks a regression test for that provider wording.

PROPOSED FIX
Normalize "executable" and "executable_as_written" to ReadinessClassificationReady, and add a decoder-level regression test proving the payload maps to PreClaimIntakeActionableAtomic with no system_unready/schema_drift reason.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change blocking behavior for genuinely unknown classifications. Do not change the readiness prompt or provider routing.
title: agent: normalize executable readiness classification

description:
PROBLEM
Genuinely undecomposed epics (IssueType==epic, totalChildCount==0, no closure-pending state) need automated decomposition into child task beads so ddx work can drain them. Today the only decomposition path is operator-invoked (bead-breakdown skill) or post-TooLarge recovery (cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go). FEAT-010 §Idle-Path Diagnosis and Auto-Remediation now requires the work loop to auto-dispatch decomposition for this specific case (RC-6) with strict preconditions to avoid the v1-plan duplicate-child bug.

ROOT CAUSE
No handler exists that bridges the diagnoser's genuinely_needs_decomposition reason code to runPreClaimDecomposer (cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:48). The existing post-TooLarge hook (NewDecomposePostLadderExhaustionHook at recovery_decompose.go:107) gates only on TooLarge failure class, not on idle-scan diagnosis.

PROPOSED FIX
Add cli/internal/agent/auto_decompose_epic.go exporting AutoDecomposeEpic(ctx, store, runner, rcfg, projectRoot, beadID) (DecomposeResult, error). It calls runPreClaimDecomposer (reused unchanged) after asserting every precondition. Preconditions (each must hold; first failing precondition produces a typed error AND increments the per-bead auto_decompose_attempted event count):
- store.Get(beadID).IssueType == "epic"
- totalChildCount(beadID) == 0 (use the same index ReadyExecutionBreakdown uses)
- bead is not currently in the EpicClosureCandidate bucket
- bead has no open dep_blocked_by or closed_or_missing_parent diagnoses (call the new Diagnose function on the bead; if it returns either, return ErrDepsBlockDecompose)
- bead carries no label in {manual-hold, no-auto-decompose, container}
- bead description is non-empty AND contains PROBLEM AND PROPOSED FIX sections AND has at least one acceptance criterion AND has at least one label matching ^(spec|area):
- per-bead event count of auto_decompose_attempted < 3
- bead has no active execution cooldown
- (operator override --no-auto-epic-decompose checked at the caller, not here)

On success: parent epic's execution_eligible is set to false (mirrors recovery_decompose.go behavior), child beads are created via store.Create, the auto_decompose_attempted event is emitted with body {child_ids: [...], cost_usd: N}.

On failure: SetExecutionCooldown(beadID, now+15m, "auto_decompose_failed", reason, baseRev), emit auto_decompose_failed event. On the 3rd cumulative attempt failure also emit auto_remediation_exhausted so the diagnoser surfaces it.

NON-SCOPE
- Wiring this into the work loop (separate bead).
- Changing the runPreClaimDecomposer prompt (reused as-is).
- Surfacing the operator override flag (work-loop bead handles flag plumbing).

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent: ddx-2a1ece2b. Depends on ddx-79e66725 (diagnose function) and ddx-e9f3adaf (RC-1 lifecycle fix — the closure-bucket check needs the correct classifier).

description:
PROBLEM
Unpinned `ddx work --watch` on a medium Story 16 server/GraphQL bead inferred ordinary implementation work, but the implementation route still ran under Fizeau `policy=default` and selected `codex/gpt-5.5`. DDx should introspect Fizeau profiles/policies and choose the best request-level profile for the task. Profile names are configurable Fizeau data, so DDx must not hard-code names such as `cheap`, `standard`, `smart`, or `frontier`; those are shortcuts only when a Fizeau installation chooses to expose them.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/profile_select.go:27-37 defines `ProfileSnapshot` and `LoadProfileSnapshot`, fetching Fizeau `ListPolicies` plus `ListModels`.
- cli/internal/agent/profile_select.go:99-157 already has profile selectors, but they are only used by lifecycle/reviewer dispatch paths and currently prefer fixed named concepts rather than a general implementation selector.
- Fizeau `PolicyInfo` currently exposes `Name`, `MinPower`, `MaxPower`, `AllowLocal`, `Require`, and manifest metadata; `ModelInfo` exposes `Power`, `Cost`, `PerfSignal`, `Billing`, `Available`, `AutoRoutable`, and related route facts.
- cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:138-144 detects zero-config auto-inference, but cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:351-361 loads only models into a MinPower ladder.
- cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:377-391 computes `initialMinPower` and calls `singleTierAttempt(..., spec.Harness, spec.Provider, spec.Model)` without setting `spec.Profile`/Fizeau policy for the inferred task need.
- cli/cmd/try.go:230-250 has the same model-ladder-only path for `ddx try`.
- cli/cmd/try.go:267-293 then sends `Profile: profile` (empty for unpinned zero-config invocations) plus inferred `MinPower`, so Fizeau receives no selected policy/profile and falls back to its default policy.
- cli/cmd/try_test.go:345-385 currently codifies the wrong behavior by asserting inferred work becomes a numeric MinPower rather than selecting a Fizeau profile by metadata.
- docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-037-bead-execution-hints.md now specifies that DDx should infer task need, introspect Fizeau profiles/models, choose the cheapest/fastest viable request profile, reserve strongest profiles for hard work or evidence-backed escalation, and treat profile names as opaque.
- docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-006-agent-service.md now specifies that DDx chooses request-level profile/power intent while Fizeau owns concrete routing.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add a profile selector for implementation dispatch that maps inferred task need to a satisfiable Fizeau policy/profile returned by `ListPolicies`, considering available auto-routable models and preserving DDx's existing precedence rules.
- The selector must be criteria-based, not name-based: infer what the task needs, classify profiles by metadata (power range, availability, cost/billing, speed/perf signal, locality policy, and future diversity data), then choose the cheapest/fastest profile that is likely to get the work done.
- Default execution should start with weaker viable models/profiles and work upward only when evidence justifies escalation. Strongest profiles should be reserved for bead breakdown, debugging, difficult reviews, high-risk or architecture-sensitive work, and retries where lower tiers produced concrete failures.
- In zero-config `ddx try` and `ddx work`, set `Profile`/Fizeau policy to the selected profile name returned by Fizeau when no explicit `--profile`, `--harness`, `--provider`, `--model`, `--min-power`, `--max-power`, or project routing config is present.
- Preserve explicit operator passthrough exactly: if a profile or other routing flag/config is supplied, do not override it with task inference.
- Keep concrete route selection in Fizeau. DDx may choose the abstract profile/policy name and power bounds but must not select a model/provider/harness.
- If the ideal profile is unavailable but any free/available provider can try the bead, dispatch the attempt through the best available weaker/free profile and record a degraded routing intent rather than blocking before execution.
- Return an execution/provider-availability error only when no provider/profile can attempt the work at all.
- If Fizeau profiles are unavailable and DDx falls back to `MinPower`, derive the fallback floor from the inferred task need as a reasonable lower bound, not the strongest available model.
- Record routing-intent evidence with inferred task need, selected Fizeau profile/policy name when selected, fallback MinPower when used, and degradation notes when DDx tries a weaker/free profile than the ideal.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/profile_select.go and profile_select_test.go
- cli/cmd/try.go and try_test.go
- cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go and work/work tests
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go routing-intent evidence if a requested profile field is needed
- docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-037-bead-execution-hints.md and FEAT-006 only if wording must be reconciled

NON-SCOPE
- Do not pin a concrete model/provider/harness in DDx.
- Do not hard-code Fizeau profile names.
- Do not reintroduce legacy `agent.routing.profile_ladders`, `model_overrides`, or DDx-owned provider fallback.
- Do not change Fizeau's route ranking algorithm inside a selected profile.
- Do not change lifecycle/reviewer hook routing except to share the same selector if useful.
- Do not enable local providers by default merely because they appear in `.ddx/config.yaml`; only Fizeau profiles with available auto-routable models and appropriate policy metadata should be selected.

OBSERVED LIVE EVIDENCE
On 2026-05-13, an unpinned worker started as `ddx work --watch --idle-interval 30s` on ddx-7c256284. The worker printed `route codex/gpt-5.5 reason=policy=default` and `route codex/gpt-5.5 power=10 cost_source=subscription`, even though the bead's durable metadata inferred ordinary implementation work rather than a strong-profile request.
title: routing: select Fizeau profile for inferred implementation tier

description:

Review area: single-project execute-bead automation. Evidence covers FEAT-006, FEAT-010, SD-012, API-001, the closed single-project loop design bead ddx-8bb9af7c, and the requirement to ship a tested single-project execution loop before multi-project or multi-host expansion.

Implement the first shipped single-project loop that continuously works one project's executable-bead queue using the explicit execute-bead contract.

## Scope
- Monitor one project queue for execution-ready beads using the documented queue-ordering contract and the generic execution validator as a gate
- Run `ddx agent execute-bead` for the selected bead from the project root; do not introduce a second worktree lifecycle around the command
- Run required post-run validity checks and execution checks before classifying the attempt
- On execution failure, validation failure, or land conflict, preserve the iteration and evidence exactly as the execute-bead contract specifies, leave the target branch untouched, record the non-landed result, and continue scanning
- On success, land by rebase plus fast-forward, reset loop state to the updated branch tip, and continue scanning for the next executable bead
- Support a minimal control surface suitable for standalone use now and ddx-server hosting later without pulling in multi-project scheduling

## Boundaries

description:
PROBLEM
`ddx work` does not have a crisp human-facing contract for run modes or stdout. The current docs and code use `--poll-interval` as if it were the mode selector, but every queue worker scans the queue between attempts. Operators need explicit semantics for one-shot work, drain-and-exit work, and long-running watch work, plus output that answers whether the worker exited, why it exited, what queue state remains, and why an idle watcher is sleeping.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-010-task-execution.md:685-702 currently describes the behavior as a `--poll-interval` default, conflating idle sleep tuning with the operator's chosen work mode.
- cli/cmd/work.go:37-50 presents `ddx work --poll-interval 30s` as the continuous-worker example rather than naming the mode directly.
- cli/cmd/work.go:75 exposes `--poll-interval` as the primary stay-alive control, even though `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:649-682` treats any positive interval as idle/watch behavior.
- cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go:1885-1937 prints terminal summaries without stop reason, already-satisfied breakdown, remaining queue-state context, or blocked-behind-human-review explanation.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:656-688 emits idle progress internally but does not define the human stdout contract for idle or next-ready-bead transitions.

PROPOSED FIX
Update FEAT-010 and FEAT-006 with an explicit stdout and mode contract:
- `once`: process at most one execution-ready bead and exit. Public flag remains `--once`.
- `drain`: process the currently execution-ready queue until a terminal stop condition, then exit. Direct CLI `ddx work` uses this unless `--watch` is supplied.
- `watch`: process ready work, then remain idle and rescan for newly arriving execution-ready work until signal, fatal config, budget/resource stop, or operator stop. Public flag is `--watch`.
- `idle interval`: the sleep duration between empty-queue scans while in watch mode. Public flag is `--idle-interval <duration>` with a 30s default in watch mode.
- `--poll-interval` is removed from the public CLI and generated docs. There is no compatibility alias. New server/API inputs use `mode` + `idle_interval`, not `poll_interval`.
- Server-managed workers default to watch mode with a 30s idle interval unless the request explicitly asks for `once` or drain mode.

Also define the human stdout contract:
- Terminal summaries state attempts, closed count, changed/already-satisfied breakdown, failures, stop reason, and remaining queue state.
- Remaining queue state distinguishes execution-ready, blocked, needs-human, cooldown/deferred, not-eligible, superseded, and epic/closure-candidate buckets where DDx can compute them.
- Queue summaries explain dependency pressure from human-review blockers: if 30 unique open beads are transitively blocked behind 3 open `needs_human` / needs-investigation blockers, say so and list the blocker IDs/titles with blocked counts.
- Watch idle output says the worker is still running, gives the idle interval, includes queue-state summary, and uses direct wording such as `idle: no execution-ready beads; sleeping 30s`.
- Every idle poll prints a compact queue-state line. The full blocker list may be suppressed on unchanged repeated polls, but counts and sleep duration remain visible every poll.
- When watch mode wakes up and claims new work, stdout separates the new bead from the prior block and says `taking next ready bead from queue: <id> — <title>` before the bead block starts.
- Fizeau typed service events remain opaque; DDx may project route/model/tool summaries into phase-labeled human stdout without mutating the event schema.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not implement CLI flags or renderers in this docs bead.
- Do not change Fizeau event schemas, routing policy, structured JSONL timestamps, or stored event names.
- Do not create or modify Go tests in this docs bead; the Go command below is a regression gate only.

PARENT + DEPS
Parent: ddx-eeced112. No deps.

description:
PROBLEM
Human and JSON summaries cannot reliably answer why `ddx work` stopped or what queue state remained when it stopped. Idle watch output also cannot explain why the worker is sleeping beyond a flat "no ready work" signal. The loop emits `exit_reason` only in the structured `loop.end` event, while `ExecuteBeadLoopResult` exposes attempts/successes/failures and a partial `NoReadyWorkDetail` only for the zero-attempt no-ready path.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:531-542 keeps `exitReason` as a local variable and writes it only through the deferred `loop.end` event at lines 577-581.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:399-407 defines `ExecuteBeadLoopResult` without stop condition, exit reason, or a reusable queue-state summary.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:632-647 populates `NoReadyWorkDetail` only when `result.Attempts == 0`, so a drain that completed work and then emptied the queue cannot summarize the remaining queue state.
- cli/internal/bead/store.go:1576-1715 exposes `BlockedAll` with dependency blockers, retry cooldowns, needs-human/investigation blockers, execution-ineligible beads, superseded beads, and epic-only blockers, but the work loop does not aggregate those into a queue snapshot.
- cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go:1885-1937 can only print attempts/successes/failures and bare route lines because the loop result does not carry stop and queue-state fields.

PROPOSED FIX
Expose stop and queue state as first-class loop-result data:
- Add stable fields to `ExecuteBeadLoopResult` for stop condition/exit reason and a compact queue snapshot.
- Populate stop condition/exit reason whenever `applyStop` classifies a terminal stop, and preserve existing `loop.end.exit_reason` behavior.
- Populate queue snapshot whenever the picker reaches the no-candidate path, including after successful attempts, not just the zero-attempt case.
- The queue snapshot should distinguish at least: execution-ready count, blocked count, needs-human/investigation count, cooldown/deferred count and next retry time, execution-ineligible count, superseded count, skipped epics, and epic closure candidates where the store can compute them.
- Add a transitive dependency-pressure summary for human-review blockers. A human blocker is an open bead that carries `needs_human`, `needs_investigation`, or the existing no-changes triage labels. For each such blocker, compute how many open downstream beads are transitively blocked by it. Expose total blocked-by-human count plus blocker entries with ID, title, priority, and downstream count.
- Keep existing JSON field names for `no_ready_work` and `no_ready_work_detail` compatible; add new fields rather than removing old ones.

acceptance:
**User story:** As a developer on the plugins page, I want clicking Update or Install to give me continuous feedback until the operation completes, and I want the card to reflect the new installed state automatically — without a page reload.

**Acceptance criteria:**

1. **Per-card in-flight tracking.** Clicking Update/Install records the workerId under the plugin's name in a `Map<string, string>`. The same plugin cannot be dispatched again while it is in flight (button disabled; tooltip shows the worker link). A different plugin can be dispatched concurrently and tracks its own worker.

2. **Worker-driven refresh.** For each in-flight plugin, the page subscribes to that worker's progress via the existing `subscribeWorkerProgress` channel. On a terminal event, the page refetches the plugins list and clears that plugin's entry from the in-flight map. Within 2s of worker terminal event, the card reflects the new status (e.g., `update-available` → `installed`, new `installedVersion`).

3. **Fallback polling.** If no terminal event arrives within 30s of dispatch, the page begins polling `plugins { name status installedVersion }` every 2s until the card's status or installedVersion changes, then stops. Integration test simulates a stream dropout and asserts the card eventually refreshes via the poll path.

4. **In-flight visual state.** While a card is in flight, its status badge is replaced by a spinner + "Updating…" or "Installing…" text. The action button is disabled with a tooltip pointing to the worker.

5. **Failure surfacing.** If the worker terminates in a failure phase, the card shows an error badge + tooltip "Update failed — view worker" linking to the worker page. The card's status/version remains whatever it was before dispatch (no false success). The global `dispatchError` stays for synchronous mutation errors only.

6. **Concurrent dispatch.** Dispatching Update on two different cards at once shows two active worker links (a row or small stack in the header instead of the single slot), and each card tracks its own state. Playwright asserts.

7. **No extra refetch overhead.** Refetch is scoped to the plugins list, not the full page data. Manual verification is enough; no specific perf test required.

8. **Playwright e2e.**
   - Seeds a fixture with one outdated plugin.
   - Clicks Update.
   - Asserts the card enters the in-flight visual state and the action button is disabled.
   - Simulates the worker completing successfully.
   - Asserts within 2s the card shows `installed` and a newer `installedVersion`.
   - Runs a second scenario where the simulated worker fails; asserts the failure badge and that status stays `update-available`.

9. **No regressions.** Install-from-registry flow (the ConfirmDialog path) adopts the same in-flight tracking; existing Playwright install flow still passes.
description:
## Observed

On `/nodes/.../projects/.../plugins`, clicking Update on the outdated `helix` card:

1. Fires the mutation — works.
2. Shows a link to the dispatched worker — helpful.
3. Worker completes and the plugin is actually updated on disk — verified.
4. **Card still shows `update-available`.** The UI never closes the loop.

The user has no in-UI signal that the update succeeded. They must reload the page (or navigate away and back) to see the new state. Worse, nothing prevents them from clicking the button again during the gap — firing a second update.

## Root cause

`cli/internal/server/frontend/src/routes/nodes/[nodeId]/projects/[projectId]/plugins/+page.svelte:74-89` —

```js
async function dispatchPlugin(name, action, scope = 'project') {
  const result = await client.request(PLUGIN_DISPATCH_MUTATION, { name, action, scope });
  workerId = result.pluginDispatch.id;
}
```

That is the entire post-dispatch behavior. `data.plugins` is the snapshot from `+page.ts` at load time. There is no:

- subscription to the dispatched worker's progress,
- polling of the plugin list,
- refetch on worker terminal event,
- optimistic card state while the worker runs,
- per-card in-flight tracking (only a single `workerId: string | null` at module scope, which means dispatching a second plugin overwrites the first worker link).

The workers layout already has `subscribeWorkerProgress(workerID, cb)` (`cli/internal/server/frontend/src/routes/nodes/[nodeId]/projects/[projectId]/workers/+layout.svelte:22-30`) — the plugins page just doesn't use it.

## Proposed direction

Two changes, smallest first:

### Fix A — Close the loop on the dispatched worker.

- Per-card in-flight tracking: replace the singleton `workerId` with a `Map<pluginName, workerId>`. Each card shows its own worker link + in-flight state; clicking Install/Update is disabled while that plugin is in flight.
- Subscribe to `subscribeWorkerProgress` for each in-flight plugin. On a terminal phase event (`completed`, `failed`, etc. — whatever the existing worker event vocabulary uses), refetch the plugins list and clear that plugin's in-flight entry.
- If the existing worker-progress stream doesn't emit a terminal event with enough detail, fall back to polling `plugins { name status installedVersion }` every 2s while any card is in flight, stopping when none are.

### Fix B — Optimistic card state (optional polish).

- While a card is in-flight, show "Updating…" / "Installing…" with a spinner in place of the status badge, and disable the action button. This is orthogonal to Fix A and can ship with it.

### Fix C — Persistent failure surfacing.

- Currently `dispatchError` is a single string. If the worker terminates with a failure phase, surface that per-card (error badge + tooltip with detail link to the worker page) rather than relying on `dispatchError` which only covers the synchronous mutation error.

## Out of scope

- Designing new worker terminal events. Use whatever the workers layout already consumes.
- Cancelling an in-flight plugin update — follow-up if needed.
- Bulk update ("update all outdated"). Follow-up.

description:
PROBLEM
`ddx work --watch` can appear healthy while repeatedly skipping claims on a ready queue. A top-level operator-visible signal is needed when the worker's recent claim success rate drops to zero or below a configured threshold over a rolling window.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The work loop owns claim-attempt telemetry and operator-visible events. Runtime configuration for claim throughput belongs with `ExecuteBeadLoopRuntime` in `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:86-92`, and operator-visible loop events are emitted from the loop. description:

Fine for projects (rarely mutate) but broken for beads, documents, commits, sessions, workers (mutated or resorted per query). Replace with ID-based or (sort-key, ID)-based stable cursors. As Stage 2 grows this becomes 50+ copy-pasted guards. Replace with a NewResolver(state StateProvider, workingDir string) *Resolver constructor that rejects nil/empty and returns an error, drop the runtime checks.

3. Snapshot struct vs direct domain types. Current inconsistency: resolver_node.go uses ProjectSnapshot / NodeStateSnapshot (adapter structs) while resolver_documents.go uses docgraph.Document directly. Pick ONE approach and migrate the other. Recommendation: direct domain types (simpler, less boilerplate). Migrate resolver_node.go to drop ProjectSnapshot.

Not in scope: the prefix-registry for node(id) dispatch (concern 5 from the Stage 2.3 note) — keep that for when bead/doc/worker prefixes are added. Not in scope: splitting StateProvider into sub-interfaces (concern 1) — decide that lazily when the interface actually grows.

description:
PROBLEM
  DDx accumulates per-attempt evidence (manifest.json, prompt.md,
  result.json, reviewer-stream.log, agent stream logs in
  .ddx/agent-logs/, worker state in .ddx/workers/) without a
  documented retention or storage architecture. Today the
  executions/ dirs are explicitly tracked in git via un-ignore
  rules; agent-logs/ are local-only but unbounded. After today's
  cleanup discoveries (12,096 tracked execution files, 860 MB
  agent-logs locally) we need a formal design that balances
  reconstruct-the-past against repo bloat.

  The architecture must enable optimization analysis (model /
  prompt / harness / spec performance) WITHOUT forcing all
  detailed evidence into git.

CURRENT STATE
  - No ADR or spec describes the storage tiers, retention
    policy, or the operator interface for archive.
  - Implementation is inconsistent: executions/ tracked via
    un-ignore, agent-logs/ gitignored, workers/ not in gitignore
    but also not actively tracked.
  - No central "metrics" extraction; queries across attempts
    require fanning out reads.

PROPOSED FIX
  New ADR at docs/helix/02-design/adr/ADR-NNN-evidence-storage-architecture.md.

  Principles:
    P1. Git holds durable, small, structured state.
        - bead rows (.ddx/beads.jsonl)
        - closed-bead events (.ddx/attachments/<id>/events.jsonl)
        - aggregate per-attempt metrics (.ddx/metrics/attempts.jsonl)
        - code, docs, ADRs/TDs/FEATs
    P2. Local disk holds detailed, ephemeral, retention-bounded
        evidence (per-machine, never in git).
        - .ddx/executions/<attempt-id>/ (full evidence bundle —
          prompt.md, manifest.json, result.json, usage.json,
          checks.json, reviewer-stream.log, decisions.md, etc.)
        - .ddx/agent-logs/agent-*.jsonl (raw model stream)
        - .ddx/workers/worker-*/ (per-worker runtime state)
        Default retention: 90 days. Configurable.
    P3. External archive is operator-configured (mirror hook),
        not a built-in. Backends: local-dir (default), remote
        (e.g., S3) deferred.
    P4. Aggregate metrics are denormalized, queryable, durable.
        .ddx/metrics/attempts.jsonl is the analytics table; each
        row is one bead-attempt with structured fields for
        cross-bead queries.

  Per-bead git footprint after this architecture:
    - 1 row in .ddx/beads.jsonl (~2-5 KB)
    - 1 file in .ddx/attachments/<bead-id>/events.jsonl
      (~1-3 KB, lifecycle events for the bead)
    - N rows in .ddx/metrics/attempts.jsonl (~300 bytes/attempt)
    Total for a typical 3-attempt bead: ~5-8 KB tracked. 20x
    reduction vs current ~95 KB.

  ADR sections:
    1. Context (why this decision is needed)
    2. Decision (the 3-tier architecture)
    3. Principles P1-P4 with rationale
    4. Per-bead git footprint summary
    5. Local retention default and operator override
    6. External archive interface (hook-point, no built-in
       backend mandate)
    7. Cross-machine considerations (single-machine assumption
       for the attempts.jsonl; partition when federation lands)
    8. Migration plan (sister beads B29/B30/B31/metrics-extraction)

NON-SCOPE
  - Implementing retention (sister bead B29).
  - Removing gitignore un-ignores (sister bead B30).
  - Implementing the mirror backend (sister bead B31).
  - Implementing metrics extraction (sister bead).
  - Implementing the analyze CLI (sister bead).

INTERSECTIONS
  - All other architecture beads (B29 retention, B30 gitignore
    flip, B31 mirror, metrics extraction, analyze CLI) anchor
    against this ADR.
  - Cross-refs TD-031 §5 (existing event vocabulary) and
    SD-025 (existing execution lifecycle).
title: docs(ADR): formalize 3-tier evidence storage architecture (git/local/archive)

description:
## Two-layer problem

### Layer 1 (mechanical bug)

When a worker invokes `ddx bead create` from inside its execute-bead worktree, the resulting bead IDs are malformed. Reproduced today on this project:

  /home/erik/.local/bin/ddx bead ready  → 11 entries with IDs like
  `.execute-bead-wt-ddx-44236615-20260429T185004-ffa9adf1-e630aeae`

These were the read-coverage child beads spawned from the ddx-44236615 worker (commit ebeb2464). They have valid descriptions, AC, priorities, and labels — only the ID field is mangled. The pattern `.execute-bead-wt-<parent>-<timestamp>-<short>-<random>` matches the worktree directory name format used by `ddx agent execute-bead`. Most likely failure path: the bead-id resolver consults `os.Getwd()` (or equivalent) to derive a project context prefix, sees the worktree dir, and uses it instead of the real project root + a fresh `ddx-<8hex>` short hash.

Concrete impact:
- 50+ char IDs are unwieldy in CLI commands (`ddx bead show <id>`, `ddx bead dep add ...`).
- Cross-project readers and the bead store assume `ddx-<8hex>` prefix matching for tooling (filtering, GraphQL adapters, MCP responses) — these long IDs may sort or filter unexpectedly.
- The IDs encode ephemeral attempt timestamps, which leaks worker-internal state into a permanent identifier.
- 12 such beads exist in the tracker as of this filing (grep `.execute-bead-wt-` in `.ddx/beads.jsonl`).

### Layer 2 (design question — separate decision)

Even if the IDs were correctly formed `ddx-<8hex>`, it is not obvious that `ddx bead create` from inside an execute-bead worker is the right pattern at all. Two alternatives the design has not articulated a position on:

**(a) Append to the parent bead.** When the worker discovers sub-tasks, it appends them as structured items in the parent's description, notes, or a new `kind:discovered-subtask` event. The parent bead becomes the durable record of "what this run found"; future runs (or the operator) can decompose if/when the work warrants its own tracker entries.

**(b) Surface via the execute-bead result.** The agent emits a structured `discovered_subtasks: [...]` field on result.json; the loop / operator decides whether to file new beads. Keeps tracker mutations gated by an explicit decision point.

**(c) Create new beads in-band (current behavior).** The worker calls `ddx bead create` directly. Pro: fastest decomposition. Con: sub-tasks land in the queue without operator review; can flood the queue if the agent over-decomposes; complicates "what was THIS run's contribution" auditing.

Today's behavior is (c) but undocumented. The 11 read-coverage children landing as a single agent's decomposition is exactly the failure mode (c) makes easy: one analysis bead spawned 11 implementation beads in a single run, all P0, all without operator review. The work may be valid — but the pattern needs a position.

## In-scope outcomes

This bead's job is to surface both layers; the implementation work decomposes into follow-ups.

1. **Concrete fix for layer 1**: bead-id resolver should normalize worktree paths to the real project root before allocating an ID. Test: `ddx bead create` invoked with cwd=`<repo>/.execute-bead-wt-...` produces `ddx-<8hex>`, not `.execute-bead-wt-...-<random>`.
2. **Mass repair for the 12 existing malformed beads**: either rewrite their IDs to fresh `ddx-<8hex>` (with a redirect or alias map for any external references), or close them as deferred and re-file with proper IDs. Decision deferred until layer 2 is settled.
3. **Layer 2 decision**: file a separate design bead (or amendment to FEAT-006 / FEAT-010) that picks (a), (b), or (c) and documents the rationale. This bead does NOT pre-decide; it captures the question.

## In-scope files (layer 1 fix)

- `cli/cmd/bead_create.go` (or wherever bead-create resolves project context).
- `cli/internal/bead/store.go` or `cli/internal/bead/id.go` if ID generation lives there.
- A unit test that drops cwd into a worktree-shaped dir and asserts the resulting bead id matches `^ddx-[0-9a-f]{8}$`.

(Locate via: `grep -rn "execute-bead-wt\|FindProjectRoot\|projectRoot" cli/internal/bead/ cli/cmd/bead_*.go`.)

## Out of scope

- The 11 read-coverage child beads' actual implementation work — that's separate beads.
- Default behavior change for whether workers can/should create beads — that's the layer-2 design bead.
- GraphQL or MCP changes to handle long IDs — fix the source instead.

## Acceptance

Layer-1 only (this bead):

1. `cd cli && go test ./cmd/... ./internal/bead/...` passes after the fix.
2. New unit test in `cli/internal/bead/` (or `cli/cmd/`) that simulates a bead-create call from `cwd=<project>/.execute-bead-wt-ddx-XXXXX-<timestamp>-<random>` and asserts the new bead's `id` field matches `^ddx-[0-9a-f]{8}$`. Test fails before the fix, passes after.
3. `grep -E '"id":"\.execute-bead-wt-' .ddx/beads.jsonl` returns either 0 (mass repair) or 12 with a recorded decision in this bead's notes that the existing 12 are deferred to a follow-up bead.
4. A separate bead is filed (or referenced existing one updated) that captures the layer-2 design question (a/b/c). Reference its ID in this bead's events.

## Why one bead, not an epic

Layer 1 is a tight 1-3 file fix. Layer 2 is a design discussion that should be its own artifact, not a sibling task. Splitting them keeps each bounded.

22 existing malformed beads with .execute-bead-wt-* IDs are DEFERRED to a mass-repair follow-up. Decision pending on layer-2 design question (ddx-d3a4f89c) — once the in-band vs. append vs. result-field question is decided, the repair approach will be clearer. The malformed beads have valid descriptions, AC, priorities, and labels; only their IDs are wrong.

Fix in store.go correctly threads workingDir through detectPrefix and resolves the worktree-cwd contamination. However, the new test does not simulate the bug scenario: it never chdirs into a worktree-shaped path, so it would pass on main too — failing AC #2's 'fails-before-fix, passes-after' requirement. Layer-2 bead and deferral note are acceptable.
