description:
PROBLEM
During the 2026-05-15 Fizeau grendel-off routing incident, the operator had to run a targeted `ddx try fizeau-a54e0299` from a clean side worktree because the active fizeau checkout was dirty. The worker succeeded and printed `✓ fizeau-a54e0299 → merged (0d70176c)`, but that success was branch-local to the side worktree branch `ddx/a54e0299-burndown-232516`. The active fizeau `master` checkout later advanced independently and still did not contain the route-time health fix. The operator had to inspect git history manually, notice that `master` lacked the landed branch, create a rescue branch, and run `git merge --no-ff ddx/a54e0299-burndown-232516` to make the successful bead reachable from current project history.

This is not a model/routing bug. It is DDx operator UX and audit-safety around side-worktree landings. A successful `ddx try` must make the landing coordinates and recovery command unambiguous when the code lands in a worktree branch that is not the operator's active target branch.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/cmd/try.go:503-514` writes the terminal try result but only prints `bead`, `status`, `detail`, `result_rev`, and `preserve_ref`. It omits existing `ImplementationRev` / `LandedRev` fields and has no branch/worktree/rescue summary, so `merged` looks complete even when it landed on a side branch.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:1056-1068` resolves the target branch internally, and `LandRequest.TargetBranch` documents the branch contract at `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:88-90`, but `LandResult` at `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:111-130` does not carry the resolved target branch back to reports.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:397-430` already has `ImplementationRev` and `LandedRev`, and `cli/internal/agent/try/attempt.go:31-47` already mirrors them. The data exists but the CLI result surface does not expose enough to distinguish worker commit, landed branch tip, and branch-local landing.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_conflict_recovery.go:212-220` records unresolvable land conflicts with `preserve_ref`, but it does not attach an operator-ready rescue command such as creating a clean worktree and merging the preserve ref with `--no-ff`.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add resolved landing metadata to the success path: `LandResult.TargetBranch`, and propagate it through `ExecuteBeadResult`, `ExecuteBeadReport`, `agent/try.Report`, and the try adapter.
- Update `ddx try` output to always print `implementation_rev` and `landed_rev` when they differ, and to print `landed_branch` / `project_root` for landed attempts.
- When `ddx try` is run from a side worktree or non-default branch, print a clear follow-up block naming the branch-local landing and the no-rewrite rescue command: `git merge --no-ff <landed-branch>` from the desired target worktree, or a `git worktree add ... && git merge --no-ff ...` variant when the active checkout is dirty.
- For `land_conflict_unresolvable` / `land_conflict_operator_required`, include a rescue command in the bead event body and terminal detail using the preserve ref, not just the ref name.
- Keep merge-policy intact: do not squash, rebase, or rewrite execute-bead histories. The rescue path must preserve the worker commits and tracker/evidence commits.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change Fizeau routing, provider health, or grendel-specific behavior.
- Do not auto-merge side branches into another checked-out dirty worktree.
- Do not change `ddx work` queue ordering or bead priority policy.
- Do not rewrite existing execute-bead branch history.

INTERSECTIONS
- `ddx-06cbaa90` will eventually add a per-project worktree registry. This bead is narrower: expose/rescue the landing coordinates for today's in-tree mode.
- `ddx-c191e91a` covers stale worktree cleanup. This bead is not cleanup; it is successful-result discoverability and manual rescue guidance.
notes: Additional rescue observation: after creating rescue branch rescue/a54e0299-route-health-235101, the committed file /tmp/fizeau-a54e0299-rescue.235101/.ddx/beads.jsonl contains fizeau-a54e0299 with status=closed and closing_commit_sha=0d70176c, but running ddx bead show fizeau-a54e0299 from that rescue worktree reported status=open because the installed ddx command resolved state from the active/canonical fizeau checkout instead of the command worktree's committed .ddx file. The fix should print the state root/worktree used by try/bead commands, or otherwise make side-worktree state resolution explicit; this reinforces the need for branch/worktree landing coordinates in the terminal result.
title: try: surface side-worktree landings with rescue commands

description:
PROBLEM
Reliability principle P9 (docs/helix/06-iterate/reliability-principles.md:71-87) states "`git fetch` and `git push` are never called from `Land()` or from the `ddx work` queue loop." The CLI pre-claim hook violates this every iteration: it shells `git fetch origin <branch>` before each claim from the drain loop, which couples the queue's forward progress to network reachability and origin availability. This is one of the recurring blockers operators see (`pre-claim hook blocked queue: ...`) when origin is unreachable or the local branch has diverged.

ROOT CAUSE
- `cli/cmd/shared_helpers.go:51-69` (`buildCLIPreClaimHook`) calls `gitOps.FetchOriginAncestryCheck(projectRoot, branch)` for every iteration of the drain loop.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:806` is the actual `git fetch origin <branch>` invocation inside `fetchOriginAncestryCheckLocked` (called from `RealLandingGitOps.FetchOriginAncestryCheck` at line 782).
- The hook is wired into `ddx work` at `cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:544` (`PreClaimHook: buildCLIPreClaimHook(projectRoot, cliLandingOps)`) and into `ddx try` at `cli/cmd/try.go:480`.

PROPOSED FIX
Remove the `git fetch` from the per-claim hot path. Two acceptable shapes:
  (a) Drop the fetch entirely from `buildCLIPreClaimHook` and rely on local ancestry against `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` as last-observed; FEAT-023 `ddx sync` is the operator-driven refresh path.
  (b) Move the fetch to a one-time pre-drain preflight that runs at the start of `runWork`/`runTry` before the loop begins (still violates P9 for `try`, but `try` is a single-bead path so it's bounded).

Recommend (a). The ancestry check itself (comparing local SHA vs `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>`) can stay; only the fetch is forbidden.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- `cli/cmd/shared_helpers.go` (buildCLIPreClaimHook)
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go` (FetchOriginAncestryCheck, fetchOriginAncestryCheckLocked)
- `cli/internal/server/workers.go:1677` if the server-side preclaim has the same defect — audit and apply parallel fix.
- `cli/cmd/work_test.go` (new TestWork_NetworkFreeDrain_NoFetchInLoop)
- `cli/cmd/try.go:480` (callsite parity)

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change `ddx sync` semantics.
- Do not remove the ancestry comparison itself — only the fetch.
- Do not touch the `Land()` post-claim git push path (P9 also forbids it but that's separate, file a sibling bead if it's still present).

REFERENCES
- Helix align audit run-id: helix-align-20260518T074735Z (R2)
- Reliability principles: docs/helix/06-iterate/reliability-principles.md (P9)
title: agent: stop calling git fetch from buildCLIPreClaimHook; restore P9 network-free drain

description:
PROBLEM
During the 2026-06-16 DDx repo canary after rebuilding/installing 764fe0084, worker worker-20260616T215629-cc7c claimed ddx-7f5092f2, completed readiness, then was killed before an execution attempt started. Its status.json records action=index-lock-violation with detail operation=index.commit outcome=removed reason="managed worker exited; no live owner". Its worker.log shows tracker_lock section=pre_dispatch_commits wait=0s hold=10.017s followed by "Cancel received, shutting down gracefully". .ddx/metrics/locks.jsonl records pre_dispatch_commits for holder_pid=680596 from 2026-06-16T22:01:42.882688293Z to 2026-06-16T22:01:52.89652651Z, duration_ms=10013. This violates the worker/server reliability goal: a pre-dispatch checkpoint must not cross the cap boundary, leave a stale index.lock, or require server kill/restart before execution begins.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:842-860 runs commitTrackerLocked and checkpointPreDispatchDirt together under withTrackerLock(projectRoot, "pre_dispatch_commits", ...), so tracker commit plus checkpoint/index sync can hold the parent repo mutation path long enough to hit cap-boundary behavior before the isolated attempt exists.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1702-1713 stages and commits tracker changes through runGitWithIndexLockRecovery without a pre-cap timeout proof for the pre-dispatch path.
- cli/internal/agent/predispatch_dirty.go:260-299 performs temp-index checkpoint work and then runGitWithIndexLockRecovery(..., "read-tree", "HEAD") while still inside the pre_dispatch_commits mutation window.
- cli/internal/server/workers.go:833-867 recovers .git/index.lock after managed-worker exit, but the canary shows this is happening after the worker is killed rather than preventing the cap-boundary failure.

PROPOSED FIX
Bound pre-dispatch tracker/checkpoint git operations so ordinary checkpoint commits do not run to the index.lock cap or cause a managed worker kill before execution. Prefer splitting tracker commit and checkpoint/index sync into separately bounded mutation windows, using a temp-index path that avoids parent index.commit where possible, or timing out before DefaultIndexLockCap with clean stale-lock recovery and an operator-visible retryable event. Preserve the pre-execute-bead checkpoint and tracker audit history.

NON-SCOPE
Do not raise DefaultIndexLockCap, disable lockmetrics violations, remove checkpoint commits, change durable-audit behavior already covered by ddx-15fdc1e1, or change plugin topology.

PARENT
- ddx-d5dfa702

DEPENDENCIES
- None.
title: agent: prevent pre-dispatch checkpoint commits from killing managed workers

description:
PROBLEM
An author can supply a `spec:verification-waiver` in place of proof and thereby make an unverified Complete/Implemented document pass. A reasoned waiver is legitimate for work that is not yet claiming completion, but it must never suppress a Complete-status coverage failure.

A waiver can never suppress a Complete-status coverage failure. Analyzer remains read-only.

acceptance: Both reasoningByteLimit and reasoningStallTimeout are configurable via ddx-agent config.yaml with raised defaults (>=256KB, >=300s). Setting either to 0 disables the check. Error messages include the model name and current threshold. Existing tests updated, new tests cover custom thresholds and disabled checks.
description:
The ddx-agent stream consumer has two hardcoded constants that abort model responses prematurely:

- `reasoningByteLimit = 32 * 1024` (32KB) — aborts if pure reasoning_content exceeds 32K chars before any content delta
- `reasoningStallTimeout = 120 * time.Second` — aborts if only reasoning tokens arrive for 2 minutes

Both are in `stream_consume.go` (github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/agent v0.3.5, lines 13 and 18).

## Observed
- google/gemma-4-31b on bragi: reasoning overflow at 32KB on ddx-e14c86ef (P3, small bead)
- qwen3.5-27b on bragi: same reasoning stall on the same bead
- Both models use extended thinking by default; coding tasks routinely produce >32KB of reasoning before the first content token
- qwen3-coder-next on vidar does NOT hit this (different reasoning behavior — produces content tokens earlier)

The 120s stall timeout is particularly problematic: local models generating at 5-15 tok/s can easily spend 2+ minutes reasoning through a complex prompt before producing output. This is normal behavior, not a stall.

## Required changes
1. Make both thresholds configurable via ddx-agent config.yaml (e.g. `reasoning_byte_limit`, `reasoning_stall_timeout`)
2. Raise defaults: at least 256KB byte limit and 300s stall timeout
3. Allow 0 = unlimited for both (same pattern as max_iterations)
4. When the threshold fires, include the model name and configured limit in the error message so operators can tune

## Scope
- stream_consume.go: replace const with config-driven values
- config.go: add fields to Config struct
- Defaults() should set the raised defaults
- Tests: verify configurable thresholds, verify 0 = unlimited
title: Raise and make configurable reasoning stall/overflow thresholds in ddx-agent

description:
PROBLEM
  cli/internal/agent/try/attempt.go:256-269 sets a 24h cooldown on
  declined_needs_decomposition outcomes. This violates TD-031 §5
  invariant: "work-retry-after may be set only when
  retrying the same bead after time passes could plausibly succeed
  without human/spec/dependency changes."

  Decomposition requires operator action: filing sub-beads, wiring
  dependency edges, possibly amending the parent's AC. Time elapsed
  alone changes nothing. After 24h, the drain re-attempts, fails
  again with the same "needs decomposition", and re-parks for
  another 24h. Infinite cycle until operator acts.

  Per TD-031 §5 row "parent/epic/decomposed container": the correct
  signal is execution-eligible=false (which excludes the bead from
  ordinary drain claim) plus optional decomposed label, NOT a
  time-based cooldown.

ROOT CAUSE
  - cli/internal/agent/try/attempt.go:256-269: returns OutcomePark

  - The bead exits ready queue for 24h based on wall-clock, then

      - Optionally add label "needs-decomposition" or
        "triage:decomposition-required" for operator visibility.
      - Status transition: in_progress → open (claim released)

  - The bead drops out of ordinary drain claim (execution-eligible

  - When the operator decomposes the bead (files children, wires

     - TestDeclinedNeedsDecomposition_NotEligible: assert
       execution-eligible=false is set.
     - TestDeclinedNeedsDecomposition_NotInReady: assert the bead

NON-SCOPE

  - Auto-decomposition (separate beads, e.g., ddx-008d288f).

INTERSECTIONS
  - Sister bead "docs(TD-031): codify push_failed/push_conflict
    outcome rows" — the same spec invariant motivates this fix.
  - Sister bead R1 (push_failed no cooldown) — same pattern.

description:
PROBLEM
Operators have no documented contract for the pre-claim intake, no mapping of failure classes (warn-only vs operator-attention escalation vs hard error), and no playbook for diagnosing silent-idle on a full queue. During the Fizeau idle, the warn payload's suggested_action ("check the readiness route or harness configuration and retry") actively misdirected the operator: the real fault was DDx's own decoder, not the route or harness config.

ROOT CAUSE
The README lacks a pre-claim intake section, so the readiness_checks verdict forms, the failure-class mapping, the warn-fingerprint escalation threshold, the claim-rate window flags, and the silent-idle diagnosis steps are undocumented.

PROPOSED FIX (parent AC5)
Add a "Pre-claim Intake and Silent-Idle Diagnosis" section to README.md documenting: (a) the readiness_checks contract including the canonical verdict forms (bool/string/null); (b) the failure-class mapping warn-only -> operator-attention -> hard error; (c) the consecutive-warn-fingerprint escalation threshold and the --claim-rate-window / --claim-rate-threshold flags; (d) a step-by-step silent-idle diagnosis playbook (how to tell a stuck full queue from a legitimately empty one via the agent-loop log and status surfaces).

DEPENDS ON
All four code children (decoder coercion, schema lock, warn-fingerprint escalation, claim-rate window) must land first so the documented contract, flags, and thresholds match shipped behavior.

NON-SCOPE
- Any code changes to the decoder, schema, loop, or CLI (covered by the four sibling code children this depends on).

CROSS-REF
Governing artifact: AR-2026-05-17 follow-up beads. Adjacent silent-failure bugs documented alongside: ddx-57c40485, ddx-8f2e0ebf.
title: Document pre-claim intake contract, failure-class mapping, and silent-idle diagnosis in README

description:
PROBLEM
During the 2026-06-13 dogfood merge recovery, `.ddx/beads.jsonl` had real Git conflict stages visible via `git ls-files -u` and `git show :1:.ddx/beads.jsonl`, but `ddx bead merge` failed with `read Git stage 1 for .ddx/beads.jsonl: exit status 128`. That forced abandoning the worktree instead of using DDx's supported tracker merge surface.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/cmd/bead.go registers `newBeadMergeCommand`, and the merge implementation reads Git conflict stages for `.ddx/beads.jsonl`. The observed error means the helper's stage-read command is not equivalent to the working `git show :1:.ddx/beads.jsonl` path in a linked worktree or conflict state. This violates AGENTS.md's rule to prefer supported `ddx bead` operations over direct tracker edits.

PROPOSED FIX
- Reproduce the conflict with a test repository that has stages 1/2/3 for `.ddx/beads.jsonl` in a linked worktree.
- Fix the Git stage reader to use a working-tree-root-relative path and the correct repository/worktree directory.
- Add verbose diagnostics that print the exact stage/path being read when stage access fails.
- Keep the merge command tracker-only; do not introduce ad hoc JSONL editing as recovery.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change bead merge semantics for non-conflicted files. Do not bypass Git conflict stages by reading arbitrary temporary files. Do not rewrite existing execute-bead history.
title: beads: repair merge conflict stage reader

description:
PROBLEM
Every pre-land bead review dispatched by the execute-bead worker fails instantly with provider_empty (0-byte reviewer output), parking each otherwise-successful implementation as review_malfunction and converting all auto-landings into manual operator verify+merge work. Observed 5-for-5 on 2026-07-22/23 (ddx-09dcaa39, ddx-6f4b96ec x2, ddx-074a82c2, ddx-dfeb5b20, ddx-c4497391). The ddx-dfeb5b20 retry logic rides through transient flakes but cannot help because the failure is deterministic.

ROOT CAUSE
cli/internal/agent/reviewer_readonly.go:7 defines PermissionsReadOnlyReviewer = "readonly", sent as PermissionsOverride for every reviewer dispatch by BuildReviewExecuteRequest (cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go:842). Fizeau v0.15.x's permission vocabulary is {"safe","supervised","unrestricted"} (fizeau@v0.15.2 service.go:280 SupportedPermissions doc; internal/harnesses/registry.go:15-17). "readonly" matches no candidate, so ResolveRoute rejects every route. Reproduced directly: ddx run --min-power 9 --permissions readonly fails with 'ResolveRoute: no viable routing candidate ... 20 candidates rejected' in ~450ms, while the identical prompt with --permissions safe succeeds (10-minute genuine review, 4.4KB verdict JSON).

PROPOSED FIX
Change PermissionsReadOnlyReviewer to "safe" (Fizeau's most restrictive preset, matching the reviewer's read-only intent) in cli/internal/agent/reviewer_readonly.go, citing fizeau service.go:280 in the comment. Add a regression test asserting the constant is a member of Fizeau v0.15's documented vocabulary so a future rename fails loudly instead of silently rejecting all routes.

NON-SCOPE
Fizeau-side acceptance of a 'readonly' alias; reviewer routing policy; the ddx-dfeb5b20 retry semantics; the fallback route-label issue in exhaustion messages.
title: review: send Fizeau-supported permissions constraint for reviewer dispatch

description:
PROBLEM
During dogfood of ddx-3b721804 on 2026-06-13, a Claude execute-bead attempt repeatedly spawned shell monitor commands such as `until ! kill -0 $(pgrep -f "lefthook run pre-commit") ...`. After the real `lefthook`/`go test` process exited, the watcher shells remained alive because `pgrep -f` matched the watcher command text itself. The worker made no progress until the operator killed only those watcher PIDs. DDx must not let provider/tool monitor children create an unbounded hidden stall.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:337-366 arms idle and tool-call timers around service events, but it does not track or bound shell children that remain alive after the useful tool process exits.
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1992-1996 tells agents to run tests and pre-commit, but the execute-bead contract does not prohibit self-matching background watchers or require bounded monitor commands.
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2010 tells the agent to stop after the commit, but DDx has no enforcement that stale background monitor shells are terminated and reported before the provider resumes.

PROPOSED FIX
Add attempt-scoped supervision for background shell/monitor children launched under the execution worktree. Detect stale monitor commands whose watched process has exited or whose command pattern matches themselves, terminate them without killing the main provider process, and record durable evidence. Expose the stale command count/oldest age in worker status or attempt evidence so operators do not have to inspect `ps`.

NON-SCOPE
Do not ban all background commands. Do not assume only Claude can produce this pattern. Do not rely on real provider CLIs in tests.
title: agent: supervise background monitor shells during execute-bead

description:
PROBLEM: `ddx try` creates a fresh git worktree under
`~/.cache/ddx/exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-<bead>-<attempt>/` per attempt
(FEAT-010 layer 2). For projects with native build toolchains (Rust + cargo,
JVM + gradle, Go + module cache, etc.), the fresh worktree starts with an
empty toolchain build cache, so the agent's first build inside is a cold
build from scratch. FEAT-010 §Layer 2 and TD-010 §Storage Model are silent
on this — they specify worktree creation and evidence capture but make no
statement about toolchain build-cache sharing or per-worktree I/O budgets.

OBSERVED COST (2026-05-28, niflheim project):
- A single in-flight `ddx try` attempt accumulated `target/` = 14 GB in the
  execute-bead worktree.
- Two concurrent workers + the project's own niflheim recovery run
  collectively wrote ~23 GB to the same SSD over ~30 minutes.
- The project's WAL recovery (read-bound, ~2 MB written) was visibly
  starved by worker cargo build I/O.
- Each fresh attempt repeats this cost — the worktree is destroyed at
  attempt end (or preserved with `--no-merge`), so the cache is lost.

ROOT CAUSE (spec-level): FEAT-010 treats worktree resource cost as a
non-concern. The feature explicitly lists "workspace creation, bead
attempt, merge or preserve, evidence bundle" but lists no resource-budget
or cache-reuse hook surface. There is no ADR governing per-worktree I/O,
no documented hook for projects to opt into shared toolchain caches, and
no operator-visible counter that would surface this contention in
`ddx work status` or `ddx doctor`.

PROPOSED EVOLUTION (the executing agent should choose how to slot these
into the artifact stack; below is the recommended shape):

1. **Amend FEAT-010 §Layer 2** (`docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-010-task-execution.md`):
   - Add a "Worktree resource expectations" subsection acknowledging that
     execute-bead worktrees do not, by default, share native toolchain
     build caches with the parent checkout or with sibling attempts.
   - State the operator's responsibility (set per-project env like
     `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `GRADLE_USER_HOME`, `GOPATH/pkg/mod`, etc., or
     project-level config) versus DDx's responsibility (pass through
     environment unchanged, do not invent toolchain-specific knobs).
   - Document that `ddx work` makes no concurrency guarantee for native
     build steps inside attempts; concurrent workers may contend.

2. **Amend TD-010** (`docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-010-executions.md`):
   - Add a §Worktree environment passthrough subsection naming
     `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `GRADLE_USER_HOME`, `MAVEN_OPTS`, `GOPATH`,
     `GOMODCACHE`, `npm_config_cache`, `PIP_CACHE_DIR`, etc. as
     environment variables that flow unmodified from the `ddx try`
     caller into the agent process inside the worktree.
   - Specify the invariant: DDx never sets, overrides, or unsets any
     toolchain cache env var. Operator/project owns the policy.

3. **Optionally add an ADR** (e.g., `ADR-027-worktree-resource-isolation.md`)
   recording the decision to keep build-cache policy outside DDx, with the
   rationale (cross-language, single-responsibility, prevents lock-in to a
   specific toolchain). If the executing agent decides one ADR is overkill,
   adding the same paragraph as a §Rationale block at the end of TD-010 is
   acceptable.

4. **Update CLAUDE.md "Execution Evidence Convention" section** if needed
   to cross-reference the new TD-010 environment-passthrough subsection
   so agents working in execute-bead worktrees know they may set
   `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (or equivalent) per project policy.

NON-SCOPE:
- Implementing build-cache mounting, sccache integration, or any
  toolchain-specific knob inside ddx itself. This bead is documentation
  only — it locks down the boundary so future implementation work has
  a clear policy to refer to.
- Changing `ddx try` worktree creation semantics or evidence capture.
- Changing the worktree path under `~/.cache/ddx/exec-wt/`.
- Adding `ddx doctor` or `ddx work status` instrumentation for disk
  contention (potential follow-up bead, not this one).
- Project-side fixes (niflheim has its own bead niflheim-e5cd7c69 for
  the cargo-target-dir workflow documentation).

IN-SCOPE FILES:
- docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-010-task-execution.md
- docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-010-executions.md
- Optionally: docs/helix/02-design/adr/ADR-027-worktree-resource-isolation.md
  (new) — only if the agent chooses the ADR path over TD-010 §Rationale.
- Optionally: CLAUDE.md (cross-reference paragraph only, no behavior change).

OUT-OF-SCOPE FILES:
- Any cli/ code — this is a docs-only evolution.
- Other FEAT/TD/ADR documents — touch only the listed artifacts unless
  the agent discovers a direct conflicting claim in another doc, in
  which case file a follow-up bead rather than expanding scope here.
title: specs: worktree resource-isolation expectations (build-cache reuse, I/O budgets) for ddx try/work

description:
PROBLEM: Epic auto-close exists but the autonomous factory bypasses it, so epics linger open forever during real drains. The walk-up-and-close logic (walkUpClosureCandidate, cli/internal/bead/store.go:1639-1697; entered via cascadeAndWalkUp at store.go:1588) is wired ONLY into the manual Store.Close path (store.go:1554). So when ddx work/ddx try closes the last child of an epic, the epic stays open. This violates FEAT-004 §Queue Semantics For Epics (docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-004-beads.md:122-163), which mandates the closure cascade.

DECISION (operator-ratified): a CANCELLED child counts as terminal/done for epic rollup (cancelled = "work that will not run", types.go:72-73 — a deliberate terminal, never retried), matching the existing walkUpClosureCandidate non-terminal test (store.go:1651: status != closed && != cancelled). Refinement: if ALL children are cancelled (zero closed), the epic is CANCELLED, not closed-as-done. The dependency-DAG "does not satisfy dependents" rule is a separate axis and is unaffected.

ROOT CAUSE: the walk-up is hooked only into Store.Close, not CloseWithEvidence (store.go:1939).

Guard so a REJECTED close (gate refusal, bead still open) does NOT trigger walk-up. Add the all-cancelled-children -> cancel-the-epic refinement to walkUpClosureCandidate. Update FEAT-004:134-136 to state cancelled-counts-as-terminal explicitly.

NON-SCOPE: idle-loop cascade (separate bead); reconcile pass (separate bead); multi-hop recursion (separate dependent bead).

description:
PROBLEM: On 2026-05-27 the installed ddx-server systemd user unit was found in a crash-loop with NRestarts/StartCounter at 4382. Its ExecStart was failing persistently (a stale singleton lock at ~/.local/share/ddx/server.lock held dead pid 724, and the legacy unit also had a nonexistent WorkingDirectory). Because the unit sets Restart=on-failure + RestartSec=5 with NO start-limit, systemd restarted it forever (every 5s), spamming the journal and burning CPU, never giving up.

ROOT CAUSE: cli/internal/service/systemd.go:15-31 — the `unitTemplate` constant defines Restart=on-failure (line 23) and RestartSec=5 (line 24) but declares no StartLimitIntervalSec/StartLimitBurst in the [Unit] section. The systemd --user manager's default start-limit is not effective here, so a persistently-failing ExecStart loops indefinitely instead of entering `failed` state.

PROPOSED FIX: Add StartLimitIntervalSec= and StartLimitBurst= to the [Unit] section of `unitTemplate` (suggested: StartLimitIntervalSec=300, StartLimitBurst=5). Keep Restart=on-failure and RestartSec=5. After N failures within the interval, systemd enters `failed` (operator can `systemctl --user reset-failed ddx-server` after fixing the cause) instead of crash-looping.

NON-SCOPE: Do NOT modify singleton stale-lock detection in cli/internal/server/singleton.go (separate concern). Do NOT touch the launchd/macOS backend. Do NOT change WorkingDirectory or the XDG paths set by buildServerServiceConfig.
title: server systemd unit: add StartLimitIntervalSec/StartLimitBurst so persistent startup failure stops crash-looping

description:
PROBLEM (captured live): Two `ddx work --watch` workers on the same checkout /Users/erik/Projects/ddx collided. Worker 1 ran ddx-69a9ecd3 to completion (closed, 1h11m) but its durable-audit commit was SIGKILLed and the worker exited "operator attention required", leaving .ddx/beads.jsonl, .ddx/beads-archive.jsonl, .ddx/metrics/attempts.jsonl, .ddx/attachments dirty. Memory was healthy (31Gi free) — NOT OOM. Error: `commit durable audit outputs: committing durable audit outputs: : signal: killed`.

ROOT CAUSE: cli/internal/agent/durable_audit.go:88 wraps the WHOLE commit body (status/add/diff/commit) in context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second); that ctx flows to exec.CommandContext (cli/internal/git/exec.go:38). While the git commit was blocked behind the concurrent worker's hold on the shared main-git lock (.ddx/.git-tracker.lock via withTrackerLock, tracker_lock.go:133-152) / .git/index.lock, the 30s deadline fired and Go sent SIGKILL to git -> CombinedOutput() returns empty output + *exec.ExitError("signal: killed") (durable_audit.go:125-127). The classifier isTransientGitContention (cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1026-1041) matches index.lock / "unable to write new index file" / "cannot lock ref" / "unable to update the ref" but NOT "signal: killed"/context-deadline, so finalizeDurableAuditOrStop (execute_bead_loop.go:1311-1336) sets OperatorAttention and exits. The commit is ALREADY idempotent on re-entry (durable_audit.go:98-122), so a retry would succeed — only the misclassification-driven EXIT blocks the idempotent re-run.

PROPOSED FIX: Make isTransientGitContention (execute_bead_loop.go:1026) a SUPERSET that returns true for: (a) errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) and substrings "signal: killed" and "context deadline exceeded" (the SIGKILL/deadline class — defense-in-depth since the exec.ExitError from a ctx kill may not retrievably wrap context.DeadlineExceeded), AND (b) the "tracker lock timeout (...)" string from tracker_lock.go:283 (the lock-acquire-wait-exhausted class). This SUPERSEDES ddx-2189a07f (which adds only the tracker-lock-timeout string and is currently wedging on a routing issue) — folding both transient forms into one coherent classifier change avoids two beads racing to edit the same function. Keep all existing matches.

NON-SCOPE: changing the 30s deadline value or decoupling it from the lock wait (that is the sibling bead B2); worktree-leak cleanup (ddx-274943fc); classifier call sites other than the durable-audit branch.
IN-SCOPE FILES: cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go (classifier), cli/internal/agent/durable_audit_test.go (extend the transient table ~lines 175-185 via runAuditWithFinalizeErr).
title: execute-bead: classify SIGKILL/context-deadline durable-audit commit (signal: killed) + tracker-lock-timeout as transient, not operator-attention

description:
PROBLEM (Principle 2 of epic ddx-602ae31a)

First-time machine setup and runtime plugin lookup need a separate, testable implementation unit. `ddx init --global` should install the default `ddx` plugin globally and wire agent-tier skill links, while plain `ddx init` should create project state without installing plugins. Runtime lookup must prefer project installs, then global installs, then the baked-in default `ddx` plugin.

ROOT CAUSE
- `cli/cmd/init.go:73` owns the `ddx init` command path and must branch between global setup and project initialization.
- `cli/cmd/init.go:132` creates project `.ddx/` state and must not materialize plugin content in plain project init.
- `cli/cmd/init.go:314` is the global setup hook that must install the default plugin under `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/plugins/ddx/`, link skills, and write global config.
- `cli/internal/registry/resolve.go:25` is the runtime plugin lookup boundary and must encode project > global > baked-in precedence.
- `cli/internal/ddxroot/ddxroot.go:70` and `cli/internal/ddxroot/ddxroot.go:90` define the project and global roots this behavior depends on.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement or verify `ddx init --global` as the umbrella machine setup command: materialize the bundled default `ddx` plugin to `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/plugins/ddx/`, create `~/.claude/skills/ddx` and `~/.agents/skills/ddx` pointing into that plugin tree, and write `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/config.yaml` with convention defaults. Keep plain `ddx init` project-only: create `<project>/.ddx/` and project config, but do not write `plugins/`; plugin content lazy-resolves through runtime lookup. Runtime lookup must prefer `ddxroot.Path()/plugins/<name>/` over global, and only fall back to baked-in content for the default `ddx` plugin.

GOVERNING ARTIFACTS
- Principle 2 of epic ddx-602ae31a.
- Depends on ddx-06cbaa90: project lookup uses `ddxroot.Path()` and global lookup uses `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/`.
- ADR-027 skill install topology or equivalent must document the precedence.

PARENT
- ddx-602ae31a

DEPS
- ddx-06cbaa90

NON-SCOPE
- Removing the existing per-project install entirely; global and per-project modes coexist.
- Migrating `~/.config/ddx/` legacy paths if any exist.
- Agent-harness path discovery beyond Claude Code and Codex-facing `.agents/skills`; add others only when those harnesses define their skill paths.
title: init and registry: resolve project, global, and baked-in plugin layers

description:
PROBLEM
The current tracker can contain stale management metadata from prior attempts: latest events may show success while work-last-status still says no_changes; verified no_changes may remain open; retry-after may be expired or attached to a non-retryable lifecycle condition; parent/epic beads may have repeated no_changes attempts even though children own the work. Without a reconciliation path, fixing future ddx work behavior strands the existing pile-up.

ROOT CAUSE
- cli/internal/bead/store.go:744-752 SetExecutionCooldown writes mutable work-* Extra fields, but there is no companion repair path that reconciles those fields against append-only events.
- cli/internal/bead/store.go:754-779 IncrNoChangesCount accumulates no_changes counters, but no command classifies or clears stale counters when a later terminal event supersedes them.
- cli/cmd/bead.go has cooldown show/clear around lines 1171-1273, but no broader lifecycle reconciliation dry-run/apply command.
- Live tracker evidence shows the failure class this bead must encode as fixtures: latest execute-bead event summary=success while work-last-status=no_changes; open verified no_changes; non-retryable needs_investigation parked with retry-after.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add a supported reconciliation command or worker reconciliation pass, preferably `ddx bead reconcile`, with dry-run default and explicit apply mode.
- Reconciliation reads bead events and Extra fields through the store API, not by manual JSONL editing.
- Implement conservative rules only:
  - latest success/already_satisfied event may clear stale no_changes/cooldown Extra and close only when close evidence is present or verifiable through existing close path;
  - verified no_changes may be re-run/validated and closed as already_satisfied when the verification command passes;
  - expired retry-after may be cleared;
  - parent/epic repeated no_changes may be marked execution-eligible=false only when child/dependency evidence proves ordinary ddx work should not pick it;
  - non-retryable needs_investigation may clear retry-after and leave triage labels/blocked explanation.
- Output every proposed mutation with bead id, reason, current fields, proposed fields, and whether it is safe to apply.

NON-SCOPE
- Free-form human judgment or LLM review during reconciliation.
- Broad historical migration of closed beads.
- Manual edits to .ddx/beads.jsonl.
- Creating or deleting beads; this command only reconciles state on existing beads.

PARENT
- ddx-a9d130d0.

DEPS
- ddx-fd1766e5: reconciliation should use the same lifecycle action semantics as live execution.
- ddx-49eeb476: reconciliation output should use the same durable skip reasons exposed by queue diagnostics.

INTERSECTIONS
- Existing `ddx bead cooldown clear` handles one field manually; this bead should reuse or complement it without changing its simple behavior.
- Existing bead doctor repairs malformed/oversized tracker rows; this bead is lifecycle metadata reconciliation, not JSONL structural repair.
title: beads: reconcile stale no_changes lifecycle metadata

description:
Second child of ddx-b7ee0d6f. When a worker successfully lands a bead (status = success), the new commit sits on the local branch forever. There is no git push. The source in cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_commit.go has ZERO references to push/fetch/origin (grep verified). Result: successful work on one machine is invisible to every other machine, and the local branch grows indefinitely with unsynced commits.

## Evidence

cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_commit.go defines the commit step but never calls git push. The only mention of 'git' in that file is a comment about trailers.

cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go at the success branch (around line 343):

    if report.Status == ExecuteBeadStatusSuccess {
        if err := w.Store.CloseWithEvidence(candidate.ID, report.SessionID, report.ResultRev); err != nil {
            return result, err
        }
        result.Successes++
        result.LastSuccessAt = now().UTC()
    }

The tracker is updated (CloseWithEvidence writes to beads.jsonl) but the working tree / commits are never pushed to origin.

## Required behavior

After a successful landing (merge outcome = 'merged' AND bead status = success), the worker must:

1. Run `git push --ff-only origin <default-branch>`
2. On rejection:
   - Classify as ExecuteBeadStatusLandConflict (this status already exists in execute_bead_status.go)
   - Preserve the commits under refs/ddx/iterations/ (the infrastructure already exists for the preserved-result case)
   - Unclaim the bead so a later attempt can pick it up again AFTER divergence is resolved
   - Emit a 'push_rejected' event with the local HEAD and the remote tip
   - Stop the worker loop (divergence requires human attention)
3. On network failure: similar to fetch — log a warning, mark the attempt with a 'push_pending' flag, continue
4. Pair this push with the fetch-first bead (sibling ddx-bd42f640) so the loop is: fetch → verify ancestry → run bead → push — a closed consistency loop

## Why --ff-only

Force-with-lease is tempting but wrong here — if push is rejected, it means another machine pushed in the meantime, and we want to detect that and reconcile, not overwrite. --ff-only ensures we only ever advance origin, never rewrite it. A rejection is a signal, not a problem to work around.

## Test cases

- Fresh clone, worker lands a bead, push succeeds, origin advances to new HEAD
- Another machine pushed between fetch and commit (race): second worker lands, push is rejected, bead is unclaimed and marked land_conflict, loop stops
- Network unreachable: push is deferred, attempt records 'push_pending', worker continues but subsequent workers halt on the same branch
- Default branch is configurable

description:
PROBLEM
DDx can correctly classify an attempt as no_evidence_produced or execution_failed inside the execution engine, then overwrite that typed outcome as no_changes at the ddx try and ddx work command boundaries merely because ResultRev equals BaseRev. A harness that returns no commit and no rationale is therefore reported as a legitimate no-change attempt, hiding execution failures and bypassing the no-evidence retry/operator-attention path.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1529-1584 distinguishes clean no-evidence from rationale-backed no_changes, and populateWorkerStatus at lines 1803-1816 records no_evidence_produced. cli/cmd/try.go:389-399 and cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:476-485 later normalize solely from ResultRev == BaseRev and overwrite the typed status/outcome. docs/execute-bead-self-commit-contract.md:3-17 requires a commit or explicit no_changes_rationale; absence of both is a harness failure, not no_changes.

PROPOSED FIX
Normalize try and work results from the typed worker status/outcome first. Preserve no_evidence_produced, execution_failed, and other authoritative non-success outcomes even when revisions are equal. Map equal revisions to no_changes only when the engine has positively classified rationale-backed no_changes. Keep both command paths on one shared normalization helper so they cannot drift.

NON-SCOPE
Do not parse provider stderr, Stop-hook messages, harness/model/provider identity, or route diagnostics. Do not implement the post-v0.15 Fizeau attempt-policy adapter tracked by ddx-66a8883f, change MinPower escalation, weaken repository/gate evidence, or select a Fizeau route.

PARENT
ddx-8b22914e.

DEPS
No deps. This is the pre-v0.15 repository-evidence correction; ddx-66a8883f owns later typed Fizeau retry policy.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx currently increments no_changes counters and parses no_changes rationale, but the try layer does not expose a sufficiently explicit lifecycle action for the work loop to distinguish already satisfied, needs human, unjustified bad attempt, retryable transient, parent/decomposed, or external blocker cases. description:
PROBLEM
TestTrackerLock_RecordsRetryCount (cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock_test.go:553) is flaky under parallel-package test load. Failure: 'expected Retries > 0 for contended lock, got 0'. Observed reproduction rate before fix: ~2/20 (10%) when run with -count=20.

ROOT CAUSE
cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock_test.go:576-579 releases the held lock via a time-based goroutine:
    go func() {
        time.Sleep(30 * time.Millisecond)
        _ = os.RemoveAll(lockDir)
    }()
Under scheduler load the releaser goroutine can run BEFORE withTrackerLockPolicy (line 588) reaches its os.Mkdir call. When that happens Mkdir succeeds on the first attempt, retries stays at 0, and the assertion at tracker_lock_test.go:598 fails. The contention is not deterministic — it depends on the releaser losing the schedule race against the contender's Mkdir.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Add a test-only hook trackerLockContendedAttemptHook in cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go fired inside the retry loop after a real (directory-classified, not stale) failed Mkdir, just before time.Sleep(policy.step(attempt)).
2. In the test, replace the time.Sleep+RemoveAll goroutine with a hook installation that calls os.RemoveAll(lockDir) inside sync.Once on first contended attempt. This guarantees retries >= 1 before release, independent of scheduling.

NON-SCOPE
- No change to TrackerLockMetricsSink contract.
- No change to LockRetryPolicy or DefaultLockRetryPolicy.
- Other TestTrackerLock_* subtests untouched (their contention sources differ).
title: fix(agent): make TestTrackerLock_RecordsRetryCount contention deterministic

description:
PROBLEM
  Today's cost cap is ONLY a global drain-level CostCapTracker
  (cli/internal/escalation/infrastructure.go:128). There is no
  per-bead budget. A bead that fails repeatedly can burn unbounded
  budget escalating up the ladder before the global cap fires —
  one expensive bead can exhaust the entire drain's budget while
  cheap beads sit unworked.

  ADR-024 P1 (cheapest first, sister bead at rank 19) only works
  in practice if there is a per-bead "stop" condition to bound the
  escalation cost. Without it, "cheapest first" devolves into
  "cheapest first, then the most expensive thing imaginable,
  infinitely."

  Per ADR-024 Operator escape hatches subsection (sister bead
  rank 19), operators must be able to override the per-bead
  budget on a specific bead via a label budget:<USD>.

CURRENT STATE
  - cli/internal/escalation/infrastructure.go:128 CostCapTracker is
    a single drain-level accumulator.
  - cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go and
    cli/cmd/agent_execute_loop_escalation.go runEscalatingSingleTierAttempts
    do NOT instantiate per-bead trackers.
  - There's no --max-bead-cost flag.
  - There's no budget:<USD> label override mechanism.

PROPOSED FIX
  - Add a new flag --max-bead-cost (default $5; configurable):
    cli/cmd/work.go (or wherever drain flags live).
  - cli/internal/escalation/infrastructure.go: rename
    CostCapTracker to GlobalCostCapTracker (or split). Add a
    PerBeadCostTracker that takes a budget at construction.
  - cli/cmd/agent_execute_loop_escalation.go
    runEscalatingSingleTierAttempts: instantiate a
    PerBeadCostTracker per bead claim, accumulate per-attempt cost,

Skills, personas, and plugin content need to install in two distinct locations depending on operator intent:

- **install-to-agent (global)**: written under the user's agent-tier paths (e.g. ~/.claude/skills/<name>, ~/.codex/skills/<name>, or the equivalent each harness reads). After rebuilding/installing DDx at commit b98896c2c and running `systemctl --user restart ddx-server.service` on 2026-06-16, `ddx work status --json` for /Users/erik/Projects/ddx and /Users/erik/Projects/sesame reported no workers even though desired worker state was expected. Reconcile also tried stale desired projects such as /Users/erik/Projects/pqueue and /Users/erik/Projects/tablespec, which spawned throwaway exited workers. This blocks the server from being trusted as the primary worker process manager across binary upgrades and service restarts.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/server/server.go:360-381 calls reconcileDesiredWorkersAfterStartup from ListenAndServe/ListenAndServeTLS and schedules delayed passes, but the production systemd restart did not restore desired workers before manual reconcile.

- cli/cmd/worker.go:118-123 and :169-174 explicitly call POST /api/agent/workers/reconcile after worker set/start; this manual path masked the startup reconcile failure.

PROPOSED FIX
Add process-backed coverage and fix startup reconciliation so a server service restart restores desired workers without an operator running `ddx worker reconcile`. The fix should make startup reconcile observable, bounded, and stale-safe: desired entries for projects that are missing, no longer registered as valid, or repeatedly exit before producing liveness should be skipped/pruned with an audit event instead of causing noisy exited workers. Ensure `server.addr` is rewritten before clients observe a dead pid fallback during normal restart.

acceptance: work never selects `script` or `virtual` harness via tier routing (cheap/standard/smart). Explicit `--harness script` still works. Regression test covers the fallback-when-real-harnesses-fail case.
description:
## Problem

The `script` harness is a test-only sentinel (`cli/internal/agent/registry.go:127` — comment says "Binary: ddx-script-agent // sentinel — never actually exec'd") that interprets directive files for deterministic test execution. It has no LLM and cannot produce real work.

Despite being test-only, it shows up in production tier fallback chains. Observed 2026-04-17 on bead agent-ecc79bf0:

```
22:28:39  tier=cheap      harness=lmstudio  model=qwen3.5-27b    execution_failed (exec: no command)
22:28:43  tier=standard   harness=script    model=<prompt.md>    execution_failed (unknown directive "<execute-bead>")
22:28:47  tier=smart      harness=codex     model=gpt-5.4        (succeeded)
```

The `<execute-bead>` XML prompt that execute-bead emits is obviously not a valid script directive file — script's parser choked on it on the first line.

## Root cause

`cli/internal/agent/registry.go:125-132` registers `script` with:
- `CostClass: "local"`
- `IsLocal: true`

`cli/internal/agent/routing.go:scoreCandidate` rewards any `local` harness with +25 (standard profile) or +40 (cheap profile). Because script is registered as local AND always "available" (it doesn't need an LLM or network), it scores highly whenever real local harnesses (LM Studio, ollama, embedded agent) are missing or failed.

There is no filter in the routing logic that excludes `script` (or `virtual`) from execute-bead candidate selection.

## Expected behavior

`script` and `virtual` should be test-only harnesses, never selected by execute-bead / work production routing. They should only be reachable via an explicit `--harness script` / `--harness virtual` override, not via tier-based profile routing.

## Proposed fix

1. Add a `TestOnly bool` field on the registry struct (or reuse an existing negative marker).
2. Filter test-only harnesses out of the candidate list in routing.go before scoring.
3. Keep explicit opt-in (`--harness script`) working so the existing script tests still pass.
4. Add a regression test that work never selects script/virtual when real harnesses are unavailable.

## Files likely touched
- cli/internal/agent/registry.go — add TestOnly flag
- cli/internal/agent/routing.go — filter TestOnly before scoring
- cli/internal/agent/routing_test.go — regression test
title: bug: script test-harness leaks into production tier fallback chain

acceptance: A single per-project land coordinator goroutine owns all writes to target refs. Unit tests in cli/internal/agent/ (or cli/internal/server/) prove: (1) happy path — worker submits base=A result=B, coordinator fetches current tip X, rebases B onto X, fast-forwards, asserts the new tip is the rebased commit and no merge commits exist in the history between A and the new tip (use git log --merges --count to assert 0); (2) rebase conflict path — worker submits a commit that cannot rebase cleanly, coordinator preserves the submission under refs/ddx/iterations/<bead-id>/<attempt-id> and returns a "preserved" status, target branch is unchanged; (3) serialization path — 5 concurrent submissions against the same project against base=A produce 5 sequential rebased commits on the target branch with linear history (git log --merges returns 0), and the coordinator processes them in order; (4) server runWorker integration — a server-managed worker whose task produces a commit B actually advances the target branch to a rebased B, via the coordinator path, visible in git log main -1 after the worker exits; (5) --local mode integration — the --local work path runs a process-local coordinator that provides the same semantics. Secondary acceptance: RealOrchestratorGitOps.Merge is deleted from execute_bead_orchestrator.go OR clearly marked as the legacy path to remove; no production code path calls git merge --no-edit on the target branch; FEAT-006, API-001, FEAT-012 still describe the same contract (rebase + ff-only, linear history). Operator-visible smoke: running ddx agent work --harness claude --model sonnet against a seeded queue produces a linear history on main with no merge commits between the run's first and last commit.
description:
Today's work orchestration is a pile of patches on a flawed mental model. The user's target model is "human picks PR off the queue → rebases onto current tip → merges → next worker starts from the new tip." The code implements "worker branches off whatever main was when it started → runs task → git merge --no-edit that result back → 2-parent merge commit fan." The two models are incompatible; no patch to the second model gets you to the first.

Evidence the current model is wrong:

1. FEAT-006 §"Landing" (line 414), API-001 §"Landing & Preservation" (lines 217-222), and FEAT-012 §"Execute-Bead Git Operations" (line 413) all explicitly require rebase + fast-forward with linear history. The code in cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_orchestrator.go:61 Merge() runs `git merge --no-edit` with a defensive `chore: checkpoint before merge` commit — zero rebase, zero ff-only, zero fetch, zero push. Three spec files aligned on one model; code implements a different one.

2. cli/internal/server/workers.go:runWorker (around line 237) calls agent.ExecuteBead via an inline ExecuteBeadExecutorFunc closure at workers.go:248 and never calls LandBeadResult. LandBeadResult is only wired into two call sites: cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go:1372 (the `--local` work path) and cli/cmd/agent_execute_bead.go:134 (the interactive single-bead CLI). The default `ddx agent work` path (which submits to the server) produces worker commits that are NEVER landed on main. Commits sit in worktree refs and the loop reports "success" to the tracker anyway.

3. The "worker simplification" commit 49c3d2b that closed ddx-679d2fc7 moved Merge/UpdateRef out of execute_bead.go's GitOps interface into a new OrchestratorGitOps in execute_bead_orchestrator.go. That is a code-level function split, not a process-level split. The "parent orchestrator" runs synchronously in the worker process from whichever call site reaches it first. Two workers racing on the same projectRoot will both call LandBeadResult with stale baseRev assumptions; the current Merge implementation papers over conflicts with ort-strategy merge commits. The user was explicit in their feedback: "we may not be separating concerns appropriately — we have pushed too much functionality into work and it's causing us issues; it needs to be very simple: 'I've been handed a worktree and a task, I will execute that task and make commits, produce progress output, notify done.'" The current code does not reflect that intent.

4. Six open child beads of ddx-b7ee0d6f (bd42f640 fetch-before-claim, 6aa50e57 rebase-instead-of-merge, 83ec1430 push-on-land, 2791dc4f tracker concurrency, 42dd982c divergence monitoring, b0374901 multi-machine docs) each correctly identify one piece of the gap but do not compose into a coherent end-to-end workflow. The fix is not "implement all six"; the fix is to adopt the human-PR model as the single source of truth and then let those beads fall out as sub-tasks of a coherent design.

## Target design

The human-PR mental model, encoded as code:

1. **Worker.** Accepts a pre-made worktree and a prompt. Runs the agent harness. Emits structured progress events. Produces zero or more commits in the worktree. Exits with a simple terminal status (task_succeeded / task_failed / task_no_changes) and reports its worktree branch + commit SHAs to the server. The worker NEVER fetches, rebases, merges, pushes, or writes a ref. The worker NEVER interacts with target refs on the shared project repo. The worker does not care what main is doing.

2. **Land coordinator.** A single goroutine per project (hosted on the ddx server) that owns all writes to the project's target refs. Workers submit their completed worktree branch SHAs to the coordinator via a server endpoint. The coordinator, for each submission, in order: (a) `git fetch origin <target-branch>` to refresh the target tip; (b) `git rebase --onto <target-tip> <base-rev> <result-rev>` to replay the worker's commits onto the latest tip; (c) if the rebase is clean, `git push --ff-only origin <target-branch>` (or equivalent local update-ref if no remote); (d) on rebase conflict or push rejection, move the submission to `refs/ddx/iterations/<bead-id>/<attempt-id>` and mark the bead as needing human review. The coordinator handles one submission at a time. No locks needed internally because there's only one goroutine.

3. **Worker-to-coordinator handoff.** Workers submit to a new `POST /api/agent/workers/:id/land-submission` endpoint with {worktree_branch, base_rev, result_rev, bead_id}. The endpoint enqueues the submission onto the land coordinator's channel and returns 202 Accepted. Workers block (via long-polling GET, SSE, or channel-await) for the land result — success (pushed to target), preserved (moved to iteration ref), or failed (rejected, worker should retry from new tip).

4. **Worker isolation.** Workers run in /tmp/ddx-exec-wt/ worktrees per the alpha14 worktree-relocation fix. They fetch their starting base from the coordinator ("what is the current tip?"), branch off it, work, and submit. They never touch the shared project .git beyond their own worktree's read-fetch.

5. **Tracker (beads.jsonl) coordination.** Separate concern from the git target refs. ddx-2791dc4f stays as its own bead because the tracker is a second shared resource with its own write-serialization requirement. The land coordinator and the tracker lock must both be respected, but they are orthogonal locks.

6. **Multi-machine.** When the server grows to multi-machine topology, each machine runs its own land coordinator against its local clone of the project. Coordinators push to a common origin. The origin becomes the single source of truth for the target branch. Rebase-then-push gives the per-machine coordinators a clean serialization point via origin's ref update (push is atomic at the remote).

## What this replaces

- ddx-bd42f640 (fetch+ancestry check before claim) → subsumed. The land coordinator owns the fetch; workers don't need to check ancestry because they're handed a branch from the coordinator.
- ddx-6aa50e57 (rebase instead of merge) → subsumed. The coordinator's rebase step is the canonical implementation.
- ddx-83ec1430 (push-to-origin on landing) → subsumed. Push is part of the coordinator's sequence.
- ddx-42dd982c (divergence monitoring) → reframed. Becomes monitoring of the coordinator's rejection rate and conflict rate.
- ddx-b0374901 (multi-machine topology docs) → reframed. Document the per-machine coordinator + push-to-origin model.
- The missing "server runWorker never lands" bug (new P0 child, filed alongside) → subsumed. The new model HAS a land step by design.

What this does NOT replace:

- ddx-2791dc4f (beads.jsonl concurrent-write safety) — separate concern, separate lock.
- ddx-679d2fc7 (simplify worker to task-only) — this bead is nominally closed by commit 49c3d2b, but that commit did a cosmetic function split, not the architectural process split. Re-open or file a follow-up that cleans up the nomenclature ("OrchestratorGitOps" → "CoordinatorGitOps" scoped to the single coordinator goroutine) and deletes Merge() in favor of Land(). OR leave it closed and track that cleanup under this meta-bead.

## Why this is better

The core insight: **target-ref writes must be serialized through a single writer that always sees the current tip.** That is how every real PR queue works (GitHub merge queue, gerrit, Zuul). The current design has every worker trying to be its own merge-master; the fix is to have exactly one merge-master per project and let workers be contributors.

## Rollout

This is a redesign, not a patch. Rollout steps:

1. Land a new Land(projectRoot, baseRev, resultRev, targetBranch) coordinator function that implements fetch → rebase → ff-push → preserve-on-fail. Unit tests that cover the happy path, the rebase conflict path, and the concurrent-submission serialization path.
2. Add POST /api/agent/workers/:id/land-submission + the land coordinator goroutine + per-project queue channel to cli/internal/server/workers.go.
3. Rewrite workers.go:runWorker to have the worker's executor closure submit to the local coordinator (via channel; no HTTP round-trip needed since it's in the same process) instead of calling LandBeadResult inline.
4. Delete or mothball the current LandBeadResult and its "orchestrator" naming. The new coordinator replaces it.
5. Leave --local mode working by having it instantiate a process-local single-goroutine coordinator at startup. --local remains useful for single-bead debugging.
6. Add a --coordinator-only server mode for the multi-machine eventual topology (out of scope for the first cut; reference ddx-e2f497c3 for the design).

Out of scope for this bead (but related):

- Interactive conflict resolution UI. The meta-bead says "preserve under refs/ddx/iterations/" and move on; a separate UI flow for human merge-conflict resolution is its own work.
- Cross-machine coordinators talking to each other. Out of scope; origin push suffices.
- PR approval / review gates before the coordinator lands. Separate feature.
title: work: adopt human-PR landing model end-to-end (meta redesign)

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-c191e91a is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
DDx-managed filesystem state accumulates indefinitely. On the Fizeau project (sibling repo, /Users/erik/Projects/fizeau) on 2026-05-14:
- /var/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/ contained 9,735 inodes across ~9700+ directories. Many were .execute-bead-wt-* worktrees dating back to 2026-05-07 (a week stale). Each is a full repo checkout, multiplying repo size on disk.
- .ddx/workers/ held 35 agent-loop-<nano-id>/ directories. Most show last_activity_at older than 1 hour with no live process. They keep persisting per-attempt status.json entries.
- .ddx/executions/ held 44 attempt directories. Some have unmerged result.json state (a previous merge or worker crash left them in DU). No automatic GC.
- .ddx/attachments/ holds 355 per-bead artifact directories. They flood `git status` as untracked since nothing gitignores them.

ROOT CAUSE
- `ddx try` creates a worktree under `/var/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-<bead>-<timestamp>-<hash>/` and only sometimes cleans up. Failure paths (worktree_lost, execution_failed, process crash) consistently leave the worktree behind. There's no startup reaper for stale worktrees.
- `ddx work` and `ddx try` write a worker status.json under .ddx/workers/agent-loop-<nano-id>/ and the writer is responsible for cleanup. Process crashes leave the directory behind; no startup reaper claims them.
- .ddx/executions/<timestamp>/ is meant to be retained as evidence (per CONTRACT-003 / FEAT-010 evidence pile). But there's no retention policy: directories accumulate forever. Some land in unmerged git state after partial commits.
- .ddx/attachments/ and .ddx/run-state*.json are written by every ddx invocation, but the project's .gitignore policy for them is inconsistent (.ddx/executions is ignored; .ddx/attachments and .ddx/run-state.json appear in `git status` constantly).

PROPOSED FIX
1. Add a startup reaper to `ddx work` and `ddx try`: on launch, scan /var/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/, identify worktrees whose parent ddx-try/ddx-work process is dead (no PID match), `git worktree remove` + `rm -rf` them. Bound the scan to N=200 per launch so a cold start doesn't take forever. Configurable via DDX_WORKTREE_REAP_MAX_AGE (default 72h).
2. Add a startup reaper for `.ddx/workers/agent-loop-*/`: read status.json's `pid` and `last_activity_at`; if pid is gone OR activity > 30 min stale, remove the directory.
3. Add a configurable execution-evidence retention policy:
...[truncated]

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- TestWorkStartup_ReapsStaleWorkerDirs asserts that .ddx/workers/agent-loop-*/ directories whose status.json shows pid=dead or last_activity_at > 30 min stale are removed at startup.
- TestExecutionsRetention_ArchivesOldEvidence asserts that .ddx/executions/<timestamp>/ entries older than DDX_EXECUTION_RETAIN_DAYS are moved under .ddx/executions-archive/<year>/<month>/ (or deleted if DDX_EXECUTION_RETAIN_DAYS=0).
- `ddx doctor` reports the count of stale worktrees, worker dirs, and execution dirs without making changes. `ddx doctor --apply` runs the reaper paths.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.
title: housekeeping: reap orphan ddx worktrees and stale worker/execution state: part 2

acceptance:
**User story:** As an operator using a browser — on a machine without a terminal, or a phone, or a laptop away from my dev box — I can open my project's home page, type a prompt into a chat pane, and see the DDx agent work on it in real time. Tool calls stream as they happen, costs accrue visibly, and the conversation persists so I can come back to it.

**Acceptance criteria (written for Option A; rewrite if design note chooses B/C/D):**

1. **Design note landed.** One-pager in `docs/helix/02-design/` records the chosen option, the answers to the six subsidiary questions, and the message/thread schema. Implementation PR links to it.

2. **Thread model.** Chat threads persist under `.ddx/chat/<thread-id>/{manifest.json,messages.jsonl}`. One thread per project per operator by default; operators can create named threads. Messages.jsonl is append-only, one JSON object per message (user or assistant), with `sessionId` linking each assistant turn back to an entry in the sessions index (`ddx-2ceb02fa`).

3. **GraphQL surface.** New resolvers:
   - Query: `chatThreads(projectId)`, `chatThread(id)`, `chatMessages(threadId, since?)`.
   - Mutation: `chatThreadCreate(projectId, title?)`, `chatSend(threadId, message, harness?, profile?)` → kicks off a session via `service.Execute`.
   - Subscription: `chatStream(threadId)` → emits assistant message chunks + tool call events (same event vocabulary as `workers.recentEvents`).

4. **Home page UI.** Project home page gains a chat pane below the actions section. Pane shows thread list, active thread messages, input box, harness/profile picker. Tool calls render inline within assistant messages. Streaming updates as chunks arrive.

5. **Session linkage.** Each assistant turn creates one session in the sessions index. Clicking an assistant message shows the session id and a link to the session detail (`/sessions/<id>`). Chat thread header shows cumulative session count + total cost for the thread.

6. **Concurrency.** Two browsers open on the same thread see each other's messages within 2s (subscription-driven). Two operators on different threads in the same project do not interfere.

7. **Interrupt.** The in-flight assistant turn can be cancelled via a Stop button; server sends the harness the equivalent of `ddx agent workers stop <id>` for the in-flight session. The thread records a cancelled turn, does not try to auto-resume.

8. **Cost guardrail (soft).** If the cumulative thread cost passes a configurable ceiling (`.ddx/config.yaml: chat.cost_ceiling_usd`, default unset), the UI warns but does not block. Hard block is a follow-up.

9. **Auth posture.**
   - Per design note. If the chosen posture is "single-operator localhost / tsnet only for v1," the chat routes are served unauthenticated behind tsnet and the design note records the gap to close before broader deployment.
   - A small middleware gate is in place even for v1 so adding auth later is schema-local, not route-local.

10. **Playwright e2e.**
    - Seeds a project with zero chat threads.
    - Navigates to project home, asserts the chat pane renders with "Start a new thread" affordance.
    - Starts a thread, sends a short prompt, simulates a streamed session response with one tool call, asserts chunks appear in order and the session id link is present.
    - Opens a second browser context on the same thread, asserts both see new messages within 2s.
    - Cancels an in-flight turn, asserts the cancelled state is persisted.

11. **Depends on.**
    - `ddx-2513f08c` (home page reachable from sidebar) — hard dependency.
    - `ddx-2ceb02fa` (sessions index) — hard dependency for the session linkage + cost rollup.

12. **Explicitly deferred.** PTY integration (Option B / pop-out terminal from Option C) is its own bead, filed only if the Option A rollout surfaces real interactive-steering needs.
description:
## Observed / Motivation

User wants to "lift work out of the TUI entirely and allow non-tmux users to work remotely." Today the only way to prompt the DDx agent stack interactively is a terminal session. The web UI is read-mostly: dispatch three actions (drain/align/checks) and review results. There is no surface that lets an operator say "go do X" against the project in natural language from a browser.

Related UX: the project home page already exists (`/nodes/.../projects/<id>/`), renders queue summary + actions, and is the natural host for a chat affordance. First the home page needs to be reachable from the sidebar (`ddx-2513f08c`) — this bead depends on that work.

## The tension

The DDx harness abstraction (`cli/internal/agent/service_run.go`, `service.Execute`) is designed for **non-interactive** use: prompt in, structured result out, optional streaming. This is the right shape for queue-draining, quorum, evaluation, and automation. It is **not** the shape of a TUI conversation with tab completion, mid-run steering, and back-channel signals.

An operator-facing chat can land on either side of that line. The bead records all four options so the design phase can pick one deliberately.

## Options (design phase decides, recommended path noted)

### Option A — Chat over the harness abstraction (RECOMMENDED starting point)

- Chat UI posts a prompt → server dispatches a session via `service.Execute` (or a wrapper) → streams tool calls + response chunks back over a GraphQL subscription.
- Message history is persisted as a thread; each user turn = one new session. Responses reuse the existing `recentEvents` stream shape already used on the workers detail page.
- Works with every harness today because the harness abstraction is what it is. claude, codex, agent (embedded) all participate.
- **Trade-off:** no mid-run steering, no tab completion, no live back-and-forth inside one agent invocation.
- Matches the user's stated target audience (non-TUI users who want remote browser access). Those users aren't trying to steer a TUI — they're trying to leave it behind.

### Option B — PTY gateway per harness

- Server owns a PTY pool. Each chat thread attaches to one harness process (claude/codex/etc.) over a WebSocket; browser renders xterm.js.
- Full interactivity, including TUI steering.
- **Trade-off:** PTY lifecycle, auth, resource limits, tab-close-loses-session semantics, multi-user access control — all real. The harness abstraction is bypassed for this mode, which creates a second execution path to maintain.

### Option C — Hybrid (chat-first + pop-out terminal)

- Option A is the primary surface. When a chat reaches a point that needs interactive steering, a "Open terminal" escape hatch attaches a PTY to the current harness session.
- **Trade-off:** more surface area, but honest about both use cases. Most sessions stay on the cheap path.

### Option D — Web-tmux / ttyd wrapper

- Embed the existing terminal tooling directly: ttyd or xterm.js over a tmux socket owned by the server.
- **Trade-off:** fastest to ship, zero harness work, but the UX is a terminal in a browser — not "chat." Requires tmux. Doesn't serve the stated "non-tmux users" audience.

### Recommendation

Start with **A**. If the design note documents real interactive-steering needs we can't paper over, the right follow-up is **C** (A + PTY escape hatch), not B (PTY-only).

## Scope of this bead

- Design note in `docs/helix/02-design/` locking the option, the message schema, persistence model, and auth posture. Implementation PR links to it.
- First implementation pass: Option A.
- Home page gains a chat pane as its primary interaction surface, alongside the existing queue summary + actions (which stay — they're quick-dispatch affordances, not replaced by chat).

## Subsidiary questions the design note must answer

1. **Message persistence.** Are chat threads per-project or per-user? Stored where (`.ddx/chat/<thread-id>/` or elsewhere)? Is history shared across operators on the same project, or isolated per operator identity?
2. **Harness selection.** Does the chat pick a harness per-thread (picker in the UI) or per-message (re-route each turn)? Default to profile-based selection?
3. **Cost accountability.** Every chat message spawns a session. Sessions are already tracked in the sessions index (`ddx-2ceb02fa`). The chat thread should surface cumulative cost to the operator so they don't blow budget unknowingly.
4. **Tool execution scope.** Chat prompts will trigger agent tool calls that read/write the project tree. Is the chat session bounded to the same permissions as `ddx agent run`? Does it run in the project worktree, a worktree per thread, a scratch dir? Default safe answer: same worktree as `ddx agent run` (user trusts ddx running anyway), but design note records it.
5. **Concurrency.** What happens if two operators have the chat open on the same project and both send messages? Default: independent threads, each with its own session — no shared state.
6. **Auth.** Today the server assumes single-operator localhost. Remote use implies some identity concept. Design note picks a posture: delegate to reverse proxy, ship a simple token, or punt and require tsnet + single-operator for v1.

## Out of scope

- Full PTY implementation (Option B). Follow-up bead if A+hybrid doesn't suffice.
- Cross-project chat.
- Voice input.
title: Add chat interface to project home page: prompt ddx remotely without the TUI

description:
PROBLEM
The release workflow advertises manual tag dispatch but ignores its tag input, and contributor guidance points to a deleted release skill instead of a durable checklist. A tag-push release works, but the alternative entry point can build/release the wrong ref and the repository has no checked-in operator proof contract for the nine expected assets and post-release smoke checks.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- .github/workflows/release.yml:7-12 accepts workflow_dispatch.inputs.tag, but lines 35-54 and 324-337 read github.ref_name; manual dispatch from main validates, builds, names, and links the branch rather than the requested tag. Checkout steps also omit the requested ref and build metadata uses github.sha instead of the resolved tag commit.
- CONTRIBUTING.md:138-149 directs operators to nonexistent .ddx/skills/ddx-release/SKILL.md and /ddx-release.
- docs/helix/02-design/solution-designs/SD-007-release-readiness.md:174-186 requires a repository release checklist covering tag, CI, artifacts, site, and installer verification, but no current checklist exists.

PROPOSED FIX
Resolve one immutable release tag and commit for both tag-push and manual-dispatch events. Propagate that value through every checkout, version, changelog, build metadata, prerelease decision, release tag/name, and final URL. Add structural tests that fail if any release consumer falls back to github.ref_name/github.sha for release identity. Add docs/releasing.md with pre-tag gates, annotated tag/push, expected four archives + four sidecars + aggregate checksum, workflow/release verification, checksum and binary-version smoke checks, prerelease installer behavior, evidence fields, and rollback/no-history-rewrite rules. Point CONTRIBUTING.md at that checklist.

NON-SCOPE
Do not claim bit-reproducible artifacts while Bun, runner images, actions, and timestamps remain floating; do not pin those dependencies in this bead, change release asset formats, publish a tag, rewrite an existing tag, or bypass the full Go/pre-commit/release workflow gates.

PARENT
None; release infrastructure repair discovered during alpha105 audit.

DEPS
ddx-305e8ddb, which establishes the verified frontend artifact consumed by this workflow.
title: release: make tag identity and operator proof checklist truthful

description:
PROBLEM
A `no_changes_rationale.txt` with `verification_command:` can time out, leave its child process tree running, and let `ddx work --watch` move on to another bead while the old verification is still consuming the project. Live reproduction on 2026-05-15 in `/Users/erik/Projects/fizeau`: `fizeau-bc9586d7` returned `verification_command: sh -lc "go test ... && lefthook run pre-commit"`; the watcher logged `• fizeau-bc9586d7 → no_changes` and started `fizeau-7af3f548` at 13:07:21Z, while `ps` still showed orphaned PID 3510889 (`sh -lc go test ...`) and child PID 3512539 (`go test ./... -count=1`) under PPID 1.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
`cli/internal/agent/try/no_changes.go:117-128` hard-codes `DefaultVerificationCommandTimeout = 60 * time.Second` and runs the command with `exec.CommandContext(cctx, "/bin/sh", "-c", command)`. `exec.CommandContext` kills only the direct shell on timeout; because workers commonly emit nested shell commands such as `sh -lc "go test ..."`, the actual test process survives as an orphan. The 60s timeout is also shorter than normal bead acceptance gates like `go test ./...` plus `lefthook run pre-commit`, so legitimate already-satisfied checks are classified as unverified/no-progress instead of closing the bead.

PROPOSED FIX
Run no_changes verification commands with the same process-tree discipline used by agent executors: start the shell in its own process group on Unix, terminate the group on timeout/cancel, and wait/reap before returning. Replace the hard-coded 60s ceiling with a worker/config-derived timeout that is long enough for normal acceptance gates, or make it configurable with a conservative default. Preserve the contract: exit 0 closes as `already_satisfied`; non-zero/timeout keeps the bead open with clear `no_changes_unverified` evidence.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken no_changes verification semantics. Do not let verification run asynchronously. Do not close a bead without a passing command. Do not change readiness classification or route selection.
title: work: reap and correctly budget no_changes verification commands

ddx-6036e1bc is framed as status/catalog evidence, but its acceptance also mentions a helper that selects thresholds for the retry policy. That overlaps with ddx-67ed1062 and risks turning status display into policy logic.
