description:
PROBLEM
On provider_connectivity failure, applyProviderConnectivityRouteExclusion calls nextFloorFn(actualPower). When the configured power ladder has no step above actualPower (common when the local config exposes only cheap-tier providers), nextFloorFn returns powerladder.ErrLadderExhausted. The current code silently swallows that error and does NOT set b.Extra[TriagePowerHintKey]. As a result the next claim sees no hint, the routing intent re-derives "cheap", and the same dead (provider, model) is selected again. The failed-route list is appended to but never consulted by Fizeau, so it has no effect on the next decision. A drain in this state attempts each bead once, times out for ~2m45s in Fizeau retries, gets the same provider_connectivity outcome, and bottoms out at 100% failures with no escalation ever taking effect. Reproduces exactly when local LM Studio hosts (bragi/grendel) are unreachable: every bead routes to power=5 cheap models, fails, retry-after expires 15min later, re-routes to the same model, fails again.

ROOT CAUSE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3862-3866 in applyProviderConnectivityRouteExclusion:
    nextFloor, err := nextFloorFn(report.ActualPower)
    if err != nil {
        return
    }
    b.Extra[TriagePowerHintKey] = nextFloor

The early return swallows ErrLadderExhausted. The same silent-swallow pattern also lives in applyNoChangesSmartRetry (execute_bead_loop.go:3454) and applyRepairCycleExhaustedEscalation (execute_bead_loop.go:3497). The bead-event log gets a route-failure entry but no operator-visible signal that escalation aborted.

PROPOSED FIX
- When nextFloorFn returns ErrLadderExhausted (or any error), emit a kind=execution-escalation-aborted event with a summary naming the failed (provider, model, actualPower) and the reason "ladder exhausted at power N".
- Set TriagePowerHintKey to actualPower+1 anyway (or to a sentinel >=actualPower+1) so the next route decision at least knows "anything but the failed tier" — this is a no-op for routers that ignore the hint, but it gives clear signal to Fizeau-side exclusion honoring (separate bead).
- After 2 consecutive provider_connectivity failures on the SAME (provider, model), promote the bead's outcome to operator_required with a clear message ("provider X / model Y unreachable on 2+ attempts; check ddx config or provider health") so the queue does not silently re-loop forever.
- Apply the same change to applyNoChangesSmartRetry and applyRepairCycleExhaustedEscalation so all three escalation paths surface ladder exhaustion uniformly.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change Fizeau-side routing exclusion (separate bead in upstream repo).
- Do not introduce a new bead status; reuse open/blocked/operator_required.
- Do not auto-edit operator config; just signal clearly.

DEPS
None.
title: work: surface and act on ladder-exhausted escalation instead of silently no-op'ing

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-130cf9ab is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-e19185aa is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
The decomposition action (currently invoked when a bead is too large for one execution and the agent splits it into child beads) is writing the parent's ID as a dep edge on every child. This produces an unbreakable deadlock:

  e29892a4 (parent, open) -- parent --> child_A
  e29892a4 -- parent --> child_B
  child_A.deps = [e29892a4]           <- BAD: parent is also a dep
  child_B.deps = [child_A, e29892a4]  <- BAD

The parent stays open until its children close. Every child is blocked on the parent. Nothing can be claimed. ddx work loops on the parent, the orchestrator emits 'mixed_commit_and_no_changes_rationale', the worker retries, and burns claim budget without progress.

Observed scenario (niflheim, 2026-06-04 04:30-05:13 UTC):
- Parent: niflheim-e29892a4 ('feat(delta): async write-behind ...')
- 10 children created during planning loops (23223661, a44a8ceb, 054c89b7, 0470ba0d, f10e9e35, f076b08c, 6c041162, 94e1df73, 9da62c2d, 5e4f9fb2)
- Every child carried deps=[..siblings.., niflheim-e29892a4]
- ~50 minutes of agent time + 4 strong-policy claude/opus attempts with zero feature commits; only tracker chores
- Unwedged manually by closing the parent via 'ddx bead close', after which siblings drained correctly in foundational order

Root cause is structural, not model-capability — auto-upgrading to a stronger model does NOT fix this. The orchestrator already detects the no-progress state but its only remediation is 'retry parent', which re-enters the same loop.

There is also a 'project root mutation rejected (continuing)' warning emitted by the readiness check during this state; that's a downstream symptom of the same problem, not the cause.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- Programmatic decomposition path (the action that fans a too-large bead into children) MUST NOT add the parent as a dep. Existing action templates / system prompts are audited and amended; one golden e2e test (decompose_does_not_self_dep) creates a bead with N children and asserts every child's deps set excludes the parent.
- 'ddx bead doctor' (existing subcommand) gains a check 'parent_ancestor_in_deps' that scans the tracker, lists violating beads, and (with --fix) removes the offending edges. Output is stable / scriptable.
...[truncated]

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- 'ddx bead doctor' (existing subcommand) gains a check 'parent_ancestor_in_deps' that scans the tracker, lists violating beads, and (with --fix) removes the offending edges. Output is stable / scriptable. Test: ddx_doctor_detects_and_repairs_back_edge.
- ddx work no-progress remediation: when an attempted bead's outcome is 'mixed_commit_and_no_changes_rationale' AND any freshly-created child carries the attempted bead in its deps, ddx auto-emits an 'operator_attention' event with reason 'parent_back_edge' and stops re-claiming that bead. (Today it loops indefinitely.) Test: ddx_work_halts_on_parent_back_edge.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

description:
PROBLEM
The release workflow derives changelog history from the nearest local tag, not the previous published GitHub Release. Tags v0.6.2-alpha103 and v0.6.2-alpha104 exist but have no published releases, while v0.6.2-alpha102 is the latest published release. An alpha105 changelog based on alpha104 would silently omit every unpublished alpha103/alpha104 commit from user-visible notes.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
.github/workflows/release.yml:71-80 runs git describe --tags --abbrev=0 on the release parent and exports that tag as previous_tag without checking GitHub Release publication. .github/workflows/release.yml:288-299 then logs only PREVIOUS_TAG..RELEASE_COMMIT. cli/internal/server/release_workflow_test.go:143-161 asserts immutable release identity and the range endpoint but does not exercise a repository containing unpublished intervening tags.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add a deterministic baseline selector used by release.yml that chooses the newest published, non-draft GitHub Release tag reachable from RELEASE_COMMIT; for alpha105 the current evidence requires v0.6.2-alpha102.
- If GitHub Release metadata is unavailable, fail closed or choose a documented deterministic range that includes all commits since the last provably published release; never silently use the nearest tag.
- Put selection/range logic in a testable script or helper and keep RELEASE_COMMIT as the immutable upper bound.
- Add hermetic tests with local commits/tags alpha102 through alpha105 and injected/stubbed release metadata; tests must not call the network.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not publish alpha103 or alpha104 retroactively.
- Do not change tag identity, artifact build inputs, prerelease classification, or release asset naming.
- Do not infer publication from tag existence alone.

PARENT
None; this is a root alpha105 release-correctness blocker.

DEPS
ddx-8976c5cc must remain closed because it establishes immutable tag identity and release proof. No alpha105 release bead exists as of filing.

description:
PROBLEM
`ddx bead status` can report `In progress: 0` while `ddx work status` and `ddx work focus` show active workers currently running beads. In the current project state on 2026-06-08, `ddx bead status --json` reports `"in_progress": 0`, while `ddx work status --json` reports three live workers on beads `ddx-a509613d`, `ddx-e9542e0d`, and `ddx-9b78b617`. Operators asking "how many workers are running and what are they doing?" get contradictory answers depending on which status surface they use.

ROOT CAUSE
`cli/internal/bead/store.go:2768` implements `Store.Status()` as persisted lifecycle counts only; `cli/internal/bead/store.go:2817-2823` increments `InProgress` only when `b.Status == StatusInProgress`. `cli/cmd/bead.go:1689-1705` prints that raw lifecycle count as `In progress`, so active work represented by fresh worker sidecars or fresh claim/run-state data is invisible. Meanwhile `cli/cmd/work_status.go:83-96` scans live worker data and enriches it with fresh liveness/run-state, and `cli/cmd/work_focus.go:157-166` separately treats fresh `.ddx/workers/<id>/status.json` sidecars as active capacity. `cli/internal/workerstatus/liveness.go:14-20` documents that sidecar as the operator-facing answer to "is the worker alive and what is it doing?" The GraphQL queue summary already has a partial precedent at `cli/internal/server/graphql/resolver_feat008.go:298-315`, where it adds in-flight attempts to the lifecycle in-progress count.

PROPOSED FIX
Create a shared active-work snapshot/helper for project-scoped status surfaces that reconciles persisted lifecycle state, fresh worker liveness sidecars, and fresh run-state/claim data. Update `ddx bead status` text and `--json`, `ddx work focus`, and any queue-summary resolver that exposes the same concept so they agree on active worker count, bead IDs, attempt IDs, phase, and freshness rules. The CLI output must make the distinction explicit if lifecycle `status == in_progress` is still shown separately: lifecycle count and active worker/fresh-claim count must not both be labeled simply as "In progress".

NON-SCOPE
- Do not count stale/dead worker sidecars or expired claims as active.
- Do not scan global processes outside the selected project root except through existing `ddx work status --all-projects` behavior.
- Do not redesign the worker scheduler or worker concurrency model.
- Do not change claim/release lifecycle semantics unless the regression tests prove an active claim is incorrectly being left as `StatusOpen`; if so, fix that narrowly and preserve child-bead workability.
- Do not make closing/decomposed parent beads block their children. If a decomposed bead is tracked as a parent and is completed/closed, children must remain execution-eligible according to their own dependencies and readiness.
title: status: reconcile active worker counts across bead status and work views

description:
PROBLEM
In watch mode, an idle `ddx work` process should explain why it is sleeping and what queue state remains on each idle poll. Current behavior only emits an internal `loop.idle` progress signal and leaves human stdout without enough context. When new work later appears, the next bead can start abruptly after an idle period without a visible transition.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:656-688 emits `loop.idle` and sleeps, but it does not print a human idle line with queue-state context.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:689-699 clears idle state on `loop.active`, but it does not separate the next bead block from the prior idle block or announce the bead selected from the queue.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:722-737 currently owns direct bead header logging; the scoped renderer introduced by ddx-55900861 should own the human transition lines.
- ddx-7dcbd40b will expose the queue snapshot and human-review blocker pressure that this renderer needs.

PROPOSED FIX
Render watch-mode idle and wake transitions through the scoped work-log renderer:
- On every idle poll where no execution-ready bead exists, print a concise line such as `HH:MM:SS idle: no execution-ready beads; sleeping 30s`.
- Every idle poll line must include compact queue-state counts: execution-ready count, blocked count, needs-human count, cooldown/deferred count with next retry when known, and other non-executable buckets available in the queue snapshot.
- If open work is transitively blocked behind human-review blockers, include a sentence such as `30 beads blocked behind 3 needs-human blockers:` followed by numbered blocker entries with ID, title, and downstream blocked count.
- The full numbered blocker list may be rate-limited when unchanged, but the compact counts and the total `N beads blocked behind M needs-human blockers` summary must remain visible on every idle poll.
- Cap very long blocker lists with an explicit `and N more` suffix, but do not omit all blocker IDs when the list is short.
- When watch mode later finds work after an idle period, print a blank line and `taking next ready bead from queue: <id> — <title>` before the bead header/block starts.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go
- cli/internal/agent/work_log_renderer.go
- cli/internal/agent/work_log_renderer_test.go or execute_bead_loop stdout tests

NON-SCOPE
- Do not implement the queue snapshot fields; ddx-7dcbd40b owns them.
- Do not change server worker state/substate semantics beyond preserving the existing `loop.idle` / `loop.active` progress signals.
- Do not change queue selection, readiness, retry, or cost policy.
- Do not change final terminal summary output; ddx-dc300be9 owns that.

PARENT + DEPS
Parent: ddx-eeced112. Depends on ddx-7d9e1e82 (contract), ddx-55900861 (renderer), ddx-f9acb86d (watch mode), and ddx-7dcbd40b (queue snapshot).

acceptance: The design stack defines a single-project loop that watches execution-ready beads, consumes the generic DDx execution validator, executes beads in isolated worktrees, runs required post-run checks, preserves failed iterations with explicit bead/result state, lands successful runs by rebase+fast-forward, and is explicitly scoped for first release without depending on multi-project or multi-host server behavior
description:
<context-digest>
Review area: execute-bead automation and single-project worker supervision. Evidence covers FEAT-006, FEAT-010, SD-012, the execute-bead contract bead ddx-5448b39c, and the requirement to ship a tested single-project loop before broader multi-project or multi-host server work.
</context-digest>
Design the long-running single-project loop that watches for execution-ready beads and drives `ddx agent execute-bead` safely.

## Goals
1. Define a single-project loop that monitors one project queue for execution-ready beads using the generic DDx execution validator rather than HELIX-specific hidden policy
2. Define the exact state machine: claim/select bead, validate structural executability, execute in an isolated worktree, run post-run validity checks / required executions, classify outcome, and continue scanning
3. Make success and failure outcomes explicit: on failed execution or failed post-run validity checks, mark the bead/result accordingly and preserve the iteration/evidence exactly as the execute-bead contract specifies; on successful validation, land by rebase + fast-forward, reset the worker worktree to the updated branch tip, and continue
4. Keep the first shipped loop single-project scoped; do not require multi-project discovery, cross-project scheduling, or multi-host coordination in this bead
5. Define the minimal control surface for running the loop standalone or under `ddx server`, without coupling the design to later multi-project topology decisions

## Required outputs
- Single-project loop and worker state machine
- Failure/preservation semantics and retry surfaces
- Post-run validation / required-execution integration
- Minimal operator control surface and observability for the shipped loop
title: Design the single-project execute-bead loop and supervisor contract

description:
PROBLEM
DDx correctly intends to request a stronger reviewer, but today it queries Fizeau profile metadata, selects a profile, clears the primary operator envelope, and may set review-specific concrete routes. DDx must express review strength only as abstract MinPower while Fizeau independently chooses the harness, provider, model, and internal policy.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go:819-866 builds reviewer requests with HarnessOverride and ProfileOverride and clears routing pins, profile, and MaxPower.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go:869-939 calls LoadProfileSnapshot and SelectStrongestProfile or SelectStrongestProfileAbove.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go:941-949 and 1222-1248 apply review-specific model/profile pins.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go:1375-1388 turns concrete provider pairing into an escalation signal.
- cli/internal/agent/dispatch.go:70-84 and service_run.go:226-277 prove these fields reach the public Fizeau Execute request.

PROPOSED FIX
Build reviewer requests from the immutable primary-attempt operator passthrough envelope, preserved byte-for-byte including MaxPower and any explicit Harness, Provider, Model, or public Policy constraint. Add only a stronger abstract MinPower than the implementer actual power. Delete reviewer profile/catalog loading, review-specific concrete pins, implementer route correlation used as policy, and provider-pairing escalation. Keep the Fizeau-returned concrete route in execution audit evidence only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change primary-attempt difficulty mapping, reviewer cardinality, typed transport retry, gate repair, or Fizeau routing internals.

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent: ddx-b8cacbeb. Depends on ddx-666456c8 and ddx-af65a486 so review-tier and global difficulty/profile cleanup land before the overlapping reviewer request rewrite.

  applies to reconciliation closes, and the implementation diverges from the
  evidence-close path without that divergence being declared.

ROOT CAUSE
  - cli/internal/bead/store.go:1234-1257 closeWithEvidence enforces ClosureGate(b)
    before the in_progress -> closed transition. ClosureGate requires evidence
    in the form of session_id + closing_commit_sha or equivalent attachments
    per the gate's contract.
  - cli/internal/bead/reconcile.go:236-242 closes beads via
    UpdateWithLifecycleStatus(StatusClosed, {ManualClose: true, Reason, Source})
    when applyReconcilePlan sees CloseSatisfied=true, then calls
    externalizeEvents at line 252. The ClosureGate is never invoked.
  - Reconcile-close happens when all dependencies are closed and the satisfied
    work is recognised post-hoc; it has no execution session of its own.
  - TD-031 §5 (docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-031-bead-state-machine.md
    lines ~264-316) does not enumerate this path, leaving readers to infer it
    from store.go and reconcile.go.

PROPOSED FIX
  - Edit docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-031-bead-state-machine.md:
    - Add a new outcome row in §5 covering "dependency-satisfied reconcile
      close" with status transition open -> closed (via UpdateWithLifecycleStatus,
      ManualClose=true), event lifecycle_reconciled (already emitted by
      reconcile.go:227), and Extra updates clearing the listed
      work-* fields.
    - Add an explicit invariant: ClosureGate applies to evidence-bearing
      execute-bead closes (CloseWithEvidence path); reconcile-close is a
      distinct meta-close that intentionally bypasses the gate because the
      bead has no execution session and no closing_commit_sha to provide.
      The justification is that all dependencies are closed (each of which
      individually passed ClosureGate or was a meta-close itself), so the
      parent's closure inherits its evidence by reference through the
      dependency edges.
    - Reference reconcile.go:208-254 and ClosureGate at store.go:1245 by file:line.

NON-SCOPE
  - Changing the runtime behavior of reconcile.go or closeWithEvidence (B2
    handles any code-side follow-up if the spec amendment requires it).
  - Adding new ClosureGate variants or evidence types.
  - Updating ADR-023; this is purely a TD-031 §5 amendment.

INTERSECTIONS
  - ddx-ca1c66ee (epic parent).
  - B2 depends on this bead landing because the call-site comment B2 adds
    quotes the amended TD-031 invariant.
title: docs(TD-031): specify reconcile-close vs evidence-close semantics

None.

acceptance: 1. ddx classifies each outcome per the addendum table (table-driven test). 2. Exactly one middle->max escalation, only on typed genuine failure; no_changes/dirty/transport/quota/auth do NOT escalate. 3. Per-pool in-flight max-attempt cap enforced (test simulates concurrent genuine failures, asserts cap). 4. quota-exhausted -> global pool cooldown, not N per-bead mutations (test). 5. cd /Users/erik/Projects/ddx/cli && go test ./internal/agent/... green. 6. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description: Implement the ddx side of the FEAT-004 failure-classification table: ddx work maps each attempt outcome to exactly the action in the addendum table (success/already_satisfied=close; no_changes=close/unclaim NO tier-escalation; genuine impl/capability failure=escalate middle->max ONCE; dirty=clean+same-tier retry; transport=same-tier reroute; quota-exhausted=global pool cooldown; auth/setup=operator-attention; timeout=clean+retry then operator-attention; merge-conflict=unclaim+retry; max genuine failure=operator-attention). ddx owns the ONE middle->max tier escalation (per the escalation-owner decision bead fizeau-994604ec); a per-pool in-flight max-attempt cap prevents multi-worker stampede. Depends on the escalation-owner contract + the shared classifier (fizeau-44e98499).
notes:
SELF-CONTAINED SPEC (the ddx-side FEAT-004 here is Beads; the ROUTING policy lives in the fizeau repo, NOT accessible to a cold ddx agent — so the normative failure-classification table is inlined below; implement against THIS, do not look for a ddx FEAT-004 routing addendum):

Map each ddx-work attempt outcome to exactly one action:
- success / already_satisfied -> close bead
- no_changes (agent produced nothing + rationale) -> close or unclaim per rationale; do NOT escalate tier
- genuine implementation/capability failure (tests fail after real work; AC unmet) -> escalate middle->max ONCE
- dirty worktree / partial write -> clean/reset worktree, same-tier retry (not escalation)
- provider transport failure (i/o timeout, conn refused, 5xx) -> same-tier reroute to another dispatchable candidate; no tier change
- quota exhausted (retry_after) -> GLOBAL pool cooldown/sleep until reset; NOT per-bead mutation, not escalation
- auth/config missing, toolchain/setup failure -> operator-attention (typed bead state); do not escalate
- timeout / no-progress watchdog -> clean + same-tier retry once, then operator-attention
- merge/land conflict -> unclaim + retry later; not escalation
- max-tier genuine failure -> operator-attention (stop escalating)

operator-attention = explicit bead state transition (not a notification/indefinite wait). The single middle->max escalation owner is ddx work; a per-pool in-flight max-attempt cap prevents multi-worker stampede. Scope tests to avoid hangs (the prior attempt hit a 3m test timeout — bound any test that spawns/loops).
title: routing P1: ddx applies shared failure-classification table; single-owner one-hop middle->max escalation

description:
PROBLEM

The staged pre-commit Go hook blocks small cli/cmd changes by running the entire cmd package with race enabled, and that package currently fails on unrelated tests. During ddx-7952776a verification, `lefthook run pre-commit` invoked `scripts/lefthook-go-test.sh ./cmd/execute_loop_shared.go ./cmd/work.go ./cmd/work_resource_exhausted_test.go ./cmd/work_test.go ./cmd/zero_config_work_test.go`; the script mapped those staged files to `go test -short -race -timeout 30m ./cmd`. After fixing two provider-spawning tests, the command no longer leaked provider CLIs, but still failed on unrelated command-suite tests.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE

- `scripts/lefthook-go-test.sh:8-20` maps any staged cli/cmd file to package `cmd` and runs the full package, so unrelated cmd tests gate every small command edit.
- `cli/cmd/bead_doctor_test.go:100-101` fails under the hook with missing XDG project bead storage: `open .../xdg/ddx/projects/local/.../beads.jsonl: no such file or directory`.
- `cli/cmd/doctor_housekeeping_test.go:50-63` expects stale execution evidence counts/archive, but the hook run reports stale execution dirs=0 and leaves old evidence in place.
- `cli/cmd/skills_test.go:46-49` expects `validated 2 skill files`, but the hook run reports `validated 1 skill files`.
- `cli/cmd/update_test.go:193-197` expects `.ddx/update-backup` to exist, but the hook run fails opening that directory.
- `cli/cmd/work_durable_audit_test.go:162-163` expects dirty tracker/metrics status after durable audit commit failure, but got empty status.
- `cli/cmd/work_startup_cleanup_test.go:128-157` expects old execution evidence to archive/delete, but the hook run leaves the old evidence directory and reports zero archived/deleted dirs.

Observed earlier in the same verification: `TestWorkResourceExhaustionEndToEnd_StopsBeforeNextClaim` and `TestZeroConfigWork_NoConfigDoesNotEmitUnderSpecified` started `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/codex --no-alt-screen` through Fizeau discovery; those two tests were patched in commit 97b5ba4c8, but the broader hook still fails on the tests listed above.

PROPOSED FIX

Make the staged command hook usable as a reliable gate. Either isolate/fix the failing cmd tests so `go test -short -race -timeout 30m ./cmd` passes without provider discovery or host-specific state, or narrow `scripts/lefthook-go-test.sh` so staged-file hooks run only the affected tests/packages while a separate full-suite CI gate covers all cmd tests. Prefer fixing tests that are supposed to be hermetic.

NON-SCOPE

Do not weaken the ddx-7952776a interrupt behavior or remove its focused regression tests. Do not hide provider CLI launches; if another cmd test starts claude/codex/gemini during unit tests, stub it and add coverage that the test is hermetic.
title: cmd: make staged Go command hook hermetic and green

description:
PROBLEM
ddx work --watch can claim a bead, fail to resolve a route, and hang in the route-resolution step indefinitely. Heartbeats keep emitting (phase=running, last_activity_at advancing every 30s) but harness/model/route fields stay empty and no LLM call ever happens. The bead's lease is held but no work progresses, and the worker cannot pick up any other bead because it is single-threaded.

OBSERVATION (Fizeau, 2026-05-18 02:05–03:27 EDT)
- Worker: PID 560430 (ddx work --watch, no flags, cwd /Users/erik/Projects/fizeau).
- Claimed bead: fizeau-86f2bac0 (bench-pr-A3b) at attempt_id 20260518T020552-18b086b2.
- 80+ minutes of heartbeats logged in .ddx/agent-logs/agent-loop-1779069470069950671.jsonl, every 30s, all with phase=running, harness="", model="", route="".
- ddx bead status shows In progress: 0 — the state machine never marked it in_progress despite the lease.
- ddx bead ready returned 30 dispatchable beads — none would be picked up because the worker is single-threaded and wedged.
- Related earlier event on fizeau-856b7957: routing-intent event with routing_intent_degraded=true, routing_intent_note='actual route facts unavailable'. Strongly suggests the same wedge: route resolution returns 'no route' but the worker treats it as 'wait forever' instead of 'release bead with error'.

WHY THIS IS A BUG
1. Lease without progress: holding a lease for 80+ minutes with no LLM call, no commit, no resolved route is indistinguishable from a crashed worker, but heartbeats keep ticking so the staleness reaper (if any) never fires.
2. Single-worker starvation: 30 ready beads, one stuck worker, queue stops advancing.
3. State inconsistency: bead has a claim but bead status reports 0 in_progress, suggesting the claim and the lifecycle status are not atomically coupled.
4. No actionable error surface: the operator only learns about the wedge by tailing agent-logs and noticing the empty harness/route fields. The watch loop's stdout shows nothing because heartbeats are JSONL-only.
5. The harness for execute-bead inherits zero feedback when route resolution silently fails — even when a route eventually resolves, the wedge has stolen 80 minutes of throughput.

PROPOSED FIX
A. Route-resolution timeout: the resolution step must be bounded by a configurable timeout (default 60s). On timeout: release the lease with a structured error, mark the attempt as failed, do not retry without operator attention.
B. Progress timeout independent of heartbeats: a watchdog that fires when last_activity_at has not advanced beyond a phase-specific budget (e.g., 5 minutes in 'resolving', 30 minutes in 'running' with a harness/model set, etc.) — phase-empty heartbeats with no real work are the failure signature.
C. Lease+lifecycle atomicity: claiming a bead must atomically set status to in_progress; releasing on failure must atomically clear the claim. ddx bead status counts must reflect claimed beads.
D. Operator-visible error surface: when a worker releases a lease due to timeout or wedge detection, emit a top-level operator-attention event with bead-id, attempt-id, last-activity, and a short diagnosis. ddx bead operator-attention should surface it.
E. Worker exit on repeated wedge: if the same bead wedges twice in a row, the worker should exit (or stop claiming that bead) rather than keep eating the queue.

CROSS-REF
Filed from Fizeau session 2026-05-17/18 during the claude-tui chain rollout. Adjacent bug: ddx-57c40485 (workers hold git index.lock for minutes). Both bugs share root cause: long-running operations inside the worker without bounded timeouts or operator-visible failure modes.

title: worker wedges on route resolution without timeout; no progress and no release for hours
work-smart-retry-reason: ddx-8f2e0ebf is feature-sized (6 acceptance criteria plus a notes-added 7th requirement) spanning unrelated subsystems — routing/preflight, the 5538-line execute-bead worker loop, heartbeat/liveness, the bead store, the `ddx bead operator-attention` command, and docs — and mixes implementation, integration tests, and documentation. It exceeds the single-pass size budget (Step 0), so it was decomposed (no implementation in this pass). Decomposed into 5 children (created with --parent ddx-8f2e0ebf; inter-child dependency edges record landing order): - ddx-449baa1d  bead: add atomic Store.Release so failure-release clears the claim and status reflects the lease   [AC3; foundation, no deps, currently ready] - ddx-d8970a7b  worker: bound route resolution and routing preflight with a configurable timeout and release on expiry   [AC1; depends on ddx-449baa1d] - ddx-dc23f001  worker: add progress watchdog for phase-empty heartbeats and terminate when the bead is closed externally   [AC2 + notes; depends on ddx-d8970a7b] - ddx-9714eaac  worker: stop claiming a bead that wedges on consecutive claims and surface it for operator review   [AC5; depends on ddx-d8970a7b] - ddx-58a69bb0  bead: surface every wedge/timeout lease release in ddx bead operator-attention and document the contract   [AC4 + AC6; depends on ddx-d8970a7b, ddx-dc23f001, ddx-9714eaac] Dependency direction note: this repo's own decomposer (cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:184-210) records the parent/child edge via Parent=<parentID> and marks the parent execution-ineligible; it does NOT add a `dep add <child> <parent>` blocking edge. Following Step 0's literal `dep add <child-id> <parent-id>` (child depends-on parent) would make every child blocked by the open parent and never become ready, stalling drain. So the parent/child edge is recorded via --parent (children stay ready because the parent is open), and only correct-direction inter-child ordering edges were added with `ddx bead dep add`. The parent now carries a `decomposed into ...` note; the orchestrator owns the parent's lifecycle from here.

description:
PROBLEM
ddx try can claim/checkpoint and then fail during worktree setup when the temp worktree or evidence root is out of bytes/inodes or unwritable. In the May 6 incident, git worktree add failed with No space left on device after creating partial execution artifacts, and the failure was treated as ordinary execution_failed instead of a resource guardrail.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:686-714 creates the temp worktree parent, commits/checkpoints, resolves base, and calls WorktreeAdd before any resource-health check of $TMPDIR/ddx-exec-wt or .ddx/executions/.ddx/runs.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:713-714 returns immediately on WorktreeAdd failure, so partial unregistered directories can remain outside the deferred WorktreeRemove path.
- cli/cmd/try.go:306-342 routes ddx try through ExecuteBeadWorker without a pre-claim resource gate that can fail before claiming the target bead.
- docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-010-task-execution.md:454-467 requires ddx try to validate roots, run one cleanup pass, re-check, and return resource_exhausted without claiming when still unhealthy.

PROPOSED FIX
- Introduce a resource checker abstraction that validates temp worktree root and durable evidence root writability, free bytes, and free inodes where supported.
- Run resource preflight before claim/worktree creation in ddx try paths, using the cleanup manager once before final failure.
- Classify persistent resource failure as resource_exhausted with structured detail, not generic execution_failed/quota.
- Ensure WorktreeAdd failure removes partial unregistered worktree directories created for the attempt.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not decide ddx work loop stop behavior here; sibling ddx work bead consumes the resource_exhausted outcome.
- Do not add background cleanup cadence here.
- Do not implement a real low-disk integration test that fills a filesystem; use injectable resource checker/fake filesystem boundaries.
title: try: preflight execution resources before claim and worktree setup

description:
PROBLEM
A live DDx server-managed worker dogfood run allowed two workers for the same project to execute the same bead concurrently. On 2026-06-16, `ddx work status --all-projects --json` showed worker `worker-20260616T020728-afbd` (pid 1408898, attempt `20260616T021109-1940d5f0`) and worker `worker-20260616T020731-c3ac` (pid 1410320, attempt `20260616T021150-fea20ed9`) both running `ddx-6ae5134b` in separate execution worktrees. `active_work.records` only showed the second owner, so the server status surface under-reported the duplicate execution. Both workers had live Claude TUI children before the non-owner worker was stopped.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/bead/store.go:932-972` implements `Store.ClaimWithOptions` by writing the external claim heartbeat sidecar but does not transition the tracked bead row to `in_progress`.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:4715-4731` and `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:5021-5056` rebuild candidates from `ReadyExecution`; if an `open` bead with a fresh external lease remains in the ready view, another worker can select it.
- `cli/internal/server/workers.go:578-614` starts independent external `ddx work` processes for desired workers, and there is no server-side per-project/per-bead single-flight guard before those workers enter the queue.

PROPOSED FIX
Make a fresh external claim lease remove the bead from every worker-ready path before any second worker can start an attempt. Add a regression that starts two server-managed workers against a fixture project with exactly one ready bead and proves only one attempt/worktree/provider child is created for that bead. The second worker should report a `claim_race`/idle condition or pick different ready work, never execute the same bead concurrently. Ensure `ddx work status --all-projects --json` surfaces duplicate attempt evidence if it ever detects multiple live workers with the same bead ID.

NON-SCOPE
Do not reduce desired worker count globally. Do not remove support for multiple workers on different beads. Do not change Claude TUI routing. Do not kill unrelated interactive Claude/Codex processes.
title: server workers: prevent duplicate live attempts for one bead

description:
There is no CLI command to see which workers are running and which bead each is executing. The WorkerManager in cli/internal/server/workers.go already tracks this (WorkerRecord.CurrentBead at line 51, WorkerRecord.State, WorkerRecord.Harness, WorkerRecord.Model, WorkerRecord.Attempts/Successes/Failures) but it is only accessible through the server API. Local --local workers are not tracked by the server at all.

This bead adds ddx agent workers as a top-level CLI subcommand. It must not depend on worktrunk (wt) or any external tool.

## Required changes

### 1. New command: ddx agent workers (cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go)
Register alongside the existing ddx agent log command. Flags:
  --json         emit raw JSON array
  --watch        re-render every 2s (like watch -n2) until Ctrl-C
  --project      filter to a specific project root (default: CWD project)

### 2. Data sources (two paths)
A. Server-submitted workers: GET http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/agent/workers — deserialize []WorkerRecord from the server. Already implemented in cli/internal/server/workers.go List() / HTTP handler.
B. Local --local workers: the server does not track these. Detect them by:
   1. Reading .ddx/workers/*/status.json files in the project root (server writes these even for local workers when they self-register — confirm in workers.go; if not, fall back to scanning active execute-bead worktrees)
   2. Scanning .ddx/.execute-bead-wt-* directories (from ExecuteBeadWtPrefix constant in cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go line 403) and reading the manifest.json inside each to extract bead_id, attempt_id, harness, model, started_at

### 3. Local worker detection via manifest scan
For each directory matching .ddx/.execute-bead-wt-*:
  - Read .ddx/executions/{attemptID}/manifest.json (path encoded in worktree name suffix)
  - Check if worktree is still active (git worktree list --porcelain)
  - Read work-heartbeat-at from bead.Extra (requires ddx-7651506a) if available
  - Derive synthetic WorkerRecord from manifest fields

### 4. Table output (default)
Columns: STATE | BEAD | TITLE (truncated 40 chars) | HARNESS | MODEL | ELAPSED | ATTEMPTS
- STATE: running (green), exited (dim), failed (red)
- ELAPSED: human-readable (e.g., 4m32s)
- If current bead title unavailable (local worker pre-manifest), show bead ID

### 5. Merge and deduplicate
When both server and manifest sources are available, deduplicate by worker_id or attempt_id. Server record takes precedence over manifest-derived record for the same worker.

## Key files
- cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go — add newAgentWorkersCommand(), register in newAgentCommand()
- cli/internal/server/workers.go — WorkerRecord struct (lines 31-54), List API
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go — ExecuteBeadWtPrefix constant (line 403), manifest shape (lines 726-771)
- cli/internal/agent/types.go — SessionEntry Correlation map (bead_id field)
title: Add ddx agent workers command — native live worker status with current bead

description:

  Multiple tests in cli/cmd/ pass the literal "/tmp" as the working-directory
  argument to NewCommandFactory(...). Today these tests don't write files at
  that path, but a future change to NewCommandFactory or its commands could
  silently start writing into /tmp without any cleanup. Discovered by the
  2026-05-09 test-cleanup audit.

ROOT CAUSE

INTERSECTIONS

acceptance:
1. `ddx work` readiness/preflight hooks run under a bounded timeout with a clear default and, if configurable, documented config/flag behavior.
2. On readiness timeout, the attempt records evidence containing the readiness command/context, timeout duration, and resulting bead outcome.
3. A timed-out readiness check does not leave the bead indefinitely claimed/in_progress.
4. In watch mode, after handling the timed-out readiness outcome, the worker can continue to other eligible ready beads.
5. Regression coverage proves a hanging readiness hook cannot block the worker indefinitely.
description:
In Niflheim, `ddx work --watch --profile smart` claimed bead `niflheim-edcb2b7c` and then parked at `readiness check: starting` without spawning an agent child, timing out, recording a terminal non-success outcome, or releasing/blocking the bead. The readiness check was for a live soak bead whose previous evidence already showed PgWire unavailable on `127.0.0.1:5433`.

Observed behavior on 2026-05-13:
- Worker was alive in tmux (`ddx` pane process), but no child agent process existed.
- Worker log stopped after `▶ niflheim-edcb2b7c ...` and `readiness check: starting`.
- Bead remained `in_progress`/claimed.
- Queue had many ready beads, but the worker could not move past this readiness phase.

Expected behavior: readiness hooks must be bounded. If readiness cannot complete inside a configured/default timeout, `ddx work` should write evidence explaining the failed readiness command, map the outcome to blocked/open according to the no_changes contract, unclaim the bead when appropriate, and continue draining other ready work instead of parking the whole worker.

This is separate from the underlying Niflheim PgWire availability bug; DDx should not require the target service bug to be fixed before the queue can keep moving.
title: Bound ddx work readiness hooks so blocked beads cannot hang a worker forever

description:
PROBLEM
Pre-claim readiness currently treats recoverable quality/refinement findings as operator-required, which can park otherwise executable open beads and interrupt continuous forward progress. In default WARN-ONLY behavior, these findings should warn and proceed unless DDx has a hard manual-decision blocker.

ROOT CAUSE
- cli/internal/agent/readiness_classification.go:90-94 maps ReadinessClassificationNeedsRefine to PreClaimIntakeOperatorRequired when no validated rewrite is present. That causes refinement needs to follow the proposed parking path instead of advisory warning.
- cli/internal/agent/preclaim_ac_quality.go:115-124 documents and implements the AC quality gate as execution-ineligible plus PreClaimIntakeOperatorRequired when score < threshold, even though ADR-023 default mode is WARN-ONLY.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1207-1226 parks every terminal non-actionable intake outcome to proposed, without a policy distinction between recoverable rubric noise and hard operator_required findings.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add/consult the readiness quality mode defined by the spec bead: WARN-ONLY by default, explicit BLOCK/factory mode when configured.
- In WARN-ONLY mode, recoverable rubric gaps, needs_refine findings, low AC-quality scores, and readiness infrastructure noise append warning evidence and proceed to claim/implementation.
- Keep parking for true hard blockers: explicit operator_required from ambiguity/contradiction, lossy decomposition, depth cap with no executable path, unsafe commitment loss, or BLOCK/factory mode low-quality findings.
- Preserve existing post-attempt review and no_changes operator-required behavior unless this pre-claim path directly calls it.

NON-SCOPE
- No operator-override history detection here; that is ddx operator-override child work.
- No new event vocabulary; structured evidence is covered by the observability child.
- No Fizeau routing/profile/model behavior.

PARENT/DEPS
Parent: ddx-cc0641a7. Depends on ddx-ef9e8aec.
notes: Operator reviewed pre-claim parking on 2026-05-12. Bead is execution-ready as written; readiness rewrite dropped part of the ROOT CAUSE file:line citation cli/internal/agent/readiness_classification.go:90-94. Preserve the original prompt and skip lifecycle rewrite for execution.
title: agent: make WARN-ONLY readiness findings proceed

description:
src/lib/components/D3Graph.svelte nodeColorClass() function (lines 65-72) returns hardcoded Tailwind palette color classes for graph node staleness states:

- stale: 'fill-amber-400 stroke-amber-600 dark:fill-amber-500 dark:stroke-amber-400'
- missing: 'fill-red-400 stroke-red-600 dark:fill-red-500 dark:stroke-red-400'
- fresh (default): 'fill-green-400 stroke-green-600 dark:fill-green-500 dark:stroke-green-400'

These staleness states are semantic domain concepts (stale = warning, missing = error, fresh = success) and should map to semantic tokens. The project has error tokens (error / dark-error) and accent tokens. Warning (stale) and success (fresh) states should either map to existing tokens or be added as semantic CSS utilities (e.g. using accent-load for warning, accent-fulcrum for success) consistent with the design system palette.

Line 189: graph node label uses raw font-size '12px' and lacks a semantic size token reference.
title: D3Graph: node color uses raw amber-/red-/green- palette instead of semantic tokens

description:
CONTRACT-001 assigns dirty-tree checkpointing before managed execution to DDx, but current execute-bead/work flows create isolated worktrees from HEAD without automatically checkpointing pre-existing dirty parent-tree state. DDx has a manual `ddx checkpoint` command, yet managed execution does not create or reference a pre-run checkpoint artifact.

Add deterministic dirty-parent-tree checkpointing so a managed run can always point to the pre-execution state it started from.
spec_grounding: Per FEAT-012 §22 ('Checkpoint a dirty caller worktree before execution — creates a commit, does not discard changes') and FEAT-012 US-126 AC#1 ('DDx creates a checkpoint commit from those changes and uses it as the effective base revision'). Implementation: a real git commit on the current branch via the existing SynthesizeCommit helper before the worker worktree is created. NOT a stash, NOT a hidden ref, NOT an evidence file, NOT a new ExecuteBeadResult field. The checkpoint commit IS the artifact.
title: Checkpoint dirty parent trees before managed bead execution

During preclaim decomposition of ddx-29491a0e on 2026-07-13, `ddx work status --json` reported active_work.count=0 with no bead_id, phase, or last_activity_at while a queue-critical provider was already running. Add candidate-scoped resolving liveness publication before PostAttemptDecompositionHook dispatch. The sidecar status must expose the candidate bead ID, phase=resolving, and an initialized last_activity_at while preserving the fact that no claim or lease has been created.

NON-SCOPE
Do not claim the parent before decomposition, change decomposition prompts or AC-map validation, change queue ordering, or make preclaim model work count as an implementation attempt. Do not implement heartbeat refreshes or provider-child metadata in this child beyond any minimal fields needed for the candidate resolving state.

description:
PROBLEM
Per epic ddx-a9d130d0: bead-lifecycle quality framework needs an ADR documenting the policy + amendments to existing FEATs to formally adopt the lint/triage hooks and the sub-skill packaging change.

ROOT CAUSE
Today no policy artifact exists for bead-quality enforcement. RELIABILITY-PRINCIPLES bead ddx-06b77652 documents P7 as a principle but does not specify the enforcement mechanism, waiver model, staged rollout, or recovery UX. Existing FEAT docs are stale on relevant points:
- FEAT-011 at docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-011-skills.md:180 says DDx ships exactly one skill, but .agents/skills/ddx/bead-breakdown/SKILL.md already demonstrates nested sub-skill packaging.
- FEAT-004 at docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-004-beads.md:150 owns bead validation hooks but doesn't describe authoring-quality lint or post-attempt triage.
- FEAT-010 at docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-010-executions.md:21 documents the layer-1/2/3 invocation model but doesn't spec hook insertion points for ddx try / ddx work.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Author ADR-023 at docs/helix/02-design/adr/ADR-023-bead-lifecycle-quality-policy.md covering:
   - Policy: lint pre-dispatch + triage post-attempt; both invoke the same bead-lifecycle sub-skill
   - Staged rollout: WARN-ONLY default → BLOCK opt-in after baseline confirms
   - Waiver model: rubric-level by bead-type (doc/epic/deletion skip certain criteria, per docs/helix/06-iterate/bead-authoring-template.md:219); per-bead lint-waiver:<criterion> label for rare exceptions; --force --reason records an event (does not silently bypass)
   - Fail-open hook behavior (P1 from RELIABILITY-PRINCIPLES): infrastructure failure proceeds; only valid low lint score blocks (in BLOCK mode)
   - Operator recovery UX: blocked dispatch prints missing fields + suggested ddx bead update commands

2. Amend FEAT-004 (beads): add §"Authoring quality lint" describing the rubric, sub-skill location, waiver storage (label-based), and tracker metadata (no new schema fields; lint output ephemeral in evidence dir).

3. Amend FEAT-010 (executions): add §"Quality hooks" describing PreDispatchLintHook + PostAttemptTriageHook insertion points in ExecuteBeadLoopRuntime; OutcomeReason field beside existing Disrupted in ExecuteBeadReport.

4. Amend FEAT-011 (skills): replace "ships exactly one skill" with the nested workflow-skill model demonstrated by bead-breakdown/, replay-bead/, etc. Document the 5 shipped-skill paths per codex review (skills/ddx/, cli/internal/skills/ddx/, .agents/skills/ddx/, .claude/skills/ddx/, .ddx/skills/ddx/).

5. Cross-link: ADR-023 references RELIABILITY-PRINCIPLES (ddx-06b77652) + evidence (ddx-f339c399) + bead-authoring-template.md as the canonical template.

NON-SCOPE
- New FEAT (codex: not warranted; existing FEATs cover the surface)
- ADR for the in_progress-eligibility bug (separate concern)
- Cross-project skill packaging (deferred per FEAT-015)
- Schema changes to bead JSON (waivers via labels; no new fields)
title: ADR-023 + FEAT-004/010/011 amendments: bead-lifecycle quality enforcement policy

acceptance:
1. A harness child spawned by the execute-bead executor does NOT survive abnormal death of its parent worker. Verified by a test that starts the executor against a fake harness binary which forks a long-lived grandchild, then SIGKILLs the parent worker process (not graceful SIGTERM) and asserts the harness child + grandchild are gone (not PID-1 orphans) within a bounded grace. On Linux this is satisfied via SysProcAttr.Pdeathsig in cli/internal/agent/executor_unix.go.
2. cmdSetProcessGroup sets Pdeathsig (Linux) and the thread-migration caveat is handled (LockOSThread or equivalent) so the death signal actually fires; a test or documented rationale covers the non-Linux fallback.
3. `ddx work` startup reaps orphaned execute-bead harness children from prior dead workers scoped to the current project/workspace, and does NOT kill harness children of other live workers. Verified by a test that plants a fake orphaned harness process (parent gone) and a fake live-owned one and asserts only the orphan is reaped.
4. The docker-clone backend (attempt_backend.go:293) configures process-group/container cleanup so its nested harness is reaped on worker exit; covered by a test or, if container teardown already guarantees this, a documented justification.
5. Graceful SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown still terminates in-flight harness children (regression guard).
6. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... green; lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
When a `ddx work` orchestrator dies abnormally (SIGKILL, crash, OOM, host reboot of the supervising process) while a bead attempt is in flight, the spawned harness child (e.g. `claude --print -p --verbose --output-format stream-json ... <execute-bead>` or `codex exec --json ...`) is NOT reaped. It reparents to PID 1 and keeps running indefinitely. Observed 2026-05-27 on the dev host: a `claude --print` execute-bead child orphaned with PPID 1 for ~9h53m after its `ddx work` parent had gone — burning a harness session and (per the sibling fizeau leak) anchoring leaked subprocess trees. This is the orchestrator-side mirror of fizeau-50b6f055 (harness-runner-side leak).

ROOT CAUSE (file:line)
- cli/internal/agent/executor.go:156 — OSExecutor.ExecuteInDir spawns the harness via exec.Command(binary, args...) then cmdSetProcessGroup(cmd).
- cli/internal/agent/executor_unix.go:13-15 — cmdSetProcessGroup sets ONLY SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}. There is NO Pdeathsig. So the kernel does nothing automatically when the parent dies.
- cli/internal/agent/executor_unix.go:20-25 — cmdKillProcessGroup(cmd) SIGKILLs the negative pgid, but it is only invoked from the executor's graceful paths (stopProcess at executor.go:190-194, triggered by idle/wall-clock timeout, auth/rate-limit pattern, or ctx cancellation at executor.go:231-255).
- cli/cmd/root.go:49-54 — the worker context is a signal.NotifyContext on os.Interrupt + SIGTERM only. Graceful shutdown works; SIGKILL and crashes cannot be caught, so the defer/stopProcess chain never runs and the child survives.
- Net: child harness lifetime is governed entirely by parent-run cleanup. If the parent does not get to run cleanup, the child orphans. There is no kernel-enforced parent-death signal and no startup reaper that adopts/kills harness children whose parent PID is gone.

SECONDARY VECTOR
- cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:293 — the docker-clone backend spawns `exec.CommandContext(ctx, "docker", ...)` WITHOUT cmdSetProcessGroup, so even graceful cleanup may not reach the nested harness inside the container. (worktree/local-clone backends at attempt_backend.go:120-122 / :182-184 share the executor.go:156 path and do get Setpgid.)

PROPOSED FIX
1. Primary (Linux): set SysProcAttr.Pdeathsig = SIGKILL (or SIGTERM) in cmdSetProcessGroup so the kernel signals the harness child when the parent thread dies, regardless of how the parent died. Note the well-known caveat: Pdeathsig keys off the spawning OS *thread*, so pin/guard against Go runtime thread migration (runtime.LockOSThread around Start, or re-check parent PID in the child path). Document the macOS/Windows gap (Pdeathsig is Linux-only) and the chosen fallback there.
2. Backstop: on `ddx work` startup, reap orphaned harness children from prior dead workers — e.g. when registering/claiming, scan for execute-bead harness processes whose parent is PID 1 (or whose recorded owner PID is gone) and SIGKILL their process groups, gated to this project/workspace to avoid nuking unrelated work. Ties to the existing lease-release / operator-attention machinery (cross-ref ddx-8f2e0ebf).
3. docker-clone backend: apply cmdSetProcessGroup to the docker invocation at attempt_backend.go:293 (and/or run with --rm + a container-stop on cleanup) so the container tree is reaped too.

NON-SCOPE
- Graceful SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown already works (executor.go:231-255); do not regress it.
- The harness-runner-internal leak in fizeau is covered by fizeau-50b6f055; this bead is the ddx orchestrator -> harness-child boundary.

CROSS-REF: fizeau-50b6f055 (fizeau harness-runner process-group cleanup), ddx-8f2e0ebf (lease release / operator-attention).
title: execute-bead: harness child orphans to PID 1 when ddx work parent dies abnormally (SIGKILL/crash) — no Pdeathsig, no startup reaper

description:

Review area: embedded ddx-agent runtime observability and live worker progress. Evidence covers FEAT-006 execution/evidence ownership, FEAT-002 server activity surfaces, FEAT-008 web UI expectations, work worker supervision, and the need for DDx-owned progress telemetry beyond coarse session logs when DDx runs the embedded harness.

## Goals
- Define structured phase/heartbeat output for embedded-agent runs (queueing, launch, running, post-checks, landing, preserved, done)

- Clarify which live progress artifacts remain runtime-only and which summaries/indexes are exposed through DDx-owned APIs and UI surfaces
- Keep provider-native transcript ownership external; DDx progress output should be normalized runtime telemetry, not transcript duplication

## Required spec work
- Update FEAT-006, FEAT-002, and FEAT-008 so embedded-agent progress visibility is an explicit contract rather than an implementation detail
- Clarify how progress events relate to tracked execution artifacts, session logs, and server-managed worker state

## Required implementation planning
- Define the server/API/UI read model for live worker progress and recent phase history
- Define how CLI and UI consume the same structured progress feed without introducing hidden workflow policy

description:
PROBLEM
The DDx execute loop returns from lifecycle model discovery after the two-second deadline, but the PTY probe can keep running as a direct worker child and accumulate CPU after the caller has moved on.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:519-533` gives `svc.ListModels(modelCtx, modelFilter)` a two-second context but does not prove probe teardown before returning to the queue loop.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a DDx call-site containment wrapper around lifecycle model discovery that binds probe lifetime to the worker/caller context, waits for the spawned PTY session/process group to exit on success, error, timeout, or cancellation, and adds a regression harness for the queue-drain path.

NON-SCOPE
Disabling model discovery, extending the two-second caller timeout, killing manual Codex sessions or provider processes that predate the call, changing route selection, or restarting the DDx server.

PARENT
None; root reliability/performance regression observed while draining the Niflheim queue.

DEPS
Related to `ddx-092f0d34` (preclaim lifecycle containment) and regression of `ddx-403e9a23`; do not touch unrelated provider processes.
notes:
Prior attempt `20260713T121749-836fcbe4` failed after 68 minutes and was discarded. Do not repeat its broad containment design: it snapshotted every descendant of the worker, matched provider basenames plus `/model`, and killed all new process groups. That races concurrent legitimate providers, can target the worker process group, uses unbounded `ps`, ignores cleanup errors/survivors, and was not portable off Unix. It also passed live contexts into preflight service variants whose canceled quota context intentionally suppresses background probes. Required tests must cover concurrent provider ownership, worker-PGID safety, bounded enumeration failure, cleanup errors, portability, and preservation of intentional preflight cancellation; containment must be scoped to the lifecycle discovery call, not the whole worker descendant tree.

Concurrent attempt `20260713T125244-84b1d082` landed commit `020853315` on main with the two named tests; the focused AC command passed again on 2026-07-13 in 0.786s. The bead remains open because the attempt recorded `required_exec_summary: skipped` and no closing SHA. Treat the landed code as the starting point: verify/fix it and produce required gate evidence rather than creating a second parallel wrapper. Ownership and bounded-cleanup hardening is queued as `ddx-e1e229f5`.
title: Bind execute-loop model discovery to worker cancellation

acceptance:
1. `DDX_AGENT_LOG_VERBOSE=1 ddx agent ...` produces a trace where llm.response events include `content`, `finish_reason`, `usage`, and tool.call events include `input`, `output`, `duration_ms`, `error`.
2. Schema documented in cli/internal/agent/session_log_format.go (Go doc comment listing all fields per event type for both lean and verbose modes).
3. Default behavior unchanged (lean mode by default; existing tooling that consumes the lean schema continues to work).
4. Test fixture added for verbose mode that asserts every required field is populated.
description:
## Problem

`.ddx/agent-logs/agent-claude-*.jsonl` (lean schema) records only:
  - `session.start` (model, harness, bead_id)
  - `llm.response` (turn, input_tokens, output_tokens, elapsed_ms)
  - `tool.call`     (turn, tool name)

Notably absent: model output content, tool call arguments, tool call results, finish_reason, full usage breakdown (cache reads, cache writes), error/stop reasons.

Meanwhile, `agent/demos/sessions/*.jsonl` from the sibling `Projects/agent` repo demonstrates a richer schema for the same event types:

```jsonl
{"type":"llm.response","data":{"content":"...","finish_reason":"tool_calls","usage":{"input":899,"output":21,"total":920},"latency_ms":3040,"tool_calls":1}}
{"type":"tool.call","data":{"tool":"edit","input":{"path":"...","old_string":"...","new_string":"..."},"output":"Replaced 1 occurrence","duration_ms":0,"error":""}}
```

## Why it matters

- Cannot replay a real session to reproduce a bug — the inputs are gone.
- Cannot root-cause provider failures (e.g. RotatingKVCache Quantization NYI seen in sessions.jsonl) because the prompt that triggered it is not in the per-event log; only the whole-session metadata in sessions.jsonl has it.
- The lucebox-hub/dflash `bench_server.py` replay-mode benchmark needs full prompt text from real traces, not just metadata, to be representative.
- Inability to tell what tool args caused a slow call.

## Proposed fix

Add a verbose mode to the agent-logs writer (env var `DDX_AGENT_LOG_VERBOSE=1` or config flag) that adopts the agent/demos schema:
  - llm.response: include `content`, `finish_reason`, full `usage` object
  - tool.call: include `input` (tool args), `output` (truncated to N KB), `duration_ms`, `error`
  - new event: `llm.request` with messages_count and possibly truncated message preview

Verbose mode off by default to avoid bloating logs. On for any session with `--debug` or for failed sessions (auto-bump-on-error).

## Side note

`sessions.jsonl` (the 37 MB whole-session log) does have full `prompt` text but no per-turn breakdown. So we have two log formats and neither captures the full picture. This bead is about the per-event log only; whole-session log is out of scope.
title: FEAT: agent-logs jsonl schema is metadata-only; add verbose mode capturing tool I/O and content

2. Add `TestCoverageRatchetFailsBelowBaseline` proving a measured aggregate below the configured baseline returns a non-zero/failing result with a useful message.
3. Add `TestCoverageRatchetAllowsEqualOrImprovedCoverage` proving equal or improved measured coverage passes without updating the baseline.

description:
PROBLEM
The default DDx test path currently answers only pass/fail. It does not produce an aggregate coverage number, does not persist a baseline, and does not fail when coverage regresses. That made it easy to miss that the interrupted work/watch tracker-noise path had no real integration coverage until production behavior exposed it.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- Makefile:23-24 delegates `make test` to `cli-test` without any coverage gate.
- Makefile:59-61 delegates CLI tests to `cd cli && $(MAKE) test`, so root-level default testing inherits the CLI target behavior.
- cli/Makefile:111-114 runs `go test -v ./...` with no `-coverprofile`, aggregate coverage parsing, baseline comparison, or ratchet persistence.
- cli/Makefile:116-120 has `test-full` run `go test -race -cover ./...`, but it only prints package coverage and has no enforced ratchet.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a coverage measurement and ratchet workflow for the default Go test suite. The implementation must read its baseline/threshold from a checked-in repo config or data file, not from hardcoded defaults in Go source. Add a Make target that runs coverage, reports aggregate coverage, compares it to the configured baseline, and fails on regression. Decide whether `make test` should invoke the ratchet directly or whether CI/default-test documentation should make the ratchet target mandatory; if not wired into `make test`, document the reason in the bead implementation.

NON-SCOPE
Do not require live harness tests, perf tests, or networked integration tests for the coverage ratchet. Do not make developers update a baseline implicitly during ordinary test runs. Do not hide coverage failures behind verbose-only output. Do not manually edit `.ddx/beads.jsonl`.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- Makefile
- cli/Makefile
- cli/tools/ or cli/internal/ test-support package for coverage-ratchet parsing/comparison
- a checked-in coverage ratchet config/baseline file under cli/ or .ddx/

OUT-OF-SCOPE
- Fizeau routing policy
- worker execution semantics
- live_harness and perf test inclusion policy
title: test: measure coverage and enforce a ratchet

When the same bead wedges on consecutive claims (default threshold 2), the worker stops claiming it, transitions it to an operator-attention/proposed state, surfaces it via an event, and the loop continues to the next ready bead. Verified by TestSameBeadTwiceWedgeGuardStopsClaiming which injects two consecutive wedges.
2. The consecutive-wedge marker resets when the bead next makes real progress, so a bead that wedges once then succeeds is not sidelined. Verified by TestWedgeMarkerResetsOnProgress.

description:
PROBLEM
A single wedged bead can starve the queue: ddx bead ready showed 30 dispatchable beads while one single-threaded worker re-claimed and re-wedged the same bead (parent ddx-8f2e0ebf, criterion E). There is no per-bead consecutive-wedge guard — a freshly released wedged bead is immediately re-claimed and re-wedged.

ROOT CAUSE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go: the claim/dispatch loop keeps no record of "this bead wedged on its previous claim", so it re-claims a just-released wedged bead. The only existing per-bead suppression is route-exclusion dedup at execute_bead_loop.go:4970-4978, which dedups failed (provider, model) routes — not wedge/timeout releases. A route-independent wedge (e.g. resolver hang from child ddx-d8970a7b) therefore recurs indefinitely.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Record a per-bead wedge marker when a bead is released due to route-resolution timeout (child ddx-d8970a7b) or watchdog fire (child ddx-dc23f001).
2. On the next claim cycle, if the same bead still carries a wedge marker from the immediately preceding claim (consecutive wedge), the worker does NOT re-claim it; it transitions the bead to a proposed/operator-attention state, surfaces it via an event, and continues to the next ready bead so the queue keeps draining.
3. Make the consecutive-wedge threshold configurable (default 2 consecutive wedges). Reset the marker when the bead next makes real progress (a resolved route / LLM call / commit), so a transient single wedge does not permanently sideline a bead.

NON-SCOPE
Timeout detection (child ddx-d8970a7b), watchdog (child ddx-dc23f001), operator-attention query surface + docs (child E). Reuses the release/event primitives from those children and the atomic release from child ddx-449baa1d. This is a decomposition child of ddx-8f2e0ebf.

description:
PROBLEM
A drain worker on a full ready queue that never successfully claims (because every pre-claim attempt warns and skips) presents as healthy: loop.idle every ~50s, process alive, no error. Silent idle on a non-empty queue is a stuck state masquerading as healthy. The operator has no top-level signal that claim throughput has collapsed.

CONTEXT / WHERE
ddx work --watch is wired in cli/cmd/work.go; the drain loop is cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go. A worker-status surface already exists (cli/internal/workerstatus/ and a work_status command per cli/cmd/work_status_test.go). Claim attempts and their outcomes (claimed vs skipped/warn) pass through the loop each iteration.

PROPOSED FIX
Track claim attempt outcomes over a rolling window (default 10 attempts, configurable) in the drain loop. When the claim success rate over the window falls below a configurable threshold (default 0%, i.e. zero successes across the full window) while ready beads remain, surface a top-level operator-visible warning:
  - to stderr (a single, deduplicated warning line, not per-iteration spam), AND/OR
  - via the existing worker-status surface (cli/internal/workerstatus or ddx work status) so an operator can query it.
The window size and threshold must be configurable with documented defaults.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change the decoder (ddx-606fe854), the consecutive-fingerprint escalation (ddx-d67f124e), the CI schema gate, or README docs. Only the rolling claim-success-rate signal.
title: ddx work --watch: surface low claim-success-rate over a rolling window

description:
PROBLEM
Silent idle on a full queue is a stuck state masquerading as healthy. During the Fizeau idle (2026-05-18), ddx work --watch kept polling (resource.preflight ok -> loop.idle every ~50s) while 23 beads sat ready and zero were claimed; the commit log was empty for the same 30-minute window. From the outside the worker looked alive. There was no top-level operator-visible signal that the claim success rate had collapsed to 0%.

The watch loop emits loop.idle at cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1513 but tracks no rolling claim-success metric, so a 0% claim rate over a full queue produces the same output as a legitimately empty queue. The --watch flag is defined at cli/cmd/work.go:88.

PROPOSED FIX (parent proposed-fix E)
Track claim attempts versus successes over a configurable rolling window (default 10 attempts). When the success rate over that window falls below a configurable threshold (e.g. 0% over 10 attempts), surface an operator-visible warning via stderr and/or a status surface (ddx bead status or a ddx work status view). Add --claim-rate-window and --claim-rate-threshold flags to ddx work.

- Decoder coercion (sibling decoder child).
- CI schema drift gate (sibling child).
- Same-fingerprint warn escalation (sibling escalation child; complementary but distinct trigger).

Governing artifact: AR-2026-05-17 follow-up beads. Adjacent silent-failure bugs: ddx-57c40485, ddx-8f2e0ebf.

description:
PROBLEM (Principle 2 of epic ddx-602ae31a)

Operators need `ddx doctor` and the shipped docs to explain which install layer is active. The ddx-validate pre-commit hook must keep its scoped behavior so skill-related validation runs only when skill files are staged, regardless of whether skills are installed globally or project-locally. This documentation and diagnostic work should be separate from the install/update/init implementation beads.

ROOT CAUSE
- `cli/cmd/doctor.go:35` owns full doctor execution and must report installation topology without breaking existing health checks.
- `cli/cmd/doctor.go:292` invokes skill install topology reporting, and `cli/cmd/doctor.go:429` renders the global and project layer statuses.
- `cli/cmd/doctor.go:487` is the scoped doctor path used by the ddx-validate hook; it must stay scoped to staged paths rather than running global install checks.
- `docs/helix/02-design/adr/ADR-027-skill-install-topology.md:31`, `library/skills/ddx/SKILL.md:37`, `library/skills/ddx/reference/agents.md:144`, and `CLAUDE.md:220` are the durable documentation surfaces that must describe install locations and precedence.

PROPOSED FIX
Have `ddx doctor` render two explicit lines for the default `ddx` plugin layer: `Global Install (${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/plugins/ddx) — ok | missing` and `Project Install (ddxroot.Path()/plugins/ddx) — ok | missing | lazy-resolves-to-global`. Preserve `ddx doctor --paths` behavior for ddx-validate so only relevant scoped checks run for staged files. Update or file the topology ADR, `library/skills/ddx/SKILL.md` How this skill works/install topology section, `library/skills/ddx/reference/agents.md` if present, and the `CLAUDE.md` Persona System section so they all describe project-local, global, and baked-in precedence.

- Depends on ddx-06cbaa90 and its home-resolution spec updates.
- Spec impact: `docs/helix/02-design/adr/ADR-025-or-equivalent` skill install topology, `library/skills/ddx/SKILL.md`, `library/skills/ddx/reference/agents.md` if it exists, and `CLAUDE.md` Persona System.

PARENT
- ddx-602ae31a

DEPS

NON-SCOPE
- Removing the existing per-project install entirely; global and per-project modes coexist.
- Migrating `~/.config/ddx/` legacy paths if any exist.
- Agent-harness path discovery beyond Claude Code and Codex-facing `.agents/skills`; add others only when those harnesses define their skill paths.

acceptance: The DDx pre-push `no-debug` hook runs without regex parse errors in a default ripgrep environment; the debug-scan command fails closed when the scan itself errors; and the hook still blocks actual debug statements it is meant to catch.
description:
<context-digest>
Observed during `git push` in /Users/erik/Projects/ddx after landing tracker commits for work alpha findings. The DDx pre-push hook `no-debug` invoked `rg` with a look-ahead pattern and emitted a regex parse error, but the hook summary still reported success and the push continued.
</context-digest>

The DDx pre-push `no-debug` hook uses an `rg` pattern that requires PCRE2 look-around support, but it invokes plain `rg` without `--pcre2`. In the current environment that produces a parse error while the hook still exits successfully.

## Reproduction
1. In `/Users/erik/Projects/ddx`, run `git push`.
2. Observe pre-push hook output from `no-debug` containing:
   `rg: regex parse error: ... look-around ... is not supported`
3. Observe the hook summary still marks `no-debug` as passed and the push continues.

## Why this matters
The hook currently gives a false sense of enforcement. A broken regex should either be written in ripgrep-compatible syntax or use `--pcre2`, and failures in the debug scan should not be silently treated as success.
title: Fix pre-push no-debug hook regex compatibility and failure semantics

description:
Incident observed in sibling repo `/home/erik/Projects/axon` on 2026-06-13 while running `ddx work --watch --idle-interval 15s --request-timeout 45m` from Codex.

Symptoms:
1. Two background launches of `ddx work --watch` exited immediately with empty logs: PID 819208 `/tmp/axon-ddx-worker-20260612-232505.log`, then PID 819691 `/tmp/axon-ddx-worker-20260612-232537.log`. `ddx work plan --json` showed a valid next bead, so the queue was not empty.
2. Foreground `ddx work --once --request-timeout 45m` succeeded on Axon bead `axon-5c6af8f0`, proving the route/queue could execute.
3. Foreground `ddx work --watch --idle-interval 15s --request-timeout 45m` repeatedly emitted pre-claim readiness warnings: `readiness route unavailable: lifecycle dispatch: project root mutation rejected for bead <id> (continuing)`. Seen for Axon beads `axon-5c6af8f0`, `axon-7e75384c`, and `axon-a8e564c1`. The warning was recorded as `intake.warn` with `rule_id=pre_claim_intake.system_unready`.
4. For Axon bead `axon-7e75384c`, watch/attempt output included `Cancel received, shutting down gracefully`; DDx recorded `status: success` and closed the bead even though the landed implementation commit trail contained only execution evidence / harness metadata, no product code diff. The acceptance tests happened to pass independently, but `.ddx/beads.jsonl` closure was left dirty and had to be committed manually (`7351979f`).
5. For Axon bead `axon-a8e564c1`, the watch session exited with code -1 during implementation after reading CI/package files. After exit, `ddx work status --json` reported no live workers but still reported active work from `.ddx/run-state/20260613T034907-3d00f60f.json`; the bead remained open/claimed and queue status was `ready=0`, `worker_ready=0`, `active_work.count=1`. That jams the queue until an operator manually unclaims/cleans/restarts.

Expected behavior: if the worker process exits or its harness subprocess is cancelled, DDx should either complete/close with committed tracker evidence, or release the bead and clear stale active run-state. `ddx work --watch` should not leave the project with zero workers, a claimed open bead, stale active run-state, and no ready work. The readiness route should not attempt a project-root mutation during pre-claim analysis, or the warning should include a precise non-blocking explanation and not recur on every bead.

Reproduction context from Axon:
- project: `/home/erik/Projects/axon`
- ready beads: `axon-5c6af8f0`, then `axon-7e75384c`, then `axon-a8e564c1`
- stale files after crash: `.ddx/run-state/20260613T034907-3d00f60f.json`, `.ddx/workers/agent-loop-1781322253776691221/status.json`
- command: `ddx work --watch --idle-interval 15s --request-timeout 45m`

In-scope files: DDx worker/watch loop, run-state/liveness cleanup, pre-claim readiness/lifecycle dispatch, and tests around process exit/cancel handling.
Out-of-scope: Axon product code, model routing policy, and general host process cleanup not tied to DDx run-state.

This repeated the prior slow-close behavior seen on Axon tracker-only closes. The command eventually updated the tracker, but the silent delay is operationally ambiguous for agents because it looks like a stuck close while holding the tracker workflow.
title: fix: keep ddx work watch from leaving stale active run-state

description:
PROBLEM
A bead can become dependency-waiting while its model-backed readiness check is running, yet DDx still dispatches it from the stale claimed snapshot. In live attempt 20260713T184450-fa9ca5d7, ddx-1f1c3f0f was claimed for readiness, an operator then added dependency ddx-02200b1e, the tracker mutation was committed into the attempt base, and DDx nevertheless launched the implementation harness. description:
PROBLEM
During the same live canary window, `.ddx/metrics/locks.jsonl` recorded an `index.lock` hold-time violation for `operation=index.commit`: duration 10027ms against the 10000ms cap. After the server restart/worker claim cycle, `.git/index.lock` remained with no live owner and blocked a tracker-only commit until manually verified with `lsof` and removed. This violates the lock lifetime contract and is a direct blocker to reliable server-managed workers.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:990-1003` documents `landEvidence` as a short ref-advancing commit boundary, then calls `CommitStaged` to create the trailing evidence commit.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:1458-1460` runs `landEvidence` inside `withMainGitLock(projectRoot, "land_post_land_finalize", ...)`.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:772-780` implements `CommitStaged` with a real `git commit -m ...` subprocess.
- `cli/internal/lockmetrics/lockcap.go:18-24` treats `index.lock` holds over 10s as hung and force-releases the lock. When the cap fires during the `git commit` subprocess, DDx can record the violation but still leave a stale `.git/index.lock` / interrupted commit state behind.

PROPOSED FIX
Make evidence finalization resilient to capped index commits. Either split the expensive evidence `git commit` out of the over-strict critical section or add explicit recovery/retry around cap-triggered commit interruption. The worker must remove only verified-stale `.git/index.lock` files, record durable violation evidence/operator diagnostics, and leave the landing worktree resumable so the next tracker-only or evidence commit succeeds without manual cleanup.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not raise the default 10s cap as the only fix.

Deps: none. Related to the closed lock-contention work, but this is a newly observed stale-lock recovery failure from the Claude TUI canary.
