description:
PROBLEM

DDx execution still converts DDx project model, reasoning, endpoint, credential, and timeout configuration into a Fizeau `ServiceConfig`. `NewServiceFromWorkDir*` ignores the worktree it receives, so Fizeau cannot discover its own project configuration. DDx also invents a 15-minute provider timeout when the operator did not set one. These paths leave DDx owning provider policy even after concrete route selection moved to Fizeau.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE

- `cli/internal/agent/serviceconfig.go:41-82` derives provider timeout behavior from DDx endpoint configuration and supplies `DefaultProviderRequestTimeout`.
- `cli/internal/agent/serviceconfig.go:98-111` accepts `workDir` but does not give Fizeau a deterministic project `ConfigPath`.
- `cli/internal/agent/serviceconfig.go:145-367` converts DDx endpoints/models/reasoning/defaults into provider registries and route/session paths.
- `cli/internal/config/resolved.go:73-80,123-128` retains project model fallback and per-harness reasoning maps in resolved execution state.
- `cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:69-81` emits a stale DDx endpoint-timeout migration hint; `cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:197-223` always sends the DDx-resolved provider timeout.
- `cli/cmd/work.go:114` and `cli/cmd/try.go:100` still describe project/model defaults that route-neutral execution must not consume.

PROPOSED FIX

- Construct every execution-facing Fizeau service with `ServiceOptions.ConfigPath=filepath.Join(workDir, "config.yaml")`, or the equivalent deterministic public path contract. Fizeau interprets the directory as the project root and owns its documented global-plus-project configuration merge, including `<project>/.fizeau/config.yaml`.
- Delete execution-reachable DDx endpoint-to-`ServiceConfig` conversion, provider registry/default synthesis, URL/port provider inference, provider route-health/session-path manufacture, and project-model/reasoning fallback from execution construction.
- Forward `ProviderTimeout` only when the operator explicitly supplied the public request constraint. Omitted input remains zero/unset; timeout behavior then belongs to Fizeau/provider while DDx generic execution `Timeout` and `IdleTimeout` remain intact.
- Preserve explicit public execution constraints byte-for-byte: Harness, Provider, Model, Policy/Profile, MinPower, MaxPower, Reasoning/Effort, Permissions, Timeout, IdleTimeout, ProviderTimeout, Role, working directory, and correlation metadata.
- Remove stale CLI and error text that promises DDx project-model or endpoint-timeout defaults.

NON-SCOPE

- Do not suppress, replace, or reinterpret the documented Fizeau global-plus-project configuration merge. Tests isolate HOME and Fizeau config fixtures so developer-machine state cannot determine their result.
- Do not yet delete or hard-reject legacy config fields; `ddx-e2c3453b` owns the migration after all consumers are removed.
- Do not delete `ConfiguredProviderSnapshots` or helpers retained solely by that server compatibility surface; `ddx-d7800ef7` owns their removal with REST/MCP/GraphQL inventory and hypothetical route display.
- Do not change pricing, billing inference, harness display names, session cost, or evidence caps; `ddx-1b3272a6` owns them.
- Do not choose, validate, or predict a concrete Fizeau route.
title: agent: delegate project configuration and provider timeout policy to Fizeau

description:
PROBLEM
The route-resolution watchdog can recognize an expired Execute-relative deadline yet leave the active Fizeau attempt running while DDx performs synchronous tracker bookkeeping. Under ordinary tracker or host I/O contention this violates the bounded route-timeout contract, makes the race suite nondeterministic, and delays process cancellation after the deadline has already expired.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3527-3544 calls routeResolutionTimeoutReport before attemptCancel after term.set succeeds. routeResolutionTimeoutReport releases the lease, updates the consecutive-wedge record, and appends operator_attention through locked JSONL persistence. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_route_exclusion_test.go:400-465 uses a 150ms wall-clock assertion after deliberately delaying guard startup; repeated baseline proof under CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race fails because tracker writes can exceed that threshold even though the remaining timer is correctly clamped to zero.

PROPOSED FIX
Cancel the attempt context immediately after the route-timeout termination reason wins, before any durable timeout/release bookkeeping. Then perform the existing release, consecutive-wedge, operator-attention, and release-failure handling while the worker waits for the guard to finish. Replace the load-sensitive cancellation assertion with a blocking tracker/store seam that holds timeout bookkeeping and proves the executor context is cancelled while persistence is still blocked. Retain an eventual assertion that durable release and operator_attention complete after the block is removed.

NON-SCOPE
Do not lengthen timeout thresholds, weaken or delete route-timeout coverage, change the configured timeout/default, move route selection into DDx, change Fizeau routing, alter consecutive-wedge policy, or make tracker writes asynchronous beyond the existing guard lifetime.

PARENT
ddx-8f2e0ebf.

DEPS
None. This is a release-gate defect discovered while committing ddx-e2c3453b; the failure reproduces on unchanged main.

acceptance:
**User story:** As a developer browsing the web UI beads view, I want clicking a bead to open its detail pane within ~200ms on a repo with hundreds of beads across several projects, so the UI feels interactive.

**Acceptance criteria:**

1. A benchmark/harness exists (Go benchmark or scripted GraphQL client) that measures end-to-end `bead(id:)` latency against a fixture repo with ≥ 5 projects and ≥ 500 beads total. Output is a p50/p95 number, not a pass/fail bool.
2. Baseline is recorded in the bead notes (actual number measured on the current `main` binary at the time of fix).
3. After the fix, p95 for `bead(id:)` on the fixture is ≤ 50ms in-process / ≤ 200ms over HTTP on a dev laptop.
4. The fix does not introduce a stale-read regression: writing a bead via `ddx bead update` and then fetching it via GraphQL returns the new value on the next request (verified by a test that does write-then-read).
5. Concurrency-safe: an integration test spawns N concurrent `bead(id:)` queries interleaved with `bead update` mutations and asserts no panics, no torn reads, and consistent responses.
6. Playwright e2e: open `/nodes/.../beads`, click a bead row, assert the sidepane shows the bead title within 1s (generous budget; guards against regressions not the p95).
description:
## Observed

Opening a bead in the sidepane on `/nodes/.../projects/.../beads?q=test` takes 5+ seconds. The beads list renders quickly; the delay is on single-bead lookup.

## Root cause

`cli/internal/server/graphql/resolver.go:93-100` — the `Bead(id)` resolver calls `r.State.GetBeadSnapshots("", "", "", "")` with no filters, which at `cli/internal/server/state_graphql.go:49-105` walks **every project**, constructs a `bead.Store` per project, calls `ReadAll()` (full directory scan + JSONL parse of every bead file), then iterates the result in Go to find one matching ID.

So every sidepane open = `O(projects × beads_per_project)` disk reads + parses, for a lookup that should be `O(1)` or `O(log n)`.

`bead.Store` already exposes `Get(id)` (`cli/internal/bead/store.go:450`), but the resolver doesn't use it — nor does it know which project the bead lives in, because the GraphQL schema exposes `bead(id:)` without a project scope.

## Proposed direction (not prescriptive)

Any of these would resolve it; pick based on measurements:

1. **Project scope the query.** Change schema to `bead(projectId:, id:)` (or accept a composite global id) and call `Store.Get` directly.
2. **Maintain an in-memory index** `beadID → projectID` refreshed on bead mutations and on a debounced filesystem watcher; resolver does one map lookup + one `Store.Get`.
3. **Short-TTL snapshot cache** behind `GetBeadSnapshots`, invalidated on bead writes.

Before picking: add a baseline measurement harness (see acceptance) so we know the actual p50/p95 before and after, not just anecdote.
notes:
Baseline/after measurement for bead(id:) lookup fixture (5 projects, 500 total beads, go test ./internal/server -run ^$ -bench "BenchmarkGraphQLBeadLookup(LegacyScan)?Latency$" -benchtime=80x -count=1, linux/arm64):

- Legacy full-scan path matching main resolver behavior before fix: p50=13.38ms, p95=14.81ms.
- Optimized resolver path after bead ID -> project index warmup from beadsByProject: p50=2.593ms, p95=3.156ms.

Focused latency tests on the same fixture also measured GetBeadSnapshot p95=3.105871ms and GraphQL bead(id:) p95=3.450579ms over 80 requests.

REVIEW:BLOCK

Missing implementation change in `cli/internal/server/graphql/resolver.go`: `Bead(id:)` is not shown using a scoped lookup, cache, or index instead of scanning all bead snapshots.
Missing benchmark or scripted GraphQL latency harness for a fixture repo with at least 5 projects and 500 beads.
Missing bead-note update recording the baseline p50/p95 measured on the current `main` binary.
Missing post-fix performance evidence showing p95 within the required in-process or HTTP budget.
Missing write-then-read regression test covering `ddx bead update` followed by GraphQL `bead(id:)`.
Missing concurrent integration test interleaving `bead(id:)` queries with bead updates.

description:
PROBLEM
The internal/server package intermittently fails after otherwise successful tests because Go cannot remove a test-owned temporary project directory. Observed failures include TestUnpinnedEntryPointsLeaveModelSelectionToFizeau/server-managed leaving files beneath .ddx and TestWorkerSupervisor_ActiveBlockedTerminalConsumesOneDesiredSlot/does_not_suppress_all_starts_when_desired_count_exceeds_one leaving files beneath .ddx/workers. These unrelated tests share the same worker teardown helper.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor_test.go:1252-1271 implements stopProjectWorkers by calling WorkerManager.Stop and then waiting only until runningManagedWorkerCount returns zero.
cli/internal/server/workers.go:1684-1697 makes Stop set the in-memory worker state to stopped and return before the runWorker goroutine has completed.
cli/internal/server/workers.go:1332-1339 makes List overlay that stopped in-memory state, so runningManagedWorkerCount reaches zero while finalization is still active.
cli/internal/server/workers.go:1220-1293 subsequently records FinishedAt and writes the final status.json. That late write races removal of the test-owned project directory.
cli/internal/server/workers_resolve_route_test.go:213-216 and cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor_test.go:545-547 register the faulty helper in the two observed failing fixtures.
cli/internal/server/workers.go:1705-1806 already provides WorkerManager.Shutdown, which cancels live workers and waits for in-process runWorker finalization.

PROPOSED FIX
Replace the Stop-plus-state-poll implementation of stopProjectWorkers with a teardown path that delegates to WorkerManager.Shutdown and does not return until runWorker has written its final record.
If a separate error-returning test helper is useful, keep it private to internal/server tests and have stopProjectWorkers delegate to it.
Add TestStopProjectWorkersWaitsForRunWorkerFinalization. Use an injected ExecuteBeadWorker whose executor observes cancellation and then blocks on a test-controlled release channel. Start teardown asynchronously through the error-returning helper, prove teardown has not returned while finalization remains blocked, release the executor, then prove teardown returns, FinishedAt is persisted, and immediate removal of the fixture root succeeds.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change the asynchronous contract of WorkerManager.Stop.
Do not change managed subprocess termination, server supervisor cancellation deadlines, worker reconciliation, Fizeau routing, bead execution semantics, or production temporary-directory placement.
Do not weaken or skip either existing failing test.

PARENT
None. This is a standalone package-gate reliability defect.

DEPS
None. WorkerManager.Shutdown already implements the required join.
title: server tests: join in-process workers before fixture teardown

acceptance:
AC1. `ddx agent route-status reset` (or equivalent verb) exists and clears the trailing-window adaptive metric for the current project, returning min-tier evaluation to a clean baseline. Output names every file/store touched.

AC2. `ddx agent doctor` (or `ddx agent route-status`) prints current adaptive state per tier: window size, trailing attempts, success rate, threshold, current effective floor, and whether the tier is currently being skipped. Diagnostic output is enough to debug a 'why is cheap being skipped' scenario without reading source.

AC3. Routing failures classified as 'no viable provider', 'harness not installed', or 'configuration error' are recorded but EXCLUDED from the adaptive success-rate computation — only failures that reached an actual model invocation count.

AC4. Documentation in docs/ describes the adaptive min-tier mechanism, the metric store path and schema, the reset workflow, and the relationship between --no-adaptive-min-tier (temporary bypass) and reset (permanent state clear).

description:
work's adaptive min-tier promotion (escalation.AdaptiveMinTierThreshold etc.) silently skips cheap tier when trailing cheap-tier success rate falls under threshold. Today the only visible signal is a single log line:

  adaptive min-tier: skipping cheap tier (trailing success rate 0.00 over 9 attempts; threshold 0.20) — min-tier=standard

There is no documented or discoverable way to reset this state. Issues with the current design:

1. STATE LOCATION IS NOT DOCUMENTED. The trailing-window metric is computed from .ddx/agent-logs/routing-outcomes.jsonl per-project (and possibly other sources — rotating that file alone did NOT clear the 0% verdict in a recent test, so additional state may live elsewhere). A user who wants to reset cannot find authoritative documentation of where the state lives.

2. NO RESET CLI. There is no `ddx agent route-status reset`, no `ddx agent metrics clear`, no `ddx agent doctor --reset-adaptive`. The only path is to edit/truncate JSONL files by hand, which is fragile and breaks compatibility with any future schema.

3. SILENT NOISE. Every cheap-tier failure permanently affects future routing without surfacing to the user. If a configuration bug (e.g. the model_overrides issue tracked as ddx-5538aa5b) caused 9 immediate failures, the adaptive logic now blocks cheap tier even after the configuration is fixed. The user has no way to know 'this is stale state, not real performance signal' without reading source.

4. MITIGATION VIA --no-adaptive-min-tier IS NOT A FIX, IT'S AN OVERRIDE. The flag bypasses the gating but also defeats the legitimate purpose of the metric. We need ability to RESET the metric and re-evaluate from a clean slate, not permanently disable the feature.

5. THE THRESHOLD/WINDOW DEFAULTS ARE AGGRESSIVE. Trailing window of 9-50 attempts at threshold 0.20 means a single cheap-tier provider misconfiguration (which is easy to hit, see ddx-5538aa5b) condemns cheap-tier for many subsequent invocations. Meanwhile EVERY configuration error is recorded as cheap-tier failure even when the failure was 'no viable provider' rather than 'model produced bad output'.

Requested behavior:

- A first-class CLI: `ddx agent route-status reset [--scope cheap|all]` that clears the adaptive metric for the current project, with a confirm prompt by default.
- A flag on `ddx agent doctor` that displays current adaptive state per tier (success rate, attempt count, threshold, current floor) so users can SEE the problem.
- An option to record only EXECUTION outcomes (model produced output) in adaptive metrics, NOT no-viable-provider/configuration failures — those should be tracked separately and never count against a tier's reputation.
- Documented location and schema for the metric store, so users who want to inspect or surgically edit understand the on-disk format.

acceptance: Push-failure produces non-closing terminal status; bead remains open with last_status=push_failed and the push stderr captured; subsequent claims refuse until operator clears.
description:
**Reporter**: nexiq (downstream consumer). Observed across 2026-04-22 → 2026-04-26 on master.

## Observed

`ddx agent execute-bead` can land a commit locally (worktree merged into local master), then fail at the `git push origin master` step, and still classify the bead as `execute-bead: success`. The push failure shows up as `landed locally; push failed:` in the event body, but the bead transitions to closed and the loop moves on.

Concrete blast radius: ~969 unpushed commits accumulated on nexiq's master across multiple days because every bead that landed in that window had a 258 MB turbopack `.sst` file somewhere in its commit history. GitHub rejected each push with the 100 MB-per-file limit error. The work's success rate looked normal — operators saw bead = closed, dashboard = working — but origin was untouched.

Recovery required `git filter-branch --index-filter 'git rm --cached -r packages/web/.next .next'` across ~1000 commits plus a `.gitignore` hardening change. By that point the only signal that something was wrong was an operator manually running `git rev-list --count origin/master..master`.

## Root cause

The execute-bead orchestrator currently classifies the result of the *merge* step. The push step happens after, and a non-zero exit there is logged in the event body but does not bubble up to the bead's terminal status. As far as routing/state machines are concerned, the bead is done.

This is the worst-case classification: silent for operators, irreversible for state (bead closes, primary doesn't re-run, the work that needs to be re-pushed isn't tracked anywhere).

## Failure modes this masks

- Large blob in commit history (the case we hit) — every subsequent bead inherits the bad ancestor and fails to push.
- Auth expiration / credential rotation on the origin remote.
- Branch protection rules added on the remote between the loop's last successful push and now.
- HTTP 5xx / network flake against origin.
- Local divergence from origin (someone else pushed; non-fast-forward refused).

In all five cases the current behavior is: bead closes, loop picks the next bead, the divergence grows monotonically.

## Suggested fix

1. Promote push to a first-class step in execute-bead's outcome classification.
   - On non-zero exit from `git push`, emit `execute-bead: push_failed` (or similar terminal that explicitly is NOT success) with the push stderr captured in the event body.
   - Reopen the bead with `last_status=push_failed` and a retry_after that buys time for an operator to investigate.
2. Surface push failure on the next claim attempt: when a worker tries to claim a bead in `last_status=push_failed`, refuse the claim and show the operator the prior push stderr — don't blindly redo the primary work, since the local commit is already there.
3. (Optional, defense in depth) Have work maintain a per-repo divergence counter (`git rev-list --count origin/<branch>..<branch>`); if it crosses a threshold (e.g. >5), pause new claims and emit a loop-level warning event.

## Reproduction

1. On a local fork, install a `pre-receive` hook on the remote that rejects all pushes (or use a remote that requires a permission the runner doesn't have).
2. Queue any bead and run work normally.
3. Observe: bead closes as success despite the push failing. The merge commit lives only on local master.
4. Confirm: `git rev-list --count origin/master..master` is non-zero, but ddx still routed a new worker to the next bead.

## Files to inspect

- nexiq commit `f2c2ed33` (the .gitignore + .next scrub) is the recovery commit on the downstream side.
- nexiq's own follow-up bead (`nexiq-e57b41eb`) lists this as a blocker; I'll amend it once this ddx bead has an ID.

## Acceptance

- A forced push failure (e.g. pre-receive hook rejecting) results in a bead that does NOT show as closed and shows up in `ddx bead list --status open` with a `last_status=push_failed` field.
- The operator can see the push stderr in the bead's events.
- Subsequent claim attempts on that bead fail loudly until the operator clears the state (retry, force-skip, etc.).
title: agent/execute-bead: classify failed git push as a hard failure (do not close bead)

description:
PROBLEM

DDx parses `triage.estimated_difficulty`, but production `ddx work` and `ddx try` do not apply it to the initial Fizeau request. An unpinned ordinary bead therefore starts with `MinPower=0`, while the parsed difficulty is used only as `cheap`/`standard`/`smart` telemetry. The command paths also use one overbroad “any routing flag” predicate, so immutable Harness, Provider, Model, or MaxPower constraints suppress difficulty inference even though only an explicit MinPower or public Fizeau Policy should do so. Configuration still accepts `agent.routing.profile_priority`, and current routing-intent evidence records profile/power-class vocabulary instead of the requested numeric policy boundary.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE

- `cli/internal/escalation/powerinfer.go:20-27,61-70` maps difficulty through DDx `PowerClass` values rather than directly to Fizeau’s public numeric MinPower scale.
- `cli/internal/escalation/execution_hint.go:21-35,53-72,95-108` carries `InferredPowerClass` and suppresses all difficulty inference through broad `ExplicitRouting`/`ProjectRouting` booleans.
- `cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:206-211` treats Harness, Provider, Model, Profile, MinPower, and MaxPower alike when deciding whether inference is allowed. `cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:505-519` calculates routing intent but seeds the first work attempt only from `rcfg.MinPower()`.
- `cli/cmd/try.go:253-256,283-295,410-417` has the same overbroad suppression and starts the try ladder from the CLI `minPower` value without applying the bead/readiness estimate.
- `cli/internal/config/types.go:498-508`, `cli/internal/config/schema/config.schema.json:458-471`, and `cli/internal/config/clone.go:37-47` still model and accept `profile_priority`. `cli/internal/config/config.go:30-54,131-136` rejects other retired routing fields but merely warns for this one.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:5449-5598` and `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_routing_evidence_test.go:147-234` record `requested_profile` and `requested_power_class` rather than `requested_policy`, `inferred_min_power`, and the resolved requested power bounds.
- Current regressions in `cli/cmd/work_test.go:541-640` and `cli/cmd/try_test.go:601-738` explicitly lock the missing behavior by expecting an absent/medium bead to dispatch with `MinPower=0`.

PROPOSED FIX

- Replace difficulty-to-PowerClass inference with `InferInitialMinPower` or an equivalently small numeric helper. It must map `easy -> 0`, `medium -> 7`, `hard -> 9`, and nil/absent/invalid -> `7`. It must ignore `triage.power_hint`, `power:*` labels, priority, issue type, kind, prose length, acceptance length, and every other numeric bead field.
- Carry numeric inferred MinPower plus explicit presence through `ExecutionHint`; preserve the distinction between inferred `easy=0` and “inference suppressed.” Do not query Fizeau catalogs, policies, profiles, models, providers, harnesses, or route viability.
- Separate inference precedence from passthrough/retry eligibility. Only an explicit operator MinPower or a non-empty public Fizeau Policy suppresses inference. The current CLI calls that policy input `--profile`; preserve its bytes and forward it as `ServiceExecuteRequest.Policy` without interpreting its value.
- Harness, Provider, Model, and MaxPower remain byte-identical sticky constraints but do not suppress the initial inferred MinPower. If the inferred floor conflicts with MaxPower or another constraint, surface the existing request-shape or typed Fizeau error; do not clamp, remove, widen, or repair either constraint.
- Seed both production `ddx work` and `ddx try` first attempts from the resolved inferred MinPower when inference is active. Authored bead difficulty wins over transient readiness difficulty; transient readiness applies to the current request only and never mutates bead metadata.
- Add `profile_priority` to `checkRoutingMigration`, remove it from accepted config types/schema/clone behavior, delete the warning path, and replace acceptance/warning tests with a `RoutingMigrationError` regression.
- Record `routing_intent_source`, normalized `estimated_difficulty`, `inferred_min_power`, `requested_policy`, `requested_min_power`, `requested_max_power`, and Fizeau-returned actual route facts. `easy` must record inferred zero rather than look suppressed. Concrete Harness/Provider/Model identity is audit-only; only public abstract ActualPower may contribute to a permitted later MinPower decision.

description:
Sixth and final child of ddx-b7ee0d6f. The axon divergence happened partly because the multi-machine topology was never written down. Two machines (eitri and sindri) both ran work against the same project, neither was designated authoritative, and nobody had defined the pull/push contract. The result was predictable once you look at it, but there was no document that said 'this is wrong' before it happened.

## Required documentation

Write docs/EXECUTE-LOOP.md (or expand the ddx README) covering:

### Topology models

**Single-machine solo**: one machine, one work. No coordination needed beyond the fetch/push/rebase triad (ddx-bd42f640, ddx-83ec1430, ddx-6aa50e57).

**Primary + secondary(s)**: one machine is authoritative (pushes to origin). Secondaries pull-only — they can run the work if and only if the fetch bead guarantees they fast-forward from origin before every bead, and they refuse to land any work locally. Useful for running review/eval passes in parallel without forking.

**Peer mesh**: multiple machines all push to origin. Each must implement the fetch → verify ancestry → rebase → push invariant from the P0 beads. Requires the tracker concurrency bead (ddx-2791dc4f) to be solved or all machines will step on each other's beads.jsonl.

### Invariants

- Before claiming a bead: local HEAD must be a strict ancestor of origin/<default-branch> (or equal). If not, refuse to claim.
- After landing a bead successfully: push --ff-only or mark land_conflict and stop. Never leave work trapped locally.
- Between sibling workers on the same machine: rebase onto the latest master, never merge.
- Every bead claim must be visible to every other work before the claimer starts work (tracker concurrency).

### Operator runbook

- How to add a new worker machine safely (fresh clone + verify divergence is 0 + start loop)
- How to recover from a diverged state (the current axon situation): reconcile manually, reset secondaries to origin, restart loops
- How to migrate existing diverged projects to the new safety model (one-time cleanup)
- How to stop all works globally (e.g., during a freeze window)

### Troubleshooting

- 'divergence_detected' event: what caused it and how to recover
- 'push_rejected' event: what caused it and how to recover
- 'checkpoint before merge' commits in history: legacy pattern, should not appear after ddx-6aa50e57 lands
- Multiple 'Merge made by ort' commits: same as above, legacy pattern

### ADR reference

Once the tracker concurrency bead (ddx-2791dc4f) picks option A / B / C, cite the ADR here so operators understand the coordination model.

## Why this matters

The P0 beads will prevent future divergence, but operators need to understand WHY the rules exist to avoid bypassing them with --force or manual git operations. Documentation is what keeps the fixes effective a year from now.
title: work: document multi-machine topology and operator contract

description:
PROBLEM
The mandatory `cd cli && go test -short -race -timeout 30m ./internal/agent` gate recursively launches the package test binary as DDx's hidden provider wrapper. During attempt `20260713T190502-df5adc46`, the parent `agent.test` spawned five concurrent `agent.test __provider-launch <real-provider>` helpers for more than three minutes, grew a 666 MB testlog, and left a real `codex --no-alt-screen` process reparented to the managed worker for 12 minutes at about 188 MiB RSS. This makes the package gate itself create the CPU/memory/orphan condition it is supposed to prevent.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:102-113` calls `os.Executable()` unconditionally and passes that path to `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH`.
- `cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:152-163` repeats the same unconditional installation for the resolved-service path.
- `cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go:83-118` writes each shim as `<ddxBinary> __provider-launch <realBinary>`. Under `go test`, `os.Executable()` is `agent.test`, not the DDx CLI and it has no Cobra `__provider-launch` dispatch. Re-executing it starts the test suite again; the recursive process can install shims and launch real providers that escape the original gate process group.
- `cli/cmd/provider_launch.go:25-68` is the actual hidden-command implementation, and exists only in the DDx CLI command graph.

PROPOSED FIX
Introduce one injectable resolver for the provider-wrapper executable and use it from both service call sites. In package-test builds, install a suite-wide test resolver/guard that refuses to use the current `agent.test` executable as a provider wrapper while leaving direct `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH` tests free to supply an explicit real/fake DDx CLI binary. Fail closed with actionable evidence if a test fixture attempts to install a provider shim from a Go test binary. Preserve production PATH shim, `Pdeathsig`, process-group, and real CLI hidden-command behavior.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not remove provider parent-death protection in production.
- Do not replace Fizeau routing or provider discovery.
- Do not weaken the full `internal/agent` race gate or merely increase its timeout.
- Do not kill unrelated provider processes from other repositories.
- Scanner injection remains owned by `ddx-02200b1e`; fixture-specific spawn tripwires remain owned by `ddx-26bf19c7`.

PARENT AND DEPS
Root reliability bug. No implementation deps. Cross-references: `ddx-02200b1e` and `ddx-26bf19c7`.

description:
PROBLEM
After rebuilding/installing `ddx` from commit `2193aa658` and restarting `ddx-server.service` on 2026-06-16, the server came up healthy but with no child workers. Desired workers for `/Users/erik/Projects/ddx` and `/Users/erik/Projects/sesame` did not all restart until manual `ddx worker start` / `ddx worker reconcile` calls. `ddx worker start --project /Users/erik/Projects/ddx` saved desired state but printed only `{"desired_count":1,...}`; a separate `ddx worker reconcile --project /Users/erik/Projects/ddx` was needed before `worker-20260616T084349-8105` appeared. Server-managed workers are not reliable if boot requires an operator nudge.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/server/server.go:349-350` writes the address file and calls `reconcileDesiredWorkersAfterStartup()` before `http.ListenAndServeTLS` enters Serve.
- `cli/internal/server/server.go:364-381` performs delayed reconcile attempts in a goroutine, but the live service still had a window/state where no desired workers were running after restart.
- `cli/internal/server/server.go:397-429` discovers project roots only from `s.WorkingDir` and `s.state.GetProjects(false)` plus existing desired-state files; a missing/stale project registration or delayed state load can skip desired projects at startup.
- `cli/internal/server/worker_supervisor.go:125-137` treats absent desired-state as manage-nothing, so any skipped root produces no worker and no visible startup failure.
- `cli/cmd/worker.go:135-176` proves the manual `ddx worker start` path saves desired state then explicitly calls the reconcile endpoint, which succeeded where startup reconciliation did not.

PROPOSED FIX
Make startup reconciliation deterministic and observable. On server startup, every project with `.ddx/workers/desired.json` or a registered desired state must be reconciled after the listener is accepting requests, and failures must be surfaced in server logs/status rather than silently leaving desired workers absent. Add an integration-style regression that starts a real server instance with desired state for at least two projects, waits through startup reconciliation, and asserts workers are launched without calling the reconcile endpoint manually.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change worker claim authority or make the server own bead claims.
- Do not disable manual `ddx worker start` / `ddx worker reconcile`; they remain operator controls.
- Do not change federation worker forwarding.

PARENT + DEPS
Parent: `ddx-d5dfa702`.
Deps: none. Related to `ddx-c713d75e`, but this is specifically restart/desired-state reconciliation, not count caps or audit fields.
title: server: restart must restore desired managed workers

description:
PROBLEM
  Per sister bead "docs(ADR): formalize 3-tier evidence storage",
  the local-tier comprises three paths that share a lifecycle:
    - .ddx/executions/<attempt-id>/ (full evidence bundle)
    - .ddx/agent-logs/agent-*.jsonl (raw model session)
    - .ddx/workers/worker-*/ (per-worker runtime state)

  These three are pruned together (sister bead B29 RetainDays).
  When operators want longer-term archival (beyond the 90-day
  retention) they need a mirror — but the mirror must cover all
  three paths together, not just executions/. Today's
  ExecutionsMirrorConfig (cli/internal/config/types.go:253-259)
  is unwired and was scoped to executions only.

CURRENT STATE
  - ExecutionsMirrorConfig: declared, unused, executions-only.
  - No code path copies agent-logs or workers to any external
    location.
  - When B29 prunes locally, anything not archived is lost.

PROPOSED FIX
  Implement a mirror hook-point that operates on the local-tier
  BUNDLE for each completed attempt.

  1. Rename / generalize the config:
     - cli/internal/config/types.go: add LocalEvidenceMirrorConfig
       (or rename ExecutionsMirrorConfig). Fields:
         kind: local-dir | none (default none; remote backends
               like s3 are future scope)
         path: target directory (for local-dir kind)
         retention_days: independent of in-tree RetainDays
         include_agent_logs: bool (default true)
         include_workers: bool (default false; workers are
                          large and rarely useful retrospectively)

  2. Implement local-dir backend:
     - cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go (or a new
       cli/internal/agent/evidence_mirror.go): on attempt
       finalization, copy:
         a. The full .ddx/executions/<attempt-id>/ directory
            to <mirror-path>/executions/<attempt-id>/.
         b. The agent-log for the attempt's session_id (if
            include_agent_logs) to <mirror-path>/agent-logs/.
         c. The worker dir (if include_workers and attempt
            corresponds to a worker) to <mirror-path>/workers/.
     - Files are copied (not moved) so the local copies remain
       for the RetainDays window.

  3. Mirror retention:
     - The mirror has its own retention_days independent of the
       in-tree RetainDays.
     - Pruning the mirror is a separate concern (a sibling
       method, or an operator-run command). For v1, just
       implement the copy; document that the mirror must be
       pruned manually OR via an external retention policy.

  4. Failure modes:
     - Copy failure: log a warning, emit a structured event
       (mirror-copy-failed), continue execution. Do NOT block
       attempt finalization on mirror failure.
     - Disk full at mirror destination: same — log + continue.
     - Mirror path doesn't exist: log + continue (or auto-create
       on first attempt, configurable).

  Tests:
     - TestMirror_CopiesExecutionDir
     - TestMirror_CopiesAgentLog
     - TestMirror_CopiesWorkerDirWhenIncluded
     - TestMirror_SkipsWorkerDirWhenExcluded
     - TestMirror_CopyFailure_DoesNotBlockFinalization
     - TestMirror_PathAutoCreate

NON-SCOPE
  - Remote backends (S3, GCS, etc.) — deferred to follow-up bead.
  - Mirror compression / tarball formats — deferred.
  - Mirror pruning / retention automation — deferred (operators
    manage mirror retention out-of-band for v1).
  - Federation cross-machine sync — separate concern.

INTERSECTIONS
  - Sister bead "docs(ADR)" — defines the 3-tier architecture
    this implements.
  - Sister bead B29 (RetainDays) — copy MUST happen before the
    prune deletes local content. Ordering: in-attempt
    finalization → mirror copy → RetainDays runs on its own
    cadence (cleanup loop).
  - Sister bead "feat(metrics)" — metrics row extraction happens
    independently of mirror; both fire on finalization.
  - Sister bead "refactor(vocab): rename run-id → attempt-id" —
    mirror dir naming follows the canonical attempt-id.

description:
## Symptom

Every `llm.response` event in `.ddx/agent-logs/agent-claude-*.jsonl` has `latency_ms == elapsed_ms`. Examples from agent-claude-1776370404950042448.jsonl:

```jsonl
{"data":{"elapsed_ms":7373, "latency_ms":7373, "turn":1, ...}}
{"data":{"elapsed_ms":7995, "latency_ms":7995, "turn":2, ...}}
{"data":{"elapsed_ms":12054,"latency_ms":12054,"turn":3, ...}}
```

`elapsed_ms` is monotonic across the session (cumulative wall time), so per-call LLM latency is unrecoverable from the log.

## Impact

- Cannot answer "what was the LLM-side latency for turn N?" — required for any performance investigation.
- Cannot diff the agent's local-LLM benchmark numbers against captured traces.
- The lucebox-hub/dflash bench_server.py harness needs real per-call latency to validate against reality.

## Likely root cause

Logging code in `cli/internal/agent/session_log_format.go` (or equivalent emit site) is writing the wrong value into `latency_ms`. Probably copy-paste from the elapsed-time field. Per-call latency should be `t_response_received - t_request_sent` for that single call.

## Fix sketch

Capture the per-call latency inside the harness adapter (point where the LLM HTTP call is made) and pass it through to the event emitter. Add a unit test asserting `latency_ms < elapsed_ms` for any non-first event.
title: BUG: latency_ms field in agent-claude-*.jsonl traces equals cumulative elapsed_ms

description:
<context-digest>
Alpha validation run from /Users/erik/Projects/helix using `ddx agent work --once --json` against a live HELIX queue. Evidence includes the generated execution bundle `.ddx/executions/20260411T011535-bbda19d7`, worktree `.ddx/.execute-bead-wt-helix-fef22846-20260411T011535-bbda19d7`, and the current work implementation in `cli/internal/bead/store.go` and `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go`.
</context-digest>

`ddx agent work` selected and launched an open `epic` bead from the HELIX execution queue instead of a bounded executable bead.

## Reproduction
1. In `/Users/erik/Projects/helix`, run `ddx bead ready --json --execution`.
2. Observe the first candidate is `helix-fef22846`, `issue_type=epic`, title `Audit deleted HELIX artifact types for restoration or retirement`.
3. Run `ddx agent work --once --json`.
4. Observe DDx creates `.ddx/.execute-bead-wt-helix-fef22846-20260411T011535-bbda19d7` and `.ddx/executions/20260411T011535-bbda19d7/manifest.json` with `bead_id=helix-fef22846`.

## Observed gap
`ReadyExecution()` currently treats any open, unblocked bead as execution-ready unless `execution-eligible=false`, `superseded-by`, or cooldown metadata says otherwise. `work` then takes the first candidate without a stronger structural execution screen. That behavior is weaker than the API-001 execute-bead supervisor contract, which says the loop should run a generic execution-ready validator against ordered candidates before launch.

## Why this matters
Open epics represent umbrella planning/decomposition work, not necessarily a bounded workspace transform. Launching them directly makes queue-drain behavior unstable and can strand the loop on non-executable work even when bounded tasks are ready behind the epic.

description:
PROBLEM

Operators need to explicitly order the DDx queue. Today `ddx bead create --set queue-rank=0` stores the rank (verified by `ddx bead show`), but `ddx bead ready --json` still lists older priority-0 beads ahead of the newly ranked bead. That means a custom field is not enough in the live backend: `ddx work` can ignore the operator's intended top-of-queue item. This directly blocks forcing urgent dogfood findings, such as provider-process failure classification, to the front of the queue.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE

- `cli/internal/bead/operation.go:8-31` defines `QueueSetTop` / `QueueSetPosition` as `Extra["queue-rank"]` mutations, so the intended model is a numeric rank within the priority bucket.
- `cli/internal/bead/gaps_test.go:58-73` and `:104-120` prove JSONL store ready and execution-ready sorting honors `Extra["queue-rank"]`, but the live queue did not place `ddx-ef9df563` (priority 0, `queue-rank=0`) ahead of unranked priority-0 beads.
- `cli/internal/bead/store.go:2715-2716` sorts from `beads[i].Extra["queue-rank"]`; if the active backend exposes custom fields as top-level JSON/show output but does not hydrate `Bead.Extra`, sorting silently treats ranked beads as unranked.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:4997-5011` delegates worker picking to `PreviewQueue` and `ReadyExecution`, so any backend rank hydration bug affects both `ddx bead ready` and `ddx work`.

PROPOSED FIX

Make queue rank a first-class numeric field in the ready/work ordering contract across storage backends. Either hydrate `queue-rank` into `Bead.Extra` for every backend before sort, or add explicit accessors that read both Extra and backend/custom-field storage. Add command-level coverage proving `ddx bead create --set queue-rank=0`, `ddx bead update --set queue-rank=N`, and any queue helper command affect `ddx bead ready --json`, `ddx bead ready --execution --json`, `PreviewQueue`, and `ddx work` candidate selection.

NON-SCOPE

Do not replace priority buckets; rank sorts within priority unless the operator also changes priority. Do not hand-edit tracker storage. Do not rely only on JSONL tests; cover the active Axon/current backend path used by this repository.
title: queue: honor explicit numeric rank in ready and work ordering

description:
PROBLEM
Candidate-cycle worktrees will live longer than today because implementation, checks, review, and repair can run in one attempt worktree. Cleanup and crash recovery need a hardening pass after the new pipeline exists so stale resources are reclaimed without deleting active review/repair state.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:754-767 writes cleanup metadata and immediately defers WorktreeRemove for today's short-lived attempt model.
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:104-124 preserves worktrees based on run-state/liveness/preserved metadata, but does not know candidate-cycle phases, candidate refs, or repair loops.
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:245-260 preserves live candidates when the liveness probe says live, but recovery of pinned candidate refs after crash is not tied to candidate-cycle events.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:508-510 and 558 run cleanup passes before claims; those passes must not reclaim active candidate-cycle worktrees.

PROPOSED FIX
- Extend cleanup metadata/run-state with candidate-cycle phase, candidate_ref, candidate_rev, cycle_index, and repair/review liveness where needed.
- Recover or preserve latest pinned candidate after crash before cleanup removes the worktree.
- Reclaim stale unpinned candidate-cycle worktrees and prune temporary candidate refs according to the retention policy from the spec bead.
- Add resource-pressure behavior that reports long active cycles without deleting them.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not redesign the candidate-cycle coordinator.
- Do not change review classification or repair routing policy.

title: cleanup: harden active-cycle recovery and stale cleanup

description:
Follow-up to ddx-f8a11202. Once per-field size caps (65,535 bytes) are enforced on the write side, existing beads.jsonl files in the wild may already contain rows that violate the constraint — e.g. the 1.46MB row that surfaced the original bug, plus any similar rows on other machines / branches that haven't been hand-trimmed yet.

Add a tracker-repair capability:

- Detection: `ddx bead doctor` scans the project's beads.jsonl, flags rows whose fields exceed the per-field cap, and reports them with bead id, field name, and current size. No mutation.
- Repair: `ddx bead doctor --fix` offers to rewrite the oversized fields in place. Overflow content persists as a new artifact under .ddx/executions/<bead-id>/repair-<timestamp>/<field>.log and the field's in-place value becomes a truncated summary plus artifact path reference (same shape as the write-side overflow path f8a11202 establishes).
- Safety: before any rewrite, write a backup of the original beads.jsonl to .ddx/backups/beads-<timestamp>.jsonl. Print the backup path before proceeding. Operator must confirm (or pass --yes).
- Audit trail: append a repair event to each rewritten bead (kind=repair, actor=ddx-bead-doctor, body=summary of which fields were truncated and to what artifact paths).

Scope: only the per-field cap from f8a11202. Do not generalize into a broader bead validator here — separate bead if we want JSON schema enforcement or dep-graph lint.
title: bead doctor: detect and repair oversized fields in existing beads.jsonl

description:
PROBLEM
When a spoke node starts with --hub-address, it must register with the hub and maintain a heartbeat so the hub's FederationRegistry knows the spoke is alive. Today no --hub-address flag exists and no spoke lifecycle (register / heartbeat / stale detection / URL-change re-register) is implemented.

ROOT CAUSE
- cli/internal/server/server.go: no --hub-address flag wired.
- cli/internal/federation/: no spoke-side registration client or heartbeat loop exists.
- The hub's FederationRegistry (from ddx-90f48012, a dep) provides the register endpoint and stale detection, but the spoke side has no code to call it.
- Per locked decisions from the federation planning: register is idempotent on stable node_id; duplicate node_id rejected (not silently merged); heartbeat jittered at 30s; stale threshold at 2 minutes.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add --hub-address string flag to the server command (cli/cmd/server.go or equivalent).
- Add cli/internal/federation/spoke_lifecycle.go:
  - RegisterWithHub(ctx, hubAddress, nodeID, localURL): idempotent POST to hub register endpoint.
  - StartHeartbeat(ctx, hubAddress, nodeID): jittered 30s heartbeat loop; on failure → stale detection.
  - HandleURLChange(ctx, hubAddress, nodeID, newURL): re-register when local URL flips.
- Stale threshold: hub marks spoke offline after 2 minutes without heartbeat.

NON-SCOPE
- Hub-side registry implementation (ddx-90f48012, a dep).
- Federation query fan-out (existing fanout.go).
- Mutation routing (S15-7b / ddx-eb75a32d).

acceptance:
**User story:** As an operator on any page in the project, I always see whether a drain worker is running and how much work is queued. One click takes me to the worker overview where I can scale capacity up or down with a single button, without picking a harness or profile every time.

**Acceptance criteria:**

1. **Nav indicator visible everywhere.**
   - A component in `NavShell.svelte` renders the drain indicator on every route inside a selected project.
   - Idle state: dot + "Queue: X ready".
   - Active state: spinner + "N workers · X ready".
   - Clicking navigates to the workers overview.
   - Playwright: navigate to beads, documents, sessions, efficacy — assert indicator is present on each with the expected text.

2. **Live updates.**
   - The indicator updates within 2s when a worker starts, finishes, or changes state. Backed by the existing worker-progress subscription.
   - When ready-bead count changes (a bead is created/closed), the indicator updates within 5s. Either subscription-driven or short poll.

3. **Summary query.**
   - New `queueAndWorkersSummary(projectId) { readyBeads runningWorkers totalWorkers }`. Returns zeros on unknown or empty projects — no error.
   - Resolver is cheap: reads the ready count from the same path bead-status queries use, not by iterating every bead.

4. **Overview page — count control.**
   - Header shows "Drain workers: N" prominently.
   - `+ Add worker` button dispatches a default-spec worker (`workerDispatch(kind: "work", args: null)`). On success the row appears in the table within 2s and the indicator updates.
   - `− Remove worker` button stops the oldest-running drain worker. Confirm-gated ("Stop worker-XYZ?"). After confirm, the worker transitions to `stopped` within 2s.
   - Help text below the buttons: "Adds a general-purpose drain worker. Use the per-harness picker below for custom specs."

5. **Default-spec + safety rail.**
   - `.ddx/config.yaml: workers.default_spec` is respected by `+ Add worker`. Integration test asserts a configured `profile: cheap` is propagated.
   - `.ddx/config.yaml: workers.max_count`: when set, `+ Add worker` refuses past the cap; button disabled with tooltip "at workers.max_count limit". Not set → no cap. Integration test covers both.

6. **Playwright — flow.**
   - Seeds a project with 3 ready beads, zero workers.
   - Asserts indicator shows "Queue: 3 ready", dot state.
   - Clicks indicator → navigates to overview.
   - Clicks `+ Add worker` → asserts new row and indicator transitions to spinner + "1 worker · 3 ready".
   - Clicks `+` again → asserts "2 workers · 3 ready".
   - Clicks `− Remove worker` → asserts one worker stops and indicator shows "1 worker · ..." within 2s.
   - Navigates to /beads → asserts indicator persists and stays live.

7. **No regressions.**
   - Existing Drain button on project home continues to work (dispatches the same kind). Can stay or be removed depending on design note; recommend keeping it as the initial-kickoff affordance when zero workers run.
   - Existing Workers table rendering + live-phase subscription is unchanged.
   - Existing per-worker Start/Stop from `ddx-69789664` coexists unchanged.

8. **Cross-references.**
   - Hard dependency: `ddx-05b4cc9d` (fixes `workersByProject` filter — without it, the running-workers count is always 0 on a per-project query).
   - Adjacent: `ddx-69789664` (per-worker lifecycle + Sessions IA). These beads are complementary; implementation should not re-introduce either's functionality, just use it.
   - Adjacent: `ddx-9ce6842a` (perf harness). The `queueAndWorkersSummary` resolver gets a perf target in that harness: p95 ≤ 30ms in-process on a 5k-bead fixture. No full scan allowed.
description:
## Observed / Motivation

Today the queue-drain worker is invisible unless the operator is on the project home page or the Workers tab. An operator on any other page (Beads, Documents, Efficacy) has no idea whether a drain is active, how many ready beads are left, or whether they should kick off more capacity. The per-project home page's "Drain queue" button is one-shot and offers no scaling control — you start one worker and that's it.

User feedback: the drain should be a **top-level always-visible affordance** with:
1. A persistent spinner/badge in the global nav showing drain state + an at-a-glance count (ready beads, running workers).
2. Clicking the badge goes to a workers overview where the operator can see what each worker is doing.
3. That overview needs a "number of workers" control — `Add worker` / `Remove worker` to scale drain capacity up or down, not just start-one-at-a-time.

## Why this is a new surface, not just a tweak to existing Workers page

- **Global spinner** is a nav-shell concern, not a page concern. It needs to be mounted in `NavShell.svelte` so every route sees it.
- **Worker-count control** is a different interaction model from the per-worker Start/Stop flow proposed in `ddx-69789664`. That flow is "pick a harness + effort + filter, start one worker with those specs." This flow is "I want N general-purpose drain workers; add/remove one at a time." Both should coexist.
- A **worker-count affordance** implies a default worker spec (default harness, default profile). That's fine — it mirrors `ddx work` with no flags — but it has to be explicit so the operator knows what they're spawning.

## Scope

### Part 1 — Global drain indicator in `NavShell`

- New element in the top nav bar, visible on every route (fits next to the theme toggle).
- Two states:
  - **Idle** (zero running drain workers): subtle dot + "Queue: X ready" (where X is project-scoped ready-bead count). Clicking navigates to the workers view.
  - **Active** (≥1 running drain worker): animated spinner + "N workers · X ready". Clicking navigates to the workers view.
- Data: new lightweight query `queueAndWorkersSummary(projectId) { readyBeads, runningWorkers, totalWorkers }`, subscribes to worker-progress events to stay fresh.
- Scope: tied to the currently-selected project in the `ProjectPicker`. If no project is selected, the indicator is hidden.
- Perf: the query must be cheap — must not trigger the N·M scan already tracked in `ddx-9ce6842a`. Depends on those fixes for the ready-bead count.

### Part 2 — Workers overview with count control

- Repurpose the existing `/workers` route (or add a separate `/workers/overview` — design call) to include a header section with:
  - Large "Drain workers: N" number.
  - `+` button ("Add worker") — dispatches a new default-spec drain worker via the existing `workerDispatch(kind: "work")` mutation.
  - `−` button ("Remove worker") — stops the oldest-running drain worker. Confirm-gated.
  - Small help text: "Adds a general-purpose queue-drain worker. Use the per-harness picker below for custom specs."
- The existing per-worker table and per-row Start/Stop (from `ddx-69789664`) remain for fine control.
- "Default spec" is: harness unset (route via profile), profile `default`, no effort override. Operator can change the project default in config.

### Part 3 — Defaults + config

- `.ddx/config.yaml: workers.default_spec` — object with optional harness, profile, effort, min_tier, max_tier. Used by Part 2's `+ Add worker`. Unset = use `ddx work` defaults.
- `.ddx/config.yaml: workers.max_count` — optional safety rail, default unset. When set, `+ Add worker` refuses past the cap and tooltips "at workers.max_count limit".

### Part 4 — Empty/error states

- Indicator on a project with no ready beads and zero workers: "Queue: 0 ready — nothing to drain". Clicking still navigates (so operator can spawn one anyway).
- Indicator when the per-project workers query is broken (pre-`ddx-05b4cc9d`): falls back to the global count; logs a one-time console warning.
- Add-worker failure: surfaces inline on the overview page (error toast + detail), doesn't silently drop.

## Out of scope

- Per-harness-specific queue views (e.g., "drain with codex" as a distinct indicator).
- Bead prioritization rules for multi-worker draining — beads already have a priority field, and `work` already claims in ready-order. No change.
- Concurrency safety review of multi-worker draining. It already works (beads are claimed atomically), but if `ddx-05b4cc9d` surfaces issues there, file a follow-up.
notes:
**`+layout.svelte` (workers overview)**: The `+ Add worker` button has no awareness of `workers.max_count`. The AC requires the button to be **disabled with a tooltip** ("at workers.max_count limit") when the cap is reached, rather than allowing the click and surfacing a server error. This needs the `queueAndWorkersSummary` query (or a new field) to expose the cap, and the button's `disabled` binding to incorporate it.
**`workers.spec.ts`**: The e2e test asserts `dispatchCalled` and `stopCalled` booleans but does not verify the **indicator text transitions** after add/remove. AC #6 explicitly requires asserting "1 worker · 3 ready" after the first add, "2 workers · 3 ready" after the second add, and updated text after remove. The test also only clicks `+` once, not twice as the AC specifies. The mock's `QueueAndWorkersSummary` handler dynamically computes `runningWorkers` from the mocked `workers` array, so the data is available — the assertions are just missing.

**`DrainIndicator.svelte:75-85`** — poll-only refresh via 3s `setInterval`. AC #2 requires subscription-driven updates (`subscribeWorkerProgress`) so worker-state changes reflect within 2s. Add a `workerProgress` subscription (filtered to the current project) that triggers `refresh(projectId)` on every event, keeping the 3s poll only as a backstop for ready-bead count changes.
title: Persistent drain-queue worker indicator in nav + N-worker count control on dashboard

description:
Finding from fresh-eyes review of passthrough-only provider/model/harness flags.

Problem:
The plan says --harness, --provider, and --model are passthrough-only and sticky across retries, but it does not specify the terminal behavior when those hard pins make a higher MinPower request unsatisfiable or otherwise prevent escalation. The upstream agent contract says exact pins remain hard constraints and are not widened by escalation.

Why this matters:
If DDx retries blindly when a hard pin prevents stronger routing, it either loops uselessly or is tempted to reinterpret/override passthrough pins. Either outcome violates the boundary: DDx must not route, widen, downgrade, or fallback provider/model choices.

Required fix:
Define a typed terminal classification such as blocked_by_passthrough_constraint or agent_power_unsatisfied. DDx should preserve the original passthrough envelope, record the agent-supplied incompatibility/exhaustion evidence, stop retrying, and report operator action required. DDx must not remove pins, choose alternatives, or call ResolveRoute to preflight around the issue.

Acceptance:
- FEAT-006/FEAT-010 document hard-pin exhaustion behavior.
- ddx-20047dd5 and ddx-9f82f325 include implementation and tests for passthrough-plus-power conflict.
- A retry from MinPower N to N+M with a pinned low-power model stops with a typed blocked result rather than mutating the pin or looping.
- Audit output shows requested MinPower/MaxPower, passthrough pins, agent-reported actual/attempted model evidence when available, and the terminal classification.
title: review finding: specify stop semantics for passthrough pins that cap escalation

description:
Operators should not need to author any project-level routing config (.ddx/config.yaml, --harness, --profile, --model, --provider) for `ddx work` to drain a project's bead queue. The platform should auto-select harness, model, and provider based on bead complexity, retry/fall back on failures, and decompose work that is too coarse for one dispatch.

## Observed behavior (HELIX project, 2026-05-01)

Running `ddx work --once --local` from `/Users/erik/Projects/helix`:

```
warning: triage complexity gate is disabled; coarse beads may waste dispatch attempts
▶ helix-13cfe23f: Align HELIX execution contract to shipped DDx work / execute-bead capabilities
✓ helix-13cfe23f → error: routing under-specified: pass at least one of Harness/Profile/ModelRef/Model/Provider, or auto-selection inputs
project: /Users/erik/Projects/helix
completed: 1  |  successes: 0  |  failures: 1
```

Workarounds tried, all failed or were rejected by users as the wrong layer to address this:

1. `ddx work --once --local --profile cheap` — same routing-under-specified error.
2. `ddx work --once --local --harness openrouter` — `harness "openrouter": no configured provider matches type "openrouter" (available: [])`, despite `~/.config/agent/config.yaml` having multiple openrouter-typed providers.
3. `--min-tier cheap` — unknown flag.

By contrast, the same `ddx work` invocation succeeds for the DDx project itself — workers in `ddx server workers list` show recent successful runs against ddx-* beads. So the per-project config gap is the difference, not anything global.

## Expected behavior

`ddx work` (and `ddx agent work` directly) should:

1. Auto-select routing for each bead with no flags and no project config required, given that the global agent config (`~/.config/agent/config.yaml`) has providers configured.
2. Make routing decisions from bead complexity: doc-only or single-file changes → cheap tier; multi-file refactors → standard; cross-cutting work → smart. The 'triage complexity gate' warning suggests this exists but is disabled by default.
3. Retry on transient failure within the same tier; escalate to a higher tier on substantive failure (this is documented behavior — `winning_tier=exhausted` events show the escalation chain works once dispatched, but auto-routing has to dispatch first).
4. When a bead is too coarse for any tier to execute reliably, either decompose it into child beads or surface a 'needs operator triage' status with a clear reason — never silently wedge with `routing under-specified`.
5. Default to using the global agent config's `default_provider` when no project override exists, instead of treating the absence of project config as a hard error.

## Why this matters

- **Adoption friction**: Every new project that adopts DDx hits this wall. Authoring `.ddx/config.yaml` requires understanding DDx's routing internals before an operator can run `ddx work` once.
- **Methodology coupling**: HELIX's value proposition includes 'supervised autopilot' — the autopilot is supposed to drain ready beads. When `ddx work` requires per-project routing config, HELIX projects have to ship operational setup that distracts from the methodology.
- **Operator surprise**: The DDx-vs-HELIX boundary contract (HELIX/CONTRACT-001) explicitly says HELIX should not own routing config. But projects can't run `ddx work` without it. That's a contract violation manifesting as setup burden.
- **Triage gate disabled by default**: The warning 'triage complexity gate is disabled; coarse beads may waste dispatch attempts' is emitted on every run but the operator has no obvious way to enable it. The default should be enabled with a documented opt-out, not the inverse.

## Suggested approach (not prescriptive)

1. Audit the auto-selection input requirements: what inputs are needed to pick a tier when no project config is present? Likely the bead's labels, `kind`, file-touch estimate, and prior-attempt history. All available without operator input.
2. Make 'use global agent config defaults' the fallback when project routing is unspecified — currently the code requires explicit project routing OR explicit flags.
3. Enable triage complexity gate by default; document the opt-out flag.
4. Add an integration test: `ddx work --once --local` succeeds against a fresh project with no `.ddx/config.yaml` and a single bead in `.ddx/beads.jsonl`, given a minimal `~/.config/agent/config.yaml` with one provider.

## Out of scope

- Changing the global agent config schema. The fix is to reduce dependency on per-project config, not redesign the global one.
- Per-bead model overrides for advanced users — those should remain available via flags but should not be required for the common case.

## Reference

- HELIX alignment review where this surfaced: `docs/helix/06-iterate/alignment-reviews/AR-2026-05-01-public-examples.md` (in the easel/helix repo). The audit's 12 follow-up beads were drained via direct sub-agent dispatch instead of `ddx work` because of this gap.
title: ddx work should auto-route execution without project config

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM: Restarting the DDx user service during active supervised work can hang until systemd times out, leaving systemd to SIGKILL server child processes. Live evidence from 2026-07-07 03:05:19 EDT: `ddx server stop` did not return until systemd marked `ddx-server.service` failed with `Result: timeout` and killed leftover git subprocesses, interrupting the Axon worker attempt that was in post-execution handling.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE: `cli/internal/server/server.go:379-385` cancels the supervisor and then waits on `supervisorDone` with no timeout. Worker cleanup is only reached afterward at `cli/internal/server/server.go:388-395`. The worker shutdown path itself has a bounded wait (`cli/internal/server/workers.go:1696-1703`), but it is unreachable while the supervisor goroutine is stuck in a reconcile/git operation. The installed systemd unit generated from `cli/cmd/server_service.go:26-42` has no explicit stop timeout or ExecStop mitigation, so the default systemd timeout eventually kills the whole cgroup.

PROPOSED FIX: Make server shutdown bounded and ordered so worker cleanup always runs promptly even when supervisor reconciliation is slow or stuck. A good implementation is to cancel the supervisor, wait only a short bounded grace for `supervisorDone`, continue to `supervisorRegistry.Shutdown()` / `workers.Shutdown()` on timeout, and surface/log the supervisor timeout without preventing worker cleanup.

NON-SCOPE: Do not rewrite worker execution semantics, change bead claim/lease policy, or alter unrelated service install behavior.

Parent: none. Dependencies: none.

Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- Add `TestServerShutdownBoundsSupervisorWaitBeforeWorkerShutdown` (or an equivalently named test) in `cli/internal/server/server_shutdown_test.go` that simulates a supervisor goroutine stuck after cancellation and proves `Shutdown()` still invokes worker cleanup within a bounded duration.

Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

description:
Root cause epic for the multi-machine divergence problem discovered on axon 2026-04-14 during a planning session. Execute-loop treats master as a private branch and produces divergent histories that never reconcile with origin.

## Evidence

On axon, two machines running work (`eitri` and `sindri`) produced 14 days of independent history from a shared merge-base at 27c54ded (2026-04-06):

- eitri: 134 local commits that never reached origin
- sindri: 336 commits that pushed to origin
- Same FEAT-026 slot used for two unrelated features (sync protocol on eitri, markdown templates on sindri)
- Same beads.jsonl touched by both machines with divergent bead IDs and lifecycle state
- `refs/ddx/iterations/` preservation never fired because merges kept succeeding textually while producing semantically incoherent state
- 12+ "Merge made by 'ort' strategy" commits on 2026-04-13 afternoon on eitri alone, each bringing in a sibling local execute-bead worker's output

## Root causes identified

1. No `git fetch origin` at the top of a worker loop iteration — each bead starts from the worker's stale local HEAD (child bead DDX-agent-fetch)
2. No `git push` on successful landing — successful work stays trapped on the local branch (child bead DDX-agent-push)
3. Intra-machine sibling workers land via `git merge --no-edit` (ort strategy) instead of rebase, producing a fan of merge commits instead of a linear history (child bead DDX-agent-rebase)
4. .ddx/beads.jsonl is a git-tracked mutable ledger with no concurrent-write semantics (child bead DDX-agent-tracker)
5. No divergence monitoring — the 134/336 split grew silently over two weeks (child bead DDX-agent-monitor)
6. Multi-machine topology undocumented — which machine is authoritative, who pulls, who pushes (child bead DDX-agent-topology)

## Primary source evidence

- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_orchestrator.go:59-69 — Merge function uses `git merge --no-edit` with 'ort' strategy, no rebase alternative, commits a 'chore: checkpoint before merge' before attempting each merge
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_commit.go — has ZERO references to push/fetch/origin
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:~320 — worker loop runs Executor.Execute without any fetch-origin or ancestry-check step

## Impact

Any project that has run the work for more than a few days across more than one machine is silently divergent from origin. Content written by this session cannot be pushed to the axon origin without a multi-hour manual reconciliation. The axon repo currently has two weeks of unshared work on two machines.

## Scope of this epic

Six child beads covering: fetch-before-work, push-on-success, rebase-vs-merge, tracker concurrency, divergence monitoring, multi-machine topology docs. Each is actionable and self-contained.

## Blocks

Any further `ddx agent work` runs on projects with more than one participating machine should be paused until at least the first three child beads (fetch, push, rebase) are landed. Running the loop in the current state compounds divergence.

acceptance: `ddx agent workers stop <id>` gracefully terminates a running worker and updates its state to 'stopped'. `--all-over <duration>` reaps all workers older than the threshold. PID is exposed in `--json` output. Worker cleanup hook runs on graceful stop. Test coverage for stop/grace/force paths.
description:
## Problem

`ddx agent workers` lists running workers but provides no way to stop them.
Workers can hang indefinitely (today observed: 9 workers running 33h–142h on
agent projects). Operators have no clean way to terminate them — they have to
hunt for the process manually (`ps aux | grep claude`) and `kill -9`, which
bypasses any cleanup the worker might perform (temp files, worktree cleanup,
bead state updates).

Workers tracked in JSON today expose only: id, kind, state, bead_id, harness,
model, started_at, attempts, failures. No PID is surfaced, so external tooling
cannot cleanly target them either.

## Proposed shape

```
ddx agent workers stop <worker-id>        # graceful stop (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after grace)
ddx agent workers stop --all-over 1h      # stop every running worker older than 1h
ddx agent workers stop --state running    # stop all running workers
ddx agent workers stop --bead <bead-id>   # stop the worker assigned to a bead
```

Graceful path:
1. Send SIGTERM to worker process group
2. Wait configurable grace period (default 30s)
3. Send SIGKILL if still alive
4. Mark worker state as 'stopped' (distinct from 'failed' and 'exited')
5. Run worker cleanup hook (worktree teardown, bead state revert if still claimed)

Also surface PID in `ddx agent workers --json` so external tooling can target
processes directly when the CLI path is unavailable.

## Related

Observed on agent project 2026-04-17: nine workers running 33h–142h with no
bead assigned; root cause unclear. Even if the root cause gets fixed, operators
need a supported way to reap them.

## Files likely touched

- cmd/agent/workers.go — add stop subcommand and pid JSON field
- internal/agent/worker/registry.go — surface pid; add Stop() with graceful-then-force semantics
- internal/agent/worker/process.go — process group signaling, grace timer
- worker state machine — add 'stopping' and 'stopped' states

Implementing this bead's SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL process-group design is the correct mitigation and should be shipped first — but operators will keep needing it until sibling bead (RC1 in ddx-0a651925) lands context propagation.

See .ddx/executions/20260418T043148-1346e8a3/incident_report.md for full analysis and list of child beads. RC1 follow-up: child of ddx-0a651925 with suffix …-526efaf1.

description:
PROBLEM
A server-managed ddx work process can be terminated mid-attempt even while its bead lease and worker heartbeat are fresh. On 2026-07-13, worker worker-20260711T204017-68e9 (PID 303304) emitted a fresh heartbeat for ddx-69591a68 at 05:47:15Z, then received cancellation, exited 130 at 05:47:45Z, and was replaced by the supervisor. The attempt had active provider/test descendants and produced no terminal result. This regresses the incident addressed by ddx-57faa17c: that fix preserved the bead claim but did not protect the live process.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/server/workers.go:1447-1449 calls cleanupManagedWorkerProcessTree for every live PID named by a disk record before cli/internal/server/workers.go:1451-1467 asks staleDiskEntryCanReleaseClaim whether the fresh lease is safe to reclaim. cli/internal/server/workers.go:1586-1614 correctly refuses claim release for fresh or live same-machine leases, but that decision arrives after the process has already been killed and the record is still rewritten stopped at cli/internal/server/workers.go:1470-1482. cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:270-279 sends every snapshot stale ID through this path. TestSupervisorReconcile_FreshClaimingWorkerSurvivesTicks at cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor_test.go:882-962 keeps the live worker in the manager handle map and gives the stale fixture PID 0, so it cannot detect a live PID represented only by a stale disk entry.

PROPOSED FIX
- Classify whether a stale disk record is reclaimable before sending any signal or rewriting its state.
- Preserve or adopt a live same-machine process when its bead lease/heartbeat is fresh, even if the current server lacks an in-memory handle after restart, re-exec, or reconciliation.
- Reap the process tree, unclaim, and mark stopped only when ownership and liveness evidence prove the record is stale.
- Emit a diagnostic lifecycle/supervisor event for preserved live disk records so operators can distinguish adoption/preservation from cleanup.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change desired worker count, generic process cleanup, provider parent-death behavior, or manual/server coordination owned by ddx-635ae251. Do not weaken cleanup of dead PIDs or genuinely stale leases.

PARENT
None; root regression bead.

DEPS
None.
title: server: preserve live managed PIDs during stale-record cleanup

description:
PROBLEM
The pre-push full-tests hook can fail before running tests because the Go race detector requires cgo, but the hook invokes `go test -race` without ensuring `CGO_ENABLED=1` or producing a clear skip when cgo is unavailable. This blocks otherwise valid tracker/agent work at push time with a host-environment error.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- lefthook.yml:545-550 defines the pre-push `full-tests` command as `go test -race -cover ./...` under `cli/`.
- Recent push attempts failed with `go: -race requires cgo; enable cgo by setting CGO_ENABLED=1` because the hook inherited an environment with cgo disabled.
- cli/internal/server/perf/perf_test.go:32-37 already accounts for race builds by disabling perf percentile budgets under `-race`, so the intended gate is to run the race build, not to fail before test startup.

PROPOSED FIX
- Make the pre-push full-tests hook explicitly set `CGO_ENABLED=1` before `go test -race -cover ./...` on platforms where the Go toolchain supports cgo.
- If cgo is genuinely unavailable, fail with an actionable message or skip only the race flag while still running a non-race full package gate. Pick one policy and document it in the hook/test so operators understand the behavior.
- Add a regression test that parses lefthook.yml and proves the full-tests command cannot regress to a bare `go test -race` without CGO handling.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not weaken the pre-commit hook or merge-policy hook.
- Do not change package-level race/perf test behavior except as required to make the hook invoke the intended gate.
- Do not make local pushes depend on network access.

acceptance: Doctor reports both manifest schema and structural issues for a single broken plugin in one diagnostic pass. The split tests in cli/cmd/doctor_plugins_test.go can be re-merged into one combined test.
description:
When LoadPackageManifest rejects a package.yaml for missing required fields (e.g. description), it returns nil for the package. AuditInstalledEntry then falls back to &Package{}, which has empty Install.Skills. As a result collectSkillRoots returns nothing and auditSkillRoot is never called, so structural problems like missing SKILL.md files are silently swallowed whenever the manifest also has a schema problem.

The two audit dimensions should be independent: a malformed manifest should not blind us to install-tree problems.

description:
Today users with DDx checked out on multiple machines manually pull/stash/pop/commit-tracker/push to keep .ddx/beads.jsonl, .ddx/executions/, and committed plugin assets in sync. The dirty-tracker problem is constant because workers churn beads.jsonl every few minutes during work drains. Manual sync is friction; missing a sync risks divergent tracker state.

There is no good remote-only solution: routines in Anthropic cloud cannot touch a local working tree, and a server-side sync only helps if every endpoint is the server (DDx is per-project local).

REQUESTED FEATURE

1. ddx sync — one-shot command that runs the canonical flow:
   a. git fetch origin
   b. if working tree is dirty in tracked DDx-managed paths only (.ddx/beads.jsonl, .ddx/executions/, .ddx/plugins/), git stash
   c. git pull --rebase=false origin main (merge, never rebase — preserves execute-bead history per the project's standing merge policy)
   d. git stash pop
   e. stage and commit DDx-managed dirty paths (.ddx/beads.jsonl as 'chore: tracker', .ddx/executions/ as 'chore: add execution evidence')
   f. git push origin main; on non-fast-forward, retry from (a) once
   - Refuses to touch any path outside the DDx-managed allowlist.
   - Never uses --force, --no-verify, or destructive flags.
   - Aborts cleanly with a structured exit status if stash-pop conflicts or push fails twice.
   - Exit 0 = clean; non-zero = something needs human attention.

2. ddx sync --watch (or 'ddx sync daemon') — runs the above on an interval (default 15min, configurable). Local-only, runs in foreground or as a backgrounded process.

3. ddx-server can run sync as part of its loop when a project is registered with the server. The server already runs continuously per-project; adding sync to its loop costs almost nothing and turns the server into the canonical multi-machine sync hub.

4. Conflict surface: when sync aborts, doctor should pick up the issue ('ddx doctor' surfaces 'sync aborted at <timestamp>: <reason>') so users see it without having to remember to check.

5. Cross-platform: must work on macOS and Linux at minimum. No symlinks, no bash-isms. Probably implemented in Go using existing git-shell-out helpers (cli/internal/git/).

OUT OF SCOPE
- Conflict resolution beyond stash-pop (that's the preserved-iteration problem; ddx-0097af14 covers).
- Sync of paths outside the DDx-managed allowlist (intentional — never touches user code).
- Multi-remote sync (single origin only for v1).

ACCEPTANCE OF FAILURE: when something can't be auto-resolved (stash-pop conflict, double push fail, divergent base after fetch+merge), 'ddx sync' exits with a structured non-zero code and doctor surfaces it. No retries, no force, no surprise commits.

EVIDENCE THIS IS NEEDED: in the 2026-04-29 dogfood session, the operator manually invoked the sync flow ~6 times in ~3 hours while workers chewed through beads. Without sync, both machines drift; with this command, sync is one keystroke or zero (daemon).

REVIEW:BLOCK

No `cli/cmd/sync*.go` or `cli/internal/sync/` code added — entire feature missing from diff.
No `docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-*-sync.md` spec added (AC8 explicit gap from prior iteration still unaddressed).
