description:
## Context

ddx-agent v0.3.14 shipped the SSE comment-frame filter that unblocks omlx. Manual dogfooding (2026-04-18) confirmed a single bead executing via vidar-omlx for 6+ minutes with 17,000+ streaming events before the fix caused the regression this bead is meant to prevent: we have no automated assertion that the omlx path actually stays healthy.

Both fresh-eyes reviews (codex + opus, 2026-04-18) flagged: 'missing bead for v0.3.14 consumer-side smoke test in DDx'. This is that bead.

## Fix

Add an end-to-end smoke test that runs a real ddx work invocation against a recorded-or-live omlx endpoint and asserts the attempt closes (or at least produces a closing-status result: success / already_satisfied / a genuine model-side error) without surfacing 'unexpected end of JSON input' or silent stream termination.

Two implementation options:

1. **Record + replay via virtual harness** (preferred for CI isolation). Capture a full AGENT_DEBUG_WIRE_STREAM_FULL=1 trace of a successful vidar-omlx run, store it as a fixture, replay via a test double that emulates omlx's SSE quirks (keep-alive comment frames, reasoning warmup silence, reasoning_content deltas). Test asserts ddx-agent SDK consumes the full stream, ddx work's execute-bead orchestrator records closing status, and bead state mutates correctly.

2. **Live smoke, opt-in** (developer-machine only). A test file guarded by build tag  that makes a real request to vidar-omlx. Useful for catching provider-side regressions (e.g., omlx server ships a breaking change). Skip in CI.

Do BOTH: option 1 for CI signal, option 2 for manual release verification.

## What this prevents

- Regression: a future ddx-agent bump reintroduces the SSE-comment-frame bug or similar streaming defect. CI fixture test catches it before the bump merges.
- Regression: DDx-side change breaks the omlx dispatch path (e.g., adds a header that trips omlx's parser). CI catches it.
- Silent-success: ddx work completes but actually landed a bogus result_rev because of a subtle SSE-frame-dropping bug. Fixture replay asserts the expected final outcome.

## Coverage target

Minimum: one happy-path fixture (successful bead close) AND one error-path fixture (model returns malformed tool-call; execute-bead records task_failed cleanly without corrupting the bead tracker).

## Files likely touched

- cli/internal/agent/omlx_e2e_test.go (new) — fixture replay + assertions
- testdata/omlx-wire/ (new) — captured AGENT_DEBUG_WIRE JSONL fixtures
- scripts/capture-omlx-fixture.sh (new) — helper to regenerate fixtures against a live endpoint

## Depends on

- agent-941e7e42 (AGENT_DEBUG_WIRE_STREAM_FULL=1) shipped in v0.3.14 — needed to capture full fixtures.

description:
## Target UX

The user-facing profile vocabulary (cheap / default / fast / smart) should map to concrete routing policies that take full advantage of local models without blocking on their limits. Specifically:

### default profile (the common case)
Try local models first, escalate to cloud if:
- local model's context window is too small for the bead prompt
- local model lacks a capability the bead requires (tools, structured output, etc.)
- local dispatch fails (provider unreachable, timeout, model-side error)
- bead reopens due to post-run check failure (review-malfunction, land-conflict, etc.)

Escalation target: next tier up in the ladder (standard cloud — e.g. codex gpt-5.4 within subscription). If THAT fails, escalate once more to smart cloud. Then stop and unclaim.

### cheap profile
Local only. Never escalate. Intended for high-volume exploratory work where cost dominates and adequate-quality is sufficient. If the cheap tier can't serve the bead, the bead unclaims and waits.

### fast profile
Cloud-first, skip local entirely. Intended for latency-critical or interactive work where local inference's 9s warmup is unacceptable. Starts at a fast cloud model (e.g. gemini-flash or haiku) and escalates to smart on failure.

### smart profile
Cloud-high-quality from the start. Intended for bead-review, adversarial checks, or beads whose AC demands high-quality reasoning. No escalation — if smart fails, the work fails meaningfully.

## Why this matters (dogfooding signal)

As of 2026-04-18, DDx's default is cheap = qwen/qwen3.6 local (vidar-omlx). With v0.3.14 shipping the SSE-comment-frame filter, the local path actually works end-to-end. The queue can drain mostly on local hardware for pennies per bead, escalating only when the bead genuinely needs cloud quality. That's the throughput-per-dollar goal (goal:throughput-per-dollar label).

## Prereqs (already filed under ddx-2d974641 or sibling beads)

This epic is blocked on the autorouting epic delivering its exit-gate UX — 'declare provider + use canonical ref + autorouting works'. Specifically:

- ddx-8610020e (RouteRequest.Provider field) — foundation
- ddx-0486e601 (fuzzy normalization + per-provider) — lets cheap-tier model refs resolve to provider-native IDs
- ddx-2f5a2284 (catalog/Profile discovery integration) — lets Profile tier overrides retarget to provider-native IDs
- ddx-3c5ba7cc (tier escalation --provider affinity) — the lower half of this epic's 'escalate on failure' semantics
- ddx-4817edfd (capability gating) — prevents routing to a model that can't serve the bead

With those in place, the profile-level policy here is mostly CONFIGURATION + a small amount of scoring-layer logic.

## Scope

### Config schema additions

.ddx/config.yaml agent.routing extends with an explicit per-profile ladder:

    agent:
      routing:
        profile_ladders:
          default: [cheap, standard, smart]      # local first, escalate
          cheap:   [cheap]                        # local only
          fast:    [fast, smart]                  # cloud fast, escalate to smart
          smart:   [smart]                        # cloud high-quality, no escalation
        model_overrides:
          cheap:    qwen/qwen3.6
          fast:     kimi/k2.5
          standard: codex/gpt-5.4                # new: subscription cloud, mid-quality
          smart:    minimax/minimax-m2.7

Current profile_priority field (a flat list) becomes a legacy alias for profile_ladders.default with a deprecation warning.

### Tier-escalation policy (routing.go)

For a given profile P, iterate profile_ladders[P]:
- Evaluate model_overrides[tier] resolves on a viable candidate (with --provider affinity from ddx-3c5ba7cc).
- If yes, try it; on failure (execution_failed / land_conflict / post_run_check_failed), move to next tier.
- Record tier decision + escalation chain in routing event on the bead so telemetry reflects where work actually landed.

### User-facing CLI

- ddx work --profile default — the new primary invocation. Most users run this.
- ddx work --profile cheap / fast / smart — opt-in deviations.
- --max-tier continues to cap the ladder (explicit user override beats config).

### Telemetry + measurement

Every execution event records: requested_profile, requested_tier, resolved_tier, escalation_count, final_tier. Aggregated metrics (FEAT-016 / ddx-4b59b816) report per-profile throughput, per-tier cost, per-bead escalation rate.

## Exit gate

'ddx work --profile default --once --local' against a ready bead on a host with a healthy local provider AND healthy cloud fallback:
- Claims the bead.
- Tries cheap tier (local). If it succeeds, closes bead with tier=cheap recorded.
- If cheap fails for any escalation-triggering reason, automatically retries at standard tier without operator intervention.
- If standard fails, retries at smart.
- Final outcome recorded faithfully (success at whatever tier landed, or exhaustion if all tiers failed).

## Out of scope

- Dynamic profile selection ('auto-pick profile based on bead complexity'). Too much magic; explicit profile choice is fine.
- Cost budgets / circuit breakers. FEAT-014 (token awareness) tracks this separately.
- Per-bead profile overrides (bead-level 'requires-profile: smart'). Could be a future follow-up but out of scope here.

## Metadata

Governing spec: FEAT-006 (agent service) + the autorouting epic ddx-2d974641. This bead is the PROFILE-layer policy that sits on top of the routing fixes from ddx-2d974641. Do not start until ddx-2d974641's Phase-1 children are closed.
title: profile/automation: default = local-first with escalation; fast/smart = cloud-first

description:
PROBLEM
The pre-claim readiness/intake hook is producing malformed `readiness_checks` shapes during live `ddx work` runs, including object-shaped and string-shaped values. Decoder hardening is tracked separately, but there is also a prompt/skill contract mismatch that encourages model drift: the bead-lifecycle skill documents a readiness schema with `readiness_checks` as an array, while the runtime prompt asks for a partially different field set.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `.agents/skills/ddx/bead-lifecycle/SKILL.md:30-31`, `.claude/skills/ddx/bead-lifecycle/SKILL.md:30-31`, and `cli/internal/skills/ddx/bead-lifecycle/SKILL.md:30-31` say `MODE: intake` is compatibility readiness mode unless the caller gives a narrower schema.
- The same skill copies at lines 71-125 document the readiness JSON schema with `tractability`, `score`, `rationale`, `readiness_checks` as an array of objects, `suggested_fixes`, `rewrite`, `suggested_child_beads`, and `waivers_applied`.
- `cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:242-248` builds the live pre-claim prompt with `MODE: intake` but asks for `classification, confidence, reasoning, readiness_checks, suggested_fixes, suggested_child_beads, and waivers_applied`; it omits `tractability`, `score`, and `rationale`, uses legacy `confidence/reasoning`, and also says not to include rewrite fields.
- This split contract leaves the model deciding which schema to follow, so malformed `readiness_checks` values can appear even when the skill itself shows an array example.

PROPOSED FIX
Align the live pre-claim prompt and all shipped bead-lifecycle skill copies around one explicit intake/readiness contract. Either make the runtime prompt quote the exact readiness-mode JSON shape DDx decodes, or make the skill define a deliberately narrower intake schema that exactly matches the runtime prompt. In either case, explicitly state that `readiness_checks` MUST be a JSON array, may be empty, and every entry MUST be an object with `reason`, `verdict`, `evidence`, and `checkable_before_attempt`. Keep the operator-required threshold strict: prompt-quality nits go in `suggested_fixes`; only true blockers become `operator_required`.

NON-SCOPE
Do not replace decoder hardening in ddx-c81c3cad; DDx must still tolerate malformed model output. Do not change readiness classifications or queue state-machine semantics. Do not make readiness failures block work by default.

description:
PROBLEM
Operators cannot inspect what 'ddx work' would pick without actually picking. When an unexpected bead claims (or an expected bead is skipped), the only diagnostic is the diagnostic events emitted AFTER claim attempt — by then the operator has already lost the chance to intervene. There is no read-only 'show me your decision' surface.

ROOT CAUSE
The picker logic at cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1145 (ExecuteBeadWorker.nextCandidate) reads the bead store via Store.ReadyExecution (cli/internal/bead/store.go:1246) and applies filters (per-Run attempted map, label_filter intersection) before returning the first eligible candidate. The picker is invoked only INSIDE the loop — there is no standalone API to query 'what would you pick?'.

The existing 'ddx bead ready' command returns ready beads but does NOT apply the picker's per-Run attempted filter (which is non-deterministic across runs anyway), nor does it visualize the picker's tie-breaking rules (priority asc, then updated_at asc per FIFO).

Bead metadata IS deterministic. Given the bead store + stable filter inputs (label_filter, capabilities), the picker's output for the FIRST eligible bead must be 100% deterministic. There is no reason this shouldn't be inspectable interactively.

NAMING NOTE
Originally proposed as 'ddx queue plan'. Renamed to 'ddx work plan' because 'queue' is not an established concept in the CLI surface; 'work' is (the existing 'ddx work' drain command). This makes the new subcommand a natural sibling: 'ddx work' executes the drain; 'ddx work plan' previews what the drain would do.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a new subcommand at cli/cmd/work_plan.go (sibling file to cli/cmd/work.go):

  ddx work plan [--label-filter=<labels>] [--capabilities=<csv>] [--limit=<N>] [--json]

Behavior:
1. Read the bead store via the same Store.ReadyExecution path the worker uses (so filters like cooldown, superseded, execution-eligible apply identically).
2. Apply the same sort the worker applies: priority asc, then updated_at asc within priority.
3. Apply optional --label-filter and --capabilities to mirror worker filtering exactly.
4. SKIP the per-Run attempted map (it's non-deterministic across runs; not a stable picker decision).
5. Output an ordered table: Position | Bead ID | Priority | Updated | Status | Filter-decision | Why
   - 'Why' column explains each bead's pick-or-skip reason: 'next claim', 'eligible (rank N)', 'skipped: in cooldown until <RFC3339>', 'skipped: label_filter mismatch (bead labels=[a,b]; worker filter=[c])', 'skipped: capability mismatch (bead requires=[review]; worker has=[bead-attempt])', 'blocked: dep <id> open', etc.
6. Default --limit=10 (top of queue); --limit=0 = full queue.
7. Support --json for machine-readable output (operator scripts; comparison with actual claim events).

Implementation strategy: extract the picker's filter+sort logic from ExecuteBeadWorker.nextCandidate into a reusable function in cli/internal/agent (or cli/internal/bead) — call it 'PreviewQueue(filters PickerFilters) []QueueEntry'. The worker's nextCandidate then calls PreviewQueue + filters out attempted; the new 'ddx work plan' command calls PreviewQueue directly.

This factoring is itself the key insight: the picker logic SHOULD be a pure function over (bead store, filters) returning an ordered list. The worker's role is just 'call picker, claim first, execute'. Separating preview from claim gives us the dry-run + makes the picker testable in isolation.

NON-SCOPE
- Modifying picker semantics (this is read-only preview)
- Predicting downstream effects (e.g., 'after I claim X, what's next?' — out of scope; operator can re-run plan after each claim)
- Server-side picker integration (rev 5 architecture: there is no server-side picker; this command queries the bead store directly)
- Removing the per-Run attempted map (that's owned by C7 ddx-06eb05d8)
- Making 'ddx work' itself accept --plan as a flag instead (subcommand is clearer scope)

INTERSECTION
- Pairs with 'ddx try <bead-id>' (ddx-f261d2a0): operator runs 'ddx work plan' to see ordering, then 'ddx try <id>' to dispatch deterministically.
- Picker priority bug bead ddx-9d55601f shipped diagnostic events at commit 80f51574 (picker.priority_skip, picker.claim_race). 'ddx work plan' is the COMPLEMENT: events show what HAPPENED; plan shows what WOULD happen.
- C8 (ddx-848069a3) relocates routing preflight; 'ddx work plan' should NOT call routing preflight (it's a 'show me the queue' query, not 'show me what could execute given routing health').
notes: Shipped at commit c0f95380: PreviewQueue + ddx work plan subcommand. 13 tests added.

description:
First child of ddx-b7ee0d6f. Execute-loop workers currently start each bead from their local HEAD without verifying that HEAD is an ancestor of origin/master. When it isn't (because another machine pushed work), the worker produces commits that can never be fast-forward pushed, and the local branch silently diverges.

## Evidence

cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go around line 320 contains the worker-loop body:

    nextPhase("queueing", false)
    ...
    nextPhase("running", false)
    report, err := w.Executor.Execute(ctx, candidate.ID)

There is no `git fetch origin` and no ancestry check between these phases and the executor call. The worker enters Execute with whatever HEAD happens to be checked out.

Grep confirms: `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_commit.go` has zero references to push/fetch/origin. `execute_bead_orchestrator.go` has git merge/commit calls but never git fetch.

## Required behavior

Before claiming a bead (or at minimum before invoking the executor on a claimed bead), the worker must:

1. Run `git fetch origin <default-branch>` with a timeout. On network failure, log a structured warning and continue (so air-gapped runs still work), but record the staleness in the attempt metadata.
2. Run `git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/<default-branch>`. If HEAD is NOT an ancestor of origin, the local branch has diverged. This is a hard error:
   - Mark the bead as land_conflict and unclaim it
   - Emit a structured event 'divergence_detected' with both commits and the count
   - Stop the worker loop (do not pick another bead) until a human reconciles
3. If HEAD IS an ancestor but there are upstream commits (origin is ahead), fast-forward the local branch to origin before starting work. This rebases cleanly onto the latest server state.

## Test cases

- Fresh clone, no divergence: worker claims and runs normally
- Upstream is ahead by N commits, local has no uncommitted work: worker fast-forwards then runs
- Local is ahead of upstream (diverged): worker refuses to claim, emits divergence_detected, stops the loop
- `git fetch` times out / network unreachable: worker continues with a staleness warning
- Default branch is configurable (not always 'master') — config read from .ddx/config.yaml

## Related

Complementary to the push-on-success bead (sibling). Both are required for the loop to stay synchronized. Fetch alone is useless without push; push alone is useless without fetch.
title: work: fetch origin + verify ancestry before claiming a bead

description:
PROBLEM
The process-shared main-git tracker lock has no crash-safe advisory guard primitive that lets a single stale-breaker win a cross-process transition. There is currently no OS advisory lock and no package-local sidecar path helper to build one on.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go:215-278 (withTrackerLockPolicy) retries os.Mkdir on the canonical lock and classifies existing objects with no cross-process advisory serialization. cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock_unix.go:9 and cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock_windows.go:10 only implement trackerProcessAlive; there is no advisory-lock acquire/release. cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go:99-101 (trackerLockPath) resolves the canonical lock via lockmetrics.SharedTrackerLockPath but exposes no sibling sidecar path.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
Phase 0 WB-5 single-winner cross-process stale-break protocol: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase0-stop-the-self-harm-plan-2026-07-13.md:124-132.

PROPOSED FIX
Add one package-local path helper (e.g. trackerLockGuardPath(projectRoot)) that derives a deterministic never-deleted sibling advisory-lock file whose name ends in .lock, adjacent to the canonical trackerLockPath. Add a crash-safe guard type with Acquire/Release: Unix uses syscall.Flock(fd, LOCK_EX) on a never-deleted file, Windows uses LockFileEx on a never-deleted HANDLE; the OS lock releases automatically on handle close or process death. Add keyed same-process coordination (package-level map keyed by resolved sidecar path + sync.Mutex) so two goroutines in one process serialize before touching the shared fd. Ordinary acquisition and release MUST NOT delete, truncate, rename, or recreate the sidecar inode/path — only open/lock/unlock/close. Non-contention open/lock errors fail safe (return an error, do not proceed as if held). Provide both Unix and Windows implementations. Because the dependency graph does not cross-compile for Windows, include a self-contained cross-compile smoke command in AC 4 naming the final guard source/test files.

NON-SCOPE
This child does NOT change withTrackerLockPolicy's observe/mutate flow, breakStaleTrackerLock, or wire the guard into the stale-break transition (owned by the sibling integration child). It does NOT touch synthesizeCommitExcludePathspecs, preDispatchCheckpointIgnoredPath, or checkoutSyncDeferralIgnoredPath (owned by the ignore-wiring child). Do not change tracker mutation semantics, tracker record format, trackerLockStaleAge, LockRetryPolicy defaults, lockmetrics caps, harness/Fizeau behavior, bead-store locks, git index locks, or the execution-cleanup lock in cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_loop.go:116-156. Do not extract a shared lock package; ddx-dffb7454 and ddx-3f156500 own separate sites and Phase 1 WB-8 owns unification. Do not implement token-bearing lease release or stale directory/file disposal beyond what is needed to exercise guard acquire/release.

PARENT
ddx-1c8d9319

DEPS
None. ddx-dffb7454 is a related collection-lock implementation, not a prerequisite or shared-package dependency.

During dogfood on 2026-06-13, one `ddx work --once` attempt for bead ddx-0be85773 reported active route `claude/sonnet`, but the worker process retained multiple direct provider CLI children at the same time: `codex --no-alt-screen` (PID 1875100, older than 7 minutes), `claude --print ... --model sonnet` (PID 1882389, active implementation route), and later `gemini` (PID 1890368). - `cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:140-142` treats Fizeau `Execute` as one event stream after process setup; DDx does not currently expose per-provider child process ownership/phase in worker status.

Track provider subprocesses per attempt with route/phase metadata. When a route is selected, DDx/Fizeau should either avoid starting unrelated provider CLIs or immediately terminate any provider child not owned by the active route. Worker status/evidence should surface provider_children with provider, pid, phase, route_owner, age, and cleanup_result. At attempt end, DDx must reap every provider child and fail or flag the attempt if cleanup is incomplete.

NON-SCOPE

Do not ban legitimate short-lived helper probes if they are bounded and recorded. Do not kill unrelated same-user provider processes outside the worker process tree. Do not rely on real provider CLIs in regression tests; use fake long-lived child processes.

description:
PROBLEM
  Two places answer "is this bead ready?" and they disagree. The lifecycle
  module (lifecycle.go) classifies a bead's queue bucket from facts; the
  store.go Ready() helper then re-filters by raw status, producing a different
  answer than the lifecycle classifier when an in_progress bead has a stale
  claim.

ROOT CAUSE
  - cli/internal/bead/lifecycle.go:155-208 EvaluateLifecycleQueue routes
    StatusInProgress at line 190-194 through evaluateOpenLifecycleQueue when
    !ClaimFresh, which can produce LifecycleBucketReady at line 232.
  - cli/internal/bead/store.go:1754-1766 readyFiltered then iterates the
    classifier output and applies a second filter at line 1763:
        if entry.Status == StatusOpen { ready = append(...) }
    This filter is gated by !executionOnly, so external readers
    (ddx bead ready non-executionOnly path) see a different result than
    queue-execution callers (executionOnly path).
  - Net effect: a stale-claimed in_progress bead with deps satisfied is
    "ready" per EvaluateLifecycleQueue, "not ready" per store.Ready() in
    operator-facing mode, and "ready" per store.Ready() in execution mode.
    Three answers; one question.

PROPOSED FIX
  - Decide the canonical answer: per TD-031 §6, claim metadata is not status,
    and a stale-claimed in_progress bead is recoverable through the heartbeat
    TTL mechanism. The lifecycle module's classifier already encodes this.
    Therefore the second filter at store.go:1763 is redundant and incorrect.
  - Edit cli/internal/bead/store.go:1754-1766: remove the
    "if entry.Status == StatusOpen" branch; both executionOnly and
    operator-facing paths consume LifecycleBucketReady directly.
  - Add regression test TestReady_StaleClaimedInProgressIsReady in
    cli/internal/bead/store_test.go (or extend an existing nearby test) that:
      a. Creates a bead, claims it (open -> in_progress).
      b. Manually expires the heartbeat (set claimed-at + heartbeat TTL).
      c. Asserts Ready() returns the bead in operator-facing mode (not just
         the executionOnly path).
  - Verify no other call sites of readyFiltered or Ready depend on the
    removed filter; grep for s.Ready, store.Ready, .Ready( across cli/.

NON-SCOPE
  - Changing EvaluateLifecycleQueue or the lifecycle bucket enumeration.
  - Adding new claim-recovery semantics.
  - Migrating callers between executionOnly and non-executionOnly paths.

INTERSECTIONS
  - ddx-ca1c66ee (epic parent).
  - No deps on B1/B2; can run in parallel with the TD-031 amendment.

## Report
External report at /tank/home/erik/Downloads/ddx-agent-run-invalid-timeout-exits-zero.md claims `ddx agent run --timeout 60ss ...` exits 0 on bad input, breaking wrapper exit-code inference (canonical caller: helix CLI).

## Real gaps
1. No regression test guards the exit-code semantic. cli/cmd/agent_run_profile_test.go only exercises happy-path `--timeout 3s`.
2. SilenceUsage is not set on `agent run` — flag parse errors dump the entire usage block above the error message (the cosmetic part of the reporter's complaint).

## Plan
(a) Set `SilenceUsage: true` on `newAgentRunCommand` (cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go:91 area) and on `newAgentDoctorCommand` (sibling, ~line 647). Per-command scope, not root — matches existing precedent (cli/cmd/init.go:99 sets SilenceUsage only; cli/cmd/doc.go:89,118 set both). Do NOT set SilenceErrors=true; keep cobra's stderr error line.

(b) Add a regression test asserting `agent run --timeout 60ss --harness codex --text "..."` returns a non-nil err from executeCommand whose message contains `invalid timeout`. This is sufficient to catch the regression because main.go:31-43 turns any non-nil err into exit 1 — no subprocess test needed. Place the test in a neutrally named file, not agent_run_profile_test.go (the profile-specific filename is misleading for a generic flag-parse test).

(c) Optional polish: assert the captured output after SilenceUsage does NOT contain `Usage:`/`Flags:` lines.

(d) Do NOT extend coverage to other duration-typed inputs across the CLI; out of scope for this bug.

## Out of scope
- Helix-side fix (already done at /home/erik/Projects/helix/scripts/helix line 70 per reporter).
- Root-level cobra UX changes.
- Validation hardening of other duration flags elsewhere.

## Refinement log
Reviewed by fresh-eyes (general-purpose subagent) and codex (`ddx agent run --harness codex`). Fresh-eyes verified main.go propagates cobra errors faithfully — command-level test is sufficient. Codex pushed for a subprocess exit-code test; rejected because main.go:31 invariant makes the command-level assertion equivalent. Both reviewers agreed per-command SilenceUsage is the right scope (matches init.go/doc.go precedent). Folded in: doctor-command parity, SilenceErrors warning, test-file placement note. Rejected: broader CLI sweep, subprocess test.

`ddx work` currently reports dependency-ready epics only as structural skips. That is correct for epics with open child work, but stale for epics whose direct children are all closed. 1. Update CLI help text and any nearby command docs so `ddx agent execute-bead` is described as the single-bead primitive and `ddx agent work` is described as the queue/supervisor command built on top of it.
2. Add or update user-facing operator docs and CLI reference surfaces so users discover `work` first for normal queue-driven work, with concrete examples for:
   - `ddx agent work`
   - `ddx agent work --once`
   - `ddx agent work --poll-interval <duration>`
   - `ddx agent execute-bead <bead-id>` for bounded/manual runs
3. Update the ddx-bead skill and any relevant internal skill/operator guidance so agents are told explicitly:
   - planning/document-only beads are valid execution targets
   - work is the default queue-driven entrypoint
   - execute-bead is the lower-level primitive for targeted/manual execution
4. Document the result/close semantics operators need in practice:
   - which outcomes/statuses close a bead
   - which outcomes preserve and leave the bead open
   - which JSON fields automation should read (`status`, `outcome`, `preserve_ref`, `result_rev`, `session_id`)
5. Make the operator guidance consistent with the current merge model:
   - merge is the default successful outcome
   - explicit required execution documents are the automatic merge gates
   - `--no-merge` is the manual preserve override

## Boundaries
- Do not invent a new bead shape or merge-gate field
- Use the existing execute-bead / work / execution-document contract
- Keep the user-facing guidance aligned with the actual shipped command behavior and documented result surface

description:
PROBLEM
The live server-managed ddx worker `worker-20260616T084349-8105` claimed `ddx-67cdc109` on 2026-06-16, ran Claude readiness intake, and then logged: `decode readiness classification result: json: cannot unmarshal array into Go struct field preClaimIntakePromptRewrite.rewrite.acceptance of type string (continuing)`. The bead remains claimed with an `intake.warn` event even though the provider route was viable and produced a syntactically useful rewrite shape. This blocks reliable `ddx work` because provider/schema drift in an optional rewrite field is treated as system-unready instead of normalized or ignored.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:47-50` defines `preClaimIntakePromptRewrite.Acceptance` as `string`, so JSON arrays for `rewrite.acceptance` fail the entire intake decode before policy can use the classification.
- `cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:255-281` already has `decodeReadinessAcceptanceList` for `suggested_child_beads[].acceptance`, tolerating either a JSON string or an array of numbered criteria.
- `cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:674-684` tells providers that suggested child acceptance may be an array but says rewrite acceptance should be `acceptance`; live Claude still returned an array for rewrite acceptance.
- `cli/internal/agent/bead_lifecycle_skill_contract_test.go:132-134` currently asserts array `rewrite.acceptance` is an error, which conflicts with live Claude TUI canary behavior and the forward-compatible worker reliability goal.

PROPOSED FIX
Normalize `rewrite.acceptance` using the same string-or-array decoder used for suggested child acceptance. Arrays of numbered criteria should be joined into the canonical multiline acceptance string before `ValidatePreClaimRewrite` runs. Malformed non-string/non-array shapes should still produce a structured decode warning/error. Update prompt/contract tests so arrays are accepted for rewrite acceptance while preserving strictness for invalid shapes.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not make arbitrary rewrite fields untyped.
- Do not accept lossy rewrites that drop or alter acceptance criteria; existing `ValidatePreClaimRewrite` must still enforce preservation.
- Do not change provider routing or model selection.

PARENT + DEPS
Parent: `ddx-3106674f`.
Deps: none. This is a live canary blocker for server-managed `ddx work` reliability.

description:
PROBLEM
After a successful land, DDx attempts to refresh the operator checkout so the files match the new target branch tip. That sync currently mutates the main index and force-checks out changed paths. When the operator checkout has local edits in those same paths, syncing can overwrite or destabilize those edits even though the agent work happened in an isolated worktree.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:338-405 SyncWorkTreeToHead runs git read-tree HEAD and checkout-index -f for files changed between fromRev and HEAD.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:710, :775, :811, :1129, and :1193 call SyncWorkTreeToHead as best-effort after ref updates, merge, rollback, push auto-recovery, or preserved iteration recovery.
- The May 7 ddx-377ebf92 push-conflict event showed dirty projectRoot paths overlapped the landed branch paths, including .ddx/beads.jsonl, AGENTS.md, execute_bead_loop.go, and FEAT docs.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add an overlap check before syncing the operator checkout: compare files changed by the landed/recovered commit range with dirty tracked and untracked projectRoot paths.
- If there is no dirty overlap, keep the existing sync behavior.
- If there is dirty overlap, skip checkout sync, leave refs/result/evidence intact, and record an observable checkout_sync_deferred detail/event rather than failing the bead.
- Ensure push auto-recovery and preserved-iteration recovery also use the guard.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change how clean temp landing worktrees merge/push; the dependency bead owns that.
- Do not auto-stash or discard operator changes.
- Do not change retry cooldown policy for real merge conflicts.

DEPS
Depends on clean landing/evidence isolation so sync is the only remaining projectRoot mutation after successful land.
title: land: defer operator checkout sync on dirty overlap

description:
PROBLEM
When an attempt worktree vanishes before DDx can read HEAD, the result is reported as generic execution_failed/transport with ResultRev equal to BaseRev. That hides the root cause and makes the work look like an agent/task failure even when the agent ran to completion and infrastructure lost the worktree.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:940-978 reads gitOps.HeadRev(wtPath) after agent execution; on failure it writes a task_failed result with ResultRev set to baseRev and Reason set to the raw rev-parse error.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_status.go:25-44 defines failure modes but has no worktree_lost class.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1901-1909 derives outcome reason from status/error text and can collapse missing-worktree infrastructure into generic transport/unknown handling.
- The May 7 ddx-c2a66f45 and ddx-b1cf1f6b attempts both failed with git rev-parse HEAD: chdir ... no such file or directory after non-trivial agent runtime/cost.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add a stable FailureModeWorktreeLost and classify missing worktree/chdir rev-parse failures into it.
- Write result.json diagnostics that include attempted worktree_path, attempt_id, bead_id, cleanup metadata presence, run-state/liveness state, and whether the path was registered with git worktree.
- Ensure worktree_lost is infrastructure/transport, does not increment no-progress/no_changes budget, and leaves the bead retryable or parked according to existing transport policy.
- Preserve prompt/manifest/result evidence even when the worktree is gone.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not recover lost uncommitted implementation changes.
- Do not change cleanup deletion policy; sibling cleanup bead prevents the loss.
- Do not change model/provider routing.

DEPS
Depends on per-attempt liveness so diagnostics can include the live-state record that should have protected the worktree.

description:
fizeau v0.13.1 is released and contains the autorouting fix the ddx workers were stalling on. Bump the ddx-side fizeau pin to v0.13.1 and restart the ddx work / ddx server processes so they pick up the new binary.

Context: with v0.13.0, every first dispatch attempt after a host (e.g. bragi) went off-network burned the full ~165s retry budget (5 attempts × ~30s dial timeout + exponential backoff) before the routing layer learned the host was unreachable. v0.13.0's hard-gate (`Inputs.ProviderUnreachable`) only populated from snapshot discovery errors, which lagged the first dispatch failure.

v0.13.1 closes two gaps:
- Route-attempt failures with dial-class errors (dial tcp / connection refused / no route to host / i/o timeout / no such host / 502 Bad Gateway / 503 / 504) now populate `Inputs.ProviderUnreachable` immediately. One failed dispatch hard-gates the provider for the cooldown TTL on the very next call. Non-dial failures (context canceled, 4xx, wall-clock timeouts) stay as soft demotion so sticky-lease keeps working through single transient hiccups.
- New `RefreshIfStale` snapshot refresh mode + `Cache.MaybeRefreshSync` primitive. `buildRoutingInputs` now uses it so a cold-start route call re-probes stale providers in-line (bounded by 5s discovery timeout per source) before scoring. The first call after a host dies is now at worst the 5s probe rather than the full retry budget.

Release: https://github.com/easel/fizeau/releases/tag/v0.13.1
Commit: 52c436e8 (fix routing) + the v0.13.1 tag.

Integration steps:
1. Update whatever pins the ddx workers carry on the fizeau SDK / agent / binary to v0.13.1 (go.mod replace block, install.sh hash, agent_binary_url, whatever the actual mechanism is).
2. Rebuild / reinstall ddx workers.
3. Restart any long-running `ddx work --watch`, `ddx server`, or similar processes so they load the new binary.
4. Verify by killing bragi (or pointing at an off host) and watching `ddx work` — instead of ~165s of `WARN provider error, retrying attempt=N` against bragi, the router should pick an alternative on the second-or-later request without burning the retry budget.
title: integrate fizeau v0.13.1 (routing hard-gate fix)

description:
PROBLEM
Operators and agents asking "is the worker still working beads?" or "how is the queue progressing?" can receive the status of a DDx worker from the wrong repository. In the observed incident, the user was asking about the Niflheim queue, but the agent ran a global `ps aux | grep -E "(ddx work|ddx try)"` and reported a DDx repo worker on `ddx-bbdbc903`. This is actively harmful: it makes project A look busy because project B has a worker, and it hides whether project A has stalled.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `.agents/skills/ddx/reference/status.md:22-31` tells agents how to check queue state with `ddx bead ready`, `ddx bead blocked`, `ddx bead status`, and `ddx bead list`, but it gives no required project-root confirmation or project-scoped live-worker check.
- `.agents/skills/ddx/reference/status.md:82-99` warns not to mix health/status commands, but does not warn against global process scans or require that worker reports match the requested project root.
- `.agents/skills/ddx/reference/work.md:143-159` documents `ddx work` and `ddx try`, but does not document a safe way to ask "which live workers belong to this project?".
- `cli/cmd/work.go:76` exposes `--project`, and `cli/cmd/work.go:144-165` includes `project_root` in terminal/JSON loop output, but DDx has no corresponding `ddx work status` / `ddx worker status` local CLI that lists live worker processes for the current project and filters out other repositories.
- `cli/cmd/server_workers.go:13-175` provides server-backed worker listing/logging, but that only helps when the local server worker registry is running; it does not solve ordinary inline `ddx work` shells that operators check from a terminal.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a project-scoped live-worker status surface and update skill guidance so agents cannot accidentally answer with cross-project workers.

Recommended implementation shape:
- Add `ddx work status` (or an equivalent `ddx worker status`) that defaults to the current git/project root, accepts `--project`, and lists only live `ddx work` / `ddx try` processes whose process cwd, `--project`, execution worktree, or durable worker record maps to that root.
- Include `--all-projects` for explicit global inspection. The default must never report workers from other repositories.
- Output should include project root, pid, age, command, active bead ID when inferable, execution worktree or bundle path when inferable, and a clear `no live workers for <project>` result when none match.
- Update `.agents/skills/ddx/reference/status.md` and `.agents/skills/ddx/reference/work.md` to require: first resolve the requested project root; then use the project-scoped status command; never use raw global `ps | grep ddx work` as evidence without filtering by project root; always name the project whose worker status is being reported.
- If a live worker is found for another project while answering a scoped question, mention it only as an explicitly out-of-scope process, not as proof that the requested project is progressing.

NON-SCOPE
Do not build a full multi-project scheduler. Do not require the DDx server to be running. Do not change bead claiming semantics. Do not kill or restart existing workers. Do not remove the server-backed worker APIs.
title: work: report live workers only for the requested project

description:
PROBLEM
  Local plugin installs need to make DDx skills live-editable by symlinking package-owned skill directories, but the current local path uses its own discovery rules and can choose the wrong skill source when pointed at the DDx repo root.

ROOT CAUSE
  cli/cmd/install.go:254-372 implements local install separately from the registry package installer. It loads the manifest but then calls `installLocalSkillSymlinks(absPath, absProject, force)` without passing `pkg.Install.Skills`. cli/cmd/install.go:510-563 chooses `<pluginRoot>/.agents/skills` before `<pluginRoot>/skills`, so `ddx plugin install ddx --local .` can target destination copies in the repo root instead of the intended package source. The plan requires local overlays to honor manifest mappings and either resolve the repo root safely to `library/` or fail before modifying skill outputs.

PROPOSED FIX
  - cli/cmd/install.go: replace hard-coded local skill discovery with mapping-driven symlink creation from `pkg.Install.Skills`.
  - Symlink each child skill directory from the mapping source to each mapping target, e.g. `library/skills/ddx -> .agents/skills/ddx` and `.claude/skills/ddx`.
  - Add repo-root safety: if a local path is not a package root but contains `library/package.yaml` for the requested package, resolve to that package root, or fail clearly before writing outputs.
  - Preserve local overlay invariants: do not mutate plugin version pins and do not auto-commit.

NON-SCOPE
  - Remote registry real-file installs; sibling bead owns package mapping copy behavior.
  - Moving the actual skill content to `library/skills/ddx`.
  - Changing public plugin command names.

PARENT + DEPS
  Parent: ddx-6862f2ac. Depends on the registry mapping bead so local and remote installers share mapping semantics.
title: plugin install: symlink local package skill mappings safely

description:
## Goal

Simplify DDx agent execution so DDx does not participate in model/provider/harness routing while still owning bead retry policy.

DDx may:
- estimate work effort;
- request abstract agent power bounds using MinPower and optional MaxPower;
- accept operator passthrough constraints (`--harness`, `--provider`, `--model`) and send them unchanged to the agent;
- inspect the agent's available model/power catalog only to choose abstract MinPower thresholds, including top-model-only retries;
- decide whether a bead attempt succeeded using DDx-owned evidence: commits, merge/preserve result, no-changes rationale, post-run gates, review verdicts, cooldowns, and run metadata;
- retry a bead with higher MinPower when policy permits;
- pass non-routing execution intent to the agent: prompt/workdir, power bounds, effort/reasoning, permissions, timeouts, session/evidence metadata, passthrough constraints, and task facts such as EstimatedPromptTokens or RequiresTools.

The agent owns all routing inside the power bounds and passthrough constraints: harness/provider/model validation, endpoint choice, candidate scoring, health, quota, fallback, compatibility errors, and route errors. The agent reports actual model and actual power used, e.g. `running with qwen 3.6-27b (power 10)`.

## Non-goals

- No legacy compatibility paths for DDx-side ladders, model overrides, profiles, or default-path preflight routing.
- No DDx interpretation of harness/provider/model passthrough values.
- No DDx-owned provider probing/filtering in execution setup.
- No candidate traces in execution evidence from ResolveRoute.
- No cheap/standard/smart profile taxonomy in DDx execution policy.

## Required command layering

1. `ddx run`: one invocation atom. Calls agent Execute exactly once with requested MinPower/MaxPower and optional passthrough constraints. Does not call ResolveRoute.
2. `ddx try <bead>`: one bead attempt. Builds bead prompt/worktree/evidence context, estimates initial or retry MinPower, carries passthrough constraints unchanged, then calls run.
3. `ddx work`: queue drain and retry policy. Picks beads, invokes try, classifies results, and schedules higher-MinPower retries when policy permits. It does not inspect passthrough constraint values.

## Passthrough envelope rule

Harness/provider/model fields must live in one narrow agent-passthrough envelope. DDx may copy the envelope between layers and persist it for audit. DDx must not validate, branch on, fallback, rewrite, widen, or use these fields for queue/retry policy. If retry MinPower changes, the passthrough envelope remains unchanged and the agent resolves compatibility.

If hard pins make requested power bounds unsatisfiable, DDx stops with a typed terminal classification such as `blocked_by_passthrough_constraint` or `agent_power_unsatisfied`, records the agent evidence, and reports operator action required. DDx must not remove pins, choose alternatives, call ResolveRoute, or keep escalating.

## Retry eligibility

DDx may raise MinPower only for classified outcomes where stronger reasoning could plausibly help after a valid attempt started, such as capability-insufficient results, post-run check failures after an attempted change, review-blocked capability failures, or no-changes-after-attempt within the no-progress budget.

DDx must not use power retry for deterministic setup/operator-action failures: dirty worktree, merge or land conflict, missing checkout, invalid bead metadata, unresolved dependencies, config parse errors, missing harness binaries, auth failures, command-not-found/toolchain setup, passthrough exhaustion, or any case that would require inspecting/removing/replacing passthrough pins.

## Guardrails

Allowed raw passthrough touchpoints are CLI parsing, the single AgentPassthrough/AgentExecutionIntent value, Execute request construction, execution-record persistence, and human-facing evidence rendering. Retry/work/queue/catalog-threshold code carries the opaque value and may not read Harness, Provider, or Model fields. A routinglint/package-boundary check must enforce this allowlist.

Catalog/status rendering is observability only. Retry threshold policy may consume abstract catalog power numbers to compute MinPower thresholds. Status/catalog code must not feed concrete model/provider/harness choices into execution.

## Documentation corpus gate

This cleanup is not complete when only FEAT-006/FEAT-010 and the DDx skill are updated. The active documentation corpus must be scrubbed so operators, agents, and future implementation beads do not learn stale routing surfaces from older feature docs, test plans, technical designs, solution designs, or operator guides.

Active governing docs must describe `ddx run` / `ddx try` / `ddx work`, MinPower/MaxPower, passthrough-only pins, and status/debug-only ResolveRoute. Remaining references to `ddx agent run`, `ddx agent execute-bead`, `ddx agent work`, quorum/profile flags, or DDx-side routing vocabulary must be either removed from active docs or explicitly allowlisted as historical/deprecation/migration context with a reason. A grep-based docs check must make this enforceable.

## Review findings incorporated

- ddx-da19756a: execution path reinjects informational RouteDecision.
- ddx-d4100b7e: execution request drops DDx-owned power intent and actual-power evidence.
- ddx-1997b22d: ddx work preserves legacy work routing surface.
- ddx-b6a2417b: FEAT-006/specs still bless DDx-side ladders and overrides.
- ddx-a65fea8a: DDx service adapter performs endpoint/model policy.
- ddx-0f42c934: route-status scope leaks candidate traces into execution evidence.
- ddx-d06ae28c: live symptom where default work routes to cheap/incorrect model.
- ddx-6036e1bc: status/catalog work must remain observability and power-threshold only.
- ddx-8e9a11c4: plan aligned to upstream MinPower/MaxPower contract.
- ddx-52ce6249: public docs/skills use run/try/work instead of legacy agent run/execute surfaces.
- ddx-6232daf5: retry eligibility matrix added.
- ddx-b74d4ac6: passthrough exhaustion stop semantics added.
- ddx-b0d96cb9: mechanical passthrough ownership guardrails required.
- ddx-8a617e91: catalog/status display separated from retry threshold policy.
- ddx-02335e0b: repo-wide active docs corpus scrub is a first-class gate.

## Execution order

1. Align specs/docs and test expectations to the MinPower/MaxPower boundary with passthrough constraints.
2. Scrub the active docs corpus and add the docs grep allowlist/check so stale legacy command/routing guidance cannot remain hidden outside the core feature docs.
3. Pull the upstream agent power-bounds interface release: Execute accepts MinPower/MaxPower and passthrough constraints, responses report actual model/power, and model catalog exposes available powers.
4. Remove ResolveRoute and route preflight from run/try/work execution paths.
5. Pass MinPower/MaxPower and passthrough envelope through ServiceExecuteRequest and persist requested bounds, actual power/model, and requested passthrough in run evidence.
6. Replace work alias/work surface with run <- try <- work layering.
7. Implement DDx retry power policy using the eligibility matrix and agent catalog power thresholds, without inspecting passthrough values.
8. Remove DDx endpoint/model policy from execution adapter.
9. Rescope route-status/provider UI candidate traces to status/debug only.
10. Add routinglint and regression tests that forbid ResolveRoute/model-policy code in execution paths while allowing passthrough envelope plumbing.
notes: Amendment incorporated: --harness/--provider/--model are allowed as passthrough-only agent constraints. They must live in a narrow envelope, remain sticky across retries, and never drive DDx routing/retry decisions.

description:
PROBLEM
`ddx work --watch` can burn through multiple unrelated beads and then exit with opaque operator attention when the project root's git config is corrupted, for example when `.git/config` contains `core.bare=true`. In that state `git status` fails with `fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree`, but the worker output currently degrades to `exit status 128` and repeated pre-claim warnings across distinct bead IDs. Operators should not have to stop the factory, run a separate diagnosis, and restart for a known safe DDx-era corruption mode: `ddx work` should repair the known safe git config corruptions and continue.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/predispatch_dirty.go:179-183` only checks whether `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` exits successfully. For `core.bare=true`, git can exit 0 and print `false`, so the checkpoint path proceeds as if the project root were valid instead of triggering a repair.
- `cli/internal/agent/predispatch_dirty.go:292-293` and `cli/internal/agent/predispatch_dirty.go:377-381` call git with `Output()` and wrap only `exit status 128`, dropping git stderr such as `fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree`.
- `cli/internal/agent/lifecycle_dispatch.go:104-106` has the same stderr-dropping pattern for readiness/lifecycle project-root status snapshots.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1153-1174` only recognizes the implementation-dirty checkpoint refusal as a project-level stop. Other pre-execute checkpoint failures fall through normal attempt failure handling, so the loop can move on to the next ready bead and eventually trip the unrelated repeated-warning operator-attention path.
- `cli/cmd/doctor.go:990-1127` already detects and fixes the known safe local git config corruptions: `core.bare=true`, stray `core.worktree`, and local `core.hooksPath`. That logic is trapped behind `ddx doctor --fix` (`cli/cmd/command_factory_commands.go:98`) instead of being available to the work-loop preflight/remediation path.
- Existing coverage around `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_stay_alive_test.go:916-962` proves dirty implementation files stop after one claim, but there is no equivalent test for project-root git config corruption being repaired and retried. `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_checkpoint_test.go:426-430` covers ordinary dirty-file refusal, but not `core.bare=true` / non-worktree project roots.

PROPOSED FIX
- Extract/reuse the `doctor --fix` git repo health remediation as a reusable internal helper, rather than duplicating ad hoc config unsets in `ddx work`. The helper must preserve the existing safe set: unset `core.bare` when a working tree exists, unset stray `core.worktree`, unset local `core.hooksPath`; do not auto-enable `extensions.worktreeConfig` because doctor currently treats that as warning-only.
- Add a work-loop project-root git health preflight/remediator before readiness dispatch and before pre-execute checkpointing. When the known safe corruption is detected, repair it, emit durable/structured evidence naming the issue types and commands applied, then re-run the git health/status operation and continue the same drain cycle.
- Ensure a repaired first bead is not counted as a failed attempt and does not cause the worker to claim the next bead. The expected path is: detect corruption, repair, continue readiness/checkpoint for the same candidate, and then execute normally if the checkout is healthy.
- If repair fails, or if git remains unusable after the known repairs, then and only then release the claimed bead, emit `loop.operator_attention` with a stable reason such as `pre_dispatch_git_repair_failed`, include git stderr, and stop before claiming another bead.
- Preserve the existing implementation-dirty checkpoint behavior unchanged, including watch-mode preservation behavior for real dirty files.
- Add regressions for `core.bare=true` repair, failure-after-repair operator attention, and stderr preservation.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not redesign execute-bead loop extraction or the unrelated `ddx-f2a366db` code-health work.
- Do not auto-repair arbitrary git repository corruption. Keep remediation limited to the known safe local config keys already handled by `ddx doctor --fix`: `core.bare`, stray `core.worktree`, and local `core.hooksPath`.
- Do not silently hide repair. The operator must see a concise log/event that DDx repaired project git config before continuing.
- Do not prove the original writer of `core.bare=true` in this bead. If the corruption source recurs after this repair path lands, file a separate prevention/investigation bead.
- Do not change Fizeau routing, provider/model selection, or readiness classification semantics except for preserving git stderr in the existing lifecycle status error.
- Do not land the existing local branch `fix/pre-dispatch-git-corruption-stop` as-is. It is a diagnostic/stop-first prototype and must be revised to repair-and-continue.

PARENT AND DEPS

Deps: none.

acceptance: After a `no_changes` work result where `base_rev == result_rev`, the bead persists `work-retry-after`, `work-last-status`, and `work-last-detail`; `ddx bead ready --json --execution` suppresses the bead until the retry-after time; and a deterministic test covers the tracker-backed path rather than only in-memory worker logic.
description:
<context-digest>
Follow-up observation from the HELIX alpha run that launched `helix-fef22846` via `ddx agent work --once --json` and returned `status=no_changes`, `detail=agent made no commits`, `base_rev=result_rev=de67981a79a27ab8449bf6c475dda677fb25acfc`.
</context-digest>

`ddx agent work` reported a no-progress result but did not persist the retry-suppression metadata that `ReadyExecution()` expects, so the same bead remained at the front of the execution-ready queue immediately after the attempt.

## Reproduction
1. In `/Users/erik/Projects/helix`, run `ddx agent work --once --json` and get a `no_changes` result where `base_rev == result_rev`.
2. Inspect bead `helix-fef22846` in `.ddx/beads.jsonl` or via `ddx bead show --json`.
3. Observe the new `execute-bead` event is present, but `work-retry-after`, `work-last-status`, and `work-last-detail` are absent.
4. Run `ddx bead ready --json --execution` again.
5. Observe `helix-fef22846` is still the first execution-ready candidate instead of being suppressed for the cooldown window.

## Observed gap
`ExecuteBeadWorker.Run()` calls `SetExecutionCooldown()` for no-progress outcomes, but the tracker-backed HELIX run did not retain any of the cooldown fields that `ReadyExecution()` checks.

## Why this matters
Without durable cooldown metadata, `work` can repeatedly burn agent time and tokens on the same no-op bead in back-to-back scans.
title: Persist work cooldown metadata after no-progress attempts

description:
PROBLEM
`ddx work` without flags produces `lint hook: dispatch-failure: ResolveRoute: no viable routing candidate for pins min_power=7 max_power=8: N candidates rejected` because the pre-dispatch lint hook inherits `rcfg.Profile()="default"`, and fizeau's "default" profile pins `min_power=7,max_power=8`. Operators whose providers fall outside that band — local providers (power<=6) or frontier cloud providers via openrouter (power=9) — see every candidate rejected and the agent exits in <1s with no_evidence_produced. The post-attempt triage hook has the same latent bug. Pre-claim intake already sidesteps this with `ClearProfile: true`. Repro: in this repo with no flags, `ddx work --once` will emit the dispatch-failure event on the next claimed bead — see `.ddx/executions/20260508T173611-c6069449/manifest.json` events for a captured instance.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/routing_profile.go:11` normalizes empty profile to `"default"`.
- `cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:186-189` flows `rcfg.Profile()` into `ServiceExecuteRequest.Profile` when no `ProfileOverride` is set and `ClearProfile` is false.
- `cli/internal/agent/lint_hook.go:128-132` constructs the dispatched `AgentRunRuntime` without `ClearProfile` or `ProfileOverride`, so the lint hook's request carries `Profile="default"`.
- `cli/internal/agent/triage_hook.go:114-118` has the same omission.
- `cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:96-106` demonstrates the fix shape: `ClearProfile: true`.
- Downstream: fizeau's `internal/modelcatalog/catalog/models.yaml` pins the `default` profile to `min_power: 7, max_power: 8`; `service_routing.go` `routePowerPolicyForRequest` overlays that on every request whose `Profile` field is set.

PROPOSED FIX
- In `NewPreDispatchLintHook` (`cli/internal/agent/lint_hook.go:128-132`), set `ClearProfile: true` on the dispatched `AgentRunRuntime`. Lint is a mechanical scoring task; no profile constraint is needed.
- In `NewPostAttemptTriageHook` (`cli/internal/agent/triage_hook.go:114-118`), set `ClearProfile: true` for the same reason.
- Do not change `executeOnService`, `NormalizeRoutingProfile`, or any caller that legitimately uses Profile="default" with explicit `--harness/--model` overrides (those bypass the profile bound via fizeau's `routePowerBoundsForRequest`).
- Do not touch `NewPreClaimIntakeHook`; it already does the right thing.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change `NormalizeRoutingProfile` or the meaning of "default" — execute-bead and `ddx run` callers still rely on it as the default request shape and supply their own `--harness`/`--model`/`--profile` to bypass the bound.
- Do not modify fizeau's catalog.
- Do not add a new global setting; the fix is local to the two hook constructors.

PARENT + DEPS
No parent. No deps.
title: agent: clear default profile in pre-dispatch lint and post-attempt triage hooks

description:
PROBLEM
During dogfood of ddx-3b721804 on 2026-06-13, the execute-bead attempt ran a Go verification command from the wrong directory and got `go: go.mod file not found in current directory`, then later attempted to inspect `.ddx/executions/` from the wrong location and got `No such file or directory`. The same attempt temporarily moved new source files through `/tmp` while debugging. DDx instructions already say to work inside the execution worktree and keep evidence under the bundle path, but instructions alone did not prevent wrong-cwd verification or `/tmp` round-trips.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1925-1934 defines the no_changes rationale path in prose but does not make evidence-path checks mechanical for ordinary verification commands.
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1936-1941 says reports must go under the bundle path and never `/tmp`, but DDx does not reject transcript/tool activity that uses `/tmp` as an implementation or evidence staging area.
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1961-1967 says work only inside the execution worktree, but DDx does not validate that shell commands affecting verification ran from the repo/module root or execution worktree.
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_validation.go:147-161 validates commit/gate integrity after the attempt, but it skips checks it cannot observe and does not classify wrong-cwd verification or `/tmp` file round-trips as attempt-integrity defects.

PROPOSED FIX
Add structured transcript/session validation for execute-bead attempts that detects verification commands run from the wrong cwd, evidence-path lookups outside the execution bundle, and source/evidence file moves through `/tmp`. When detected, preserve the attempt or require repair before closure with a typed integrity reason and durable evidence.

NON-SCOPE
Do not ban temporary compiler caches or harmless OS temp usage by build tools. Do not parse arbitrary shell perfectly; target high-signal patterns DDx can observe from tool command arguments, cwd, and output.

description:
V1 of 3 children under epic ddx-53c96967.

REFINE (do not rewrite) docs/helix/00-discover/product-vision.md and docs/helix/01-frame/principles.md to reflect what's settled.

CURRENT STATE:
- product-vision.md (177 lines) — written before several decisions landed. Has aspirational language and outdated references.
- principles.md (72 lines) — short list of guiding principles. Some are load-bearing, some are filler.
- prd.md (370 lines) and concerns.md (257 lines) are reference context — read for background, but DO NOT modify them in this bead.

DECISIONS THAT HAVE SETTLED AND SHOULD BE REFLECTED:
1. DDx is the platform layer; HELIX is the workflow layer; Dun is the quality layer. Three-project stack with explicit boundaries.
2. Project-local everything: ddx init/install only touch <projectRoot>. The only global ddx artifact is ddx-server. (FEAT-015, just shipped.)
3. Cost-tiered work: cheap models do, strong models review, deterministic fixes at the top of the ladder. Goal is closed-bead throughput per dollar.
4. Endpoint-first routing redesign: providers are endpoints + live discovery + fuzzy model match (in progress; reference don't promise).
5. Single-skill consolidation: DDx ships ONE 'ddx' skill (not seven). Per FEAT-011.

description:
Re-filed from agent-9465287e in /Users/erik/Projects/agent (closed there as 'tracked upstream'; the agent service is not the failure surface). Originally observed in ddx v0.6.2-alpha1 against agent v0.9.9 during SD-024 work.

## Symptom

Worker spawned with explicit pin:

    ddx work --harness claude

First attempt on a bead routes correctly to claude (e.g. opus-4.7) and produces a result. When the post-merge reviewer returns REQUEST_CHANGES the bead reopens. The next work iteration retries the bead but the worker's --harness override is NOT propagated to that retry. Tier-attempt events show:

    kind:tier-attempt body=tier=standard harness= model= probe=no viable provider, no viable harness found
    kind:tier-attempt body=tier=smart    harness= model= probe=no viable provider, no viable harness found
    kind:escalation-summary winning_tier=exhausted

Note harness= and model= empty — the retry constructs a service request with Harness="". Smart-routing returns zero candidates at every tier above cheap (cheap suppressed by adaptive min-tier from prior failures). Bead bounces between REQUEST_CHANGES (cycle 1) → execution_failed (cycle 2 with no harness routing) repeatedly.

Concrete instance: ddx-dd7fce7e in /Users/erik/Projects/ddx/.ddx/beads.jsonl shows the pattern at events around 2026-04-25T21:46-21:47Z.

## Principle

**Retries should use the same parameters as the initial work.** A reopened bead's retry must inherit every explicit pin (harness, model, model-ref, profile, provider) that the worker was spawned with. Otherwise the retry is a different request, not a retry — and the work cannot converge.

This is a general invariant, not specific to harness overrides. Any explicit pin the worker was launched with must propagate to every iteration on every bead the worker handles, including post-reopen retries.

## Diagnosis (from agent-9465287e worker analysis)

The agent service surface (CONTRACT-003) is correct. The agent has no tier concept — tier classification and adaptive min-tier floors are ddx-side abstractions layered on top of the agent's per-call routing. Loosening the agent's routing engine to return candidates when the harness is empty would change behavior for every other caller and is not the right lever.

The fix is a few lines of option-propagation in the ddx work's reopen-retry path: when a bead reopens after REQUEST_CHANGES (or any review-driven reopen), the loop must copy the worker-level explicit pins into the next iteration's ExecuteBeadOptions / service.Execute request, the same way it does on the initial claim.

## In-scope files

- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go (or wherever the retry path constructs its execute-bead invocation)
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go if review-driven reopens have a separate path
- Regression test asserting the second service.Execute call carries the same Harness, Model, Profile values as the first when the bead was reopened by a reviewer

## Out of scope

- Agent-side routing engine changes — the surface is correct
- Adaptive min-tier behavior tuning (separate concern)
- Tool-loop detection (separate concern, see agent-1bdb9b60 in agent repo)
title: work: reopen-retry must reuse initial worker params (harness, model, profile)

description:
## Goal

Align `cli/internal/server/workers.go`'s default-path escalation semantics with the migration that already shipped on the CLI path via bead `ddx-87fb72c2` (epic `ddx-fdd3ea36`, see `docs/migrations/routing-config.md`). Today the two paths disagree:

- **CLI path** `cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go:1792`: `escalationEnabled := escalate && harness == "" && model == ""` — escalation is opt-in via the `--escalate` flag.
- **Server path** `cli/internal/server/workers.go:650`: `escalationEnabled := spec.Harness == "" && spec.Model == ""` — escalation is implicitly on whenever neither harness nor model is pinned. No `--escalate` equivalent plumbed through the worker spec.

Because `ddx work` submits to the server worker by default (not `--local`), the user-facing surface still runs the tier loop + `ResolveTierCandidates` cooldown probe + `escalation.AdaptiveMinTier` filter on every dispatch — even though the migration declared the tier ladder opt-in. This is the proximate cause of the "all tiers exhausted — no viable provider" failure observed on `worker-20260429T033325-bedf` against this project today, and was confirmed by a control probe in this session: `ddx work --once --local` against `ddx-fdd3ea36` (no flags, no pin) reproduces "all tiers exhausted" while `ddx work --once --local --no-adaptive-min-tier` succeeds end-to-end on the cheap tier (qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b @ lmstudio-bragi, zero cost).

## Concrete change

Plumb an explicit escalation-opt-in flag through the worker spec, matching the CLI path's `--escalate` semantics:

1. Add a boolean field to `WorkerSpec` (in `cli/internal/server/workers.go` or wherever `WorkerSpec` is defined) named e.g. `Escalate`. Default `false`.
2. The `--escalate` flag on `ddx work` (already exists for the CLI path; verify it's plumbed to the worker submission, add the wiring if not) sets `WorkerSpec.Escalate = true`.
3. Change `cli/internal/server/workers.go:650` from:

       escalationEnabled := spec.Harness == "" && spec.Model == ""

   to:

       escalationEnabled := spec.Escalate && spec.Harness == "" && spec.Model == ""

4. Update `cli/internal/server/workers_test.go` to assert: with `spec.Escalate=false` (default), `executor` follows the `singleTierAttempt` path at line 692-702 — no `ResolveProfileLadder` call, no tier loop, no `AdaptiveMinTier` evaluation. With `spec.Escalate=true`, the existing tier-loop behavior is preserved.

That is all. Do not delete any helper functions in this bead — `ResolveProfileLadder`, `ResolveTierModelRef`, `AdaptiveMinTier` all remain (they're still consumed via the `--escalate` opt-in path). Their deletion is reserved for a separate cleanup bead after this lands and there's evidence no caller uses them.

## In-scope files

- `cli/internal/server/workers.go` — line ~650, plus any `WorkerSpec` struct definition (could be in this file or `cli/internal/server/types.go` / `models.go` — locate via `grep -nE "type WorkerSpec\b" cli/`).
- `cli/internal/server/workers_test.go` — add the two assertions above.
- The `ddx work --escalate` flag wiring on the worker-submit path. If `--escalate` is currently CLI-only (i.e. only consulted in the `--local` branch), this bead also plumbs it through `cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go`'s server-submit code path. Locate via `grep -nE "GetBool\\(\"escalate\"\\)|--escalate" cli/cmd/`.
- Possibly `cli/internal/server/server.go` if `WorkerSpec` is constructed there from an HTTP/MCP request body.

## Out of scope (do NOT touch)

- `cli/internal/agent/profile_ladder.go` — keep all helpers; deletion is a separate bead.
- `cli/internal/escalation/escalation.go::AdaptiveMinTier` — keep; deletion is a separate bead.
- Default profile change from `default` to `local` — separate bead (`routing-unify-2`).
- `cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go:1792` — already correct; no change.
- `docs/migrations/routing-config.md` — already correct; describes the migration this bead completes for the server path.
- Any work on `cli/internal/agent` or `agent` SDK — agent already exposes everything DDx needs.

## Acceptance

1. `cd cli && go test ./internal/server/... ./internal/agent/...` passes.
2. `cd /home/erik/Projects/ddx && /home/erik/.local/bin/ddx work --once --local` (no flags, no pin) against this project resolves and dispatches a single-call attempt. Verifiable by:
   - The bead receives at most one `kind:routing` event from the new flow (matches the `singleTierAttempt` pattern), not multiple `kind:tier-attempt skipped` events from the tier loop.
   - The work log line `adaptive min-tier: skipping cheap tier ...` does NOT appear.
3. `cd /home/erik/Projects/ddx && /home/erik/.local/bin/ddx work --once --local --escalate` against this project preserves the existing tier-loop behavior. Verifiable: at least one `kind:tier-attempt` event appears, the `adaptive min-tier` line still prints when applicable.
4. Unit test in `cli/internal/server/workers_test.go` asserts: with `spec.Escalate=false`, `agent.ResolveProfileLadder` is not called (use the existing call-counter test seam in `cli/internal/agent/profile_ladder.go::ResolveProfileLadderCallCount`); with `spec.Escalate=true`, the call counter advances.
5. Operator policy preserved: `ddx work --harness X` and `ddx work --model Y` continue to work and bypass escalation regardless of `--escalate` (the existing `&& spec.Harness == "" && spec.Model == ""` predicate handles this).
6. The migration doc `docs/migrations/routing-config.md` is updated to mention that the worker path now matches the CLI path semantics, OR a one-line cross-reference is added if its current text is sufficient.

## Why this is a tight bead

It is a single 1-line behavioral change in `workers.go:650` plus the worker-spec field plumbing. The supervisor checkpoint mandate is "one bead/fix at a time"; this is the smallest meaningful step toward unification given the current tree state. Do not bundle helper deletions, default-profile changes, or schema cleanups — those are reserved for follow-up beads.

## Rollback

If the change breaks anything: revert the workers.go diff. The pre-change behavior was the prior implicit-on default; reverting restores it. Worker-spec field can stay (additive, default false). Migration doc edit is independent.

description:
PROBLEM
  Three observed cases on 2026-05-10 of fake-work: implementer
  models write aspirational commit messages but the actual diff
  is minimal/absent. The reviewer rubber-stamps the attempt and
  the bead closes with AC not satisfied.

  Cases:
    - ddx-1f774edf "remove network I/O from Land()" — claimed
      PreClaimGitOps interface + LandingGitOps cleanup; diff
      was 4 files / 30 lines.
    - ddx-94a368b6 "conformance transition-matrix coverage" —
      preserved on iteration ref, never landed.
    - ddx-d22293ba "wire RetainDays prune" — claimed prune loop,
      counters, 5 tests, agent-logs/workers scope; diff was 5
      lines setting a default value.

  The reviewer ALREADY emits per_ac[].grade + per_ac[].evidence
  (cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go:204-234). The
  defect is that the evidence string is UNVERIFIED TEXT. A
  rubber-stamping reviewer can write "evidence": "types.go:42"
  for an AC it never checked. Strengthening reviewer prose
  without a mechanical forcing function would create
  false-positive BLOCKs on legitimate work (renamed tests,
  negative AC, mechanical refactors, etc.) and still fail to
  catch fake-work convincingly.

  This bead is the FIRST of two: it adds a mechanical
  AC-verification tool that both implementer (pre-commit
  self-check) and reviewer (gate ratification) invoke with the
  SAME inputs. Sister bead changes the reviewer behavior to
  ratify this tool's output rather than re-grep the diff
  independently.

CURRENT STATE
  - No CLI subcommand performs per-AC verification mechanically.
  - The reviewer prompt asks for per-AC grading but provides no
    structured input — reviewer must grep a possibly-30k-line
    diff to find evidence, which scales poorly and invites
    rubber-stamping.
  - Implementer has no way to self-check whether its work would
    pass review before committing — pure information
    asymmetry.

PROPOSED FIX
  Implement `ddx bead ac-check <id>` (or `ddx bead check <id>`)
  with the following behavior:

  1. Inputs: bead ID; the working tree (or a specific rev
     range, default: merge-base..HEAD).

  2. Read b.Acceptance from the bead; parse into numbered AC
     items.

  3. Per-AC inspection pipeline. Classify each AC by
     lightweight regex/heuristic, then mechanically resolve:

     a. test-name AC (matches /Test[A-Z]\\w+/):
        - Run `go test -run '^<name>$'` on relevant packages.
        - Record pass/fail/missing.

     b. build/gate AC (matches "passes", "green", "lefthook",
        "pre-commit"):
        - Invoke `lefthook run pre-commit` or `go test ./...`
          per AC text.
        - Record exit code.

     c. negative AC (matches "no calls to", "does not",
        "remove", "no longer"):
        - `git grep` the named symbol on POST-IMAGE.
        - Pass if 0 hits (or fewer than baseline).

     d. symbol AC (matches `` `Foo.Bar()` `` or similar
        backtick-quoted identifier):
        - `git grep` the symbol; require ≥1 hit AND at least
          one diff hunk touching it.

     e. mechanical AC (matches "rename", "doc", "comment"):
        - File existence / rename detection via `git
          diff --name-status`.

     f. prose AC (everything else):
        - Emit `needs-judgment=true`. NEVER auto-pass, NEVER
          auto-fail.

  4. ACAliases support. The bead body may include an optional
     `ACAliases:` map (e.g., `AC #3: TestFooBar -> TestFoo/bar`)
     so a legitimate refactor can declare its substitutions.
     The tool reads it; the reviewer sees it.

  5. Output. Both human-readable and machine-readable:
     - Stdout: human-readable table per AC.
     - File: `.ddx/executions/<attempt-id>/ac-check.json` with
       structured per-AC results.

     Example structured output:
       {
         "schema_version": 1,
         "attempt_id": "...",
         "bead_id": "ddx-...",
         "summary": {"pass": 3, "fail": 1, "needs_judgment": 1},
         "items": [
           {"ac": 1, "kind": "test-name", "name": "TestFoo",
            "result": "pass", "evidence": "package x; test ran 0.04s"},
           {"ac": 4, "kind": "symbol", "name": "RemovedExecutionDirs",
            "result": "fail",
            "evidence": "grep found 0 hits; AC requires symbol present"},
           {"ac": 3, "kind": "prose",
            "result": "needs_judgment",
            "evidence": "no mechanical anchor; defer to reviewer"}
         ]
       }

  6. CLI: `ddx bead ac-check <id> [--rev-range <base>..<head>]
     [--package <go-package>] [--json]`. Idempotent. No
     side effects on the bead store.

  7. Tests:
     - TestACCheck_TestNameAC_Passes
     - TestACCheck_TestNameAC_Renamed_WithAlias
     - TestACCheck_TestNameAC_Missing_Fails
     - TestACCheck_NegativeAC_FlagsResidue
     - TestACCheck_NegativeAC_AbsenceConfirmed_Passes
     - TestACCheck_SymbolAC_PresentInDiff_Passes
     - TestACCheck_SymbolAC_NotInDiff_Fails
     - TestACCheck_MechanicalAC_RenameDetection
     - TestACCheck_ProseAC_NeedsJudgment_NeverAutoFail
     - TestACCheck_ProseAC_NeedsJudgment_NeverAutoPass
     - TestACCheck_JSONOutput_SchemaVersion1
     - TestACCheck_RegressionFakeRetainDays: replay the
       917cfbfa7 fake-work diff; assert ac-check yields
       multiple `fail` results for the missing prune logic
       and tests.

NON-SCOPE
  - Changing the reviewer prompt or gate behavior (sister bead).
  - Wiring ac-check into execute-bead workflow (sister bead).
  - Strictness modes by bead label (sister bead).
  - New verdict types like REQUEST_CLARIFICATION (sister bead).

INTERSECTIONS
  - Sister bead "fix(review): reviewer ratifies ac-check" —
    that bead consumes ac-check.json as the reviewer's primary
    input and changes the gate semantics. THIS bead is purely
    additive and can land independently.
  - Existing reviewer per_ac[] structure (execute_bead_review.go:204-234)
