The worker converts this infrastructure failure into a landing failure (review_malfunction), releasing the claim and preserving the result as dangling-success, so every auto-landing becomes manual operator verify+merge work.

ROOT CAUSE
cli/internal/agent/candidate_cycle.go:425-436: when c.Reviewer.Review returns any error, the cycle immediately sets ExecuteBeadStatusReviewMalfunction and returns — there is no retry and no distinction between transport-class failures and genuine verdict failures. The classification ALREADY exists one layer down: cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go:1267-1279 distinguishes evidence.OutcomeReviewProviderEmpty (0-byte output, transport/backend availability) from evidence.OutcomeReviewUnparseable (non-empty but malformed, prompt/format drift), and cli/internal/evidence/marker.go:22 defines the marker string — but candidate_cycle.go discards that distinction.

PROPOSED FIX
In the review step of the candidate cycle (cli/internal/agent/candidate_cycle.go:425-436):
1. When the review error is transport-class (error chain or reviewRes.Error matches evidence.OutcomeReviewProviderEmpty), retry the review up to 2 more times (same route).
2. If still transport-failing, exhaust and set review_malfunction as today, but the report Detail must name the failing route (harness/model from the review artifacts manifest) and the retry count, so dead review routes are operator-visible.
3. Genuine verdict outcomes (parseable REQUEST_CHANGES/BLOCK, or OutcomeReviewUnparseable non-empty output after retries) keep today's behavior — they are not transport failures and must not be retried as such (a REJECT is a verdict, not a flake).
4. Log each retry via the existing appendReviewGateError event path (cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_post_review.go:519-532) so bead events show the retry trail.
Note the bead's original AC asked for fallback re-route to an alternate provider/model; DDx does not own routing (Fizeau does, per SD-024 sealed ResolvedConfig in cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go:1290-1309). - The multi-slot review-group reducer semantics (execute_bead_post_review.go:554+).
- Fixing whatever makes the reviewer provider return 0 bytes (infra issue, tracked separately).

description:
PROBLEM
Two contenders can both observe a stale bead-store collection lock and mutate the canonical lock pathname from different snapshots. A unique tombstone name alone does not make stale breaking single-winner. A stable stale-break guard alone is also insufficient when the age rule supersedes a still-live holder: that old holder can later release by pathname and delete the replacement.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/bead/lock.go:54-83 retries os.Mkdir on the canonical lock directory. cli/internal/bead/lock.go:86-110 reads pid/acquired_at and removes the canonical directory without serializing the observation and mutation across processes. Lines 100-105 may classify an over-age lock stale even when its PID is still live, while cli/internal/bead/lock.go:112-113 later releases the old holder with unconditional RemoveAll. cli/internal/bead/backend_jsonl.go:126-135 and cli/internal/bead/axon_backend.go:196-205 also acquire the same directory primitive and release by unconditional pathname removal.
The previously landed candidate 7feaa1b67264e153dc5abdf1e1cf68a6b5226d21 replaced RemoveAll with an unconditional unique rename, but f08a2cdaa reverted it because source identity was still not protected. Counterexample 1: contenders A and B inspect the old stale directory; A renames/removes it and installs a fresh canonical lock; delayed B renames that pathname to B's tombstone and deletes A's lock. Counterexample 2: live holder A becomes age-stale, breaker B safely tombstones A and acquires a replacement, then delayed A releases by pathname and deletes B.
Phase 0 WB-5 requires a single-winner cross-process stale-break protocol at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase0-stop-the-self-harm-plan-2026-07-13.md:124-132.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a package-local crash-safe cross-process transition guard for the collection lock. Use a never-deleted sibling sidecar advisory-lock file whose deterministic name ends in .lock, plus a keyed same-process mutex. The OS file lock must release automatically on process death. Ordinary acquisition/release must never delete or recreate the sidecar inode/path. Non-contention lock/open errors fail safe and propagate where the caller can return them.
Change acquireDirLock to return a lease containing the canonical path and a strong unique owner token. On successful os.Mkdir, write owner_token with pid and acquired_at before publishing success. Migrate Store.WithLock, JSONLBackend.WithLock, and AxonBackend.WithLock to defer the lease Release method and join any release error into the named return.
Stale break must acquire the transition guard within the original LockWait budget, then re-read and reclassify the current canonical directory, verify its identity, and rename only that freshly inspected stale directory to a contender-unique sibling tombstone whose name also ends in .lock. Remove only the exact tombstone produced by a successful rename. Release the guard before retrying ordinary os.Mkdir. Preserve existing OR semantics: a valid dead PID or valid over-age acquired_at is sufficient; missing/malformed metadata alone is not.
Lease release must acquire the same transition guard, re-read canonical owner_token, and remove the canonical directory only when the token exactly matches the lease. Missing/mismatched tokens mean the lease was superseded, so release preserves the replacement. If guarded release cannot be proven, return an error and leave the lock in place; never fall back to unconditional RemoveAll.
Add deterministic subprocess/barrier tests with stage signals emitted inside guard acquisition, not sleep-based ordering, for delayed stale observers, live-age-stale delayed release, crash-released guard ownership, stable sidecar identity, and byte-identical replacement metadata.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change tracker record format, StaleLockAge, LockWait, backend selection, agent tracker locks, main-git locks, git index locks, or lockmetrics caps. Do not extract a shared lock package; ddx-1c8d9319 and ddx-3f156500 own separate sites and Phase 1 WB-8 owns unification.

description:
PROBLEM
There is no mechanical way to read a DDx document's status stamp, so downstream verification-coverage, duplicate-id, and stale-observation checks have nothing to build on. Status markers are heterogeneous: some docs use a body line `**Status:**` with free-text qualifiers, some use YAML frontmatter `status:`, and 40 of 56 design docs (including SD-013 and TD-027) have no status marker at all.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The package `cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/` does not exist. The intended pattern is the sibling analyzer at cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer.go with a CLI entrypoint at cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/cmd/evidencelint/main.go and testdata fixtures under cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/testdata/. The mechanical contract is defined in docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md under WB-1, steps 1-2.

PROPOSED FIX
Create `cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/` (analyzer.go, analyzer_test.go, cmd/spechonesty/main.go, testdata/ fixtures) modeled on evidencelint. Implement a status parser that (a) recognizes both encodings — a body `**Status:**` line and YAML frontmatter `status:` — and normalizes free-text qualifiers to a base status (e.g. `Complete`, `Implemented`, `Proposed`, `In Progress`, `Deferred`, `Aspirational`), and (b) treats a missing status on any SD/TD/ADR document as a lint failure requiring a stamp. This missing-status rule — not the Complete-check — is what catches SD-013 and TD-027. Parsing must be deterministic and read-only; the linter never mutates documents.

NON-SCOPE
Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Do not implement verification-coverage, waiver, duplicate-id, or stale-observation logic here (later children). Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope.

PARENT: ddx-2e992616. DEPS: none — this child lands first as the package foundation; later children depend on it.
title: spechonesty lint: scaffold package and status parser (body + frontmatter)

After execution and server consumers are detached, DDx configuration still accepts concrete provider/model ownership fields: project models, per-harness reasoning, endpoints, URLs, credentials, endpoint timeouts, and dead embedded-runner presets. Silently ignoring them would leave operators believing DDx controls Fizeau routing and credentials. The migration must hard-error consistently through every config entry point and the supported schema/types must no longer expose these fields.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE

- `cli/internal/config/types.go:443-495` defines `agent.model`, `agent.models`, `agent.reasoning_levels`, `agent.endpoints`, `AgentEndpoint`, URLs, API keys, endpoint defaults, and request timeouts.

- Hard-error on the exact legacy fields `agent.model`, `agent.models`, `agent.reasoning_levels`, and `agent.endpoints`, including empty and null values. The error must name the exact field, absolute config path, and Fizeau migration instruction.

No supported DDx type may contain provider URL, credential, provider default, model catalog, or per-harness reasoning configuration.
- Remove legacy endpoints from this repository's `.ddx/config.yaml` so the migrated repository loads under its own rules.
- Update `docs/migrations/routing-config.md` with DDx-to-Fizeau global/project config examples and explicit preservation of generic one-request constraints.
- Preserve only generic DDx execution controls and explicit public request passthrough: Harness, Provider, Model, Policy/Profile, MinPower, MaxPower, Reasoning/Effort, Permissions, Timeout, IdleTimeout, ProviderTimeout, Role, work directory, and correlation metadata.

description:

description:
PROBLEM
On 2026-06-29 an 8-core niflheim host sustained load averages of 38-52 while one DDx worker produced four provider transport failures in roughly two hours and closed no beads. The worker immediately selected more work even though the host was already overloaded, compounding latency and failure probability.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2365 selects the next candidate and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2579-2672 proceeds from candidate selection to claim without sampling normalized host load or applying a cancellable delay. cli/internal/workerstatus currently has process/status scanning but no injectable load-pressure snapshot, so the pre-claim path cannot distinguish ordinary utilization from load far above runtime.NumCPU().

PROPOSED FIX
Add a small platform-aware, injectable load snapshot under cli/internal/workerstatus that reports 5-minute load, CPU count, normalized ratio, support state, and threshold comparison. Before claim, consult that snapshot; above a configurable default ratio of 2.5, emit a structured load_pressure_backoff observation and use a bounded, context-cancellable delay proportional to overload. Unsupported platforms and unavailable /proc/loadavg must fail open with diagnostics.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change queue ordering, add a general host load manager, alter provider outcome classification, implement clustered transport cooldowns, or hold any bead lease during the delay. Preserve the parent constraint not to change durable_audit commit flow.

PARENT
ddx-29491a0e. This child owns load sampling and pre-claim load-pressure pacing only.

DEPS
ddx-aa6cc320 must land first because this child changes internal/agent code and its required package gate currently launches live providers.
notes: Refined after the deterministic preclaim fallback produced a vague first-slice AC; this replacement assigns the load-sampling/backoff half of parent ddx-29491a0e without changing intent.

description:
Sibling to ddx-738edf47. Codex review of the sequencing plan flagged that the false-closure bug has a broader fix than just its pinpoint: the work has no invariant check enforcing that every `status: closed` transition carries execution evidence plus a parseable terminal verdict (review APPROVE, review SKIPPED_BY_FLAG, or manual close).

Reporter context: axon bead `axon-c5cc071a` closed in 4m33s with `events: []`, no bundle, no commit — the closure path was walked without any gate.

## Work

1. Identify every call site in cli/internal/agent and cli/internal/server that transitions a bead to `status: closed`. At minimum: work happy path, reviewer APPROVE path, `--no-review` skip path, manual `ddx bead close`.
2. Centralize closure through a single `ClosureGate` (or similar) that refuses to close unless:
   - execute-bead has a success event referencing a base_rev/result_rev pair, AND
   - a terminal verdict event exists (kind=review with summary APPROVE, or kind=review-skipped with an explicit reason, or kind=manual-close with actor set).
3. Add a table-driven invariant test that constructs synthetic bead states (missing execution evidence, missing verdict, malformed verdict, manual close) and asserts the gate's verdict.
4. Explicit escape hatch for `ddx bead close --force` (manual operator close) — logged with actor + reason, bypasses the gate.

## Relationship to ddx-738edf47

738edf47 is the specific false-closure symptom report + suspected root cause. This bead is the structural invariant test that catches similar regressions regardless of which upstream component (reviewer, work, worker) walks the close path incorrectly. Both can land together; this one owns the test harness, 738edf47 owns the repro fix.

description:
## Problem

No single document traces the provider/model/harness resolution path from CLI flags to the final HTTP request. SD-015 and SD-023 are SPECS — they describe what should happen in 5 routing modes. The code lives across routing.go, discovery.go, agent_runner.go, runner.go, and agent_cmd.go. A newcomer debugging a routing bug must infer the flow by reading all of them.

The audit for epic ddx-2d974641 turned up a RouteRequest struct missing its Provider field, and a parallel RunOptions.Provider path that bypasses routing — neither of which is documented. This is the kind of hidden structural defect a Resolution Path document would have flagged on first read.

## Fix

Write docs/helix/02-design/solution-designs/SD-015-resolution-path-trace.md (or similar location; coordinate with SD-015's author). The document traces one concrete invocation end-to-end:

    ddx work --once --local --provider vidar-omlx --model-ref qwen/qwen3.6

Walk through every layer, with file:line citations:

1. **CLI parse** — cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go flag extraction (line references).

2. **RouteFlags -> RouteRequest normalization** — routing.go:NormalizeRouteRequest. What each CLI flag maps to; which flags are discarded when they don't match an expected shape; the current gap around --provider.

3. **Discovery probe** — discovery.go:DiscoverProviderModels. When it fires; what it caches; the 30s TTL; how failures are handled.

4. **Candidate planning** — routing.go:BuildCandidatePlans / evaluateCandidate. For each registered harness, the state map lookup and the viability checks.

5. **Fuzzy matching** — discovery.go:FuzzyMatchModel. Pool selection (global vs per-provider), normalization (current gaps), prefix + tiebreak algorithm.

6. **Scoring** — routing.go:scoreCandidate. Per-profile scoring, cost class, historical success rate, provider-affinity bonus (when implemented).

7. **Candidate ranking** — routing.go:RankCandidates / SelectBestCandidate. Non-viable rejection, stable tiebreak.

8. **Dispatch** — runner.go:Run. Harness-specific branches (virtual, agent, script, HTTP-provider-embedded, default exec). For embedded: agent_runner.go:RunAgent -> resolveEmbeddedAgentProvider -> agent library call.

9. **Wire-level request** — ddx-agent builds the HTTP body (system_prompt + messages + tools), sends to the provider. What the server receives.

10. **Response parsing** — streaming or non-streaming decode; where 'unexpected end of JSON input' (ddx-6a5dfe35) surfaces.

Include a SEQUENCE DIAGRAM (mermaid or ASCII) showing the layers.

Include a GAP TABLE at the top listing every currently-missing piece (as of whatever the SD-015 implementation state is) with links to the specific beads tracking each gap.

Keep the document MAINTAINED alongside the code: update it when RouteRequest gains a field, when a new routing mode lands, when fuzzy match gains a normalization step.

## Files likely touched

- docs/helix/02-design/solution-designs/SD-015-resolution-path-trace.md (new)
- docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-006-agent-service.md — add a single-line pointer at the top of the 'Overview' section
- skills/ddx/reference/agents.md — add a one-line pointer in 'Harness / profile / persona dispatch' section so agents consulting the skill can follow up to the full trace when needed

## Out of scope

- Rewriting SD-015 or SD-023 — this doc complements them; they describe intent, this describes current reality.
- Documenting future routing modes that haven't landed.
title: docs: add 'Resolution Path' developer guide tracing CLI flag -> final HTTP dispatch

## Superseded — wrong diagnosis

Filed under the belief that DDx needs hand-authored omlx surface entries in the model catalog to map qwen/qwen3.6 -> Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit on vidar-omlx.

**This is not the right fix.** An audit of the resolution path (see parent epic ddx-2d974641) showed that the real defect is in fuzzy matching + the RouteRequest plumbing: the fuzzy matcher exists (discovery.go:FuzzyMatchModel) and provider discovery exists (DiscoverProviderModels probes /v1/models on each provider), but:

1. The matcher uses STRICT case-sensitive prefix — qwen/qwen3.6 can't match Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit even semantically.
2. The matcher runs over a provider-union (d.AllModels()) that loses provider identity.
3. --provider is silently discarded at NormalizeRouteRequest (types.go:330 RouteRequest has no Provider field).
4. Catalog-resolved refs (ModelRef path) don't go through the fuzzy matcher at all.

Once those are fixed, no catalog entries are needed — canonical refs fuzzy-match against discovered omlx model IDs at runtime. See sibling beads filed under ddx-2d974641.

Closing as invalid: catalog-first approach would require hand-authoring entries for every new MLX model name format that appears, which defeats the purpose of discovery.

description:
PROBLEM
During the live Claude TUI canary for bead `ddx-e2fd88f3` attempt `20260616T081050-c092a258`, Claude auto-backgrounded `lefthook run pre-commit 2>&1 | tail -30` after the 120s tool timeout, then launched a second `lefthook run pre-commit 2>&1` before consuming the first background task completion. The first background task later completed exit 0; the duplicate later failed exit 1. This wastes worker time and can create false-red verification or git/index contention in a worktree that already has valid acceptance evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/harness_config.go:58-79` runs Claude through `--print -p --verbose --output-format stream-json`, which permits Claude's long-running shell commands to be auto-backgrounded by the harness surface.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2072-2078` only prohibits rerunning identical long-running commands without documenting why prior output is invalid; it does not require the agent to wait for or inspect an auto-backgrounded command's completion notification before launching the same verification command again.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_guardrails_test.go:49-94` enforces the prompt guardrails but has no `background_verification_completion` guardrail.

PROPOSED FIX
Add an explicit Claude/agent execution guardrail and regression coverage: when a long-running verification command is auto-backgrounded, the worker prompt must instruct the agent to wait for/read the background completion/output before rerunning the same command, and not start duplicate `lefthook` or `go test` processes in the same worktree unless inputs changed and the prior result is invalid. If attempt-integrity parsing already sees multiple equivalent verification commands, it should preserve the earlier successful acceptance evidence and surface the duplicate as a warning rather than converting the attempt to false-red solely because the duplicate failed.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change the Claude CLI or disable Claude's backgrounding behavior.
- Do not loosen the no-red-code or staged pre-commit acceptance gates.
- Do not change routing/provider selection.

PARENT + DEPS
Parent: `ddx-3106674f`.
Deps: none. This is a canary reliability bug discovered after `ddx-e2fd88f3` succeeded.

1. **Fixed**: HTTP provider-backed native harnesses (lmstudio, omlx, openrouter, ollama, openai) now dispatch through the concrete provider identity instead of by configured provider name. (agent-285a05d2)

We never wrote any `ProviderPreference` code on the DDx side, so (2) is purely subtractive for us — nothing to remove.

description:
PROBLEM
  scripts/demos/_lib.sh defines cleanup_demo_dir() but does not register it
  via trap, so callers (04-project-create.sh, 05-evolve-feature.sh,
  06-full-journey.sh) only invoke it on the happy path. An early exit
  caused by `set -e` (or a manual Ctrl-C) leaks $DEMO_DIR. Low severity
  because these are demo recording scripts, not CI scripts, but the leak
  is real and accumulates across demo runs. Discovered by the 2026-05-09
  test-cleanup audit.

ROOT CAUSE
  - scripts/demos/_lib.sh declares cleanup_demo_dir() that runs
    `rm -rf "$DEMO_DIR"` but the caller pattern is:
        DEMO_DIR=$(mktemp -d ...)
        ... happy path ...
        cleanup_demo_dir
    No `trap cleanup_demo_dir EXIT` or `trap '...' INT TERM`.
  - Files affected:
        scripts/demos/04-project-create.sh
        scripts/demos/05-evolve-feature.sh
        scripts/demos/06-full-journey.sh
    (07-quickstart.sh already cleans correctly; check before edit.)
  - When `set -e` is in effect and an early command fails, the script
    exits before cleanup_demo_dir is called, leaving $DEMO_DIR on disk.

PROPOSED FIX
  - In scripts/demos/_lib.sh, add a `register_demo_cleanup()` helper that
    callers invoke immediately after `mktemp -d`. The helper sets
    `trap cleanup_demo_dir EXIT INT TERM`.
  - Update 04-project-create.sh, 05-evolve-feature.sh, 06-full-journey.sh
    to call register_demo_cleanup right after DEMO_DIR is created.
  - Verify 07-quickstart.sh either already uses trap-based cleanup or
    gets the same treatment if it doesn't.

NON-SCOPE
  - Other shell scripts under scripts/ (the audit confirmed test-hooks.sh,
    test-doc-snippets.sh, check-legacy-routing-docs.sh, capture-omlx-fixture.sh
    already trap cleanup correctly).
  - Refactoring the demo scripts beyond adding the cleanup hook.

INTERSECTIONS
  - No deps.
title: scripts/demos: add trap-based cleanup_demo_dir to all demo recording scripts

acceptance:
1. lefthook.yml contains a pre-commit hook (e.g., skill-dir-anchor) that asserts every direct subdirectory of .agents/skills/ and .claude/skills/ — VISIBLE AND HIDDEN — has a SKILL.md file.
2. The hook uses ls -A (or equivalent) so hidden dirs (.ddx/, .github/, .obsidian/, etc.) are NOT skipped.
3. The hook fails the commit with a clear error message naming each offending directory when SKILL.md is missing.
4. Manual test 1: drop a contaminated visible dir (e.g., .agents/skills/contamination/) into the tree, run lefthook run pre-commit, assert the hook fails.
5. Manual test 2: drop a contaminated HIDDEN dir (e.g., .agents/skills/.contamination/) into the tree, run lefthook run pre-commit, assert the hook ALSO fails.
6. lefthook run pre-commit passes on the current cleaned repo (all skill dirs have SKILL.md).
description:
PROBLEM
  On 2026-05-10 cleanup, ~5,800 tracked files (~625K lines) were
  removed from .agents/skills/ and .claude/skills/. They were
  source-tree mirrors of cli/, website/, docs/, library/,
  scripts/, tests/, skills/, AND HIDDEN dirs .ddx/, .github/,
  .obsidian/, .helix/, .claude/. The hidden-dir contamination
  was the worst (.ddx alone was 2,041 files per side).

  No validation gate caught any of it. Visible-dir cleanup found
  contamination via globbing */; the hidden-dir cleanup required
  an explicit pass for .*/ entries. A robust prevention guard
  must catch BOTH visible and hidden contamination at commit
  time.

  Without a guard, this contamination class is invisible: it
  doesn't break tests, doesn't fail builds, doesn't show up in
  CI. It just bloats the repo by an order of magnitude over time.

CURRENT STATE
  - lefthook.yml has pre-commit gates for secrets, debug
    statements, merge policy, etc., but nothing for skill-dir
    structure.
  - cli/internal/skills/install.go validates skills at install
    time but doesn't validate the on-disk layout from the
    operator-side.
  - No CI step or pre-commit hook examines .agents/skills/ or
    .claude/skills/ for entries without SKILL.md, visible or
    hidden.

PROPOSED FIX
  Add a pre-commit hook that:
    1. Iterates over EVERY direct entry of .agents/skills/ and
       .claude/skills/ (visible AND hidden — i.e., ls -A; do not
       use shell glob */ alone, which skips dotfiles).
    2. Skips files (SKILL.md and equivalents at the top of each
       skills/ root may be acceptable if the convention permits;
       err on the side of "every direct subdir must have
       SKILL.md").
    3. For each direct subdirectory, asserts a SKILL.md file
       exists.
    4. Fails the commit with a clear message naming the
       offending directories: "skill-dir <X> has no SKILL.md;
       skill directories must be real skills with a SKILL.md
       anchor. If this is contamination, remove the directory.
       If this is a new skill, add a SKILL.md."
    5. EXPLICITLY scans hidden dirs (.* pattern) — these were
       the worst offender in the 2026-05-10 cleanup.

  Implementation:
    - Add a hook entry in lefthook.yml under pre-commit:
        skill-dir-anchor:
          name: "Skill dirs must have SKILL.md"
          run: |
            failed=0
            for base in .agents/skills .claude/skills; do
              [ -d "$base" ] || continue
              # Use ls -A to include hidden dirs but skip . and ..
              for d in $(ls -A "$base"); do
                full="$base/$d"
                [ -d "$full" ] || continue
                if [ ! -f "$full/SKILL.md" ]; then
                  echo "ERROR: $full has no SKILL.md (contamination?)"
                  failed=1
                fi
              done
            done
            exit $failed

NON-SCOPE
  - Auto-removing contamination (humans should investigate why
    something is there before deleting).
  - Validating SKILL.md content (separate concern; spec quality
    is governed by skill authoring docs).
  - Naming convention enforcement (separate, smaller bead).

INTERSECTIONS
  - Free-standing prevention guard.
  - Memory note about Claude's intransigence with .agents folder
    + Windows symlink antipathy: this guard works for both base
    paths without requiring symlinks; it just enforces both
    have the same shape (every subdir is a real skill).
title: feat(lint): pre-commit guard rejects skill dirs without SKILL.md

description:
PROBLEM
DDx decomposition guidance and implementation currently frame decomposed parents as open, execution-ineligible containers. That leaves stale open parent beads in the queue and makes the safe operational answer unclear when an agent splits a bead: the correct answer is that a losslessly decomposed bead is completed by decomposition and should be closed. The downstream invariant is that children must still be work-ready: `parent` is hierarchy metadata, not a dependency gate, and generated children must not depend on the decomposed parent.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- docs/triage/decomposition.md:20-22 says `too_large_decomposed` leaves the parent `status=open` with dependency edges to children, and docs/triage/decomposition.md:63-73 says the parent remains open and depends on all children.

description:
PROBLEM: The pre-claim intake hook (cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go + preclaim_intake_rewrite.go) flags well-formed beads as ambiguous_needs_human with the generic detail "acceptance criteria dropped or altered", blocking them from execution.

{"detail":"acceptance criteria dropped or altered","intake_outcome":"ambiguous_needs_human"}

- axon-044a5b5b: original AC was a single sentence (legitimately weak — refinement was warranted, but intake should have produced a concrete suggested rewrite, not just a needs_human outcome).
- axon-11508cde: 7 numbered ACs with file:line refs, in-scope/out-of-scope sections, and a rollback plan. This is a strongly-formed bead and should pass intake; it was flagged anyway.

- preclaim_intake_rewrite.go:256 validateAndApplyPreClaimIntakeRewrite returns "acceptance criteria dropped or altered".
- preclaim_intake_rewrite.go:289 acceptancePreservesCriteria validates whether a rewrite preserves AC.
- The intake LLM is rewriting beads as part of intake; the rewrite validator (acceptancePreservesCriteria) is firing when the rewrite is structurally different even when the AC content is preserved or improved. EXPECTED BEHAVIOR:
- For weak ACs, intake should produce concrete suggested_fixes pointing at exactly what is missing (named test, file:line, etc.), not a needs_human outcome.
- For strong ACs, the intake rewriter should leave them alone (or recognize "no rewrite needed" as a pass), not generate a no-op rewrite that the validator flags.
- The validator should compare AC at a structural/semantic level (numbered points, named tests, verifiable claims) rather than literal-text equivalence.

description:
PROBLEM
A live holder can be age-superseded by a replacement lock, then later release by pathname and delete the replacement. Acquisition also lacks a strong owner identity and currently ignores metadata publication failures, so release cannot prove whether the canonical lock still belongs to the releasing holder.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go:224-230 publishes the canonical lock acquisition before requiring metadata publication success. cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go:282 later releases every holder with unconditional RemoveAll. cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go:323-328 may classify an over-age lock stale even when its PID is still live, and cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock_windows.go:7-16 makes age the only effective stale criterion on Windows. Without a token-bearing lease, an old holder has no way to distinguish its own canonical lock directory from a replacement.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
Phase 0 WB-5 requires a single-winner cross-process stale-break protocol at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase0-stop-the-self-harm-plan-2026-07-13.md:124-132.

PROPOSED FIX
Internally change main-git lock acquisition to return a lease containing the canonical path and a strong unique owner token while preserving withMainGitLock, WithMainGitLock, and withTrackerLock callback APIs. On successful os.Mkdir, write pid, acquired_at, and owner_token successfully before publishing acquisition. withTrackerLockPolicy must defer lease Release and join any release error with the callback error. Lease release must acquire the transition guard within a bounded policy, re-read canonical owner_token, and remove the canonical directory only when the token exactly matches the lease. Missing or mismatched tokens mean the lease was superseded and release preserves the replacement. If guarded release cannot be proven, return an error and leave the lock in place; never fall back to unconditional RemoveAll.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change tracker mutation semantics, tracker record format, trackerLockStaleAge, LockRetryPolicy defaults, lockmetrics caps, harness/Fizeau behavior, bead-store locks, git index locks, or the separate execution-cleanup lock in cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_loop.go:116-156. Do not extract a shared lock package; ddx-dffb7454 and ddx-3f156500 own separate sites and Phase 1 WB-8 owns unification. Do not implement delayed stale-breaker winner/loser disposal tests beyond the lease-release replacement-preservation case.

PARENT
ddx-8b22914e

DEPS
None. ddx-dffb7454 is a related collection-lock implementation, not a prerequisite or shared-package dependency.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx synthesizes a `default` routing profile for any operator who does not pass `--profile`, then sends `Profile="default"` to fizeau. Fizeau's `default` profile (`fizeau/internal/modelcatalog/catalog/models.yaml:438-443`) hard-pins `min_power: 7, max_power: 8`. For operators whose model catalog has no power-7-or-8 entries — e.g., local providers (power 5–6) plus frontier cloud (power 9) — `routePowerPolicyForRequest` overlays those bounds and the routing engine rejects every candidate as `below_min_power` or `above_max_power`. Result: zero-config `ddx work` claims a bead, dispatches with empty intent, fizeau returns "no viable routing candidate," and the agent exits in <1s with `no_evidence_produced`. Power was meant to be a hint, not a gate; synthesizing a constraint the operator never asked for inverts that policy. Repro: in this repo with no flags, `ddx work --once` triggers the dispatch-failure on hooks today and would trigger it on the implementation dispatch too if explicit `--harness/--model` flags weren't bypassing the bound via fizeau's exact-pin escape (`routePowerBoundsForRequest`).

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/routing_profile.go:9-15` returns the constant `"default"` whenever the operator-supplied profile is empty.
- `cli/cmd/work.go:70` registers the `--profile` flag with default value `agent.DefaultRoutingProfile`, so cobra fills in `"default"` even when the operator omits the flag.
- `cli/cmd/try.go:86` does the same for `ddx try`.
- `cli/cmd/run.go:137`, `cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go:298`, `cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go:1613`, `cli/cmd/try.go:215`, and `cli/internal/server/workers.go:{303,409,705}` all call `NormalizeRoutingProfile`, inheriting the synthesis.
- Downstream fizeau gating: `routePowerPolicyForRequest` (`fizeau/service_routing.go:1117-1141`) returns zero bounds only when `req.Profile == ""`; any non-empty profile string causes a catalog lookup that overlays its `min_power`/`max_power` onto the request.

PROPOSED FIX
- Change `NormalizeRoutingProfile` to return the trimmed input as-is; an empty operator value stays empty. Keep the function (callers want trim+normalize), drop the synthesis branch.
- Remove the `DefaultRoutingProfile = "default"` constant, or repurpose it strictly for the help-text label rather than a runtime default. Update `cli/cmd/work.go:70` and `cli/cmd/try.go:86` so the cobra flag's default is `""` and the help string reads "Routing profile: cheap, fast, smart (empty = unconstrained, let the agent service choose)".
- Audit every caller of `NormalizeRoutingProfile` to confirm they tolerate `""` (today they all forward the value into `CLIOverrides.Profile` or a workers spec — empty is already valid downstream).
- After this change, zero-config `ddx work` sends `Profile=""` → fizeau applies no profile-derived power bound → routing picks any available model regardless of power tier, honoring the "power is a hint" policy.
- The pre-dispatch lint and post-attempt triage hooks (`lint_hook.go`, `triage_hook.go`) still need `ClearProfile: true` so they ignore an explicitly operator-set `--profile fast`/`--profile standard` (those profiles also pin power 7-8); that defensive change is tracked in ddx-c54b817c and remains correct.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change fizeau's `default` profile or its power-gating semantics; making power bounds advisory rather than hard is a fizeau-side change and out of scope here.
- Do not change `--min-power`/`--max-power` flag handling. When the operator explicitly asks for a power bound, honor it; this bead only stops DDx from inventing one.
- Do not remove `cheap`/`fast`/`smart`/`standard` profile values — they remain available as explicit operator opt-ins.
- Do not modify ddx-c54b817c's hook-level fix; it is independently defensive against operator-set profiles.

PARENT + DEPS
No parent. No deps. ddx-c54b817c is sibling/defensive; both can land in either order.
title: agent: stop synthesizing default routing profile from empty input

After read-tree HEAD + update-ref, the main worktree reflects the new HEAD for exactly the files changed by the landing commit (no phantom D or M entries), while unrelated local modifications (agent-logs, beads.jsonl heartbeat) are preserved. Both Land() fast-path and merge-path call sites pass the correct fromRev. FetchOriginAncestryCheck same. description:
RealLandingGitOps.SyncIndexToHead in cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go only runs `git read-tree HEAD` after update-ref, which syncs the INDEX to HEAD but does NOT update files on disk in the main worktree. Every worker-landed commit that adds or modifies a tracked file leaves the main worktree showing phantom "D" or "M" entries in git status, even though HEAD is correct.

Impact during the Svelte+GraphQL migration epic: opus reviewers have been misled multiple times (reading stale working-tree copies instead of HEAD blobs), and I have manually run `git checkout -- <path>` after nearly every worker close (~6+ times this session). Subsequent agents that read files from the worktree see old content.

Scope of fix:
1. SyncIndexToHead -> SyncWorkTreeToHead. Take a fromRev parameter.
2. After read-tree HEAD, compute `git diff --name-only <fromRev> HEAD` to find the exact files changed by the landing commit
3. Run `git checkout-index -f -- <files>` to restore only those files (preserves unrelated local modifications like agent-logs and beads.jsonl heartbeats)
4. Apply to both call sites in Land() (fast-forward path and merge path) and the FetchOriginAncestryCheck update-ref block
5. Update LandingGitOps interface + test stubs

Alternative considered: git checkout-index -a -f (restore ALL files from index) — rejected because it would clobber legitimate local modifications to files unrelated to the landing commit (agent-logs, beads.jsonl heartbeat writes).

This is a P0 blocker for running the migration epic without constant human babysitting. Fix directly via deterministic edit, not via worker dispatch, because the surface is small, the fix is mechanical, and the diagnostic cost of a worker misunderstanding the fix is higher than the implementation cost of just applying it.
title: bug: Land() leaves main worktree stale — update-ref + read-tree doesn't materialize files

description:
PROBLEM
HELIX is available as a marketplace plugin, so DDx should stop treating plugin install as "copy all plugin assets into each repository." The desired operator model is npx-like: a project records plugin intent/version pins, plugin payloads resolve into an XDG cache or compatible global install, and local agent skill directories are generated shims/links that can be recreated at any time.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-015-installation-architecture.md:60 still described `ddx init` as writing `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` project files.
- docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-015-installation-architecture.md:63 described registry plugin install as writing real files under `<projectRoot>/.ddx/plugins/<name>/`.
- docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-015-installation-architecture.md:317 said `ddx init` and registry plugin installs copy real files for clone portability.
- docs/helix/02-design/adr/ADR-027-skill-install-topology.md:46 described default project install as plugin content under project/convention plugin trees with agent-tier outputs under the project.
- docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-018-plugin-api.md:58 described `install.root` as copying the entire plugin to a target and had no materialization/cache contract.
- cli/cmd/install.go:150 calls `adjustInstallTargets` and `registry.InstallPackage`, which copies package payloads into the resolved install root.
- cli/cmd/install.go:216 rewrites package install targets to `plugins/<name>`, preserving the copy-tree model for registry installs.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement the marketplace materialization contract now documented in FEAT-015, FEAT-018, and ADR-027:

description:
PROBLEM
Federation today supports query fan-out only (cli/internal/federation/fanout.go). For the multi-node operator-prompt path, the coordinator (hub) must route a mutation to a single spoke that owns the project, NOT fan out. No mutation routing envelope, no project-based spoke selection, and no forwarding client exist.

ROOT CAUSE
- cli/internal/federation/fanout.go: FanOut function sends read queries to all spokes; has no concept of routing to a single owning spoke for mutations.
- FederationRegistry (from ddx-90f48012): stores spoke records by node_id but no lookup-by-project-id helper exists.
- No HTTP client method ForwardMutation exists in the federation package.
- Plan-locked decision (point 6 from story-15 planning): hub picks single owning spoke by project ID from FederationRegistry; no broadcast of mutations; mutation envelope is HTTP POST to spoke /graphql with X-DDx-Origin-Identity and X-DDx-Coordinator-Identity headers preserved verbatim.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add RouteMutationToProjectOwner(registry FederationRegistry, projectID string) (*SpokeRecord, error): looks up the spoke that owns the project; returns error when no owner registered.
- Add federation client method ForwardMutation(ctx context.Context, target *SpokeRecord, body []byte, headers map[string]string) (*http.Response, error): issues HTTP POST to <spoke>/graphql with supplied headers preserved verbatim.
- Add hub HTTP handler that accepts forwarding requests and routes by project (the handler that S15-7c and S15-7d build on top of).
- Identity header values are NOT populated in this bead (that is S15-7c / ddx-ba31fec8); this bead lays the envelope and routing.

NON-SCOPE
- Dual authorization on the spoke side (ddx-ba31fec8).
- Identity attestation structure (ddx-e2c217d1).
- Changing existing query fan-out behavior.

description:
PROBLEM
Five DDx call sites talk to fizeau in mixed dialects: hardcoded profile names ("smart", "default", "cheap"), DDx-side model catalog lookups (`ResolveModelTier`), homemade power-floor tricks (`MinPowerOverride = max(all model powers)`), and brittle string-matching retries (`isSmartRouteUnavailableError`). Fizeau is realigning around a single concept — **profile** — defined and enumerated by fizeau's catalog and exposed via `svc.ListProfiles`. DDx-internal callers (lint, triage, intake, reviewer) need to talk to fizeau in that one vocabulary: select a profile by criteria against fizeau's live list, send it as `Profile`. The other knobs (`Harness`, `Provider`, `Model`, `ModelRef`) are **operator-supplied pins for fallback only** — DDx-internal code must never invent them. Power bounds (`MinPower`, `MaxPower`) are a numerical refinement on top of a profile, legitimately used only by the reviewer's `MinPower = impl.actualPower+1` bump.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:91-105` pins `ProfileOverride: "smart"` plus `MinPowerOverride = max(all model powers)` plus `ClearMaxPower: true`. The MinPower trick is a hard floor masquerading as a hint; the "smart" string is brittle to fizeau's policy realignment.
- `cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:122-133` `dispatchPreClaimIntakePayload` retries with empty ModelRef when `isSmartRouteUnavailableError` matches a substring of the dispatch error — exists only because the hardcoded "smart" reference is fragile.
- `cli/internal/agent/lint_hook.go:128-132` and `cli/internal/agent/triage_hook.go:114-118` set no profile at all; both inherit `rcfg.Profile()` (currently broken under default-profile synthesis, addressed structurally by ddx-ea91688b — but the *positive* signal "this is a cheap auxiliary call" is never expressed).

That call hits the DDx-side `BuiltinCatalog` (deleted by ddx-cd641910) and pins `Model` directly — DDx-internal code inventing a pin, which is the boundary violation this bead also closes.

description:
PROBLEM

Underspecified worker/provider-process failures are a DDx correctness bug. DDx/FIZ is the abstraction that should keep work moving across provider availability and local configuration variance. If a provider executable is missing, a harness process exits early, model routing fails, or Fizeau returns a pre-dispatch/provider-boundary error, `ddx work` must classify it with a typed provider/process reason, record fallback/stop evidence, clean up any children, and continue when an alternate route is eligible. It must not surface a generic worker failure, raw "routing under-specified" text, or leave the bead/operator unable to tell whether this is provider_auth, provider_model_unavailable, provider_harness_unavailable, provider_connectivity, no_viable_provider, provider_config_invalid, or unknown_provider_failure.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE

- `cli/internal/agent/provider_failure.go:1-17` defines the intended DDx/Fizeau boundary contract: generic untyped provider failures are product bugs, and each provider failure needs typed reason, retryability, fallback decision, and durable evidence.
- `cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:140-142` still returns `fmt.Errorf("agent: execute: %w", err)` for Fizeau `Execute` setup failures before the event stream exists; every caller must prove this error is classified and does not fall through as generic execution/worker failure.
- `cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:337-385` bounds event-stream silence/tool loops, but provider-process startup/early-exit failures can occur before useful stream evidence, so they need a separate typed classification/cleanup path.
- `cli/cmd/zero_config_work_test.go:15-27` documents the prior "routing under-specified" regression and explicitly avoids real provider dispatch; coverage must be extended from "do not print under-specified" to "classify provider-process failure and choose fallback/stop semantics."
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_escalation_aborted_test.go:18-60` and `:285-342` prove provider_connectivity fallback semantics after reports exist, but do not prove raw provider-process failures are converted into those reports before worker/operator surfaces see them.

PROPOSED FIX

Add an end-to-end worker/process-boundary classification path for provider process startup, missing executable, early child exit, model-unavailable, under-specified routing, and Fizeau pre-dispatch errors. Normalize them through the provider failure taxonomy, write `ProviderFailureEvidence`, include requested/resolved harness/provider/model plus retryability and fallback_stop_reason, and ensure unpinned workers automatically retry eligible alternate routes while pinned workers stop loudly with hard_pin_exhausted. Ensure cleanup reaps provider-process children before the worker continues.

NON-SCOPE

Do not move model catalog/routing ownership out of Fizeau. Do not call real Claude/Codex/Gemini providers in tests. Do not silently widen explicit operator pins. Do not weaken existing provider_connectivity/no_viable_provider fallback tests.
title: agent: type worker provider-process failures before generic failure

description:
PROBLEM
DDx needs an explicit readiness lifecycle contract that optimizes for continuous forward progress. Today the specs both allow readiness to move ambiguous/underspecified open beads to status=proposed and say quality gates default to WARN-ONLY, leaving workers and lifecycle hooks free to park operator-accepted work repeatedly.

ROOT CAUSE
- docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-010-task-execution.md:219-224 defines ambiguous_requires_operator as moving the bead to status=proposed, and docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-010-task-execution.md:485-493 repeats that ambiguous or underspecified work moves to proposed. It does not define operator promotion as an override.
- docs/helix/02-design/adr/ADR-023-bead-lifecycle-quality-policy.md:85-99 says WARN-ONLY is the default, but docs/helix/02-design/adr/ADR-023-bead-lifecycle-quality-policy.md:136-173 still permits readiness to block for human input or lossy decomposition without spelling out which findings are advisory versus hard blockers.
- docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-027-bead-collection-abstraction.md:70-75 and :785-792 define proposed -> open as triaged, but the operator-acceptance semantics are not connected to readiness re-evaluation.
- docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-031-bead-state-machine.md:160-172 allows open -> proposed for depth overflow or ambiguity, but does not require idempotency after proposed -> open.

PROPOSED FIX
Update the governing docs to state:
- open is the forward-progress execution lane; proposed is the hard operator-decision escape hatch.
- Default pre-claim readiness is warn/improve/decompose; it must proceed for recoverable rubric gaps, lint noise, uncertain model judgment, and readiness infrastructure failures.
- Automatic open -> proposed is reserved for true operator_required outcomes, lossy decomposition, contradictory requirements, unsafe commitment loss, or explicit hard manual-decision blockers.
- proposed -> open via operator action is durable acceptance. Re-readiness must not re-park the same bead for the same rule/finding unless prompt-relevant bead fields changed or the operator explicitly requests re-triage.
- Reuse the TD-027 triaged event for proposed -> open. If new warning event kinds are needed, amend TD-027 event vocabulary in the same spec change; otherwise use existing event kinds with structured fields.

NON-SCOPE
- No Go implementation in this bead.
- No change to Fizeau routing/profile/model/provider behavior.
- No weakening of post-attempt review/manual-required outcomes that already have concrete execution evidence.

PARENT/DEPS
Parent: ddx-cc0641a7. No deps.
notes: Operator reviewed readiness downgrade on 2026-05-12. Bead is execution-ready as written; readiness parked it because its attempted rewrite dropped the explicit NON-SCOPE commitment about not weakening post-attempt review/manual-required outcomes. Add triage:skip so this bead can proceed and fix the downgrade-loop policy.

acceptance: FEAT-002, FEAT-013, architecture.md, and TP-002 describe one `ddx server` process managing multiple project roots on one machine with explicit project registry, request scoping, per-project isolation, and migration semantics from the current single-project host
description:
<context-digest>
Review area: ddx server topology. Evidence covers FEAT-002, FEAT-013, architecture.md, TP-002, and the current assumption that one `ddx server` serves exactly one repo.
</context-digest>
Design the first-step multi-project `ddx server` module for a single machine.

## Goals
1. Replace the single-project server assumption with a project registry / project-root collection managed by one server process on one machine
2. Define project-scoped API, MCP, and UI routing semantics so clients can enumerate projects and then operate within one selected project context
3. Define per-project config, cache, and adapter boundaries so one bad project cannot poison other served projects
4. Define how project-scoped worktrees and worker pools are managed under one server process without assuming only one active repository
5. Define migration from today's single-project `ddx server` invocation and data adapters without breaking current local use

## Required outputs
- Project registry/discovery contract
- Request routing and project selection model
- Per-project isolation and failure-mode analysis
- Impact on FEAT-008 UI and TP-002 end-to-end coverage
title: Design one-machine multi-project ddx server topology

acceptance:
AC1. Land-coordinator refuses to merge a bead result whose net diff deletes more than N lines from a single file (configurable threshold, default 200) UNLESS the agent's no_changes_rationale.txt or commit message explicitly acknowledges and justifies the deletion (e.g. 'intentional file removal: <reason>').

AC2. Land-coordinator runs a basic sanity gate before merging: the file must still parse for its filetype (TypeScript files compile, Svelte files have valid <script>/<template>/<style> structure if they had one previously, JSON is valid JSON, etc.). Failed parse = preserve as iteration ref, do not merge.

AC3. When a parse-fail or large-deletion gate trips, the bead is marked 'preserved-needs-review' and the operator is alerted via the bead's notes field, with a link to the iteration ref and a one-line summary of what gate fired.

AC4. Post-merge typecheck/build is run as a final gate (project-level command from .ddx/config.yaml or sensible default like 'cargo check' / 'bun run build'). If post-merge build fails, AUTOMATICALLY revert the merge and preserve the result instead. This is the safety net for cases AC2 doesn't catch.

AC5. Documentation in docs/ explains the safety gates, how to override them when intentional (e.g. for genuine large deletions), and what 'preserved-needs-review' means operationally.

AC6. A regression test on the harness validates that an attempt to merge a result deleting >N lines (or producing a parse failure) is correctly preserved+rejected, not merged.
description:
Today on axon repo, the ddx-land-coordinator merged a bead-result branch onto master that deleted 1448 lines from one Svelte component (1552 → 104 lines). The same merge also corrupted a second test file (1043 → 158 lines, overwritten with unrelated content). Master became unbuildable: vite-plugin-svelte threw 'Expected token }' because the policies/+page.svelte file lost its <script lang="ts"> wrapper along with the entire HTML template and style sections.

The damaging merge:

  commit be1073f4333c289e48680cf8c05ceefa7ea9c075
  Merge: 0c5557b 2f35ad2
  Author: ddx-land-coordinator <coordinator@ddx.local>
  Date:   Wed Apr 29 20:56:46 2026 -0400

      Merge bead axon-80979cb8 attempt 20260430T005434- into master

       .../databases/[database]/policies/+page.svelte     | 1448 --------------------
       1 file changed, 1448 deletions(-)

The post-merge codex reviewer DID block subsequent attempts that built on the broken base ('the diff only adds execution metadata' / 'the new Playwright coverage is incorrect... the collection view never loads'), but the original 1448-line deletion went through unchecked. Five subsequent worker attempts ran on top of the now-broken master, each adding ~80 lines of partial reconstructions, none producing a valid Svelte file.

Net damage on master before manual recovery:
  ui/src/routes/.../policies/+page.svelte      1552 → 186 lines (1366 lines lost)
  ui/tests/e2e/policy-enforcement.spec.ts      1043 → 158 lines (885 lines lost)
  master state: vite-plugin-svelte fails to compile, UI bundle cannot build, docker e2e harness cannot start

Manual recovery (commit bc4b492 on axon master): git checkout HEAD~14 of both files, re-stage, commit, push. 2415 lines restored across 3 files.

Why this happened (hypothesis):
  1. The bead-attempt branch had a partial reconstruction of the file (104 lines of just imports/state, no template).
  2. The land-coordinator did a 3-way merge with master at base_rev. The base_rev was ALSO the partial reconstruction (because EARLIER attempts had already truncated it).
  3. Three-way merge produced a 'clean' delete of the 1448 lines that existed only on master's side because base_rev was already broken.

Or alternatively: the agent's tool calls deleted content from the worktree without re-emitting the full file (e.g. used Edit with overlapping replace blocks that effectively truncated), the harness committed whatever was on disk without sanity-checking magnitude, and the land-coordinator merged the partial content as authoritative.
title: execute-bead: land-coordinator merged a result that deleted 1448 lines from a single file (catastrophic damage)

description:
PROBLEM
  lefthook.yml pre-push hook runs `go test -race -cover ./...` (full
  suite, ~168s) on every push. This blocks the operator's session-end
  push for the duration of the full suite, even though CI on origin
  already runs the same suite on every push. The pre-push run is
  duplicate work and duplicate wait time. Full-suite execution is still
  required on a semi-regular basis (regression detection), but
  blocking the operator's single push at session end is the wrong
  place to do it.

  Note (per the 2026-05-09 plan-review): after sister bead
  ddx-1f774edf removes network I/O from Land(), the drain itself
  stops pushing entirely (operator pushes once at session end). So
  this bead's impact lands on the operator's session-end push, not on
  per-bead drain throughput.

ROOT CAUSE
  - lefthook.yml line ~572 (full-tests run command):
        `go test -race -cover ./...`
    runs on every pre-push event.
  - .github/workflows/ci.yml runs the same suite on push to origin,
    making the pre-push run redundant for regression detection.
  - There is no opt-in local target for "verify before push" workflows;
    today's only option is the always-on pre-push hook.

PROPOSED FIX
  1. Edit lefthook.yml (line ~572 area): remove the `full-tests` step
     from the pre-push hook entirely. Keep all other pre-push steps
     (git-config-health, merge-policy, no-debug, build, lint, etc.).
     If lefthook supports skip-by-default-but-runnable commands, mark
     full-tests skip-by-default; otherwise just delete the step from
     pre-push and surface it elsewhere.

  2. Add (or confirm) a local opt-in path for "verify before push"
     workflows:
        a. Existing Makefile `test` target runs `go test -v ./...` —
           document this as the local pre-push verification path.
        b. Optionally add a new `test-full` target that mirrors CI's
           invocation exactly (`go test -race -cover ./...`).

  3. Verify .github/workflows/ci.yml still runs the full suite without
     -short on every push to origin. (The earlier audit confirmed it
     does; just verify nothing has changed.)

  4. Update CLAUDE.md (or docs/helix/06-iterate/) with a one-paragraph
     note on the pre-push / CI split:
        - Pre-push runs cheap safety checks (build, lint, secrets,
          git-config-health, merge-policy, no-debug) for fast operator
          feedback.
        - CI on origin runs the full suite for every push.
        - Operators wanting "verify before push" run `make test` or
          `make test-full` manually.

NON-SCOPE
  - Adding -short to pre-push (deliberately superseded; full removal is
    cleaner).
  - testing.Short() skips on individual hot tests (sister bead
    ddx-1fda33d2 still useful — those skips help local `make test`

  - perf-tag separation (sister bead ddx-150758e7 still useful —

INTERSECTIONS

description:
PROBLEM
Operators have no way to dispatch a SPECIFIC bead through the production execution machinery (claim → try.Attempt → land → review). Today's surfaces:
- 'ddx work' drains by picker priority — can't force a specific bead
- 'ddx work --once' drains the top of the queue once — still picker-controlled
- 'ddx agent run --prompt' invokes the agent but doesn't claim, doesn't merge, doesn't write to bead event log

This blocks: (1) deterministic queue ordering during refactor execution, (2) the 3-path comparison study (ddx-31f745cd) which needs a way to target one fixture bead at a time, (3) operator-driven debugging when a bead misbehaves under autonomous drain.

ROOT CAUSE
'ddx try' was originally bundled into refactor child C13 (ddx-387a0178) along with the file rename. C13 is sequenced AFTER C7 / C9 because the rename touches execute_bead_loop.go which those children also touch. But 'ddx try' itself is ADDITIVE — a new CLI subcommand that delegates to existing machinery — and doesn't conflict with the refactor children. Splitting 'ddx try' out lets it ship FIRST and unblocks operator-controlled execution for the entire rest of the refactor work.

Code today (relevant entry points):
- cli/cmd/work.go: 'ddx work' command implementation (calls into agent.ExecuteBeadLoopRuntime)
- cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go: 'ddx agent work' (the underlying loop runner)
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go: ExecuteBeadWorker.Run + nextCandidate
- cli/internal/bead/store.go:1246 ReadyExecution + Claim

PROPOSED FIX
Add a new top-level command at cli/cmd/try.go:

  ddx try <bead-id> [--harness=<name>] [--model=<name>] [--profile=<name>]

Behavior:
1. Look up the bead by ID via the bead store; fail-fast with a clear message if not found.
2. Verify the bead is in a claimable state (status open OR stale-in_progress per existing semantics); fail-fast if status closed/cancelled OR if it has unmet dependencies.
3. Force-target this single bead. Two implementation strategies (pick simpler):
   STRATEGY A (thin wrapper): construct an ExecuteBeadLoopRuntime with --once + a custom nextCandidate that returns ONLY this bead-id, skipping the picker. Call ExecuteBeadWorker.Run.
   STRATEGY B (direct invocation): claim the bead, build the runtime config, call try.Attempt directly (or whatever the underlying single-bead execution function is today). Skip the loop.
   Recommend STRATEGY A — reuses the existing claim + executor + outcome paths; smaller diff; less risk of behavior divergence.
4. Honor --harness / --model / --profile / --opaque-passthrough exactly the way 'ddx work' does (same flag plumbing).
5. Exit with the bead's terminal status (success → 0; preserved/no_changes/blocked → non-zero with structured stderr).

NON-SCOPE
- File rename of execute_bead_loop.go (still owned by C13)
- Refactor of execute-bead surface into try/work packages (refactor epic)
- Multi-bead try (use 'ddx work' for that)
- Server-side targeting (a future enhancement; v1 is local CLI only)
- Auto-discovery of dependencies (operator must use 'ddx bead ready' first)

INTERSECTION
- C13 (ddx-387a0178) currently includes 'ADD ddx try CLI command' in its scope. After this bead lands, amend C13 to drop that line.
- 3-path comparison study (ddx-31f745cd) Path A uses 'ddx try' as the production-path executor; this bead unblocks that study.
- Refactor children Wave 2 dispatch will use 'ddx try' (codex harness) to deterministically dispatch each child in dep order.

description:
PROBLEM
The 2026-06-15 DDx server-managed Claude TUI canary completed ddx-cf0cafef successfully, then exposed two reliability violations. First, the land/audit path appended `.ddx/metrics/locks.jsonl` entries showing index.lock held for 20.177s during index.commit and tracker.lock held for 20.651s during durable_audit, exceeding the 10s/30s lock lifetime contract risk envelope for short-lived mutation locks. Second, when the watch worker immediately claimed ddx-2b15342f and was stopped through POST /api/agent/workers/<id>/stop, the worker process exited with status 130 but `ddx work status --json` still reported active_work for ddx-2b15342f until an operator manually ran `ddx bead update ddx-2b15342f --unclaim`.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go land/durable-audit finalization still performs git index commit work while the durable_audit tracker lock remains held, and lock metrics recorded the over-cap hold in `.ddx/metrics/locks.jsonl`. cli/internal/server/workers.go stop handling terminates a managed worker process group but does not release any bead claim owned by that managed worker ID when the process exits before starting an attempt. `ddx work status` reads the claim as active even though the server record is stopped/pid_alive=false.

PROPOSED FIX
Split durable-audit finalization so git index add/commit work is not performed while tracker.lock is held, and keep index.lock hold below its cap. On managed-worker stop/process exit, release open bead claims whose owner/assignee is the stopped server-managed worker ID, append durable operator/worker lifecycle evidence, and make `ddx work status --json` report no active work for a stopped managed worker with no live process.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change the successful implementation from ddx-cf0cafef. Do not weaken lock caps. Do not hide lock violations from metrics. Do not auto-release claims for unrelated external workers that the server does not own.

description:
# PROBLEM
Orphan `codex` processes (ppid=1, ~90-100% CPU) accumulate on any host running `ddx work --watch`, despite the Pdeathsig-shim fix landing in `851d9e2b3` / `c318e1934` / `623166130`. Verified in production 2026-07-01: fresh worker binary contains `__provider-launch` and `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH` symbols, but 4-day-old orphan `codex` processes exist and new orphans continue appearing at ~1 per 1-2 hours on each active worker. Reaping by hand each loop tick is not tenable.

# ROOT CAUSE
`cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go:83` `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH` installs the PATH shim (which wraps codex/claude in `ddx __provider-launch` so the kernel sets PR_SET_PDEATHSIG=SIGKILL on the provider before execve).

The shim install is called from ONE place only: `cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:103` inside `runAgentViaService`. That function is **legacy** — reachable only from `RunAgent(r, opts)` in `cli/internal/agent/agent_runner.go:5-7`, which per its own doc-comment is used by the virtual/script harnesses only.

The production provider-spawn entry point is `cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:110` `RunWithConfigViaService`, called by:
- `cli/cmd/run.go:164` (ddx run)
- `cli/cmd/exec.go:101` (ddx exec)
- `cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:312` (ddx try / ddx work smoke path)
- `cli/internal/server/server.go:2519` and `:5068` (server HTTP)
- `cli/internal/server/review_dispatcher.go:72` (review dispatch)

`RunWithConfigViaService` does NOT call `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH`. Every `ddx work` / `ddx try` / `ddx run` therefore constructs a Fizeau service whose `LookPath("codex")` finds the raw `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/codex`, spawns it with Fizeau's default `SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}` (no Pdeathsig), and any SIGKILL/OOM of the worker leaks the codex child as an orphan.

# EVIDENCE
- Isolated Pdeathsig test PASSES: `ddx __provider-launch /bin/sleep 30 & sleep 0.5; kill -9 $!` → sleep dies within 1s. So the seam itself is correct.
- Fizeau `internal/harnesses/codex/runner.go:64,84,105` uses `osexec.LookPath("codex")` at spawn time — so a PATH prepend by DDx WOULD intercept.
- Grep confirms `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH` has exactly one non-test caller: `agent_runner_service.go:103`. Nothing in the production flow reaches it.
- Production symptom: 5-28 orphan codex procs accumulate per day of drain activity.

# PROPOSED FIX
Install the shim inside `RunWithConfigViaService` before `resolveService` — best-effort, mirroring the pattern already at `agent_runner_service.go:102-106` verbatim. `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH` is idempotent (sync.Mutex + early-return when providerShimDirPath != ""), so calling it from both paths is safe.

# NON-SCOPE
- Zombie/orphan reaper strategy (`ddx-ae98c450`, `ddx-096129b9`, `ddx-24a3da84`) — separate reliability layer.
- Server-managed worker supervisor (`ddx-9d1af129` epic) — separate initiative.
- Windows/darwin — Pdeathsig is Linux-only; other platforms no-op via `provider_spawn_windows.go` etc.
- Reviewing/replacing the legacy `RunAgent` path — separate cleanup; keep both shim installs for safety.

description:
# PROBLEM
`ddx work --watch` gets into an unrecoverable spawn-loop where the worker keeps launching codex subprocesses that its own status.json labels as "non-route provider ... terminated by running-phase guard" — but the guard does NOT terminate them. Result: no bead progress, stale claude/opus attempt state, infinite codex churn. Observed live 2026-07-02: worker pid 3893557 on bead ddx-68b48c9e, attempt 20260702T105934-18be73ef.

# EVIDENCE (captured)
Worker `status.json` reports:
- `harness: claude`, `model: opus`, `phase: running`
- `provider_children: [{pid: 1229443, provider: codex, non_route: true, diagnostic: "non-route provider codex terminated by running-phase guard (active route claude)"}]`

BUT `ps --ppid 3893557` shows only:
- `git` (age 14:41)
- `codex` (age 14:17, the "non-route" one)
- NO claude process

The claude/opus process that the status says is "running" is gone. The codex that the guard claims to have "terminated" is alive. When I manually `kill 1229443`, the worker immediately respawns a fresh codex (1416758) within seconds — same non-route state. Worker itself is in `futex_wait_queue` in kernel wait.

Log shows `worker.heartbeat` every ~30s with `phase=running` but no actual work events for 1h+. Zero bead outcome events (no ✓/✗/no_changes/timeout/etc.).

# ROOT CAUSE HYPOTHESIS
Two candidate bugs:

1. **Running-phase guard doesn't actually kill**: some code path emits the `terminated by running-phase guard` diagnostic string without calling kill/wait on the non-route pid. So the message is aspirational, not reflective.

2. **Claude harness dispatch died but the worker didn't detect it**: the ExecuteBeadLoop harness=claude route's process died (SIGKILL, panic, EOF on stream) without emitting a final event, so the worker's outcome detection never fires. Then something (readiness probe, review dispatch, model discovery?) keeps re-invoking codex as a background helper, hitting the guard, spinning.

Grep entry points:
- `cli/internal/server/workers.go:1214-1483` (Stop/watchdog reap)
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go` (main execute loop)
- `cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_process*.go` (reaper)
- Any code emitting the exact string `non-route provider ... terminated by running-phase guard` — that's the diagnostic source

# PROPOSED FIX
1. Locate the emission site of the `"non-route provider %s terminated by running-phase guard"` diagnostic. Verify it actually calls `syscall.Kill(pid, SIGTERM)` (or SIGKILL after grace) — NOT just labels the child. Add a wait-with-timeout to prove termination.
2. Add a watchdog: if `provider_children[].non_route=true` for a child that has been alive >N seconds AND the child's pid still exists AND no successor process replaced it via a legitimate route, kill it hard (SIGKILL + wait) and log at level ERROR.
3. When the claim's route harness (claude/opus) subprocess exits without emitting a final event, the worker MUST synthesize a terminal outcome (execution_failed or transport-classified) instead of remaining `phase=running` forever. Currently it appears to just sit in futex_wait indefinitely.

# NON-SCOPE
- The specific test-harness deadlock inside ddx-68b48c9e itself (that's a separate story if it exists).
- Server-managed workers (ddx-9d1af129 epic) — this bug affects both server-managed and standalone `ddx work`.

# IMPACT
Without this fix, any transient claude subprocess death mid-attempt puts a worker into a permanent stuck state with 100% CPU codex spawn churn. Queue drain stalls. On my machine this required manual `kill 1229443` + kill worker + restart to unstick.
title: worker: non-route provider spawn-loop when claude harness subprocess dies silently

description:
PROBLEM
Server-managed worker records can show a stale current_attempt from an old worker. During live dogfood on 2026-06-15, a newly started ddx server worker worker-20260615T165912-4cb5 had pid=1043072/pgid=1043072 and its log showed it starting ddx-cf0cafef, but ddx server workers show hydrated current_attempt from old run-state 20260615T135134-8c4db98d / bead ddx-f93e6ef9. The sesame canary similarly showed old sesame-4a08e922 while its log was idle. This makes the web UI and server status untrustworthy for live worker monitoring.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/server/workers.go:860-905 refreshWorkerCurrentAttemptFromRunState calls agent.ReadRunState(projectRoot) for every running/stopping WorkerRecord and copies the returned attempt into rec.CurrentAttempt. It does not check that the run-state is unexpired, that the pid is alive, or that the run-state belongs to this WorkerRecord/PID/worker id. cli/internal/agent/run_state.go:204-223 ReadRunState returns a compatibility file or newest per-attempt record without filtering expired records; stale .ddx/run-state/*.json entries with expires_at hours in the past can therefore be reused.

PROPOSED FIX
Make server worker current_attempt hydration worker-specific and freshness-aware. Running WorkerRecord hydration must ignore run-state whose expires_at is before now, whose pid is dead, or whose pid/worker identity does not match the WorkerRecord PID/ID. Prefer in-memory ProgressEvent state when available. If no matching fresh state exists, leave CurrentAttempt nil rather than showing stale work. Add a cleanup or read-time filter so historical .ddx/run-state/*.json records do not poison server status.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change execute-bead claim semantics. Do not delete tracked execution evidence. Do not hide LastAttempt history for completed workers.
title: server: ignore stale run-state when hydrating worker attempts

description:
PROBLEM
Agent tests and fixture helpers that call `git config` can select the invoking checkout's shared common gitdir instead of a temporary fixture repository. When a fixture writes values such as `core.bare=true`, `core.worktree`, `user.name`, or `user.email`, the full agent test suite can corrupt the repository configuration used by the primary checkout and linked worktrees.

cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_git_isolation.go:20-55 enables worktree config and seeds per-worktree config for execute-bead isolation, and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_git_isolation.go:169-229 wraps commands executed through the agent harness. The helper must clear inherited repository-selection environment (`GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, and related config selectors as applicable) unless it deliberately sets fixture-local values. Production execute-bead callers must remain wired through the same isolation helper surface instead of growing an ad hoc test-only workaround.

  - Inside a "## What HELIX Is Not" section: "HELIX is not a CLI." → does NOT fire (section-context suppression)

cli/internal/docprose/docprose_test.go includes a unit test for the rule covering positive-predicate detection and section-context suppression.

description:
ddx doc prose today catches surface hedge words via contains_any matchers ("robust", "comprehensive", "seamless"). It does not catch a more damaging structural defect: defining a subject by what it isn't.

A real example from a recent HELIX prose pass:

> HELIX models software development as a continuous control loop with seven activities, **not a sequential pipeline**.

The sentence tells the reader what HELIX *is not* (a pipeline) without ever giving the positive shape. The same offense appeared fourteen times across seven documents in different surface forms ("cyclic, not linear", "loop, not pipeline", "not sequential", "not waterfall"). Human review caught it; the prose checker passed it clean.

The defect is structural: a clause whose main predicate is `not <noun-phrase>` with no positive predicate in the same sentence describing what the subject *is*. Prose like that reads as hedging and forces the reader to infer what the author meant.

Proposed rule shape:

Add a new kind: negation_predicate to the ruleSpec schema (cli/internal/docprose/assets.go). Implementation in the embedded checker (cli/internal/docprose/checker.go) scans sentences for the pattern:

  <subject> [is|are|stays|remains] not <noun-phrase|adjective>

Fires only when no positive predicate appears in the same sentence describing the subject. A positive predicate is anything matching `<subject> [is|are|...] <noun-phrase|adjective>` *without* the `not`.

Default rule in the planning pack:

  - id: prose.definition_by_negation
    severity: warning
    kind: negation_predicate
    rationale: This sentence defines its subject by what it is not. Readers infer what you mean; stronger prose names the positive shape directly.
    suggested_edit: Replace the negation with a sentence whose main predicate describes what the subject is. Keep the negation only if a positive predicate follows in the same paragraph.

Scope notes — legitimate uses of negation should not fire:
- Sections explicitly enumerating what something is not ("What HELIX Is Not", "Non-Goals", "Out of Scope", "Anti-Patterns").
- Contrastive constructions where the positive follows immediately ("HELIX is not a CLI; it is a methodology") — the second clause supplies the positive predicate.

The rule needs section-context awareness: ignore matches inside H2/H3 sections whose heading matches `What .+ Is Not|Non-?Goals?|Out of Scope|Anti-Patterns?`. This is the first prose rule that needs heading context, so it likely requires a small extension to the checker per-rule context model.

Out of scope:
- AI-grade semantic detection. The heuristic above catches the structural defect; deeper analysis is a separate request.
- Cross-paragraph context. Start with same-sentence detection; widen if false-negative rate is high in practice.
title: doc prose: detect definition-by-negation as a structural rule
